<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof"></a>
<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof--sharpness-for-every-n--2s-r-1"></a>
### Sharpness for every n >= 2s-r-1

This note gives the complete proof of the manuscript's uniform larger-gap construction. It concerns only avoid-or-compress lengths. It does not determine all remaining parameters.

**Proposition.** For integers r >= 1, g >= 2 and M >= 2g, there is a binary, strongly connected, synchronizing automaton with n=r+M+1, a reachable image S of size s=r+g+1, and A of size r such that ac(S,A)=M+1=n-r. Consequently both maxima equal the known upper bound U whenever s-r >= 3 and n >= 2s-r-1.

The upper bound is the existing avoid-or-compress lemma. Here n-s=M-g=m>=g>=2, and n-r=m+g+1<=2m+1<=binom(m+2,2). Thus it suffices to prove the lower bound with all structural requirements.

Use disjoint sets P={p_0,...,p_r} and U={u_1,...,u_M}. Put A=P\{p_r} and S=P union {u_1,...,u_g}. All actions and matrix products below act on the right.

<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof--the-construction-for-m--2g1"></a>
#### The construction for M >= 2g+1

Put h=1+((M-1) mod g). Then 1<=h<=g, M-h is a positive multiple of g, and M>=2g+h. Define a to fix P, send u_j to u_(j+1) for j<M, and send u_M to u_(h+1). Define b by

* p_0 b=u_h and p_i b=p_(i-1) for 1<=i<=r;
* u_j b=p_r when j is congruent to h-1 modulo g;
* u_g b=u_1 when h>=2;
* u_M b=u_(h+g);
* every remaining u_j goes to u_(j+1).

The cases are disjoint: neither g (when h>=2) nor M is in the first U-case. On S, b cycles

```
p_0,u_h,u_(h+1),...,u_g,u_1,...,u_(h-1),p_r,p_(r-1),...,p_1.
```

For h=1 the middle wraparound segment is empty. Every outside state reaches this cycle under b in at most g+1 steps. Ordinary states follow an increasing-index path to the next index congruent to h-1, then enter p_r. The exceptional path from u_M is u_(h+g),...,u_(h+2g-1),p_r and has length g+1. All these indices exist because M>=2g+h. Hence Qb^(g+1)=S. The a-path from u_1 covers U, and the b-cycle covers P, proving strong connectivity.

<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof--safety-of-every-word-of-length-at-most-m"></a>
##### Safety of every word of length at most M

Partition Q into singleton P-cells and g color cells, with color(u_j)=1+((j-h-1) mod g). Thus u_h and u_M have color g. Let C be the n-by-s state-to-cell incidence matrix. Let T_a fix P and cycle the colors 1,...,g, and let T_b cycle

```
p_0,g,1,...,g-1,p_r,p_(r-1),...,p_1.
```

Write D_l for the row-action transformation matrix of a letter l, f_q for a standard state column and e_c for a standard cell row. Directly from the transitions,

```
D_a C = C T_a,
D_b C = C T_b + f_(u_M) (e_g-e_1).
```

The last term is an outer product. S has one state in each cell. For any word w=l_1...l_t, its cell multiplicity row is therefore

```
chi_S D_w C = 1_s + sum_i mu_i (e_g-e_1) T_(l_(i+1)...l_t),
```

where the sum is over b-positions and mu_i is the nonnegative number of trajectories at u_M immediately before position i. This identity counts trajectories even after collisions.

A trajectory from S needs at least M-g letters to reach u_M: initial U-indices are at most g, transitions within U increase an index by at most one, and entrances from P have index h<=g. Hence mu_i>0 implies i>=M-g+1. In the cell graph, color g needs at least g-1 letters to reach color g-1, and color 1 needs at least g letters to reach A. Indeed, reaching g-1 from g requires the path through 1,...,g-1; a detour through P cannot shorten it. To reach A from 1 one must traverse the colors to g-1, take b to p_r, then b again into A.

For a prefix of length at most M-1, every nonzero correction has a suffix of length at most g-2. Thus its positive part cannot reach color g-1, whose trajectory count is at most one.

Suppose a word of length at most M has a first collision. If its colliding letter is b, the preceding prefix has two trajectories in b's only non-singleton fiber, whose states all have color g-1. This contradicts the preceding count bound. If the colliding letter is a, its two source states must be u_h and u_M, the only non-singleton a-fiber. They do not both belong to S. If the preceding prefix ends in b, this is impossible because u_M has no b-preimage. If it ends in a, their preimages must be u_(M-1) and u_(h-1). For h=1 there is no preimage of u_h; for h>=2 these are two distinct states of color g-1 one step earlier, again contradicting the count bound. Hence every word of length at most M preserves |S|.

For a word of length at most M, all correction suffixes have length at most g-1. No negative term can reach A, so each singleton A-cell has multiplicity at least one. Every such word is safe.

<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof--attainment-and-synchronization"></a>
##### Attainment and synchronization

The word a^(M-g)b^(g+1) has length M+1. After its a-run the moving states have indices M-g+1,...,M, all in the cyclic tail. Exactly one trajectory is at u_M before the first b; no later b has a trajectory there because b has no image u_M. In the cell identity the unique negative correction is e_1 T_b^g=e_(p_(r-1)), while its positive correction is e_g T_b^g=e_(p_r). Therefore the final image omits p_(r-1), including when r=1. This proves ac=M+1.

Let c=a^(M-h)b^s. On S, c fixes P and every u_j except u_h, which goes to p_0. To check this, the a-run fixes the cyclic tail u_(h+1),...,u_M. For j<h it sends u_j to u_(M-h+j); this point and u_j have identical remaining b-distance h-j to p_r and therefore the same b-cycle position after s steps. For j=h it sends u_h to u_M, which takes g+1 b-steps to p_r and r further steps to p_0, totaling s. Thus c is a unit sending u_h to its predecessor p_0 in the b-cycle on S. The word c(bc)^(s-2) resets S: after c the hole is u_h, and each bc extends the missing interval by one point in forward b-order until only p_0 remains. Prepending b^(g+1) resets Q. Every displayed word uses only a and b.

<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof--the-boundary-m2g"></a>
#### The boundary M=2g

Here a fixes P and cycles U. Define b by p_0 b=u_g, p_i b=p_(i-1), and

```
u_j b = p_r       if j is congruent to g-1 modulo g,
        u_(j+1)  if j<M and not in that case,
        u_M      if j=M.
```

Let B=P union {u_g,...,u_(2g-1)} and E=B union {u_(2g)}. Letter b cycles B in the order p_0,u_g,...,u_(2g-1),p_r,...,p_1 and fixes u_(2g). Every remaining state enters B within g+1 steps, so Qb^(g+1)=E. Define d=a^(g-1)b^s. On E it fixes P and acts by

```
u_g d = u_(2g-1),   u_(g+1) d = u_(2g),
u_(g+j) d = u_(g+j-1)  (2<=j<=g-1),
u_(2g) d = u_(2g-1).
```

Thus Ed=P union {u_(g+1),...,u_(2g)} and (Ed)a^g=S. In particular S=Qb^(g+1)d a^g is an actual reachable image. The a-cycle and the b-cycle establish strong connectivity.

Assign u_j color 1+((j-1) mod g). With the same cell permutations T_a,T_b as above, the identities are again D_a C=CT_a and D_b C=CT_b+f_(u_M)(e_g-e_1). The earliest arrival at u_M is M-g=g. The color-distance arguments above apply unchanged: the only b-kernel pair {u_(g-1),u_(2g-1)} is in color g-1, and a is a permutation. Consequently every word of length at most M is safe.

The word a^g b^(g+1) attains avoidance. Each of its b-positions has a trajectory at u_M, which b fixes. Of the negative corrections, only the first has a suffix of length g and reaches p_(r-1); later ones have shorter suffixes and cannot reach A. None of the positive corrections reaches A, since color g needs g+1 b-steps to do so. Thus p_(r-1) is missing and ac=M+1.

Finally d cycles the g states {u_(g+1),...,u_(2g)} and sends u_g into that cycle. Its g-th power e=d^g is therefore the unit u_g -> u_M on E, fixing all other points of E. Since b cycles B and fixes u_M, e(be)^(s-1) resets E to u_M: each application removes one further point of B. Prepending b^(g+1) resets Q. This proves every requirement also at the boundary.

<a id="problem4-cofinal-proof--independent-finite-checks"></a>
#### Independent finite checks

`check_cofinal.py` independently rebuilds the cycles and exceptional fibers, verifies the cell identities and distances, the complete actions of the unit words, reaching and reset words, strong connectivity, and exact ac by ordinary subset BFS. Its report covers 316 parameter choices, every residue h, and sizes through n=39. `check_boundary.py` checks 33 choices through n=30. These checks support the implementation; the uniform proofs are the preceding arguments.

<a id="problem4-defect-two-proof"></a>
<a id="problem4-defect-two-proof--sharpness-at-codimension-two-in-the-compression-range"></a>
### Sharpness at codimension two in the compression range

**Proposition.** For n>=7 and 1<=r<=n-6 there is a binary, strongly connected, synchronizing n-state automaton with a reachable (n-2)-element image S and an r-element A subset S such that ac(S,A)=6. This equals min(n-r,binom(n-|S|+2,2)).

Set L=n-3>=4. Use states T={x_0,...,x_(L-2),z} and three additional states w,v,u. Let b cycle T in the displayed order and cycle w,v,u. Let a fix T\{z} and w, interchange z and u, and send v to z. Its only non-singleton fiber is {u,v}. The a-edges between the two b-cycles prove strong connectivity.

Put S=T union {v} and choose any r-element subset A of {x_2,...,x_(L-2)}. This set has L-3=n-6 elements, including when L=4. Until compression, describe an image by its two holes. Starting with H_0={w,u}, the following is the complete transition table needed before depth six:

| Holes | Earliest depth | Under a | Under b |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| H_0={w,u} | 0 | H_1 | H_1 |
| H_1={w,v} | 1 | H_1 | H_2 |
| H_2={u,v} | 2 | H_3 | H_0 |
| H_3={z,v} | 3 | H_2 | H_4 |
| H_4={x_0,u} | 4 | H_5 | H_6 |
| H_5={x_0,v} | 5 | not needed | not needed |
| H_6={x_1,w} | 5 | compression | not needed |

Each displayed transition preserves image cardinality n-2. Induction on word length shows that every word of length at most five has one of these seven hole sets. None intersects A. Hence every word shorter than six is safe. The word ababb reaches H_6, where both u and v are present; its final a compresses. Therefore ac(S,A)=6.

Here are explicit original-letter words certifying reachability and synchronization. Let N=lcm(L,3), so b^N is the identity. The word e=a^2 is the unit v -> u, fixing all other states. The conjugate f=b^(N-1)e b is the unit u -> w. Thus k=ef collapses {w,v,u} to w and fixes T, and Qkb=T union {v}=S.

Let c=k a f a k. It sends each state in {w,v,u,z} to w and fixes T\{z}: the initial k sends the three extra states to w; z follows z -> u -> w -> w -> w through a,f,a,k. The word c(bc)^(L-1) resets Q to w. After the initial c, only states of the b-cycle T other than z remain besides w. Each bc sends the predecessor of z to z and then to w; the cyclic order ensures that all L states of T have disappeared after L-1 repetitions. Meanwhile w follows b to v and c back to w. This proves synchronization without adjoining any letter.

`defect_two.py` generates these words and transitions. `check_defect_two.py` independently verifies the transition table, complete actions of e,f,k,c, exact ac by ordinary subset BFS, strong connectivity, actual reachability and the full reset. The saved audit covers 300 parameter choices, all 7<=n<=30 and all admissible r. These are implementation checks; the proof above applies to every stated parameter.

<a id="problem4-defect-two-proof--codimension-one"></a>
#### Codimension one

For completeness the other compression face also has a direct construction. For n>=4 let b cycle u,v,z,x_0,...,x_(n-4), and let a interchange z,u, send v to z, and fix the other states. Put S=Q\{u}. For 1<=r<=n-3 choose A inside the n-3 states {x_0,...,x_(n-4)}. The successive possible holes through depth two are u, v and z: the initial hole u goes to v under either letter; from hole v, a preserves that hole and b takes it to z. Hence all words shorter than three are safe. The word bba compresses, because after bb the hole is z and both u,v are present. Thus ac=3.

Letter b alone proves strong connectivity. The word e=a^2 is the unit v -> u. Therefore e(be)^(n-2) resets Q by the same cyclic-interval argument as in [Sharpness for every n >= 2s-r-1](#problem4-cofinal-proof). Moreover Qa=Q\{v}, so Qab^(n-1)=Q\{u}=S. This proves binary sharpness 3 whenever n-r>=3. The existing first face covers r=n-2 with value 2. Together with the full-image boundary and the codimension-two proposition, every triple with n-s<=2 is determined.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof"></a>
<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--uniform-two-block-construction-proof-and-adversarial-case-audit"></a>
### Uniform two-block construction: proof and adversarial case audit

For p>=4, t>=2 and k>=0, construct disjoint sets
P={p_0,...,p_(p-1)}, X={x_1,...,x_t}, Y={y_1,...,y_t}, {z},
H={h_1,...,h_k}. Letter a swaps the last two P states, fixes the other
P states and H, and cycles x_1,...,x_t,y_1,...,y_t,z.
Letter b maps p_i to p_(i-1) for i>=1; subdivides the edge p_0 -> y_1
by the H chain; increases X and Y indices when below t; maps x_t,y_t
to p_(p-1); and fixes z. Set S=P union X union H and A={p_0} union H.
Then all structural requirements hold and

    ac(S,A)=min(p+2t,3t+2).

Here n=p+2t+1+k, s=p+t+k and r=k+1, hence n-r=p+2t and m=n-s=t+1.
Consequently for all m>=3 and q=n-r>=2m+2 the binary construction attains
min(q,3m-1). In particular F_bin=F=U=q on 2m+2<=q<=3m-1.
For larger q it is only a lower bound. Together with the separately proved
cofinal region, exactness holds throughout q<=3m-1, m>=3; the existing
codimension-three family extends that face to q=9. No unrestricted upper
bound 3m-1 or global equality with this family is claimed.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--compression-lower-bound-in-the-unpadded-base"></a>
#### Compression lower bound in the unpadded base

Initially k=0. Put L=3t+2 and rho_i=min(i,p-2). Give diagonal pairs
potential zero and the following symmetric potentials on distinct pairs:

| pair | D |
| --- | --- |
| P-P, P-X, X-X | L |
| x_i,y_j, j=i | t-i+1 |
| x_i,y_j, j>i | 2t-i+1 |
| x_i,y_j, j<i | L-j |
| x_i,z | 2t-i+1 |
| y_i,y_j, i<j | L-j |
| y_i,z | 2t+1 |
| p_i,y_j | min(L,max(L-j,2t+3+rho_i)) |
| p_i,z | min(L,2t+2+rho_i) |

For every pair E and original letter l, D(E)<=1+D(E l).
The following ledger checks every type, including all index boundaries.
Clipping at L cannot increase a positive difference. Swapping the last
two P indices preserves rho; under b, rho decreases by at most one.

* P-P: a preserves type; b either preserves type or gives P-Y with j=1,
  whose potential is at least L-1.
* P-X: a stays in type unless x_t crosses to y_1, again potential >=L-1.
  Under b, p_i with i>=1 stays P-X or becomes P-P. For i=0 and j<t,
  the image is {y_1,x_(j+1)} with potential L-1; for j=t it is
  {y_1,p_(p-1)} with potential >=L-1.
* X-X: a stays in type unless the larger index is t, when the target
  X-Y potential is L-1. Under b a crossing gives P-X, potential L.
* P-z: a gives P-X, potential L; b with i>=1 decreases rho by <=1,
  and i=0 gives Y-z, potential 2t+1, exactly one below 2t+2.
* P-Y, a: for j<t the L-j term decreases by one and rho is unchanged.
  For j=t the source is min(L,2t+3+rho_i) and the target is
  min(L,2t+2+rho_i), differing by at most one.
* P-Y, b: for i>=1,j<t both terms decrease by <=1; j=t gives P-P.
  For i=0,j<t the source is exactly L-j (since j<=t-1) and the
  target {y_1,y_(j+1)} has L-j-1. For i=0,j=t, the source 2t+3
  is <=L and the target P-Y at j=1 has potential >=L-1.
* X-Y, j=i: a or b increments both indices and decreases potential
  by one. The last a boundary gives Y-z with a larger potential; the
  last b boundary is the unique kernel pair, of potential one, merging.
* X-Y, j>i: incrementing both or crossing y_t to z under a gives
  2t-i, one below the source. Under b the y_t boundary gives P-X.
* X-Y, j<i: incrementing both gives L-j-1. The x_t boundary under
  a gives {y_1,y_(j+1)} with that same value; under b it gives P-Y
  with potential >=L-j-1.
* X-z: a with i<t gives X-X; i=t gives {x_1,y_1} of potential t,
  one below the source t+1. Under b, i<t decreases the value by one,
  and i=t gives P-z with a larger value.
* Y-Y: both indices increment unless the larger is t. Under a that
  boundary gives Y-z of potential 2t+1=L-t-1. Under b it gives
  P-Y at index <=t, with potential at least L-t.
* Y-z: a always gives potential 2t, exactly one less; b preserves
  type unless y_t enters P, when the target potential is >=2t+2.
* Diagonal pairs have zero and remain diagonal, trivially satisfying the inequality.

Every distinct pair in P union X has potential L. Telescoping along a
merging word gives |w|>=D(E), since its final potential is zero. Every
compressing word merges some initial pair, so compression needs >=L letters.
This proof uses symbolic inequalities for arbitrary p,t, not a finite grid.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--avoidance-lower-bound-in-the-unpadded-base"></a>
#### Avoidance lower bound in the unpadded base

Use singleton P-cells and t color cells, giving x_i and y_i color i,
and z color 1. Let C be the incidence matrix. T_a swaps the last two
P-cells and cycles the colors; T_b cycles
p_0,1,...,t,p_(p-1),...,p_1. With row-action matrices D_l and a state
column f_z and color rows e_i, both original letters satisfy

    D_l C = C T_l + f_z (e_1-e_2).

The final term is an outer product. Initially S=P union X contains one
state per cell. Iteration gives the exact trajectory multiplicity identity

    chi_S D_w C = 1 + sum_i mu_i (e_1-e_2) T_suffix,

where mu_i>=0 counts trajectories at z just before the ith letter.
The formula remains true after collisions.

No trajectory from S reaches z before t+1 steps. From X its increasing
U-index requires at least t+1 steps; any P entrance into y_1 costs at
least one step and then at least t further steps to reach z. Departing U
through b cannot shorten this. Thus mu_i>0 requires i>=t+2.

In the prescribed cell graph, color 2 needs t-1 letters to enter P at
p_(p-1), and p-1 more to reach p_0. The only P interchange is between
the adjacent last two points and cannot shorten the descending path.
Hence a negative correction reaches p_0 only with suffix length >=p+t-2,
requiring total length >=(t+2)+(p+t-2)=p+2t. Before that length the
p_0 coordinate is >=1, proving its presence. Positives need not be bounded.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--attaining-words"></a>
#### Attaining words

After a^(2t)b, the missing P state is p_(p-1). Applying a makes p_(p-2)
missing. This state is the unique b^(p-2)-preimage of p_0. Therefore
a^(2t)b a b^(p-2) omits p_0 and has length p+2t.

The U portion after a^(2t)b is {x_2,...,x_t,y_1,z}. After a^t it contains
x_t (from z) and y_t (from x_t, which exists in this set since t>=2).
The following b merges them. Thus a^(2t)b a^t b compresses at length L.
These two words prove ac=min(p+2t,L) together with both lower bounds.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--protected-subdivision-and-all-structural-requirements"></a>
#### Protected subdivision and all structural requirements

For every old T containing p_0, (T union H)a'=Ta union H and
(T union H)b'=Tb union H. Each proper prefix of a shortest old unsafe
word contains p_0. Induction through the first unsafe step transfers the
event, and all new states remain present. Thus the local value and the
corresponding attaining word are preserved with A={p_0} union H.

Let B=P union H union Y, s=|B|=p+t+k and E=B union {z}. Letter b cycles
B in the order p_0,H,y_1,...,y_t,p_(p-1),...,p_1. Qb^t=E. The a-cycle
connects every remaining state to B and vice versa, so the automaton is
strongly connected.

On E, d=a^(2t)b^s fixes P union H, cycles y_1 -> y_t -> ... -> y_1,
and sends z to y_t. Therefore e=d^t fixes B and sends z to y_1. This
gives Qb^t e=B and Ba^(t+1)=S, so b^t e a^(t+1) is a reaching word.

The word a^(2t+1) fixes U and H and interchanges the last two P states,
adjacent on the b-cycle. Along with b it generates Sym(B), with inverses
realized by positive powers. Further,
Ba=(B minus {y_1}) union {z}, Bab=(B minus {y_2}) union {z}, and
Babe=B minus {y_2}. For t>=2, y_1 remains in the latter intermediate B
image, so the retraction of z creates a collision. Permutations send any
pair in a current image into that kernel; repeat abe after suitable
permutations to synchronize B. Prepend b^t e to synchronize Q.
No auxiliary input letter or uncharged macro is introduced.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--equivalent-canonical-prefix-form-used-by-the-paper-and-release"></a>
#### Equivalent canonical prefix form used by the paper and release

Reverse the H chain and place it before the old P chain. This gives a single
P-chain of size p'=p+k, with A={p'_0,...,p'_(r-1)}, r=k+1. In this form
there is no separate H block: a swaps the last two P' points and cycles
X,Y,z; b sends p'_0 to y_1 and shifts the other P' points down.
The hypothesis is p'>=r+3, t>=2, and the result is

    n=p'+2t+1, s=p'+t, ac(S,A)=min(n-r,3t+2).

The pair-potential ledger applies directly with p' replacing p. In the cell
graph, color 2 first enters P' at p'_(p'-1) after t-1 letters, and needs
p'-r further letters to reach the nearest A point p'_(r-1). Thus its distance
to A is p'+t-r-1. Combined with the first-error position t+2, no protected
coordinate can be lost before n-r. The avoider is
a^(2t)b a b^(p'-r-1), of length n-r, whose missing point is p'_(r-1).
All powers are nonnegative; the hypothesis makes the last exponent >=2.
The same compression word, retraction, reaching word and adjacent
transposition establish the other claims. The release generator/checker use
this canonical prefix form and have no dependency on exploratory modules.

<a id="problem4-two-block-proof--finite-implementation-audit"></a>
#### Finite implementation audit

The finite symbolic-potential audit checked 618999 pairs and 1237998 letter
inequalities through t=40, including small p, p=t+1,t+2,t+3, and large p.
The separate ordinary subset-BFS probe checked 105 cases through t=8,
including k=0,1,2, both parities of t and the clipped range p=t+3.
These checks support the implementation. The universal theorem rests on
the preceding exhaustive symbolic case ledger, matrix delay and structural proof.

The release's canonical-prefix generator supplies 221 records through n=65.
The independent checker rebuilds transitions from named states and verifies
216 values by ordinary subset BFS. The five larger instances use complete
finite pair-potential and signed cell-delay certificates instead; it checks
every original-letter inequality and exact incidence identity and both graph
distances. All instances have checked actual reaching/attaining/reset words
and structural macro actions. Its totals are 68744 pair checks, 137488 letter
inequalities and eight deliberately corrupted records rejected. No generator
module is imported by the checker. The uniform proof does not depend on
whether these finitely many implementation checks passed.

<a id="problem4-signed-chain-rigidity"></a>
### 双链下界族对全部颜色次序与换轨选择的刚性

**受限构造族的全参数纸面定理。** 本节固定两块构造的局部循环字母和
P 链，完整处理另一字母的颜色重排、逐边换轨及入口选择；上界不要求
同步、强连通或 S 可达。它没有分类一般自动机，也没有增加已有下界。

为使下标计算透明，本节把原 X、Y 下标改为从零开始。取 t≥2、p≥2，
P={p₀,…,p_{p−1}}，X={x₀,…,x_{t−1}}，Y={y₀,…,y_{t−1}}，以及 z。
a 在 P 上交换末两点、固定其余点，并在活动部分循环

\[
 (x_0,\ldots,x_{t-1},y_0,\ldots,y_{t-1},z).
\]

令 S=P∪X，所以 m=t+1。选任意颜色排列 o₀,…,o_{t−1}。
b 将 p_i 送到 p_{i−1}（i≥1），将 p₀ 送到 x_{o₀} 或 y_{o₀}；
每条颜色边 o_j→o_{j+1} 可同时保持或同时交换 X、Y 两轨，
两个终端 x_{o_{t−1}},y_{o_{t−1}} 都送到 p_{p−1}，并固定 z。
这个明确的转移域共有 t!·2^t 个 b。

原型是自然颜色次序、全部边保持两轨、入口 p₀b=y₀。则

\[
 \boxed{\text{除原型外，全部转移表均有 }c(S)\le3t+1=3m-2.}       \tag{CR1}
\]

在原两块下界证明适用的 p≥4 域，原型 c(S)=3t+2，
所以它是此转移域中唯一达到最大值 3t+2 的参数型。
对 p=2,3，本节只给 (CR1) 的纸面上界，不扩大原下界定理的参数声明。

**无换轨重排的更强界。** 若入口仍进入 Y，全部边保持两轨，
但 o 不是自然排列，则

\[
 \boxed{c(S)\le2t=2m-2.}                                        \tag{CR2}
\]

令 k 是首个 o_k≠k 的位置，v=o_k>k，i=v−1，j=pos(i)>k。
Sa^k 的 Y 颜色为 0,…,k−1。施 b 后，活动 Y 颜色恰为
{0,…,k−1}∪{v}：入口补上第一颜色，原自然前缀的最后一条边进入 v。
因此 Sa^k b 同时含 x_i,y_{i+1}。而

\[
 \{x_i,y_{i+1}\}a^t=\{y_i,x_i\}.
\]

同色对沿两条 b 链再走 t−j 步即合并，所以实际字母词
a^k b a^t b^{t−j} 压缩，长度 2t+k+1−j≤2t，证明 (CR2)。

**带换轨的一般证明。** 对 0≤k≤t，Sa^k b 的全部 P 点仍被占用，
活动部分 B_k 不含 z，并从每个颜色对中恰取一点。把 y 位记为 1、
x 位记为 0。设入口颜色为 v₀、入口位为 β。入口位恒为 β，
其余颜色 v 的位为 1_{pred(v)<k} XOR ε_{pred(v)}，
ε 表示对应边是否换轨。

如果某个 B_k 的位串不是若干个 1 后接若干个 0，则有相邻位 01，
即含 x_i,y_{i+1}（0≤i≤t−2）。同色化后，换轨不影响两粒沿共同
颜色路径走向同一终点。因此

\[
 a^k b a^t b^{\,t-\operatorname{pos}(i)}
\]

压缩 S，长度 2t+k+1−pos(i)≤3t+1。

余下假定每个 B_k 均为前缀位串，且 B₀ 的 1 集为 {0,…,ℓ−1}。
B_t 除入口外的每一位恰与 B₀ 相反。仅由这两个端点也是前缀，
就只剩以下四种形状：

| 入口位 β | 入口颜色 v₀ | B₀ 的前缀长度 ℓ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | t |
| 0 | t−1 | 0 |
| 0 | t−1 | t−1 |

确实，β=1 时 B_t 的 1 集是 {ℓ,…,t−1}∪{v₀}；
若 ℓ<t，它包含末位，作为前缀必须是全集，迫使 ℓ=1、v₀=0；
若 ℓ=t，则单点入口只能是 0。β=0 时该集合是
{ℓ,…,t−1}\{v₀}；若 v₀≠t−1，它包含末位却缺中间入口，不可能
是前缀。剩下 v₀=t−1 时只能 ℓ=0 或 t−1。

第一形状没有换轨；(CR2) 的证明说明任何非自然排列都会产生一个
非前缀 B_k，因此它恰为原型。第二形状满足 Sb=P∪Y，入口为 y₀。
Sbab 含 z,y₀，而 {z,y₀}a^{t+1}={y₀,x₀}，故
b a b a^{t+1} b^t 压缩，长度 2t+4≤3t+1（t≥3）。
t=2 时只能取颜色次序 (0,1)，长度七的 b a b² a² b 压缩：
Sbab 含 z,y₀，再施 b 得 z,x₁，a² 得 x₁,y₁，最后 b 合并。

后两形状的入口均为 x_{t−1}。Sa^{t+1}b 含 z,x_{t−1}，
再施 a 得 x₀,y₀；所以 a^{t+1} b a b^{t−pos(0)}
压缩，长度至多 2t+3≤3t+1。所有参数至此全部处理，证明 (CR1)。

若沿 p₀ 的入口边作已有的
[保护细分](#problem4-two-block-proof--protected-subdivision-and-all-structural-requirements)，
令细分点集为 H，明确取 p₀∈A₀⊊S（例如 A₀={p₀}），
S′=S∪H、A′=A₀∪H。对每个含 p₀ 的 T，两个实际字母均满足
(T∪H)a′=Ta∪H、(T∪H)b′=Tb∪H；满占用的细分链恰好替代原入口边。
旧安全前缀因 p₀∈A₀ 始终含 p₀，故这些等式可归纳到首次失败步，
得到 ac(S′,A′)=ac(S,A₀)≤c(S)。因此 (CR1)–(CR2) 也给对应加垫族
的 ac 上界；这里不声称加垫后纯压缩长度仍等于未加垫值。

**独立控制。** check_chain_rigidity.py 对 t=2,…,5、
p∈{2,3,6,11} 的整个转移域共 17120 表，逐个直接作用证明给出的词，
并用独立点对 BFS 核对最短压缩距离。全部 17104 个非原型通过；
16 个原型作必须保留的正控制。各端点分支及 t=2 特例均被覆盖。
有限核对检查下标与边界，(CR1)–(CR2) 由上述任意参数证明给出。
另外，对 t=2,3 的全部转移表、相同四个 p、A₀={p₀} 或 {p₀,p₁}，
分别加一个或两个保护细分点；普通子集 BFS 的 896 次比较全部满足
加垫前后 ac 相等。这里核对的是带保护的首次成功时间，不以压缩距离
相等代替它。

<a id="problem4-arbitrary-core-cycle-rigidity"></a>
### 任意活动圈次序与任意保护部分置换的统一刚性

**纸面定理；任意 t≥2、p≥2，不要求同步或可达。** 本节与前一节改变的
自由度不同：现在固定链字母 b，让循环字母在 P 上为任意置换，在活动
部分为任意一个 (2t+1)-圈。使用 P={p₀,…,p_(p−1)}、
X={x₀,…,x_(t−1)}、Y={y₀,…,y_(t−1)}、z，S=P∪X。固定

\[
 p_0b=y_0,\quad p_ib=p_{i-1}\ (i\ge1),\quad
 x_ib=x_{i+1},\ y_ib=y_{i+1}\ (i<t-1),\quad
 x_{t-1}b=y_{t-1}b=p_{p-1},\quad zb=z.
\]

设 a 保持 P 与 U=X∪Y∪{z}，a|P 任意，a|U=σ 是单圈。记原型圈
α=(x₀,…,x_(t−1),y₀,…,y_(t−1),z)。则

\[
 \boxed{c(S)\le3t+2;\qquad
 \sigma\ne\alpha\Longrightarrow c(S)\le3t+1.}                 \tag{ACR1}
\]

因此当 p≥4 时，这整个包含 p!·(2t)! 个转移表的参数族的纯压缩极值
恰为 3t+2=3m−1；原型圈与原先的 P 末端换位给出匹配下界。
一般 P 置换即使保留原型圈也未必达到等号。b 的颜色次序也可同时任意
改变：若两条链共同采用排列 o₀,…,o_(t−1)，入口为 y_(o₀)，用同一个
颜色重命名把它化回上述定义即可；S=P∪X 不变。因此唯一可能达界的
活动圈相应变为 (x_(o₀),…,x_(o_(t−1)),y_(o₀),…,y_(o_(t−1)),z)。
这同时允许两个字母中的这些自由度，但不包含逐边换轨，亦不覆盖
σ 含多个圈的情形。

**第一步：一个短对轨道迫使共同奇圈。** 反设 c(S)≥3t+2，写 N=2t+1。
任意颜色对 E_i={x_i,y_i} 经 b^(t−i) 合并。因此对每个 0≤j<N，
Xσ^j 不含任何 E_i；否则 a^j b^(t−i) 长至多 3t，已经压缩 S。

用 σ 把 U 标为 Z_N。设 E_(t−1) 两端的差为 δ，g=gcd(N,δ)。该边的
全部旋转组成 g 个长度 N/g 的不交奇圈，独立数为 (N−g)/2。
X 的大小为 t=(N−1)/2，故 g=1；旋转图 H 是一个 N 圈，X 是其最大独立集。
圈上最大独立集的间隔为一个三、其余全为二，所以存在 v 使

\[
 X=\{v+2j\delta:0\le j<t\},\qquad
 (X-X)\setminus\{0\}=\mathbb Z_N\setminus\{0,\delta,-\delta\}.
\]

后一等式也可直接数出 2jδ（−t+1≤j≤t−1）：这 N−2 个不同剩余类
恰漏掉 ±δ。因此任何旋转轨道都避开 X 的点对，其差只能为 ±δ。
全部 E_i 均为 H 边，得到固定匹配 M={E₀,…,E_(t−1)}⊆H。

**第二步：链前缀唯一确定奇圈。** 对 0≤k≤t，直接作用 b 得

\[
 Sb^k=P\cup X_k,\qquad
 X_k=\{y_0,\ldots,y_{k-1},x_k,\ldots,x_{t-1}\}.
\]

所有 b^k a^j b（0≤j<N）长至多 3t+1，所以 X_k 的全部旋转都不含
E_(t−1)。每个 X_k 因而是 H 的最大独立集。特别 X、Y 均独立。
若 H 含 x_i y_j 且 j<i，则 X_(j+1) 同时含这两点，矛盾。

H 中每个点的度为二，且已含全部匹配边。删去 M 后，每个 X、Y 点
还需要一个邻点，z 需要两个邻点。x_(t−1) 不能连任何别的 Y 点，
y₀ 不能连任何别的 X 点，故它们都连 z。其余边须将
{x₀,…,x_(t−2)} 与 {y₁,…,y_(t−1)} 完美匹配，并满足 j>i。
从 x_(t−2) 反向归纳，这个匹配唯一，只能是 x_i y_(i+1)。故

\[
 E(H)=M\cup\{x_i y_{i+1}:0\le i<t-1\}
       \cup\{x_{t-1}z,zy_0\}.                                  \tag{ACR2}
\]

α 是这个奇圈的一个 N 阶自同构。σ 也保持 H 且阶为 N；圈的自同构
只有旋转和反射，N≥5 时反射阶为二，故 σ=α^k，其中 gcd(k,N)=1。
这将任意圈次序归约为原型圈的互素幂，不是对有限扫描结果作外推。

**第三步：全部非原型幂的显式短词。** 令 r∈{1,…,N−1} 满足 kr≡1 (mod N)，
置 A=tr mod N、B=N−r，所以 1≤A≤N−1。以下两个词都压缩 S：

\[
 w_1=a^B b a^A b,\qquad w_2=a^{N-A} b a^B b.                    \tag{ACR3}
\]

这里是实际 a 的幂，不把 α 作为原字母。活动部分上 a^B=α^(2t)、
a^A=α^t、a^(N−A)=α^(t+1)。对于 w₁，Sa^B b 的活动部分含
{x₁,…,x_(t−1),y₀,z}；再施 α^t 后同时含 x_(t−1)、y_(t−1)，最后 b 合并。
对于 w₂，Sa^(N−A)b 同时含 z、y₀；施 α^(2t) 后恰为
{y_(t−1),x_(t−1)}，最后 b 合并。这些包含关系不依赖 a|P。

由于 min(A,N−A)≤t，两词较短者满足

\[
 \min(|w_1|,|w_2|)=B+\min(A,N-A)+2\le3t+3-r.                  \tag{ACR4}
\]

r≥2 时右侧至多 3t+1，与假设矛盾。因此慢候选只能有 r=k=1，即 σ=α。
此时 w₁=a^(2t)b a^t b 长 3t+2，直接给出原型上界。若压缩距离原本
小于 3t+2，已满足非原型结论；以上论证也排除了无限压缩距离。
结合已有原型纸面下界，完成 (ACR1) 的全参数证明与该受限族的匹配极值。

**有限计算范围。** `two_block_cycle_orders.cpp` 固定循环中第一个点为 x₀，
遍历其余点的全部排列，每个 N 圈恰出现一次；可另遍历 P 的全部置换。
按循环前两个后继划分互不重叠的线程任务。反向点对 BFS 算出固定 S 的
最短压缩距离；长度低于目标即可提前拒绝，高目标者才检查全部点对同步性。
没有将这些表视为全部自动机，更不从未找到见证推出一般上界。

首轮完整扫描 (p,t)=(7,4) 的全部 203212800 个表，没有达到十五的 S；
固定 P 原末端换位、(p,t)=(8,5) 的全部 3628800 个活动圈，没有达到十八的 S。
两域最大有限压缩值分别为十四、十七，原型提供真实强连通同步可达锐例。
随后按上述证明逐表直接核对显式压缩词：同一 203212800 表完整通过，
耗时 7.121 秒；(p,t)=(8,5) 的 3628800 圈完整通过，耗时 0.259 秒。
(4,3) 的全部 17280 表也通过。四个证明分支（早期颜色对碰撞、链前缀
碰撞、原型、非原型幂）的活动圈计数分别为
(12,8,1,3)、(648,66,1,5)、(39960,354,1,5)、(3625200,3590,1,9)，
对应 t=2,3,4,5；这些是圈数，不是乘过 P 置换数的表数。

小域控制 (p,t)=(4,2) 完整核对 576 表：普通子集 BFS 独立比较最短压缩，
并从 Q 遍历到单点独立检查同步性，24 个八步正例保留。扩大到 U 上全部
置换的 2880 表时，控制同样通过，仍保留 24 个正例，并出现 264 个没有
有限压缩或达到阈值但不同步的输入。后者不被用作同步自动机下界。

**多圈情形只有有限结果。** 放开 σ 的单圈条件，使用 U 上全部 9! 个
置换，并同时遍历 P 上全部 7! 个置换；(p,t)=(7,4) 的 **1828915200 个表**
完整结束，耗时 49.243 秒。没有强连通同步的十五步候选；其中 2232720 个
长距离或不压缩输入不满足同步性。最大有限初始压缩值为十四。
这是固定链字母 b、固定 S 的完整受限扫描，未证明任意 t 的多圈上界，
也没有改进原 Problem 4 的 [14,15] 区间。单圈定理的奇圈轨道证明不能
直接用于多圈，因为点对轨道可能跨越两个长度不同的循环。

固定 P 为原末端换位的更大多圈域也完整结束：

| p,t | 状态数、余维 | 完整 U 置换数 | 压缩目标 | 强连通同步目标候选 | 最大有限初始压缩 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,5 | n=19,m=6 | 39916800 | 18 | 0 | 17 |
| 9,6 | n=22,m=7 | 6227020800 | 21 | 0 | 20 |

两次运行分别耗时 1.568、222.228 秒；未压缩或达到阈值但不同步的表数
分别为 4283、50363。线程按固定的前两个输出划分剩余排列，所有表数
均与阶乘计数相等。这里没有遍历 P 的其余置换，也没有放开 b 的链形或
初始 S；负结果不改变 m=6、7 的一般参数极值边界。

<a id="problem4-full-cycle-exact"></a>
### 含全状态循环原字母的自动机：二字母与任意字母表的全部参数精确极值

**纸面定理；完整覆盖这个受限自动机类，包括非互素和非稠密参数。**
令 n≥2、1≤r<s≤n、m=n−s。记 F_cyc(n,s,r) 为原有限字母表含一个全状态 n 圈的
强连通同步自动机中，S 为可达 s-集、A⊂S、|A|=r 时的最大 ac。
再记 F_cyc,bin 为其中二字母自动机的极值。则

\[
 \boxed{F_{\mathrm{cyc,bin}}(n,s,r)=F_{\mathrm{cyc}}(n,s,r)
       =\min\{s-r+1,\ 2m+1\}.}                                 \tag{CY1}
\]

上界对任意 S 成立，不要求可达。下界在全部参数均由两个原字母达到，
不再要求 gcd(n,m)=1。下面先保留稠密区间的三字母构造作为证明基础，
再将两个非循环字母合并，并补齐 n≤2m 与 m=0。没有对这个循环类结论作独立
文献优先权声明，且它不确定一般自动机的 F(n,s,r)。

**避免上界（m≥1）。** 设 a 为全状态循环字母，H=Q\S，|H|=m，
q=n−r。U_j=∪_{i=0}^j Ha^i 在未等于 Q 时每步至少增加一个点：
若 U_{j+1}=U_j，则 U_j a⊆U_j，置换性迫使 U_j 对整个 n 圈不变，
与非空真子集矛盾。因此 |U_j|≥min(n,m+j)。
若全部 a⁰,…,a^j 的像均包含 A，则 U_j⊆Q\A。
取 j=q−m+1=s−r+1，右侧只能容纳 q 点而左侧至少 q+1 点，
故存在长度至多 s−r+1 的避开词。

**点对旋转引理。** 若 a 为 Q 上的 n 圈、|Q\S|=m、n>2m，
则对每个二元集 E⊆Q，存在 0≤i≤2m 使 Ea^{−i}⊆S；若 E 为
偶数圈的对跖点对，还可取 0≤i≤m。

证明：给状态以模 n 的坐标。非对跖点对的无向旋转轨道恰有 n 条
不同边，每个点至多关联两条轨道边（轨道图不必连通）。每个洞至多
覆盖两条，m 个洞不可能覆盖前 2m+1 条不同边；这些边确实存在，
因为 n≥2m+1。未被洞覆盖的边全在 S 中。对跖点对的轨道则是
n/2 条边的匹配，每个洞至多覆盖一条；n/2>m 保证前 m+1 条中
有未覆盖边。两种情况分别给出所述下标，证毕。

**压缩上界。** 同步性保证某个原字母 b 奇异（若所有原字母均为置换，
任何词仍为置换），取其核对 E。对旋转引理给出的 i，Ea^{−i}⊆S
使实际原词 a^i b 压缩，得到 c(S)≤2m+1；对跖情形甚至≤m+1。
这与避免上界合得 (CY1) 的上半部分。
a、b 在这里均为原字母；若用长度 d、h 的词来实现，同一压缩论证
只给 2md+h，不能把宏字母当作一步。

**稠密区间的基础达界构造（m≥1、n>2m）。** 取 Q={0,…,n−1}，

\[
 a:i\mapsto i+1\pmod n,\qquad
 b:m-1\mapsto2m-1\quad\text{且固定其余状态},\qquad
 c=(n-2,\ n-1).
\]

令 q=n−r，S={m,…,n−1}，A={q,…,n−1}，并记
L=min(q−m+1,2m+1)。初始洞为 {0,…,m−1}。

证明每个长度小于 L 的词都安全。考虑首次成功前的前缀，洞数为 m。
只要没有循环回绕，每次 a 把所有洞加一；安全的 b 要么不改变洞集，
要么把洞 2m−1 换回 m−1。后一操作保持洞的模 m 同余类。
归纳得到：洞模 m 各恰有一个，且最大洞坐标至多 m−1+#a。
对长度小于 L 的前缀，

\[
 m-1+\#a\le m+L-2\le q-1\le n-2,
\]

所以确实没有回绕，也没有洞进入 A。若下一步为 c 且总长度仍小于 L，
它之前的洞至多 m+L−3≤q−2≤n−3，故两个换位点均被占用，
c 根本不改变该集合。

若总长度小于 L 的词末字母 b 首次压缩，则此前 m−1 与 2m−1
都被占用。模 m 的 m−1 类的唯一洞只能位于至少 3m−1，
但此前 #a≤L−2≤2m−1，所有洞至多 3m−2，矛盾。
a、c 是置换不压缩，因此全部短词确实安全。

当 L=q−m+1 时，a^{q−m+1} 使洞 m−1 到达 q，避开 A 中的 q。
当 L=2m+1 时，q≥3m，故 n≥3m+1；a^{2m} 后洞为
{2m,…,3m−1}，接 b 合并 m−1 与 2m−1，达到长度 L。
两分支均由真实原字母词达到。

**强连通、同步与可达。** a 保证强连通。a,c 生成全部相邻换位，
从而生成 Sym(Q)；逆循环由正幂实现。因此置换共轭 b 可实现任意
单点转移 i→j（i≠j），其余状态固定，依次应用这些实际词即可重置。
这里仅用这些长词证明结构，不将其长度计入前面的短词上界。

更直接地，令 r_i=(m−1−i) mod n。实际词

\[
 e_i=a^{r_i}ba^{n-r_i}
\]

仅把 i 送到 i+m mod n，固定其余状态。
从 Q 依次施 e₀,e₁,…,e_{m−1}，每次删除指定洞 i，其目标
i+m∈{m,…,2m−1} 始终保留，最后恰得到 S。这不要求 gcd(n,m)=1。
若 gcd(n,m)=1，0,m,2m,… 模 n 遍历全体状态；
依次施 e₀,e_m,…,e_{(n−2)m} 即沿此圈合并全部状态，因此可删除 c，
得到二字母锐例。m=1、n=3 也包含在 (CY1)，此时唯一 r=1 的值为二。
一般 n<3m+1 时只断言上述 ac 精确式，不外推 c(S)=2m+1。

对这个明确的二字母构造，同步条件也恰为 gcd(n,m)=1。若 d=gcd(n,m)>1，
a 在模 d 的剩余类上同时加一，b 保持每个剩余类；两个初始剩余类不同
的状态在任何实际词后仍不同类，因而不能合并。这只是原二字母表
{a,b} 的障碍；下面的二字母表 {a,bc} 对非互素参数同样同步。

**把合并与换位合成一个原字母。** 仍取上述 a、b、c，定义实际转移
d=bc，即先 b 后 c，但在新自动机中 d 是一个原字母。由于 c 固定
u=m−1，b 只把 u 送到 v=2m−1，且 c(v)≠u，逐点得到

\[
 d^2=b.                                                        \tag{CY2}
\]

对 x≠u，两次 c 把它送回 x，途中不经过 u；对 u，两步像为
u→c(v)→v。这也覆盖 v=n−2 的边界 n=2m+1。

新字母不会缩短目标 L=min(s−r+1,2m+1)。沿前述洞归纳，在长度小于 L
的词中，若下一原字母是 d，应用其 b 部分前已有 #a≤L−2。
如果 b 压缩，前面的模 m 论证已经给出矛盾；否则 b 后全部洞仍不超过
m−1+#a≤m+L−3≤q−2≤n−3。因此随后 c 交换的 n−2、n−1 均被占用，
对集合没有任何作用。由归纳每个短词都安全；不能把 d 当成两个收费
字母来使用原下界，以上检查直接按新的一字母成本证明安全性。
a^{s−r+1} 仍给避免分支的最短词；在压缩分支，a^{2m}d 合并原 b 核对，
后接置换 c 不会恢复基数。因此 ac=L。

S 的到达词也保留：把此前每个 e_i 中的 b 替换为 dd，(CY2) 保证
实际转移完全相同；依次使用 i=0,…,m−1 得到 Q→S。a 仍保证强连通。

**非互素情况下的同步证明。** 令 g=gcd(n,m)。由 (CY2) 和循环共轭，
新字母表能实现每个单点转移 e_i:i→i+m (mod n)，其余点固定。
这些转移在各模 g 剩余类内形成一个有向圈。沿该圈顺序合并，能把
每个剩余类送到其中任意指定代表，且不改变其他类；所以可实现任意
“每类任选一个代表”的回缩。当 g=1 时已经同步。

设 g>1，则 n≠2m+1，故 n≥2m+2，b 的源和目标均不属于
{x=n−2,y=n−1}，且每个剩余类至少有三个状态。取尚在不同剩余类的
任意两点。先施 a 的适当正幂，使第一点的剩余类为 g−2；循环作用
保持两个剩余类的模 g 差。再用上述类内回缩把第一点送到 x，把第二点
送到其剩余类内某个 z≠y。两点的类不同，所以 z≠x；这样的 z 总存在。
应用 d 时，第一点 x→y，使其剩余类加一。第二点不受 c 的换位影响；
即便 z 是 b 的源，b 的像仍同余且不是 x、y。因此第二点的剩余类不变。

若原模 g 差为 δ∈{1,…,g−1}，这一步将差减为 δ−1。重复至多 g−1 次
便使两点处于同一剩余类，再用类内回缩合并。于是任意点对都有实际
合并词；反复合并当前全像中的点对，得到原字母表上的重置词。
这里的长共轭和回缩只证明同步及可达，不作为短词上界中的一步收费。

**非稠密区间及全状态初始集。** 若 m≥1、n≤2m，则 s≤m，(CY1) 右端
等于 s−r+1，单独使用循环避免上界已经足够。取经典的两个转移
a:i→i+1 (mod n)、b:n−1→0（其余点固定），令
S={0,…,s−1}、A={s−r,…,s−1}。在长度≤s−r 的词中，实际集合始终
只是 S 的循环正移；因为最大坐标至多 2s−r−1≤n−2，没有回绕，也未
到达 b 的唯一非固定输入。故 b 一直不改变像，A 仍全部包含且没有压缩。
a^{s−r+1} 避开 A 的最小点，得到精确值 s−r+1。

a 的正幂共轭 b 给出每个单点转移 i→i+1。依次删除 s,s+1,…,n−1，
最后一个点进入仍在 S 中的 0，给出实际到达词 Q→S；沿全圈合并给出
同步词。m=0 时 S=Q，同步性保证存在一个奇异原字母，一步即压缩，
同一个二字母例达到值一。至此 (CY1) 覆盖所有合法 n,s,r。

m≥3 时 2m+1<3m−1，所以具有原全状态循环字母的自动机不能达到
一般问题在大 q 区域已有的两块下界。这给出全部余维的结构性排除，
同时保留了三字母与二字母达界条件的区别。

**独立控制。** check_full_cycle_extrema.py 检查 m=1,…,5、
2m+1≤n≤min(4m+2,24) 的全部合法 r：300 个三字母参数和
204 个互素二字母参数的普通子集 BFS 均与 (CY1) 相等。
40 个三字母、28 个二字母自动机的共轭、S 可达、点对距离与实际重置词
均独立核对；另有 12 个非互素二字母不同步的负控制。
三字母与二字母的 BFS 分别访问 2512、1735 个安全子集，两类各含 30 个 n=3m+1
边界参数。三字母的避免、相等、压缩分支分别为 220、25、55 例，
二字母分别为 150、18、36 例；这些检查不替代 (CY1) 的纸面证明。
另完整检查固定循环字母的三、四状态二字母域：221 个同步自动机的
全部 |S|≥2 与全部非空真保护子集，共 10252 例均满足上界（不要求 S 可达）。
对 n=4,6,8 的单一对跖核对，全部稠密集合共 117 例另满足 c(S)≤m+1；
这是上界证明中短旋转轨道的独立边界控制。

新的二字母构造另在 2≤n≤36 上独立核对：稠密区间取 1≤m≤8 的全部
可用参数，非稠密区间与 m=0 则取该 n 范围内全部参数。共 540 个自动机、
6195 组 (n,m,r)，其中稠密 3780 组、非稠密 1785 组、m=0 的 630 组。
全部用实际二字母转移表做普通子集 BFS，访问 65852 个安全子集，精确
ac 均等于 (CY1)；全部初始 S 的实际到达词及同步性通过直接作用和
独立反向点对 BFS 核对。216 个稠密自动机中有 74 个非互素例。
再对其中 n≤18 的全部非互素实例逐点对构造上述模类路由词，2080 个
实际合并词全部通过直接作用；没有用三字母同步性代替新二字母同步性。
这些次数是明确有限控制范围，一般参数的等式来自上面的纸面证明。

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--sharp-avoid-or-compress-examples-for-every-fixed-cardinality-gap"></a>
### Sharp avoid-or-compress examples for every fixed cardinality gap

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for every r>=1, g>=2, k>=2.
Priority **OPEN**; no **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim; general Cerny **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--the-result-and-the-remaining-scope"></a>
#### The result and the remaining scope

Put M=kg+1, n=r+M+1, s=r+g+1. There is a BINARY strongly connected
synchronizing n-state DFA and an ACTUAL image S with |S|=s, together
with A properly contained in S, |A|=r, such that

    ac(S,A)=n-|A|=M+1=kg+2.

Consequently for EVERY fixed pair of cardinalities 1<=|A|<|S| with
|S|-|A|>=3, the known n-|A| bound is sharp at INFINITELY MANY state
counts n. The first two faces are covered separately in
[[Sharp avoid-or-compress bounds on the first two cardinality faces](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces)](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces). The g2
specialization is exactly [[Sharp avoid-or-compress bounds on an infinite part of the third face](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face)](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face).
This is stronger than adding isolated states to a pair: every example
is binary, SC and synchronizing, and S is an actual original-word image.

The upper bound is Szykula's KNOWN avoid-or-compress lemma, attributed in
[the 2026 survey, Lemma3/Open Problem4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245).
It is NOT claimed as new. This resolves sharpness for every fixed
cardinality pair along the stated infinite arithmetic progressions;
it does NOT give the exact maximum for every triple (n,|S|,|A|).
The remaining state-count ranges and general Cerny are OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--construction-and-actual-reachability"></a>
#### Construction and actual reachability

Take P={p_0,...,p_r}, U={u_1,...,u_M},

    A=P\{p_r},                S=P union {u_1,...,u_g}.

Letter a fixes P and cycles U. Letter b is

    p_0 b=u_1; p_i b=p_(i-1) for 1<=i<=r;
    u_j b=p_r                 if g divides j;
    u_j b=u_(j+1)             if g does not divide j and j<M;
    u_M b=u_(g+1).

On S, b is the cycle p_0,u_1,...,u_g,p_r,p_(r-1),...,p_1.
Every outside state reaches this cycle within g+1 b's: each ordinary
block advances to its multiple of g and then p_r; u_M takes the path
u_(g+1),...,u_(2g),p_r. M>=2g+1 guarantees this last path is valid.
Therefore Q b^(g+1)=S. The two cycles and p_r routes prove SC.
Only the states u_g,u_(2g),...,u_(kg) collide under b. Every other
fiber has size one. Letter a is a permutation.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--linear-propagation-proves-all-short-words-safe"></a>
#### Linear propagation proves ALL short words safe

Partition the state coordinates into the r+1 SINGLE protected states P
and g color cells: u_j has color j mod g, with color g representing0.
Let C be the n-by-s cell-incidence matrix. On the s cell coordinates,
define permutations T_a,T_b by

* T_a fixes P and cycles colors1,...,g.
* T_b cycles p_0,1,...,g,p_r,...,p_1.

These cells are NOT a congruence. For BOTH original letters, the only
departure from the indicated cell action occurs at u_M, of color1:
its actual image has color1, whereas the permutation prescribes color2.
In row-matrix notation the exact identity is

    M_l C=C T_l+e_(u_M)^T (e_1-e_2),     l in {a,b}.        (1)

Here e_(u_M)^T is a column and e_1-e_2 is a row on the CELL coordinates.
Initially chi_S C is the all-ones row on those coordinates. Both T's
preserve that row. For ANY original word w=l_1...l_t, iterating (1) gives

    chi_S M_w C=1_s+sum_i mu_i (e_1-e_2) T_(l_(i+1)...l_t), (2)
    mu_i=(chi_S M_(l_1...l_(i-1)))_(u_M)>=0.

The vectors chi_S M_w count initial-S trajectories with MULTIPLICITY;
(2) remains valid even after a collision. Their positive coordinates
are exactly the ordinary image S w.

The argument is a GENERAL delay principle. Suppose a cell projection
has an initial transversal S, its prescribed letter maps are permutations,
and each actual error is a nonnegative source column times e_p-e_q.
Suppose an error source cannot be reached from S before h letters,
every colliding original-letter fiber lies wholly inside one designated
cell in B, and all A-points are singleton cells. If permutation-cell
distance p->B is d_plus and q->A is d_minus, the same expansion proves

    ac(S,A)>=h+1+min(d_plus+1,d_minus).                     (3)

Indeed no positive error can reach a collision cell before h+1+d_plus
steps, so a first collision needs one more letter. No negative error
can reach A before h+1+d_minus steps. This is a conditional paper
theorem about the stated exact matrix identities and fibers, not an
assertion that an arbitrary DFA admits such a projection. In the present
family h=M-g, d_plus=g-1 and d_minus=g, yielding M+1. The finite checker
verifies those hypotheses directly rather than treating cells as a
genuine quotient or selecting one successful trajectory.

Starting in S, reaching u_M costs at least M-g letters: the initial
maximum U-index is g, and each letter increases an index by at most
one; all jumps from P or wraps go to smaller indices. Thus mu_i can
be nonzero only at positions i>=M-g+1.

In the CELL permutation graph, color1 cannot reach color g in fewer
than g-1 letters, and color2 cannot reach ANY state of A in fewer
than g letters. Before entering P one must traverse the intermediate
colors, and then take b from color g to p_r and b again into A.

For a prefix of length <=M-1, no POSITIVE correction in (2) has yet
reached color g. Therefore its total trajectory count in that cell is
at most1. All colliding b-sources belong to this cell. A first collision
at a word position <=M is therefore impossible; a has no collisions.
This proves |S w|=s for EVERY |w|<=M.

For a prefix of length <=M, no NEGATIVE correction in (2) has yet
reached any A-coordinate. Each such coordinate still has count>=1.
Thus A is contained in S w for EVERY |w|<=M. Taken together these
two conclusions give ac(S,A)>=M+1, without selecting a preferred word,
ignoring other original letters, or assuming images preserve the cells.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--the-attaining-original-word-and-synchronization"></a>
#### The attaining original word and synchronization

The word a^(M-1)b^2 has length M+1 and final image

    {p_0,...,p_(r-2)} union {p_r,u_1,...,u_g,u_(g+2)}.

It misses p_(r-1) from A and STILL has cardinality s. Hence ac=M+1
exactly, with avoidance and no rank drop for this attaining word.

Synchronization is certified independently of that lower bound.
Let c=a^(M-1)b^s. On S it fixes P and sends

    u_1 c=p_0;       u_j c=u_(j-1) for 2<=j<=g.

The exceptional u_M branch takes g+1 b's to p_r, then s-(g+1) b's
to p_0. Ordinary u_(j-1) are on the s-cycle, so b^s fixes them.
Thus c^g maps all u_1,...,u_g to p_0 and fixes P.
The ACTUAL word v=c^g b has unique fixed root u_1 on S, and maximum
rooted height r+1: p_r walks down P and then into u_1; all moving
core points go directly to u_1. Therefore

    b^(g+1) v^(r+1)

resets Q. Its fully charged ORIGINAL length is

    g+1+(r+1)[g(n+g-1)+1].

This word may exceed the Cerny square, and is NOT alleged shortest or
a new square proof. It establishes synchronizability for all parameters.
The matrices in (1) are bookkeeping, not free word generators.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--post-proof-continuation-toward-a-compatible-cost-bound"></a>
#### Post-proof continuation toward a compatible cost bound

Two shorter ORIGINAL core macros are available:

    tau=a b^(g+1),              h=a^(M-g)b^(g+1).

Both return S into S. On the core, tau is a PERMUTATION: it is the
g-cycle R on u_1,...,u_g (fixing P), followed by b^(g+1). To check the
last moving point, u_g a=u_(g+1) takes g b's to p_r and one more to
p_(r-1), exactly the image u_1 b^(g+1) prescribed by R.

The second macro has corank ONE on S and satisfies

    h=e tau,       e: u_g->p_0, all other core states fixed.

For j<g, u_(M-g+j) takes g-j b's to p_r and then j+1 further b's,
giving the same target as u_j tau. The exceptional u_M takes all g+1
b's to p_r=p_0 tau. Thus the only changed
core source is u_g, and the kernel is {p_0,u_g}.
The charged lengths are |tau|=g+2 and |h|=M+1=n-|A|.

This is a paper algebra continuation, NOT an additional registered
computational claim. A read-only 192-parameter calculation agreed with
these identities, but that exploratory control is not in the independent
seal and is not used as proof. The preceding paper calculation is complete.

These macros expose a local unit paired with a short permutation, but
the unit e itself is h tau^(-1). In the ORIGINAL alphabet that inverse
needs an actual positive word, with its length counted. Treating it as
free would repeat an already failed cost shortcut. No bound here shows
that a sequence of these operations stays within (n-1)^2. The all-gaps
theorem remains a sharp LOCAL obstruction and an exact signed-error
delay result, with the global reset-cost coupling OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps--independent-verification-and-implications"></a>
#### Independent verification and implications

The independent checker constructs the core cycle first, verifies EVERY
state/letter instance of (1), and computes the two cell distances by
ordinary graph BFS. It runs ordinary set BFS for exact ac, checks actual
reachability and SC, evaluates complete ORIGINAL c/v rows, verifies the
root graph and the whole-Q reset, and literally checks retained words.
Small scopes also have independent full-image rt BFS. No negative random
search is used to prove the general claim. The g2 family was already
sealed at checkpoint110; the new finite scopes focus on g>=3.

The new scope has48 parameters, g3..11, throughn1025,542068 safe BFS
vertices,732192 subset/letter edges,12234 exact cell-identity controls,
26538765 ORIGINAL macro state/letter controls,5694 rooted states and
20894 literal reset letters. Five n<=12 full-image BFS controls use10719
vertices, and9 corruptions are rejected. Checkpoint111/195 preserves110
captures and appends only this generator/replay/check, not a full111 run.

The construction rules out improving n-|A| strictly for all state counts
using only a FIXED pair of cardinalities, SC, synchronization, actual-image
reachability or a binary alphabet. A pointwise improvement at the remaining
arithmetic ranges is still possible. More significantly, a quadratic reset
proof still needs to control how successful LOCAL steps fit into ONE word;
sharpness of each individual step does not prove that all those costs must
be incurred successively. This compatibility/cost question remains OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces--sharp-avoid-or-compress-bounds-on-the-first-two-cardinality-faces"></a>
### Sharp avoid-or-compress bounds on the first two cardinality faces

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for the parameter ranges below.
Priority is **OPEN**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim is made.

For nonempty A properly contained in S, define

    ac(S,A)=min{|w|: A is not contained in S w OR |S w|<|S|}.

All words use ORIGINAL letters, with right actions. Szykula's known
avoid-or-compress lemma gives ac(S,A)<=n-|A| when some state of A is
avoidable. It applies to every strongly connected synchronizing DFA.
See [Szykula 2026, Lemma 3 and Open Problem 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245),
which attributes the lemma to the STACS 2018 paper. Its question about
tightness as a function of both cardinalities motivates this result;
the general upper bound is NOT claimed as new.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces--exact-extremal-statement-with-actual-reachable-images"></a>
#### Exact extremal statement, with actual reachable images

Among n-state strongly connected synchronizing DFAs, even requiring
S=Qv for an original word v, the following maxima are exact:

* |S|=|A|+1: maximum ac(S,A)=n-|A|, for every 1<=|A|<n.
* |S|=|A|+2 and S properly contained in Q: maximum ac(S,A)=n-|A|,
  for every 1<=|A|<=n-3.
* S=Q: maximum ac(Q,A)=1, for every nonempty proper A. A synchronizing
  DFA must have an original singular letter, which immediately compresses Q.

The lower bounds have BINARY strongly connected synchronizing examples.
The upper bounds are the known lemma and the elementary last observation.
For the first face, the later [bounded-kernel refinement](#problem4-bounded-kernel-first-face)
also determines every parameter when original-letter fiber sizes and rank
defects are capped, with a binary construction meeting both caps.
Thus the second face includes |S|=3, |A|=1 for every n>=4, and neither
face is limited to isolated-state extensions of a pair. The two faces
do NOT settle all of Open Problem 4. The subsequent
[third-face continuation](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face) proves equality
when |S|-|A|=3 and n-|A| is even and at least6. The general remaining
cardinality problem is OPEN.

The subsequent [all-gaps theorem](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps) proves
sharpness at infinitely many n for EVERY fixed cardinality pair with
gap>=3. Exact maxima at the remaining state counts are still OPEN here.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces--first-face-one-moving-point-and-an-anchored-core"></a>
#### First face: one moving point and an anchored core

Put k=|S|>=2, L=n-k+1>=1. The states are 0,...,n-1. Letter a advances
0,...,L-1 by one and fixes L,...,n-1. Set

    S={0,L,L+1,...,n-1},       A=S\{0}.

Letter b cycles S in the displayed order, and sends every other state
to L. Hence Q b=S: the subset is an actual image. Strong connectivity
follows by taking the a-path from0 to L, then the b-cycle through the
anchored states and back to0.

For 0<=j<L write S_j=A union {j}. The only safe transitions before
compression are

    S_j a=S_(j+1)   (j<L-1),       S_j b=S_0.

At j=L-1, a maps the moving point into L in A. Every word of length
less than L therefore has image S_j for j<L, contains A and has size k.
The ORIGINAL word a^L compresses S. Thus ac(S,A)=L=n-|A|.

Synchronization is not assumed: c=a^L acts on S as the unit 0->L and
fixes all other core states, while b acts as a k-cycle. The standard
cycle/unit word

    c (b^(k-1) c)^(k-2)

resets S and also Q, since Q c=S c=A. Its ORIGINAL length is

    (k-1)L+(k-2)(k-1)=(k-1)(n-1)<=(n-1)^2.

No exact reset-threshold claim is required for the extremal statement.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces--second-face-two-moving-points-and-an-alternating-timer"></a>
#### Second face: two moving points and an alternating timer

Put r=|A|>=1, M=n-r>=3, s=r+2. Write the states as

    A={p_0,...,p_(r-1)},       U={u_1,...,u_M},
    S=A union {u_1,u_2}.

Letter a fixes A. Both constructions below have

    p_i b=p_(i+1) for i<r-1,      p_(r-1) b=u_1.

If M is ODD, a cycles u_1,...,u_M, and

    u_j b=p_0 for odd j,         u_j b=u_2 for even j.

If M is EVEN, necessarily M>=4, and

    u_1 a=u_2;  u_j a=u_(j+1) (2<=j<M);  u_M a=u_2;
    u_1 b=u_2;
    u_j b=p_0 for even j>=2,     u_j b=u_2 for odd j>=3.

In either case Q b=S. The protected b-path reaches u_1, and a then
reaches every u_j; a suitable u_j b returns to p_0. This proves strong
connectivity, including the transient state u_1 in the even case.

The two points in S a^j remain distinct for EVERY j>=0. For
0<=j<=M-2 their b-images are the two different states p_0,u_2.
At j=M-1 they have the SAME b-image p_0:

* Odd M: the pair at that layer is {u_M,u_1}, both with odd index.
* Even M: the pair is {u_M,u_2}, both with even index.

Because A b=(A\{p_0}) union {u_1}, the safe b-transition returns
S a^j to S, and the first exceptional b-transition compresses it.
Every a-run of fewer than M-1 letters followed by b is safe. Every
shorter word can be split into such a-runs; a trailing run is also
safe because a fixes A and keeps the two moving points distinct.
Consequently ALL words of length less than M are safe, while

    h=a^(M-1)b

compresses S. Therefore ac(S,A)=M=n-|A|, as claimed. Avoidance and
compression are BOTH included in this lower bound; it is not only a
claim about the first rank drop of a preferred word.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces--a-charged-synchronization-certificate-for-the-second-face"></a>
#### A charged synchronization certificate for the second face

Let t=a b for odd M, and t=b for even M. On S, t is the full cycle

    p_0,...,p_(r-1),u_1,u_2.

On S, h agrees with t except that u_1 h=p_0 instead of u_2; both
u_1,u_2 map to p_0. Let g be the core unit u_1->u_2. Thus h=g t
on S (equivalently t followed by the unit u_2->p_0).
The original-word macro

    h (t^(s-2) h)^(s-2)

acts on S as g (t^(s-1)g)^(s-2)t, and resets it. To verify the
standard unit/cycle identity directly, after g the missing point is
u_1. Applying t^(-1)g successively shortens the remaining cyclic
interval by one, until only u_2 remains. The final t keeps it a singleton.
Prepending ORIGINAL b gives a whole-Q reset, of charged length

    1+(s-1)M+2(s-2)^2     when M is odd,
    1+(s-1)M+  (s-2)^2    when M is even.

These are explicit upper bounds, not exact rt formulas. They certify
synchronization for ALL parameters; some of these upper bounds exceed
the Cerny square, so they are NOT alleged square proofs for this family.
All occurrences inside a macro are counted as ORIGINAL letters.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces--verification-and-research-consequence"></a>
#### Verification and research consequence

avoid_compress_sharp_faces.py produces the rows, a reaching word,
an attaining word, and a charged reset program. The independent
check_avoid_compress_sharp_faces.py uses ordinary set transitions and
an independent construction in core/cycle coordinates. It checks
ALL safe subset/letter edges before the first successful BFS layer,
strong connectivity in both graph directions, Q b=S, the complete
original-letter macro rows, and the composed whole-Q reset. Small
scopes additionally have exact ordinary full-image reset BFS.
Explicit reset words are literally checked where retained. The finite
scope and corruption counts are recorded in the generated check report.
This is COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED in those scopes, not a formal kernel.

The saved scope has 381 parameters through n1025, 26992 subset vertices,
53222 subset/letter edges, 17305572 original macro state/letter controls,
and 109418 literal reset letters. All cardinalities at n2..18 are covered
on the stated two faces, with selected larger parameters. There are 73
exact full-image reset BFS controls at n<=10 (9926 vertices), and nine
corruptions are rejected. Checkpoint109/193 preserves the previous108
captures and appends only the present generation/replay/check; it is
NOT a full109 rerun. None of these finite counts proves the all-n result;
the preceding timer and charged-core proof supplies that result.

The known local bound cannot be improved strictly merely by using
either of these cardinality relations, actual-image reachability,
strong connectivity, synchronizability, or a binary alphabet.
A proof strategy may still exploit the relation BETWEEN successive
successful steps. These examples do not show that every step in one
reset construction simultaneously incurs its worst local bound. That
missing cost coupling remains the central Cerny obstacle. Cerny OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face--sharp-avoid-or-compress-bounds-on-an-infinite-part-of-the-third-face"></a>
### Sharp avoid-or-compress bounds on an infinite part of the third face

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for EVERY r>=1 and ODD M>=5.
Priority **OPEN**. General Cerny **OPEN**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim.
The known upper bound and its literature attribution are documented in
[[Sharp avoid-or-compress bounds on the first two cardinality faces](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces)](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-sharp-faces).

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face--the-all-parameter-result"></a>
#### The all-parameter result

Put n=r+M+1. There is a BINARY strongly connected synchronizing DFA
with an ACTUAL image S, |S|=r+3, and A properly contained in S, |A|=r,
such that

    ac(S,A)=n-|A|=M+1.

Thus the known bound is exact on the third cardinality face whenever
n-|A| is EVEN and at least6. This is an infinite range for EVERY |A|,
not a claim for the missing parity or every admissible small parameter.
In fact n-|A|=4 cannot have equality on this face: |S|=n-1 admits a
compressing word of length at most3 by the known Pin-Frankl bound.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face--construction"></a>
#### Construction

The states are P={p_0,...,p_r} and U={u_1,...,u_M}. Let

    A=P\{p_r},              S=P union {u_1,u_2}.

Letter a fixes P and cycles U in the displayed order. Letter b is

    p_0 b=u_1,       p_i b=p_(i-1)  (1<=i<=r),
    u_j b=p_r                       (j even),
    u_j b=u_(j+1)                   (j odd, j<M),
    u_M b=u_3.

On S, b is the cycle p_0,u_1,u_2,p_r,p_(r-1),...,p_1.
Every outside state reaches this cycle under at most THREE b's:
even states enter p_r immediately; ordinary odd states enter in two;
u_M follows u_3,u_4,p_r. Therefore Q b^3=S, proving actual reachability.
This is also a one-cluster letter, but no general one-cluster reset bound
is being inferred from that fact. Strong connectivity follows from the
core b-cycle and the a-cycle through all of U.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face--all-short-words-are-safe"></a>
#### ALL short words are safe

For every prefix of length d<=M-2 the image of S consists of ALL P
and two U-points of opposite index parity, with maximum index <=d+2.
This is induction on ORIGINAL letters. Before reaching u_M, a advances
both indices without wrapping, while b sends the even point to p_r,
the odd point to its even successor, and P to A union {u_1}. Thus b
restores all P and produces one odd and one even U-point. The maximum
index increases by at most one per letter.

At layer M-1 the image STILL consists of all P and two distinct U-points.
Their parities are opposite or both odd, NEVER both even. The only new
possibilities are an a-wrap from u_M to u_1, or the exceptional b-image
u_M b=u_3; each produces two odd indices.

At layer M, an a is safe because it is a permutation fixing P. A b on
an opposite-parity pair restores P and two distinct U-points. A b on two
odd U-points is also safe: b is injective on odd U, with all their images
outside {u_1}, so the result consists of A and THREE distinct U-points.
Its cardinality remains r+3, and it contains A. Hence EVERY word of
length at most M neither avoids a point of A nor compresses S.

The attaining ORIGINAL word is a^(M-1)b^2. Its final image is

    {p_0,...,p_(r-2)} union {p_r,u_1,u_2,u_4},

where the first set is empty for r1. It misses p_(r-1) from A while
STILL having size r+3. Thus ac(S,A)=M+1 exactly. In particular this
attaining word demonstrates avoidance without any cardinality drop;
the lower-bound argument nevertheless checks BOTH success conditions.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face--charged-synchronization-not-an-assumed-hypothesis"></a>
#### Charged synchronization, not an assumed hypothesis

Write s=|S|=r+3 and c=a^(M-1)b^s. Its restriction to S fixes P and maps

    u_1 c=p_0,        u_2 c=u_1.

Indeed a^(M-1) sends u_1 to u_M, which takes three b's to p_r and then
s-3 b's to p_0; u_2 goes to u_1 and a full s b-cycle fixes that point.
All images are back in S. Thus c^2 collapses u_1,u_2 to p_0 and fixes P.

In core cycle coordinates 0=p_0,1=u_1,2=u_2,3=p_r,...,s-1=p_1,
the ACTUAL word v=c c b sends 0,1,2 to1, and sends j>=3 to j+1 mod s.
It has the unique fixed root u_1, with maximum height s-2=r+1.
Consequently

    b^3 v^(r+1)

resets Q. Every occurrence is charged in the ORIGINAL alphabet:

    |v|=2[(M-1)+s]+1=2n+3,
    reset length=3+(r+1)(2n+3).

This certificate can exceed (n-1)^2 and is NOT alleged to be shortest
or a square proof. It establishes synchronization for ALL parameters.
The full general Cerny conjecture is not resolved by a locally sharp step.

<a id="direct-attack-avoid-compress-third-face--self-attacks-and-finite-counterexample-to-a-stronger-bound"></a>
#### Self-attacks and finite counterexample to a stronger bound

The proposed ac(S,A)<=n-|S|+2 for |S|-|A|>=2 is **REFUTED**, even for
a binary SC synchronizing DFA and an ACTUAL S. A six-state witness is

    a=(2,0,5,1,3,1),       b=(0,1,3,2,4,4),
    S={0,1,2,3}=Q a a b a, A={0}.

An independent ordinary-set BFS gives ac=5>6-4+2=4 and rt18<25.
The word a b b a a attains ac5. Its exact finite certificate is included
with the family data; it does NOT prove a missing-parity all-n formula.

Adding one more protected anchor to the present timer DOES NOT prove
the fourth-face claim. For odd M>=5, the ORIGINAL word
a b a^(M-3) b b already compresses that padded S in M+1 steps, whereas
n-|A| there is M+2. The moving pair becomes {u_1,u_(M-2)} before the
last two b's; their distinct even images then collide at p_top.
This is a failed padding route, not a universal fourth-face upper bound.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--exact-specified-state-compression-in-the-completed-figure-3-family"></a>
### Exact specified-state compression in the completed Figure 3 family

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper), EVERY p>=3**, n=3p. Finite
corroborations are separately **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. Priority
**OPEN**; no **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. General Cerny **OPEN**.

For the COMPLETE ORIGINAL rows in [A charged reset construction for the published compress-with-another family](#direct-attack-published-compress-other-family),
the shortest word merging state0 with ANY other state has length

    mu(0)=4p=4n/3.                                        (1)

The earlier note already proves SC, synchronization and an original
reset of length4p^2+6p<(3p-1)^2. This continuation supplies the missing
ALL-word lower bound in (1); it does not change that reset certificate.
It resolves the specified-state threshold assertion for the explicitly
diagram-completed family attributed to [Szykula2026 Figure3/Conjecture8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245v1).
No general linear upper bound or unrestricted square proof follows.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--coordinates-and-the-only-two-merging-pairs"></a>
#### Coordinates and the only two merging pairs

Use the main states M_i=i, 0<=i<=2p. For the outer states q>2p,
write O_h=4p-h, where p+1<=h<=2p-1. The coordinate h runs in REVERSE
order on the outer path. Away from the exceptions, a sends an odd
coordinate to coordinate+1 and an even coordinate to coordinate-1;
b does the opposite. The branch remains unchanged. The exceptions are

    M_0 a=M_0;
    M_(2p) a=O_(2p-1),       M_(2p) b=M_2;
    O_(2p-1) a=M_3;
    O_(p+1) x=O_(p+1) for the decreasing matching letter x.

At the outer bottom, that decreasing letter is a if p+1 is even,
and b if p+1 is odd. Its other letter increases the coordinate.
All other ordinary matching rules apply. This follows directly from
the complete rows, including both endpoint parity cases.

The ONLY letter-kernel pairs are

    K={M_3,M_(2p)} for b;       L={M_4,O_(2p-1)} for a.    (2)

Every ORIGINAL state index increases by at most1 in one step. Hence
on a pair path starting at {0,q}, the elapsed length t satisfies

    t>=min(original indices of the two current states).   (3)

The particle starting at0 is one of those two states. Jumps only
decrease its original index, so (3) holds even after branch changes.
We consider distinct pairs until their FIRST collapse.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--an-excluded-main-pair-region"></a>
#### An excluded main-pair region

Let J contain opposite-parity MAIN pairs {M_i,M_j} whose coordinate
sum exceeds2p+1. From any initial {0,q}, the only reachable member of
J is K. This is an ALL-word invariant, not a cutoff enumeration.

For ordinary matching steps an opposite-parity main pair preserves
its sum, while a same-parity pair retains parity type. The fixed state0
cannot create such a large sum. The b-jump from M_(2p) to M_2 can only
create an opposite-parity sum<=2p+1. The a-step from M_(2p) leaves the
main branch. An outer-to-main a-jump lands at M_3; with the other
main image the sum is at most2p+3, and a sum>2p+1 occurs only when
that other image is M_(2p), giving K. Two outer states cannot create
two main images in one step. Finally K a=L and K b collapses. Thus
no step from an admissible pair creates J\{K}, proving the invariant.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--first-entry-layer-c"></a>
#### First entry layer C

Let C consist of opposite-parity main pairs of sum2p+1. Write
x=min(i,j) and set

    phi_C=2p-2+|x-3|.                                    (4)

Every reachable pair in C has elapsed length at least phi_C.
The initial star at0 contains no C pair. An ordinary step within C
changes its smaller coordinate by at most1, so phi_C increases by
at most1. Among admissible pairs outside C, the only entrances are

| Original step | Source | Target | Lower elapsed time after the step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | {M_(2p-3),O_(2p-1)} | {M_3,M_(2p-2)} | 2p-2 |
| b | {M_(2p-2),M_(2p)} | {M_2,M_(2p-1)} | 2p-1 |

Both source-time bounds follow from (3). They equal (4) at the
targets. Inspection of the matching rules gives this complete entrance
list: all other preimages of a C pair are themselves in C or in the
excluded J region. Induction, allowing arbitrary exits and reentries,
proves the claim. In particular the C pair {M_1,M_(2p)} needs at least2p.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--second-entry-layer-h"></a>
#### Second entry layer H

Let H be the disjoint union of

    A={ {M_x,O_h}: x+h=2p+1, x and h of opposite parity };
    E={ {M_x,O_x}: p+1<=x<=2p-1 }.

Here A has 2<=x<=p. Give BOTH types the potential

    phi_H=2p-1+x.                                        (5)

Every reachable H pair has elapsed length at least (5).
The initial star has no H pair. Ordinary steps change x by at most1.
At the outer bottom, the decreasing letter exchanges A's x=p with
E's x=p+1; their potentials differ by1. The remaining admissible
entrances from OUTSIDE H are exactly

| Step | Source | Target | Source-time bound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | {M_1,M_(2p)} in C | {M_2,O_(2p-1)} | >=2p by (4) |
| b | {M_(2p),O_(2p-2)} | {M_2,O_(2p-1)} | >=2p by (3) |
| a | {O_(2p-1),O_(2p-3)} | {M_3,O_(2p-2)} | >=2p+1 by (3) |
| a, p3 ONLY | {O_5,O_4} | {M_3,O_4} | >=7=2p+1 by (3) |

The penultimate row exists only when p>=4. At p3 the outer bottom4
is fixed by a, giving the separate last row. Both have the SAME paid
potential at x3. All other entrances either stay
in H or have an excluded main source. Adding the entering letter
gives respectively (5) at x2,x2,x3. Within H, (5) increases by at
most1. Induction proves the claimed lower bound, including repeated
exits/reentries. In particular E at its top x=2p-1 requires at least
4p-2 steps.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--a-delayed-entrance-to-the-merging-region"></a>
#### A delayed entrance to the merging region

The ONLY admissible entrance to K is

    {M_(2p-1),O_(2p-1)} a=K.                              (6)

Its source is E's top. The other a-preimage of K, namely
{M_4,M_(2p-1)}, is an excluded J pair; b has no main image M_(2p).
Consequently K cannot be reached before length4p-1.

To rule out an earlier collapse by a, let U be the disjoint union

    B={ {M_x,O_h}: x+h=2p+3, x and h of opposite parity };
    F={ {M_(h+2),O_h}: p+1<=h<=2p-2 }.

B has 4<=x<=p+2 and contains L. No initial star pair belongs to U.
The ONLY admissible entrance from OUTSIDE U is K a=L. For ordinary
steps, a B pair preserves its sum and an F pair preserves the
coordinate difference2. At the outer bottom the decreasing letter
exchanges B's x=p+2 with F's x=p+3. All other exceptional transitions
leave U, collapse L, or come from K; an outer-to-main jump produces
M_3 and cannot enter these types. This checks all branch/boundary cases.
Thus every U pair has first entrance length at least4p, regardless
of subsequent departures and reentries.

A b-collapse must start at K and therefore has length>=4p. An
a-collapse must start at L in U and therefore has length>=4p+1.
This covers ALL initial partners and ALL original words, proving
mu(0)>=4p.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower--matching-upper-bound-and-the-general-certificate-mechanism"></a>
#### Matching upper bound and the general certificate mechanism

The ACTUAL word (ba)^p(ab)^p has4p letters and merges0 with2. The
earlier core calculation gives (0,2)(ba)^p=(2p,1) and both of those
states are sent to2 by (ab)^p. Hence mu(0)<=4p, completing (1).
This also proves that any universal bound mu(q)<=Cn+C_0, even for
binary SC corank-one inputs, requires C>=4/3 asymptotically.

The reusable lemma is a finite directed-pair certificate. Suppose
an index ell obeys ell(q0)=0 and ell(qa)<=ell(q)+1. On every initial
q0-pair path, time>=min ell. If a first marked layer C has a potential
that rises by at most1 on internal edges, and each outside entrance
is paid by min ell, its potential is a lower bound on time. A second
layer H can additionally use already proved C potentials to pay
entrances. If every entrance to a merging pair K comes from H at
potential>=B-2, K costs at leastB-1. If another region U has only K
as an outside entrance and contains every other letter-kernel pair,
those cost at leastB before a final letter. All q0-merging words then
have length>=B. Excluded pairs must first be proved unreachable, and
the entrance lists must cover EVERY original edge. This lemma assumes
no corank restriction; it is a lower certificate, not a universal
upper bound. Here B=4p and the two potentials provide such a certificate.

The new generator records C/H/U membership hashes, entry counts, all

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-non-sc-boundary"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-non-sc-boundary--marked-compression-a-displayed-lower-bound-error-and-two-safe-bounds"></a>
### Marked compression: a displayed lower-bound error and two safe bounds

Date: 2026-10-02. General Cerny **OPEN**. The original-word cost gap
remains. These elementary bounds are reconstructed; novelty is not claimed.

**REFUTED:** the literal construction in
[Szykula2026, Proposition7, printed page36 / PDF page4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245v1)
does not have the asserted quadratic marked compression cost. It adds a
state p fixed by the original two letters, and a letter c mapping p to
the core state0 and every core state to t=floor(n/2). Both0 and t are
core states. Consequently c squared maps ALL states to t, for every
n>=3. Neither an original letter nor c compresses p with another in
one step, so **mu(p)=2 exactly**. This refutes the displayed construction's
claimed cost, not the existential statement of Proposition7. Whether
that existential claim admits a different proof remains **OPEN here**.
No contact with the author, unpublished correction, or literature-wide
nonexistence result is asserted. The archived primary PDF has SHA256
62fcce9693c7e44f209f65c95939c48a08d5cf035627ffe67f56b7da59889208.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-non-sc-boundary--a-general-marked-star-counting-bound"></a>
#### A general marked-star counting bound

**PROVED (paper, ANY DFA):** if a state q can be compressed with some
other state, then

    mu(q) <= binom(n-1,2)+1.

Synchronization and strong connectivity are unnecessary. Work in the
pair automaton, with all diagonal pairs terminal. Let P be a shortest
path from ANY of the n-1 off-diagonal pairs containing q to a diagonal;
its length is mu. Its mu off-diagonal vertices are distinct. After its
first vertex, P cannot visit another initial q-pair: the remaining suffix
would compress that pair in less than mu steps. Therefore the other
n-2 initial q-pairs are disjoint from all those mu vertices. There are
only binom(n,2) off-diagonal pairs, so mu+n-2<=binom(n,2).

The proof includes pairs that never merge: those initial star vertices
are still distinct excluded vertices. One must not infer that every
pair is mergeable from the assumption that this one state is compressible.
The four-state synchronizing binary rows

    a=[0,0,3,2], b=[2,0,1,3]

attain mu=4 at state3, so this counting bound can be exact. This one
example does not establish asymptotic sharpness or quadratic growth.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-non-sc-boundary--an-original-letter-obstruction-to-a-large-marked-cost"></a>
#### An original-letter obstruction to a large marked cost

**PROVED (paper, ANY DFA):** if q is not on a cycle of some original
letter f, and h is its height above its eventual f-cycle, then

    mu(q) <= h <= n-1.

The cycle contains a state r satisfying f^h(r)=f^h(q), because f acts
bijectively on that cycle. This r differs from noncyclic q. The literal
word f^h is thus a paid merging witness. In particular, mu(q)>n-1
requires q to be cyclic under EVERY original letter. This condition is
necessary, not sufficient. A cyclic state in a cycle with an incoming
tree need not merge with any other state under powers of that letter:
for f=[1,2,0,0], state0 has no such partner. We do not strengthen the
condition to a claim about its whole functional-graph component.

If Q=C union {p}, C is invariant under every letter, and p has any
outgoing original-letter edge into C, this lemma applies to p. Hence
**mu(p)<=n-1**, independently of how hard synchronization inside C is.
This excludes the entire one-added-state strategy for obtaining a
quadratic cost at that added state, not just the displayed letter c.
It does not cover a nonterminal strongly connected component of size>1.

For q inside an invariant terminal component C, mu_A(q) is at most
mu_(A restricted to C)(q), since the latter permits fewer partners.
Thus a proposed non-SC quadratic example must identify whether its
marked state lies in the terminal component or outside it. A universal
linear bound for outside states has NOT been proved or refuted here.

A separate corrected mutation pressure uses invariant Cerny or the

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-short-reset"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-short-reset--a-shorter-original-reset-and-an-actual-reflection-return"></a>
### A shorter original reset and an actual reflection return

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper), EVERY p>=3** for the completed
Figure3 rows, n=3p. General Cerny and publication priority **OPEN**.
Exact ordinary threshold below is **CONJECTURED**, not proved or formal.

The older reset bound4p^2+6p improves to

    rt(A_p)<=3p^2+4p-1=n^2/3+4n/3-1.                      (1)

This is a fully charged original word. The all-p specified-state threshold
mu0=4p from [Exact specified-state compression in the completed Figure 3 family](#direct-attack-compress-other-exact-lower) is unchanged.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-short-reset--an-actual-pure-reflection-on-the-cyclic-image"></a>
#### An actual pure reflection on the cyclic image

Use c=ba, u=ab and the cyclic image

    R=(0,2,4,...,2p,1), r=p+2, Q c^p=R.

Positions of R are0..p+1. On R, c is the forward cycle. For every j>=p,
the ACTUAL return d_j=a c^j has row

    d_j(i)=j-i mod r,               0<=i<=p-1;
    d_j(p)=d_j(p+1)=j+1 mod r.                            (2)

State2i reaches odd2i-1 after a, then reaches1 after i-1 applications
of c. The outer state a(2p)=2p+1 reaches1 after p applications of c.
The endpoints0 and1 give the other cases directly. This proves (2)
without treating a cycle inverse as an original word.

There is also an ACTUAL pure reflection, overlooked by the previous
rooted-return construction:

    h_j=a^3 c^j,       j>=p-2;
    h_j(i)=j-i mod r,  EVERY 0<=i<=p+1.                  (3)

Indeed a^3 sends2p to4 instead of the outer path, while its action on
the other R points equals a. The longest remaining odd-state c-height
is p-2. At position p the output is j+2 mod r, which equals j-p mod r;
the other positions give (2)'s ordinary reflection rule. Thus
h_(p-2), of ORIGINAL length2p-1, is an involutive permutation of R.
It is an actual return word even though a itself is singular on Q.
This does not give a free reflection or inverse on an arbitrary image.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-short-reset--preparing-the-shrinking-interval"></a>
#### Preparing the shrinking interval

After the original prefix

    F_p=c^p u^(p-1) a^4 c^(p-2),       |F_p|=6p-2,

the exact R-position image is

    S_(p-2)={0,...,p-2} union {p,p+1}.                   (4)

Here is the full original-row calculation. The image of R under u^(p-1)
is {0,1,3,...,2p-1,2p+1}: the main even points descend to the u-cycle,
while2p ends at the last outer point of its u-chain. The two exceptional
points2p-1 and2p+1 both go to4 under a^4. All remaining points are fixed
by a^4. The image is therefore {0,1,3,...,2p-3,4}. Finally c^(p-2)
carries this set exactly to (4): its positions are0..p-2 together with
p and p+1. The calculation includes p3, where the odd-state list has
only3 and the interval endpoint p-4 is absent.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-short-reset--each-paid-return-removes-one-interval-point"></a>
#### Each paid return removes one interval point

For t>=0 put S_t={0,...,t} union {p,p+1}, and set S_(-1)={p,p+1}.
Equation (2) gives, for EVERY 0<=t<=p-2,

    S_t d_(p+t)=S_(t-1).                                  (5)

For t>=2, the reflected interval p,...,p+t reduces modulo p+2 to
{p,p+1} union {0,...,t-2}; the merged pair goes to t-1. At t1 its
two interval points go to p+1/p and the pair goes to0. At t0 the point0
goes to p and the pair goes to p+1. These check both terminal cases.

Thus use original returns in the descending order j=2p-2,...,p.
They leave exactly {p,p+1}, meaning original states{2p,1}. The literal
word u^p then sends both to2, as already proved in the earlier note.
An all-Q reset is consequently

    W_p=c^p u^(p-1) a^4 c^(p-2)
          [ product_(j=2p-2 down to p) (a c^j) ] u^p.     (6)

Its letter count is

    (6p-2) + sum_(j=p)^(2p-2)(2j+1) + 2p
      = (6p-2)+(3p-1)(p-1)+2p=3p^2+4p-1.

For p>=3 its square slack is

    (3p-1)^2-(3p^2+4p-1)=6p^2-10p+2>0.

This improves the earlier genuine quadratic special-family result;
it does not give an unrestricted reset bound. Equations (2)--(5) also
give a conditional shrinking-return lemma on ANY actual image R with
the same stated rows, preparation and final merging word. Their ORIGINAL
costs must all be paid, and the action hypotheses must all be proved.

<a id="direct-attack-compress-other-short-reset--exactness-remains-a-separate-lower-bound-problem"></a>
#### Exactness remains a separate lower-bound problem

Ordinary complete subset computations in small parameters suggest

    rt(A_p)=3p^2+4p-1 for EVERY p>=3.                      (7)

This is **CONJECTURED**. The specified-state4p pair-entry proof does NOT
prove (7); first merging0 is much cheaper than resetting ALL Q. Nor does
matching the observed shortest word pattern give a global lower potential.
There is no claim that every shortest word has form (6), or that all
current images are the sets (4)--(5). A proof would need to control every
alternative original word, not just the displayed shrinking program.

The independent checker reconstructs the original rows and pays the
preparation on every state. It verifies the original base return a c^p,
then every further return by original ba steps, separately verifies the
pure reflection a^3 c^(p-2), and checks every shrinking-set equality.
Small expanded words and independent full forward/reverse subset
computations corroborate (7) only in their finite scopes. The proof of
(1)--(6) is paper only; the earlier abstract Lean theorem is a lower
certificate and does not formalize this reset construction.

Completed finite scope:67 parameters p3..64 and100/128/256/512/1024,
n through3072,35850770 original macro state/letter controls and867768
