Let X supply H={1,9} as pre(G), and let L have pre(B)=C. Both exist
in the earlier entrance flag. Their roles are distinct because H meets C;
for a binary alphabet they are the only letters. The literal fields force

    X permutes0,3; X5=gamma in C; X6=5; X7=6;
    X2=X8=7; X1,X9 in G.

The remaining inputs I={4,10,11,12}, all outside K, biject to
R={9,10,11,12}. For L, pre(C)={u} with u in {0,3,5}; put Lu=delta.
The six input fields pre(A),pre(C),pre(D),pre(E),pre(F),pre(G)
use all P={0,3,5,6,7} and G. Specifically pre(F),pre(G) are G and
the remaining singleton of P in either order. Its ordinary inputs R
therefore permute R. These facts are checked on all48 original H19
field pairs. Strong connectivity forces {gamma,delta}=C; otherwise
one C state has no incoming edge under either original letter.

If gamma=1, take x in I with Xx=9. The protected pair {5,x} follows

    {5,x} X = {1,9}, then X maps it into G, then X merges G to7.

Thus X^3 merges it. If gamma=4,delta=1, take q in R with Lq=9.
Then {u,q} L = {1,9}, and X^2 merges it to7. Thus LX^2 merges a
protected pair. Both contradict P7 isolation of the mandatory core P.
In particular, no individual isolation of2,8 or9 is needed here.

The complete normalized thirteen-state control retains all protected
assignments, both locations of the G input pair, and every ordinary
permutation. It contains6912 L rows and384 X rows,2,654,208 coupled
pairs. Half omit an incoming C state; each other pair has the displayed
literal three-letter protected witness. The normalized pool enlarges
some earlier field restrictions and so cannot miss an actual target.
This control verifies the symbolic proof at actual n13, not by extrapolation.

<a id="problem4-b1-g28-seventh-entrance--independent-check-and-scope"></a>
#### Independent check and scope

The independent checker imports no generator. It checks all19 labelled
geometries and every outside3 mask by augmented ranks modulo100003;
Boolean minors have order<=9 and absolute value<100003, so these are
exact rational ranks. Exact coefficients, every actual nine-set family,
each mandatory intersection, every companion, and all capacity2 parent
field extensions are reconstructed. Every actual family point in its
intersection is isolated in P7 by [Isolation of the mandatory core at the reaching depth](#problem4-mandatory-core-isolation).

Consequently binary E6/F7/G28 retains H9/H29:two geometries/eight labels,
1337 necessary seventh field pairs, still covering all365 parent sixth
pairs. The unrestricted seventh keeps H9/H19/H29:three geometries/twelve
labels. H19's binary exclusion is not transferred to larger alphabets.
The whole G28/E6/F7 geometry is not excluded by this admission alone;
other sixth branches and both F(13,9,1) intervals[11,12] remain.

Run enumerate_b1_g28_seventh.py followed by check_b1_g28_seventh.py
with Python>=3.10 and assertions enabled. This is an auxiliary
conditional certificate; the accepted article and109-file release
supplement remain unchanged.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--a-common-singleton-fourth-entrance-in-the-disjoint-b1c3d2-profile"></a>
### A common singleton fourth entrance in the disjoint B1/C3/D2 profile

9 October 2026. Conditional binary necessary condition at (13,9,1).
This note is outside the article and release. It does not determine F.

Assume ac(S,{3})=12, |S|=9, with strong connectivity and synchronization.
Use H={0,1,2}, B={4}, C={0,1,5}, D={2,6}, J={7,...,12}.
The established equality flag gives dim K_i=12-i, where K_i annihilates
all characteristic image rows through depth i. All these images are
nine-sets through depth eleven. They contain 3,4 through depth ten,
meet C once through nine and D once through eight. H covers P5;
3,4 are isolated in P6. No initial reachable-image assumption is used.

Write h_X=9 chi_X-1. The four h_3,h_4,h_C,h_D form a basis of K8.
Every image under discussion has the form

    T(c,d,h)={3,4,c,d} union (J minus {h}), c in C, d in D, h in J.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--common-fourth-entrance-and-complete-row-admission"></a>
#### Common fourth entrance and complete row admission

The preimage of D under each letter meets every image through depth
seven once. Since D is a collision clique in P2, this preimage is a
clique in P3. A preimage containing 3 or 4 must therefore be its
singleton. The proper set {3,4} union C union D is backward closed
unless some preimage of D meets J: preimages of the earlier protected
cells are already contained in that set. Strong connectivity gives
such a preimage E. The H-cover of P3 then forces

    E={7} union U, U subset H,

after relabelling J. In particular it contains neither 5 nor 6.
Its h_E is independent of the four earlier vectors (use coordinates
7 and J minus {7}), so they form a basis of K7.

Any other preimage R of D, outside {3,4}, has its indicator in
span{1,chi_C,chi_D,chi_E}. The remainder J minus {7} meets S in at
least four states. Its coefficient is zero: otherwise the Boolean
indicator would contribute at least four to |S intersect R|=1.
The private cells 5,6,7 make the three remaining coefficients Boolean.
Since S meets C,D,E once, their sum is one. Thus R is C,D or E.
This proves that E is common; extra Boolean fibers are not discarded.

The eight earlier row types, in the order (pre(3),pre(B),pre(C)), are

    0 ABC, 1 ABD, 2 ACB, 3 ACD, 4 BAC, 5 BAD, 6 BCA, 7 BCD,

where A={3}. The fourteen admitted unordered pairs are
(0,7),(1,6),(1,7),(2,5),(2,7),(3,4),(3,5),(3,6),(3,7),(4,7),
(5,6),(5,7),(6,7),(7,7). For each row retain every pre(D) in
{A,B,C,D,E} disjoint from its three earlier input cells. At least one
row must use E. Also require enough combined input capacity to supply
each output cell. This gives the following complete necessary inventory:

| E | Earlier pairs retained | Full fourth-field pairs | Image forms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 7 | 14 | 41 | 30 |
| 07 | 6 | 6 | 22 |
| 27 | 9 | 9 | 18 |
| 017 | 6 | 6 | 14 |
| 027 | 0 | 0 | 13 |
| 0127 | 0 | 0 | 8 |

The last two shapes meet both C and D. Every earlier row uses one of
those cells, so no letter can have E as its additional disjoint input
cell. They are impossible without a transition search. The stabilizer
interchanges 0,1 and permutes J: these six shapes cover all 48 labelled
sets {j} union U, j in J, U subset H.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--two-shapes-intersecting-c-only"></a>
#### Two shapes intersecting C only

Put E=07 or 017. Its supplying letter F has type 1 or 5, with
pre_F(C)=D, pre_F(D)=E. The other letter L has type 2/6 or 3/7.
In type 2/6 it maps C constantly to 4, maps the other protected input
to a constant delta in C, and maps D into D. In type 3/7 it maps C
constantly to 4, maps D into C and has a constant delta in D supplied
by the other protected input. In both cases L permutes J. These are
all six admitted pairs; no ordinary permutation is normalized away.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--e017"></a>
##### E=017

Every short image has T7=T5, equivalently c=5 iff h is not 7.
F maps {5} union (J minus {7}) bijectively onto J: there are six such
inputs, all outside H, so the cover forbids their collisions.

First let L have constant C-output delta. If delta is 0 or 1, all
L-images omit 7. Its unique J predecessor is then absent in every
image through depth six, contradicting strong connectivity, which
reaches any state from S within four steps. Hence delta=5. Incoming
C targets now force F to map D bijectively onto {0,1}. Put t=F5.
If t is not 7, an image containing 0 at depth at most four has hole 7;
its F-image has c in {0,1} but hole t, violating the equation. If
t=7, any S L has c=5 and hole h not 7; its F-image has c in {0,1}
and hole Fh not 7, again a contradiction. Lengths are at most five.

Now let L have constant D-output delta. Both letters use D as pre(C).
Let W_F,W_L subset D be their respective preimages of 5, and let
r_F in {5} union (J minus {7}), r_L in J be their preimages of 7.
Preserving T7=T5 puts

    chi_{r_F}-chi_{W_F}, chi_{r_L}-chi_{W_L} in K6.

An exact coordinate elimination in the displayed basis of K7 gives
rank at most six precisely when W_F=W_L and either
(I) r_F=5,r_L=7, or (II) r_F=r_L=j in J minus {7}.
This table covers all 6*6*4*4=576 possibilities. Each second column
is outside K7. Incoming transitions to all three C states force the
common W to be a proper singleton {d0}; write D={d0,d1}.

In case I, every image satisfies c=5 iff d=d0. If delta=d1, every
L-image omits 7, and L's predecessor of 7 is 7, giving the same
reachability contradiction. If delta=d0, reach d1 within four steps
and apply L: its C-output is in {0,1} and D-output is d0, impossible.

In case II, d=d1 iff h=j, so d=d1 implies c=5. If delta=d1, all
L-images have hole j; its J predecessor is absent from all short
images, contradicting reachability. Thus delta=d0. The image S L L
has (c,d)=(5,d0). If F7=d0, this class is invariant under L and F:
all its images still have (5,d0), so reaching 0 from it within four
steps is impossible (total depth at most six). If F7=d1, its F-image
has (5,d1), and its next F-image has c in {0,1},d=d1, impossible.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--e07"></a>
##### E=07

Here T0+T7=1. F's inputs to J are {1,5} union (J minus {7}).
The C triangle already consumes three immediate pairs, and |P1|<=4.
To fit seven inputs into six J targets while respecting the H-cover,
the sole kernel is 15 or 1q, q in J minus {7}; its six blocks map
bijectively onto J. Thus P=pre_F(7) is one of
{1,5}, {5}, {1,q}, or {j}, j in J minus {7}.

If L has constant C-output delta, delta=0 would force every L-image
to omit 7 and hence every short image to omit its J predecessor.
Thus delta is 1 or 5. Incoming C targets force F to map D bijectively
onto C minus {delta}. Its preimage of 0 is a proper singleton of D.
Preservation of the equation under L puts h_{r_L} in K6, with r_L
in J; this vector is outside K7. K7 and h_{r_L} are constant on D.
Preservation under F puts h_{pre_F(0) union P} in K6, nonconstant
on D. This would make dim K6 at least seven, a contradiction.

If L has constant D-output delta, let W_F,W_L subset D be the
preimages of 0. The two vectors h_{W_F union P},h_{W_L union {r_L}}
belong to K6. Exact coordinate elimination gives rank at most six
precisely when W_F=W_L and either
(I) P={1,5},r_L=7, or (II) P={j},r_L=j in J minus {7}.
All 12*6*4*4=1152 possibilities are covered. Incoming C transitions
again force W={d0} proper; put D={d0,d1}.

In case I, c=0 iff d=d0. If delta=d0, all L-images omit 7, whose
L predecessor is 7. If delta=d1, an image containing d0 at depth
at most four has an L-image with c=0,d=d1. Both are impossible.
In case II, d=d0 iff h=j, whereas c=0 iff h=7. If delta=d0,
every L-image has hole j, giving a fixed absent J predecessor.
Hence delta=d1, and S L L has c in {1,5},d=d1. If F7=d1,
this class is invariant and cannot reach 0 within four more steps.
If F7=d0, two applications of F give c=0,d=d0, which would require
the distinct holes 7 and j simultaneously. Total depth is four.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--the-shape-intersecting-d-only-e27"></a>
#### The shape intersecting D only: E=27

Every short image has T7=T6. Its supplying letter L has type
0/2/4/6. It maps {6} union (J minus {7}) bijectively to J. Put
r_L=pre_L(7) in that set and K_L=pre_L(6) subset {2,7}.
The other letter F has type 1/5 or 3/7, and permutes J; write
r_F=pre_F(7) in J. It maps either C or a protected singleton into D.

First suppose F is constant on its D-input cell. Constant output 2
forces all short images to omit r_F, contradicting reachability.
Thus its output is 6, and every short image contains r_F. If r_F=7,
every short image has d=6, also contradicting reachability of 2.
For r_F in J minus {7}, h_{r_F} and
chi_{r_L}-chi_{K_L} lie in K6. Coordinate elimination (120 cases)
permits only (I) r_L=6,K_L={7}, or (II) r_L=r_F,K_L={2,7}.
Case II leaves state 2 without any incoming transition under either
letter. In case I, L2=2,L7=6,L6=7. On images with T7=T6, L preserves
the D-coordinate, and F resets it to 6. From S F no later image can
contain 2; strong connectivity
would reach it in four more steps (total depth at most five).

Otherwise F has pre(D)=C and W=pre_F(6) is a proper nonempty
subset of C. The vector chi_{r_F}-chi_W in K6 is nonconstant on C;
K7 and chi_{r_L}-chi_{K_L} are constant on C. Since dim K6=6,
the latter vector must lie in K7. Coordinate elimination (864 cases)
forces r_L=6,K_L={7}: L2=2,L7=6,L6=7, and it permutes
J minus {7}. The C-merging letter must be L (type 2/6), so its
constant C-output is delta. Incoming C targets force F2=g2,F6=g6
distinct, with delta the third C state.

Preservation of T7=T6 under F says c in W iff h is not r_F.
If delta is not in W, all L-images have hole r_F. For r_F=7,
this fixes their D-coordinate at 2 and, since L preserves that coordinate, fixes
every short input image at 2. For r_F not 7, its unique L predecessor
is absent in every short image. Both contradict reachability. Thus
delta is in W. If r_F=7, L similarly forces every short input
D-coordinate to be 6. Hence r_F is not 7. Any image with d=2 has
hole 7 and consequently c in W.

An image T with c=delta,d=6 is S L if S contains 6, and S F L
otherwise: when S contains 2 its C-coordinate is in W, so S F
contains 6. If g6 is in W, the class d=6,c in {delta,g6} is
invariant under both letters and cannot reach 2 within four more
steps (total depth at most six). Otherwise T F F has c=g6,d=2,
contradicting the just established implication d=2 => c in W.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-fourth-entrance-reduction--conclusion-and-audit-limits"></a>
#### Conclusion and audit limits

Every nonsingleton fourth entrance is excluded. In this conditional
binary profile the common fourth entrance must be E={7}, hence all
images through depth seven contain 7. The 41 fourth-field pairs over
all fourteen earlier pairs remain admitted. No entire third or joint
orbit has yet been excluded by this note. The binary and unrestricted
extrema at (13,9,1) remain in [11,12]; no alphabet separation follows.

The exact-rational rank tables and an independently enumerated
fourth-field inventory are reproduced by check_b1_mixed_c3_fourth.py.
Its literal smaller row controls are checks under the stated local
premises, not claims of equality at those smaller sizes. The proof
above retains all ordinary permutations and uses only counts through
depth seven, short safety, and the established equality flag.

The independent audit also checks 144 constant-C rank configurations
for E=07. For E=017 and constant C-output under L, it evaluates all
23,040 parameterized thirteen-state F rows, including every J-output
bijection, on 76,800 relevant nine-sets. Complete normalized local row
controls have 12,744 assignments at n=8 and 53,568 at n=9. Each is
rejected independently by connectivity, synchronization, or a failing
entrance prefix. These are supplementary controls; the symbolic proof
and exact rank tables supply the thirteen-state conditional result.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-four-point-third-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-four-point-third-exclusion--four-point-third-entrance-in-the-b1c3-mixed-joint"></a>
### Four-point third entrance in the B1/C3 mixed joint

9 October 2026. Conditional binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the release.

Suppose ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9, in a binary strongly connected synchronizing
automaton. Normalize H={0,1,2}, a=3, b=4, B={4}, C={0,1,5}. We exclude
D={0,1,2,6}. Write U={0,1}, J={7,...,12}, R={2,6} union J,
and O={5,6} union J. Established premises are |P1|<=4, H covering P5,
the entrance flags and isolation of a in P7. Also b is isolated in P6:
all images through depth ten contain a,b, so ac(S,{a,b})>=11; the
avoid-or-compress upper gives equality 11, and [A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag)'s
protected-pair inequality gives the asserted isolation. No reachability
of the initial set is needed for this negative.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-four-point-third-exclusion--complete-row-and-kernel-cover"></a>
#### Complete row and kernel cover

The third fiber is common in this geometry. Any other outside preimage
of C has indicator alpha+beta chi_B+gamma chi_C+eta chi_D. The remainder
outside B,C,D meets S at least five times, so alpha=0. The private cells
{4}, {5}, {2,6} make beta,gamma,eta Boolean. Its count on S is their sum,
which must be one. Thus the only outside fibers are B,C,D. Since D
overlaps C, the unique C-merging letter L has pre_L(B)=C and pre_L(C)
a protected singleton p in {a,b}. Put pL=delta in C. The other protected
input maps to a. The second letter F permutes {a,b}, has pre_F(C)=D,
and maps all its other inputs (5 and J) to R. L maps R to R.

The C triangle consumes three immediate pairs. Four D inputs must map
to the three C outputs. A triple kernel block would add at least two
pairs outside the C triangle. Thus F has one two-point block, one
of 01,02,06,12,16,26, or the two blocks 01 and 26. In the last case
F uses two C outputs and delta must be the remaining point. In the
other cases F uses three distinct C outputs. F is injective on {5} union J because these inputs
are all outside H. Its seven R outputs miss exactly one point nu of R,
and every used R output has an outside-H predecessor.

L is either bijective R to R, or has just one pair {2,q}, q in R minus
{2}, and seven R blocks injecting into eight R outputs. In the latter
case all blocks contain an outside-H point. Its missing R output mu
is in {2,q}, or pulling this kernel pair under L gives an outside-H
two-step pair. Only when the F block is 01 can q be arbitrary; when
it is 26 the L pair must be 26, and the other F blocks force L bijective.

D is a collision clique in P2 (F followed by L). If F used both R
outputs 2,6, its two outside predecessors would merge by F^2 L.
Therefore nu is 2 or 6. At least one of 2,6 has an outside L predecessor:
for bijective L there is only one H input in R, and for singular L all
used R blocks contain outside points. If delta were in U, pulling
{delta,d} subset D, for such an L-used d in {2,6}, would give an
outside pair merged by L F L. Hence delta=5.

Similarly F has an outside predecessor of its used output d in {2,6}.
If F6 were in U, the outside pair consisting of 6 and that predecessor
would follow F into D and merge by F L. Hence F6=5. The double-block
case is now impossible: delta=5=F6 would leave one C point without
any incoming transition. The complete core
cover consequently has twelve maps: two for each of the six kernel
blocks. Write G0=binomial(H,2). The words below are concatenations in
the usual left-to-right action order.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-four-point-third-exclusion--f2-in-u-blocks-0102120616"></a>
#### F2 in U: blocks 01,02,12,06,16

First suppose nu=6. Let x be the outside F predecessor of 2 and let
y be an outside F predecessor of x. Such y exists: x is either 5,
whose outside predecessor is 6, or in J, every point of which is used.
The pair {x,y} follows F to {2,x}, then to {F2,2} subset D, and merges
by F L. Word F^3 L has length four. Thus nu=2.

Now F permutes O, and x=F^(-1)(6) is in O minus {6}. If L is bijective
on R, pulling the D pair {2,6} forces L2 in {2,6}. If L2=6, choose
outside L predecessors of 2 and x (the latter is p when x=5).
They follow L F to {F2,6} subset D and merge by F L. Thus L2=2.
If L is singular, using both 2 and 6 would pull the D pair to an
outside pair merged by L F L, so mu is in {2,6} as well as {2,q}.
If mu is not 2, necessarily q=6 and mu=6; L uses both 2 and x with outside
predecessors (x is never 6), giving the same word L F^2 L. Thus mu=2.

For blocks 01,02,12, F maps H into H. If L is bijective and L2=2,
neither letter has a predecessor of H outside H, contrary to strong
connectivity. In the singular case use

  G = G0 union { {h,o}: h in H, o in O }.

F preserves H and O and permutes {a,b}, so G is backward closed under
F. L uses only O as G output vertices, so cannot map a pair onto a
distinct G edge. All direct kernels lie in G; {a,b} does not. Thus
G is also backward closed under L and synchronization is impossible.

For block {u,6}, u in U, let h be the other point of U. L must be bijective,
L2=2, L permutes {6} union J, F u=F6=5, and F maps {h,2} bijectively
to U. If x=5, the protected pair {2,p} merges by L F^2 L, length four.
Therefore x is in J. There are two remaining maps:

* If Fh=h and F2=u, use

    G = G0 union h*O union u*{5,6} union 2*(O minus {5}).

* If Fh=u and F2=h, let y=F^(-1)(x). If y=5, the protected pair
  {2,p} merges by L F^3 L, length five. Thus y is in J. Use

    G = G0 union h*{5,6,x} union u*{5,6} union 2*(O minus {5}).

Here v*T means the set of unordered distinct pairs {v,t}, t in T;
U*T is the union of those stars over v in U.
Both graphs contain all direct kernels and omit {a,b}. Under L,
the only distinct G edges with used output endpoints are 2 paired
with {6} union J; their preimages are again of that form. There is
no edge 25, so the protected L predecessor p of 5 creates none.
Under F, the relevant singleton preimages are pre(2)=empty,
pre(5)={u,6}, pre(6)={x}; in the second graph pre(x)={y} subset J.
The displayed h,u stars pull back respectively into the displayed
2,h,u stars and G0. All other ordinary outputs have arbitrary O
predecessors. This checks backward closure and proves nonsynchronization.

The protected-pair words above contradict isolation of p in at least P6,
even though their other endpoint 2 is in H. They are not claimed to be
outside-H pairs.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-four-point-third-exclusion--f-kernel-26"></a>
#### F kernel 26

Here F2=F6=5, F permutes U, and nu is again 2 or 6. Put

  G1 = G0 union U*O union { {2,6} }.

For either nu, G1 is backward closed under F: pre(U)=U,
pre(5)={2,6}, pre(6) is empty if nu=6 and is an ordinary singleton
if nu=2, and pre(2) is empty if nu=2. In the latter case also

  G2 = G1 union 2*(O minus {5})

is backward closed under F. All direct kernels are included.

If L is singular, its pair is 26 and it misses 2 or 6. Among the G1
vertices it uses 5 and at most one of 2,6, together with J; no two of
these form a G1 edge. Thus G1 is backward closed under L as well.

If L is bijective, the D-clique cover forces L2 in {2,6}. For nu=2,
if L2=2 use G2: L permutes {6} union J, so its 2-stars pull back
to 2-stars, and it uses no U output or edge 25. If L2=6, let z be
the ordinary L predecessor of 2. If z is in J, an outside pair follows
L to {2,z}, then L to {6,2}, and F merges it; word L^2 F has length
three. Otherwise z=6, L permutes the pair {2,6} and J, and G1 is
backward closed under L.

For nu=6, let z be the ordinary L predecessor of whichever of 2,6
is not L2. If z is in J, its outside F predecessor and the outside
F predecessor of 2 follow F to {2,z}, then L to {2,6}. Thus F L F merges
that outside pair in three steps. Otherwise z=6, L permutes {2,6}
and J, and G1 is backward closed under L.

Every surviving graph omits {a,b}, hence prevents synchronization.
This completes all six kernel blocks without fixing any ordinary
injection or permutation. D={0,1,2,6} is excluded. No full thirteen-state
scan, new F value, arbitrary-alphabet exclusion or numerical alphabet
separation is asserted.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-four-point-third-exclusion--independent-audit"></a>
#### Independent audit

The standalone checker enumerates the complete 15 D partitions, 4,140
L R partitions and 877 F R partitions. Its literal C-output enumeration
has 42 F maps and 114 (delta,F) cores, including all six double-block
maps with their necessary delta. It checks 564,480 L output assignments
over the six distinct extra-pair constraints and all 40,320 F R injections.
The universal graph checks cover 312 configurations, using conservative
sets of all unspecified thirteen-state outputs rather than fixed cycles.

Complete small normalized row controls have 1,872 assignments at n=7,
18,792 at n=8 and 331,776 at n=9. Each explicit proof word or obstruction
is checked on each row; independent forward pair BFS also finds an
outside pair through depth five, a protected pair through depth six,
failure of strong connectivity or failure of synchronization. The
n=9 control has two ordinary points and exercises the distinct x,y
graph branch. These are controls, not a full thirteen-state scan or
an extrapolated extremal upper bound. The result leaves only
D={2,6} and {0,2,6} in this B1/C3 mixed joint. Residual binary third
admission has 165 typed orbits and 918 letter pairs. Joint cases remain
26/43 and both extrema stay [11,12].

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-new-point-2-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-new-point-2-exclusion--excluding-third-entrances-with-sole-new-point-2-in-the-b1c3-mixed-case"></a>
### Excluding third entrances with sole new point 2 in the B1/C3 mixed case

9 October 2026. Symbolic binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the release.

Assume binary strongly connected synchronizing equality ac(S,{3})=12,
|S|=9. Normalize H={0,1,2} covering P5, B={4}, C={0,1,5}. The established
five-pair endpoint argument gives |P1|<=4. We exclude the four third
profiles D={0,2},{2,5},{0,1,2},{0,2,5}. D={2} was excluded earlier.
No initial-set reachability assumption is used.

Put a=3,b=4,q=6, J={7,...,12}, O={q} union J, R={2} union O.
The label q will denote the outside partner of a necessary extra kernel
pair, not a new point of D. Write U=D intersect C and V=C minus D.
Here U is nonempty proper and D=U union {2}.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-new-point-2-exclusion--complete-kernels-and-r-output-blocks"></a>
#### Complete kernels and R-output blocks

[Singleton first entrance and a covered second entrance](#problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover) proves a common third fiber and
the complete binary row cover for this one-new-point geometry. The unique
C-merging letter L satisfies pre_L(B)=C, pre_L(C)={p}, p=a or b, and
pre_L(A)={the other protected point}; let delta=pL in C. The other letter
F permutes {a,b}, has pre_F(C)=D, and has a protected singleton as
preimage of B. Its remaining inputs map into R.

The same proposition proves that L is not injective outside C. Its C
triangle already contributes three immediate pairs. An outside-C pair
must meet H at 2. L2 belongs to R, whereas La,Lb belong to {a} union C;
so its other endpoint is ordinary, normalized to q=6. Consequently the
full immediate-pair set is exactly

  K = binomial(C,2) union {{2,q}}.

L has precisely the C block, the {2,q} block and all other points as singletons.
Its seven R-input blocks are {2,q} and the six J singletons, injected
into the eight R outputs. It misses exactly one R point mu. Every used
R output has an outside-H L predecessor. If both 2 and q were used,
pulling the pair {2,q} back under L would give an outside-H pair merging
in two steps. Thus mu is 2 or q. Likewise, if a short mergeable pair
joins delta to a used R output, pulling it under L gives an outside-H
pair: delta has the outside-H singleton predecessor p in {a,b}.

The R-inputs of F are V union O. Any F kernel pair must belong to K.
Since 2 is not among these inputs, only pairs inside V can occur.
For V of size two there are nine inputs into eight R outputs; the sole
permitted collision is the V pair, so its blocks map bijectively to R.
For singleton V there are eight inputs and no permitted collision,
again bijective to R. These assertions exhaust the abstract kernels;
no guessed cycle type or unproved higher-layer edge cap is used.

If U={0} or {0,1}, V contains 5. Every F R-input block then has an
outside-H point (5 or an ordinary point). The two R outputs 2,q both
have outside-H F predecessors, so an outside-H pair merges by F L.
This excludes D={0,2} and D={0,1,2}.

It remains to treat U={5} or {0,5}. Then V is {0,1} or {1}. Its F
kernel block consists entirely of H points and has some R output e;
all other R-output blocks have ordinary predecessors. Pulling {2,q}
under F forces e in {2,q}; otherwise an outside-H pair merges by F L.
The restriction F:O -> R minus {e} is bijective.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-new-point-2-exclusion--the-exceptional-output-e2-is-impossible"></a>
#### The exceptional output e=2 is impossible

If mu=2, both letters preserve the proper nonempty ordinary set O:
LO=O and FO=O. This contradicts strong connectivity. Hence mu=q.
If delta belongs to U, {delta,2} is a pair in D and merges by F L;
pulling it under L gives an outside-H pair in at most three steps.
Therefore delta belongs to V.

Let x be the unique ordinary F predecessor of q. The pair {delta,x}
merges by F L, because Fdelta=2 and Fx=q. If x differs from q, its
L output-preimage block exists since L misses only q, so pulling this
pair under L gives an outside-H pair in three steps. If x=q, Fq=q
and L has no predecessor of q. Thus q has no incoming transition
except its self-loop, again contrary to strong connectivity. This
excludes e=2 for both remaining U shapes.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-new-point-2-exclusion--exceptional-output-q-a-complete-finite-core-cover"></a>
#### Exceptional output q: a complete finite core cover

Now e=q and F(V)=q. Let x in O be the F predecessor of 2. If F5 belongs
to U, the outside-H pair {5,x} maps under F into D and merges by F L,
giving a three-step contradiction. Thus F5 belongs to V. If x differs
from q, choose an ordinary F predecessor y of x. The outside-H pair
{5,y} maps under F to {F5,x}, then under F to {q,2}, and L merges it.
Consequently x=q, so Fq=2 and F permutes J.

If delta is in U, pulling {delta,2} in P2 under L forces mu=2.
If delta is in V, pulling {delta,q} in P2 under L forces mu=q.
The predecessor requirements for all C points and the budget K now
leave the following exhaustive cases. Values at a,b merely select
which outside-H protected point is the singleton L predecessor of delta.

For U={5}, write gamma=F5 and eta=F2. The three points delta,gamma,eta
are distinct and exhaust C. Since gamma belongs to V={0,1}:

* If delta=5, both gamma and eta are in V. The outside pair {5,q}
  follows F three times to {2,q}, then L merges it. Word F^3 L has
  length four, a contradiction.
* If delta is in V, eta=5 and mu=q. Let
  G=binomial(C,2) union {{2,q},{2,5},{0,q},{1,q}}.
  It contains every immediate kernel pair and is backward closed under
  F. Under L the only possible G output vertices with predecessors are
  delta and 2; G contains no pair between them. Thus inverse images of
  distinct G pairs under L are empty. G is backward closed under both
  rows and omits {a,b}, so that pair can never merge. Synchronization
  is impossible. This covers both choices of gamma.

For U={0,5}, V={1}, necessarily F5=1. F2 differs from F0 and F5:
collisions involving input 2 would add a pair outside K. Thus F2 is
0 or 5, and F0 is either 1 or the other point of {0,5}.

* If F0=1, F0=F5 is the allowed {0,5} block. Put h=F2 in {0,5};
  delta is its other point and mu=2. The graph
  G=binomial(C,2) union {{2,q},{0,2},{2,5},{1,q}}
  contains all kernels and is backward closed under F. L has only
  delta,q as G output vertices with predecessors, and G has no edge
  between them. Hence G is also backward closed under L, omits {a,b},
  and contradicts synchronization. This covers two core assignments.
* If F0=0 and F2=5, delta may be any C point. For delta=1 or 5, only
  the self-loop 0F=0 enters state 0, contradicting strong connectivity.
  For delta=0, mu=2; choose the protected L predecessor p of 0 and an
  ordinary L predecessor y of q. The outside-H pair {p,y} follows
  L F^2 to {0,5}, then L merges it. Word L F^2 L has length four.
* If F0=5 and F2=0, F cycles 0,5,1,q,2. For every possible delta,
  the outside-H pair {5,q} follows F four times to {0,1}, and L
  merges it. Word F^4 L has length five, a contradiction.

The last three bullets cover respectively two, three and three core
assignments, all eight possibilities for U={0,5}. The two earlier
bullets cover all four possibilities for U={5}. The closure assertions
concern distinct output pairs; direct collisions are separately included
in G. Ordinary J inputs have no F output in these graphs, while under
L their possible outputs cannot form a graph edge with delta. The graph
argument therefore covers every unspecified ordinary permutation or
injection, not only a selected completion.

All four profiles are excluded symbolically, with merging words of
length at most five or a structural contradiction. The independent audit
checks every abstract R kernel, every finite core case, and complete
literal row families with zero and one unmarked ordinary point. Those
small-family controls do not replace the symbolic treatment of six J
points at n=13. No SAT answer or full transition-table scan is claimed.

The B1/C3 mixed joint still remains, but its third entrances are reduced
to {6},{0,6},{2,6},{0,1,6},{0,2,6},{0,1,2,6}. The intact small-first
inventory now has 169 residual binary typed third orbits and 930 letter
pairs. Joint cases remain 26 binary / 43 unrestricted; both extrema at
(13,9,1) remain [11,12]. No new F value or alphabet separation is claimed.

The displayed remaining D labels use the original third-inventory
normalization. Its state 6 is a marked D point and must not automatically
be identified with the kernel partner q of the excluded cases above.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-one-new6-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-one-new6-exclusion--excluding-one-new-point-overlapping-third-entrances-in-b1c3-mixed"></a>
### Excluding one-new-point overlapping third entrances in B1/C3 mixed

9 October 2026. Symbolic binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the release.

Normalize H={0,1,2}, a=3,b=4,B={4},C={0,1,5}. Suppose binary strongly
connected synchronizing equality ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9. We exclude D={0,6}
and D={0,1,6}. The established hypotheses are H covering P5 and |P1|<=4.
No initial-image reachability assumption is used.

Put U=D intersect C, so U={0} or {0,1}, V=C minus U, and R={2,6,...,12}.
[Singleton first entrance and a covered second entrance](#problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover) proves a common D here and the
complete row cover: the C-merging letter L has pre_L(B)=C, pre_L(C)={p}
with p=a or b, and pL=delta in C. The other protected input maps to a.
F permutes {a,b} and has pre_F(C)=D. Write g(u)=uF on D.

The same proposition forces L noninjective outside C. The C triangle
and pair budget leave exactly one outside-C pair E={2,q}, q in R minus
{2}. Normalize q=6 if it is the D point, otherwise q=7. L's R-input
kernel has the E block and other singletons, seven blocks into eight R
outputs. Every block has an outside-H input; if both E outputs were used,
pulling E under L would give an outside pair merging in two steps. Thus
L misses exactly one R output mu in E. Every other R output has an
outside-H L predecessor. Delta has the outside-H singleton predecessor p.

The R-inputs of F are V union (R minus {6}). Their kernels can only use
pairs of E, when both inputs are present, and the V pair when |V|=2.
For D={0,6}, there are nine such inputs; for D={0,1,6}, there are eight.
The allowed output count is eight. When q=6, E is not among those input
pairs: the first case has exactly the V={1,5} block, the second has no
collision. Both have eight blocks, bijective to R, and their only block
entirely inside H is {2}.

When q differs from 6, the complete kernel options are: the V block
alone, E alone or both for U={0}; and no pair or E for U={0,1}. Eight
blocks have exactly one H-only block, whose R output e must be in E,
or pulling E under F would give an outside two-step pair. Seven blocks
all have outside-H inputs; their one missing R output nu must be in E
for the same reason. In particular, since 6 is not in E, F has an
outside-H predecessor of 6, as does L.

If delta belongs to U, pulling the D pair {delta,6}, mergeable by F L,
under L gives an outside-H pair in three steps. Thus delta belongs to V.
If g(6) belongs to U, the outside-H point 6 and an outside-H F predecessor
of 6 map into D under F, then F L merges them, again within three steps.
Thus g(6) belongs to V. The nonempty U consequently has no predecessor
outside U under either letter: its only possible incoming inputs are U
under F. This contradicts strong connectivity and excludes q different
from 6 for both profiles. This argument keeps every ordinary output choice.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-one-new6-exclusion--kernel-partner-equal-to-the-d-point"></a>
#### Kernel partner equal to the D point

Now q=6 and E={2,6}. Let J={7,...,12}. F is bijective on its eight
R-input blocks, with unique H-only block {2}. Thus e=F2 is 2 or 6.
Let r be the common R output of V (a singleton if U={0,1}). It differs
from e, and all J inputs map bijectively to R minus {e,r}.

If e=2 and mu=2, only the self-loop 2F=2 enters 2, contradicting strong
connectivity. Hence mu=6. If r is in J, an outside-H pair maps under
L to {2,x}, x in J the F predecessor of 6, then F L merges it. If r=6
but delta is in V, use the protected L predecessor of delta and an
outside L predecessor of 2 to obtain the same three-step word L F L.
Therefore r=6 and delta belongs to U. If g(6) belongs to U, the outside
pair {5,6} maps into D under F and merges by F L, giving F^2 L.
Consequently g(6) belongs to V; F now permutes J.

For U={0}, delta=0 and the two distinct D outputs g(0),g(6) exhaust V.
Choose outside-H L predecessors of 0 and 2. Their pair follows L F^2
to {6,2}, then L merges it; word L F^2 L has length four.
For U={0,1}, g(6)=5 and F maps U into U, since any U input mapped to 5
would collide with 6 outside the immediate-pair budget. Set

  G = binomial(C,2) union binomial(D,2) union {E,{2,5}}.

F swaps 5 and 6, fixes 2, maps U into U and permutes J. Thus G is
backward closed under F and contains all kernels. L has only delta and
2 as G vertices with predecessors, and G has no edge between them;
inverse images of distinct G pairs under L are empty. G omits {a,b},
which can never merge, contradicting synchronization. This finishes e=2.

Let e=6. If r is in J, write x in J for the F predecessor of 2 and
choose an outside-H F predecessor y of x. The outside pair {x,y} follows
F^2 to E, then L merges it. Hence r=2 and F permutes J. If delta is in
U, pulling {delta,6} under L forces mu=6. If delta is in V, pulling
{delta,2} in F^(-1)(E) under L forces mu=2. If g(6) is in V, {5,6}
follows F^2 to E; word F^2 L gives an outside three-step contradiction.
Thus gamma=g(6) belongs to U.

For U={0}, gamma=0. Nonzero incoming targets for all C points force
delta and g(0) to be the two distinct points of V, so mu=2. The graph

  G = binomial(C,2) union {E,{0,6},{1,2},{2,5}}

is backward closed under F: F maps V to 2, 2 to 6, 6 to 0 and 0 into V.
It contains all kernels. L has only delta and 6 as G output vertices
with predecessors, and G has no edge between them. Thus G is also
backward closed under L, omits {a,b}, and prevents synchronization.

For U={0,1}, let h be its point other than gamma. Collisions between
6 and a U input are outside the pair budget, so g(U) is contained in
{h,5}. Nonzero incoming targets for all C points leave exactly these cases:

* If g(gamma)=h, g(h) is h or 5. The outside pair {5,6} follows F^3
  into C, and the final L merges it. Word F^3 L has length four.
* If g(gamma)=g(h)=5, delta=h and mu=6. Use the graph G from the
  e=2, U={0,1} case. It is backward closed under F (U maps to 5,
  6 to gamma, 2 to 6 and 5 to 2), and L again cannot map a pair to
  a distinct G edge. It contains all kernels and omits {a,b}.
* Otherwise g(gamma)=5 and g(h)=h. If delta=gamma, only the self-loop
  hF=h enters h, contradicting strong connectivity. If delta=h,
  mu=6: outside-H L predecessors of h and 2 follow L F^2 into C,
  then L merges them; word L F^2 L has length four. If delta=5,
  mu=2: enlarge that same graph G by the edge {2,h}. It is backward
  closed under F, contains all kernels, and has no edge between the
  only L-used G output vertices 5 and 6. Synchronization is impossible.

This is the complete finite core cover: g(6) is distinct from both
U-input outputs, and g(U) is either constant or injective. Delta plus
the D outputs must include every C point. The independent checker
enumerates these conditions literally and verifies the explicit words,
graph closure with every possible ordinary output, and complete small
normalized row families. No arbitrary permutation is fixed by the proof.
All short merging words have length at most four. The graphs concern
distinct output pairs; their direct kernels are included separately.

Both third profiles are excluded. B1/C3 mixed now retains only
D={2,6},{0,2,6},{0,1,2,6}, the three multi-new-point profiles. The
inventory remains intact; residual binary admission is 166 typed third
orbits and 921 letter-profile pairs. Joint cases remain 26/43 and both
extrema stay [11,12]. No full thirteen-state row scan, new F value or
alphabet separation is asserted.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-exclusion--excluding-the-remaining-singleton-third-entrance-in-b1c3-mixed"></a>
### Excluding the remaining singleton third entrance in B1/C3 mixed

9 October 2026. Symbolic binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the release.

Normalize H={0,1,2}, a=3,b=4,B={4},C={0,1,5}, and singleton D={6}.
Suppose ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9 in a binary strongly connected synchronizing
automaton. H covers P5 and |P1|<=4 by the earlier established reductions.
No initial-image reachability assumption is used.

[Singleton first entrance and a covered second entrance](#problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover) gives the complete row profile:
the unique C-merging letter L has pre_L(B)=C, pre_L(C)=D and a protected
singleton as preimage of a. The other protected input maps into R=Q minus
({a,b} union C)={2,6,...,12}. F permutes {a,b} and has pre_F(C)=C.
The same proposition makes L noninjective outside C. Its C triangle and
the pair budget therefore leave exactly one outside-C block {2,q},
where q is ordinary. q cannot be 6 since L6 belongs to C and L2 to R.
Normalize q=7 and J={8,...,12}. Write E={2,q}, G=binomial(C,2) union {E}.

All seven R-input blocks of L contain an outside-H point: the other
protected input, E and the five J singletons. They inject into the eight
R targets and miss one target mu. Pulling E back under L gives an outside
pair in two steps if both endpoints are used, so mu is 2 or q.

F's restriction R->R has either singleton blocks, or the sole E block
and other singletons; any other collision would add a pair outside G.
In the latter case its seven blocks all contain outside-H points and
miss one R target nu. Pulling E under F similarly forces nu in E.
Then G contains all kernels and is backward closed under both letters:
L's preimage of C is a singleton and its preimage of E is empty at one
endpoint; F's preimage of C is C, and its preimage of E is empty at one
endpoint. The pair {a,b} outside G can never merge, contradicting
synchronization. Thus F restricts to a permutation of R.

Only input 2 among R lies in H. Pulling E under F therefore forces
F2 in E; otherwise an outside pair merges by F L. If F2=q and Fq differs
from 2, then F^2(2) is outside E. Both points of F^(-2)(E) are outside H
and merge by F^2 L, of length three. Hence Fq=2. F now permutes E, so
the same graph G is backward closed under F, and the L argument is
unchanged. Synchronization is again impossible.

The last possibility is F2=2. If mu=2, no L input maps to 2 and only
the self-loop 2F=2 enters that state, contrary to strong connectivity.
Thus mu=q. If Fq=q, the same incoming-self-loop contradiction holds at
q. Otherwise x=F^(-1)(q) differs from q and belongs to R minus {2}.
Both output points 2,x are used by L and have outside-H predecessors
y,z. Their image under L is {2,x}, under F is E, and the final L
merges them. The word L F L has length three, contradicting the cover.

All possibilities are excluded symbolically. The argument leaves F's
C map arbitrary, including singular maps, and leaves all unspecified
ordinary injections and permutations arbitrary. The independent audit
checks the full R-kernel partitions and permutations, graph closure, and
an entire small normalized row family by literal forward pair BFS.
These controls do not replace the thirteen-state symbolic argument.

This removes b1_out_c5_third2. With the earlier sole-new-point-2 proof,
B1/C3 mixed retains D={0,6},{2,6},{0,1,6},{0,2,6},{0,1,2,6}. These
are original inventory labels; the kernel partner q here is a distinct
marked point, not the singleton D point 6. Binary typed third cases
decrease to 168 with 927 letter pairs. Joint cases stay 26/43 and both
extrema stay [11,12]. No new F value or alphabet separation is asserted.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion--excluding-the-singleton-fourth-entrance-in-disjoint-b1c3d2"></a>
### Excluding the singleton fourth entrance in disjoint B1/C3/D2

9 October 2026. Conditional binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the
accepted article/release. This uses the independently proved common
singleton-fourth reduction, not any bounded solver negative.

Assume ac(S,{3})=12 and the established normalization
H={0,1,2}, B={4}, C={0,1,5}, D={2,6}, E={7}, J={7,...,12}.
All images through eleven are safe nine-sets. They contain 3,4 through
ten, meet C once through nine, D once through eight, and contain 7
through seven. Thus the images relevant below have form

    T(c,d,h)={3,4,c,d} union (J minus {h}), c in C,d in D,h in J.

Up to depth seven h is not 7. H covers P5, 3,4 are isolated in P6,
and |P1|<=4. Strong connectivity reaches any state from any nine-set
within four letters. Initial reachability of S is unnecessary here.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion--complete-extra-kernel-classification"></a>
#### Complete extra-kernel classification

Retain all 41 fourth-field pairs over all fourteen earlier row pairs.
Every pre(D) is A={3},B,C,D or E, disjoint from the earlier input cells.
The eight earlier types are 0 ABC,1 ABD,2 ACB,3 ACD,4 BAC,5 BAD,
6 BCA,7 BCD. Each pair has a C-merging letter (pre(B)=C), so its
three immediate C pairs are present. Only one additional immediate
pair is allowed. Put G=the triangle on C union the pair 26.

If both immediate kernels lie in G, G is backward closed under both
letters. Indeed pre(C) is a singleton,C or D; pre(D) is a singleton,C
or D as well. Inverse images of C-pairs and of 26 therefore add only
G-pairs, and immediate kernels add only G-pairs. Hence a pair outside
G never merges. Synchronization forces an immediate pair outside G.

All non-E-supplying letters map J bijectively to J: their six inputs
to J are exactly J, all outside H. The E-supplying letter has:

* Type 0/2/4/6: J-inputs D union (J minus {7}), seven inputs into
  six targets. Its unique pair is 2q, q in {6} union (J minus {7}).
  The extra pair outside G requires q in J minus {7}.
* Type 1/5: J-inputs C union (J minus {7}), eight inputs into six
  targets. Its kernel is the whole C block, or two blocks C minus {i}
  and {i,q}, i in {0,1},q in J minus {7}. The second case supplies
  the extra pair iq. Each of the six blocks has an outside-H input.
* Type 3/7: J-inputs one protected state union (J minus {7}), all
  six outside H, bijectively mapped to J; there is no extra pair.

These alternatives follow from the H-cover and the one-extra-pair
budget. In particular every J output, under either letter, has an
outside-H predecessor. No ordinary output permutation is fixed.

The independent complete partition inventory has 264 row-kernel
patterns and 555 compatible kernel pairs over all 41 field pairs:

| Case | Kernel pairs |
|---|---:|
| Both kernels contained in G | 210 |
| Extra 2q, both D-input cells mapped constantly | 210 |
| Extra iq, both D-input cells mapped constantly | 60 |
| Extra iq, other letter permutes D | 30 |
| Extra 2q, other letter maps C nonconstantly into D | 45 |

The table includes necessary combined output-block capacities. For iq,
the other letter has type 3/7 (constant on its D-input) or 2/6 with
pre(D)=D and a permutation of D. A second E-supplying type 2/6 would
need its own 2q pair, exceeding the budget; collapsing D also exceeds
it. For 2q, a nonconstant other letter must have type 1/5, pre(D)=C,
while its supplier has type 2/6. The table is a check of this structural
classification, not an enumeration of complete thirteen-state rows.

Throughout, pulling the extra pair under letters gives a merging word.
Two outside-H inputs merged in at most five steps contradict the cover;
a pair incident to 3 or 4 merged in at most six steps contradicts
protected-pair isolation.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion--both-letters-are-constant-on-their-d-input-cells"></a>
#### Both letters are constant on their D-input cells

Their two constants must be 2 and 6, otherwise the other D state has
no incoming transition. Let T be the letter with constant D-output 2.
Its preimage of 2 has an outside-H input y: the input cell is one of
A,B,C,D,E, each having such a point.

For an extra 2q merged by letter Z, choose an outside-H predecessor x
of q under T. The distinct pair {y,x} follows T to {2,q}, then merges
by Z. This is an outside-H pair merged within two steps.

For an extra iq merged by Z, every letter M must avoid mapping 6
or a protected state to i. Such a predecessor and an outside-H
predecessor of q would merge by M Z in two steps. Both letters in
this iq/constant case have pre(C)=D. Incoming transitions to i thus
force some M2=i. Its preimage of q either contains an input r in
J union {3,4}, or is the block C minus {i}. In the first case r has
an outside-H T-predecessor x: this was shown for J, and preimages of
3,4 are A,B or C, each containing an outside-H state. Then {y,x}
follows T M to {i,q} and merges by Z.
In the second case M is the iq-supplying type 1/5. Since T6 is in C
and is not i, choose r=T6 in C minus {i}; {y,6} has the same path.
In either case an outside-H pair merges in three steps. The complete
kernel cover guarantees both pre(C)=D in this iq/constant case.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion--extra-iq-and-a-permutation-of-d-under-the-other-letter"></a>
#### Extra iq and a permutation of D under the other letter

Let F supply/merge iq, with pre_F(C)=D,pre_F(D)=E. The other letter
L has type 2/6, pre_L(D)=D, and constant C-output delta supplied by
a protected singleton. If delta=i, its protected predecessor and an
outside-H L-predecessor of q merge by L F. If F6=i, 6 and an
outside-H F-predecessor of q merge by F F. Thus delta is not i and
F6 is not i. Incoming C targets now force F2=i,F6=beta, with
{delta,i,beta}=C.

If L swaps 2,6, pull iq first under F. When pre_F(q) contains a J
input r, choose an outside-H L-predecessor x of r; {6,x} follows
L F to {i,q}, then merges by F. Otherwise pre_F(q)=C minus {i}
contains delta; use its protected L-predecessor x instead. The first
pair is outside H and the second is protected; both merge in three
steps. Hence L fixes 2,6 pointwise.

On images through depth seven, F resets the D-coordinate to F7,
whereas L preserves it. Starting from S F, no subsequent image within
four more steps can contain the other D state. Strong connectivity
reaches that state from this nine-set within four steps, a contradiction.
If an intermediate word violates safety or the count conditions, it
already contradicts the assumptions at depth at most five.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion--extra-2q-and-a-nonconstant-map-c-into-d-under-the-other-letter"></a>
#### Extra 2q and a nonconstant map C into D under the other letter

Let L supply/merge 2q, with type 2/6 and pre_L(D)=E. Its J blocks
are {2,q}, {6}, and the singletons J minus {7,q}, bijectively mapped
to J. The other letter F has type 1/5, pre_F(C)=D,pre_F(D)=C,
and permutes J. Write delta for L's protected C-output and
g2=F2,g6=F6. Incoming C targets require {delta,g2,g6}=C.

If L7=2, 7 and an outside-H L-predecessor of q merge by L L.
Thus L7=6. If F5=2, 5 and an outside-H F-predecessor of q merge
by F L. Thus F5=6. Put W=pre_F(2), a proper nonempty subset of
{0,1}; F maps C minus W to 6.

Any image with D-coordinate 2 through depth ten must omit q:
otherwise the next L compresses it, within depth eleven. Its hole is q.
If delta is in W, every image T L F (for |word(T)|<=4) has D-coordinate
2 and hole q. Since F permutes J, T L must have the fixed hole
F^{-1}(q). A chosen outside-H L-predecessor of that state is therefore
absent from every image through depth four, contradicting reachability.
Hence delta is not in W.

If g6 is not in W, the image class d=6,c in {delta,g6} is invariant
under L,F as long as the short count conditions hold. It contains
S L and cannot reach 2 within four more steps, another contradiction.
Thus g6 is in W. Put T=S L, with c=delta,d=6 (depth one).
Its next images have

    T F:   (g6,6),
    T F F: (g6,2),
    T F F F: (g2,2).

Both last images have hole q. Since F permutes J, this forces Fq=q.
Apply L to T F F, whose D-coordinate is 2 and hole is q. The block
{2,q} is occupied and the block {6} absent, so the new hole is s=L6;
the C,D coordinates are delta,6. Two more F steps give D-coordinate
2, hence F^2(s)=q. As Fq=q and F is a permutation of J, s=q.

If g2 is in W, the outside-H pair {6,q} follows F^2 to {2,q} and
merges by L in three steps. Therefore g2 is not in W. The image
T F^4 then has C,D coordinates g2,6 and hole q (depth five). Apply
L: the block {2,q} is now absent and {6} occupied, so the new hole
is t=L2=Lq, and the C,D coordinates are delta,6. Again two F steps
give D-coordinate 2, forcing F^2(t)=q and hence t=q.

The distinct J blocks {2,q} and {6} have distinct outputs, so s is
not t. This contradicts s=t=q. The last image has depth eight; the
hole-q implication uses only one further safe L, at depth nine.
L is applied at depths four and six to inputs through depth five,
so presence of 7 through seven suffices. No count on E beyond seven
is used.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-singleton-fourth-exclusion--consequence-and-scope"></a>
#### Consequence and scope

Every singleton-fourth configuration is impossible. Together with the
previous complete exclusions of the other ten D profiles and of all
nonsingleton fourth shapes, this excludes the whole binary joint
record b1_out_c5 (B={4},C={0,1,5}). It does not exclude the joint for
larger alphabets. No new F value or numerical alphabet separation
follows; both extrema at (13,9,1) remain in [11,12].

The full immediate-kernel inventory and backward-closed G controls are
independently checked. Literal normalized row controls at smaller sizes
verify the explicit short-pair witnesses and image-prefix obstructions.
These controls use the stated local premises; they are not all-n equality
claims or a full thirteen-state transition-table enumeration.

The complete normalized smaller controls contain 111,168 assignments
at n=9 and 1,272,672 at n=10. Every explicit proof-word witness is
checked on the literal rows. The other cases use the universal graph
check, missing incoming states, strong connectivity, or independent
actual-subset prefix search. In the final thirteen-state count case,
all ordinary F permutations give 108,000 initial-hole controls; the
3,600 survivors force Fq=q. The two remaining C-coordinate alternatives
give 1,200 F^2-pair controls and 72,000 distinct L-port controls. The
four unspecified L block labels can be permuted arbitrarily: in each
L image used by this proof their blocks are all occupied, so only the
two displayed ports affect the hole.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-three-point-third-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-three-point-third-exclusion--the-three-point-overlapping-third-entrance-in-b1c3-mixed"></a>
### The three-point overlapping third entrance in B1/C3 mixed

9 October 2026. Conditional binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the release.

Suppose ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9, in a strongly connected synchronizing binary
automaton. Normalize H={0,1,2}, a=3, b=4, B={4}, C={0,1,5} and
D={0,2,6}. Put V={1,5}, J={7,...,12}, R={2,6} union J, O=V union {6}
union J. We use the established |P1|<=4, H-cover of P5, and isolation
of a,b in at least P6. For b, all safe images through depth ten contain
a,b, so ac(S,{a,b})=11, and the protected-pair bound gives P6 isolation.
Images through depth eight meet B,C,D once; they are characteristic
rows of nine-sets containing a,b. Initial reachability is unnecessary.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-three-point-third-exclusion--full-rowkernel-cover-and-eight-cores"></a>
#### Full row/kernel cover and eight cores

The private cells {4}, V and {2,6}, with the remainder meeting S at
least five times, force any outside preimage of C to be B,C or D:
its indicator in span{1,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D} has constant coefficient
zero, three Boolean private-cell coefficients, and their sum one.
Since C overlaps D, the C-merging letter L has pre_L(B)=C,
pre_L(C)={p}, p in {a,b}, with pL=delta in C. The other protected
input maps to a. F permutes a,b and has pre_F(C)=D. L maps R into R,
and F maps V union J into R. This covers all three protected row types.

The C triangle consumes three immediate pairs. On D, F is injective
or has exactly one pair 02,06,26. On its R-inputs V union J, F is
injective or has exactly one pair 15 or 1q, q in J. A triple block
would add two extra pairs; every other ordinary collision has two
outside-H endpoints. L on R is injective or has just one pair 2q,
q in R minus {2}. The combined kernel must add at most one pair to
the C triangle. Thus a non-C F pair forces L injective, except F pair
26 permits the same L pair; an F pair in D permits only injective F
R-inputs or pair 15 there. This includes all thirty split-kernel patterns.

An injective R row is bijective. A singular R row has seven blocks,
each with an outside-H input, injecting into eight R targets and
missing one. Since D is a collision clique in P2 (F L), the H-cover
forces L2 in {2,6} for injective L, or its omitted output mu in {2,6}
for singular L. Similarly, injective F has F1 in {2,6}; singular F
omits nu in {2,6}. In a singular L, mu must also lie in its extra
kernel pair, or L^2 merges an outside pair.

L has an outside predecessor of at least one of 2,6. If delta=0,
pulling a D pair under L gives an outside pair merged by L F L.
Therefore delta is in V. Likewise F has an outside predecessor of
at least one of 2,6; if F6=0, that predecessor and 6 merge by F^2 L.
Hence gamma=F6 is in V. Counting all incoming C targets now shows
that F2=0. Indeed, for injective F on D the alternative F0=0 leaves
0 with only its self-loop; pair 26 gives the same obstruction. The
other pair types directly force F2=0. The eight surviving cores are:

| D kernel | F0 | F2 | F6 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | beta | 0 | gamma | either point of V |
| 02 | 0 | 0 | gamma | beta |
| 06 | gamma | 0 | gamma | beta |

Here gamma is either point of V and beta is its other point.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-three-point-third-exclusion--singular-f-on-its-r-inputs"></a>
#### Singular F on its R-inputs

First, an extra pair 1q with q in J forces delta=gamma=5. If delta=1,
the protected L predecessor of 1 and an L predecessor of q merge by
L F, contradicting protected-pair isolation. If gamma=1, the outside
F predecessor of q and 6 merge by F^2. (q is used because nu is 2 or 6.)
Thus in this extra-pair case F is injective on D, with F0=1,F2=0,F6=5,
and L is injective on R.

For every singular F, nu=6 gives an outside pair merged by F^3 L.
If its outside predecessor x of 2 lies in J, choose an outside F
predecessor y of x: all J outputs are used. The pair {x,y} follows
F^2 to {0,2} subset D. If F5=2, use {5,6}: its second F-image is
{0,2}, because either V is a kernel block or gamma=5. Thus nu=2.

Write x for an outside F predecessor of 6. If it comes from the V
block, use delta in V in place of x when pulling back under L; in
the 1q case one may choose q or the singleton 5=delta. If L2=6 or
singular L omits 6, L has outside predecessors of 2 and of that
chosen input. Their pair follows L F to {0,6} and merges by F L.
Word L F^2 L has length four. Consequently L2=2 or mu=2.

For the extra pair 1q, these conclusions leave H with no incoming
transition from its complement under either letter: F's only H
predecessors are H inputs, and L2=2, delta=5. This contradicts strong
connectivity. The remaining singular F therefore has pair 15.
Put r=F1=F5, in {6} union J.

If F has D pair 02, L is injective. The case r=6 merges the protected
pair {2,p} by L F^2 L, so r is in J. Any nine-set T containing a,b
and meeting C,D once that contains 0 must be

  T0={a,b,0} union J.

Its F-image contains both 0 and 6, since F0=0 and the J outputs are
{6} union (J minus {r}). Thus every image through depth seven avoids
0. Strong connectivity reaches 0 from S within n-|S|=4 steps, a
contradiction.

Otherwise F0 is in V and pre_F(0)={2}. For injective L, r=6 again
merges {2,p} by L F^2 L, so r is in J. Use the graph

  G0 = binomial(C,2) union binomial(D,2) union 2*({6} union J).

For singular L use G1=G0 union 2*V; then mu=2 and F is injective on
D, while r may also be 6. Here u*T denotes unordered pairs {u,t},
t in T, u different from t. Both graphs include every direct kernel
and omit {a,b}. Under F, pre(0)={2}, pre(2)=empty, and pre(6) is a
J singleton for G0, or V/J for G1. The preimages of C are contained
in {0,6} or {2}, so all inverse distinct edges stay in the displayed
graph. Under injective L, 2 is fixed and {6} union J is permuted;
neither 2 nor an ordinary R target is adjacent to delta in G0. Under
singular L, 2 is unused and the other used G1 output vertices form
no edge. Thus each graph is backward closed under both letters.
Since it contains all kernels but omits {a,b}, synchronization fails.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-three-point-third-exclusion--injective-f-on-its-r-inputs"></a>
#### Injective F on its R-inputs

Let e=F1 in {2,6}. If e=6, an outside pair merges by F^3 L. Let x
be the outside F predecessor of 2. If x is in J, choose its outside
F predecessor y and use {x,y}, whose second image is {0,2}. If x=5,
use {5,6}; its second image is {0,F gamma}, and F gamma is 2 or 6.
Both points are in D. Hence only e=2 remains.

Now F5=r is in {6} union J. The argument pulling {2,x}, where
x=F^(-1)(6), forces L2=2 or mu=2. When x=5, use the protected
predecessor of delta instead: F delta is either 2 or 6, so the
same L F^2 L gives an outside pair if L2=6 or mu=6.

For injective L, delta=1 merges {2,p} by L F^2 L. Thus delta=5;
r=6 also merges that protected pair by the same word. Hence r is in J.

Suppose gamma=1. If r is in J, the following table covers every
possible nine-set containing a,b and meeting C,D once. Apart from
T0, it consists of a,b, one C point c in V, one D point d in {2,6},
and J minus {z} for z in J. Put x=F^(-1)(6), necessarily in J.
Each entry either fails the one-count condition or has the given form:

| input form | necessary condition | F-image form |
|---|---|---|
| T0 | F0=0 | fails (both 0,6) |
| T0 | F0=1 | (1,6), missing r |
| T0 | F0=5 | (5,6), missing r |
| (1,2), missing z | none | fails (both 0,2) |
| (1,6), missing z | z=x | (1,2), missing r |
| (5,2), missing z | z=x | T0 |
| (5,6), missing z | z different from x | (1,6), missing Fz |

If the indicated condition fails, the image has zero or two D points.
This directed form graph has no cycle; every path fails within five
F steps. That contradicts the one-count conditions through depth eight.
This argument is independent of all J permutations.

The only r=6 possibility left is singular L, which forces F injective
on D and hence F0=5. F is then the cycle (0,5,6,1,2) on those five
states and a permutation on J. Every admissible nine-set contains
one or two of the five cycle states. Across all five rotates, its
total D count is respectively 3 or 6, whereas one count at each
rotate would sum to 5. This is impossible.

Finally gamma=5. For injective L, delta=5 leaves H with no external
predecessor under either letter (F cycles 0,1,2 and L fixes 2),
contradicting strong connectivity. For singular L, F is injective on
D, F0=1, mu=2. If delta=1 and x is in J, an outside pair follows
L F to {2,6} and merges by F L, length four. If x=5, F swaps 5,6;
outside L predecessors of 1 and 6 merge by L F^3 L, length five.
Thus delta=5. The graph

  G = binomial(H,2) union { {h,o}: h in H, o in {5,6} union J }

contains all direct kernels, omits {a,b}, and is backward closed:
F preserves H and {5,6} union J, while L uses only the latter as G
output vertices. Synchronization is impossible.

All split kernels and ordinary injections/permutations are covered.
Thus D={0,2,6} is excluded at (13,9,1) for binary equality. No full
thirteen-state scan, arbitrary-alphabet exclusion, new F value or
numerical alphabet separation is asserted.

<a id="problem4-b1-mixed-c3-three-point-third-exclusion--independent-audit"></a>
#### Independent audit

The checker independently enumerates all 5 D partitions and both sets
of 4,140 R partitions. It checks all thirty compatible split-kernel

assignments for each letter's distinct R-kernel partitions. Universal

The count-form lemma is independently checked on all 13,680 parameterized
F rows and all 342,000 actual nine-set controls, including every J
permutation. Another 8,640 F rows verify the T0/zero-reachability step.
The proof, rather than these checks, keeps the ordinary outputs arbitrary.

Complete small normalized row controls contain 1,440 assignments at n=7,
18,792 at n=8 and 393,984 at n=9. Every explicit proof word, graph or
count obstruction is checked. Independent forward pair BFS and, where
needed, literal subset-prefix BFS discharge all rows under the stated

equality entrance premises hold for their smaller subset sizes; they
are not an all-n upper bound or a full thirteen-state scan.

Only D={2,6} remains in this B1/C3 mixed joint. Residual binary third
admission has 164 typed orbits and 915 letter pairs; joint counts

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-e16-exclusion--all-necessary-ordinary-row-templates"></a>

Let F supply pre_F(5)=E and L merge C to0. They are distinct because

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-e16-exclusion--gamma1-delta4"></a>

have distinct outside-K F-predecessors, since F maps its outside-K

The only remaining immediate kernels are14,16,24,26. L omits1,2 and
F omits4,6. These kernels form the four-cycle joining {1,2} to {4,6}.
Each letter image is independent in that graph, so no pair maps into

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-e16-exclusion--gamma4-delta1"></a>
#### gamma=4, delta=1

If L has a predecessor x of6, the protected pair {u,x} follows L F

{6}, and L2=Lq for a unique q in J. If q differs from6, both2,q have

Hence q=6 and L2=L6.

The outside-K ordinary F outputs are T minus {z}, z in T. If z is

So z is2 or6.

If z=6, incoming coverage of6 (which L omits) requires F2=6. F has

All cases are exhausted. No actual-prefix equality claim at another

(13,9,1), with B={0},C={1,4},D={5},E={2,4}. This is a binary-only
fourth-profile exclusion outside the article. It neither excludes the

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-e24-exclusion--necessary-row-description"></a>
#### Necessary row description

Use the proved common-fourth space of [The fourth entrance when B={0}, C={1,4}, D={5}](#problem4-b1-partial-cover-fourth).
K={1,2} covers P5, where P_h consists of pairs merged within h letters.
States0,3 are isolated in P6, and5 is isolated in P4. Thus any pair

is injective on S. Original reachable-image requirements remain in
force, although reachability is not needed in the exclusion.

Some letter F has pre_F(5)=E, while another letter L has pre_L(0)=C.
They are distinct because4 belongs to C and E. There are exactly two
letters. F has protected inputs0,3 permuting those states: pre_F(0)

L's preimage of C is a singleton u in U; write delta=Lu in C.
The other input among5 and the protected point not supplying3 maps
to5. Let J={6,...,12}, T={2} union J. L maps its eight T inputs into

T, with J injective, and is either bijective there or has exactly one

Strong connectivity requires both C targets to have incoming edges,
so {delta,gamma}=C. No higher-layer edge-count cap is used.

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-e24-exclusion--gamma4-delta1"></a>
#### gamma=4, delta=1

If F has a predecessor x of2, the protected pair {5,x} follows F^2
to a singleton, since F5=4 and F2=F4=5. This contradicts isolation
of5. Therefore F omits2. Its seven J outputs are distinct and are
exactly J, so F1=Fq for a unique q in J.

If L has a predecessor x ofq, the protected pair {u,x} follows L F
to a singleton, because Lu=1 and F1=Fq. Hence L omitsq. Its J outputs
are exactly T minus {q}; L2=Lr for a unique r in J. If r differs from
q, both2 andr have distinct L-predecessors in J. That outside-K pair
follows L^2 into a singleton, contradicting the K-cover. Thus r=q.

Only the following hard profile remains:

    L(J)=T minus {q}, L2=Lq; F(J)=J, F1=Fq.

L omits4,q, while F omits1,2. Their immediate kernels together are
the four-cycle G with edges14,24,1q,2q. Every G edge joins {1,2}
to {4,q}. Each letter image omits one whole side, hence contains no
G edge. No distinct pair maps into G under either letter, and each
immediate kernel is contained in G. Therefore G is backward closed:
the only mergeable pairs are its four edges. The automaton cannot
synchronize (for example pair03 is never merged). This covers all
ordinary permutations in this hard profile without fixing their labels.

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-e24-exclusion--gamma1-delta4"></a>
#### gamma=1, delta=4

If L has a predecessor x of2, {u,x} follows L F into a singleton,
because Lu=4 and F4=F2=5. Thus L omits2 and maps J bijectively to J,
with L2=Lq for a unique q in J.

The seven distinct F(J) outputs form T minus {z}, for some z in T.
If z is neither2 norq, the distinct outside-K F-predecessors of2,q
follow F L into a singleton. Hence z is2 orq.

If z=2, incoming coverage of state2 forces F1=2 (L already omits2).
F permutes J. Choose x in J with F^2 x=q. The protected pair {5,x}
follows F^2 L to a singleton, since F^2 5=2 and L2=Lq. Contradiction.

Now z=q, so F(J)=T minus {q}. If F1=q, let r be the J-predecessor
of2 under F. For r different fromq, choose x in J with Fx=r; then
{5,x} follows F^2 L into a singleton, since F^2 5=q and F^2 x=2.
If r=q, the port values are F1=q,Fq=2. Here a short actual-image
argument replaces a pair shortcut: pre_F(E)={q},pre_(F^2)(E)={1}.
The one-count conditions on SF and SF^2 force q,1 into S. Since S
meets C={1,4} once,4 is absent; since it meets E={2,4} once,2 is
present. But L2=Lq then collides two S states in one letter. This
contradicts safety. No guessed reachability path or multiplicity is used.

Otherwise F1=Fr for a unique r in J. If r differs fromq, a J input
x with Fx=r exists because r belongs to T minus {q}. The protected
pair {5,x} follows F^2 into a singleton: its first images are1,r and
F1=Fr. Therefore r=q. The final hard profile is

    L(J)=J, L2=Lq; F(J)=T minus {q}, F1=Fq.

Again the immediate kernels are exactly G={14,24,1q,2q}. L omits1,2,
and F omits4,q; each image is independent in G. Thus no pair maps

four-cycle obstruction prevents synchronization. All cases have failed.

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-fourth--the-effective-cover-is-k12"></a>

intersection test. Its row/kernel admission is retained as a control,

<a id="problem4-b1-partial-cover-fourth--a-common-fresh-fourth-fiber-exists-in-the-singleton-d-geometry"></a>
#### A common fresh fourth fiber exists in the singleton-D geometry

Assume the fresh third fiber is D={5}. Every image through eight
contains 3,0,5 and meets C once. For every letter ell, pre_ell(5)
meets every image through seven once. A preimage containing 3,0 or5
must be that singleton: otherwise its one-count condition omits
another point from every such image. Strong connectivity gives a
word from S to that point of length at most n-|S|=4, a contradiction.
Distinct one-count fibers are incomparable by the same argument.

Some preimage E of 5 is not one of {3},B,C,D. If all were among
these, U={3} union B union C union D would be backward closed under
every letter: the established first, second and third preimages are
already contained in U. U has only five states, is nonempty and proper,
contradicting strong connectivity. E is therefore outside {3},
incomparable with B,C,D and disjoint from the singleton sets B,D.

Local equality gives dim V7=8 and an annihilator of dimension five.
Writing h_X=9*chi_X-1, its restriction to O=Q minus {3} contains
1_O,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D,chi_E. The first four are independent. A Boolean
column in their span that meets S once has constant coefficient zero:
the remainder outside B union C union D meets S at least five times,
so it cannot belong to such a one-count fiber. On their three private
cells the other coefficients are Boolean, and their sum is one.
Thus only B,C,D are possible. Fresh E supplies a fifth independent
column, so these columns form a basis of the restricted annihilator.

Consider any other outside preimage R of 5. Its indicator is in this
five-column span. On the remainder outside B,C,D,E it is the constant
coefficient. At least four S points are in that remainder, so that
coefficient must again be zero. B,D are private singleton cells;
C minus E and E minus C are both nonempty. On these four private
cells the four remaining coefficients are Boolean. Since S meets
B,C,D,E once, their sum is one. Therefore R is one of B,C,D,E.
Every letter's preimage of 5 is consequently one of {3},B,C,D,E.
This common-E conclusion is proved for this geometry; it is not an
assumption about other third or fourth entrance configurations.

Each E is an immediate collision clique, because a letter maps E to
the singleton 5. The K-cover of P1 therefore implies |E minus K|<=1
and |E|<=3. All the ordinary-label permutations remain admitted.

<a id="problem4-b1-seventh-entrance--fresh-h-and-the-eight-column-space"></a>
#### Fresh H and the eight-column space

Every image through five meets G={8} once, so each preimage R

fiber, so pre(F) in {A,B,C,D,E,F,G}. No common sixth description
for an arbitrary different geometry is assumed. If all pre(G)
were among these known fibers, their proper nonempty eight-state
union would be backward closed. Strong connectivity therefore
supplies a fresh H outside the known fibers.

Let O=Q minus A. Equality gives dim V4=5 and annihilator dimension
eight. Its restriction to O is injective, since an annihilating
column supported on3 must vanish. It contains the eight columns
1_O,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D,chi_E,chi_F,chi_G,chi_H.
The first seven are independent: the six known fibers are disjoint
and nonempty with nonempty remainder. That remainder meets S in

coefficient zero and exactly one of its six private coefficients
equal to one; it is a known fiber. Fresh H is independent, so
the eight columns form a basis. Every outside pre(G) is a Boolean
one-count column in this span and a clique in P1, since G is a
singleton. The K={1,2} cover of P5 gives |R minus K|<=1.
