<a id="problem4-b2-four-point-second-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-b2-four-point-second-exclusion--excluding-the-b2--four-point-second-entrance"></a>
### Excluding the B2 / four-point second entrance

9 October 2026. Symbolic binary exclusion at (13,9,1), outside the release.

Assume ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9 in a binary strongly connected synchronizing
thirteen-state automaton. The established cover and pair-budget reductions
give H={0,1,2} covering P5, a=3, and |P1|<=4. We exclude the joint orbit
b2_mixed_c12, B={0,4}, C={0,1,2,5}. Initial reachability is unnecessary.
Write A={3}, W=C minus B={1,2,5}, J={7,...,12}, R={6} union J.

<a id="problem4-b2-four-point-second-exclusion--complete-third-preimage-reduction"></a>
#### Complete third-preimage reduction

Because B,C overlap, the first two entrance lemmas force the two rows M,F:

  pre_M(A)=B, pre_M(B)=A; pre_F(A)=A, pre_F(B)=C.

Here pre denotes the full inverse image, not just the inputs in S.
Each preimage of C is A or a nonempty outside one-count fiber covered
by H, as proved in [A third entrance space, without assuming a common third fiber](#problem4-third-entrance-space). Such a fiber contains at
most one point outside H. If pre_M(C)=A, M's sole C output is aM=0.
F must then provide predecessors for all three points of W. Their
F predecessors are in pre_F(C) minus pre_F(B)=pre_F(C) minus C.
If pre_F(C)=A this set has only one point, and otherwise it has at most
one point because H is contained in C. Neither can supply three distinct
targets. This contradicts the nonzero indegrees required by strong
connectivity. Thus pre_M(C) is an outside fiber D disjoint from B.
It differs from B and C; the third-space lemma makes it incomparable
with C. A point of D outside C must be a new outside-H point, normalized
as 6. The cover forbids any second outside-H point, while disjointness
from B excludes 0 and 4. Therefore, up to exchanging 1 and 2,

  D={6}, {1,6}, or {1,2,6}; and aM=4.

In these three cases all outside preimages of C are B,C or this same D.
Indeed their indicators lie in span{1,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D} on Q minus A.
The remainder has several outside-H points, so the constant coefficient
is zero. The private points 4,5,6 make the other three coefficients
Boolean. Counting on S, which meets each fiber once, makes their sum
one. This proves the common-third claim here only.

F cannot have preimage A of C since F fixes a. Preimage B is excluded
by [A forbidden backward crossing and the remaining three-point profile](#problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing). Preimage C would map all four C
inputs to B intersect C={0}, giving six immediate collision pairs.
Consequently pre_F(C)=D. If D={6}, F has no predecessor of 0 since
pre_F(B intersect C)=C intersect D is empty. M's sole B output is 4.
So 0 has no predecessor, again contradicting strong connectivity.
Only D={1,6} or {1,2,6} remains.

<a id="problem4-b2-four-point-second-exclusion--the-required-outside-predecessors-of-6"></a>
#### The required outside predecessors of 6

For D={1,6}, F maps 1 to 0 and maps 0,2,5 to 4. Together with the
M kernel pair {0,4}, its three kernel pairs exhaust the bound |P1|<=4:

  P1={{0,4},{0,2},{0,5},{2,5}}.

The inputs 4,J under F map to R. These are seven points outside H,
so F is injective there and maps them bijectively onto R. In particular
6 has an outside-H F predecessor. Under M, the eight inputs 2,5,J map
to the seven points of R. Any collision among them must be {2,5}, the
only already admitted pair in this input set. Therefore their kernel
has exactly that block and six ordinary singletons, bijective to R.
Every block contains a point outside H, so 6 also has an outside-H
M predecessor. No guessed rank or cycle type is used.

For D={1,2,6}, the R-inputs under M are 5,J, and under F are 4,J.
Each consists of seven outside-H points and must map injectively,
thus bijectively, onto R. Again 6 has an outside-H predecessor under
each row. This uses only the immediate-pair cover, independent of any
additional collision in the three D inputs.

<a id="problem4-b2-four-point-second-exclusion--short-pair-contradiction-or-backward-closure"></a>
#### Short-pair contradiction or backward closure

Put U=D intersect H, so U={1} or {1,2}. The third-space lemma makes
D a clique in P3. If either row L sends 6 to u in U, choose an
outside-H predecessor q of 6 under that same row. The points 6,q
are distinct since 6L=u differs from qL=6. Their image pair {u,6}
lies in D and merges in at most three further steps. Thus {6,q} is
an uncovered pair in P4, contrary to H covering P5. Explicitly the
four-letter word L M F M merges it: L takes it into D, M into C,
F into B, and the last M into {a}.

It follows that neither row sends 6 into U. But the only predecessors
of U under either row now lie in U: M sends its D inputs into W,
its A input to 4, B to a, and all remaining inputs into R. F sends
C intersect D to 0, C minus D to 4, the sole D minus C input 6 into W,
A to a and all remaining inputs into R. Neither 0,4,a,R nor 6 can
therefore enter U. A nonempty proper U with no incoming transition
from its complement contradicts strong connectivity. This excludes
both remaining profiles and completes the joint-orbit exclusion.

The argument is symbolic and binary. No solver negative, incomplete
scan, native histogram or reachable-image cutoff is used as proof.
The independent audit enumerates the abstract kernel partitions,
literal third-fiber geometry and the finite core alternatives.
With the earlier B3 exclusions, binary joint cases decrease from 29
to 28; all 43 unrestricted joint cases remain admitted. Both extrema
at (13,9,1) remain in [11,12]. No new F value is asserted.

<a id="problem4-b3-inverse-clique-maximal-graph"></a>
<a id="problem4-b3-inverse-clique-maximal-graph--inverse-clique-constraints-and-the-maximal-allowed-transition-graph-for-b3"></a>
### Inverse-clique constraints and the maximal allowed transition graph for B3

This is a conditional arbitrary-alphabet audit at(13,9,1),ac=12.
It excludes additional normalized third geometries, not a numerical
extremum. The accepted article and supplement are unchanged.

<a id="problem4-b3-inverse-clique-maximal-graph--known-pair-edges-and-the-global-immediate-graph"></a>
#### Known pair edges and the global immediate graph

Existing premises give H={0,1,2} covering P5, |P1|<=4, and
B={0,1,4} a triangle in P1. Thus the actual P1 graph is that
triangle, possibly with one additional edge. Enumerate every such
edge covered by H and disjoint from the literal mandatory core J.
The intersection J of all admissible nine-sets is mandatory through8
and P7-isolated. Current surviving B3 geometries have J disjoint H.

Let G be the union of this proposed immediate graph and the cliques
on C and D. G is contained in P3: C is a two-step clique and D a
three-step clique. No higher-layer edge-count cap is used.

For every actual letter f, two necessary inverse conditions follow:

1. f(Q minus H) is an independent set of G. Otherwise an edge of
   G between two such distinct outputs lifts to a P4 edge outside H.
2. Every f(j),j in J, is isolated in the graph induced by G on Qf.
   A distinct available neighbor would lift to a P4 pair incident
   to j, contradicting J isolation. Immediate collisions touching J
   are separately prohibited by the exact kernel restriction.

All letter kernels are clique unions contained in the proposed P1.
Every block has at most one point outside H. No nontrivial block
meets J. Consequently f is injective on Q minus H, and each kernel
quotient block has one of three types: an outside input not in J,
a singleton J input, or a block wholly contained in H. Each block
also has its input membership atom for pre(A),pre(B),pre(C).

<a id="problem4-b3-inverse-clique-maximal-graph--exact-realization-of-a-constrained-letter"></a>
#### Exact realization of a constrained letter

Assign each output state a colour:0 if omitted,1 if it receives an
outside non-J block,2 if it receives a J block,3 if it receives an
H-only block. Outputs in colours1/2 must be independent in G, and
a colour2 output may have no positive-coloured neighbor. In each
output membership atom, the counts of each positive colour must
equal the corresponding input quotient-block counts. These conditions
are necessary and sufficient for the given exact field/kernel and
the two inverse conditions: independently biject the blocks of each
atom/type to the outputs of that atom/colour. Distinct blocks use
distinct outputs, and all required inverse restrictions then hold.

The generator colours only nonisolated vertices of G and keeps
per-atom counts. Isolated outputs can fill the remaining type quotas
iff all remaining counts are nonnegative and their sum fits the
number of isolated outputs in that atom. For a given active count
signature, record every colour that each active output can take in
any colouring with that signature. Every isolated output can receive
a type exactly when its leftover quota is positive. This determines
all possible input/output arrows exactly for this one-letter domain.
Colour correlations are unnecessary for a single arrow: field/kernel
feasibility depends only on the signature, so every colouring counted
in its marginal is admissible and the atom/type bijection can send
the specified block to that output.

Only three guard inputs exist. Since the immediate graph is a
triangle plus at most one edge, every kernel has rank loss at most3:
at worst a three-state block and a disjoint pair. The generator may
therefore limit omitted outputs and H-only blocks to three. This is
a kernel-graph consequence, not a new cap on later pair graphs.

The independent checker instead enumerates literal output sets:
choose a ten-state independent set I for f(Q minus H), a subset T
of its three-state complement for images of H-only blocks, and a
|J|-subset L of I consisting of vertices isolated in G[I union T].
The colours are2 on L,1 on I minus L,3 on T and0 elsewhere. It
matches full per-atom quotas and reconstructs all possible arrows.
This enumerates exactly the same letter domain without active-core
colouring, unused-output cancellation, or generator imports.

<a id="problem4-b3-inverse-clique-maximal-graph--arbitrary-alphabets-and-strong-connectivity"></a>
#### Arbitrary alphabets and strong connectivity

For each proposed global P1 graph retain every allowed field/kernel,
including every Boolean companion. The actual alphabet must supply
pre(A)=B,pre(B)=C,pre(C)=D; suppliers may coincide. If a supplier is
absent from this larger allowed domain, that class is impossible.

Take the union of all arrows over every allowed letter in the class.
Every actual alphabet's transition graph is a subgraph of this maximal
graph. If some state's reachable set in the maximal graph is proper,
the actual automaton cannot be strongly connected. The stored closed
set is a direct certificate: no allowed arrow leaves it. If the
maximal graph is strongly connected, no realization follows; selecting
an alphabet, further pair/image flags, synchronization and S reachability
are still required. There is no reduction to a bounded alphabet size.

The proposed extra P1 edge need not be used by the retained letters;
this is not imposed for the overapproximation. Every true P1 graph
is among the enumerated classes, so a complete absence of surviving
classes excludes the geometry conservatively. All earlier excluded
geometries remain historical premises, and binary B3 remains excluded.

All sets, kernel partitions, output colours, quota equations, possible
arrows and closed-set witnesses commute with state relabelling that
preserves H,A,B,C. Thus canonical rejection excludes its entire labelled
D orbit. The intact third inventory supplies complete orbit counts;
the checker additionally constructs each within-cell permutation and
verifies the transported mandatory family and closed-set certificates.

<a id="problem4-b3-staircase-flag-exclusion--an-actual-staircase-basis-for-the-equality-flag"></a>
#### An actual staircase basis for the equality flag

Let V_i span the rows chi(Sw) for words of length at most i. The frozen
equality lemma gives dim V_i=i+1 for 0<=i<=11. All these words are safe,
so the rows are characteristic nine-set rows containing 3. There are
actual images R_0=S,R_1,...,R_11 such that R_(i+1)=R_i f_i and
{chi(R_0),...,chi(R_i)} is a basis of V_i.

Inductively, suppose this holds through i<11. For j<i and every letter f,
chi(R_j) D_f belongs to V_(j+1), hence to V_i. If every chi(R_i) D_f also
belonged to V_i, then V_i would be invariant under every letter and the
span would stabilize. Strong connectivity and synchronization instead
give limiting span R^13. Thus some R_i f lies outside V_i. It is a safe
actual image of depth i+1, and adjoining it gives a basis of V_(i+1).
Every actual alphabet therefore admits at least one enumerated staircase.
The alphabet must supply each chain step; suppliers can coincide.

For every letter and every j<i, its image of R_j lies in the already
specified prefix span V_(j+1). At a search node with basis through R_i,
first require every remaining letter's image of R_i to be safe at depth
i+1. Enumerate every possible such image outside V_i as R_(i+1), and
retain every letter whose image of R_i lies in the enlarged span.
If no candidate exists, or a required supplier/chain-step domain is empty,
or the maximal remaining transition graph is not strongly connected, the
node cannot contain an actual witness. No invariant-image-family assumption
or reduction to a bounded alphabet size is made.

This negative search does not assert that safe images of a basis alone
make every word safe, nor that a surviving flag realizes an automaton.
Actual alphabets are subalphabets of the enumerated domains at each node;
this containment suffices for the exclusions.

<a id="problem4-b3-staircase-flag-exclusion--complete-initial-domains-and-safe-image-tests"></a>
#### Complete initial domains and safe-image tests

Use the frozen immediate-graph/entrance-fiber premises. Q={0,...,12},
H={0,1,2}, A={3}, B={0,1,4}. All first images are S or one common T.
All second images lie in one common plane; the independent prefix audit

b3_mixed_c8_third1. Every surviving plane has exactly three feasible cube

The complete letter pool for this prefix retains all frozen fields/kernels,

It imposes the frozen inverse-clique conditions, including J isolation.
The generator enumerates full output colours and every atom/type bijection,

At every later depth d<=11 a safe image must have cardinality9 and contain3.

<a id="problem4-b3-staircase-flag-exclusion--symmetry-and-exact-linear-algebra"></a>
#### Symmetry and exact linear algebra

All prefix planes in this selected scope are enumerated before quotienting.
Transport C8's extra edge {2,q} to {2,6} by swapping the two outside states
q,6, which preserves H,A,B,C,D. Then sort state columns within cells having
the same membership in H,A,B,C,D and the extra edge, using their ordered
membership in S,T,R. This gives eight C1 and two C8 canonical prefixes.
The checker verifies each literal transport is bijective, preserves every
control set, carries the immediate/known graph correctly, and carries each
field's complete kernel-mask catalogue to the canonical catalogue. Thus the
exact constrained letter pools and all flag rejections transport too.
Labelled D orbits are already exhaustive in the frozen third inventory;
within-cell state relabelling transports all new image/flag conditions.

The generator computes row ranks and characteristic-row span membership
over F_p, p=1000000007. This is exact for the matrices used here: every row
is a characteristic nine-set row. Every square minor has absolute determinant
at most 3^13=1594323 by Hadamard's inequality (restricted row norm at most3).
A nonzero minor cannot vanish modulo p. Hence every real rank, including
the augmented rank for a candidate characteristic row, equals its F_p rank.
All rows have sum9, so row-span membership among nine-set rows is equivalent
to affine-span membership. The independent checker uses rational elimination,
literal labelled-map images, and an independently built transition graph.

The tree stores every possible next basis image, the full remaining-domain
digest and size, required-group checks, and a specific proper closed set for
SC rejections. The checker rebuilds every node and branch, so no timeout or
sampled negative supports the cut. Rejection occurs already using safety at
depths at most5; no full equality-flag realization is claimed. Complete small
controls check rank equivalence and letter-domain reconstruction.

<a id="problem4-b3-third-cover"></a>
<a id="problem4-b3-third-cover--completing-b3-third-admission-for-the-known-cover-cut"></a>
### Completing B3 third admission for the known-cover cut

9 October 2026. Investigation only, at (n,s,r)=(13,9,1) and conditional
on ac(S,{3})=12. This uses the existing compression bound and established
entrance flag; it gives no new extremal value. All statements here hold
for arbitrary finite alphabets. Binary B3 joints were already excluded;
this inventory does not reopen them.

<a id="problem4-b3-third-cover--necessary-admission-without-a-common-third-fiber-assumption"></a>
#### Necessary admission, without a common-third-fiber assumption

Use H={0,1,2}, Q={0,...,12}, a=3, O=Q minus {3}. The established
joint inventory has fourteen cases with |B|=3. [A third entrance space, without assuming a common third fiber](#problem4-third-entrance-space)
shows that a fresh third entrance D can be selected with:

* D is nonempty, disjoint from {3}, with at most one point outside H;
* D is incomparable with B and with C;
* |B union C union D|<=6;
* 1,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D restricted to O have rank four;
* an actual nine-state image contains 3 and meets B,C,D once each.

Every actual image through depth eight satisfies the last condition.
Enumerate ALL nine-sets satisfying it, not only reachable subsets of a
particular guessed transition table. Their intersection X is therefore
contained in every actual image through depth eight. This direction is
essential: a larger candidate family weakens the intersection, and cannot
create a false mandatory point.

For each D retain every covered, nonempty Boolean fiber R in the span of
1,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D, whose count on the initial nine-set is one and which
is either one of B,C,D or incomparable with each distinct such fiber.
The count of the constant term on O is eight, not nine. These fibers
can coexist; none is discarded to assert that preimages of C share a
single fresh D. Requiring these span fibers to have count one does not
shrink the enumerated family: this follows identically from the three
one-count equations and the eight outside coordinates.

Permutations inside the eight membership cells of (H,B,C) classify D.
The signature lists its chosen cardinality in each cell. This is a
complete stabilizer-orbit invariant; the orbit size is the product of
the corresponding binomial coefficients. The full fourteen-case
inventory has 127 geometric orbits and 827 labelled D choices; 18
orbits have extra Boolean fibers. Its three cases previously inventoried
in third_entrance_inventory.json coincide exactly, including all extra
fibers (36 orbits, 188 labelled choices).

<a id="problem4-b3-third-cover--two-additional-arbitrary-alphabet-third-profile-exclusions"></a>
#### Two additional arbitrary-alphabet third-profile exclusions

The known floor from [A compression-bound floor for short-pair covers](#problem4-compression-cover-floor) prohibits a cover Z of
P_h when |Q minus Z|>=2 and binomial(|Z|+2,2)<=h. For each point x of
a set X contained in every safe image through eight, ac(S,{x})>=9.
The previously proved protected-pair inequality ac(S,{x})<=4+d_{x}
gives d_{x}>=5. Each such singleton is a proper subset of the nine-set
S; no bound for a protected set equal to S is needed. Thus X is
isolated in P4. Since H covers P5, it also covers P4; H minus X still
covers P4. A remainder of size zero or one is impossible by the known
compression theorem (bound one or three, respectively, both <=4).
The auxiliary complement need not be a reachable image; the original S
retains the paper's reachable-image requirement.

Exactly two new B3 third orbits fail this test:

| joint | B | C | D | X | H minus X | labelled D choices |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| b3_mixed_c4 | {0,1,4} | {2,4} | {0,2} | {1,2,3} | {0} | 2 |
| b3_mixed_c6 | {0,1,4} | {0,2} | {2,4} | {1,2,3} | {0} | 1 |

Both rows give the SAME Boolean equations, in a different order:

    x0+x1+x4=1, x2+x4=1, x0+x2=1.

Subtracting the last two gives x0=x4, hence 2*x0+x1=1.
Boolean coordinates force x0=x4=0 and x1=x2=1. Therefore states 1,2
are mandatory through eight. Removing them from H leaves {0}, which
would cover P4. The known three-letter compression of Q minus {0}
produces a pair outside {0} in P3, hence in P4, a contradiction.
Each canonical row has 28 candidate nine-sets. Neither row has extra
Boolean fibers; all extra fibers of the other eighteen orbits remain.

These exclusions remove third profiles, NOT their whole joints: each
of the two joints retains other geometries under this particular cut.
The other 125 B3 third orbits are merely not excluded by this test;
no transition-table existence or sufficiency is asserted.

<a id="problem4-b3-third-cover--audit-and-scope"></a>
#### Audit and scope

The generator uses exact rational rank and span coefficients. The
independent checker imports no generator code. It enumerates literal
bit masks for all nine-sets, all covered D choices and all candidate
covered R fibers, checks rank over F_101, verifies each labelled-family
intersection, orbit cardinality, span fiber and historical cross-check.
For matrices with at most five Boolean columns, every square minor has
absolute value <101 by Hadamard's inequality (at most 5^(5/2)); thus
the modular rank test is equivalent to rational rank. No numerical
floating-point rank or solver timeout is used.

Together with the intact B1/B2 inventory there are 362 geometric orbits
and 2,309 labelled D choices. The known-cover intersection cut excludes
13 of these orbits: eleven earlier B1/B2 and two B3. There remain 224
B1/B2 plus 125 B3, or 349 unrestricted geometric orbits under these
cuts. This is a necessary-condition count, not 349 automata. Unrestricted

Run python -B enumerate_b3_third_cover.py and then

It is kept outside the accepted paper's 109-file supplement.

<a id="problem4-b3-two-image-plane"></a>
<a id="problem4-b3-two-image-plane--two-safe-images-and-the-common-depth-two-plane-in-b3"></a>
### Two safe images and the common depth-two plane in B3

This is a conditional arbitrary-alphabet exclusion at (n,s,r)=(13,9,1),
assuming ac(S,A)=12. It proves no numerical value of F and does not change
the accepted partial-answer article. The scope file selects 28 of the 35
current B3 geometries. Every global immediate graph still retained in
each selected geometry is tested; none is sampled or bounded by alphabet
size. Previously rejected graphs retain their earlier certificates.

<a id="problem4-b3-two-image-plane--premises-and-exhaustive-image-families"></a>
#### Premises and exhaustive image families

Use the frozen inverse-clique certificate and its notation:
Q={0,...,12}, H={0,1,2}, A={3}, B={0,1,4}, the literal mandatory core J,
and G=P1_candidate union K_C union K_D, a known subgraph of P3.
The actual immediate graph is the B triangle, possibly with one covered
extra edge avoiding J. Its allowed fields/kernels and inverse constraints
are exactly the frozen one-letter domain. In particular every letter is
injective on Q-H, sends Q-H to an independent set of G, and sends J to
vertices isolated in G on all available outputs.

Every image of S at depth at most two has nine states, contains A and
meets B,C,D once. These one-count statements hold through depths 10,9,8
respectively in the earlier entrance-fiber premises. Such an image is
independent in G: a G edge inside an image at depth at most two would
compress S by a word of total length at most 2+3=5, contradicting 12.
Enumerate all nine-subsets with these conditions. No S reachability
restriction is imposed, which enlarges the domain for a negative proof.

The equality flag gives affine dimensions one and two at depths one
and two. Consequently there is a common T != S and every letter sends
S to S or T. Some letter sends S to T. All second images are S,T or
T f; some T f lies outside {S,T}. They lie in one common affine plane.
We do not require any invariance of T or of this plane under letters.

Any three distinct Boolean vectors are affinely independent (a line has
at most two cube vertices). A plane contains at most four cube vertices:
project injectively to two coordinates with independent restricted
linear parts. If there are four vertices, their projection is the full
Boolean square; every other Boolean-valued affine coordinate on this
square is constant, one coordinate, or its complement. Thus they form
a parallelogram. For S,T and a third feasible R, every possible fourth
vertex is one of S+T-R, S+R-T, T+R-S, when Boolean. Retain only feasible
vertices, and deduplicate the resulting plane intersections. This lists
every possible actual depth-two image family. The independent verifier
instead tests affine dependence by two pivot coordinates and exact
integer determinants, without this parallelogram construction.

<a id="problem4-b3-two-image-plane--exact-two-image-letter-domain"></a>
#### Exact two-image letter domain

Fix an exact kernel partition pi, a frozen field (preA,preB,preC), input
images S,T, and proposed output images U,V. Both input sets are independent
in the candidate P1, so each kernel block contains at most one point of
each. Give a block two membership bits indicating whether it meets S,T.
Give an output state bits indicating membership in U,V. A bijection from
kernel blocks to the available outputs realizes f(S)=U and f(T)=V exactly
if it respects these two bits. This uses the saturation of each input set
by whole kernel blocks, not pointwise S/T membership of a representative.
The selected blocks number nine and map bijectively onto all nine desired
outputs. Blocks not meeting a set cannot map into its output image.

Together with the three entrance-fiber membership bits and the three
block types (outside non-J, J, wholly H), this gives 32 output atoms and
96 type quotas. The frozen inverse graph conditions are imposed using
output colours 0=omitted, 1=outside non-J, 2=J, 3=wholly H. Equality of
every atom/type count is necessary and sufficient: independently biject
the blocks and outputs within each class. The possible arrows are exactly
the union of outputs of the appropriate atom/type over feasible colourings.
This bijection argument also applies to the first-image domain using
one additional bit. The generator enumerates literal full colourings;
the checker colours only nonisolated graph vertices with quota bounds
and fills isolated outputs by their residual atom quotas. Their exact
arrow-domain digests are compared, including existence and supplier flags.
Packed generator quotas use four bits per count; each count is at most
13, so no carry can occur. The checker uses unpacked counts.

<a id="problem4-b3-two-image-plane--conservative-alphabet-exclusion"></a>
#### Conservative alphabet exclusion

First, for each ordered S,T, union all allowed S->S and S->T letters.
Reject only if no moving letter exists, some required supplier is absent,
or this maximal graph is not strongly connected. The remaining pairs are
tested against every feasible common plane. For a plane, take the union
of all letters with f(S) in {S,T} and f(T) in that plane. Reject if a
moving letter is absent, no second-dimension letter exists, some supplier
preA=B,preB=C,preC=D is absent, or the maximal graph is not strongly
connected. Supplier and dimension letters can coincide; no independence
assumption or fixed alphabet size is used. Any actual alphabet is a
subalphabet of this maximal domain. Hence a proper reachable closed set
in the maximal graph prevents actual strong connectivity. The converse
is never asserted. Earlier feasible first-image pairs and plane domains
are overapproximations, not attaining automata.

The checker verifies all selected canonical geometries, all still-retained
global graphs, all ordered feasible S,T, and all plane intersections. All
operations commute with within-cell permutations preserving H,A,B,C; the
complete frozen D-orbit inventory already verifies those transports and
exhaustiveness. Thus rejection of a canonical geometry rejects its labelled
D orbit. The new literal small-state controls independently compare exact
two-image arrow domains against labelled maps. The certificate includes
the frozen premises, new source/data, hashes, and isolated regeneration.

The original F conjecture is already refuted at (11,8,1). This additional
conditional B3 exclusion does not settle F(13,9,1), prove alphabet
separation, or strengthen any published theorem.

<a id="problem4-basis-column-reaching-pruning"></a>
<a id="problem4-basis-column-reaching-pruning--prefix-column-consequences-of-strong-connectivity"></a>
### Prefix-column consequences of strong connectivity

This note supplies necessary conditions, not a new value of F. Its intended
application is the remaining equality flags at (n,s,r)=(13,9,1), target 12.
It does not assume two letters or require the initial subset to be reachable.

Let an n-state complete automaton be strongly connected and synchronizing.
Fix S of size s>=2, set m=n-s, and let c(S) be its shortest compression length.
For distinct p,q let d(p,q) be their shortest merging length.

<a id="problem4-basis-column-reaching-pruning--reaching-and-cooccurrence"></a>
#### Reaching and cooccurrence

Every state q can be reached from some state of S in at most m letters:
take a shortest directed path from S to q. Its vertices after its initial
vertex are distinct and outside S, so there are at most n-s of them.

If p in Su implies q in Su for every word u of length at most m, then

    d(p,q) >= c(S)-m.

Indeed choose such a prefix reaching p. It also puts q in the image. If
that prefix has already compressed S, then c(S)<=m and the assertion is
immediate. Otherwise append a shortest merging word for p,q. The result
compresses S and has length at most m+d(p,q). This proves the inequality.
The implication hypothesis is a statement about actual images, not about
an arbitrarily chosen list of test subsets. Synchronization ensures the
finite distances used here exist; the reaching argument uses strong
connectivity. No optimality claim or priority claim is made for this lemma.

<a id="problem4-basis-column-reaching-pruning--exact-column-identities-of-a-full-prefix-span"></a>
#### Exact column identities of a full prefix span

Use right actions and the transformation matrix D_w defined in the paper.
The row x_w=chi_S D_w counts trajectories and has total s even after
collisions. Let V_i=span_R{x_w: |w|<=i}, and let R_0,...,R_t be any basis
consisting of actual prefix rows and spanning V_i, with i>=m.

* A zero column in every basis row would be zero throughout V_i. Reaching
  that state from S by a word of length at most m contradicts this. Hence
  every column occurs in at least one basis row.
* Equal distinct columns p,q throughout the basis are equal throughout
  V_i. Equal nonnegative trajectory counts imply simultaneous membership
  of p,q in every actual image through m. Thus d(p,q)>=c(S)-m.
* If column j is 1 in every basis row, then x_j=(sum_q x_q)/s throughout
  V_i, since every basis row has total s. Every actual prefix through m
  consequently contains j. For ANY q!=j choose a prefix reaching q;
  j is also present. The same argument gives d(j,q)>=c(S)-m. This is
  precisely the previously audited mandatory-core isolation lemma.

These deductions use only linear equalities. Columnwise inequalities on
basis rows do NOT extend to their real linear span. For example the
weight-two rows 1100,0110,0011 all satisfy p=>q for p=0,q=1, but their
linear combination 1100-0110+0011=1001 does not. Do not add implication
rules inferred only from basis inequalities.

<a id="problem4-basis-column-reaching-pruning--letter-domain-consequences-at-the-remaining-parameter"></a>
#### Letter-domain consequences at the remaining parameter

At (13,9,1) and ac(S,{3})=12, c(S)>=12 and m=4. Thus the equal-column
pairs and all pairs touching a constant-one column have merging distance
at least eight. Let G be any verified subgraph of P3 (pairs merging within
three letters). For every actual letter f:

1. An equal-column pair p,q has f(p)!=f(q) and {f(p),f(q)} not in G.
   Otherwise it merges in one letter, or in at most 1+3=4 letters.
2. For a constant-one column j and every other input q, the same conditions
   hold. Equivalently f(j) is distinct from all other input images and
   isolated in the induced G graph on the FULL output set Qf.

Therefore each equal-column class has an injective G-independent image,
and every constant-one column obeys full-output isolation. These are
necessary restrictions on EACH letter of an arbitrary finite alphabet.

A dynamic mandatory point in the existing P5 cover H can also be stripped:
it is P7-isolated, hence incident to no P5 edge. If the remaining cover
has size at most one, the previously proved compression-cover floor
excludes the branch. A program applying this additional rule must bind
and check that earlier floor proof independently; it is not implemented
merely by asserting that a cover looks small.

Apply column deductions only to a basis spanning the entire actual V_i,
not just independent safe rows. The audited equality-flag theorem gives
dim V_i=i+1 for i<=11. A complete staircase branch that establishes its
i+1 actual independent prefix rows and constrains all preceding row
images to the branch span meets this premise. No safety or characteristic
row assumption at depth 12 is made. All finite tests are controls of this
paper proof; they are not extrapolated to an all-parameter formula.

<a id="problem4-binary-field-flag"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-field-flag--full-local-equality-flag-over-the-two-element-field"></a>
### Full local equality flag over the two-element field

8 October 2026. A synthesis encoding, not a new extremal value. The word
"binary" in the title refers to F2, not the alphabet; any finite alphabet
is allowed. The encoding here requires odd s=|S| and target t=n-r.

<a id="problem4-binary-field-flag--necessary-flags"></a>
#### Necessary flags

For a genuine strongly connected synchronizing witness ac(S,A)=n-r=t,
the span chain V_i of the trajectory rows over F2 has dim V_i=i+1 for
0<=i<=t-1. The proof is the same as [Equality flags for the avoid-or-compress bound](#problem4-local-equality-flag): safe rows are
characteristic rows of odd-size sets containing A, so each lies in the
homogeneous subspace x_q=sum x for q in A. This has codimension r, since
r<s<=n and a coordinate outside A exists. Reset words to all states give
the rows s e_q=e_q over F2, so V_infinity=F2^n. A plateau stabilizes
forever. Strict growth between dimension one and at most t therefore has
increments exactly one. This argument would fail for even s and is not
used in that case.

There is one word whose consecutive prefix rows form a basis of each V_i.
Start with v0=chi_S. Suppose its prefix rows v0,...,vi form a basis of Vi.
Every vj D_ell with j<i belongs to V_(j+1) subset Vi. If all vi D_ell also
belonged to Vi, that space would be invariant under all letters, impossible
while proper. Choose a letter for which vi D_ell is outside Vi and set
v_(i+1) to that row. It is the next prefix row and extends the basis.
All these rows are safe characteristic vectors through t-1.

For every i<=t-2 and every original letter ell, v_i D_ell is an F2-linear
combination of v0,...,v_(i+1). The prefix basis has r common coordinates,
namely A. The optional --binary-field-flag in synthesize_potential.py encodes:

* v0 is the selected initial s-set;
* each vi is an s-set, and v_(i+1)=vi ell for some original letter;
* the common intersection of all t basis sets has at least r states;
* every vi ell, i<=t-2, is an XOR combination of v0,...,v_(i+1).

Coefficients are independent Booleans for each i and letter. No input
letter is fixed to be a permutation or to have a particular kernel.
Every genuine equality witness with odd s admits this encoding. Selecting
the prefix word is existential, with no chosen-word pattern restriction.

<a id="problem4-binary-field-flag--sufficiency-in-combination-with-the-pair-potential"></a>
#### Sufficiency in combination with the pair potential

The independent lower pair potential still imposes compression length
at least t on S: every initial pair has phi=t, phi is zero on diagonals,
and every letter decreases phi by at most one. Hence every word of length
at most t-1 preserves s points. In particular all encoded basis and basis
successor images in this range are injective, so their set-image bit masks
equal the actual trajectory rows over F2. Using set images for a colliding
row would be incorrect; the compression certificate is what permits it.

The encoded relations imply by induction that every prefix row at depth
i<=t-1 lies in span(v0,...,vi). At a common protected coordinate, every
basis row has value one and total parity one. Any linear combination thus
has that coordinate equal to its total parity. Every actual trajectory
row has odd total s and, by the compression certificate, is characteristic.
The protected coordinate equals one and is present. Thus all words shorter
than t are safe for any r-set selected from the common intersection.

This proves local value at least t for the chosen S, before checking S
reachability. Strong connectivity and synchronization then give the known
upper t, so equality follows once the independent ordinary BFS confirms
all structural requirements. Unreachable chosen S does not yield a lower
witness for the manuscript; the solver checks all actual s-images of the
same automaton before blocking its rows.

The full flag does not substitute for the pair potential, and even s is
not admitted. The source checks every positive basis word and exact real
row independence, then recomputes the full avoid-or-compress value using
ordinary subset BFS. A timeout or uncertified UNSAT still is not an upper
bound or a complete solution.

<a id="problem4-binary-field-flag--boolean-counterexample-refinement-implementation"></a>
#### Boolean counterexample refinement implementation

`synthesize_flag_boolean.py` uses exact one-hot transitions and Boolean
XOR relations, with no pair potential or prescribed letter ranks. It
explicitly requires every encoded basis successor to preserve s points;
this makes its set-image relation equal the F2 trajectory relation.
The sufficiency argument above then applies once compression >=t has
been verified independently: those verified short trajectory rows are
also characteristic vectors. Independence of the encoded basis is not
needed for this implication; omitting it may enlarge the search space.

Each proposed model is checked by ordinary pair and subset BFS. A shortest
compression word shorter than t is excluded by imposing size s on its
successive images. A nonmergeable pair trap is excluded by requiring an
immediate collision or an outgoing pair transition from that trap. Both
cuts are necessary for a genuine witness. If the selected initial set
is unreachable, the implementation checks all actual size-s images of
the same automaton before excluding that entire transition table. Every
accepted positive is verified again using `alphabet_check.verify`.
The fixed n13,s7,r1 cofinal control attains twelve. The n13,s9,r1 general
binary and cycle-branch searches timed out at their first SAT call;
neither supplies a negative certificate. Cycle-branch impossibility is
established separately by the complete six-image lemma, not the solver.

The newer --cover-by-images option replaces the complete pair-transition
table by literal images of I={m-1,...,n-1}. Requiring every word through
depth h to preserve |I| is exactly the absence of P_h edges in I, hence
exactly the stated canonical (m-1)-vertex cover. No edge-count bound is
introduced by this alternative encoding.

The --no-flag mode is a separate ordinary avoid-or-compress CEGIS and
does not require odd s. It selects an explicit protected singleton and
does not encode any F2 span. Each proposed automaton and S is checked by
ordinary BFS for a short word compressing S OR omitting that singleton.
Such a word and all its prefixes are excluded by imposing size s and
presence of the protected state. Thus the full local value is checked
directly, not inferred from a compression-only check. Positives still
require reachability and all structural properties.

Optional common-predecessor and protected-isolation restrictions come
from [A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag) and [A common predecessor fiber at singleton equality](#problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag). At (13,9,1)
the protected state can be normalized outside the three-vertex cover;
the former inside-cover slice is redundant by relabeling, not empty by
itself. An optional decreasing unsigned rank for every unordered pair
certifies synchronization: a pair either collides immediately or has a
letter image of strictly smaller rank. Actual distances minus one fit
the allocated bits and admit every synchronizing automaton.

--resume replays verified necessary short-word and pair-trap constraints
from a compatible previous run. It records the previous output and source
hashes and refuses to replay whole-transition-table exclusions, which
would need their image audits rerun. The new outside-cover no-flag run
generated 69 candidates and learned four safe prefix constraints plus
66 nonmergeable-pair trap cuts, then timed out. A resumed run with the
additional synchronization rank and depth-two isolation also timed out.
Both are diagnostic, not negative certificates. Known n11 and n12
controls pass the new restrictions and ordinary verification; the n12
control tests the new equality boundary of the m>=4 span refinement.

<a id="problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion--a-binary-exclusion-for-an-entrance-with-one-new-point"></a>
### A binary exclusion for an entrance with one new point

9 October 2026. Conditional structural result only, outside the release.
No extremal value, unrestricted-alphabet exclusion or priority is claimed.

<a id="problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion--proposition"></a>
#### Proposition

Let a binary strongly connected synchronizing automaton have
ac(S,{a})=t=n-1, with s=|S|>=5. Let B,C be the two common entrance
fibers. It is impossible that B covers all immediate collision pairs
and, for some k>=3,

  |B|=k, |C minus B|=1, 0<|B intersect C|<k.

In the thirteen-state inventory this excludes both binary orbits
b3_in_c2 and b3_in_c3, B={0,1,2}, C={0,4} or {0,1,4}. The two-point-C
case also has the separate explicit proof in [A binary exclusion with a three-point entrance cover](#problem4-binary-three-cover-overlap).
Two of the 43 geometric joint orbits are excluded for binary automata.
No unrestricted orbit is excluded by these proofs.

<a id="problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Write U=B intersect C, V=B minus C, and C minus B={c}. Both U and V
are nonempty. A letter M
with preimage B of a cannot have preimage B or C of B, since those
preimages intersect B while the output sets {a} and B are disjoint.
It therefore has preimage {a} of B. The other letter F must use C
as preimage of B and must have preimage {a} of a. Put beta=aM in B.
Thus M maps B to a and has no other predecessor of a, while F fixes a.

The kernel cover makes M injective on Q minus B. Consequently equal
M-images of sets meeting B once have identical parts outside B.

Every image through depth t-3 contains a and meets B,C once. Its sole
B-point p determines its sole C-point: p if p belongs to U, and c if
p belongs to V. Thus, while these cardinality conditions hold, the
B-points obey a deterministic k-state quotient with transformations

  mu(p)=beta,
  f(p)=pF for p in U, and f(p)=cF for every p in V.

Every B-point is reached from S within m=n-s steps by strong
connectivity. Since m<=t-3, this is genuine reachability in the quotient
starting at p0, the B-point of S. Thus all k quotient states are
reachable. In a k-state graph every reachable vertex has a simple
path of length at most k-1, so every B-point occurs as the projection
of an actual image Sw with |w|<=k-1.

The equality flag gives affine dimension k-1 to these image rows.
Also |S intersect B|=1 implies k-1<=n-s=m, so k-1<=t-3. Their B-
coordinate projections include every one of the k unit vectors, of
affine dimension k-1. Projection is therefore injective on the entire
affine span: any two images through depth k-1 with the same B-point
are equal. This uses real rows, not a Boolean-field independence claim.

Since k>=3, the images SM,SMM,SFM all occur in that span. They all have
B-point beta, hence

  SMM=SM=SFM.

M's outside injectivity then gives

  S minus B = SM minus B = SF minus B = R.

All three sets meet C once, so their B-points p0,beta,f(p0) belong to
the same membership class U or V, determined by whether c is in R.
If p0 belongs to V, then beta and cF also belong to V. Both quotient
letters preserve V, contrary to reachability of the nonempty U.

Hence p0,beta,f(p0) are in U and c is absent from R. The first equality
SM minus B=R says that M preserves the outside part of any set
R union {p}, p in B: all p in B have the same M-image a. The equality
SF minus B=R, F^(-1)(B)=C, and c notin R show FR=R: F sends the
selected p0 in U into B, and every point of R outside C into Q minus B.

Take a shortest quotient word reaching V, of length at most k-1.
Before its final letter, its B-point is in U. Induction using the two
outside-part identities shows that every preceding actual image has
outside part R. The final letter must be F, because mu is constantly
beta in U. It also preserves outside part R. Its image has B-point in V,
yet omits c, so it meets neither part of C. This contradicts the
proved C-cardinality condition through t-3. QED.

<a id="problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion--boundary-and-audit"></a>
#### Boundary and audit

The size restriction k>=3 is required to place the length-two images
in V_(k-1); this proof makes no assertion at k=2. Initial-set reachability
is unused. The hypothesis s>=5 is the proved second-fiber range.
For larger alphabets there need not be a single constant quotient
letter and a single other letter, so the binary restriction is retained.

check_binary_near_equal_entrance.py exhausts every nonempty proper U
size and every k-state quotient map f constant on V, every constant
value beta and initial point p0 for k=3,4,5. It recomputes
shortest paths and checks both contradiction branches without using a
SAT answer. These finite controls support the all-k argument above;
they are not substituted for its dimension and outside-injectivity proof.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover--singleton-first-entrance-and-a-covered-second-entrance"></a>
### Singleton first entrance and a covered second entrance

9 October 2026. Symbolic conditional binary structure, outside the release.

Let ac(S,{a})=t=n-1 in a binary strongly connected synchronizing
automaton, with s=|S|>=6. Write B={b} for the singleton first entrance
and C for the second entrance, with k=|C|>=3. These fibers are from
[A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag) and [A second common entrance fiber at singleton equality](#problem4-second-entrance-fiber). In particular b is not
in C, every short image contains a,b, and it meets C once.

We prove:

1. If a fresh third entrance D has |D minus C|=1, the unique letter L
   with pre_L(B)=C cannot be injective on Q minus C.
2. Consequently C cannot be a vertex cover of P3.

Here pre means the full inverse image. A cover of P3 means that every
pair merging within three letters has an endpoint in C. No initial-set
reachability assumption is used. The size restriction s>=6 is retained;
this proof makes no assertion for s=5 or larger alphabets.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover--a-common-third-fiber-in-this-specific-geometry"></a>
#### A common third fiber in this specific geometry

Write D=U union {c}, U=C intersect D, and V=C minus D. Then c is outside
{a,b} union C, V is nonempty, and U is either empty or a nonempty proper
part of C. Since D has just one point outside C, U empty means D={c}.
Third-space incomparability with B forces b outside D.

Any other outside preimage R of C has indicator in the span of
1,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D on Q minus {a}. The remainder outside B,C,D meets
S in at least s-4>=2 points, all having the same constant coefficient
alpha in this indicator. Since R meets S once, alpha=0. The private
points b, a point of V, and c make the other three coefficients Boolean.
Counting on S, which meets B,C,D once, makes their sum one. Therefore
R is B,C or D. Each letter's preimage of C is {a},B,C or this common D.
This common-fiber assertion is restricted to the present geometry.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover--complete-binary-row-cover"></a>
#### Complete binary row cover

If D={c}, a letter using D as preimage of C has only one C output.
If the other letter also had a singleton preimage of C, the binary
alphabet could provide predecessors for at most two of the k>=3 C
points, contradicting strong connectivity. Thus the other letter F
has pre_F(C)=C. Since C and B are disjoint output sets, F cannot have
pre_F(B)=C. The first letter L must do so. Its preimage of C is D,
and it maps all of C to b. F permutes {a,b}, while L has a protected
singleton as preimage of a and sends the other protected input outside
{a,b} union C. Its sole C output is delta=cL. No other row profile exists.

If U is nonempty, a letter F using D as preimage of C cannot also have
pre_F(B)=C, because D intersects C. Thus the other letter L has
pre_L(B)=C and merges all of C to b. It cannot use C or D as preimage
of C; its preimage of C is {a} or B. Its C output delta is therefore
the image of a protected singleton present in every relevant image.
F permutes {a,b} and has pre_F(C)=D. These descriptions include all
possibilities for which letter uses B as preimage of a.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover--equality-projection-and-the-outside-part"></a>
#### Equality projection and the outside part

Suppose, for contradiction, that L is injective on Q minus C. Since
pre_L(B)=C, no point outside C maps to b. Equality of two L-images
of sets meeting C once then forces equality of their parts outside C.

Every image through t-4 meets D once, and every image through t-3
meets C once. Through the former depth its sole C point p follows
the deterministic k-state quotient

  mu(p)=delta,
  f(p)=pF if U is empty or p is in U; f(p)=cF if p is in V.

The formula for U empty uses pre_F(C)=C. For U nonempty, the D point
is p when p is in U and is c otherwise, giving the stated formula.
Strong connectivity reaches every C point from S within m=n-s steps.
Since m<=t-4, all k quotient states are genuinely reachable. A simple
path in that quotient has length at most k-1; moreover k-1<=m because
S meets C once. Thus the C-coordinate projections of images through
k-1 contain all k unit vectors.

The real equality flag gives affine dimension k-1 to those image rows.
Their C projections already have affine dimension k-1, so this projection
is injective on the entire affine span. Since k>=3, SL,SLL,SFL are in
that span. All have C point delta; hence

  SL=SLL=SFL.

Outside injectivity of L now gives

  S minus C = SL minus C = SF minus C = R0.

For U empty, the family {R0 union {p}:p in C} is invariant under both
letters. L maps every member to SL since all C points have image b.
Also F maps C into C and its complement into its complement, so
FR0=R0. Both letters preserve cardinality s on this family forever,
contradicting synchronization.

For U nonempty, the C points p0 of S, delta of SL and f(p0) of SF lie
in the same membership class U or V, as decided by whether c belongs
to R0. If p0 is in V, both delta and cF are in V; both quotient letters
preserve V, contradicting reachability of U. If p0 is in U, then delta
is in U and c is absent from R0. Since pre_F(C)=D and R0 avoids D,
the outside-part equality implies FR0=R0. L's outside-part equality
holds for every R0 union {p}, because it merges all of C to b.

Take a shortest quotient word reaching V, of length at most k-1. Its
last letter must be F, since mu is constantly in U. Before that letter,
induction keeps the actual outside part equal to R0. The last F also
keeps that outside part, but puts the C point in V. This image contains
no point of D=U union {c}, contradicting the one-count condition through
t-4. All used depths are at most k-1<=m<=t-4. This proves statement 1.

If C covered P3, the third-space lemma would force |D minus C|<=1
since D is a collision clique in P3. Incomparability makes this number
one. The same cover includes P1, so L would be injective outside C,
contradicting statement 1. This proves statement 2.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-first-second-cover--consequences-at-1391"></a>
#### Consequences at (13,9,1)

The normalized cover is H={0,1,2}, with a=3. The original joint record
b1_out_c6 has B={4}, C=H and is excluded by statement 2.

For b1_in_c5, B={0}, C={1,2,4}, C also covers P3. To justify this rather
than assuming it, every word through t-2=10 is safe and contains a,b.
Thus ac(S,{a,b})>=11; the avoid-or-compress upper gives equality 11.
Protected-pair isolation with this two-point protected set makes b=0
isolated in P_(s-3)=P6. Every P3 pair is covered by H and none touches
the sole point H minus C={b}. Hence C covers P3. This excludes b1_in_c5.

There is one additional third-profile exclusion in b1_out_c5:
B={4}, C={0,1,5}, D={2}. Statement 1 forces an outside-C collision
of L. The C triangle already uses three immediate pairs, so |P1|<=4
leaves at most one other pair. Since H covers P1, any outside-C pair
must contain the sole point H minus C=2. But pre_L(C)=D={2}, so
2L lies in C and every other input's L output lies outside C. No
such collision can occur. Thus this singleton-D profile is excluded.

Together with the preceding B3 and B2/C4 exclusions, 26 binary joint
records remain; unrestricted still has 43. The additional singleton-D
profile exclusion removes no further joint record. Both extrema remain
in [11,12]. No new F value or alphabet separation is claimed.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion--a-binary-exclusion-when-the-second-entrance-is-a-singleton"></a>
### A binary exclusion when the second entrance is a singleton

9 October 2026. Auxiliary conditional exclusion, outside the release.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion--proposition"></a>
#### Proposition

In a binary strongly connected synchronizing automaton with
ac(S,{a})=n-1 and |S|>=5, it is impossible that the first entrance B
has k>=3 points, covers every immediate collision pair, and the second
entrance C is a singleton. No unrestricted-alphabet exclusion is made.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Write C={c}; nonnesting gives c notin B. Choose a letter M with
preimage B of a. Its preimage of B cannot be B, since these output
sets are disjoint; it is {a} or {c}. If the other letter F also had a
singleton preimage of B, the entire binary alphabet would provide at
most two distinct target points in B. Strong connectivity requires a
predecessor for each of the k>=3 B-points. Therefore F has preimage B
of B. Since some letter must use C as preimage of B, M uses C. F has
preimage {a} of a, since otherwise the two preimages B would overlap.
Thus

  M^(-1)(a)=B, M^(-1)(B)={c},
  F^(-1)(a)={a}, F^(-1)(B)=B.

Put beta=cM. M is injective outside B by the kernel cover, and has
no outside predecessor of the common image a of B. Equal M-images
of sets meeting B once therefore force equal parts outside B.

Every image through depth t-3, t=n-1, contains a,c and meets B once.
Its B-point follows a k-state quotient: M is constantly beta, and F
acts as p maps to pF. Strong connectivity reaches every B-point from
S within m=n-|S|<=t-3 steps. All k quotient states are reachable;
each occurs in an actual image at length at most k-1. Also k-1<=m,
because S meets B once. The real equality flag has affine dimension
k-1 through this depth; its projection onto B includes all k unit
vectors, so projection is injective on that affine span.

For k>=3 the length-two images SM,SMM,SFM have the same B-point beta.
They are equal. The outside-injectivity implication gives

  S minus B=SM minus B=SF minus B=R.

The family of all sets R union {p}, p in B, is now invariant. For M,
every p in B maps to a, so every set in the family has the same image
SM=R union {beta}. For F, every p in B maps into B, and the preimage
identity F^(-1)(B)=B together with SF minus B=R gives FR=R. Thus
F maps R union {p} to R union {pF}. Both letters preserve cardinality
|S|>=5 on this whole family. A reset word cannot synchronize S,
contrary to synchronization of the automaton. QED.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion--consequence-for-a-two-step-cover"></a>
#### Consequence for a two-step cover

More generally, at singleton equality n-1 in a binary automaton with
|S|>=5, an entrance B of size at least three cannot itself cover P2.
Indeed C is a clique in P2, and nonnesting requires C minus B nonempty.
If B covered P2, that difference would have size exactly one. A
singleton C is excluded above; a nonsingleton C is excluded by
[A binary exclusion for an entrance with one new point](#problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion). Both proofs require only the
weaker P1 cover in their respective cases.

At (13,9,1) this excludes the entire b3_in first-fiber case B=H,
where H is the normalized three-point P5 cover. Its three joint orbits
b3_in_c1,c2,c3 are all excluded for binary automata. Five of the six
first-fiber cases, or forty of the 43 joint cases, remain admitted.
The unrestricted inventory still admits all six / all 43; no numerical
alphabet separation or new F maximum has been established.

<a id="problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion--audit"></a>
#### Audit

check_binary_singleton_second_entrance.py literally checks the finite
preimage-type alternatives: a moving letter cannot use B as preimage
of B, at least one letter must use C, and k>=3 target points cannot all
be supplied by two singleton preimages. The only admitted type pair
is M using C and F using B. It also checks quotient reachability and
the projected affine rank for every B-action of F, beta and initial
point through k=5, including singular B-actions. These controls support, and do not
replace, the arbitrary-k quotient-rank and invariant-family argument. No SAT answer
is used as a proof.

<a id="problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing--a-forbidden-backward-crossing-and-the-remaining-three-point-profile"></a>
### A forbidden backward crossing and the remaining three-point profile

9 October 2026. Conditional binary equality structure, outside release.

<a id="problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing--backward-crossing"></a>
#### Backward crossing

At ac(S,{a})=t=n-1, s>=5 in a binary strongly connected synchronizing
automaton, suppose the first two entrances B,C overlap. Name the
moving letter M and the other letter F. The first two entrance lemmas
force M^(-1)(a)=B, M^(-1)(B)={a}, F^(-1)(a)={a}, F^(-1)(B)=C.
Then

  F^(-1)(C) cannot equal B.

Suppose otherwise. If aM belongs to C, the third-entrance argument
gives M^(-1)(C)={a}. Under each letter the preimage of the proper
union {a} union B union C is then contained in that union, contrary
to strong connectivity. If aM is outside C, put U=B intersect C.
Then M^(-1)(U) is empty, since a is the sole predecessor of B and
its image is outside C. Also F^(-1)(U)=F^(-1)(B) intersect
F^(-1)(C)=C intersect B=U. The proper nonempty U has no incoming
transition from its complement, again contradicting strong connectivity.
This proves the assertion without a collision-pair cap or S reachability.

<a id="problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing--rank-obstruction-when-b3-and-c-minus-b2"></a>
#### Rank obstruction when |B|=3 and |C minus B|=2

At the thirteen-state target, |P1|<=4. The moving letter has its
three-point B block and at most one further two-point block, so
rank(M)>=n-3. If M^(-1)(C)={a}, the image of M can contain only a,
beta=aM, and points outside {a} union B union C. Since |B union C|=5,
this would give rank(M)<=n-4. Thus M^(-1)(C) is an outside third
entrance D disjoint from B. The cover H and incomparability with C
force, after relabeling its new outside point to 6,

  D={6} or D={2,6}.

Both have private points for B,C,D, namely 4,5,6. Any other preimage
R of C has indicator alpha*1+beta*chi_B+gamma*chi_C+delta*chi_D.
The constant coefficient is zero: the remainder outside B,C,D has
at least two points outside H, whereas R can contain at most one.
The private-point values beta,gamma,delta are Boolean, and meeting
S once forces beta+gamma+delta=1. Therefore each outside preimage
of C is B,C or D: the third entrance is common in these two cases.

<a id="problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing--forced-profile-for-c025"></a>
#### Forced profile for C={0,2,5}

For the retained b3_mixed_c7 case, F^(-1)(C)=B is excluded above.
It cannot be C: then F would map three points of C into the singleton
B intersect C={0}, adding three collision pairs outside B, contrary
to |P1|<=4. Hence F^(-1)(C)=D. If D={6}, no input under F can reach
B intersect C, since C intersect D is empty. M also misses that
intersection, because aM is outside C. Strong connectivity rules it out.

Consequently every binary equality realization of b3_mixed_c7 must,
up to the stated relabeling, satisfy exactly

  M^(-1)(C)=F^(-1)(C)={2,6}.

This is a necessary profile, not an exclusion of b3_mixed_c7 or a
new F value. The disjoint case b3_mixed_c3 is not covered by the
backward-crossing lemma and must not inherit this profile.

<a id="problem4-binary-three-cover-overlap"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-three-cover-overlap--a-binary-exclusion-with-a-three-point-entrance-cover"></a>
### A binary exclusion with a three-point entrance cover

9 October 2026. Auxiliary necessary exclusion, not a new maximum.
The proof is independent of a solver answer and initial-set reachability.

<a id="problem4-binary-three-cover-overlap--conditional-proposition"></a>
#### Conditional proposition

Let a binary strongly connected synchronizing automaton have
ac(S,{a})=n-1 with |S|>=5. Let B,C be the first and second common
entrance fibers. It is impossible that

  |B|=3, |C|=2, |B intersect C|=1,
  and B covers every immediate collision pair P1.

Thus, in the normalized (13,9,1) inventory, the binary orbit
b3_in_c2, B={0,1,2}, C={0,4}, is excluded. This proposition does not
apply to unrestricted alphabets or certify any alphabet separation.

<a id="problem4-binary-three-cover-overlap--proof"></a>
#### Proof

The full-image case has value one, so the hypotheses with s>=5 force
s<n and n>=6. In particular t-3>=2, where t=n-1, and the second-fiber
cardinality condition applies through depth two.

Write x for B intersect C and c for C minus B. Name a letter M that
has preimage B of a. It cannot have preimage B or C of the output set
B, since those preimages would intersect the preimage B of the disjoint
output {a}. The second-fiber theorem therefore gives

  M^(-1)(a)=B, M^(-1)(B)={a}.

Some letter uses C as preimage of B; it must be the other letter F.
Since C intersects B, that letter cannot have preimage B of a. Hence

  F^(-1)(a)={a}, F^(-1)(B)=C.

Put beta=aM in B. Every point of B has a predecessor, by strong
connectivity. The only possible predecessors into B are a under M
and the two points of C under F. Consequently F maps C injectively
onto B minus {beta}. In particular beta has no F-predecessor.
Also xF cannot equal x. Otherwise beta differs from x, M has no
predecessor of x, and F has only the predecessor x of x, so no other
state could reach x.

The immediate-pair cover implies that M is injective on Q minus B.
Moreover no point outside B maps to a. Thus equality UM=VM for sets
U,V meeting B once forces U minus B=V minus B: every outside point
has a distinct M-image, different from the common image a of B.

All images of S through length two are safe, contain a, and meet B
and C once. Their affine span is a plane, and the first-level affine
span is a line. The two first images SM and SF have distinct B-points:
SM has beta, whereas SF has a point in B minus {beta}. A line has at
most two Boolean vertices. Hence either SM=S or SF=S; let T be the
other first image.

Whenever three second-level images have three different B-points,
their projections to the three B-coordinates have affine rank two.
Projection is then injective on the entire second-level affine plane.
Two second-level images with the same B-point must therefore be equal.

If SM=S, consider first beta=x. The C-point of S is x; write
gamma=xF and delta=cF, the other two B-points. T=SF has B-point
gamma and C-point c, and TF has B-point delta. Thus S,T,TF have
three different B-points. TM has B-point beta, so TM=S=SM.
But c is absent from S and present in T, contradicting the outside
injectivity implication above.

Still suppose SM=S, now with beta different from x. Since xF is not
x, the two F-images of C must be x and the third B-point delta, with
cF=x and xF=delta. S has C-point c; T=SF has B-point x and C-point x;
TF has B-point delta. Again TM=S=SM. Now c is present in S and absent
from T, giving the same contradiction.

Finally suppose SF=S. If beta differs from x, the preceding images
cF=x and xF=delta show that no possible B-point of S is fixed under
the induced first-image rule: a set with B-point x has C-point x and
F-image B-point delta, and one with B-point delta has C-point c and
F-image B-point x. A set with B-point beta cannot be an F-image at all.
Thus beta=x. Put gamma=cF and delta=xF. The B-point of S must be gamma,
and its C-point is c. T=SM has B-point x and C-point x; TF has B-point
delta. The three B-points are distinct, and TM has B-point x, so
TM=T=SM. Again c is in S and not in T, contradicting M's outside
injectivity. This exhausts the cases and proves the proposition.

<a id="problem4-binary-three-cover-overlap--audit-and-limits"></a>
#### Audit and limits

check_binary_three_cover_overlap.py independently enumerates all four
possible induced maps from C into B allowed by the predecessor and
connectivity conditions, and all twelve initial B-point choices.
Six choices survive the first-level line condition; each gives three
distinct second-level projected B-points and the forbidden equality
of M-images with different c-membership.

The argument uses only the two-letter alphabet, the proved entrance
identities, the first two real equality levels, and the stated kernel
cover. It excludes this geometric type symbolically for all parameter
values satisfying the hypotheses. Neither a timeout nor the saved
encoding UNSAT is used as a mathematical certificate. The other
binary encoding UNSAT cases remain unproved unless separately audited.

<a id="problem4-c1-word-staircase-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c1-word-staircase-exclusion--the-last-b3-geometry-first-pair-staircase-with-actual-short-words"></a>
### The last B3 geometry: first-pair staircase with actual short words

Conditional scope: n=13, s=9, r=1, ac(S,{3})=12, arbitrary finite alphabet.
Only b3_mixed_c1_third2 is tested here. No numerical extremum or alphabet
separation is asserted. The accepted paper remains a partial answer.

Use the frozen entrance-fiber and immediate-graph enumeration, with
H={0,1,2}, A={3}, B={0,1,4}, C={5}, D={6}, and J={3,5,6}.
Every retained immediate graph in the complete inverse-clique inventory is
included. For each graph enumerate all nine-sets containing A, meeting
B,C,D once, and independent in G=P1_candidate union K_C union K_D.
Enumerate every ordered distinct pair S,T in this family, without the
exploratory first-pair pruning. The depth-one equality row span has basis
chi(S),chi(T); hence every letter maps S to S or T, and some maps S to T.
A line through two distinct Boolean vectors has no other Boolean vertex.

The initial letter domain consists of ALL frozen companion fields and
exact kernels, and ALL labelled assignments of their blocks to output
states, subject to S mapping to S or T and T mapping to a safe image at
depth two. In particular every output permutation inside an atom is kept.
The output of Q-H must be G-independent and images of J must be isolated
in the available output graph, as in the frozen inverse-clique premises.
The four initial required domains supply preimage(A)=B, preimage(B)=C,
preimage(C)=D, and S mapping to T. These suppliers may coincide.

Start the actual staircase-basis argument of [Staircase equality flags exclude two further B3 geometries](#problem4-b3-staircase-flag-exclusion)
at depth one. At a node with actual basis R0=S,...,Ri, require each letter's
image of Ri to be safe at depth i+1, enumerate every possible image outside
the current row span, and restrict all letters to the enlarged span.
Adjoin the supplier domain for the chosen chain step Ri mapping to Ri+1.
All earlier basis images already lie in their specified prefix spans.
If no growth is possible, invariance contradicts the equality dimensions.
Thus every actual alphabet is contained in at least one complete branch.

At depths <=11 safety requires a nine-set containing A; additionally the
image meets B once through10, C once through9, D once through8, and is
G-independent through8. No depth12 safety is assumed. A surviving basis
through11 would be a candidate, never a negative certificate. Every saved
branch here must end with a missing required domain, a proper closed set
in the maximal graph, or lack of growth before depth11. Basis-image safety
is necessary only and is never asserted sufficient for all-word safety.

There is no separately fixed second-image plane. All candidate Ri+1 images
are chosen as actual chain images, and every letter whose image is any
Boolean vertex in the enlarged span is retained. This includes a fourth
vertex of a two-dimensional plane without assuming it actual or invariant.

For symmetry partition columns by H,A,B,C,D membership, then sort within
each cell by extra-edge membership and ordered S,T membership. Transport
the extra edge along with the pair; the edge may be absent. The checker
enumerates every labelled pair again, verifies each permutation, all
control sets, all companion fields and all complete kernel catalogues,
and checks its canonical pair's multiplicity. No representative letter
substitutes for the full literal letter domain.

The generator uses output colours and atom bijections. The independent
checker instead assigns exact kernel blocks directly to labelled targets.
Their complete sorted row and supplier-flag digests must agree. Every flag
node is checked using independently reconstructed maps and rational row
elimination. The modular generator's ranks are exact by Hadamard's bound
3^13<1000000007 for characteristic nine-set rows. All branches and closed
sets are stored; no timeout or alphabet-size bound certifies an exclusion.

Compose this one third-geometry exclusion with the frozen previous cuts
before removing the whole C1 joint or B3-mixed first branch. The 136 B1/B2
third geometries remain, and both F_bin(13,9,1) and F(13,9,1) remain [11,12].


<a id="problem4-c1-word-staircase-exclusion--exact-forced-letter-short-word-propagation"></a>
#### Exact forced-letter short-word propagation

At a node let L be the complete remaining literal letter domain, and
L_j the intersection of L with each required supplier/chain-step domain.
Every possible actual alphabet Sigma is contained in L and intersects
every L_j. If L_j={f}, necessarily f belongs to Sigma. Let U consist of
all such uniquely forced letters. If a word over U of length<=11 omits A
or compresses the original S, no actual alphabet exists at this node.
Otherwise, for any f in L-U, a bad word over U union {f} of length<=11
proves f cannot belong to any actual alphabet. Delete every such f in a
batch, recompute all L_j, and repeat. Singleton letters are never deleted
by this batch. An empty L_j rejects the node immediately. This argument
uses actual words from the original S, not only images of the basis.

The certificate records every round's domain size and digest, every
singleton supplier premise, every deleted literal letter and its bad
word, and the resulting domain digest. The independent checker composes
these words on labelled SETS from the original S and verifies the final
avoidance/compression and length<=11. It does not need to assume that the
retained letters are mutually compatible, or that the recorded words are
shortest. Skipping propagation when no singleton exists, or in a larger
domain, simply retains an overapproximation. The implementation applies
it from basis depth3 for domains of at most10,000 literal letters; this
threshold is an algorithmic choice, never an alphabet-size assumption.

After propagation, remove zero image-domain groups, check all mandatory
groups and the maximal graph, and enumerate every remaining next image.
All prefix spans, proper closed sets and branch lists are reconstructed
independently. Source hashes, immutable packaging and isolated regeneration
must pass before this conditional exclusion is composed with prior cuts.

<a id="problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion--binary-exclusion-of-d06-in-the-disjoint-c3-case"></a>
### Binary exclusion of D={0,6} in the disjoint c3 case

9 October 2026. Conditional exclusion at (13,9,1); no new extremal value.

At binary strongly connected synchronizing equality ac(S,{3})=12,
|S|=9, normalized H={0,1,2} covering P5, B={0,1,4}, C={2,5},
the common third entrance cannot be D={0,6}. Initial reachability
is unnecessary. The first moving profile is excluded in
[The constant-B moving profile is impossible for D={0,6}](#problem4-c3-d4-profile-i-exclusion). This note treats the remaining profile

  M^(-1)(A)=B, M^(-1)(B)=C, M^(-1)(C)=A,
  F^(-1)(A)=A, F^(-1)(B)=C, F^(-1)(C)=D,

where A={3}. Put V={1,4}, J={7,...,12}, X={6} union J, R=V union J.
M maps X bijectively to itself by the H cover. F maps R into X.
The B triangle occupies three P1 pairs; the five-pair endpoint
argument gives |P1|<=4. Every R collision therefore is either the
inside-B pair {1,4} or one pair {1,h}, h in J. There must be a
collision, since |R|=8 and |X|=7. No R triple or second pair is
possible: a triple adds at least two outside-B pairs, and two disjoint
pairs would require one having both endpoints outside H. Thus F has
exactly seven R kernel blocks, mapped bijectively to X.

Let P_M=M^(-1)({6})={r}, r in X, and E=P_F=F^(-1)({6}). E is a
singleton in R or one of the possible pair blocks above; in particular
it is nonempty and has at most one point outside H. For T=M,F set
L_T={c in C:cT belongs to V}. Every safe nine-set meeting B,C,D
once contains 6 exactly when its B point is in V. Consequently

  |Sw intersect P_T|=|Sw intersect L_T|,  |w|<=7.       (1)

Write K_i=V_i perpendicular. Equality gives dim K_7=5, dim K_8=4,
and K_8 has basis h_a,h_B,h_C,h_D, h_Y=9chi_Y-1. Every K_8 column
is constant on C, on V, and on J. The columns h_r and h_E each
lie outside K_8 whenever (1) says their input count is one. For h_r
this is shown in the profile-I note. For h_E use the private-point
classification in [Typed third entrances in the disjoint three-point/two-point case](#problem4-c3-typed-third-entrances): a Boolean outside
fiber with at most one point outside H and count one on S, whose
normalized column lies in K_8, must be B,C or D. None is contained
in R, so E is not such a fiber.

No L_T can be empty. Otherwise every image through depth seven
omits every point of the nonempty P_T, contrary to strong connectivity
reaching each point from S within four steps. No L_T can be all of
C. If it is, the indegree of B point 0 requires the other letter
to map some C input to 0. Its nonempty L is then a singleton {c}.
The first letter contributes h_r or h_E to K_7, constant on C and
outside K_8; the second contributes chi_(P_T)-e_c, which is not
constant on C. These give two independent new columns beyond K_8,
contradicting dim K_7=5. Thus L_M={c_M}, L_F={c_F}.

Both letters map the other C point to 0, and map c_M,c_F to
v_M,v_F in V. Indegrees for 1,4 force v_M,v_F to be distinct.
Equation (1) puts e_r-e_(c_M) and chi_E-e_(c_F) in K_7.
Each splits the C coordinates and is nonzero modulo K_8. Their
dependence modulo K_8 forces precisely

  c_M=c_F=c_* and either
  (i) r in J and E={r}, or (ii) r=6 and E={1,4}.       (2)

For completeness, if r is ordinary, constancy on the other J
coordinates forces E to contain r and the two new coefficients to
cancel. A second point of E would be 1, splitting the V coordinates,
which is impossible for K_8. Thus E={r}, and constancy on C forces
c_M=c_F. If r=6, E cannot contain an ordinary point, nor can it be
a singleton in V (again splitting V). Thus E={1,4}. On the 0,6,V,J
cells a K_8 column satisfies value(0)=value(V)+value(6)-value(J);
this forces the coefficients to cancel, and again c_M=c_F. The
converse uses e_6-chi_V=(h_D-h_B)/9. All 420 possible r,E,c_M,c_F
coordinate profiles are checked independently with exact ranks.

In alternative (ii), a short image has C point c_* exactly when
it contains 6, hence exactly when its B point is in V. Both letters
output a B point in V exactly when the input C point is c_*.
They therefore preserve the two B classes {0} and V through depth
four. Strong connectivity must reach every B point from S within
four steps, which is impossible.

In alternative (i), a short image contains r exactly when its C
point is c_*. If its B point is 0, it is {3,0,c} union J, so it
must have C point c_*. Reach c' in C minus {c_*} from S within
four steps. Its safe image has B point in V and omits r. Applying
either letter gives B point 0 at depth at most five, so both outputs
have C point c_*. Thus M3=c_* and F6=c_*.

Now SM^2, a safe nine-set, has B point v_M and C point c_*.
Every safe image with B point in V and C point c_* remains in that
class under both letters: M uses its A input for the C output,
F uses its D input 6, and both use the C input c_* for a V output.
All words of length at most four starting from SM^2 are still short
(total depth at most six) and cannot reach c'. Strong connectivity
from this nine-set must reach c' within n-9=4 steps, a contradiction.

Both alternatives and both moving profiles are excluded. This is a
paper proof; finite coordinate and quotient audits are checks of its
explicit statements. The binary c3 branch retains D={6} or D={2,6}.
Unrestricted alphabets retain all four typed D profiles. The c3
joint orbit and the first unresolved extrema [11,12] remain open.

<a id="problem4-c3-d4-profile-i-exclusion"></a>
