<a id="problem4-c3-d4-profile-i-exclusion--the-constant-b-moving-profile-is-impossible-for-d06"></a>
### The constant-B moving profile is impossible for D={0,6}

9 October 2026. Necessary binary c3 profile reduction at (13,9,1).
This note excludes only one moving profile. The other is subsequently
excluded in [Binary exclusion of D={0,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion); no new F value is claimed.

Let a=3, B={0,1,4}, C={2,5}, D={0,6}, H={0,1,2} and suppose
binary strongly connected synchronizing equality ac(S,{a})=12,
|S|=9. [Typed third entrances in the disjoint three-point/two-point case](#problem4-c3-typed-third-entrances) forces the letter F to have
preimages A={3},C,D of A,B,C. The moving letter M uses B as the
preimage of A and has either preimages A,C or C,A of B,C.
The first possibility is impossible.

Suppose M^(-1)(B)=A and M^(-1)(C)=C. Then M3=beta in B,
and M maps X={6,...,12} bijectively to itself: no collision there
can be covered by H. Let r in X be its unique preimage of 6.
Every short safe image meets B,D once. Since D minus B={6}
and B minus D={1,4}, it contains 6 exactly when its B point is
1 or 4. Every M image has B point beta. If beta=0, all Sw with
|w|<=7 omit r, contrary to strong connectivity reaching r from
S within four steps. Hence beta belongs to {1,4}, and every such
Sw contains r. Thus h_r=9e_r-1 belongs to K_7=V_7 perpendicular.

Strong-connectivity indegrees require F(C)=B minus {beta}, since
only M3 and the two C inputs of F can reach B. These outputs are
0 and the other point of {1,4}. Let c in C map to the latter.
Let E=F^(-1)({6}). It is a subset of R={1,4,7,...,12}, because
F maps A,C,D into A,B,C, respectively. We do not need to impose
nonemptiness or enumerate its kernel: the following column argument
also covers E empty and every possible subset of R.

For |w|<=7, SwF contains 6 exactly when its B point is in {1,4},
which is exactly when Sw contains c. Consequently chi_E-e_c is
also in K_7. But dim K_7=5 and K_8 has dimension four, with basis
h_a,h_B,h_C,h_D. Every K_8 column is constant on the two C
coordinates. So is h_r, whereas chi_E-e_c is not.

Moreover h_r is not in K_8. If r is ordinary, K_8 is constant on
the entire ordinary cell J={7,...,12}, while h_r distinguishes r.
If r=6, restrict to Q minus {a}: an expression for e_6 using
1,B,C,D has zero constant coefficient on J, zero B coefficient
on 1,4, and zero C coefficient on 2,5. Its D coefficient would
have to be one at 6, giving a nonzero value at 0, a contradiction.
Since h_a restricts to -1, this also excludes h_r from K_8.
Thus h_r gives a fifth independent column, and chi_E-e_c a sixth,
contradicting dim K_7=5.

The argument does not require S to be an actual reachable image.
The remaining moving profile for D={0,6} is exactly

  M^(-1)(B)=C, M^(-1)(C)=A,
  F^(-1)(B)=C, F^(-1)(C)=D.

This is a reduction only. The checker audits the asserted rank-six
obstruction for every r in X, either c in C, and every subset E
of R, a superset of all possible actual row kernels.
The complete D={0,6} exclusion combines this lemma with the other
profile's coordinate and trap argument in [Binary exclusion of D={0,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion).

<a id="problem4-c3-d6-binary-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c3-d6-binary-exclusion--excluding-d26-in-the-binary-disjoint-c3-case"></a>
### Excluding D={2,6} in the binary disjoint c3 case

9 October 2026. Conditional thirteen-state exclusion; no new F value.

Suppose a binary strongly connected synchronizing thirteen-state
automaton has ac(S,{3})=12, |S|=9, H={0,1,2} covering P5,
B={0,1,4}, C={2,5} and common third entrance D={2,6}.
We derive a contradiction. Initial reachability is not required.

Write A={3}, J={7,...,12}, X={6} union J, W={5} union J.
Safe images meet B,C,D once through depth eight; consequently their
5 and 6 coordinates agree. The initial nine-sets are precisely
{3,b,2} union J and {3,b,5,6} union (J minus {h}), b in B,h in J.
There are twenty-one. K_8 has dimension four and basis h_A,h_B,h_C,h_D,
where h_Y=9chi_Y-1; K_7 has dimension five. These are equality-flag
annihilators. K_8 is constant on B and on J, and on the 2,5,6,J cells
satisfies value(2)=value(5)+value(6)-value(J).

<a id="problem4-c3-d6-binary-exclusion--complete-binary-preimage-profiles"></a>
#### Complete binary preimage profiles

List a row by its preimages of A,B,C. The disjoint input types are
exactly ABC, ABD, ACB, BAC, BAD, BCA. A D supplier must be ABD or
BAD, and a C supplier as preimage of B must be ACB or BCA. Both
suppliers must exist. At least one letter moves A, so ABC/ABD/ACB
cannot be the entire alphabet. Up to naming letters the only pairs are

  I: BAD, ACB; II: BAD, BCA; III: ABD, BCA.

Every D-supplier maps W bijectively onto X: all W outputs are in X,
and H permits no collision between W points. A BCA or ACB row maps
X bijectively to itself by the same argument. Let r_W in W and
r_X in X be their respective unique preimages of 6.

<a id="problem4-c3-d6-binary-exclusion--a-constant-5-row-is-impossible"></a>
#### A constant-5 row is impossible

This covers II, III and a subcase of I. In BCA, the C output is
the image of 3. It must be 5: if it were 2, coordinate equality 5=6
would omit r_X from every Sw through depth seven, contrary to strong
connectivity reaching it from S within n-s=4 steps. In ACB, consider
the subcase that the whole B maps to 5. Again all images of this
letter have C point 5. In either situation every Sw through depth
seven contains r_X. If r_X=6, every such image has C point 5, so
state 2 cannot be reached within four steps. Hence r_X is in J and
h_(r_X)=9e_(r_X)-1 belongs to K_7, outside K_8.

For the D-supplier denote its two outputs on 2,6 by u_2,u_6 in C.
If both are 2, the 5=6 relation omits r_W through depth seven,
contradicting strong connectivity. If both are 5, or if (u_2,u_6)=(2,5),
the class of images with C point 5 is preserved by both letters.
Start with a safe one-letter image of the constant-5 row; within
four further steps it cannot reach state 2, contradicting strong
connectivity from this nine-set. All total depths are at most five.
Thus the D-supplier must flip the C point: (u_2,u_6)=(5,2).

The 5=6 relation now gives e_(r_W)-e_2 in K_7. It is independent
of h_(r_X) modulo K_8 for every r_W in W and r_X in J. If r_W is
ordinary and distinct from r_X, constancy on the other J coordinates
forces both coefficients to vanish. If they coincide, cancelling
the exceptional J coordinate still leaves a nonzero violation of
value(2)=value(5)+value(6)-value(J). If r_W=5, the same cell relation
first forces its coefficient to vanish, and then the exceptional
r_X coordinate forces the other coefficient to vanish. Thus K_7
would have at least six independent columns. All forty-two possibilities
are audited by exact rank. The constant-5 cases are excluded.

<a id="problem4-c3-d6-binary-exclusion--the-remaining-acb-row-in-profile-i"></a>
#### The remaining ACB row in profile I

Name the BAD row M and the ACB row F. M maps B to 3, maps 3 to
beta in B, and maps D to C. F fixes 3, maps C to B and B to C.
Let E={b in B:bF=5}. E cannot be empty: F permutes X, so the
5=6 relation would omit its nonempty singleton preimage r_X of 6
through depth seven. E=B was excluded by the preceding argument.
Thus E is a nonempty proper subset of B.

The column e_(r_X)-chi_E belongs to K_7 and is not constant on B.
For M, e_(r_W)-chi_L belongs to K_7, where L={d in D:dM=5}; it
is constant on B. Unless the latter column belongs to K_8, these
give two independent new columns beyond K_8, violating dim K_7=5.
The only possibility for membership in K_8 is r_W=5 and L={6}:
an ordinary r_W distinguishes a J coordinate; at r_W=5 the four
choices of L are checked by the 2,5,6,J cell relation. Therefore

  M2=2, M6=5, M5=6.

M now preserves the C point, resets the B point to beta, and
permutes J. The indegrees of the three B points force F2=f_2 and
F5=f_5 to be the two distinct B points other than beta. For every
short image the core transformations on (b,c) in B times C are

  M(b,c)=(beta,c),
  F(b,c)=(f_c, 5 if b belongs to E, otherwise 2).       (1)

For an input image with C point 2, all J points are present. F
permutes X, so its J outputs are X minus {F6}. Since image coordinates
5 and 6 agree, the output C point is 2 exactly when F6=6. Thus
all such inputs through depth seven have b outside E if F6=6,
and b in E if F6 belongs to J.

There is a short image with C point 2 at depth at most two. If S
already has it this is immediate. Otherwise, if its B point is
outside E, F reaches 2 in one step. If beta or f_5 is outside E,
MF or FF reaches 2 in two steps. If all three B points appearing
in this list belong to E, (1) preserves C point 5 from S through
depth four, contradicting strong connectivity. Call the resulting
nine-set T; its initial depth is at most two.

If F6=6, every short image with C point 2 remains of that class
under both letters, by (1) and the preceding coordinate condition.
Starting from T, state 5 cannot be reached within four steps, at
total depth at most six. Hence F6 belongs to J, and every C-point-2
input through depth seven must have its B point in E. In particular
TM has B point beta, so beta belongs to E.

TFM has B point beta and C point 5, at depth at most four. If
f_5 is also in E, the core class C point 5 and B point in
{beta,f_5} is preserved by both letters. From this nine-set state
2 cannot be reached within four steps (total depth at most eight),
again contradicting strong connectivity. Therefore f_5 is outside E.
But TFMFF has C point 2 and B point f_5 outside E, at depth at
most six. Applying F once more contradicts the proved coordinate
condition through depth seven; the resulting total depth is at most
seven. All uses of the 5=6 relation lie at depth at most eight.

All three profiles are excluded. The exact finite audit checks the
complete row-type cover, forty-two rank-six cases, all twenty-eight
M-column membership cases, twenty-one initial sets, and the 432
proper-E quotient/coordinate configurations. It supports this symbolic
proof without treating an incomplete row search as an upper bound.

Binary c3 now retains only D={6}. Unrestricted alphabets retain four
typed third entrances. No whole c3 orbit, new F value or numerical
alphabet separation is asserted; (13,9,1) remains in [11,12].

<a id="problem4-c3-d9-binary-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c3-d9-binary-exclusion--binary-exclusion-of-d016-in-the-disjoint-c3-case"></a>
### Binary exclusion of D={0,1,6} in the disjoint c3 case

9 October 2026. Conditional exclusion at (13,9,1); no new F value.

At local equality ac(S,{3})=12, |S|=9 in a binary strongly connected
synchronizing thirteen-state automaton, with H={0,1,2} covering P5,
B={0,1,4}, C={2,5}, the common third entrance cannot be D={0,1,6}.
No initial-set reachability assumption is used.

[Typed third entrances in the disjoint three-point/two-point case](#problem4-c3-typed-third-entrances) supplies the common D and the only two
profiles. Write A={3}, U={0,1}, J={7,...,12}, X={6,...,12}.
The moving letter M has preimage B of A. The other letter F has
preimages A,C,D of A,B,C, respectively. F maps C to B, D to C,
and R={4} union J to X. The B triangle already consists of three
P1 pairs. Because R is disjoint from H, F is injective on R, hence
maps its seven points bijectively onto X. Similarly, in either
moving profile M maps X bijectively to itself: collisions there
would have both endpoints outside H. The extra possible collision
among the two C points does not change these bijections.

Every short safe image meets B,C,D once and contains 3. Since
D minus B={6} and B minus D={4}, it contains 6 exactly when its
B point is 4. If its B point is 0 or 1 it consists of {3,p,c} union J.
If its B point is 4 it consists of {3,4,6,c} union (J minus {h}),
for c in C,h in J. These are all sixteen possible nine-sets.

<a id="problem4-c3-d9-binary-exclusion--profile-i-m-has-preimages-ac-of-bc"></a>
#### Profile I: M has preimages A,C of B,C

Then M3=beta in B and M maps C into C. All M images have B point
beta. If beta is in U, they omit 6. Its nonempty M-preimage r in X
would consequently be omitted by every Sw of length at most seven.
Strong connectivity reaches r from S within n-s=4 steps, a contradiction.
Thus beta=4. All B states have predecessors only from 3 under M or
from C under F. Strong-connectivity indegrees now force F(C)=U.
Every F image has B point in U, hence omits 6. Its nonempty
F-preimage r in R is again omitted by every Sw through depth seven,
contradicting reachability within four steps. Profile I is impossible.

<a id="problem4-c3-d9-binary-exclusion--profile-ii-m-has-preimages-ca-of-bc"></a>
#### Profile II: M has preimages C,A of B,C

M maps C into B and maps 3 to one C point; F maps C into B as above.
Let r_M in X and r_F in R be the unique preimages of 6. Define
E_T={c in C:cT=4} for T=M,F. For every |w|<=7 the image SwT still
meets B,D once, so its 6 coordinate equals its 4 coordinate. Hence

  (chi_(Sw))_(r_T) = |Sw intersect E_T|.                 (1)

No E_T can be empty: (1) would omit r_T through depth seven,
contrary to strong connectivity reaching it within four steps.
No E_T can be all of C either: then that letter has sole B output 4,
and indegrees for 0,1 force the other letter's C outputs to be 0,1,
giving an empty E for that letter. Thus each E_T is a singleton
{c_T}, and the other C outputs u_M,u_F are the two distinct U states.

The equality flag gives dim V_7=8 and dim V_8=9. Its annihilator K_8
is spanned by h_a=9e_3-1 and h_Y=9chi_Y-1 for Y=B,C,D. This
four-dimensional space lies in the five-dimensional K_7. Equation (1)
puts e_(r_M)-e_(c_M) and e_(r_F)-e_(c_F) into K_7. They are nonzero
modulo K_8, since K_8 is constant on the two C coordinates. The only
possibilities are

  c_M=c_F=c_* and either
  (i) r_M=r_F=r in J, or (ii) r_M=6 and r_F=4.         (2)

Here are explicit column checks for (2). K_8 is constant on J and
on C. If exactly one r is ordinary, or they are two distinct ordinary
points, a nontrivial linear combination of the two new columns cannot
be constant on J; there are other untouched J coordinates to fix its
constant to zero. Thus ordinary r's must coincide and their coefficients
cancel. Constancy on C then forces c_M=c_F. If neither r is ordinary,
they are 6 and 4. On coordinates 4,6,U, the relation for any K_8 column
is value(U)=value(4)+value(6)-value(J). The combination's coefficients
therefore cancel too, and constancy on C again forces c_M=c_F.
Conversely e_6-e_4=(h_D-h_B)/9 belongs to K_8, so both alternatives
indeed give at most one new annihilator dimension.

In alternative (ii), (1) says that a short image contains c_* exactly
when it contains 6, hence exactly when its B point is 4. Both letters'
B output is 4 exactly when the input C point is c_*. Therefore both
letters preserve whether the B point belongs to U or equals 4, for
all paths through depth four. Strong connectivity must reach all
three B points from S within four steps, which is impossible.

In alternative (i), every image through depth seven contains r exactly
when its C point is c_*. A nine-set with B point in U contains all of
J, so necessarily has C point c_*. Reach the other C point c' from S
within four steps. Its safe image has B point 4 and omits r. Applying
M and F gives B points u_M,u_F in U at depth at most five, so both
outputs have C point c_*. Consequently M3=c_* and F6=c_*.

The safe nine-set SM^2 has B point 4 and C point c_* regardless of
the initial core points: every M image has C point M3=c_*, and
the next M maps that C point to 4. Both letters preserve this core
class, using M3=F6=c_* and c_*M=c_*F=4. Words of length at most
four starting from SM^2 remain safe (total depth at most six) and
cannot reach c'. Strong connectivity from this nine-set must reach
c' within n-9=4 steps, a contradiction.

Both moving profiles and both annihilator alternatives are excluded.
This is a symbolic proof. The independent audit enumerates all 196
preimage-coordinate profiles, checks exact ranks and (2), all sixteen
nine-sets, and the quotient-class and short-reachability contradictions literally.
It does not replace a missing row search by a timeout or sampling.

The further [Binary exclusion of D={0,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion) also excludes binary D={0,6}.
The c3 second-entrance orbit remains open with D={6},{2,6} for binary
automata, and all four typed D profiles for unrestricted alphabets.
The first unresolved extrema stay in [11,12]. No alphabet separation
or complete answer to Problem 4 is asserted.

<a id="problem4-c3-singleton-third-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c3-singleton-third-exclusion--excluding-the-singleton-third-entrance-in-binary-c3"></a>
### Excluding the singleton third entrance in binary c3

9 October 2026. Conditional exclusion at (13,9,1); no new extremal value.

Assume binary strongly connected synchronizing equality ac(S,{3})=12,
|S|=9, H={0,1,2} covering P5, B={0,1,4}, C={2,5}, and common
third entrance D={6}. We derive a contradiction without requiring
the initial S to be reachable. Write A={3}, J={7,...,12}, X={6} union J.
Every safe image through depth eight contains 3,6 and meets B,C once.
The five-pair endpoint argument gives |P1|<=4. The moving letter's
B triangle is already in P1, so there is at most one immediate
collision pair outside B; call it E if it exists. Every immediate
collision is covered by H. A row is named by its preimages of A,B,C.

<a id="problem4-c3-singleton-third-exclusion--row-and-kernel-cover"></a>
#### Row and kernel cover

Disjoint inputs leave the eight types ABC, ABD, ACB, ACD, BAC, BAD,
BCA, BCD. There must be a moving row, a C supplier for B and a D
supplier for C. Up to exchange of the two letters, the complete list is

  ABC/BCD, ABD/BCA, ABD/BCD, ACB/BAD, ACB/BCD,
  ACD/BAC, ACD/BAD, ACD/BCA, ACD/BCD, BAC/BCD,
  BAD/BCA, BAD/BCD, BCA/BCD, BCD/BCD.                    (1)

Let G be the three pairs inside B together with {2,5}. For every
allowed row, the pair preimage of any member of G is contained in G:
B has input preimage A,B or C, and C has input preimage A,B,C or D.
The singleton preimages contribute no pairs. Thus G is backward closed.
If all one-step collisions lie in G, all mergeable pairs lie in G;
for example {3,6} is then unmergeable. Synchronization therefore
requires an immediate collision outside G.

Such a collision can only occur among a row's inputs mapped to X.
For ABC, ACB, BAC and BCA those inputs are X, and for BCD they are
A union J. Both sets consist of seven points outside H, so the row
maps them bijectively to X. For ABD or BAD the X inputs are C union J,
eight points with just one H point, 2. They have exactly one pair
block, {2,5} or {2,h}, h in J, and seven output blocks, bijective to X.
For ACD the X inputs are B union J, nine points. Their kernel is
either the entire B block with ordinary singletons, or a B pair
B minus {i} and a pair {i,h}, i in {0,1}, h in J, with ordinary
singletons. These are the only ways to reduce nine inputs to at most
seven outputs with at most one outside-B pair and an H cover. Each
has exactly seven blocks, bijective to X. Every X-preimage block in
all these cases contains a point outside H.

Consequently synchronization needs E={2,h} or E={i,h}, i=0 or 1,
h in J. The five pairs in (1) having BCD as their sole D supplier
have no capable row and are already excluded by backward closure.

<a id="problem4-c3-singleton-third-exclusion--both-rows-have-a-constant-c-point"></a>
#### Both rows have a constant C point

A row with C preimage A or D always has one fixed C point on short
images. If the two constants agree, start with a safe one-letter
image: the other C point cannot be reached in four further steps,
contrary to strong connectivity from a nine-set. Thus the constants
must be 2 and 5. All total depths in this argument are at most five.

For E={2,h}, let T be the row with C constant 2. Its preimage of 2
is the singleton {y}, y=3 or 6, outside H. Its nonempty X-preimage
of h contains q outside H. The pair {y,q} is distinct (yT=2,
qT=h) and maps to E, hence merges in two steps. This contradicts
the H cover of P5. This treats ABD/BCA, ABD/BCD, ACD/BAD, BAD/BCA,
BAD/BCD, whose capable eight-input row must supply E={2,h}.

For E={i,h}, the two rows are F=ACD and M=BCA or BCD. Both have B
preimage C. The shared outside pair budget forces their two C outputs
to be distinct B points. If either row sends 5 to i, its preimage
of E contains a pair {5,q} with q outside H, merging in two steps.
So neither sends 5 to i. Strong-connectivity indegrees of i force
some row L to send 2 to i. Let T have C constant 2, with singleton
preimage {y}, y=3 or 6. Pull E back under L to {2,r}:

* If L=M, its preimage r of h belongs to A union J or X. Every
  T-preimage of such an r contains a point q outside H: use its A
  preimage A or B for r=3, and an X block otherwise. Then {y,q}
  maps under T,L to E and merges in three steps.
* If L=F, its preimage block of h either contains an ordinary r in J,
  handled by the same argument, or is B minus {i}. In the latter case
  choose r=5T. It belongs to that B pair since no row sends 5 to i.
  The outside pair {y,5} maps under T,F to E and merges in three steps.

These contradict the H cover and treat ACD/BCA and ACD/BCD.

<a id="problem4-c3-singleton-third-exclusion--the-nonconstant-pair-acbbad"></a>
#### The nonconstant pair ACB/BAD

Let M=BAD, F=ACB. Only M can supply an outside-G collision, so it
is E={2,h}. If M6=2, pulling E back under M gives an outside-H
pair merging in two steps. Thus M6=5. Let beta=3M and f_c=cF.
The shared pair budget makes f_2,f_5 distinct, and B indegrees force
them to be B minus {beta}. Put U={b in B:bF=2}. It is nonempty,
since only F can reach state 2. Let r be the unique F-preimage of h,
which belongs to X.

If beta is in U, the F-preimage {beta,r} of E has an M-preimage
{3,q} with q outside H, merging in three steps. Hence beta is not
in U. If f_5 is also outside U, the short core class with C point 5
and B point in {beta,f_5} is invariant under both rows. Starting
from SM, it cannot reach 2 in four steps, contradicting strong
connectivity (total depth at most five). Thus f_5 belongs to U.
Now pulling E back twice under F gives {5,q}, where q is the
unique F-preimage in X of r. This outside-H pair merges within three
steps, again a contradiction.

<a id="problem4-c3-singleton-third-exclusion--the-nonconstant-pair-acdbac"></a>
#### The nonconstant pair ACD/BAC

Let F=ACD, M=BAC. Only F can supply an outside-G collision, so
E={i,h} with i in {0,1}. Write beta=3M and f_c=cF. If beta=i,
the M-preimage of E is {3,q}, q in X, merging in two steps. Thus
beta differs from i. Indegrees force f_2,f_5 to be the two B points
other than beta. If f_5=i, an F-preimage of E is an outside-H pair
{5,q}, also merging in two steps. Hence f_2=i.

M permutes C: merging its two points would add {2,5} to the already
used outside pair E. If M fixed both C points, the C class of SF
would be invariant under both letters, contrary to reaching the
other C point from this nine-set in four steps. Thus M interchanges
2 and 5. The F-preimage block of h either contains r in J, or is
B minus {i}. In the first case pull {2,r} back under M to {5,q},
q in X. In the second beta belongs to that B block, so pull {2,beta}
back under M to {5,3}. Both outside-H pairs merge in three steps.

All fourteen pairs are excluded. Pair preimages above always use
distinct inputs and actual preimage blocks; no Cartesian-product
diagonal is counted. The finite audit independently enumerates the
row types, every possible abstract X kernel, core maps and the local
witness or short-reachability cases. The proof uses no incomplete
native scan, SAT answer or numerical histogram as an upper bound.

Together with [Binary exclusion of D={0,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion), [Binary exclusion of D={0,1,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d9-binary-exclusion) and
[Excluding D={2,6} in the binary disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d6-binary-exclusion) this excludes the entire binary c3 joint
orbit. The other audited B3 exclusions are in
[A binary exclusion when the second entrance is a singleton](#problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion),
[The three-point first entrance cannot have singleton second entrance at (13,9,1)](#problem4-singleton-three-kernel-exclusion), [Exclusion of the binary three-point entrance with one new overlap point](#problem4-overlap-three-kernel-exclusion),
[Symbolically excluding the binary three-point overlap c7](#problem4-c7-third-profile-exclusion) and [Excluding the four-point second entrance at (13,9,1)](#problem4-four-point-second-entrance-exclusion).
Combining these excludes all binary three-point first entrances at
(13,9,1); a binary equality witness must have |B|<=2. There remain
29 binary and 43 unrestricted joint cases, and four/six first cases.
Both extrema remain [11,12]. No new F value or alphabet separation.

<a id="problem4-c3-staircase-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c3-staircase-exclusion--complete-c3-staircase-exclusions"></a>
### Complete C3 staircase exclusions

Conditional scope: (13,9,1), avoid-or-compress length12, arbitrary alphabet.
The four remaining C3 third geometries are audited together. No numerical
value of F or alphabet separation is asserted; the accepted paper is unchanged.

The actual staircase-basis lemma and negative flag-domain method are those
proved in [Staircase equality flags exclude two further B3 geometries](#problem4-b3-staircase-flag-exclusion). The complete initial domains again
use H={0,1,2}, A={3}, B={0,1,4}; here C={2,5} and D is respectively {6},
{0,6}, {2,6}, or {0,1,6}. The frozen third/atom/inverse-clique inventories
give every Boolean companion field and every possible exact kernel.

Enumerate every feasible first pair S,T and every common second-image plane,
using the independent literal-colouring versus quota-bounded checker. Some
planes have four feasible vertices. For each retained plane enumerate every
R in that plane outside {S,T}; an actual alphabet must supply at least one
such R=T f, and S,T,R is a basis of its depth-two row span. Retain the full
plane in the condition on f(T), including the fourth vertex. It need not be
an actual image; retaining it enlarges the domain. Images of this fourth
vertex are not independently required to be safe or to preserve the plane.
All later flag restrictions follow by linearity on the actual basis.

A staircase step R_(i+1)=R_i f outside the current span still exists for
each actual basis: every earlier basis image belongs to the current span,
and otherwise that span would stabilize. Therefore each tree lists every
possible next actual image, restricts all letters to its enlarged span, and
retains all required supplier and chain-step domains. The same necessary
safe-image tests through depth11 are used, with one-count conditions on
B,C,D through depths10,9,8 and independence of the known P3 graph through8.
Basis-image safety alone is never claimed sufficient for all-word safety.

For symmetry, partition states by membership in H,A,B,C,D. In each cell
sort first by whether a state is an endpoint of the proposed extra P1 edge,
then by its ordered membership in S,T,R. Mapping this order to the sorted
cell produces a canonical extra edge and prefix. The extra edge may be
absent; no fixed extra edge is assumed. For each literal transport the
checker verifies the control sets, full plane, mandatory core, every field,
and complete kernel-mask catalogue. Thus both arbitrary alphabets and every
within-atom permutation are preserved. The labelled-D normalization remains
the exhaustive frozen third inventory, and all new operations are equivariant.

The literal-colouring generator enumerates every labelled letter for each
canonical prefix. The independent checker assigns exact kernel blocks directly
to output states, with the full plane and graph restrictions, and compares all
canonical serialized row and supplier-flag digests. Both programs reconstruct
every literal map; the package stores counts and digests instead of repeated
letter lists. The checker uses its independently reconstructed maps to check
every rejection-tree node using rational
linear algebra; the generator's modular ranks are exact by the previously
proved Hadamard bound 3^13<1000000007. Empty domains, missing required groups,
and proper closed sets in the maximal transition graph are direct rejections.
No timeout, sampled negative, or bounded alphabet size supports a cut.

Complete prefix and staircase inventories, source hashes, independent audits
and isolated regeneration form the certificate. The whole C3 joint is removed
only by composing the four new third cuts with its prior complete exclusions.
The remaining B3 geometry is b3_mixed_c1_third2. Both F(13,9,1) remain [11,12].

<a id="problem4-c3-typed-third-entrances"></a>
<a id="problem4-c3-typed-third-entrances--typed-third-entrances-in-the-disjoint-three-pointtwo-point-case"></a>
### Typed third entrances in the disjoint three-point/two-point case

9 October 2026. Necessary structure at (13,9,1), any finite alphabet.
No new extremal value and no joint second-entrance orbit exclusion.

Normalize H={0,1,2}, a=3, B={0,1,4}, C={2,5}, and suppose
ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9. The entrance lemmas give each letter's preimage
of a as A={3} or B, of B as A,B or C, and of C as A or an outside
Boolean fiber in the third entrance space. Some outside preimage D
of C is distinct from B,C. The union B,C is disjoint.

Because the three output sets A,B,C are pairwise disjoint, their
input preimages under each letter must be pairwise disjoint. The
possible first two preimage pairs are exactly

  (A,B), (A,C), (B,A), (B,C).

Every pair includes B or C. Therefore its third preimage D must
avoid B or avoid C. A third preimage meeting both is impossible.
This is a constraint on each actual row, not an alphabet-size bound.

Combining this constraint with the proved H cover, incomparability
of B,C,D, and a nine-set meeting all three once leaves exactly,
up to permuting equivalent ordinary points and exchanging 0,1,

  D={6}, {0,6}, {2,6}, {0,1,6}.

Indeed, a D disjoint from B is contained in {2,5} union {6,...,12}.
Incomparability with C requires a new ordinary point, while the
H-cover allows at most one point outside H, excluding 5 together
with a new point. This leaves {6} or {2,6}. A D disjoint from C
is contained in {0,1,4} union {6,...,12}. Incomparability with B
again requires a new ordinary point; the cover then excludes 4.
This leaves {6}, {0,6} or {0,1,6} up to exchanging 0,1.
Each case has an admissible nine-set, as checked independently.
There are 35 labelled sets in these four orbits, compared with
65 labelled sets in the earlier twelve-orbit geometric admission.

The third entrance is common in these specific cases. To see this,
let an outside preimage R of C have indicator

  chi_R = alpha*1 + beta*chi_B + gamma*chi_C + delta*chi_D.

The remainder outside B,C,D contains several points outside H,
on which chi_R takes the constant value alpha. The cover condition
|R minus H|<=1 forces alpha=0. There is a private B point (4), a
private C point (5), and a private D point (6). Thus beta,gamma,delta
are each Boolean. Counting R on the actual S, which meets B,C,D
once, gives beta+gamma+delta=1. Consequently R is B,C or D.
Each letter's preimage of C is therefore A,B,C or this same D.
No common-third-fiber statement outside these profiles is asserted.

For a binary alphabet and D meeting B, the letter using D as
preimage of C must fix a and have preimage C of B: the other
possible preimage pair (A,B) intersects D in B. Call it F. The
other letter M must use B as preimage of a. Its preimage pair for
B,C is either (A,C) or (C,A). There are no other profiles; D meets
B, so it cannot be used by a moving letter. Both these profiles
are treated for D={0,1,6} in [Binary exclusion of D={0,1,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d9-binary-exclusion).
For D={0,6}, [The constant-B moving profile is impossible for D={0,6}](#problem4-c3-d4-profile-i-exclusion) and
[Binary exclusion of D={0,6} in the disjoint c3 case](#problem4-c3-d4-binary-exclusion) exclude both binary moving profiles.
Binary c3 retains only the disjoint third entrances {6} and {2,6}.
The unrestricted typed admission remains all four profiles.

The old third inventory deliberately remains geometric and retains
all twelve entries. The new checker applies the disjoint input types
independently and records the four actual-row-compatible entrances.
This reduction does not exclude the c3 second-entrance orbit itself.

<a id="problem4-c4-d125-complete-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c4-d125-complete-exclusion--complete-conditional-binary-b0c4d125-exclusion"></a>
### Complete conditional binary B0/C4/D125 exclusion

At(13,9,1), assumed ac=12, B={0},C={4},D={1,2,5}, K12 covering P5.
The complete parent third inventory has14 binary profile pairs and
8 labelled D choices. The uniform common-collapsing-block trap excludes
five parent pairs with both preC=D. This leaves exactly nine.

The complete fourth inventory has precisely E6,E16,E126, representing
7,14,7 labelled E choices, total28. Each has nine admitted actual-field
pairs, covering the nine remaining third profiles. All Boolean companions
are retained; there are none in these three domains. D125 remains one
size3 output atom, never three artificially independent singleton atoms.

The complete raw generator and native input recursion agree on2540160
raw rows. Two independent algorithms agree on1068480 retained rows and
all pointwise conjugacy transports. The stabilizer fixes0..6 and includes
all720 permutations of7..12;2160 separate group checks verify preservation
of every field and initial family. First rows alone are reduced; every
second row stays labelled.45/36/27-set masks use uint64_t, with a bit44
control and562176 retained masks above bit31. Every actual row pair and
initial image is represented by simultaneous conjugation.

Each implementation tests145980000 representative pairs, all rejected
before candidate safe-prefix/reaching BFS. In E6 the failures are only
strong connectivity or synchronization (possibly an empty common initial
mask in the primary cut order). [A closed merging block](#problem4-closed-merging-block) proves the whole
binary E6 case independently on paper, with12798 complete finite M/F
controls and direct forward checks. E16/E126 strong connected survivors
fail mandatory P7 or outside-K P5 isolation, always within three steps.
No candidate attaining image or reset/reaching witness is asserted here.

The composition checker verifies every original third pair and every
fourth alternative. This excludes the whole binary b1_in_c1_third5 type,
removing nine previously remaining pairs and one typed/geometric orbit;
the original fourteen are fully discharged without counting the earlier
five again. The three unrestricted fourth alternatives remain. This
conditional thirteen-state exclusion is not a new numerical F value,
alphabet separation, whole B0/C4 joint exclusion or all-parameter answer.

<a id="problem4-c4-d125-e16-e126-unrestricted-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c4-d125-e16-e126-unrestricted-exclusion--unrestricted-c4d125e16-and-e126-exclusions"></a>
### Unrestricted C4/D125/E16 and E126 exclusions

Conditional at (13,9,1), equality ac(S,{3})=12, with B={0}, C={4},
D={1,2,5}, K={1,2} covering P5. The fresh fourth fiber is either
E={1,6} or E={1,2,6}. Both conditional geometries are excluded for
arbitrary finite alphabets. No numerical F value is asserted here.

Put A={3}, H=A union B union C, O=Q-(H union D), e=6, R=Q-K.
The complete fourth classification gives, for each letter ell,
preA in {A,B}, preB in {A,B,C}, preC in {A,B,C,D}, and
preD in {A,B,C,D,E}. These exact preimage groups are pairwise disjoint.
There are 12 individual fields for each E, all included. No binary
incoming capacity bound or binary-active field restriction is used.
There are no omitted Boolean companions in either geometry.
The fresh D and E have suppliers M,T with preC(M)=D and preD(T)=E.
This existence is part of the entry flag, not inferred from a sample.
M collapses D into the singleton C. Thus binom(D,2) is contained in P1.

Disjointness gives three exhaustive letter classes.
(F) preD=D: preA/preB/preC are the three distinct singletons of H;
    H is permuted, D maps into D, and O is permuted.
(M) preD is a singleton in H: preA/preB occupy the other two H
    inputs, forcing preC=D; O is permuted.
(T) preD=E: since E meets D, preC cannot be D, so preA/preB/preC
    are the three H singletons. The free input 5 and O-{e} are
    exactly |O| inputs that map into O. They are outside K and so
    map injectively onto O. Guard 2 may also map into O for E16.
Every letter therefore satisfies O subset R ell. Injectivity outside K
follows from the P5 cover; we use no retracted pair-count bound.

For E126, T sends all of {1,2,e} into D and M collapses D.
Both {1,e} and {2,e} merge under TM, of length two. By the universal
free-image trap (d=2), K covering P3 and e in R ell for every ell
imply that R is forward invariant. Strong connectivity is impossible.

For E16, {1,e} merges under TM. The one-target trap, using the P3
cover, forbids every transition R -> 1. Strong connectivity forces
an edge 2 -> 1: along a path from R to 1, consider the first arrival
at 1; its predecessor cannot be in R or be 1, so it must be 2.
Its letter F must have preD=D: input 2 is not in E16 or any H singleton.
Class F permutes O, so there is x in O with xF=e. The pair {2,x}
then merges under FTM in at most three letters. All letters have x in
R ell. The one-target trap at d=3, using the P4 cover, now forbids
every transition R -> 2 as well. Hence R is forward invariant, again
contradicting strong connectivity.

Only covers P3/P4 are needed in these arguments, and both follow from
the accepted P5 cover. Mandatory-core isolation is not used here.
The E16 argument permits a different sentinel x for target 2; it does
not assume F fixes e or arbitrary prefixes preserve O.

Equivalently, every strongly connected alphabet with the complete
field schema, outside-K injectivity, and D/E suppliers admits a word
merging a pair in R within four (E16) or three (E126). Construct it
directly: an edge R->1 yields LTM with both inputs in R; otherwise
choose F:2->1, an edge L:R->2, and x=F^{-1}(e) in O, obtaining LFTM.

Independent controls reconstruct all 120 preimage tuples, all 12

<a id="problem4-c4-d125-e6-unrestricted-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-c4-d125-e6-unrestricted-exclusion--unrestricted-alphabet-b0c4d125e6-exclusion"></a>
### Unrestricted-alphabet B0/C4/D125/E6 exclusion

Conditional at(13,9,1), ac(S,{3})=12, B0,C4,D125,E6, strong connectivity
and synchronization. This is a fourth-geometry exclusion, not an F value
or alphabet separation. It does not exclude E16/E126 or the whole D125
third geometry for unrestricted alphabets.

Write A={3}, B={0}, C={4}, D={1,2,5}, O=Q-(A union B union C union D),
e=6, K={1,2}, J={0,3,4,6}. The complete Boolean one-count classification
has preA in{A,B}, preB in{A,B,C}, preC in{A,B,C,D}, and preD in{A,B,C,D,{e}}.
There are16 individually admissible fields, not just the eight binary-active
fields. Each letter is injective outside K because K covers P5. J is
mandatory through seven, hence isolated in P7. No binary capacity bound
is used below.

The output groups A,B,C,D,O are disjoint, so the first four preimage groups
are disjoint as well. This gives the following exhaustive letter classes.

(1) If preD=D, the preimages of A,B,C are three distinct singletons in
A union B union C. The letter permutes these three states, maps D into D,
and permutes O (outside-K injectivity on |O| inputs). All kernels are in D.
Call these letters D-preserving.

(2) If preD is a singleton p in A union B union C, preA/preB use the
other two singletons, forcing preC=D. The letter collapses D into C,
permutes O, and has no mixed D/outside kernel. Its image contains all O.

(3) If preD={e} and preC=D, the two singleton preA/preB groups leave
one protected input and O-{e} as the |O| free inputs of the O-output group.
Injectivity outside K makes these map bijectively onto O. Kernels lie in D.

(4) If preD={e} and preC is a singleton, preA/preB/preC permute A union
B union C. All D inputs map to O. The free D input5 and O-{e} are exactly
|O| free inputs mapping injectively onto O, so the image contains all O.
Any kernel outside D is a mixed pair {k,x}, k in D, x in O.

Thus every letter either preserves D or enters D from exactly one p in J.
Every entering letter L has QL containing all O; D-preserving letters
permute O. All kernels outside D can occur only in class(4).

Suppose some class(4) letter T merges k in D with x in O. Strong connectivity
makes every D state reachable from Q-D. On any such path consider the last
entrance into D. That entrance uses a letter L from p in J; the remaining
suffix stays in D and hence uses only D-preserving letters. For k choose
a shortest such suffix u. Since D has three states, |u|<=2. Then pLu=k,
and QLu still contains O because QL contains O and u permutes O. Choose
q with qLu=x. Since k is in D and x is in O, q is distinct from p.
The pair {p,q} merges under LuT, length at most four, contradicting J's
P7 isolation. Notice that this uses surjectivity of QL onto O, not a
claim that every entering letter preserves O. Arbitrary entering-letter
prefixes are not asserted to preserve O.

Consequently every letter's kernels lie in D. All preD fibers are D or
singletons, so [A closed merging block](#problem4-closed-merging-block) traps every mergeable pair inside D.
Synchronization is impossible. This proves the unrestricted E6 exclusion.

The counting proof of the four classes works for any |O|>=1; the auxiliary
abstract statement uses the same three-state D, three protected singleton
states, e in O and outside-K injectivity. Strong connectivity plus
synchronization under this abstract field schema forces a pair touching J
to merge within four. We make no global F claim from that statement.

Independent controls reconstruct all120 preimage tuples and their16 exact
fields, every individual row at n7,8,9 by a different input recursion,

A literal strongly connected synchronizing n8 control has earliest J-pair

Write A={3}, H=A union B union C, O=Q-(H union D), and e=5. Exact

If preD=D, the three preA/preB/preC groups are the H singletons;

If preC=D, then preD is a singleton p in H, or (only for E5) {e}.

<a id="problem4-c4-d12-unrestricted-exclusion--ee"></a>
#### E={e}

Here J=H union {e} is mandatory through seven and isolated in P7.
Choose a preC=D supplier M, with preD(M)={p}, p in J, and put d=pM
in D. For each T, both D inputs map into O. If dT is not the hole h,
some x in O-{e} has xT=dT. Since O is contained in QM, choose q
with qM=x. Then q differs from p and MT merges the pair {p,q} touching
J in two steps. This contradicts isolation. Thus dT=h for every T,
and consequently O is contained in QT for every T.

Every entering letter now has its full image containing O; its exact
preD is a singleton in J. D-preserving letters permute O. The only
possible immediate kernel outside D is a mixed pair {k,x}, k in D,
x in O, under a T letter. Strong connectivity makes every D state
reachable from outside D. At the last entrance the input p is in J;
afterwards only D-preserving letters can keep the path inside D.
Since D has two states, a shortest such suffix u has length at most one.
Thus pLu=k with |Lu|<=2, and O is contained in QLu. Choose q with
qLu=x; then LuT merges {p,q} within three, again contradicting P7
isolation. No arbitrary entering-letter prefix is claimed to preserve O.

So all immediate kernels are inside D. Every letter has preD=D or a
singleton. The closed-merging-block lemma traps every mergeable pair
inside D, ruling out synchronization. This excludes E5.

<a id="problem4-c4-d12-unrestricted-exclusion--e1e"></a>
#### E={1,e}

Here J=H is mandatory through seven and isolated in P7. Choose suppliers
M0 with preC=D and T0 with preD=E. Since E meets D, every preC=D
supplier has preD={p} for p in H and permutes O. Both 1 and e map
under T0 into D, which M0 collapses, so {1,e} merges under T0M0.

Every preC=D letter M must send its unique entering p to 2. If pM=1,
choose q in O with qM=e; then MT0M0 merges {p,q} within three.
In particular fix p0 with p0M0=2. No D-preserving letter F can send
2 to 1: such F permutes O, so take x in O with xF=e and q in O
with qM0=x. The word M0FT0M0 would merge {p0,q} within four.

For every T letter, the remaining guard input 2 maps into O. It must
fill the unique hole h of the injection O-{e}->O. Otherwise some
x in O-{e} has xT=2T; choosing q in O with qM0=x makes M0T merge
{p0,q} within two.

No T can send e to 1. If eT=1 and h differs from e, choose
x in O-{e} with xT=e. Then TT0M0 merges the distinct pair {e,x}
entirely outside K within three, contradicting the P5 cover. If instead

Now examine every possible predecessor of state 1. A preC=D letter
enters D only at 2. A D-preserving letter cannot send 2 to 1, and its
only D inputs are 1,2. A T letter has preD={1,e}, with e forbidden
from mapping to 1. Thus the only possible predecessor of 1 is 1
itself. This contradicts strong connectivity. This excludes E15.

Both proofs use the full individual field schema and suppliers, not

is impossible for an arbitrary finite alphabet. It does not exclude

<a id="problem4-c4-d15-e25-unrestricted-exclusion--no-kernel-pair-inside-o"></a>

<a id="problem4-c4-d15-e25-unrestricted-exclusion--mandatory-isolation-and-strong-connectivity"></a>
#### Mandatory isolation and strong connectivity

Every M must send its protected entering point p to 1. Otherwise
pM=5; choose q in O with qM=2. The word MT0M0 merges p,q in three.

O permutations. Then M0FT0M0 merges p0,q within four. All M outputs

For this T let h again be the omitted ordinary output. If 1T!=h,
some ordinary y has yT=1T. Since QM0 covers O, M0T already merges
a pair touching p0 in two. Hence 1T=h.

If 5T=5, the free-image restriction above forces h=2. The image
QM0T contains 5 and takes p0 to 2; appending T0M0 merges a pair
touching p0 within four. If 5T=1, T is a permutation. At h=2 the
same contradiction applies. Otherwise h is ordinary and v=hT is in
O-{h}. The exact missing-set identities are

    RT^2 = Q-{1,v},       QM0T^2 = Q-{h}.

If v!=2, RT^2 contains 2,5, yielding a free pair merged by T^2T0M0
within four. If v=2, p0M0T^2=2 and QM0T^2 contains 5, yielding a
mandatory pair merged by M0T^2T0M0 within five. Both are forbidden.
Thus the transition required for strong connectivity is impossible.

This proves the conditional exclusion for arbitrary alphabet size.
Synchronization is essential in the saturated-image subcase; SC
alone is not substituted there. The argument uses only the P4 cover
after outside-K injectivity, mandatory isolation through five, exact
fields and suppliers, SC and synchronization. The accepted P5/P7
premises imply the required bounds. No binary capacity assumption,
higher-layer edge-count cap, or initial-reachability shortcut is used.

The accompanying two independent row enumerators and literal-word
checker test complete small supplier domains and seeded larger
alphabets. Sampling supports the paper argument and proves no upper
bound. Nonsynchronizing image-closure certificates are checked against
independent reverse pair BFS; boundary controls are not F witnesses.

Conditional at (13,9,1), equality12, B={0}, C={4}, D={1,5},
E={2,6}, and K={1,2} covering P5. This fourth geometry is impossible
for every finite alphabet. Neither whole D15 third type nor a numerical

Put H={0,3,4}, W=Q-(H union D union E), O=E union W, R=Q-K.
The complete fourth classification has sixteen individual fields and
no additional covered Boolean companions. Both suppliers M0 with
preC=D and T0 with preD=E exist; one letter may supply both, and is
not omitted. Since M0 collapses D into singleton C, pair15 is in P1.
The two E inputs under T0 enter D and merge under T0M0, so26 is in P2.
Write G0={15,26}, a matching on L=D union E.

Assume synchronization. [P3 graphs under a two-state P5 cover](#problem4-two-cover-p3-classification) says P3 is
matching, path4 or triangle after deletion of isolates. It contains

In particular every P3 edge has both endpoints in L.

If P2 contained the crossing edge, its three-edge path would have
exactly three independent n-2-sets. All edges belong to P2; the P5
cover and [Finite independent-image trap](#problem4-finite-independent-image-trap) forbid synchronization.
Consequently P2=G0 exactly.

We now prove the pair recurrence cannot add anything at depth3.
The inverse pairs of15 already lie in P2, since15 belongs to P1.
For inverse pairs of26, the complete sixteen fields give four
exhaustive classes (preimages here are exact sets):

* F: preC is a singleton of H and preD=D. The H inputs permute H,
  the D inputs enter D, and the O inputs enter O. Both inverse inputs
  of an E edge therefore lie in O=E union W. A P3 edge with these

* M: preC=D and preD={p}, p in H. D enters C, the two other H
  inputs supply A,B, p enters D, and O enters O. Inverse E inputs
  again lie in O, giving only26.
* T: preC is a singleton of H and preD=E. H permutes H, E enters
  D, and all inverse E inputs lie in D union W. The only possible
  P3 inverse E pair is15.
* MT: preC=D and preD=E. D enters C, E enters D, two H inputs
  supply A,B, and the remaining H input and W enter O. Every inverse
  E input lies in H union W, disjoint from L. There is no inverse E
  pair at all, since such a pair would be a P3 edge outside L.

Thus all inverse pairs of G0 lie in G0, and P1 is contained in G0.
The recurrence P_(j+1)=P1 union all letter inverse pairs of P_j
therefore stabilizes at P2=P3=G0. Induction gives P_j=G0 for every
j>=2. A pair outside this proper matching never merges, contradicting
synchronization.

The argument uses exact fields, suppliers, synchronization and the P5

Independent raw-row generators match the complete small individual

<a id="problem4-c7-third-profile-exclusion--symbolically-excluding-the-binary-three-point-overlap-c7"></a>
### Symbolically excluding the binary three-point overlap c7

9 October 2026. Conditional exclusion at (13,9,1); no new extremal value.

There is no binary strongly connected synchronizing automaton with
ac(S,{3})=12, |S|=9, normalized H={0,1,2} covering P5,
B={0,1,4}, C={0,2,5}. No initial reachability is needed.

The third-entrance proof forces D={2,6} as the common preimage of C.
The five-pair Frankl--Pin endpoint argument gives |P1|<=4. The complete
necessary row cover is proved in [Complete row cover for the binary c7 third-entrance profile](#problem4-c7-third-profile-normalization).
In its notation, M(B)={3}, M3=beta in {1,4}, M2,M6 in {2,5},
and M maps W={5,7,...,12} bijectively to X={6,7,...,12}.
Also F3=3, F2=0, F0,F5 in {1,4}, F6 in {2,5}.
On R={1,4,7,...,12}, F has precisely one pair block, either {1,4}
or {1,h} with h>=7; its other blocks are singletons and its blocks
map bijectively onto X. If F0=F5, that R block must be {1,4}.
Every F-preimage of an X point therefore contains a point outside H:
its only possible H input is 1, which is paired with an outside point.

We will contradict even the weaker assumption that H covers P4,
using backward pair preimages. If a pair merges within l steps,
every distinct pair whose images under one letter form that pair
merges within l+1 steps. All instances below involve distinct points.

First M2 and M6 must differ. If both equal 2, {2,6} merges in one
step, and its M-preimages include {6,w} where w in W is the unique
M-preimage of 6. This outside-H pair merges within two steps. If
both equal 5, strong-connectivity indegree forces F6=2, as M then
misses 2. The F-preimages of the one-step pair {2,6} include {6,r}
with r outside H in R, again merging within two steps.

Next {2,6} always merges within three steps. If F6=2, choose
v=F0 in {1,4}. The pair {0,v} is in the one-step B triangle;
its F-preimages include {2,0}. Taking another F-preimage gives
{6,2}. If F6=5, then {0,5} merges within two steps: directly when
F0=F5, or as an F-preimage of the one-step pair {1,4} otherwise.
Its F-preimage {2,6} merges within three steps.

If M6=2, its M-preimages include the outside-H pair {6,w} above,
now merging within four steps. Hence M2=2 and M6=5. If F6=2,
its F-preimages include {6,r} with r outside H, also merging within
four steps. Hence F6=5. In particular M^(-1)(2)={2} and
F^(-1)(2) is empty.

Suppose first the R block is {1,4}. Define G0 to consist of the
B triangle, {0,5}, and every pair containing 2. G0 contains all
one-step merged pairs. It is backward closed under both letters:
under M all pairs with endpoint 0 have empty preimage, the pair
{1,4} has empty pair preimage since only beta is an M output, and
preimages of pairs containing 2 still contain 2. Under F those last
pairs have empty preimage; preimages of {0,1} and {0,4} contain 2,
preimages of {1,4} are either empty or {0,5}, and the preimage of
{0,5} is {2,6}. These descriptions use the actual pair preimage,
not a Cartesian product permitting equal inputs. Thus every pair
merged by any word belongs to G0. For example {3,4} is not in G0,
so the automaton cannot synchronize.

It remains that the R block is {1,h}, h>=7, and F0 differs from F5.
If beta=1, the M-preimage of this one-step pair includes {3,w_h}
where w_h in W maps to h, an outside-H pair merging in two steps.
Therefore beta=4. If F5=1, its F-preimages include {5,r} with
r outside H in R, another outside-H pair merging in two steps.
Therefore F0=1, F5=4. Enlarge G0 to G1 by adding {1,h} and every
pair {0,r}, r in R. Again all one-step merged pairs belong to G1.
The new pair {1,h} has no M-preimage, because M misses 1; its
F-preimages are of the form {0,r}, r in R. A pair {0,r} has no
M-preimage, and all its F-preimages contain 2. Hence G1 is backward
closed. It still excludes {3,4}, contradicting synchronization.

Every case gives either a pair outside H merging by depth four or
a nonsynchronizing automaton. Since H covers P5, the c7 branch is
excluded. This proof uses no first-level flag computation, subset
enumeration, SAT result, timeout, or numerical histogram. Native and
independent literal controls check the necessary row cover and the
pair dichotomy, as auxiliary audits rather than a substitute for proof.

This excludes b3_mixed_c7 only. The disjoint c3 branch, B1/B2 branches
and unrestricted alphabets remain open. The first unresolved extrema
at (13,9,1) remain in [11,12]; this is not a complete answer to Problem 4.

At (n,s,r)=(13,9,1), normalize H={0,1,2}, protected a=3,
B={0,1,4}, C={0,2,5}. [A forbidden backward crossing and the remaining three-point profile](#problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing) proves

Write J={7,...,12}, X={6,...,12}, W={5} union J and V={1,4}.
The seven W inputs under M must go to X. No collision among them
is possible: the B triangle already consumes three of the at most

Thus M maps W bijectively onto X. Its only possible additional

The remaining F inputs R=V union J (eight points) go to X (seven).

map bijectively to X. If F0=F5 the outside-B pair {0,5} has already

If F0 differs from F5, all seven pair choices are possible.

It also requires F6 to be the other new point if M2=M6. These are
only indegree necessities; no stronger graph property is assumed.
The resulting complete row count is

  30 * 2 * (2+2*2) * (1+2*7) * 7! = 27,216,000.

This is a complete necessary row cover, possibly a strict superset:
when M2=M6, its outside-B pair may already exhaust the shared budget,
but the generator conservatively retains the F choices justified by

Every safe initial nine-set meets B,C,D once and contains 3. There

<a id="problem4-closed-merging-block"></a>
<a id="problem4-closed-merging-block--a-closed-merging-block"></a>
### A closed merging block

Let D be a nonempty proper state subset. Suppose for every letter ell:
(1) every immediate kernel pair lies in binom(D,2), and
(2) ell^{-1}(D) is contained in D or has at most one state.
Then every pair mergeable by any word lies in binom(D,2). The automaton
is not synchronizing. This criterion holds for arbitrary finite
alphabets and needs no strong connectivity or initial-image assumption.

Proof. The pair recurrence is P_(h+1)=P1 union the letter inverse pairs
of P_h. Condition(1) gives P1 subset binom(D,2). If a distinct pair
maps to a distinct pair in D, its endpoints lie in ell^{-1}(D). By(2)
they must both lie in D; the alternative singleton preimage cannot
contain a distinct pair. Induction proves P_h subset binom(D,2).
A pair with an endpoint outside proper D never merges. If some letter
collapses all D, equality P_h=binom(D,2) holds for every h>=1.

At(13,9,1), B0,C4,D125,E6, all outside preD fibers are precisely B,C,D,E;
preD can also be A={3}. Only D has cardinality greater than one.
K12 covers P1 and is contained in D, so every letter is injective
outside D. A letter M supplying preC=D collapses D into C4 and has
no mixed D/outside kernel. The common-block trap excludes both letters
having preC=D. Strong connectivity requires incoming coverage of all
three D states. If both preD fibers were singletons, only two D states
could have incoming edges. Hence the other letter F must have preD=D.
The required E6 supplier is M, with preD=E6. Exact preD=D for F means
D/outside images are disjoint, and its only kernels are inside D.
Thus F^{-1}(D)=D and M^{-1}(D)=E6, satisfying the closed-block criterion.
The entire binary E6 branch is therefore excluded on paper, independently
of the complete row scans. This does not exclude unrestricted E6,
where additional letters with other field columns are admissible.

The nine formal binary E6 field pairs are independently checked to
have exactly the M/F structure above. Finite controls normalize D012,
c3,e4, enumerate all M collapsing D to c with preD=e and injectivity
outside D, and all F with preD=D and injectivity outside D, at n5..7.
Every ordered M/F pair is tested by reverse pair BFS, with separately
selected direct forward pair checks; some controls are strongly connected
but none synchronizes. Boundary controls show failure when the kernel,
preD or proper-subset hypothesis is omitted. These finite controls
support the uniform proof; they are not an all-parameter F theorem.

<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy"></a>
<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy--a-complete-short-pair-dichotomy-at-codimension-four"></a>
### A complete short-pair dichotomy at codimension four

8 October 2026. Auxiliary reduction for investigating compression at least
twelve. It determines no new F value and is not included in the current
article or 109-file release.

The dichotomy is now sharpened, within this investigation only, by the
complete six-image lemma below: its cycle branch is impossible. Thus an
(n-4)-set of compression length at least twelve requires tau(P5)<=3.
This is a necessary condition, not a value of F or a complete upper bound.

<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy--proposition"></a>
#### Proposition

Let n>=8, and let a strongly connected synchronizing n-state automaton
have an (n-4)-set whose shortest compressing word has length at least 12.
Write P_h for the graph of pairs merged in at most h letters. Then

1. tau(P_4)<=3;
2. either tau(P_5)<=3, or P_5 is a seven-cycle and n-7 isolated vertices.

In the second case, every image reached from the initial set within six
letters is one of exactly seven sets: all isolated vertices together with
a maximum independent triple of the cycle. All seven sets have been reached
by depth six. If the local avoid-or-compress value is also at least 12, A
is contained in the isolated vertices.

These statements are alphabet-independent and do not require the initial
set to be a reachable image.

<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy--uniform-reduction"></a>
#### Uniform reduction

The first conclusion is the proved span corollary in [Short-pair span pruning for Problem 4](#problem4-short-pair-span):
tau(P4)=4 gives compression at most (2*4-1)+4=11, while a cover number
above four prevents any independent (n-4)-set and gives compression at
most four.

At P5, cover number above four likewise prevents an independent initial
set and is impossible. Suppose it is exactly four. The independent
(n-4)-sets are maximum independent sets. Their row space W has dimension
D<=7 by the maximum-independent-set rank lemma. Since 7<n, the short-pair
span bound gives compression at most D+5. Compression length at least
12 therefore forces D=7.

Use the notation of the rank lemma: a maximum set I, its four-vertex
complement C, the union U of all tight exchanges in C, and B=N_I(U).
One has |B|<=|U|<=4 and row rank at most |U|+|B|. If |U|=|B|=4, the
perfect-matching equality case bounds the rank by five. Thus rank seven
forces |U|=4 and |B|=3. In particular U=C. Every vertex of I minus B has
no neighbor in C (by definition of B) or in I (by independence), so is
isolated. All edges are on the seven vertices C union B. The induced
graph has independence number three and maximum-independent-set row
rank seven. There are exactly n-7 isolated vertices: the seven variable
coordinates cannot be isolated, since an isolated vertex belongs to
every maximum set and would not vary. Fixed isolated coordinates equal
one on each maximum set; they are recovered linearly as one third of
the sum of the seven core coordinates, so full row rank equals the core
row rank, namely seven.

The complete seven-vertex classification below shows that this graph is
C7. This reduction has no edge-count cap on P2,P3,P4 or P5 and does not
use the retracted higher-layer refinement cuts.

A seven-cycle has exactly seven independent triples. One way to enumerate
them is to record the cyclic gaps between selected vertices: they are
2,2,3, giving the seven rotations. Every word w of length at most six
preserves cardinality n-4 and has an independent P5 image; otherwise w
followed by at most five letters compresses before length twelve. Thus
R6 lies in this seven-set family. The families R_i of all images reached
within i letters grow strictly before compression: a plateau makes the
family invariant under all letters, incompatible with synchronization.
Hence |R6|>=7, and the family is fully reached. Its intersection is exactly
the isolated vertices. Local safety through six forces A into that
intersection.

<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy--complete-seven-vertex-classification"></a>
#### Complete seven-vertex classification

Among all 2^21=2,097,152 labeled simple graphs on seven vertices,
1,353,096 have independence number three. Exactly 360 of these have
maximum-independent-set row rank seven; all are the (7-1)!/2 labeled
seven-cycles.

`audit_seven_vertex_rank.cpp` enumerates every edge mask, constructs all
independent sets by deletion recurrence, and computes rank by exact
integer elimination with gcd normalization. It also checks directly that
every full-rank survivor is connected and 2-regular with seven edges.

`audit_seven_vertex_rank_independent.cpp` enumerates masks in reverse order,
tests all independent triples and quadruples directly, and computes full
rank modulo 11 or 13. This is exact over Q: every 7-by-7 minor has rows
of norm sqrt(3), so its absolute determinant is at most 3^(7/2)<11*13.
If both modular ranks were below seven, every minor would be divisible by
143 and hence zero. Conversely a nonzero modular minor is nonzero over Q.
No probabilistic modular-rank assumption is made.

`check_seven_vertex_rank.py --rerun` rebuilds and compares both complete
enumerations, including all 360 survivor codes. It independently generates
the labeled cycles from vertex permutations, checks every cycle and its
5,040 one-chord variants with ordinary integer row rank, and tests 1,000
seeded random graphs. Source and output hashes are in
`seven_vertex_rank_check.json`. These controls support the two complete
enumerations; they are not used to extrapolate to larger graphs. The
uniform reduction above is what restricts the graph to seven vertices.

<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy--canonical-synthesis-of-the-c7-branch"></a>
#### Canonical synthesis of the C7 branch

At (13,9,1),target12 normalize the core cycle as

  0,3,1,4,2,5,6,0.

P4 is a proper subgraph of P5, because otherwise its cover number would
be four. Choose a missing cycle edge and place it at {5,6}; then the
remaining six-edge path has vertex cover {0,1,2}. This normalization is
compatible with the earlier P4 cover cut, and every cycle branch admits
it by relabeling. Outside pairs have distance strictly above five; the
seven cycle pairs have distance at most five. Lower potentials alone
cannot enforce the latter: the synthesis also caps their independently
decreasing synchronization ranks at five, forcing actual distances <=5.

The --cycle-five option is only this branch, not all automata with target
twelve. Both singular binary letters and arbitrary finite alphabets remain
permitted; no common kernel, fixed rank, or permutation letter is assumed.
The local equality flags may be imposed only when target=n-r. A timeout or
uncertified solver failure does not exclude the branch.

<a id="problem4-codimension-four-p5-dichotomy--exclusion-of-the-cycle-branch-by-a-complete-six-image-lemma"></a>
#### Exclusion of the cycle branch by a complete six-image lemma

Let C be a seven-cycle and J a set of k isolated vertices. Let F be the
seven sets J union T, where T runs over the independent triples of C.
Suppose a transformation f has no colliding pair outside the edges of C
and maps six distinct members of F into F, preserving their cardinality.
Then f is a permutation; in fact it preserves J and acts on C as a cycle
automorphism. Here k>=1 is arbitrary.

It suffices to omit one fixed triple: rotation is transitive on the seven
triples. Label the cycle 0,1,...,6,0 and represent triples by bit masks.
They are 21,37,41,42,74,82,84; omit 84. Form the six-row characteristic
matrix of the remaining triples. Write c_q for its six-bit column at q.
Every nontrivial fiber of f is a cycle edge, since a fiber is a clique
in its kernel graph and C has no triangles. Those edges form a matching.
Every isolated vertex is a singleton fiber. If the matching has c edges,
there are c empty output fibers.

The pattern of a core fiber is the sum of its input columns. Adjacent
columns have disjoint supports because all six input triples are
independent; thus this sum is a six-bit Boolean pattern. Each isolated
input vertex contributes an all-one column, independently of its output
location. The six output sets contain every isolated vertex, so their
isolated output columns are also all one. Cancel these k identical
columns from the input-fiber and output-column multisets. What remains
is precisely this finite condition on seven output columns:

  {core output columns}
    = {core fiber patterns} multiset-union {c zero columns}.

There are 29 cycle matchings and 7^6=117,649 assignments of an output
triple to each input row. Exact enumeration admits only 14 combinations,
all with empty matching. Their output-column patterns are the seven
distinct original patterns and their row maps are precisely the cycle
automorphisms. This proves f is a permutation for every k. In particular
no isolated vertex can be sent into the core: the accepted core output
columns have weights two or three, whereas an isolated input contributes
weight six. Likewise no core input can be sent outside.

`check_cycle_seven_six_images.py` implements the complete multiset
enumeration and reconstructs its 14 surviving core maps. The independent
`audit_cycle_seven_six_images.cpp` directly enumerates all literal maps
on the cycle plus ONE isolated vertex, with fibers consisting of a cycle
matching and remaining singletons. It tests all injective assignments of
fibers to output states and then literally applies each map to each of
the six input sets. Its counts, by core matching size 0,1,2,3, are
40,320;282,240;282,240;47,040, totaling 651,840. Its accepted counts are
14;0;0;0, and its surviving maps exactly match the multiset checker.
No probabilistic test or finite-state extrapolation is used: cancellation
of the k identical columns supplies the uniform reduction. Rebuild both
with `python check_cycle_seven_six_images.py --rerun`; hashes and exact
scopes are in `cycle_seven_six_images_audit.json`.

Apply the lemma to the earlier cycle branch. Before compression the
families R_i of images through depth i grow strictly: a plateau would
give an invariant family of non-singleton sets. Consequently R5 contains
at least six members of F, and every letter maps any six selected members
into R6 subset F, preserving cardinality. Its kernel is contained in
P1 subset P5=C plus isolated vertices. The lemma makes every letter a
permutation, contradicting synchronization. The cycle branch is therefore
excluded, and tau(P5)<=3 follows for n>=8, independently of alphabet
size and without initial-set reachability.

The earlier cycle-branch synthesis timeouts remain recorded as timeouts;
they are superseded by this structural exclusion, not used to prove it.

[Eliminating the maximal independent-set rank case](#problem4-odd-cycle-span-refinement) subsequently supplies a symbolic rank and
cyclic-interval proof of this transformation exclusion for every odd
cycle of length at least seven. The existing literal finite certificates
remain independent controls. The graph classification can also be
derived from the cited defect-one alpha-critical graph theorem; the
complete seven-vertex enumeration is no longer the only route to it.

<a id="problem4-collapsed-three-cover-obstruction"></a>
<a id="problem4-collapsed-three-cover-obstruction--a-three-state-short-pair-cover-cannot-collapse-into-an-isolated-point"></a>
### A three-state short-pair cover cannot collapse into an isolated point

This auxiliary statement is independent of alphabet size and initial
subset reachability. It gives no new numerical F value.

<a id="problem4-collapsed-three-cover-obstruction--credited-two-cover-p4-consequence"></a>
#### Credited two-cover P4 consequence

In a synchronizing automaton on n>=4 states, a two-state cover of P4
forces |P1|<=2. If three distinct immediate pairs existed, they admit
a length-three Frankl--Pin sequence of (n-2)-sets. For a current pair
e_j omit an endpoint outside e_j from each later pair, then extend
these at most two omissions to exactly two points outside e_j.
This is possible since n>=4. The resulting set T_j contains e_j
and omits at least one endpoint of every later pair. Hence each
later pair is not contained in any earlier set, as required.

The refinement of Kisielewicz--Kowalski--Szykula, CIAA2016,
Theorem1 bounds compression of every compressible (n-2)-set by
binomial(4,2)-3+1=4. The complement of the proposed cover has size
n-2>=2 and is compressible by synchronization, but contains no pair
merged within four letters. This is a contradiction. Strong connectivity
is unnecessary for this credited consequence. For n=3 the complement
is a singleton; the consequence must not be applied there.
The theorem and its convention for sequences/height are documented in
[Unique immediate pair under a two-state P5 cover](#problem4-two-cover-unique-immediate-pair); its primary reference is
https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-40946-7_15.
No priority claim for the refinement or this consequence is made.

<a id="problem4-collapsed-three-cover-obstruction--collapsed-cover-obstruction"></a>
#### Collapsed-cover obstruction

Let n>=4, synchronization, |P1|<=4, and let a three-state K cover P5.
There cannot be a letter f with f(K)={p} where p is isolated in P4.

The three K inputs give a triangle of immediate pairs. No other input
can join their kernel block: a four-state block would give six pairs,
contrary to |P1|<=4. There can be no other nontrivial block, because
it would give a pair entirely outside K, while K covers P1. Thus f
has exactly this three-state block and all other blocks are singletons.
Its rank is n-2, and its set M of omitted output states has size two.

[Passing a short-pair cover through a letter](#problem4-letter-image-short-pair-cover) applied at h=4 says f(K) union M
covers P4. Since p is isolated in P4, M itself is a two-state cover
of P4. The credited consequence above gives |P1|<=2, contradicting
the triangle already supplied by f. This proves the obstruction.
Missing outputs are essential; the proof does not assume a permutation
letter or rank-n-1 singular letters. |P1|<=4 is an explicit hypothesis,
not an extrapolated cap on P2,P3,P4.

<a id="problem4-collapsed-three-cover-obstruction--application-to-equality-at-1391"></a>
#### Application to equality at (13,9,1)

Suppose ac(S,{3})=12, |S|=9. Existing premises give c(S)>=12, a
cover H={0,1,2} of P5 and |P1|<=4. Every point mandatory through
depth4 is P7-isolated, by [Isolation of the mandatory core at the reaching depth](#problem4-mandatory-core-isolation), hence is
P4-isolated. The established first/second/third entrance suppliers
and their one-count depths therefore exclude:

* B=H: its supplier sends H into protected3 (mandatory through11).
  This excludes every B3-in joint, independently of C and D.
* B singleton and C=H: the second supplier sends H into B
  (mandatory through10). This excludes the whole b1_out_c6 joint.
* C singleton and D=H: the third supplier sends H into C
  (mandatory through9). This excludes that whole third geometry,
  while other D geometries in its joint remain unproved.

Incomparability places these singleton targets outside H. All finite
alphabets, all Boolean companion fibers, and simultaneous suppliers
are covered. Initial reachability is unnecessary for the obstruction;
the paper's stronger requirements on any attaining example remain.
