<a id="problem4-common-collapsing-block-trap"></a>
<a id="problem4-common-collapsing-block-trap--a-common-collapsing-block-traps-the-pair-closure"></a>
### A common collapsing block traps the pair closure

Let a complete deterministic automaton have n states and a nonempty
finite alphabet. Let2<=|D|<n and c not in D. Suppose every letter has
exact preimage ell^{-1}({c})=D, and some K contained in D is a vertex
cover of P2, the pairs mergeable within two letters. Then

    P_h = binom(D,2) for every h>=1.

In particular the automaton is not synchronizing. Strong connectivity
and initial-image reachability are not needed for this necessary cut.

Proof. Every letter collapses D to c. A mixed D/outside-D pair cannot
collide, by the exact-preimage assumption. An outside-D pair cannot
collide because both endpoints lie outside K, which covers P1 subset P2.
Thus P1 is precisely binom(D,2), and each letter is injective on Q-D.
For a letter ell, R=ell^{-1}(D) is disjoint from D because c not in D.
If |R|>=2, a pair outside K maps into D and is then merged by any
second letter, contrary to the P2 cover. Hence |R|<=1 for every letter.
The usual pair recurrence P_(h+1)=P1 union all letter inverse pairs
of P_h now stays at binom(D,2): no distinct pair can map into D.
Since D is proper, at least one pair involving Q-D never merges.
This proves the conclusion for arbitrary finite alphabets.

All assumptions are essential to this proof. Omitting the P2-cover
condition admits[2,2,3,3],D01,c2, reset aa. Omitting c outside D admits
[0,0,1],D01,c0,K01, reset aa. Omitting the common-preimage condition
admits a=[2,2,0],b=[1,2,0],D01,c2,K01, reset aba.
The independent checker verifies these literal boundary controls.

At(13,9,1) in the B0/C4 joint, K12 covers P5 and hence P2. For D12
or D125, K is contained in D and4 is outside D. Therefore the two
letters cannot both have preC=D. In each complete eight-row parent
inventory this excludes exactly five originally admitted odd/odd
pairs: (1,7),(3,5),(3,7),(5,7),(7,7). The cut also forbids any larger
alphabet in which every letter has that same preC; it does not exclude
those third geometries for unrestricted alphabets, where a different
letter can be included. No numerical alphabet separation follows.

The uniform proof above is authoritative. Independent finite checks
normalize c=n-1 and D=0..d-1 at3<=n<=6,2<=d<n. They enumerate every
outside-D injection into Q-c and every two/three-letter tuple after
the necessary |pre(D)|<=1 condition. Relabelling supplies every labelled
choice. Literal pair closure and selected separate forward pair searches
confirm the trapped clique; these finite checks do not replace the
all-n proof. Both numerical extrema at(13,9,1) remain unclassified.

<a id="problem4-compression-cover-floor"></a>
<a id="problem4-compression-cover-floor--a-compression-bound-floor-for-short-pair-covers"></a>
### A compression-bound floor for short-pair covers

9 October 2026. This is a direct use of the known Frankl--Pin bound,
not a new compression theorem or a new value of F. It excludes the
whole joint B={0},C={1} at (13,9,1), for every finite alphabet.

Let P_h have as edges pairs merged by words of length at most h in
a strongly connected synchronizing n-state automaton. Suppose Z is
a vertex cover of P_h, |Z|=k and n-k>=2. The auxiliary set Q minus Z
has no pair merged within h, hence no word of length at most h
compresses it. But the Frankl--Pin theorem compresses every subset T
of size at least two in at most binomial(n-|T|+2,2) letters. Thus

    binomial(k+2,2) <= h  implies that Z cannot cover P_h.       (1)

The case k=0 is included: synchronization needs a singular letter.
The restriction n-k>=2 is essential; singleton subsets do not compress.
Strong connectivity and synchronization are retained throughout,
matching the cited theorem's hypotheses. The auxiliary set Q minus Z
need not be a reachable image: the known theorem applies to every
subset. This does not relax the paper's requirements on the original S.

For example, tau(P3)>=2 when n>=3. In the thirteen-state investigation
tau(P5)>=2, tau(P6)>=3 and tau(P10)>=4. These lower bounds concern
vertex cover size, not the earlier retracted edge-cardinality caps.

The precise source is Szykula (STACS2018), Theorem1, p.56:2, which
restates the Frankl--Pin theorem for arbitrary finite alphabets:
https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol096-stacs2018/LIPIcs.STACS.2018.56/LIPIcs.STACS.2018.56.pdf
The formula and subset-size hypothesis were independently checked
against that primary PDF on9October2026. There is no priority claim
for (1), an immediate consequence of this existing theorem.

<a id="problem4-compression-cover-floor--stripping-protected-points-from-the-thirteen-state-h-cover"></a>
#### Stripping protected points from the thirteen-state H-cover

Assume ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9, n=13. The established compression
dichotomy supplies a cover H of P5 with at most three states, enlarged
to H={0,1,2}; a=3 is outside H. The first and second entrances meet
all images once through depths ten and nine, respectively.

If B={b}, every safe image through ten contains b. If C={c}, every
safe image through nine contains c. These states are distinct from a
and, when both are singletons, distinct from each other. For any
protected set X contained in every image through depth nine,

    ac(S,X)>=10, ac(S,X)<=4+d_X,

where d_X is the shortest merging length of a pair incident to X.
The second inequality is [A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag)'s protected-pair bound.
Consequently d_X>=6: X is isolated in P5. This argument does not assume
equality of ac(S,X) unless it follows separately from its upper bound.

Remove from H every singleton B point and singleton C point. All
those points are isolated in P5; the remainder is still a cover.
If its size is at most one, (1) contradicts that cover, since the
compression bound for a twelve-set is three, and three<=five.

<a id="problem4-compression-cover-floor--whole-joint-b0-c1"></a>
#### Whole joint B={0}, C={1}

Here X={3,0,1} is protected through depth nine, so 0,1 are isolated
in P5. The H-cover reduces to {2}. Apply the known compression bound
to Q minus {2}, of size twelve. It compresses within three letters,
giving an edge of P3 outside {2}; this is an edge of P5 as well,
contradicting the claimed one-point cover. This excludes the whole
joint b1_in_c2, independently of every third/fourth entrance and
independently of alphabet size. Initial reachability is unnecessary.

In particular the original third profiles D={2},{4},{2,4} are all
excluded. There is also a separate immediate obstruction in D={2}:
the four singleton states 3,0,1,2 are protected through eight and
therefore isolated in P4. Every immediate collision must touch H,
but all H states are isolated, so every letter is a permutation.
Synchronization is impossible. The whole-joint argument above is
stronger and avoids separate row or kernel classifications.

An independent labelled audit of the intact43 joint orbits strips
protected singleton points and applies (1). Only b1_in_c2 is newly
excluded this way: six labelled ordered pairs (B,C) inside H. It
preserves all other joint records; in particular a two-point cover
of P5 is not rejected, since its Frankl--Pin bound is six, above five.

<a id="problem4-compression-cover-floor--scope-and-verification"></a>
#### Scope and verification

The symbolic argument uses the known compression theorem and the
previously proved protected isolation and H-cover. Finite controls
check (1) on complete small binary and ternary row domains, selected
larger alphabets, and all290 verified frontier examples. They also
compare cover tests with shortest pair and actual-subset compression
search. These controls supplement the proof; they are not a complete
thirteen-state automaton scan or a new all-parameter formula for F.

Counting only the whole-joint exclusion, binary joint cases are23 and
unrestricted42; binary third admission would be158 orbits /842 pairs.
Both extrema at(13,9,1) remain[11,12]; no numerical alphabet separation
or complete answer follows. The accepted paper and release are unchanged.

For a fixed admitted B,C,D, let T be the family of all nine-sets
containing3 and meeting B,C,D once, and let X be their intersection.
Every actual image through eight belongs to this family, so contains
X. Each point of X is therefore isolated in P4: apply ac(S,{x})>=9
and ac(S,{x})<=4+d_x to get d_x>=5. Since H covers P4 as well as
P5, H minus X is a cover of P4. If at most one H point remains,
(1) gives a contradiction. This uses P4, not P5: the D one-count
condition is only guaranteed through eight. Possible additional
Boolean fibers merely restrict T and cannot invalidate this necessary
intersection condition; none is assumed absent.

given by [Fourth entrances for the five nonsingleton D types in B0/C14](#problem4-b1-c14-nonsingleton-d-fourth). These two types have no
additional Boolean companion. This note does not assert an F value.

Fix states0..6 and let the group permute ordinary states7..12. This
group preserves A,B,C,D,E,K, every input/output membership atom,
the literal nine-set family, mandatory protection and every depth
condition. All actual letters are injective outside K={1,2}; in
particular, each target has at most one ordinary source preimage.

For a letter f, enumerate all 6!=720 bijections g fixing0..6, form
the conjugate f' with f'(g(q))=g(f(q)), and retain the lexicographically
least row. Emit one of its witnessing bijections. This is the entire
ordinary-label group, not a graph-isomorphism heuristic. All members
of one orbit have the same least row; the identity is included.

Only the first letter is replaced by such a representative. For every
actual pair(f,h), the simultaneously conjugated pair(f',g h g^{-1})
has the same properties and remains in the same two atom fields.
Enumerating all produced first-letter representatives and every literal
second-letter row therefore covers every actual binary pair. Both
initial-image masks are recomputed in the representative coordinates;
transporting only one letter would not justify a pair reduction.

Every retained raw row has an explicit emitted permutation witness.
The independent scanner verifies that witness pointwise, verifies
bijectivity/fixed states, checks every resulting atom and pure-letter
condition, and transports each literal initial nine-set mask. It does
not call or copy the least-row selection procedure. Thus each retained
row is demonstrably conjugate to a scanned representative, including
possible duplicate representatives of the same orbit.

Raw rows are independently enumerated by fieldwise outside-K injections
and by per-input recursion. P7 mandatory isolation and P5 outside-K
nonmerging are necessary pure-letter cuts. Every potential initial
nine-set must preserve rank and3 through11 and stay in the literal
family through7. The family sizes are36 and27; masks use uint64_t,
including a control that exercises bit35. Empty exact row domains
are checked literally, not replaced by incoming-capacity estimates.

One coupled scanner uses reverse pair BFS and forward/reverse state
reachability, the other scalar forward pair relaxation and Boolean
state transitive closure. A negative requires completed scans and
complete parent-field coverage. A positive additionally requires exact
avoid-or-compress BFS and actual Q-to-S reachability. No uninvoked
candidate function certifies a model. Binary negatives do not transfer
to unrestricted alphabets.

<a id="problem4-early-pair-types"></a>
<a id="problem4-early-pair-types--necessary-early-pair-types-for-tight-compression"></a>
### Necessary early-pair types for tight compression

Put m=n-s>=3 and T=binom(m+2,2). If a synchronizing automaton has an
s-set of shortest compression length T, [Necessary short-pair structure for tight compression](#problem4-short-pair-structure) gives
|P_h|<=h for h<=m. Conversely P_1 is nonempty and the closures P_h grow
strictly until all pairs are present. A plateau would be an inverse-closure
fixed point and persist forever, contrary to synchronization. Therefore
|P_h|=h for h<=m. In particular there are ordered distinct pairs E_1,E_2,E_3
with P_h={E_1,...,E_h} for h=1,2,3.

Every letter is a permutation or a rank-(n-1) transformation with the common
kernel E_1. Write E_1={0,1}. Up to simultaneous state relabeling the ordered
three pairs, for n>=6, have precisely these nine types:

| type | E_2 | E_3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | {0,2} | {1,2} |
| 1 | {0,2} | {0,3} |
| 2 | {0,2} | {1,3} |
| 3 | {0,2} | {2,3} |
| 4 | {0,2} | {3,4} |
| 5 | {2,3} | {0,2} |
| 6 | {2,3} | {0,4} |
| 7 | {2,3} | {2,4} |
| 8 | {2,3} | {4,5} |

Proof of completeness: E_2 shares one endpoint with E_1 or is disjoint.
In the first case normalize it to {0,2}; the ordered pair stabilizer fixes
0,1,2, and E_3 can be the remaining old edge, an edge from each of those
three vertices to one new vertex, or an edge on two new vertices.
In the disjoint case normalize E_2 to {2,3}. Its stabilizer independently
swaps the endpoints of the first two pairs. Thus E_3 joins the pairs,
joins either pair to a new point, or uses two new points. These give the
five and four types above. No missing-state or alphabet-size assumption
is used in this classification.

<a id="problem4-early-pair-types--type-1-is-incompatible-with-strong-connectivity"></a>
#### Type 1 is incompatible with strong connectivity

Suppose P_1={01}, P_2={01,02}, P_3={01,02,03}. For every letter f,
preimages of 01 are in P_2, and preimages of 02 are in P_3.

If f is a permutation, f^{-1}(01) is 01 or 02, and f^{-1}(02) is a
different edge of the three-edge star. Their intersection is {0}.
Since 01 and 02 also intersect at {0}, bijectivity gives f^{-1}(0)=0.
In particular no other state maps to 0 under f.

If f is singular, let d be its unique missing output and c the common
image of 0,1. If d is not in 01 and c is in 01, the preimages of 01 are
the two distinct pairs {0,z},{1,z}, for z outside {0,1}; both cannot lie
in P_2. If d and c are both outside 01, its unique preimage pair is
disjoint from {0,1}, again impossible in P_2. Hence d is 0 or 1.
If d=1, examine 02. When c is in 02, its two preimages {0,z},{1,z}
cannot both belong to P_3. When c is outside 02, its unique preimage
pair is disjoint from {0,1} and cannot belong to P_3. Thus d=0.
No state therefore maps to 0 under a singular letter.

Every letter either fixes 0 with no other incoming edge, or omits 0
entirely. State 0 is unreachable from every other state, contradicting
strong connectivity. The argument works for any alphabet size and any n
where this type is defined; it gives only a necessary exclusion.

<a id="problem4-entry-fiber-flag"></a>
<a id="problem4-entry-fiber-flag--a-common-entrance-fiber-for-the-protected-set"></a>
### A common entrance fiber for the protected set

8 October 2026. This is auxiliary structure at equality n-|A|, for arbitrary
finite alphabets. It gives no new extremal value and is outside the
manuscript release. It generalizes [A common predecessor fiber at singleton equality](#problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag).

<a id="problem4-entry-fiber-flag--proposition"></a>
#### Proposition

Let a strongly connected synchronizing automaton satisfy
ac(S,A)=t=n-r, where r=|A|>=1 and g=|S|-r>=3. Then there is a nonempty
set B contained in Q minus A with |S intersect B|=1 such that, for every
letter ell and protected output a in A, the preimage ell^(-1)(a) is
either a singleton {p} with p in A, or exactly B. At least one letter
uses B. In a letter using B, exactly one protected output receives B;
the other r-1 receive distinct protected singleton predecessors, and
exactly one protected input is sent outside A. A letter not using B
permutes A and has no outside predecessor of a protected output.

For g=2 the corresponding proven description permits B and its
complement (Q minus A) minus B, each meeting S in one point, in place
of only B. At most two protected outputs can receive outside fibers
in the same letter. No assertion for g=1 is made.

Initial-set reachability is not used. If |P1|<=4, a letter using B
merges all its pairs, giving |B|<=3 in the g>=3 case.

<a id="problem4-entry-fiber-flag--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Put s=|S| and let V_i be the real span of characteristic trajectory rows
chi_S D_w for |w|<=i. The equality flag gives dim V_i=i+1 for
0<=i<=t-1. In particular the annihilator K of V_(t-2) has dimension
n-(t-1)=r+1. It contains the r independent columns

  h_a=s e_a-1,  a in A.

Their independence follows by inspecting a coordinate outside A and
then the coordinates in A. For each letter ell and a in A it also
contains d_(ell,a)=chi_(ell^(-1)(a))-e_a. Indeed every word w of length
at most t-2 and its extension w ell are safe. Their characteristic
image rows contain each protected state once, so multiplication by
d_(ell,a) has value zero. Safety guarantees no collision; using set
images without that fact would not justify this linear identity.

Every protected preimage C is nonempty and |S intersect C|=1. If it
contains p in A and another point q, then every image through depth
t-2 omits q, or the next letter would collide p and q. But every state
is reached from some state of S within n-s steps by strong connectivity,
and n-s<=t-2 when g>=2. Thus such a preimage is exactly {p}. Every other
protected preimage is a nonempty subset of Q minus A.

Restrict columns in K to O=Q minus A. The span of the h_a restricts to
the one-dimensional space of constant columns; hence the image of K
under restriction has dimension at most two. An outside preimage C
restricts d_(ell,a) to its Boolean indicator chi_C. Some outside
preimage B must occur: otherwise every letter permutes A, making the
proper nonempty A closed, contrary to strong connectivity. Also B is
proper in O, since |S intersect B|=1 while |S minus A|=g>=2.
Therefore the restricted space has basis 1_O,chi_B.

The only Boolean vectors in span{1_O,chi_B} are 0,1_O,chi_B and
chi_(O minus B): their values are constant separately on the two
nonempty parts B and O minus B. A protected outside preimage cannot be
empty or O, by its intersection size one. If g>=3 it also cannot be
O minus B, since that set meets S in g-1>=2 points. Thus B is the only
outside preimage. For g=2 both complementary fibers are allowed.

Distinct outputs in a deterministic letter have disjoint preimages,
so B can be used by at most one protected output (at most two outputs
for the complementary-fiber case). If B is used, all the other r-1
outputs have distinct predecessors in A. The one remaining protected
input cannot have an output in A, and is the unique input sent outside.
Without B, all r protected outputs have their distinct predecessors in
A and the restriction is a permutation. Finally binomial(|B|,2)<=|P1|
gives the stated size bound. QED.

<a id="problem4-entry-fiber-flag--controls-and-scope"></a>
#### Controls and scope

The singleton audit completely covers all first-letter conjugacy types
paired with every labelled second letter at n=4,5,6. It checks all
relevant initial subsets, including unreachable ones, without stopping
when an extremal value is attained. At n=6 there are 6,065,280 row pairs,
2,759 singleton equality instances, including 1,025 with |S|>=4.
An independent literal-set checker reproduces the n=4 counts and checks
22 singleton frontier certificates. It verifies the g=2 counterexample
with n=4, S={0,1,3}, A={1}, rows [0,2,1,1] and [1,2,3,0]: preimages
of 1 are {2,3} and {0}, and the local value is three. S is reachable.

The general checker independently recomputes the exact value and the
annihilator restrictions on every applicable frontier certificate;
this includes 67 witnesses with g>=3 and protected sizes through seven.
These checks support the proof above and do not extrapolate a finite
classification to arbitrary alphabets or n. General search failures
using the entrance-fiber condition remain diagnostics, never uppers.

<a id="problem4-entry-fiber-flag--protected-pair-isolation"></a>
#### Protected-pair isolation

For any strongly connected synchronizing automaton and any nonempty
A subsetneq S, put m=n-|S| and let d_A be the minimum shortest merging
length among pairs with at least one endpoint in A. Then

  ac(S,A)<=m+d_A.

Choose such a pair {a,q}, with a in A. A path from some input in S
reaches q in at most m steps. If that word is unsafe, the required
avoid-or-compress word is already at most m long. Otherwise its image
contains both a and q, so appending a shortest merging word compresses
it within m+d_A steps. Synchronization makes every pair distance finite.
No reachable-image assumption is used.

Consequently equality ac(S,A)=n-r forces every pair touching A to have
merging distance at least |S|-r. Thus A is isolated in P_(|S|-r-1).
The checker verifies this on all 112 applicable frontier certificates.
At (13,9,1), A is isolated in P7. A cover of P5 can therefore be selected
and enlarged to three vertices outside A; the canonical protected state
3, outside the cover {0,1,2}, alone covers all witnesses up to relabeling.
The old protected-state-0 slice is redundant, not a proved empty slice.

<a id="problem4-exact-atom-kernel-compatibility"></a>
<a id="problem4-exact-atom-kernel-compatibility--exact-rank-n-1-kernels-in-a-membership-atom-field"></a>
### Exact rank-n-1 kernels in a membership-atom field

Let (I_i) and (O_i) be indexed partitions of a finite nonempty Q,
allowing empty atoms. A field requires f(I_i) contained in O_i.
A permutation realizes the field exactly when |I_i|=|O_i| for
every i. For a specified unordered pair e, a rank-|Q|-1 map with
that sole kernel pair realizes it exactly when:

* both endpoints of e belong to one input atom I_j;
* |I_i|-1_(i=j) <= |O_i| for every i.

Necessity follows from the disjoint output atoms and injectivity on
the quotient identifying e. Sufficiency follows by injecting each
input-atom quotient into its corresponding output atom independently.
These injections have disjoint images; the sole repeated fiber is e.
The statement applies to arbitrary atom counts, overlaps in the sets
defining memberships, and empty atoms. It asserts exact letter
realizability only, never realizability of an automaton or equality.

For a nonempty guard set K and protected set J, a realizable
permutation or specified-kernel letter can satisfy f(K) not contained
in J exactly when some output atom corresponding to a K endpoint
has an element outside J. If no such element exists, every K image
is protected. Conversely choose one guard quotient block's image
outside J, and complete the remaining injections in each atom.
The atom capacity conditions ensure completion after this choice.
If both guards belong to e, they represent the same quotient block.

At(13,9,1), retain only third geometries with an explicit two-state
P5 cover K after stripping their literal mandatory core J. Unique
P1 forces every letter to be a permutation or a rank12 map with
one global kernel e, meeting K and avoiding J. Cover transfer forbids
f(K) contained in J, since J is isolated in P7, hence P3. Apply the
exact atom criteria to each native field and each proposed global e.
Every actual equality alphabet must have all three entrance suppliers
and at least one singular letter in one surviving e class. A formal
binary pair must have both compatible fields and at least one possible
singular field in the same class. These are necessary overapproximations
of automata; no SC or subset-reachability claim follows from admission.
All covered Boolean companion fields remain in the inventory.

Seven newly removed current unrestricted types have short direct
reasons, independently matched by the finite field audit:

| type | contradiction |
| b1_out_c4_third1 | C=K={0,1} enters protected B={4} |
| b1_in_c3_third7 | global kernel14 is forced by preB=C14, but supplying preC=D125 must collide inside D125, which omits4 |
| b1_in_c4_third1 / third2 | C=K={1,2} enters protected B={0} |
| b2_in_c1_third1 / b2_in_c2_third1 / b2_in_c4_third1 | B=K={0,1} enters protected A={3} |

For D125 above, mapping three inputs into the two C14 outputs forces
a collision. Its pair cannot be the global14 kernel. Supplier letters
may coincide or differ; the global kernel is common to all singular
letters. The cover-image arguments use the actual supplier mappings.

The complete atom control compares the criteria with every labelled
map for n2..4 and one through four indexed atoms, including all
protected sets for fixed two-state K. The third checker independently
reconstructs every literal mandatory family and membership atom,
then checks all global kernels on the intact historical inventory.
Current counts are computed separately against previous cuts. These
results do not determine F(13,9,1), a full formula or alphabet separation.

<a id="problem4-extended-binary-obstruction-proof"></a>
<a id="problem4-extended-binary-obstruction-proof--the-two-additional-binary-exceptions-at-n12"></a>
### The two additional binary exceptions at n=12

The exact conclusions are F_bin(12,9,1)=F_bin(12,9,2)=9. The unrestricted
maxima remain in [9,10]. This is a finite result, not a codimension-three
upper bound for arbitrary n or alphabets.

The uniform codimension-three family gives reachable-image binary lower
examples nine with all structural requirements. The completed cover proves
that every nine-set in a binary strongly connected synchronizing twelve-state
automaton compresses within nine. Therefore it applies to every allowed A.

<a id="problem4-extended-binary-obstruction-proof--mathematical-reduction-and-the-extra-safe-prune"></a>
#### Mathematical reduction and the extra safe prune

Use the Frankl--Pin refinement from Kisielewicz, Kowalski and Szykuła,
Experiments with Synchronizing Automata, CIAA 2016, Theorem 1. As in
[The binary sharpness requirement at (11,8,1)](#problem4-binary-obstruction-proof), two distinct immediate kernel pairs give
compression at most T-1=9 when m=n-s=3 and T=binom(m+2,2)=10. A potential
length-ten example therefore has only one common kernel pair K. After
exchanging letters, a has rank n-1; b is a permutation or rank n-1 with K.

Let P_h be all pairs merging within h original letters. Any q<=m+1
distinct pairs admit a length-q Frankl--Pin sequence: for the ith pair E_i,
choose m holes outside E_i, hitting an endpoint of each later pair. There
are at most q-i-1<=m required endpoints, and n-2>=m permits filling the
holes. The resulting s-set contains E_i and no later pair.
Consequently |P_h|>=h+1, for 1<=h<=m, yields p(P_h)>=h+1 and compression
at most T-p(P_h)+h<=T-1. A tight example must have |P_h|<=h at h=1,2,3.
Both new covers use this extra prune only when their target equals T.
Partial reverse closures contain only genuine merging words. Completion
can only add pairs, so both this prune and the three-hole cover prune are
monotone and safe.

Synchronization also forces strict growth of P_h until all pairs occur:
a plateau is an inverse-closure fixed point and would remain a plateau
forever. Thus a tight synchronizing example actually has |P_h|=h for
h<=m. The complete covers need only the weaker inequalities above.

<a id="problem4-extended-binary-obstruction-proof--first-letter-forms-and-two-independent-enumerations"></a>
#### First-letter forms and two independent enumerations

The rank-(n-1) functional-graph classification in the earlier proof applies
unchanged. If its transient path has length h>=4, a^4 has rank n-4 and
compresses every (n-3)-set. The remaining forms have h=1,2,3, all cycle
lengths and all integer partitions of n-h-L. At n=12 this gives 303 forms.

compression_decision_extended.cpp widens the first cover and assigns b
successors in forward component-discovery order. It uses inverse-fiber
pair BFS, a disjoint-matching check and exact recursive vertex covers.

compression_decision_inverse.cpp uses the separately implemented bitset
closure and literal masks of all 220 three-point complements from
compression_decision_extended_independent.cpp. Its enumeration differs:
it assigns inverse b-fibers of discovered OUTPUT states.
In permutation mode each output has one unused preimage. In singular mode
one output has no preimage, one has exactly K, and every other output has
one unused source outside K. These are precisely all transformations with
the required rank and kernel.

Begin with the entire path-cycle component of a discovered. First reverse
b-entrance into an unused a-cycle normalizes its preimage to the cycle's
first vertex using rotation; equal-length unused cycles can be exchanged.
Append the entire cycle in a-order. These are automorphisms of a fixing
all discovered vertices. Strong connectivity implies that reverse discovery
eventually reaches every a-component, so no allowed strongly connected b
is omitted. The recursion discards branches that stop discovering vertices
before all n outputs can be assigned.

The adaptive priority selects only already discovered outputs: endpoints
of known short pairs are discovered, since inverse a stays within a
discovered component and inverse b uses only already assigned preimages.
Reordering discovered outputs changes neither available fiber assignments
nor the normalization of unused cycles. It therefore loses no branch.
Full strong connectivity is checked in BOTH directions from state zero;
pair mergeability is checked by closure to all binom(n,2) pairs. Actual
reachable images are inspected if any delayed set survives. No such
strongly connected synchronizing map survives the short-pair/hole test.

The inverse implementation includes the widened independent source; all
three source files must be present when compiling it. The included old
entry point is renamed and never called.

<a id="problem4-few-graph-first-pair-certificates"></a>
<a id="problem4-few-graph-first-pair-certificates--complete-first-pair-certificates-with-arbitrary-retained-class-counts"></a>
### Complete first-pair certificates with arbitrary retained class counts

These certificates are conditional at (n,s,r,ac)=(13,9,1,12), for
strongly connected synchronizing complete automata over any finite
alphabet. They do not give a numerical F value or an alphabet separation.
The current authority and selected geometries are specified by a frozen
scope, not by mutable live-state reads during enumeration.

The premises and equality-flag induction are those of
[Five B2 sibling exclusions at the remaining thirteen-state point](#problem4-b2-column-first-pair-exclusion) and [Equality flags for the avoid-or-compress bound](#problem4-local-equality-flag). Each native
immediate graph domain is reconstructed by check_b1_b2_inverse_union.
All graph classes rejected there have a checked missing supplier or
proper closed set, including every labelled D transport. No assumption
is made about the number of retained classes; every retained class must
occur in the scope and in the independent checker.

In each class enumerate ALL ordered distinct feasible nine-sets S,T.
An actual extremizer has dim V1=2, with a basis of these two actual
images. Relabelling preserves H,A,B,C,D, the mandatory intersection and
each individual native field. The whole immediate graph, all exact
kernel masks, the P3 subgraph and both images are transported together.
The checker independently rebuilds every labelled pair, permutation and
representative multiplicity. The representatives need not be a minimal
orbit transversal.

For each representative the generator enumerates literal maps by
output-atom bijections; the checker independently assigns exact kernel
blocks to output states. Full sorted-row and supplier-flag hashes must
coincide. At each equality-flag node every possible next independent
image of its last basis row is explored, and all permitted Boolean
vertices in the enlarged span are retained. Every required supplier
must survive. A true actual alphabet and its actual flag therefore
remain in some branch. A proper closed set in the union of all remaining
literal arrows contradicts strong connectivity of any actual alphabet.

Full-prefix column deductions apply only from flag depth four. Their
paper proof and audits remain separately bound. Forced-word propagation
uses explicit actual words of length at most eleven; it may reject a
letter only with a checked unsafe word, and may force a letter only
through a singleton required supplier group. The independent checker
reconstructs every deletion and every complete branch using Fraction
elimination. Modular generator elimination is exact by the previous
Hadamard bound for thirteen-column characteristic nine-set rows.

Depth eleven survivors are candidates and abort a negative certificate.
Its last basis row is never mapped under a depth-twelve safety premise.
Neither incomplete prefixes nor timeouts supply an exclusion. All four
prior binary profile-cut lists are preserved when composing exclusions.
A whole joint is removed only when no remaining geometry belongs to it.

Scope-specific generators and independent audits, immutable packaging,
byte-identical isolated regeneration and all historical source checks
gate adoption. Excluding all initial subsets is stronger than excluding
only actual reachable images, so the paper's reachability requirement
has not been weakened. Counts describe structural exclusions only;
both F values at (13,9,1) retain their recorded numerical intervals.

<a id="problem4-finite-independent-image-trap"></a>
<a id="problem4-finite-independent-image-trap--finite-independent-image-trap"></a>
### Finite independent-image trap

Auxiliary obstruction only. Let G be a graph on Q whose edges belong
to P_h, h>=1. Let K be a state set, a=|Q-K|>=2, and let N be the
number of G-independent a-element subsets. Suppose K covers P_(h+N).
Then the automaton is not synchronizing, for any finite alphabet.
Neither strong connectivity nor a reachable-image hypothesis is needed.

Put R=Q-K. The cover makes R independent in G, so N>=1. Every Rw
for |w|<=N has cardinality a: a collision would merge a pair outside K
within N<=h+N. Such an image is independent in G. Otherwise lift an
edge of G to two R inputs and append its merging word of length at
most h, contradicting the P_(h+N) cover.

All these short images belong to the N-element family I of independent
a-sets. Let F be the images reached within N-1. If F is not closed
under letters, some image X outside F is reached in N steps (a
shorter prefix would already put X in F). Its shortest reaching word
has length N. The N+1 prefix images along this shortest path are
distinct, yet all belong to I. This is impossible. Thus F is closed,
every reachable image of R belongs to I, and all have size a>=2.
A reset word for Q would reset R, which is impossible.

The count is of independent sets of the precise size a, not edges,
span dimension, or independent sets of every size. No claim is made
that every member of I occurs. Singleton R is excluded essentially.
This is an elementary subset-graph obstruction, with no priority claim.

The cases used in C4/D15 have a=n-2 and isolated states outside the
displayed active graph. Literal independent-set enumeration confirms:

* triangle126 with pendant edge15: N=2 (omitted pairs12 and16);
* path5-1-6-2: N=3 (omitted pairs12,16,56);
* path6-1-5-2: N=3 (omitted pairs12,15,56);
* star1-{5,6} and disjoint edge2-x, x not in {1,2,5,6}: N=2
  (omitted pairs12 and1x).

In each case every independent n-2-set includes all isolated states;
the count therefore does not depend on their number. With edges in
P2, N<=3 fits the established P5 cover. This lemma is a necessary
conditional obstruction, not an all-parameter formula or a new F value.

<a id="problem4-four-point-second-entrance-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-four-point-second-entrance-exclusion--excluding-the-four-point-second-entrance-at-1391"></a>
### Excluding the four-point second entrance at (13,9,1)

9 October 2026. Symbolic conditional binary exclusion; no new F value.

At (n,s,r)=(13,9,1), a binary strongly connected synchronizing automaton
with ac(S,{a})=12 cannot have normalized cover H={0,1,2}, a=3,
B={0,1,4}, C={0,1,2,5}. This excludes b3_mixed_c11. The argument
does not require the initial nine-set to be reachable.

The prior cover refinement supplies H covering P5. The five-pair
endpoint construction and cited Frankl--Pin refinement in
[The three-point first entrance cannot have singleton second entrance at (13,9,1)](#problem4-singleton-three-kernel-exclusion) give |P1|<=4. The first two
entrance identities force M^(-1)(a)=B, M^(-1)(B)={a},
F^(-1)(a)={a}, F^(-1)(B)=C. By [A forbidden backward crossing and the remaining three-point profile](#problem4-binary-third-entrance-crossing),
M^(-1)(C) cannot be {a}; it is a common third entrance D disjoint
from B, normalized as {6} or {2,6}. The private-point proof there
shows that F^(-1)(C) is B,C or D.

It cannot be B by the backward-crossing lemma. If it is D, the two
states in B intersect C={0,1} have predecessors under F only in
C intersect D, which has at most one point. M has no predecessor
of either state: its sole B output is aM in B minus C. At least one
of the two states has no predecessor under the binary alphabet,
contrary to strong connectivity.

It remains to exclude F^(-1)(C)=C. Then F(C) is contained in the
two-point intersection B intersect C. Partition the four C inputs
by their F-output. A block of at least three would contribute at
least three pairs, at most one of which is inside B, exceeding the
one-pair budget outside the already merged B triangle. Thus there
are exactly two blocks of two. One must be the pair {0,1} inside B,
and the other must be {2,5}. The outside pair budget is exhausted.
No two inputs outside C can collide, since only one of them belongs
to B. Moreover F preserves Q minus C. Therefore its restriction to
that nine-point complement is a permutation.

Every relevant short image is a nine-set meeting C and B once. It
consists of one C-point and all but one point h of Q minus C. Write
v=4, the single point in B minus C. If its C-point belongs to
B intersect C, then h=v. If its C-point belongs to C minus B,
then v is present and h is different from v.

Strong connectivity reaches a point of B intersect C and a point
of C minus B from S within n-s=4 steps. Apply F to the resulting
images, at total length at most five, where safety and both one-count
conditions hold. Both F-images have their C-point in B intersect C,
so each must omit v. In the first case this forces Fv=v; in the
second it forces Fh=v for h different from v. This contradicts the
proved injectivity of F on Q minus C. All alternatives are excluded.

The independent geometric audit checks all 59 labelled D sets for
this fixed B,C (eight stabilizer orbits) and all admissible Boolean
preimage columns, without assuming a common third fiber. It confirms
the private-point classification used above and the two moving-letter
possibilities. The proof itself is symbolic; no SAT answer, finite
search failure or numerical histogram is used as an upper bound.

There remain 31 binary and 43 unrestricted joint cases. The B3
mixed-cover branch retains c3 and c7, and c7 has the forced profile
above. The first unresolved extrema at (13,9,1) remain in [11,12].
No unrestricted-alphabet exclusion or numerical alphabet separation
has been proved; the article and release remain partial and unchanged.

<a id="problem4-joint-fiber-orbits"></a>
<a id="problem4-joint-fiber-orbits--joint-entrance-fiber-orbit-admission-at-1391"></a>
### Joint entrance-fiber orbit admission at (13,9,1)

9 October 2026. Necessary case inventory only. No upper certificate or
new exact value is asserted, and this note is outside the paper release.

For a putative twelve-step witness, use the normalized three-point
cover H={0,1,2} of P5 and protected point a=3. The first entrance B is
one of the six representatives in [Six normalized entrance-fiber cases at (13,9,1)](#problem4-six-entrance-fiber-slices).
The second entrance C is outside a, neither contains nor is contained
in B, and satisfies |B union C|<=5. If |B|=1 then |C|<=3;
otherwise |C|<=4.

An additional direct consequence is

  |C minus H|<=1.

Indeed C is a clique in P2 (in P1 when |B|=1), and H covers P5. Two
points of C outside H would give an uncovered edge. This uses cover
size, not an unproved cardinality bound on P2.

<a id="problem4-joint-fiber-orbits--group-action-and-complete-inventory"></a>
#### Group action and complete inventory

Once H,a,B are fixed, the remaining permitted relabelings act as the
full symmetric group independently on the four cells

  H intersect B, H minus B, (Q minus (H union {a})) intersect B,
  Q minus (H union {a} union B).

Thus the orbit of C is determined exactly by its four membership
counts. Equal counts permit a permutation taking one C to the other
inside each cell, and any permitted permutation preserves the counts.
The canonical representative takes the first required points of each
ordered cell. No restriction is placed on S beyond relabeling it along
with the automaton and the two fibers.

| Canonical B | Joint orbits | Labelled C for this fixed B |
|---|---:|---:|
| {4} | 6 | 63 |
| {0} | 5 | 39 |
| {0,4} | 12 | 73 |
| {0,1} | 6 | 57 |
| {0,1,4} | 11 | 71 |
| {0,1,2} | 3 | 63 |

There are 43 admitted joint orbits; 20 have intersecting B,C. Reinstating
all 70 first-fiber sets gives 4,806 labelled ordered pairs (B,C).
At this geometric-admission stage every orbit is retained. The bound
|B union C|<=5 and nonnesting also
permit a nine-element S containing a and meeting B,C once: choose one
point from each nonempty difference, and six points outside their union
and a. There are at least seven such outside points. Consequently this
inventory has not silently omitted a case by fixing S in advance.

enumerate_joint_fiber_orbits.py enumerates C for each representative B.
check_joint_fiber_orbits.py independently enumerates all labelled B,C
pairs and checks orbit sizes against the products of binomial cell
counts. This audit supports the group argument, not absence of an
automaton in any admitted orbit.

<a id="problem4-joint-fiber-orbits--adversarial-overlap-control"></a>
#### Adversarial overlap control

Take six states, a=0, B={1,2}, C={2,3}, with rows

  [1,0,0,4,5,3], [0,3,1,2,4,3].

The actual image of the first letter is S={0,1,3,4,5}. The automaton is
binary, strongly connected and synchronizing. The preimages of a are
B and {a}; the preimages of B are {a} and C; both fibers meet S once.
Yet B and C overlap. Ordinary BFS verifies these requirements and
ac(S,{a})=1. This is not an equality example. It refutes only the
attempt to exclude overlaps from these entrance identities and
structural requirements alone. The full equality hypothesis must not
be dropped in any further proposed exclusion.

<a id="problem4-letter-image-short-pair-cover"></a>
<a id="problem4-letter-image-short-pair-cover--passing-a-short-pair-cover-through-a-letter"></a>
### Passing a short-pair cover through a letter

Let P_h be the graph of distinct pairs merged by words of length at
most h; P_0 is empty. For any complete deterministic automaton, any
letter f, and any vertex cover K of P_(h+1), h>=0,

    f(K) union (Q minus Qf) covers P_h.                    (1)

Indeed, if a P_h edge {x,y} avoids both displayed sets, choose
preimages p,q of its endpoints under f. They are distinct, outside K,
and their pair merges by f followed by a word of length at most h.
This contradicts the cover of P_(h+1). No injectivity, synchronization,
strong connectivity, image reachability or alphabet restriction is
needed for (1). Omitted output states must be retained.

Now assume n>=4, synchronization, and a two-state K covering P5.
[Unique immediate pair under a two-state P5 cover](#problem4-two-cover-unique-immediate-pair), a credited application of the
known compression refinement, implies every letter has rank at least
n-1. Also P3 has no cover of size at most one: this follows from the
proved [P3 graphs under a two-state P5 cover](#problem4-two-cover-p3-classification) (or the one-cover compression
floor). Consequently no letter sends both K states to isolated
vertices of P3. Otherwise use (1) at h=3 and remove the isolated
vertices in f(K). Q minus Qf, of size at most one, covers P3, a
contradiction. The two K states may have the same image; (1) does not
count images with multiplicity.

This is an auxiliary cover observation and a necessary restriction,
not an extremal F formula or a new compression-bound claim. The
checker independently tests (1) on all labelled four-state maps and
graphs and on literal short-pair graphs in complete small binary and
ternary domains. It also checks the forbidden-image consequence and
retains an example showing why omitted outputs cannot be dropped.

<a id="problem4-localized-binary-entrance-kernel"></a>
<a id="problem4-localized-binary-entrance-kernel--localization-of-a-binary-moving-letter-kernel"></a>
### Localization of a binary moving-letter kernel

9 October 2026. Conditional equality structure; no new extremal value.
All notation and equality flags are as in [A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag),
[A second common entrance fiber at singleton equality](#problem4-second-entrance-fiber) and [Equality flags for the avoid-or-compress bound](#problem4-local-equality-flag). This note is outside
the manuscript release.

<a id="problem4-localized-binary-entrance-kernel--moving-letter-obstruction"></a>
#### Moving-letter obstruction

Suppose a binary strongly connected synchronizing automaton has
ac(S,{a})=n-1, s=|S|>=5, first entrance B of size k>=3, and second
entrance C. Suppose either C is a singleton, or C overlaps B and
|C minus B|=1. Then the letter M with preimage B of a cannot be
injective on Q minus B.

Indeed the singleton case forces M^(-1)(B)=C and F^(-1)(B)=B;
the overlapping case forces M^(-1)(B)={a} and F^(-1)(B)=C. In both
cases the other letter F fixes a and M is the unique moving letter.
The proofs in [A binary exclusion when the second entrance is a singleton](#problem4-binary-singleton-second-entrance-exclusion) and
[A binary exclusion for an entrance with one new point](#problem4-binary-near-equal-entrance-exclusion) use the P1-cover hypothesis
only to obtain injectivity of M outside B. Their remaining ingredients
are precisely the preimage identities, strong connectivity, the real
equality flag and the proved B,C cardinalities. Substituting outside
injectivity of M itself in those proofs gives the same contradictions.
In particular no assumption about the other letter's kernel is needed.

<a id="problem4-localized-binary-entrance-kernel--three-point-kernel-with-only-one-additional-collision-pair"></a>
#### Three-point kernel with only one additional collision pair

Now suppose |B|=3 and |P1|<=4. M merges the three pairs of B. Any
outside predecessor of a would enlarge that kernel block to four
points and contribute six pairs, impossible. No further kernel pair
can meet B. The moving-letter obstruction forces at least one pair
E outside B to be merged by M. The cap leaves exactly that one pair.
Thus the kernel of M consists of B, E and singleton blocks, and
rank(M)=n-3. The union of both letters' immediate collision pairs is
exactly binomial(B,2) union {E}; F has no other kernel pair.

For the singleton-C branch put T=SM. The proof of the previous
singleton exclusion establishes the B-quotient and injectivity of
B-coordinate projection on the real affine span through depth two,
without using any kernel-cover hypothesis. In particular

  SMM=SM=SFM.

These identities also hold in the overlapping one-new-point branch.
All three relevant images have the same B-point. For k=3, every
B-point is attained within two steps, making this projection injective.

Any two safe s-sets with the same M-image can differ only in their
selected B-point and in their selected E-point. Outside the two kernel
blocks M is injective, and their common output values are distinct
from all singleton-block output values. The first-level equality
flag has affine dimension one. Three distinct Boolean rows cannot
be collinear, so S,SM,SF take at most two distinct values.

Their outside-B parts cannot all agree: in that event the invariant
family proof (singleton C), or the quotient-category contradiction
(overlapping C), applies directly with that common outside part,
without requiring global outside injectivity. Consequently two of
S,SM,SF differ outside B. The M-image identities show that they swap
the E-point, and projection injectivity shows that they also have
different B-points. Besides T there is a unique other first-level
image U; T and U differ by one B-point and one E-point. Both meet E
once. M fixes T as a set and sends U to T.

For singleton C={c}, both sets contain c, so c is outside B union E.
Their common ordinary part contains a and c. The possible first-level
actions are exactly

  S=U, FU in {U,T}; or S=T, FT=U.

The cases where every first-level image equals S are excluded by the
equality flag, whose affine dimension at depth one is one.

<a id="problem4-localized-binary-entrance-kernel--complete-normalization-at-1391-singleton-c"></a>
#### Complete normalization at (13,9,1), singleton C

Label a=0, B={1,2,3}, E={4,5}, c=6, and choose

  T={0,1,4,6,7,8,9,10,11},
  U={0,2,5,6,7,8,9,10,11}; z=12.

The B-points of T,U are different; the two unselected B-points are
interchangeable, so this labeling loses no case. Since M is a
permutation on T, its forced arrows are 1,2,3 -> 0 and 6 -> 1.
It maps the remaining seven inputs {0,4,7,8,9,10,11} bijectively onto
{4,6,7,8,9,10,11}. Also 5M=4M. The only input remaining is z: its
output is outside T, not in B, and not a further collision, hence
zM is 5 or z. Arbitrary permutations of 7,8,9,10,11 preserve every
specified set, so conjugacy representatives of these M rows suffice.

F fixes 0, has F^(-1)(B)=B, and must realize one of the three
first-level actions above. On its specified nine-set L it is a
bijection onto its specified nine-set R: no word of length one is
unsafe. Its B-point image and 0-image are fixed; the other seven
outputs can be permuted freely. The two remaining B inputs have
outputs in B. Strong connectivity forces their images together with
the prescribed B image to include 2 and 3, which have no M predecessor.
The remaining E input can map to either unused non-B output or to
the selected E input's F-image. The remaining ordinary input z must
map to an unused non-B output. These choices must create no collision
outside the three B pairs and E. There are no other F choices.

This is a complete conditional row enumeration for the singleton-C,
three-point-B branch at (13,9,1), not a full enumeration of the other
entrance branches or of unrestricted alphabets. Ordinary subset BFS
and actual-image reachability still decide which enumerated rows
meet the original requirements. The same normalized row family at
smaller n is used only as a finite control of the enumerator.

<a id="problem4-local-equality-flag"></a>
<a id="problem4-local-equality-flag--equality-flags-for-the-avoid-or-compress-bound"></a>
### Equality flags for the avoid-or-compress bound

8 October 2026. Auxiliary necessary conditions for attaining n-r; no new
maximum or alphabet separation is asserted. No reachable-image assumption
is needed for these conditions.

Let a strongly connected synchronizing n-state automaton have |S|=s,
nonempty A subsetneq S of size r, and ac(S,A)=t=n-r. Put

  V_i = span_R {chi_S D_w : |w|<=i}.

For every 0<=i<=t-1 one has dim V_i=i+1. Indeed, all words of length at
most t-1 are safe. Hence these rows are characteristic rows of s-sets
containing A, and V_(t-1) is contained in the homogeneous subspace

  H = {x : x_q = (sum x)/s for q in A},  dim H=n-r=t.

The dimension calculation uses r<s; it is the one in the manuscript's
proof of Szykula's known avoid-or-compress lemma. Strong connectivity and
synchronization give reset words to every q, so V_infinity=R^n. A plateau
in V_i would stabilize forever. Therefore every inclusion from V_0 through
V_(t-1) is strict. There are t-1 inclusions starting at dimension one and
ending at dimension at most t, so each increases dimension by exactly one.
This also covers t=1 (only V_0). These flags are equality consequences of
the existing span proof, not a new upper-bound theorem.

Since every row has sum s>0, the affine dimension of the characteristic
rows in V_i is dim V_i-1=i. Thus:

* If t>=2, all one-letter images belong to {S,T} for one common s-set T.
  A line contains at most two vertices of a Boolean cube. In particular,
  for a binary alphabet, Sa=S or Sb=S or Sa=Sb. This restricts local
  avoid-or-compress equality, not compression equality alone.
* If t>=3, all images through depth two have affine dimension two, and
  there are at most four distinct such images. Writing T for the common
  non-S first image, the set family {S,T} union {T ell : ell in Sigma}
  is coplanar. All depth-two images are in this family, since every first
  image is S or T.

Here S is proper for t>=2 in the setting of interest. If all letters fixed
S as a set, S would be a proper invariant set, contradicting strong
connectivity. Equivalently synchronization would prevent an invariant
multi-element S. Hence such T exists.

<a id="problem4-local-equality-flag--exact-coplanarity-encoding"></a>
#### Exact coplanarity encoding

Four Boolean vectors are coplanar if two coincide or one of the three
pairings has equal coordinatewise sums, for example x+y=z+w. To see this
for four distinct vectors, project their affine plane injectively onto two
coordinate positions whose restricted linear parts are independent. The
four projected points are distinct elements of {0,1}^2, hence are its four
vertices. Every other coordinate is affine on these four points, takes
only values zero or one, and thus is constant, a projected coordinate, or
its complement. The vectors therefore form a parallelogram. The converse
is immediate. If the affine dimension were zero or one, there could not
be four distinct Boolean points. In any dimension, every quadruple being
coplanar is equivalent to the whole family having affine dimension at
most two: affine dimension at least three supplies four affinely
independent points.

For bit masks x,y,z,w, coordinatewise x+y=z+w is encoded exactly by

  (x AND y)=(z AND w),  (x XOR y)=(z XOR w).

Ordinary integer bit-mask addition is NOT used, because carries would mix
coordinates. The test includes the six possible vector coincidences.

<a id="problem4-local-equality-flag--search-scope"></a>
#### Search scope

The optional --local-span-prefix 1 or 2 in synthesize_potential.py applies
only with r>=1 and target=n-r, and only when the respective prefix length
is below target. It is a necessary restriction for an actual protected-set
witness, independent of its alphabet size. It may discard automata with
compression length target but no protected subset giving local value
target, which are irrelevant to this particular search. It does not impose
a common kernel, fixed row rank, permutation letter, or reachability cutoff.
Every positive still requires ordinary BFS checks of S reachability, full
synchronization, strong connectivity and protected delay. Solver failure
is not a mathematical upper bound.

The independent checker uses exact rational row rank and literal images,
tests the Boolean criterion exhaustively in small cube dimensions, and
checks every supplied frontier certificate attaining n-r. Neither these
finite controls nor equality flags alone settle (13,9,1).

<a id="problem4-mandatory-core-isolation"></a>
<a id="problem4-mandatory-core-isolation--isolation-of-the-mandatory-core-at-the-reaching-depth"></a>
### Isolation of the mandatory core at the reaching depth

9 October 2026. An alphabet-independent necessary condition for
Problem4. This note makes no priority claim and gives no new
extremal F value. It strengthens the earlier depth-only singleton
estimates without changing the validity of their weaker exclusions.

<a id="problem4-mandatory-core-isolation--lemma"></a>
#### Lemma

Let a strongly connected synchronizing n-state automaton have a
subset S of size s>=2. Write m=n-s, and let c(S) be the shortest
length of a word compressing S. Define

  J_m(S)=intersection {Sw : |w|<=m}.

For every x in J_m(S) and q distinct from x, the shortest merging
length d(x,q) satisfies

  d(x,q)>=c(S)-m.                                      (1)

Thus J_m(S) is isolated in P_(c(S)-m-1) whenever that depth is
nonnegative. The bound is vacuous if c(S)<=m+1. No initial image
reachability is required for this lemma. The original S in the
paper remains a reachable image.

<a id="problem4-mandatory-core-isolation--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Synchronization makes c(S) and every pair merging distance finite.
Strong connectivity reaches every q from some state of S within
m steps: a shortest path beginning in S cannot visit another S
state later and has at most n-s outside vertices. Choose u with
|u|<=m and q in Su. Since x belongs to J_m(S), x is also in Su.
If |Su|<s, then c(S)<=m and (1) is automatic because d(x,q)>=1.
Otherwise Su has s states including the distinct x,q. Appending
a shortest merging word v for that pair compresses Su, hence S:

  c(S)<=|u|+|v|<=m+d(x,q).

This proves (1). The argument uses compression of S, rather than
the avoid-or-compress value with a temporarily mandatory singleton.
There is no requirement that x remain mandatory after the reaching
prefix u. QED.

<a id="problem4-mandatory-core-isolation--application-to-the-current-thirteen-state-equality-flags"></a>
#### Application to the current thirteen-state equality flags

For ac(S,{3})=12, |S|=9, n=13, every compression of S has length
at least12, and m=4. Any point mandatory in all images through
depth four is therefore isolated in P7. This includes points
that are only known to be mandatory through four, five or six;
their earlier P0/P1/P2 estimates were weaker consequences of
ac(S,{x})<=4+d_x, not maximum possible isolation depths.

If a geometric one-count family contains every actual image
through some depth at least four, its intersection X is contained
in J4(S). Every X point is isolated in P7. Therefore a cover H
of P5 can be reduced to H minus X. When at most one cover point
remains, the known Frankl--Pin three-letter compression bound for
an (n-1)-set contradicts the cover of P5 (n=13>=3).
This is the existing compression-cover floor, applied after the
stronger mandatory-core isolation, not a new compression bound.

In B0/C14/D5, K={1,2} covers P5. Consequently any fourth or
later singleton2 that is mandatory through at least four is
impossible for every finite alphabet: stripping2 leaves {1}
covering P5. This includes E6/F2, E6/F7/G2 and E6/F7/G8/H2.
The latter two were previously excluded only for binary, or left
admitted, under the weaker isolation estimates. The new theorem
justifies their stronger conditional all-alphabet exclusions.
It does not exclude singleton2 at a depth below four.

Other mandatory points such as6,7,8, or a fresh singleton9 at
seventh level also enjoy P7 isolation in this branch. Pair fibers
remain one-count fibers; their individual points are not silently
declared mandatory. Binary and unrestricted values of F(13,9,1)
are still unknown.

<a id="problem4-mandatory-core-isolation--independent-checks"></a>
#### Independent checks

The checker computes ordinary subset images and compression lengths
by BFS, and each pair distance by a separate forward pair BFS. It
checks (1) for every subset of size>=2 in complete small binary
and ternary transformation domains, as well as all290 accepted
frontier certificates and seeded larger alphabets. Literal prefix
intersections use all shortest-reachable subsets through the required
depth, equivalent to all words through that depth. The small domains
include m=0 and cases with empty core or a vacuous bound.

The audit also appends a transient clone of a protected state to
a verified frontier automaton. It stays synchronizing but loses
strong connectivity, and violates (1). This guards the reaching
hypothesis. Each known cover application retains the actual
nine-set one-count family; no equality automaton is inferred from
a necessary field table or a search timeout.

Run check_mandatory_core_isolation.py with Python>=3.10 and
assertions enabled. This auxiliary note is outside the unchanged
109-file accepted article supplement. Earlier proof-bound files
remain unchanged; the current frontier supersedes their depth-only
interpretations with this independently checked stronger statement.

<a id="problem4-matching-early-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-matching-early-exclusion--excluding-three-disjoint-early-pairs-at-tight-codimension-three-compression"></a>
### Excluding three disjoint early pairs at tight codimension-three compression

**当前证明依赖。** 本节的符号分类及测试域推导仍使用；后面的有限动作/距离排除
现由[纸面替代引理](#problem4-paper-dependency-reductions)代替，保留的枚举描述为历史独立控制。

Suppose a synchronizing automaton on n>=6 has an (n-3)-subset of shortest
compression length 10. The credited Frankl--Pin refinement and strict pair
closure growth give |P_h|=h for h=1,2,3. Consider the case

    P1={01}, P2={01,23}, P3={01,23,45}.

Every letter is a permutation or has rank n-1 and the common kernel 01.
For every letter f, inverse pairs of 01 lie in P2 and inverse pairs of 23
lie in P3. These statements mean all two-point preimages, not a chosen
preimage.

<a id="problem4-matching-early-exclusion--eight-projected-images"></a>
#### Eight projected images

Every (n-3)-set whose pairs avoid P3 has a hole set containing exactly one
point from each of 01,23,45. There are eight such hole sets, indexed by
(x,y,z) in {0,1}^3, namely {x,2+y,4+z}. The initial set is one of them.
Each can be relabeled to the first hole set by independently swapping the
endpoints of the three pairs. This preserves the ordered early-pair type.

A permutation sends a hole set H to f(H). For a rank-(n-1) letter with
missing output d, H contains exactly one endpoint of its kernel. Its new
holes are {d,f(2+y),f(4+z)}. The image still has n-3 points. Mark the action
as EXIT if those holes fail to contain one endpoint of each early pair.
Such an image contains a P3 pair and hence compresses within three further
letters. Thus compression length 10 would require first exit distance at
least 7 from the initial projected image.

Synchronization requires exit to be reachable from every projected image:
otherwise its entire image orbit stays in the eight sets of cardinality
n-3, making a reset impossible. The shortest exit distance from each
projected image is consequently at most 8 (erase repeated vertices on a
shortest exit path).

<a id="problem4-matching-early-exclusion--complete-action-projection-independent-of-n-and-alphabet-size"></a>
#### Complete action projection, independent of n and alphabet size

Only f(0),...,f(5) and, for a singular letter, d affect the eight actions.
At most six distinct external labels occur among these values. Relabel
them to 6,...,11. The six distinguished labels 0,...,5 stay fixed. Thus
enumerating these values among twelve labels gives a superset of every
possible projected action for every n>=6. Small n simply realizes a
subset of this superset.

For a permutation, enumerate all injective six-tuples (12P6=665280).
The inverse pairs of 01 and 23 must both occur among the six distinguished
sources and satisfy the constraints above. Exactly 896 core cases pass.

For a singular letter, f(0)=f(1), and f(0),f(2),...,f(5) are distinct.
Choose these five images and then a different d (12P5 times 7 =665280).
If d is in an output pair its two-point preimage is empty. If the kernel
image is in a present output pair, its two inverse edges share an endpoint;
they cannot both be in the matching P2 or P3. Otherwise the unique inverse
pair must be one of the specified matching pairs. Exactly 6272 cases pass.

An independent inverse-case classification obtains the same cases:

* d in 01: inverse 23 is 23 or 45; 4032 core cases;
* d in 23: inverse 01 is 23; 2016 core cases;
* d outside 01 union 23: inverse 01 is 23 and inverse 23 is 45; 224 cases.

The permutation and singular cases yield exactly 177 distinct action
profiles. The independent checker extends the inverse cases to literal
twelve-state rows and computes all eight subset images directly. All 177
profiles coincide. Literal n=6,7 pools (111 and 407 letters) are included.

<a id="problem4-matching-early-exclusion--exact-finite-alphabet-check"></a>
#### Exact finite alphabet check

Let d(v) be the shortest exit distance in an arbitrary selected alphabet
of the 177 profiles. If all eight values are finite, their maximum is at
most 8 and every integer from 1 to that maximum occurs: a shortest exit
path descends one level at each step. Normalize the initial vertex to 0.
If d(0)>=7 there are exactly 30240 possible distance vectors:

* maximum 7 and d(0)=7: levels 1,...,7 with one duplicate, 20160 vectors;
* maximum 8 and d(0)=7 or 8: one of each level 1,...,8, 10080 vectors.

For each vector include ALL profiles satisfying

    d(v) <= 1 + d(f(v)), with d(EXIT)=0.

This includes every letter of an alphabet having that distance vector.
Under any included word to EXIT the inequality gives length >=d(v), so
adding all such profiles does not invalidate the lower bound. If the union
of allowed actions cannot make every vertex reach EXIT, no alphabet with
that vector is possible.

The complete check finds no vector for which all eight vertices reach
EXIT. Python constructs multiset permutations and uses reverse BFS; C++
independently scans all base-eight label vectors and uses repeated Boolean
exit closure. Both check 30240 vectors with zero candidates. Each accepts
the artificial eight-vertex chain, a positive control with first distance 8.
This is exhaustive arithmetic enumeration, without a SAT solver or any
bound on the selected alphabet size.

Hence in every synchronizing alphabet of these actions the first exit
distance is at most 6. Appending a P3 merging word of length at most 3
compresses the original subset within 9, a contradiction. The disjoint
early-pair type is therefore impossible for tight compression 10.

<a id="problem4-matching-early-exclusion--reproduction-and-limits"></a>
#### Reproduction and limits

Build and run matching_cube_profiles.cpp to matching_cube_profiles.json.
Run check_matching_cube.py against that report. Run audit_matching_cube.py
to generate an independent text profile list, then build/run
audit_matching_distances.cpp on that list. Reports matching_cube_check.json,
matching_cube_audit.json and matching_distance_audit.json contain the counts.

<a id="problem4-odd-cycle-span-refinement"></a>
<a id="problem4-odd-cycle-span-refinement--eliminating-the-maximal-independent-set-rank-case"></a>
### Eliminating the maximal independent-set rank case

Auxiliary uniform compression reduction for Problem 4, with the sharp
odd-cycle preservation threshold proved below. Arbitrary finite alphabets are allowed;
the initial subset need not be a reachable image.

<a id="problem4-odd-cycle-span-refinement--odd-cycle-transformation-lemma-self-contained"></a>
#### Odd-cycle transformation lemma (self-contained, sharp threshold)

Let C be a cycle of length N=2k+1, k≥1, and J a disjoint set of isolated
vertices. Let F consist of J together with each maximum independent k-set
of C. **Any singular transformation of C∪J maps at most k+2 distinct members
of F back into F.** No assumption on its kernel graph is required. The
bound is attained by the unit 0→1 fixing every other vertex.

There are exactly N maximum independent sets: their cyclic selected-vertex
gaps consist of k−1 gaps of length two and one gap of length three. Index
them by the unique uncovered edge. If M is their vertex-incidence matrix
and E the vertex-edge incidence matrix, ME=J_N−I_N. This matrix is invertible,
so all N input rows are independent, as is any selected subfamily. Appending
the fixed isolated coordinates does not change that rank.

Suppose f preserves p>0 family members and has rank defect c≥1. Every
preserved image contains J, so all c omitted outputs lie on C. Also rank f
is at least the common family size |J|+k, giving c≤k+1. The transformation
matrix has nullity c; consequently the p independent input rows have image
rank at least p−c. These images are characteristic rows: membership in F
ensures their cardinality is unchanged.

For c distinct omitted cycle vertices, at most k+2−c members of F avoid all
of them. To see this, index maximum independent sets cyclically in step-two
order. The k sets containing each vertex form a cyclic interval of length k,
and distinct vertices give distinct intervals. A union of c such intervals
has at least min(N,k+c−1) points. If the union is proper, cut at an uncovered
point: components of lengths l_i contain at most Σ max(0,l_i−k+1) ≤ |union|−k+1
such intervals. If the union is full there are no avoiding sets. Thus the
image rank is at most k+2−c, and p−c≤k+2−c proves p≤k+2.

For sharpness, the unit 0→1 preserves all k+1 maximum sets avoiding 0, and
also the unique maximum set containing 0 but not 2, namely
{0,3,5,…,2k−1} (for k=1 use {0}). Every other maximum set containing 0 also
contains 2, so its image is not independent. Exactly k+2 members are preserved.

In particular, preserving k+3 distinct members forces a permutation whenever
k≥2. The earlier N−1 formulation follows for k≥3, but is weaker for k≥4.
C5 does admit singular maps preserving four members; preserving all five
forces a permutation. The former restriction on kernel pairs is unnecessary.

<a id="problem4-odd-cycle-equality-crossing"></a>
#### Equality forces the kernel into the cycle and limits crossings

Suppose a singular f preserves exactly k+2 members of F, and let its rank
defect be c. Every inequality in the sharp-threshold proof is then an
equality: the selected input span V has dimension k+2, its image has dimension
k+2−c, and V contains the entire c-dimensional row kernel of the transformation
matrix. In particular,

\[
 \boxed{\ker f\text{ has no pair touching }J,\qquad
         |f(J)\cap C|\le c-1.}\tag{OC-E}
\]

Here the first statement concerns distinct-state kernel pairs. Indeed, all
rows v in span F satisfy v_j=(Σ_(x∈C)v_x)/k for every j∈J. A fiber difference
e_x−e_y involving an isolated vertex cannot satisfy these equations, so it
cannot belong to V. Every such difference lies in the row kernel, proving
the first assertion. Thus f is injective on J and its images do not collide
with images of core inputs.

The image family has exactly ell=k+2−c distinct members, because every
subfamily of F is linearly independent. The intersection of ell distinct
cycle maximum sets has size at most k+1−ell: in step-two cyclic order these
are distinct intervals of length k. If their intersection is nonempty, cut
at a common point; their distinct starts span at least ell−1 positions, so
the intersection has at most k−ell+1 positions. If ell>k, each vertex belongs
to only k members and the intersection is empty. Since every image contains
f(J), this bounds |f(J)∩C| by c−1.

**Consecutive omitted outputs, for k≥2.** Equality also forces the omitted
cycle vertices to be

\[
 Z=\{z,z+2,\ldots,z+2(c-1)\}\pmod{2k+1}.\tag{OC-E2}
\]

Indeed, the c length-k incidence intervals of the omitted vertices have
union size exactly k+c−1. This is smaller than 2k+1 because c≤k+1.
Cut at a point outside the union. If its t components have lengths l_i,
they can contain at most Σ(l_i−k+1)=k+c−1−t(k−1) distinct length-k
intervals. Containing c of them forces t=1. A single interval of length
k+c−1 contains exactly c length-k subintervals, so all their consecutive
starting positions must occur. In the step-two indexing of the family,
this says precisely that the omitted vertices are consecutive in step-two
order. The output family is the entire k+2−c-member family avoiding Z,
since it has that cardinality and is contained in it. These conclusions
do not require a cycle-edge kernel. The unrestricted C5/C7 controls below
also check (OC-E2) on every equality case.

A permutation preserving at least k+1 members also preserves J setwise.
Otherwise its distinct output family members would all contain one cycle
point in f(J), but only k maximum sets contain any specified cycle point.
Therefore both a permutation and a rank-(n−1) map preserving k+2 members
must preserve J. This uses the equality argument for the singular case;
it does not follow merely from the number of preserved sets.

**The defect-two crossing obstruction is real, uniformly in k.** For any
k≥2 and nonempty J, choose j∈J and fix every state except

\[
 f(1)=f(2)=j,\qquad f(3)=4,\qquad f(j)=2.
\]

This map has rank n−2, exactly two nonperiodic states 1 and 3, and stable
kernel pairs precisely {1,2} and {3,4}, both cycle edges. All of J is
periodic, but j maps into the cycle. Nevertheless it preserves exactly
k+2 members of F: all k members containing 2 are fixed, and the other two
preserved core sets are {1,4,6,…,2k} and {1,3,6,8,…,2k}. Both map to
{2,4,6,…,2k}, with J adjoined. The only maximum set containing neither 1 nor 2
loses j; every remaining set containing 1 maps 3 to 4 while retaining 5,
creating an adjacent pair. This proves the count and attains the crossing
bound |f(J)∩C|=1=c−1.

For C7 plus isolate 7, a concrete instance is
f=(0,7,7,4,4,5,6,2). Thus one cannot conclude J-invariance for defect two
by adding periodic-isolate or stable-kernel conditions to the sharp
preservation count. This is a single-letter obstruction to that proposed
argument, not a synchronizing Problem 4 witness or a counterexample to a
stronger compression bound.

<a id="problem4-odd-cycle-sharp-compression"></a>
#### Consequences for a short-pair graph that is an odd cycle

Let k≥2, m=k+1, and suppose a synchronizing automaton has
P_h=C_(2k+1) plus isolated vertices J. Every (n−m)-subset S satisfies

\[
 \boxed{c(S)\le h+k+3=h+m+2.}\tag{OC1}
\]

If c(S)>h+k+3, all images through depth k+3 are uncompressed and
P_h-independent, so belong to F. Before compression the image families
R_i grow strictly: a plateau would be an invariant family of sets of size
at least two, impossible in a synchronizing automaton. Thus R_(k+2) has at
least k+3 distinct members. Every letter maps them back into F, so the sharp
threshold makes every letter a permutation, again impossible. If S is not
initially independent, compression already takes at most h. This proves
(OC1) without strong connectivity or initial-image reachability assumptions.

If a nonempty protected A⊆S meets the cycle, the stronger local bound is

\[
 \boxed{\operatorname{ac}(S,A)\le h+k=h+m-1.}\tag{OC2}
\]

Indeed, if ac>h+k, all images through depth k are independent and contain
any fixed a∈A∩C. Only k members of F contain a, whereas R_k has at least
k+1 members. This is a contradiction. Thus in a longer safe instance the
protected set must lie entirely among the isolated vertices.

If J is nonempty, the automaton is strongly connected, and every letter
has rank at least n−1, there is a further improvement:

\[
 \boxed{c(S)\le h+k+2=h+m+1.}\tag{OC3}
\]

Otherwise all images through depth k+2 belong to F, while R_(k+1) contains
at least k+2 distinct members. Each permutation letter must preserve J by
the preceding observation. Every singular letter has defect one; the sharp
threshold forces exactly k+2 preserved members, and (OC-E) again forces
J-invariance. The nonempty proper set J would then be invariant under all
letters, contradicting strong connectivity. This proves (OC3). The rank
hypothesis is part of this statement; (OC-E) and the defect-two example
explain why this proof does not cover larger letter defects.

For m≥5, (OC1) improves the earlier odd-cycle bound h+2m−2 by m−4.
In particular, for m=5 and target ac≥15 it excludes P_7=C9 (plus isolated
vertices), and also excludes that shape at earlier layers. It does not
exclude other graphs with cover number five or prove F=14 at q=15.
The general cover-number bound below remains valid; its non-cycle
rank-(2m−2) case is not removed by this improvement.

**Independent controls.** `check_odd_cycle_span.py` rebuilds the cycle families
for C3 through C17, verifies their rational row ranks, checks all 120469
omitted-vertex sets of sizes 1,…,k+1, and verifies 480 adjacent-unit equality
examples with zero, one, or three isolates. It also enumerates all 50064
transformations in the four domains C3, C3+1, C5, C5+1; the maxima for singular
maps are respectively 3,3,4,4. The native unrestricted-map control independently
checks all 46656 maps on C5+1 and all 16777216 maps on C7+1, including arbitrary
kernels and arbitrary images of the isolate. The singular maxima are 4 and 5;
there are respectively 45936 and 16736896 singular maps. The equality cases also satisfy
the kernel and crossing assertions (OC-E). Among maps with cycle-edge kernels
and preservation count k+2, the stable-kernel-compatible crossing counts are
60 at C5 with defect two, and 308/672 at C7 with defect two/three. These are
complete finite counts, not a classification for arbitrary k. The explicit
defect-two family is independently checked for C5 through C17 with one and
three isolates, giving 14 positive controls of its preservation count, rank,
stable kernel, and periodic crossing. No maps are omitted
by a rank or kernel prefilter. Worker domains are disjoint first-output residue
classes. These finite controls support the implementation; the uniform bounds
and sharpness follow from the proofs above, not from extrapolation.

```sh
python3 run.py script scripts/problem4/check_odd_cycle_span.py
python3 run.py script scripts/problem4/audit_cycle_seven_six_images.cpp --all-maps 4
```

<a id="problem4-c9-eighth-layer"></a>
#### 余维五：第八层九奇圈的完整排除

**计算辅助证明；任意有限字母表、任意孤点数。** 设 n≥9，自动机同步，
|S|=n−5。若 c(S)≥15，则 P8 不可能是 C9 加 n−9 个孤点。
不要求强连通、初始像可达或指定保护集。这个结论只关闭余维五的一个
短对图形状，尚未证明所有 m=5、q=15 的实例都满足 ac≤14。

**完整单字母归约。** 反设 P8=C9∪J。每个长度至多六的词都将 S 映到
F={J∪T:T 是 C9 的最大独立四点集}，否则该词后接至多八步的合并词
会在十四步内压缩 S。F 恰有九个成员。同步性排除不压缩集合族的平台，
所以深度五的实际像族至少有六个不同成员；每个字母都把它们映回 F。

每个字母的秩至少 n−3。秩小于 |S| 时立即压缩，等于 |S| 时由
[词秩迁移](#problem4-problem4-short-pair-peeling--3-a-word-rank-bound-and-its-letter-consequence)
在七步内压缩；秩为 |S|+1 时由同节的二次迁移在十三步内压缩。
因此亏秩 c≤3。非平凡一步核块都是 P1⊆C9 的团，故核恰为一个大小
c 的圈边匹配，其余为单点。所有孤点输入互异，且不与核心输入碰撞。

奇圈锐界说明，奇异字母恰保持六个 F 成员。由
[等号交叉界 (OC-E)](#problem4-odd-cycle-equality-crossing)，跨入核心的孤点
输入数 t≤c−1；置换字母保持 J，故 t=0。因为至少保持一个 F 成员，
全部 J 输出都有前像，所以全部 c 个遗漏输出都在 C9 内。

对一个实际字母，删除那些从 J 映到 J 的输入及其输出。余下九个核心输入
和 t 个孤点输入，对应九个核心输出和 t 个孤点输出。分别将这两组孤点
标为 9,…,8+t，得到大小 9+t 的完整单步表示，其中：

* 核为一个大小 c≤3 的圈边匹配；
* t≤max(0,c−1)，各孤点输入单射地映入核心；
* 每个孤点输出出现，遗漏输出全在核心；
* 至少六个最大独立集连同全部孤点被保持。

输入与输出的孤点标签是独立选择的。这不是实际字母的共轭表示，不能
迭代这些代表或对其求字母幂。后续只使用子集的单步作用、核心边的单步
作用，以及非圈边输入对是否映到核心圈边，恰好都是该表示保留的信息。
被删除的输入映到 J，不会额外产生核心边的前像。若实际 |J| 小于某个
枚举的 t，则多出的情形只是必要域的放宽，不会遗漏实际字母。

**两种完整生成。** 对 N=9、匹配大小 c，匹配数为
M(N,c)=N/(N−c)·binom(N−c,c)。固定 c,t 的规范变换数为

\[
 M(N,c)\,(N)_t\binom{N-t}{c}(N-c)!.
\]

其中 (N)_t 为给 t 个孤点输入选择不同核心输出的下降阶乘；随后选择
c 个遗漏核心输出，并将余下 N−c 个输出双射分配给核心核块。对
0≤c≤3、0≤t≤max(0,c−1) 求和，得到 109952640 个规范变换。
保留数为 22698，去重后的相关作用签名为 3906。孤点标签不同的代表
可以有相同签名；并未把这些代表数解释为不同的原自动机数。

主生成器逐核块递归分配未使用输出，并提前保证所有孤点输出最终出现。
独立遍历先选择遗漏输出，再枚举剩余输出的全部排列。两个完整遍历保留的
22698 个实际转移数组逐项相同。Python 从这些数组重新计算集合像、核对、
核心边像和所有非圈边前像标记，不读取原程序声称的签名字段。

**共同距离条件。** 令 d_i 是第 i 个 F 成员的最短离开 F 的长度，
e_j 是第 j 条圈边的最短合并长度。同步性使所有这些距离有限。
子集退出路径可以删去重复顶点，所以 1≤d_i≤9，且 1,…,max d_i
各层都出现。将 S 旋转到编号零，则 d_0≥7。圈边满足 1≤e_j≤8，
而每个非圈边的合并长度至少九。

对每个单字母签名，记其集合作用为 a(i)，其中 EXIT 的距离为零；
记圈边作用为 b(j)，可能是立即合并、另一圈边或圈外点对。该签名
与距离向量相容，当且仅当以下必要不等式全部满足：

1. d_i≤1+d_(a(i))。
2. 若圈边 j 立即合并，则 e_j=1；若映到圈边 l，则 e_j≤1+e_l。
3. 若某个非圈边输入对映到圈边 l，则 e_l=8。
