test followed by a P3 merging word compresses within 4+2+3=9.

The finite projection is complete for every n. Only the five distinguished
input states matter. For singular missing-0 rows the three domain tests
013,123,02v (and 03v) force both 2 and 3 among their four distinct
nonzero outputs: if only one were present it could not meet all the
requirements on (c,z),(t,z),(t,fv),(z,fv). At most two fresh outside
labels are needed. Singular missing-1 rows already use outputs 0,2;
their two other distinct outputs need at most two fresh labels.
Thus labels 0,...,6 suffice, including represented v=4. Permutations
use the A,B,T templates. No alphabet-size bound is imposed.

path3_mixing_actions.py uses structural templates and reverse exit
closure; audit_path3_mixing.cpp independently enumerates all literal
forward partial rows, checks inverse pairs, and searches forward from
each domain vertex. Every profile and row-closure flag matches. The
reports are path3_mixing_actions.json, path3_mixing_independent.json and
path3_mixing_audit.json. ASan/UBSan also pass with identical output.

The n=5 boundary is real. Rows (1,1,2,3,4), (1,4,0,2,3), S={1,3}
are strongly connected and synchronizing, with reaching word abbabba
and reset word abbbbabbbbabbbba. Ordinary BFS gives projected exit FIVE
and actual compression TEN. The invariant five-state set is then all
of Q; consequently the claimed exclusion retains n>=6.

<a id="problem4-path3-early-exclusion--a-closed-t-permutation"></a>
#### A closed T permutation

Now T on C is (1,3,0,2). Its outside action is a permutation. For an
additional letter g, let D2(T,g) be the domain preserving H under all
words of length at most two on T,g. Direct substitution gives:

| Mixing g | Domain is contained in | Definition of v,u |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 123,03v,12u | v=g^-1(3), u=T^-1(v) |
| B | 012,03v,12u | same |
| D0 | 013,03u,12v | same |
| D2 | 023,123,12u | same |

For A, the tests g,gT,Tg remove respectively core 013,023,012;
for B they remove 023,013,123. Their outside constraints require
gx=3 for 03x and g(Tx)=3 for 12x. In the D0 case gg removes 023,123
and g removes 012; its 013 survives only if g(g0)=3, equivalently g0=v, while
the outside restrictions give the displayed unique preimages. In D2,
g removes 013, Tg removes 012, and gg removes every possible 03x.
These observations verify all four rows. Every domain has size at
most three, contradicting |R4|>=5. Thus every permutation and every
missing-1 letter preserves C. Strong connectivity requires a mixing
missing-0 letter f with core images c,t,z.

Call a core output good if it is 2 or 3. If at most one of c,t,z is
good, D2(T,f) has at most four vertices. With none good there are no
core holes, and each outside type 03x,12x has at most the two outside
preimages of 2,3. With only c good, there is at most core 012 and one
outside choice for each type. With only t good, core holes are among
023,123, with at most 03v,12T^-1(v); with only z good they are among
013,123, with at most 12v,03T^-1(v). Here v is the outside preimage
of the other good output. These counts are at most four.

If c and one of t,z are the two good outputs, the remaining core image
is outside C (otherwise f is not mixing). All outside holes are removed
by f and Tf. At least one core hole is removed by fT: if c=2 it is
013 when z is outside, or 012 when t is outside; if c=3 the holes
023,123 are removed. The domain then has size at most three.

It remains that c is outside and {t,z}={2,3}. Set v=f^-1(1) and
u=T^-1(v), both outside C. Compute D3(T,f), the domain preserving H
under all words of length at most three:

    t=2,z=3: D3={013,123,03u};
    t=3,z=2: D3={023,123,03v}, plus 12u iff f(u)=v.

For completeness the two-step domains before the last tests are

    t=2,z=3: {013,023,123,12v} union {03x: x outside C};
    t=3,z=2: {012,023,123,03v} union {12x: x outside C}.

Requiring their T- and f-successors to remain in those domains gives
the displayed D3 sets directly. Their sizes must be at least four
because |R3|>=4. Only t=3,z=2 and f(u)=v survive. Since f(v)=1,
u!=v. Relabel u=4,v=5 and order the remaining domain as

    D={023,123,124,035}.

All four images are reached by depth three, so every letter maps them
to H. The complete projection has 19 profiles. A first exit at length
four requires one of the 24 permutations of distances 1,...,4. None
allows every vertex to exit. The first exit therefore has length at
most three; a failed test of length at most three and a P3 merging
word compress within 3+3+3=9. This excludes closed T as well.

This second finite projection also has parameter-independent coverage.
Permutations use the closed A,B,T core rows, missing-1 letters the two
closed D rows. A missing-0 row has five distinct nonzero outputs from
six inputs. The domain tests on 023/123,124,035 force both 2 and 3
among those outputs. Thus at most three fresh labels are needed and
labels 0,...,8 cover every partial row. path3_closed_T_actions.py and
audit_path3_closed_T.cpp independently give the same 19 profiles and
24 negative distance checks. audit_path3_closed_T_domains.py verifies
every stated domain reduction by literal subset actions at n=6,7.

<a id="problem4-path3-early-exclusion--no-t-permutation"></a>
#### No T permutation

There must now be a B permutation and a D0 or D2 letter. A closed D0
is impossible even alone: its common domain for D0,D0D0 is precisely
the four core holes, fewer than |R4|>=5. A mixing D0 together with B
also has a two-step domain of size at most four. To see this write
v=D0^-1(3). The D0 and D0D0 tests leave at most core 013, only if
D0(v)=3 with v=D0(0), and outside holes 12v,02v,03x with x=v or
x=D0^-1(v). If B is closed it removes 02v; if core 013 is present,
D0^-1(v) is not outside, giving at most three vertices. If B is mixing,
its test forces x=B^-1(3) for 03x and for 02x. There are then at most
one core hole and three outside holes. Both counts are at most four.
Thus no D0 letter exists, and a D2 letter is necessary.

If the alphabet consisted solely of A,B permutations and D2 letters,
the family of holes 12x (x!=1,2, including x=0,3) would be invariant.
A,B preserve the pair 12. A D2 letter sends 120 to 12c and any other
12x to 12D2(x); these are again three distinct holes. This invariant
family of uncompressed (n-3)-images contradicts synchronization.
There is therefore a missing-0 letter f.

Choose one B=b, one D2=d and such an f. Let beta be 1 when b is mixing,
epsilon be 1 when d is mixing. In their common H-domain, 02x has at
most the single outside choice b^-1(3), available only when beta=1;
03x has at most the outside choice d^-1(3), available only when
epsilon=1. Core 023 is absent if beta=1, and core 013 is absent if
epsilon=1. Let c=f0=f1, t=f2, z=f3.

First suppose t is neither 2 nor 3. If neither c nor z is good, all
core holes fail and each outside type 02x,12x requires fx in {2,3};
there are at most two 12x and at most one of each other type, totaling
four. If only c is good, core holes are among 012,013, and all outside
types require the unique outside preimage v of the other good output.
There are at most three outside holes; if all three are present, both
b and d are mixing and core 013 is absent, again totaling at most
four. If only z is good, core holes are among 013,023,123; the possible
02x,03x are paid for by the respective losses of 023,013, leaving at
most three core/outside-extra holes plus the one possible 12x. If both
c,z are good, 02x and 12x are impossible since neither good output
has an outside preimage. The possible 03x is paid for by the absence
of core 013. In each case the one-step domain has size at most four.

Now suppose t=2 or t=3 and use all tests of length at most two on b,d,f.
Define a two-element output-target set V by

    t=2: V={1,b^-1(3)};
    t=3: V={2,w}, w=1 if d is closed, w=d^-1(3) if d is mixing.

The test fb in the first case, or fd in the second, forces fx in V
for every allowed outside 12x. Put a=[c in V], h=[z in V]. The kernel
output c and core output z have no outside preimages, so at most
2-a-h outside 12x survive. The same test requires c in V for core
012, and z in V for core 023,123. Hence the core count is at most

    a + h(2-beta) + (1-epsilon).

The last term bounds core 013, and the beta term removes 023 under
mixing B. The other two outside types contribute at most beta+epsilon.
The total domain size is therefore at most

    a+h(2-beta)+(1-epsilon)+(2-a-h)+beta+epsilon
       = 3+h(1-beta)+beta <= 4.

This also covers the common-kernel issue in fd: when d is closed,
preimages of output 3 are 0,1, but f omits 0, leaving only target 1.
When d is mixing the preimage is the unique outside state d^-1(3).
All targets in V are distinct and neither equals t.

Thus the common two-step domain on b,d,f has at most four images,
contradicting |R4|>=5. This completes the no-T branch and the claim.

audit_path3_no_T.py checks every literal compatible triple from the
complete n6/n7 pools, including all indicators and counts in the last
inequality. audit_path3_no_T.cpp independently generates all full rows
without reading those pools and computes complement-of-subset actions.
Both check 4320 triples at n6 and 414720 at n7, with maximum domain
size four. They also supply controls for mixing D0 with B. The proof
above is uniform; the finite controls are not used for extrapolation.

<a id="problem4-path3-early-exclusion--reproduction"></a>
#### Reproduction

From the supplementary directory, with standard-library Python >=3.10
and clang++ (or another C++17 compiler):

    python -B path3_mixing_actions.py
    clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 audit_path3_mixing.cpp -o path3_mix
    ./path3_mix path3_mixing_independent.json
    python -B audit_path3_mixing.py
    python -B path3_closed_T_actions.py
    clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 audit_path3_closed_T.cpp -o path3_closed
    ./path3_closed path3_closed_T_independent.json
    python -B audit_path3_closed_T_domains.py
    clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 audit_path3_no_T.cpp -o path3_no_T
    ./path3_no_T path3_no_T_independent.json
    python -B audit_path3_no_T.py

On Windows add .exe to executable names. The domain checkers use the
complete early_alphabet_pool_n6.json and early_alphabet_pool_n7.json
generated by early_pair_alphabet_pool.py; the standalone native no-T
audit generates all its rows independently of those files. The boundary
checker imports only the independent ordinary-BFS utilities in
verify_certificates.py. Assertions must remain enabled.

<a id="problem4-path3-early-exclusion--scope"></a>
#### Scope

<a id="problem4-protected-padding-proof"></a>
<a id="problem4-protected-padding-proof--exact-codimension-four-bands-n-r10-and-11"></a>
### Exact codimension-four bands n-r=10 and 11

There are binary strongly connected synchronizing witnesses with actual
reachable S for

    F_bin(r+10,r+6,r)=F(r+10,r+6,r)=10, r>=1,
    F_bin(r+11,r+7,r)=F(r+11,r+7,r)=11, r>=1.

The lower proof uses a complete finite twelve-state base certificate and
a parameter-uniform set-image lifting argument. The upper is the known
avoid-or-compress bound. The r=1 instance of the ten-band is the separately
checked (11,7,1) witness in frontier_certificates.json.

<a id="problem4-protected-padding-proof--finite-base-computer-assisted"></a>
#### Finite base (computer-assisted)

Use P={p_0,...,p_4}, U={u_1,...,u_7}. Letter a fixes p_0,p_1,p_2,
swaps p_3,p_4 and cycles U. Letter b maps p_i to p_(i-1) for i>=1,
p_0 to u_4, u_1 to u_2 to u_3 to p_4, u_4 to u_5 to u_6 to p_4,
and fixes u_7. Put S=P union {u_1,u_2,u_3}.

In coordinates p_0,...,p_4,u_1,...,u_7 the rows are

    a=[0,1,2,4,3,6,7,8,9,10,11,5],
    b=[8,0,1,2,3,6,7,4,9,10,4,11].

The complete 62-state short-image certificate proves every word of length
<=10 preserves |S| and contains p_0, and every word of length <=9 also
contains p_1. The word a^6 b a^3 b compresses at length eleven;
a^6 b a b^2 omits p_1 at length ten.
Thus ac(S,{p_0})=11 and ac(S,{p_0,p_1})=10.
protected_padding_base.json records every short-image set, its level and
both successors below level ten. The independent checker rebuilds the
whole BFS without reading this certificate.

<a id="problem4-protected-padding-proof--protected-edge-lifting"></a>
#### Protected edge lifting

Insert k>=0 states H={h_1,...,h_k} on the b-edge p_0 -> u_4:
p_0 -> h_1 -> ... -> h_k -> u_4. Fix H under a, and leave all other
old transitions unchanged. Put S'=S union H and A'=A union H.

For every old subset T containing p_0,

    (T union H)a' = Ta union H,
    (T union H)b' = Tb union H.

Indeed the new chain has all its internal states covered, and its last
state supplies the former b-image of p_0. Every safe old prefix contains
p_0. Induction therefore lifts all prefixes through the first old unsafe
word, preserving both cardinality loss and protected-state omission.
Consequently ac(S',A')=ac(S,A), including attainment by the same word.

<a id="problem4-protected-padding-proof--structural-requirements-for-every-k"></a>
#### Structural requirements for every k

Let B=P union H union {u_4,u_5,u_6}; b cycles B in the order
p_0,h_1,...,h_k,u_4,u_5,u_6,p_4,p_3,p_2,p_1.
Put s=|B|=8+k and E=B union {u_7}. Then Qb^3=E.
The a-cycle on U connects all outside states to B; b cycles B, proving
strong connectivity.

Set d=a^6 b^s. On E it fixes P union H and acts by
u_4 -> u_6 -> u_5 -> u_4, u_7 -> u_6. Hence e=d^3 fixes B and sends
u_7 to u_4. Thus Qb^3 e=B and Ba^4=S'; the actual reaching word is
b^3(a^6 b^s)^3 a^4.

On B, f=ae cycles u_4,u_5,u_6 and swaps p_3,p_4.
Therefore f^3 is the transposition of p_3,p_4, two adjacent b-cycle points.
The words b and f^3 generate the full symmetric group on B. Inverses are
positive powers on B, so no extra input letters are introduced.
Moreover Ba=(B minus {u_4}) union {u_7}, whence
Bab=(B minus {u_5}) union {u_7}; applying e compresses B to B minus {u_5}.
Thus h=abe is a compressing transformation of B.
Use permutations of B to send any pair in the current image into h's
colliding fiber and apply h. Iterating synchronizes B. Prepending b^3 e
synchronizes Q. Every permutation and compression is an original-letter word.

For A={p_0}, r=k+1, n=r+11 and |S'|=r+7.
For A={p_0,p_1}, r=k+2, n=r+10 and |S'|=r+6.
The two lengths meet n-r, and the compression upper is 15 at codimension
four. This establishes the stated exact bands; it asserts nothing at
n-r>=12. The independent checker audits all r through twenty and all
macro actions, reaching words, exact local lengths and literal resets.

<a id="problem4-protected-padding-proof--smaller-protected-subsets-in-the-same-eleven-valued-automaton"></a>
#### Smaller protected subsets in the same eleven-valued automaton

For any n>=12, choose k=n-12 and any r-element subset of {p_0} union H
containing p_0, where 1<=r<=k+1=n-11. Every short image through depth ten
contains {p_0} union H. The same length-eleven word compresses the image.
Consequently ac=11 for every such choice, proving F_bin(n,n-4,r)>=11.
This is not an upper bound eleven when n-r>11. The checker independently
recomputes all 210 such parameter choices through n=31.

<a id="problem4-reverse-trap-cut"></a>
<a id="problem4-reverse-trap-cut--safe-reverse-trap-cut-for-a-partially-assigned-second-letter"></a>
### Safe reverse trap cut for a partially assigned second letter

The first letter a is complete. In the inverse enumeration a set D of
output fibers of b has been assigned completely: no future assignment can
add any source to b^{-1}(q) for q in D. Start at 0 and take the reverse
closure R under a and the already assigned b-fibers. If R is a proper
subset of Q and R is contained in D, discard this branch.

Indeed, a^{-1}(R) is contained in R by reverse closure. Also b^{-1}(R)
is contained in R, and these fibers are complete. Every completion has
the same property. Thus no state outside R can reach 0, so the automaton
cannot be strongly connected. If a reachable reverse vertex has an
unassigned b-fiber, the code returns "open" immediately: this sacrifices
pruning and does not exclude a completion. If R=Q it also returns open.

This cut includes the earlier zero-state cut but adds closures of several
states. The separate zero-state test remains for speed. The second code
uses repeated numeric transition scans; the first uses a queue with the
explicit inverse fibers. Both disable the cuts in unpruned orbit-export
mode. No new maximum is asserted before their complete runs are audited.

<a id="problem4-saturated-two-guard-trap"></a>
<a id="problem4-saturated-two-guard-trap--saturated-two-guard-image-trap"></a>
### Saturated two-guard image trap

Auxiliary obstruction, not an exact value of F. Let n>=4 and let K,Z
be disjoint two-element state sets. Write P_h for the unordered pairs
merged by a word of length at most h. Suppose K covers P4 and every
pair with one endpoint in K and one in Z belongs to P2. Then the
automaton is not synchronizing. The alphabet is any finite alphabet;
strong connectivity and initial-image reachability are unnecessary.

Put R=Q-K and C=Q-Z. Every Rw for |w|<=2 has cardinality n-2,
otherwise w merges a pair outside K. It contains no K-Z pair:
lifting that pair through w and then applying its merging word would
merge a pair outside K within four. An independent set of cardinality
n-2 in the complete bipartite graph between K and Z must be exactly
R or C. Indeed it cannot meet both K and Z, and either complement
has exactly n-2 points. This also holds at n=4.

Consequently every first image of R is R or C. If no letter takes R
to C, R is invariant under every letter. Otherwise choose a letter t
with Rt=C. For every letter l, Cl=Rtl is R or C by the preceding
two-letter argument. Thus {R,C} is invariant, with every image of R
having n-2>=2 states. A reset word for Q would reset R, a contradiction.

Only the explicit K-Z seed pairs and the P4 cover are used. This
lemma must not be inferred from an edge-count cap, nor applied to a
non-saturated bipartite graph. Independent finite controls enumerate
all rows injective on R at n4 and all ordered one/two-letter alphabets
on that domain; an explicit strongly connected nonsynchronizing
control checks that the hypotheses need not contradict connectivity.

<a id="problem4-second-entrance-fiber"></a>
<a id="problem4-second-entrance-fiber--a-second-common-entrance-fiber-at-singleton-equality"></a>
### A second common entrance fiber at singleton equality

Auxiliary necessary structure for Problem 4; no new extremal value.
This note is outside the manuscript and supplementary release.

Let a strongly connected synchronizing automaton have S of size s>=5,
A={a}, and ac(S,{a})=t=n-1. The first entrance-fiber proposition supplies
a nonempty B subset Q minus {a}, meeting S once, such that every letter
has preimage of a equal to {a} or B, and some letter uses B.

Then there is a nonempty C subset Q minus {a}, distinct from B, such that

* each letter has preimage of B equal to {a}, B or C;
* some letter uses C, and |S intersect C|=1;
* neither B nor C contains the other;
* every image Sw with |w|<=t-3 meets C once; every image with
  |w|<=t-2 meets B once.

Initial-set reachability is unnecessary. If |B|=1, C is a one-step
collision clique. Otherwise C is a two-step collision clique. At
(n,s,r)=(13,9,1), the proved |P1|<=4 and cover(P5)<=3 therefore give
|B|<=3, |C|<=4 (improved to |C|<=3 when |B|=1), and |B union C|<=5.

<a id="problem4-second-entrance-fiber--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Use row trajectories chi_S D_w and V_i=span_R of trajectories with
|w|<=i. Equality gives dim V_i=i+1 through i=t-1, and all these
trajectories are collision-free characteristic rows containing a.
For a letter whose preimage of a is B, safety of w followed by that
letter shows |Sw intersect B|=1 through depth t-2.

For a letter ell put D=ell^(-1)(B). Every image through depth t-3
meets D once. In particular D is nonempty and |S intersect D|=1.
If a belongs to D, every such image already contains a, so it omits
every point in D minus {a}. Strong connectivity reaches each state
from S within m=n-s steps, and m<=t-3 since s>=4. Thus D={a}.
Otherwise D is a subset of O=Q minus {a}.

Thus each D is {a} or is contained in O. The outside preimages
cannot all equal B. Indeed, if every preimage of B
were {a} or B, then ell^(-1)({a} union B) would be contained in
{a} union B for every letter. Its nonempty complement could never
reach this proper nonempty set, contradicting strong connectivity.
The set is proper since S minus {a} has at least four points and
only one of them belongs to B. Choose an outside preimage C different
from B. It meets S once.

The annihilator K of V_(t-3) has dimension three and contains

  h_a=s e_a-1,   h_B=s chi_B-1,   h_C=s chi_C-1.

Here 1 denotes the all-one column. The restrictions to O of these
columns span {1_O,chi_B,chi_C}. This space has dimension three:
the only Boolean vectors in span{1_O,chi_B} are 0,1_O,chi_B and
chi_(O minus B); C is neither empty nor O nor B nor its complement,
because it meets S once and |S intersect O|>=4. Consequently these
three columns form a basis of K. Any outside preimage D of B has
h_D=s chi_D-1 in K, so chi_D belongs to span{1_O,chi_B,chi_C}.

Both B and C meet every image through depth t-3 once. If B were
properly contained in C, these images would all omit C minus B;
if C were properly contained in B, they would all omit B minus C.
Strong connectivity and m<=t-3 exclude both possibilities. Also
B union C is proper in O: its intersection with S has at most two
points whereas |S intersect O|>=4.

If B and C intersect, all four membership cells on O are nonempty.
A Boolean vector in their affine span is one of 0,1,B,O minus B,
C,O minus C: its four cell values are Boolean and their opposite
sums agree. Among these, only B and C meet S once. If B and C are
disjoint, their three membership cells are nonempty and the Boolean
vectors in the span are the eight unions of these cells. The remainder
meets S in s-3>=2 points; the two other cells each meet S once.
Again only B and C are permitted. This proves the common-fiber claim.
The role of s>=5 is essential to this last argument; no assertion for
s=4 is made here.

If B is a singleton, a letter using C maps its points to that single
state and merges each pair in C immediately. If |B|>=2, some letter
maps the whole B to a; appending it after a letter with preimage C
of B merges every pair in C in at most two steps. Thus C is the
stated collision clique. At the thirteen-state parameter a cover of
P5 has size at most three, so |C|-1<=3. B itself is a clique in P1,
and binomial(|B|,2)<=4. Finally an independent set in the union of
the two cliques B and C has size at most two. Its induced graph
therefore needs at least |B union C|-2 cover vertices, proving
|B union C|<=5. These are necessary cuts, not a new upper on F.

<a id="problem4-second-entrance-fiber--audit"></a>
#### Audit

check_second_entrance.py recomputes ordinary subset and pair distances,
the three-dimensional annihilator, all admitted preimages, and the
boundary restrictions on applicable known equality certificates. It
also verifies the elementary Boolean-cell classification literally.
Finite controls support the symbolic proof; neither they nor a bounded
solver run certify absence of an extremal automaton.

<a id="problem4-short-pair-span"></a>
<a id="problem4-short-pair-span--short-pair-span-pruning-for-problem-4"></a>
### Short-pair span pruning for Problem 4

8 October 2026. These are auxiliary, alphabet-independent compression lemmas,
not an exact formula for F. The manuscript's extrema are unchanged. The
finite checker is `check_short_pair_span.py`; its controls supplement, and do
not replace, the following proofs. No reachable-image assumption is needed.

<a id="problem4-short-pair-span--1-span-bound"></a>
#### 1. Span bound

Let an n-state automaton be strongly connected and synchronizing. Let P_h be
the simple graph whose edges are unordered pairs merged by a word of length
at most h. For a fixed s>=2 let W_h be the real span of the characteristic
rows of all independent s-sets of P_h, and let D_h=dim W_h.

If D_h<n, every s-set compresses in at most D_h+h letters. If there is no
independent s-set, every s-set already contains a short pair and compresses
within h; this includes the D_h=0 case.

Proof. Suppose the shortest compression of S has length L>D_h+h. Every word
w of length at most D_h has |Sw|=s. Moreover Sw contains no edge of P_h:
otherwise w followed by a merging word of length at most h compresses S
in fewer than L letters. Thus V_(D_h) is contained in W_h, where V_i is the
span of chi_S D_w for |w|<=i. Here D_w is the right-action transformation
matrix, not the scalar dimension D_h.

V_0 has dimension one. Equality V_i=V_(i+1) implies invariance under every
letter and permanent stabilization. A reset word followed by a path to any
q maps S to q, so V_infinity contains s e_q for every q and is R^n. Therefore
dim V_i>=min(i+1,n). Since D_h<n, dim V_(D_h)>=D_h+1, a contradiction. QED.

The condition D_h<n is essential: with D_h=n this argument says nothing.
Strong connectivity is used to obtain reset words to all states; one must
not silently drop it from this statement.

<a id="problem4-short-pair-span--2-rank-of-maximum-independent-sets"></a>
#### 2. Rank of maximum independent sets

For a simple graph G with minimum vertex cover size t>=2, the characteristic
rows of its maximum independent sets span a space of dimension at most
2t-1. For t=1 the corresponding valid bound is two, not one.

Proof. Fix a maximum independent set I, with complement C of size t. For
an independent T subset C write N(T) for its neighborhood in I. Maximality
of the cardinality of I gives |N(T)|>=|T| for every such T: otherwise
(I minus N(T)) union T would be larger. Every maximum independent set J
therefore has the form (I minus N(T)) union T with T=J minus I independent,
|N(T)|=|T|. Conversely each such tight T gives a maximum set.

Let U be the union of these tight T, and B=N(U). If A is a union of previously
processed tight sets and T is the next one, then A intersection T is
independent and

  |N(A union T)|-|A union T|
    <= |N(A)|-|A| + |A intersection T|-|N(A intersection T)|
    <= |N(A)|-|A|.

Starting at the empty union yields |B|<=|U|<=t. Only the coordinates U union B
vary among maximum independent sets. If this union is empty, there is just
one maximum set and the row rank is one. Otherwise B is nonempty, and the
sum of the variable coordinates in each row is |B|. All other coordinates
are fixed zero or one. Recovering those fixed coordinates as linear
multiples of that sum shows that the row rank is at most |U|+|B|. This proves
the desired bound unless |U|=|B|=t.

In that exceptional case, we prove that the bipartite edges between C=U and
B have a perfect matching. Process tight sets T in any order. The deficit
|N(A)|-|A| is nonpositive and cannot increase by the preceding inequality.
Its final value is zero, so every intermediate deficit is zero. At each
addition this forces

  N(A) intersection N(T) = N(A intersection T),
  |N(A intersection T)| = |A intersection T|.

The equality of sets follows from containment and the forced equal
cardinalities. Every subset X of T is independent and has |N(X)|>=|X|.
Hall's theorem gives a perfect matching between T and N(T). In any such
matching, A intersection T occupies exactly N(A intersection T), since its
vertices have no other neighbors and the cardinalities agree. Hence T minus
A is matched into N(T) minus N(A). Keeping a previously constructed matching
of A to N(A) and adding these edges extends the matching to A union T.
Induction gives a perfect matching from C to B.

Each maximum independent set contains exactly t vertices of C union B;
it contains at most one endpoint of each of these t matching edges, hence
exactly one from each. All t pair sums in its characteristic row equal one.
Their homogeneous versions impose t-1 independent linear equations on the
2t variable coordinates. The fixed coordinates are again determined by a
pair sum, so the row rank is at most t+1<=2t-1 for t>=2. QED.

The union-neighborhood inequality is the usual mechanism behind Hajnal's
intersection-union inequality for maximum independent sets. The proof above
is included to avoid assuming a graph result without its equality case.
No priority claim for the graph inequality or the span method is made.
Primary-source background checked on 8 October 2026:
N. Alon, *Hitting all maximum independent sets*, Section 2.2,
https://www.tau.ac.il/~nogaa/PDFS/hitmax1.pdf (Hajnal attribution).

<a id="problem4-short-pair-span--3-consequence-for-the-smallest-unresolved-parameter"></a>
#### 3. Consequence for the smallest unresolved parameter

Put m=n-s>=2 and assume n>=2m. If the vertex cover number of P_h is m,
its independent s-sets are maximum independent sets. The preceding lemmas
give compression length at most 2m-1+h, because 2m-1<n.
If that cover number exceeds m, no independent s-set exists, and compression
takes at most h. Consequently, compression length strictly greater than
2m-1+h forces the cover number of P_h to be at most m-1.

At n=13,s=9,target=12 this gives a three-vertex cover of P_4. In particular,
after relabeling states that cover can be contained in {0,1,2}. A putative
avoid-or-compress witness of value 12 has compression length at least 12,
so this pruning is necessary for every such witness, binary or unrestricted.
It neither proves nor disproves existence.

The refinement of the Frankl-Pin bound gives |P_1|<=4 at this parameter:
any five distinct pairs admit a sequence with four holes, giving compression
at most 15-5+1=11 if |P_1|>=5. More generally a cardinality cap
c=binomial(m+2,2)+h-target follows from the universal endpoint construction
only when 0<=c<=m, because it constructs sequences of c+1<=m+1 pairs.
The refined bound uses p(P_h), the maximum admitted sequence length, NOT
|P_h|. No bounds |P_2|<=5, |P_3|<=6 or |P_4|<=7 are proved here.
The earlier implementation incorrectly extrapolated the sequence argument
to those higher caps. Those cuts have been removed; every affected failed
search must be rerun without them before making a complete-family claim.
The uniform span lemmas above and all manuscript extrema are unaffected.
The refinement itself is credited to Kisielewicz--Kowalski--Szykula,
CIAA 2016, Theorem 1; see the manuscript's existing reference and proof notes.

For lower-potential synthesis phi never exceeds actual shortest pair
distance. We may impose these cuts on phi only as an existence-search
restriction: choosing phi=min(actual distance,12) admits every genuine
witness after the stated relabeling. A failed or timed-out solver run is
not a certified upper bound.

<a id="problem4-short-pair-span--4-finite-adversarial-controls"></a>
#### 4. Finite adversarial controls

The checker uses exact integer elimination over Q. It checks all 33,867
labeled simple graphs through n=6, 2,000 seeded random graphs on 7..13
vertices, all 66,281 ordered binary automata on 2..4 states, and 300 seeded
random automata on 4..7 states with two to four letters. Compression checks
use all subsets, including unreachable ones. The exact finite scopes and
counts are in `short_pair_span_audit.json`.

Boundary controls: an edge with isolated vertices has t=1 and row rank two;
C_5 has t=3 and row rank five, showing the 2t-1 bound can be attained;
t disjoint edges with isolated vertices have row rank t+1; a graph with
unique maximum independent set has row rank one. No all-parameter equality
for F follows from these auxiliary statements.

<a id="problem4-short-pair-structure"></a>
<a id="problem4-short-pair-structure--necessary-short-pair-structure-for-tight-compression"></a>
### Necessary short-pair structure for tight compression

This is a direct consequence of the credited Frankl--Pin refinement, not
an asserted exact formula. It applies to arbitrary finite alphabets.
Put m=n-s and T=binom(m+2,2). Let P_h be the pairs merging in at most h letters.
If some s-subset has shortest compression length T, then

    |P_h| <= h    for every 1<=h<=m.

Proof: any q<=m+1 distinct pairs admit an s-subset Frankl--Pin sequence
of length q, in any chosen order, indexed i=0,...,q-1. For its ith pair E_i, choose a hole set
H_i of size m disjoint from E_i, containing an endpoint outside E_i of
each later pair. Each later pair is distinct and thus has such an endpoint.
There are at most q-i-1<=m required endpoints. Fill H_i outside E_i;
n-2>=m since s>=2. Then S_i=Q minus H_i contains E_i and fails to contain
every later pair, giving the required sequence. This is exactly the
standard convention E_i is not contained in S_j for j<i: S_j was chosen
to omit an endpoint of its later pair E_i. No reversal of the sequence
or change of the Frankl--Pin convention is needed.

If |P_h|>=h+1 for h<=m, choose h+1 of those pairs, so p(P_h)>=h+1.
The bound T-p(P_h)+h from CIAA 2016 Theorem 1 yields compression <=T-1,
contradicting tightness. Merging words shorter than h can be padded with
arbitrary original letters, so the refinement's height convention agrees.

At codimension three, any length-ten compression witness therefore has
at most 1,2,3 merged pairs within respectively 1,2,3 letters, irrespective
of alphabet size. This explains a safe synthesis prune. It does not prove
nonexistence of such a witness or a general compression upper bound nine.

<a id="problem4-singleton-c-d125-unrestricted-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-singleton-c-d125-unrestricted-exclusion--two-complete-singleton-cd125-conditional-exclusions"></a>
### Two complete singleton-C/D125 conditional exclusions

At (13,9,1), ac(S,{3})=12, neither of the following third geometries
can occur in a strongly connected synchronizing automaton, for any
finite alphabet:

1. B={0}, C={4}, D={1,2,5}, id b1_in_c1_third5;
2. B={4}, C={0}, D={1,2,5}, id b1_out_c2_third5.

These are whole conditional third-type exclusions, not exact F values
or a numerical distinction between binary and unrestricted alphabets.

For case 1 the accepted fourth-space classification, under K={1,2}
covering P5, gives exactly E={6},{1,6},{1,2,6}, with respectively
7,14,7 labels. All further admissible covered preD fibers are precisely
A,B,C,D,E; there are no extra Boolean companions. Some letter supplies
preC=D and some supplies preD=E. The E6 paper proof excludes the first
geometry. The universal free-image proofs exclude the other two.
Thus every possible fourth extension is impossible. The three proofs
cover arbitrary alphabets and all individual fields (16,12,12), not
merely binary field pairs. All eight labels of D are covered by the
original stabilizer normalization.

Case 2 transports this complete argument by the state permutation
p=(0 4), which fixes A,D,K and all ordinary states. Removing mandatory
B and C from the original P5 cover leaves the same K={1,2} in both
cases. The old size-three cover itself is not asserted to be preserved:
only the residual cover K used by these proofs is preserved.

The literal initial families require 3,0,4 and one point of D; they
are identical after swapping B and C. The annihilator basis columns
(1 outside A,B,C,D,E), exact preimage hierarchy and target/input atoms
are conjugated by p. Rational linear identities, Boolean one-count
conditions, independence, incomparability, mandatory intersections,
and outside-K pair covers are invariant under a state permutation.
Consequently all fresh E labels and all companion fields are exactly
transported; an additional letter or fourth geometry is not omitted.
The individual third columns and 14 parent pairs of the actual second
inventory are independently checked against this transport. Both
types have eight D labels. A stabilizer element transports every
allowed D label in either normalization; no unlabelled row is assumed
to represent a fixed second letter.

At the previous frontier the first type was already excluded for
binary alphabets. The second retained nine parent pairs, after five
historical common-block exclusions. This proof removes those nine,
not all fourteen as newly excluded. For unrestricted alphabets both
whole types are newly excluded. The E6 removal already applied within
the first type and is not counted as an extra third geometry.

The composition checker independently enumerates all labelled fresh
E candidates satisfying the residual cover, incomparability, rank and
one-count initial-family conditions; it obtains exactly 28 labels in
each case. It transports all individual fields and the complete parent
third inventory, verifies source hashes for all three branch proofs,
and confirms all companion lists are retained. It also conjugates and
literally reevaluates the finite structural boundary controls. These
controls are not attaining F witnesses. No global upper or alphabet
separation is inferred from a conditional exclusion.

<a id="problem4-singleton-c-d15-e12-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-singleton-c-d15-e12-exclusion--two-root-singleton-cd15e12-fourth-cut"></a>
### Two-root singleton-C/D15/E12 fourth cut

At (13,9,1), equality12, the E12 fourth extension is impossible in

using all twelve individual fields, exact D/E suppliers, the residual

maps free inputs onto O, so no letter can collide inside O. Every M
then enters D at5; every F fixes5. SC needs a T:2->1, which produces
a mandatory or outside-K merger within four. No binary capacity is used.

H={0,3,4}, D15, E12, K12 and O. The old larger cover itself need not be
preserved; only residual K is used. The two actual third inventories

Guard swaps and ordinary-state permutations transport the proof to

<a id="problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag"></a>
<a id="problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag--a-common-predecessor-fiber-at-singleton-equality"></a>
### A common predecessor fiber at singleton equality

8 October 2026. Auxiliary necessary structure for local equality, not a
new extremal value. Arbitrary finite alphabets are permitted. Reachability
of the initial subset is not assumed.

<a id="problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag--proposition"></a>
#### Proposition

Let a strongly connected synchronizing n-state automaton have
ac(S,{a})=n-1 and |S|=s>=4. There is one nonempty set B disjoint from {a}
such that every letter has preimage of a equal to either {a} or B. At
least one letter uses B. If the union of all one-letter kernels has at
most four pairs, then |B|<=3.

The range s>=4 matters. At s=3, two distinct nontrivial predecessor
fibers, if present, must be complementary in Q minus {a}. This exception
is retained in the finite checks, not silently excluded.

<a id="problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Use right-action matrices D_w and characteristic row chi_S. By the
equality flag in [Equality flags for the avoid-or-compress bound](#problem4-local-equality-flag), the real space

  V_i=span{chi_S D_w: |w|<=i}

has dimension i+1 for 0<=i<=n-2. Thus the annihilator of V_(n-3) has
dimension two. It contains h=s e_a-1, with 1 the all-one column. For
each letter ell let C_ell be its preimage of a and
d_ell=chi_(C_ell)-e_a (columns). For |w|<=n-3 both w and w ell are safe:
their image rows are characteristic, include a, and have size s.
Consequently chi_S D_w d_ell=0, so d_ell also lies in that annihilator.
These uses of characteristic rows require the no-collision implication
of safety; replacing them by arbitrary set images would be invalid.

Each C_ell is nonempty and intersects S in exactly one point. If it
contains a, it cannot contain another point q. All images through depth
n-3 would then omit q, since including both a and q would cause the
next letter to collide. Strong connectivity gives a path from some
state of S to every q in at most n-s steps: before first reaching q,
a shortest such path visits only the n-s states outside S. Since
n-s<=n-3 for s>=3, this is a contradiction. Hence C_ell containing a
is exactly {a}.

Some letter has C_ell different from {a}, or every letter fixes a and
{a} is a sink, contrary to strong connectivity. Choose one such fiber B.
It is nonempty, excludes a, and is not Q minus {a}, since |S intersect B|=1
while s-1>=3. The columns h and d_B are independent: at a point outside
{a} union B, h is -1 while d_B is zero. Thus they form a basis of the
two-dimensional annihilator.

For another nontrivial fiber C, write d_C=lambda h+mu d_B. At a point
outside {a} union B, its zero-one coordinate gives -lambda in {0,1}.
If lambda=0, nonemptiness of C forces mu=1, and C=B.
If lambda=-1, C contains every point outside {a} union B. On B the
coordinate is 1+mu, hence mu is zero or minus one. In the first case
C=Q minus {a}, contradicting |S intersect C|=1. In the second,
C=(Q minus {a}) minus B and |S intersect C|=s-2. This equals one
only for s=3. Thus for s>=4 every nontrivial fiber is B.

Finally, a letter with preimage B merges all binomial(|B|,2) pairs in B.
If the one-letter kernel union has at most four pairs, this forces
|B|<=3. QED.

<a id="problem4-singleton-predecessor-flag--application-and-limits"></a>
#### Application and limits

At (n,s,r)=(13,9,1), a target-twelve witness has P1<=4 by the independently
proved refinement, so its common B has size one, two or three. A three-
vertex cover of P5 can be normalized to {0,1,2}. Within those labels the
protected state can be normalized to 0 if it lies in the cover, or to 3
if it lies outside. These two slices cover all possible witnesses;
neither location is silently assumed. The remaining labels within the
cover and outside it may be permuted while fixing the protected state.

The subsequently proved protected-pair isolation in [A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag)
makes the inside-cover slice redundant: choose a cover omitting the
isolated protected state, then use only protected label 3. This is a
choice of normalization, not a claim that a cover containing an isolated
vertex cannot be written down.

These conditions restrict general letters, not only rank-one maps or a
permutation companion. Every positive still needs ordinary BFS checks
of synchronization, strong connectivity, reaching S, and exact local
delay. A timeout in either slice is not an upper bound.

<a id="problem4-singleton-third-chain-unrestricted-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-singleton-third-chain-unrestricted-exclusion--complete-singleton-third-chain-obstruction-at-1391"></a>
### Complete singleton third-chain obstruction at (13,9,1)

Assume strong connectivity, synchronization, |Q|=13, |S|=9 and
ac(S,{a})=12. Then c(S)>=12, m=4, dim V_i=i+1 through i=11,
and every point mandatory through depth4 is isolated in P7.
Suppose a two-state K covers P5, and the first three entrances
B={b},C={c},D={d} are distinct singletons outside {a}.
Their common exact fields are pre(a) in {a,B}, pre(B) in {a,B,C},
and pre(C) in {a,B,C,D}, by the established singleton Boolean
inventory. These conditions are impossible for arbitrary alphabets.
S need not be an initial reachable image for this auxiliary obstruction.

<a id="problem4-singleton-third-chain-unrestricted-exclusion--abstract-singleton-inverse-version-of-the-kernel-obstruction"></a>
#### Abstract singleton-inverse version of the kernel obstruction

The graph argument in [Two-cover obstruction for a one-count immediate kernel](#problem4-two-cover-protected-kernel-obstruction)
uses S only to prove that every singleton fiber pre_f(e) is a P7
isolate. Therefore its same matching, path and growth proof gives:
in a synchronizing n>=4 automaton with a two-state P5 cover, if
e is its unique immediate pair, every singleton pre_f(e) is a P7
isolate, and some letter collapses e to a state outside e, there is
a contradiction. No strong connectivity or S premise is needed
once the singleton-isolation condition is given. Distinct-edge
inverse graphs and immediate kernel pairs remain separate.

<a id="problem4-singleton-third-chain-unrestricted-exclusion--two-finite-dimensional-facts"></a>
#### Two finite-dimensional facts

First, let a seven-state core J be mandatory through depth4, and
let a pair e outside J be one-count through depth4. If e is the
unique immediate pair, any singleton pre_f(e)={p} has p outside e:
the two e inputs have the same output, so either both belong to
that vertex fiber or neither does. Safety and the one-count property
make p mandatory through depth3. If p were outside J, every image
through3 would be J plus p plus one e endpoint, because |S|=9.
There would be at most two such images, giving dim V3<=2, whereas
equality gives dim V3=4. Thus p is in J and is P7-isolated.
The abstract singleton-inverse obstruction excludes any supplier
collapsing this pair to a singleton of J outside e.

Second, an eight-state core J mandatory through4 is impossible.
Every image through3 is J plus one variable state. These rows are
linearly independent for distinct variable states, so dim V3=4
forces exactly four distinct variable states. For a letter f and
target j in J, its exact fiber meets every one of these images once.
If it meets J, it can contain only that core point: any further
point would give an immediate pair incident to a P7 isolate.
If it avoids J, it contains all four variable states, hence has
at least six immediate kernel pairs, contradicting unique P1.
Every j consequently has a singleton preimage in J under every
letter. Each letter permutes J, contradicting synchronization.

<a id="problem4-singleton-third-chain-unrestricted-exclusion--growing-the-singleton-chain-without-assuming-common-fibers"></a>
#### Growing the singleton chain without assuming common fibers

Write J={a,b,c,d} initially. The entrance depth of the last singleton
is8. Every letter's preimage of that singleton is nonempty and meets
every image through7 once. A fiber meeting J must be a singleton
of J, because J is P7-isolated. If every such fiber lay in J, J
would be a proper backward-closed set, using the earlier exact
fields; strong connectivity forbids this. Choose a fresh fiber R
outside J. Since it maps to a singleton, unique P1 forces |R|<=2.

At one-count depths7,6,5 a pair R is impossible by the uniform
kernel obstruction: it maps outside itself, c(S)>=m+8, and its
one-count prefix is at least m+1. A singleton R in K is impossible
by mandatory P7 isolation and the one-cover compression floor.
Thus each surviving fresh fiber is a singleton outside J union K.

It remains essential to control all other letters' fibers, not just
this chosen supplier. After adding a fresh singleton, for each of
the first three new depths7,6,5 the annihilator has exactly the
dimension of the known singleton columns. On Q minus {a}, its
basis is 1 plus the indicators of the known outside singleton
states. A Boolean column in this span has ordinary-cell value c0
in {0,1} and singleton values v_i in {0,1}; its one-count condition
is (8-l)c0+sum v_i=1, with l=4,5,6 known outside singletons.
For c0=1 the left side is at least2; for c0=0 exactly one v_i is1.
Hence every outside one-count fiber is an already known singleton;
the {a} fiber is allowed separately. This checks all companions and
suppliers and proves the required common-column conclusion here.
It is not extrapolated to pair or overlapping-fiber geometries.

Accordingly the core grows from4 to5 to6 to7 singletons, mandatory
through depths7,6,5 respectively, while every earlier preimage
stays in the enlarged core. A fresh fiber of the last singleton
exists again by backward closure. It is outside the seven-state core,
has size at most two, and is one-count through4. If it is a pair,
the first finite-dimensional fact and abstract obstruction exclude
it. If it is a singleton, the enlarged eight-state mandatory core
is excluded by the second fact. No case remains.

<a id="problem4-singleton-third-chain-unrestricted-exclusion--scope-and-controls"></a>
#### Scope and controls

The ordinary-cell complement becomes a valid one-count column at
l=7; the proof never uses the l<=6 classification at that boundary.
The checker retains this control, exhausts every labelled eight-core
and four-variable family, and checks all seven-core/pair/singleton
placements. It also follows every labelled ordinary singleton
prefix and every covered last fresh fiber for the three current
singleton third types. Historical equality, mandatory and cover
lemmas are explicit premises; no binary capacity shortcut is used.

This excludes both complete C4/D5 third types and the third type
B4/C5/D0, independently of alphabet size. Combining the complete
five-D inventory and earlier cuts excludes the whole joints B0/C4
and B4/C0. Other three-cover joints remain. No new numerical value
of F(13,9,1), alphabet separation or complete answer follows yet.

<a id="problem4-singleton-three-kernel-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-singleton-three-kernel-exclusion--the-three-point-first-entrance-cannot-have-singleton-second-entrance-at-1391"></a>
### The three-point first entrance cannot have singleton second entrance at (13,9,1)

9 October 2026. Complete conditional computer-assisted exclusion only.
This does not determine F(13,9,1) and is outside the article release.

<a id="problem4-singleton-three-kernel-exclusion--statement-and-reduction"></a>
#### Statement and reduction

A binary strongly connected synchronizing thirteen-state automaton
cannot have ac(S,{a})=12, |S|=9, first entrance |B|=3 and singleton
second entrance C. The statement does not require S to be reachable;
it therefore excludes the branch under the manuscript's stronger
actual-image requirement as well. No unrestricted-alphabet exclusion
is asserted.

Here is the reduction to |P1|<=4. A Frankl--Pin sequence consists of
nine-sets S_i and pairs E_i contained in S_i such that E_i is not
contained in any earlier S_j. For any five distinct pairs E_1,...,E_5,
construct S_j by omitting one endpoint outside E_j from each later
E_i, then fill its complement to four points outside E_j. Each later
pair is distinct from E_j, so such an endpoint exists; at most four
omissions are required. This gives a length-five sequence. Thus if
|P1|>=5, the refinement of Kisielewicz, Kowalski and Szykula,
Experiments with Synchronizing Automata (CIAA 2016), Theorem 1, gives
compression of every nine-set within

  binomial(13-9+2,2) - 5 + 1 = 11.

This contradicts local value twelve. The cited refinement uses the
maximum admitted sequence length p(P1), not the number of pairs:
the endpoint construction is what permits p(P1)>=5 here. No higher
layer edge-count cap is used. The primary reference is
https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-40946-7_15.

[Localization of a binary moving-letter kernel](#problem4-localized-binary-entrance-kernel) proves that the unique
moving letter M must have exactly the kernel blocks B, E and
singletons, where E is a two-point set disjoint from B. It also proves
the complete normalization of all rows and initial subsets into the
three first-level actions, and of the moving row into permutation
conjugacy types. There is no fixed cycle length or prescribed cycle
type on the nine-element M-invariant set.

<a id="problem4-singleton-three-kernel-exclusion--complete-computation"></a>
#### Complete computation

One of the mixed-cover cases already has a symbolic exclusion: for

  (5+2+5) * 4 * 7! = 241,920

<a id="problem4-third-entrance-space"></a>
<a id="problem4-third-entrance-space--a-third-entrance-space-without-assuming-a-common-third-fiber"></a>
### A third entrance space, without assuming a common third fiber

9 October 2026. Auxiliary necessary structure; no new extremal value.

Let a strongly connected synchronizing automaton over any finite
alphabet satisfy ac(S,{a})=t=n-1 with s=|S|>=5. Write B,C for the
first two common entrances from [A common entrance fiber for the protected set](#problem4-entry-fiber-flag) and
[A second common entrance fiber at singleton equality](#problem4-second-entrance-fiber). Then some letter has a preimage D of C
outside {a}, distinct from B,C, with the following properties:

* Each letter's preimage of C is either {a} or a nonempty subset R
  of O=Q minus {a}. Every image through depth t-4 meets R once.
* D is incomparable with B and C. Any two distinct one-count fibers
  among B,C and the outside preimages of C are incomparable.
* The restrictions of the four-dimensional trajectory annihilator
  to O have basis 1_O,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D. Every outside preimage R of
  C has indicator in this span. This does not in general force R=D.
* Each outside preimage of C is a collision clique in P3. If H
  covers P5, it contains all but at most one point of each such fiber.

No initial-set reachability assumption is used.

<a id="problem4-third-entrance-space--proof"></a>
#### Proof

For a letter ell, every image Sw with |w|<=t-4 meets ell^(-1)(C)
once, because Sw ell meets C once through depth t-3. Safety ensures
these are collision-free characteristic rows. A preimage containing
a must be {a}: otherwise all those images would omit another point
of that preimage, contrary to strong connectivity reaching every
point from S within m=n-s<=t-4 steps.

At least one preimage D is outside {a},B,C. Otherwise the preimage
under every letter of the proper nonempty union {a} union B union C
would be contained in that union, using also the already proved
preimage descriptions of a and B. Its complement could not reach
it. The union is proper because it meets S in at most three points
and s>=5. Every outside preimage meets S once. If two such one-count
fibers, including B,C, were properly nested, images through depth
t-4 would omit their difference, again contradicting m<=t-4.

Equality gives dim V_(t-4)=t-3=n-4, so its annihilator has dimension
four. It contains h_a=s e_a-1 and h_X=s chi_X-1 for X=B,C,D. Their
restrictions to O span 1_O,chi_B,chi_C,chi_D. The first three are
independent. The Boolean classification used in the second-entrance
proof shows that only B and C among Boolean vectors in
span{1_O,chi_B,chi_C} can meet S once when s>=5. Thus D supplies the
fourth independent column. Any other preimage R has h_R in the same
annihilator, proving the span assertion. A letter taking R into C,
followed by a word of length at most two merging a specified pair
in C, merges that pair of R in at most three steps.

<a id="problem4-third-entrance-space--thirteen-state-inventory-and-a-warning"></a>
#### Thirteen-state inventory and a warning

For H={0,1,2}, a=3, B={0,1,4}, the three remaining second entrances
are {2,5}, {0,2,5}, {0,1,2,5}. A possible D is nonempty, has at most
one point outside H, is incomparable with B,C, and admits a nine-set
containing a and meeting B,C,D once. Also |B union C union D|<=6:
the union of three collision cliques has independence number at
most three, and its vertex cover has size at most three.

Exact Boolean-column enumeration gives, for these fixed B,C:

| C | D orbits | Labelled D sets | Orbits allowing an additional fiber |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| {2,5} | 12 | 65 | 4 |
| {0,2,5} | 16 | 64 | 2 |
| {0,1,2,5} | 8 | 59 | 0 |

The common-third-fiber claim must not be extrapolated from the last
row. For example B={0,1,4}, C={0,2,5}, D={0,1,5}, R={0,2,4} satisfy
chi_R=chi_B+chi_C-chi_D. All four meet the nine-set
{0,3,6,7,8,9,10,11,12} once, are incomparable, and satisfy the cover
cuts. This is a geometric/linear control, not an automaton equality
witness or a counterexample to a stronger full-automaton theorem.

enumerate_third_entrance.py enumerates the stabilizer cell counts
and solves the four-column Boolean equations over exact rationals.
The independent checker enumerates labelled D sets, each possible
covered R, literal nine-set intersections and exact augmented ranks.
No geometric admission or solver timeout is treated as exclusion.

<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility"></a>
<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility--exact-atom-compatibility-for-covered-kernel-partitions"></a>
### Exact atom compatibility for covered kernel partitions

This is an auxiliary necessary-condition audit for the (13,9,1)
equality target12, for binary and arbitrary finite alphabets. It does
not determine either extremum or assert realization of retained classes.

<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility--uniform-letter-criterion"></a>
#### Uniform letter criterion

Let I_i and O_i be indexed partitions of Q, including empty atoms.
Fix a partition pi of Q into exact kernel blocks. A transformation f
with f(I_i) contained in O_i and exact kernel partition pi exists iff
each block lies within an input atom and the number q_i of blocks
contained in I_i satisfies q_i<=|O_i| for every i. Indeed f induces
an injection of these blocks into O_i. Conversely independent such
injections define f, with no accidental collisions between atoms.

For two specified partitions pi,rho in two fields with the same
output atoms, compatible transformations whose combined images equal
Q exist iff both individual criteria hold and q_i(pi)+q_i(rho)>=|O_i|
for each i. Two subsets of O_i of the prescribed sizes can cover O_i
exactly under this inequality, and each quotient can be bijected onto
its chosen subset. This is an incoming-edge condition, not a proof of
strong connectivity, synchronization, safety, or S reachability.

<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility--complete-covered-partition-enumeration"></a>
#### Complete covered partition enumeration

Under equality12 the established arbitrary-alphabet premises give a
cover H={0,1,2} of P5 and |P1|<=4. The latter uses the credited
Frankl--Pin sequence refinement: five distinct immediate pairs admit
a length-five sequence of nine-sets by omitting one endpoint outside
each current pair from every later pair, then filling the complement
to four points. Compression would take at most15-5+1=11.
No higher-layer edge-count cap is used.

For a third geometry enumerate every nine-set containing3 and meeting
B,C,D once. Its intersection J is mandatory through8, hence isolated
in P7 by [Isolation of the mandatory core at the reaching depth](#problem4-mandatory-core-isolation) (m=4,c(S)>=12). Every letter
kernel therefore avoids J. Every nontrivial kernel block has at most
one point outside H, since two such points would form an uncovered
P1 edge. Partition H into groups; each group may be joined to at most
one outside state, and distinct groups have distinct outside partners.
All other states are singleton blocks. This enumerates every covered
kernel partition, including the empty kernel. Retain only partitions
with at most four pair edges, none incident to J. A group of size g
contributes binomial(g,2) pairs, not g-1; triples and additional pairs
are counted explicitly.

The field pre(A),pre(B),pre(C) determines input atoms by its three
membership bits; the output atoms use A,B,C. Apply the quotient-block
criterion to each field. All admitted Boolean companions are retained.
In B1/B2 the intact independently checked native fields are used.
For B3 every combination pre(A) in {A,B}, pre(B) in {A,B,C}, and
pre(C) in {A} union the full admitted outside-fiber list is considered.
Only impossible empty-output atoms and forced immediate kernel pairs
outside H or exceeding four are filtered. No binary crossing rule is
applied to an arbitrary-alphabet field.

<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility--shared-immediate-pair-graph"></a>
#### Shared immediate-pair graph

For a binary profile retain it only if its two compatible exact kernels
have a nonempty union of at most four pairs, and satisfy the incoming
coverage criterion above. The actual P1 graph is exactly that union;
all-permutation alphabets cannot synchronize. All other equality and
reachability conditions are deliberately left to further work.

For arbitrary alphabets choose, separately and with repetitions allowed,
one supplying field/kernel for each of pre(A)=B, pre(B)=C, pre(C)=D.
The union of their pairs must have at most four edges. These suppliers
may be the same letter. Every actual alphabet supplies such a choice,
because its common P1 graph contains each of the chosen kernels. A
successful choice is only a necessary overapproximation: other letters,
incoming coverage, and all later pair/image conditions remain unchecked.
In particular there is no bounded alphabet-size assertion here.

<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility--complete-joint-composition"></a>
#### Complete joint composition

Every actual B,C joint has a fresh D in its complete third inventory,
by [A third entrance space, without assuming a common third fiber](#problem4-third-entrance-space). Consequently a joint is excluded for
arbitrary alphabets if every third geometry has already been excluded
by a recorded arbitrary-alphabet proof or by the present supplier
test. For binary alphabets it suffices that every third geometry has
no remaining admitted profile pair. This uses all native third rows,
including every companion; geometric admission is not substituted for
typed binary admission. The immutable baseline state is verified
against checkpoint16 and the comparison snapshot is verified against
that state. Previously excluded joints are not counted again.

This complete composition additionally records two binary joints
(b2_in_c2,b2_mixed_c2) and five unrestricted joints
(b1_in_c3,b1_in_c4,b1_in_c5,b2_in_c2,b2_mixed_c2).
Some of their third cuts were already known at checkpoint16; this
is a reconciliation of complete joint consequences, not a claim that
every underlying third cut is newly proved here.

<a id="problem4-three-cover-atom-kernel-compatibility--verification-scope"></a>
#### Verification scope

The independent checker enumerates simple graphs of at most four edges
incident to H, accepting exactly disjoint unions of cliques, rather
than importing the guard-group generator. It reconstructs quotient
counts and both supplier and binary decisions on the complete historical
inventories. Separate literal labelled-map controls test the uniform
single-letter criterion and the two-letter incoming coverage criterion,
including empty atoms, identity kernels, triple blocks and multiple
pair blocks. Source bindings and the immutable comparison snapshot
identify the precise current counts. No sampled negative is an upper
bound and no numerical alphabet separation follows.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--triangle-early-pair-obstruction-at-codimension-three"></a>
### Triangle early-pair obstruction at codimension three

**当前证明依赖。** 本节的符号分类及测试域推导仍使用；后面的有限动作/距离排除
现由[纸面替代引理](#problem4-paper-dependency-reductions)代替，保留的枚举描述为历史独立控制。

**Claim.** For n>=6, a strongly connected synchronizing automaton with an
(n-3)-subset of shortest compression length ten cannot have

    P1={01}, P2={01,02}, P3={01,02,12}.

The alphabet is arbitrary and finite; reachability of the subset is not
assumed. Throughout C={0,1,2}. A hole set covers P3 exactly when it is C
or is {i,j,x}, with {i,j} a core pair and x outside C. Every image reached
within six letters must have such holes, else a P3 word compresses the
original subset within nine letters.

The distinct images reached within i letters grow strictly at each step
until a compressed image is included. A plateau would be invariant under
every letter and contradict synchronization. Thus the assumptions imply
at least i+1 distinct images within i letters for 0<=i<=9.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--letter-structure"></a>
#### Letter structure

The credited short-pair refinement forces every letter to be a permutation
or a rank-(n-1) map with common kernel 01. Inverse pairs of 01 lie in P2;
inverse pairs of 02 lie in P3. A permutation therefore preserves C. A
singular letter has missing output 0 or 1. If it omits 1, inverse pairs
of 02 force it to map C onto {0,2}. If it omits 0, write its kernel
image c=f(0)=f(1) and its other core image t=f(2), with c!=t and c,t!=0.

Some permutation g satisfies g^{-1}(01)=02, since singular letters have
no two-point preimages of 01. In particular g(02)=01 and g preserves C
and its complement. Strong connectivity requires a singular letter that
does not preserve C: otherwise every letter preserves this proper set.
Such a letter omits 0. Its possibilities are:

* A: c in {1,2}, t outside C;
* B1: c outside C, t=1;
* B2: c outside C, t=2;
* C: c,t outside C.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--case-a-pure-exclusion"></a>
#### Case A: pure exclusion

[Necessary exclusion of one mixing singular letter in early triangle type](#problem4-triangle-mixing-case-a) proves this case impossible. Briefly, the domain
D_f of P3-covering holes whose f-images also cover P3 consists of C,
{0,2,v}, {1,2,v}, and all {0,1,x}, where v is the unique external
preimage of the other point in {1,2}. Its intersection with g^{-1}(D_f)
has at most four elements. All images reached within four letters must
be in that intersection, contradicting strict image growth.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--case-b1-pure-exclusion"></a>
#### Case B1: pure exclusion

Let v be the unique external preimage of 2. Then

    D_f={C,{0,1,v}}
        union {{0,2,x},{1,2,x}: x outside C}.

Define D=D_f intersection g^{-1}(D_f) intersection f^{-1}(D_f).
All images reached within four letters lie in D: appending f, gf or ff
must still cover P3 within six letters.

The core pair 02 has at most one external choice in D, because g sends
02 to 01. For pair 12, membership in f^{-1}(D_f) forces x=v or f(x)=v,
so there are at most two external choices. The pair 01 has at most its
single choice v. The hole C belongs to f^{-1}(D_f) only if c=v. If c=v,
there is no external preimage of v (it is the kernel image), so the pair
12 has only its choice v. Thus |D|<=4 in both cases c=v and c!=v. Strict
image growth within four letters gives a contradiction.

This argument excludes B1 for every singular letter in any putative
tight triangle automaton. It is subsequently used as a necessary cut.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--case-b2-reduction-to-two-four-image-domains"></a>
#### Case B2: reduction to two four-image domains

Now f(2)=2. Let v=f^{-1}(1) outside C and let u=g^{-1}(v), also outside
C. Again D_f consists of C, {0,1,v}, and all {0,2,x},{1,2,x}. Put

    D=D_f intersection g^{-1}(D_f)
          intersection f^{-1}(D_f) intersection (fg)^{-1}(D_f).

The tests correspond to f,gf,ff,fgf, all of length at most three.
Every image reached within three letters therefore lies in D.

The following direct restrictions hold:

* C is in D only if c=u (test fgf);
* {0,1,v} is in D only if c=v (test ff);
* core pair 02 has at most external choice u (test gf); it further
  requires u=v or f(u)=u (test fgf);
* core pair 12 has at most external choices v and w=f^{-1}(u), where
  w is included only if it exists outside C (test fgf).

If c=u, w does not exist outside C, since u is then the kernel image.
If c!=u, C is absent. These restrictions give |D|<=4. Strict growth
forces equality and all four domain images to be reached within three
letters. Equality has only two possibilities:

1. c=u=v. Then D is {012,01v,02v,12v}.
2. c=v!=u and f(u)=u. Then D is {01v,02u,12v,12u}.

Every letter must send every image in D to a P3-covering image: each
was reached within three letters. In particular the letter assumptions
A and B1 are excluded by the pure arguments above.

Complete projection of every remaining compatible letter onto the first
domain gives 11 actions. Every domain image must eventually exit under
synchronization. Four finite exit distances are at most four, and a first
distance four requires a permutation of 1,2,3,4. All 24 vectors are checked:
none permits every vertex to exit. Thus the first exit distance is at
most three. Leaving D fails one of the defining tests of length at most
three; a further P3 word of length at most three compresses within nine.

For the second domain, the complete projection gives 38 actions. Of the
24 distance vectors, exactly three permit every vertex to exit:

    (2,3,4,1), (3,4,1,2), (4,3,1,2).

For each of these vectors every compatible letter satisfying its exit
inequalities maps the five-state set C union {v,u} into itself. This
is verified for every literal core-row template, not only for a selected
representative of each projected action. Every actual alphabet having
first exit distance four is included among those compatible actions.
Consequently C union {v,u} is invariant, contrary to strong connectivity
when n>=6. Otherwise first exit is at most three, again compressing within
nine. This is why the claim's state range is n>=6; the invariant set has
five states. No tight-compression-ten claim at n=5 is made here.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--case-c-a-six-image-domain"></a>
#### Case C: a six-image domain

Let v_1,v_2 be the distinct external preimages of 1,2. The domain D_f is
exactly the six holes formed by one core pair and one of v_1,v_2; C itself
is not in D_f. Every image reached within five letters lies in D_f, because
its f-image reached within six letters must cover P3. Strict growth gives
all six domain images by depth five. Every letter sends every domain
image to a P3-covering image.

The complete compatible projection gives 61 actions. Synchronization
requires finite exit distances for all six domain images; each is at most
six. A first distance six requires a permutation of 1,...,6. All 720
vectors are checked, and none permits every vertex to exit. The first
exit thus has length at most five. Appending f leaves the P3-covering
family and a word of length at most three then compresses. Total length
is at most 5+1+3=9, a contradiction.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--complete-finite-projections-and-independent-checks"></a>
#### Complete finite projections and independent checks

For any hole domain above, only the letter's images of the distinguished
states, and its missing output, matter. Permutations preserve C and are
bijections on the outside. Singular maps omitting 1 preserve C. Singular
maps omitting 0 with both core images inside C are also included. After
excluding A and B1, mixing possibilities B2 and C remain. The requirement
that every domain image still cover P3 forces every necessary external
preimage of 1 or 2 to be among the distinguished outside points. The code
enumerates its choice explicitly. All other represented external images
are distinct outside values; at most two fresh outside labels are needed.

triangle_reduced_actions.py enumerates these inverse/structural cases and
computes the projected holes. It scans all distance permutations, adds ALL
actions satisfying d(v)<=1+d(f(v)), d(EXIT)=0, and checks reverse exit
closure. Adding these actions cannot shorten the asserted lower distances.
For the three surviving B2 vectors it checks closure of the five-state
set for every underlying partial row.

audit_triangle_actions.cpp independently enumerates every forward partial
row on four or five represented states with five or seven output labels.
It tests all early inverse pairs literally, the separately proved A/B1
cuts, and the P3-covering image requirement. It checks exit by a forward
search from each vertex. All profiles, every profile's row-closure flag,
all distance vectors and all candidates coincide with the Python output.
The reports are triangle_reduced_actions.json,
triangle_actions_independent.json and codimension_three_upper_audit.json.

There is also an actual reachable, strongly connected synchronizing
five-state positive control with rows

    f=(3,3,2,1,4), g=(0,2,1,4,3), h=(1,0,2,3,4).

For S={2,4}, its first exit from the second four-image domain is four.
Ordinary forward BFS checks this and gives actual compression length NINE.
It is a positive control of the projected distance-four check, not a
compression-ten witness or a new exact maximum. This control prevents
mistaking projected exit distances for compression lengths.

<a id="problem4-triangle-early-exclusion--scope"></a>
#### Scope

<a id="problem4-triangle-mixing-case-a"></a>
<a id="problem4-triangle-mixing-case-a--necessary-exclusion-of-one-mixing-singular-letter-in-early-triangle-type"></a>
### Necessary exclusion of one mixing singular letter in early triangle type

Assume shortest compression length 10 for an (n-3)-subset of a
synchronizing automaton, with P1={01}, P2={01,02}, P3={01,02,12}.
Every letter is a permutation or has rank n-1 and kernel 01.

Let C={0,1,2}. The three-hole sets covering P3 are C itself and
{i,j,x}, with {i,j} contained in C and x outside C. Every image reached
within six letters must have one of these hole sets: otherwise it
contains a P3 pair, compressing within at most three more letters.

A singular letter has missing output 0 or 1. Indeed, if both 0 and 1
are present, their inverse pair is either disjoint from the kernel or
consists of two overlapping edges 0z,1z; neither is contained in
P2={01,02}. Its inverse pair of 01 is consequently empty. Since P2
contains the new pair 02, there is a permutation g with g^{-1}(01)=02.
The inverse pair of 02 is a different edge in P3, so g permutes C and
its complement. Also g(01) differs from 01.

Suppose a singular letter f omits 0, has f(0)=f(1)=c in {1,2}, and
has f(2) outside C. Let v be the unique preimage of {1,2} minus {c};
it lies outside C. Direct computation of the holes gives the domain

    D_f = {C, {0,2,v}, {1,2,v}}
          union {{0,1,x}: x outside C}

of P3-covering hole sets whose f-images also cover P3. Since g sends
01 to a different core pair, among the last family at most one member
has its g-image in D_f: its external point must be g^{-1}(v). The other
three members contribute at most three. Thus

    |D_f intersection g^{-1}(D_f)| <= 4.

Every image of the original subset reached within four letters lies
in this intersection. Its f- and gf-images must cover P3, since they
are reached within respectively five and six letters. But the family
of distinct images reachable within i letters grows strictly with i
until it contains a compressed image. A plateau would be a finite
family invariant under every letter, contradicting synchronization.
Thus at least five distinct images are reached within four letters,
contradicting the four-element intersection bound.

No such Case A singular letter exists in an automaton of the assumed
tight compression type. This exclusion uses synchronization, not strong
connectivity or reachability of the initial subset. It applies to every
n where the displayed assumptions hold and to any finite alphabet.
It is only one necessary exclusion, not a compression-nine theorem.

audit_triangle_mixing.py checks all Case A letters f and all required
permutations g in the literal complete n=6,7 pools using actual subset
images. It verifies the domain exactly and the intersection bound.
The other cases are proved in [Triangle early-pair obstruction at codimension three](#problem4-triangle-early-exclusion).

<a id="problem4-two-cover-p3-classification"></a>
<a id="problem4-two-cover-p3-classification--p3-graphs-under-a-two-state-p5-cover"></a>
### P3 graphs under a two-state P5 cover

Let n>=4 and let a complete synchronizing automaton have a two-state
set K covering P5. Then, after removing isolated vertices, P3 is
exactly a triangle, a four-vertex path, or two disjoint edges. This
necessary condition holds for arbitrary finite alphabets; it does not
require SC or initial-image reachability, and determines no F value.

First P3 has no vertex cover of size one. A synchronizing automaton
has a nonpermutational letter, hence an edge e of P1. If {k} covered
P3, the graph consisting only of e has precisely two independent
(n-1)-sets. Apply [Finite independent-image trap](#problem4-finite-independent-image-trap) with h=1, N=2
and R=Q-{k}, of size at least two. This forbids synchronization.
The zero-cover case is included since P1 is nonempty. This also
recovers the familiar one-cover compression floor; no priority claim
is made for it.

Thus the minimum vertex cover of G=P3 has size exactly two. Its
independent n-2-sets are complements of its two-state vertex covers.
Let N be their number. If N<=2, the finite-image trap with h=3 uses
only a cover of P_(3+N), which is supplied by the P5 cover K, and
again forbids synchronization. Hence G has at least three two-state
vertex covers.

Here is the complete elementary graph classification. If G has two
disjoint edges ab and cd, every two-state vertex cover chooses one
endpoint from each, giving four candidates. An additional edge with
an endpoint outside {a,b,c,d} removes at least two candidates (or all
four if both endpoints are outside). A crossing edge within those
four vertices removes exactly one candidate. The four possible
crossing edges remove different candidates. With at least three
covers, there is therefore no outside edge and at most one crossing
edge. G is exactly two disjoint edges or a four-vertex path, plus
isolated vertices.

If G has no two disjoint edges, all edges intersect pairwise. A
common incident vertex would give a one-state cover. Otherwise take
ab,ac and an edge not incident to a; that edge must be bc. An edge
intersecting all three triangle edges is itself a triangle edge.
Thus G is a triangle plus isolated vertices. This exhausts the cases.

Consequently all pairs merged within three have endpoints among at
most four active states. The three admitted shapes have three, three
and four independent n-2-sets, respectively. Admission does not assert
that every shape is realized under every additional flag constraint.

For the current singleton-C roots, residual K12 already covers P5,
so the criterion applies. In D15/E26, the supplied disjoint pairs15
and26 belong to P2. P3 must therefore be exactly those two edges,
or those edges plus one crossing edge. No third-depth pair involving
another state is possible. This is a next-step necessary restriction;
it does not exclude E26 or either whole D15 type. The broader
three-cover branches do not inherit this two-cover classification.

The checker exhausts every graph covered by a fixed labelled pair
through n9, an exact relabelling cover for all two-cover graphs at
those sizes. It uses literal cover sets and a separate degree-based
shape test. Complete n4 binary automata supply additional semantic
controls, using forward pair and subset searches. The uniform proof,
not finite enumeration or solver failures, establishes the result.

<a id="problem4-two-cover-protected-kernel-obstruction"></a>
<a id="problem4-two-cover-protected-kernel-obstruction--two-cover-obstruction-for-a-one-count-immediate-kernel"></a>
### Two-cover obstruction for a one-count immediate kernel

Use P_h for distinct pairs merged within h letters. For a letter f,
write f^*(G) for pairs with distinct f-images forming an edge of G.
Thus P_(h+1)=P1 union all f^*(P_h). Immediate collisions are included
in P1, not in f^*(G). This distinction is retained below.

<a id="problem4-two-cover-protected-kernel-obstruction--no-matching-in-p2"></a>
#### No matching in P2

In a synchronizing automaton on n>=4 states, let a two-state K cover
P5. The credited unique-immediate-pair consequence gives P1={e}, and
every letter is a permutation or a rank-n-1 map with sole kernel e.
The established P3 classification admits triangle, path4 or matching2.

Suppose P2 contains an edge d disjoint from e. P3 then is the matching
G={e,d} plus at most one crossing edge. If P2 contained that crossing,
its three-edge path would have three independent (n-2)-sets. The
finite-independent-image trap at h=2,N=3 and the P5 cover would
contradict synchronization. Hence P2=G.

For a permutation f, f^*({e}) is an edge of P2, and f^*({d}) is disjoint
from it. The only disjoint partner in P3 is the other matching edge;
a crossing edge intersects both matching edges. Thus f^*(G)=G.
