For a singular f, put t=f(e). A G edge incident to t with its other
endpoint available would lift to two edges joining the two e endpoints
to the same third input. P3 has at most one crossing edge, so this
is impossible. Such an edge has no lift. Every other lifted G edge
has inputs outside e; the only possible such P3 edge is d. Therefore
f^*(G) is contained in G for every letter. P3=P2=G stabilizes forever,
contradicting synchronization. No P2 edge can be disjoint from e.
In particular P3 cannot be matching2: P2=e alone would already be a
plateau. P3 is a triangle or a four-vertex path. This argument needs
neither strong connectivity nor initial-image reachability.

<a id="problem4-two-cover-protected-kernel-obstruction--obstruction-with-a-one-count-kernel"></a>
#### Obstruction with a one-count kernel

Let a strongly connected synchronizing automaton have a subset S of
size s>=2, put m=n-s, and suppose:

1. a two-state K covers P5;
2. c(S)>=m+8, where c(S) is its shortest compression length;
3. a two-state E satisfies |Sw intersection E|=1 for all |w|<=m+1;
4. some letter T sends both E states to the same state outside E.

These four conditions are inconsistent. The alphabet is arbitrary
finite; no reachability assumption on S is needed.

Condition4 and unique P1 give E=e. For every letter f, every Sw with
|w|<=m meets the vertex fiber f^(-1)(e) once: the appended image has
one e point and no collision, since m+1<c(S). If this fiber is a
singleton {p}, then p belongs to every image through m. The proved
mandatory-core lemma makes p isolated in P7, because
c(S)-m-1>=7. Only this conservative threshold is asserted here.

For T, the sole double output t is outside e. If both e endpoints
were available outputs, their two distinct preimages would form a P2
edge disjoint from e, impossible by the first part. T therefore omits
one endpoint x of e. The other endpoint y has a single preimage p,
which is P7-isolated. Every output except x is available. An edge
{y,q} in P6 with q!=x would lift under T to a P7 pair incident to p,
impossible. Thus y has no P6 neighbor except x.

Consequently P3 is a path y--x--z--v, with e={x,y} its end edge;
the triangle would give y two neighbors. P2 cannot equal e alone,
and cannot contain the disjoint edge {z,v}. Hence
P2={{x,y},{x,z}} exactly. Both K states are among these four active
vertices: one active point cannot cover the path.

No singular letter can generate the third edge {z,v} from P2.
To see this let f(e)=t. If t is an e endpoint and the other e endpoint
is available, lifting e produces an edge joining y to an input outside
e, which is not in P2. Hence the other endpoint must be omitted.
If t=x (so y is omitted), lifting {x,z} similarly gives a forbidden
P3 neighbor of y. If t=y and x is omitted, both P2 edges have an
omitted endpoint, so their lifts are empty.
If t is outside e, both e endpoints available would give a disjoint
P2 edge. Thus one endpoint is omitted and the other's preimage is
a mandatory singleton p, isolated in P7. Omitting x kills both P2
lifts. Omitting y leaves x,z available, so lifting {x,z} creates a
P3 pair incident to p, again impossible. This exhausts singular f.

Since P3 contains {z,v}, some permutation f must generate it. Its
e lift belongs to P2; a lift of {x,z} equal to {z,v} forces
f(z)=x, f(x)=y, f(v)=z. Put w=f^(-1)(v); it differs from x,z,v.
The edge {v,w}=f^*({z,v}) belongs to P4. If w=y, it violates y's
P6 isolation from every point except x. Otherwise w is outside the
four active vertices, hence outside K. P4 coverage gives v in K.
Put u=f^(-1)(w). The edge {w,u} belongs to P5, so u is in K.
But x,z,v map to active vertices and w is outside, so u is none of
x,z,v. Since K is active, u=y. The P5 edge {w,y} again violates
the sole-neighbor property of y. This contradiction proves the claim.

<a id="problem4-two-cover-protected-kernel-obstruction--current-application-and-limits"></a>
#### Current application and limits

For(13,9,1), equality12 implies c(S)>=12=m+8 with m=4. First,
second and third entrance pair fibers are one-count through depths
10,9,8, respectively, and fourth pair fibers through7. When the
preceding target is a singleton outside that pair, its supplier
satisfies condition4. The explicit two-state P5 cover is required;
three-cover branches never inherit this obstruction automatically.

The graph checker exhausts every permutation and every rank-n-1 map
with a fixed kernel on n4..6. It independently checks matching
stabilization, singular path lifts and permutation path growth, with
an omitted mandatory-singleton boundary retained. These are exact
graph controls supporting the uniform written proof, not a search
over all thirteen-state automata or a new numerical F maximum.

<a id="problem4-two-cover-third-unique-kernel-cuts"></a>
<a id="problem4-two-cover-third-unique-kernel-cuts--unique-kernel-restrictions-on-third-entrance-fields"></a>
### Unique-kernel restrictions on third entrance fields

At (13,9,1), equality12, the established third inventory contains
every possible exact preA/preB/preC field for its B,C,D geometry,
including every covered Boolean companion. Its literal nine-set
family contains every actual image through depth eight. Reconstruct
its mandatory intersection J and put K={0,1,2} minus J. Only records
with |K|=2 use this note. Mandatory-core isolation makes J isolated
in P7, so K still covers P5. Synchronization and the credited
unique-immediate-pair consequence imply one global kernel pair e,
meeting K and avoiding J; every letter has rank at least12.

For an exact field, partition inputs by their memberships in its
three preimage sets and outputs by memberships in A,B,C. Any input
atom must map into its corresponding output atom. Hence the rank
is at most the sum, over atoms, of min(input size,output size).
Every pair in an input atom with singleton output is an immediate
kernel. Both quantities are literally reconstructed by the checker,
including overlapping B,C and empty atoms.

Discard a field if this rank upper bound is below12. For a proposed
global e, retain only fields whose forced immediate pairs lie in
{e}. This is deliberately a necessary overapproximation: no claim
is made that every retained field realizes exactly e or synchronizes.
Every equality automaton must lie in one retained e class, and that
class must contain suppliers preA=B, preB=C, preC=D. If no e class
has all three suppliers, the whole geometry is impossible for every
finite alphabet. Suppliers may be the same or different letters.
Covered companion fibers are retained; no common-D shortcut occurs.

For a formal binary pair, either letter's rank bound below12 or two
distinct forced kernels in their union rules out that pair. Already
removed profiles are accounted for separately by the frontier
recorder. When all currently remaining pairs of a type fail, that
binary type is removed. An arbitrary-alphabet cut always uses the
supplier test above, never failure of the binary pair table.

The finite table is an exact conditional classification, not a
thirteen-state automaton scan or a sampled-negative theorem. The
underlying unique-kernel statement is uniform and previously audited.
No result for a three-state cover is inferred. These restrictions
alone do not determine F(13,9,1), an all-parameter formula or alphabet
separation. The checker emits cuts for the intact historical inventory;
the checkpoint recorder computes only newly removed current entries.

<a id="problem4-two-cover-unique-immediate-pair"></a>
<a id="problem4-two-cover-unique-immediate-pair--unique-immediate-pair-under-a-two-state-p5-cover"></a>
### Unique immediate pair under a two-state P5 cover

For n>=4, if a complete synchronizing automaton has a two-state set K
covering P5, P1 consists of exactly one pair. The alphabet is any finite
alphabet. This is a direct consequence of the known compression
refinement, not a new compression theorem or F value. SC and initial
image reachability are unnecessary.

Let R=Q-K, |R|=n-2>=2. The cover says no word of length at most five
compresses R. Synchronization makes R compressible. If two distinct
immediate pairs e1,e2 existed, their synchronizing height would be one,
and they admit an (n-2)-subset Frankl-Pin sequence of length two.
Choose an endpoint x of e2 outside e1 and another y outside e1 with
y!=x; n>=4 ensures the latter exists. Set T1=Q-{x,y}, which contains
e1 and omits an endpoint of e2. Choose any (n-2)-set T2 containing e2.
The two sets/pairs satisfy the sequence conditions.

Kisielewicz, Kowalski and Szykula, Experiments with Synchronizing
Automata, CIAA2016, Theorem1 (PDF p3) gives for every compressible
t-set the upper bound binomial(n-t+2,2)-p(P)+h(P). At t=n-2,
p(P)>=2 and h(P)=1, this is at most6-2+1=5, contradicting the cover.
The source theorem requires compressibility, not SC. P1 is nonempty
because synchronization at n>=2 needs a singular letter, so it has
exactly one edge.

Primary source checked again on10October2026:
https://kot.rogacz.com/Publications/Kisielewicz2016ExperimentsWith.pdf
The relevant theorem and sequence argument already appear in
[The binary sharpness requirement at (11,8,1)](#problem4-binary-obstruction-proof); this note only applies them to an
auxiliary (n-2)-set. No priority claim is made for the refinement or
this immediate consequence. It constrains automata, not just letters
in a binary alphabet, and does not assert a numerical F maximum.

The n>=4 condition matters: at n3, Q-K is a singleton and need not
compress, even when the automaton synchronizes. Checks retain this
boundary. Every singular letter now has rank n-1 and the same sole
kernel pair; any larger kernel would give multiple immediate pairs.

Complete n4 binary controls independently verify the refinement on
every compressible pair, including nonsynchronizing automata, and
the unique-edge consequence in the fixed-cover synchronizing cases.
All ordered distinct-pair two-step sequences are literally checked
through n13. These controls support the cited theorem/application;
they are not a new theorem proved by finite sampling.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--disjoint-tail-early-type-4-exclusion-at-codimension-three"></a>
### Disjoint-tail early-type-4 exclusion at codimension three

**当前证明依赖。** 本节的符号分类及测试域推导仍使用；后面的有限动作/距离排除
现由[纸面替代引理](#problem4-paper-dependency-reductions)代替，保留的枚举描述为历史独立控制。

**Claim.** For n>=5, a synchronizing automaton cannot have an (n-3)-set
of shortest compression length ten with

    P1={01}, P2={01,02}, P3={01,02,34}.

No alphabet-size, strong-connectivity or image-reachability hypothesis is
needed for this exclusion. [Necessary short-pair structure for tight compression](#problem4-short-pair-structure) gives the credited
short-pair refinement. Write C={0,1,2,3,4} and G={3,4}. The three-hole
sets covering P3 form H: the seven core holes

    013,014,023,024,034,123,124

and 03x,04x for x outside C. Every image reached within six letters must
have holes in H. The distinct images reached within i letters grow
strictly until compression, giving |R_i|>=i+1 for i<=9. Equality at a
step would make all reached uncompressed images invariant under every
letter, contrary to the existence of a reset word.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--all-compatible-letters"></a>
#### All compatible letters

Every letter is a permutation or a rank-(n-1) transformation with common
kernel 01. Inverse pairs of 01 belong to P2 and inverse pairs of 02
belong to P3. Permutations have core prefix A=(0,1,2) or B=(0,2,1);
they fix 0 and preserve the pair 12. An inverse pair 34 of 02 cannot
occur in a permutation: its inverse pair of 01 is 01 or 02 and would
be disjoint from 34, whereas the target pairs intersect at 0.

A singular letter omits 0 or 1, by the inverse-pair 01 test. If it
omits 1, its kernel image cannot be 0 or 2: that would produce both
0x and 1x as inverse pairs of 02, incompatible with P3. Its unique
inverse pair of 02 must therefore be 34. It has one of the core rows

    (c,c,t,0,2), (c,c,t,2,0),  c,t>=3, c!=t.

A singular letter omitting 0 has unrestricted distinct nonzero images
on the common kernel and the other core states. Some missing-1 letter
is necessary, because only such a letter can add the new pair 34 to
P3. Call it d. Swapping 3 and 4 if needed, write d=(c,c,t,0,2) on C.
This relabeling preserves the whole early-pair type.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--the-domain-of-d-has-six-images"></a>
#### The domain of d has six images

Let D be the holes in H whose d-images also have holes in H. The hole
034 always has d-image holes 012, so is absent. Core holes 013,014
survive exactly when c is in G; holes 023,024,123,124 survive exactly
when t is in G. An outside 03x or 04x survives exactly when dx is in
G. Among the two outputs in G, every one not occupied by c or t has
one outside preimage. Thus, writing a=[c in G], b=[t in G],

    |D|=2a+4b+2(2-a-b)=4+2b.

This exact count also follows by direct complement-of-image substitution.
For example, 013 has holes {1,c,0}, 014 has {1,c,2}; 023 and 123
have {1,t,0}, 024 and 124 have {1,t,2}; outside holes have {1,0,dx}
or {1,2,dx}. In each case the remaining condition is to meet G.

All images reached within five letters belong to D; hence |D|>=6.
We must have t in G and |D|=6, so every D-image is reached within five
letters. In particular EVERY letter sends EVERY D-image to an H-image,
because the resulting depth is at most six.

There are exactly two domain shapes:

* c in G: c,t are the two members of G and
  D_closed={013,014,023,024,123,124};
* c outside C: let v be the unique outside preimage under d of the
  other member of G. Then
  D_mixing={023,024,123,124,03v,04v}.

The second shape requires n>=6. The first is already meaningful at n=5.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--complete-finite-projections"></a>
#### Complete finite projections

For each domain project every compatible letter to its six successor
indices, with EXIT=-1 for an H-image outside the domain. These are
projections of actual subset images: for a permutation f the new holes
are f(H); for a singular common-kernel letter with missing output e they
are {e} union f(H) when H contains both 0 and 1, and {e} union
f(H minus {0,1}) otherwise. Each new hole set has cardinality three.

The projections are complete for every n by the following bounded
description of all relevant partial rows.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--closed-domain-five-represented-input-states"></a>
##### Closed domain: five represented input states

Use output labels 0,...,6. A permutation has prefix A or B and injective
images on states 3,4. The requirement on holes 013 and 014 actually
forces both these images to belong to G. For a missing-1 singular row,
the same domain requirements force c and t into G, so its whole core
row preserves C. For a missing-0 row write it (c,c,t,u,z) on C, where
c,t,u,z are distinct and nonzero. The six hole tests require G to meet
each of {c,u},{c,z},{t,u},{t,z}. Since these four outputs are distinct,
both members of G must occur. At most two fresh outside labels are
needed. Thus labels 0,...,6 include every relevant partial row, including
ones not extendible at the smallest n; extra rows only enlarge the
candidate set and do not weaken a negative proof.

Complete enumeration yields 33 profiles on D_closed.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--mixing-domain-six-represented-input-states"></a>
##### Mixing domain: six represented input states

Relabel v=5 and use output labels 0,...,8. Core holes 023 and 024 force
every compatible permutation to preserve G, so its row has prefix A/B,
a permutation of 3,4, and an arbitrary outside image of state 5.

For a missing-1 row, those same holes force its image of state 2 into
G. Holes 035,045 then force its image of state 5 to be the other member
of G. Its kernel image is therefore outside C. These give all missing-1
partial rows (c,c,t,0,2,x) or (c,c,t,2,0,x), where c>=5 and {t,x}=G.

For a missing-0 row write (c,c,t,u,z,x), with five distinct nonzero
outputs. The hole conditions require G to meet each of {t,u},{t,z},
{u,x},{z,x}. Thus both members of G occur among t,u,z,x, and at most
three fresh outside output labels remain among the five distinct outputs.
The nine labels 0,...,8 therefore cover every relevant partial row.

Complete enumeration yields 37 profiles on D_mixing.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--exit-distances-and-contradiction"></a>
#### Exit distances and contradiction

Synchronization forces every domain vertex eventually to exit: otherwise
a reset word could not reduce its image cardinality. Every finite shortest
exit distance in a six-vertex graph is at most six. If the initial vertex
had distance six, a shortest exit path would use all vertices with distinct
distances 1,...,6. For each of their 720 permutations d, include all
profiles p satisfying

    d(i)<=1+d(p(i)), d(EXIT)=0,

and test whether every vertex can exit. These enlarged profile graphs
contain every actual alphabet having those exit distances. In BOTH domains,
every one of the 720 vectors fails the test. Hence the first exit takes
at most five letters. Leaving D fails its defining d test; appending d
and then a P3 merging word of length at most three compresses the original
set within 5+1+3=9, contradicting the assumed compression ten.

<a id="problem4-type4-early-exclusion--independent-verification-and-reproduction"></a>
#### Independent verification and reproduction

type4_reduced_actions.py uses the structural row templates above and
reverse exit closure. audit_type4_actions.cpp independently enumerates
literal forward partial rows, checks the early inverse pairs directly,
and searches forward from each domain vertex. It does not use the Python
templates or reports. Every profile, every underlying-row closure flag,
all 720 vectors and both zero-candidate results agree. The Python exit
checker also accepts an artificial six-vertex chain as a positive control.

audit_type4_domains.py independently computes ordinary subset images for
every compatible missing-1 letter from the complete n6/n7 letter pools.
It verifies the exact 4+2b count, both domain shapes and the complete
letter classification. These finite controls support the symbolic count;
the parameter range is not extrapolated from them.

From the supplementary directory, using standard-library Python >=3.10
and a C++17 compiler:

    python -B type4_reduced_actions.py
    clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 audit_type4_actions.cpp -o type4_audit
    ./type4_audit type4_actions_independent.json
    python -B audit_type4_domains.py

Use .exe names on Windows and keep assertions enabled. The finite pool
files are generated by early_pair_alphabet_pool.py. The native audit
also passed -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer
with an identical report. The data are type4_reduced_actions.json,
type4_actions_independent.json and type4_domain_audit.json. They are included in the proof supplement.

<a id="problem4-type5-early-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-type5-early-exclusion--crossing-early-type-5-exclusion"></a>
### Crossing early-type-5 exclusion

This is one elementary case of [Uniform codimension-three compression bound](#problem4-codimension-three-upper-proof).

**Claim.** No automaton can have exactly

    P1={01}, P2={01,23}, P3={01,23,02},

where P_h denotes the unordered distinct-state pairs merging in at most
h letters. No strong-connectivity, synchronization, alphabet-size or
reachable-image assumption is needed. The labels require n>=4.

The single pair in P1 forces each letter to be a permutation or a
rank-(n-1) map with common kernel 01. Pair 02 is new at level three,
so some letter f must send it to a distinct pair in P2. It cannot send
it to 01, since that would put 02 in P2. Thus 02f=23 is necessary.

If f is a permutation, its inverse pair of 01 is either 01 or 23 by
the definition of P2. Its inverse pair of 23 would have to be 02.
Inverse pairs of the disjoint target pairs 01 and 23 must be disjoint,
but 02 intersects BOTH possible inverse pairs of 01. This is impossible.

If f is singular, its common kernel is 01. For 02f=23, f0 is an
endpoint of 23 and f2 the other endpoint. Since f1=f0, also 12f=23.
This would put the additional pair 12 in P3, contradicting the three
specified pairs. The two cases exhaust every letter and prove the claim.

check_type5_exclusion.py supplies a literal finite control: every
compatible transformation in the complete n6/n7 pools is checked
against both 02 and 12 and against inverse pairs of 23. The proof
above is independent of those finite sizes, and no extrapolation or
solver-unsatisfiability output is used.

<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion--kernel-tail-early-type-6-exclusion-at-codimension-three"></a>
### Kernel-tail early-type-6 exclusion at codimension three

**当前证明依赖。** 本节的符号分类及测试域推导仍使用；后面的有限动作/距离排除
现由[纸面替代引理](#problem4-paper-dependency-reductions)代替，保留的枚举描述为历史独立控制。

**Claim.** For n>=6, a strongly connected synchronizing automaton cannot
have an (n-3)-set of shortest compression length ten with

    P1={01}, P2={01,23}, P3={01,23,04}.

The alphabet is arbitrary finite and the set need not be reachable.
The credited short-pair refinement is in [Necessary short-pair structure for tight compression](#problem4-short-pair-structure).
Let C={0,1,2,3,4}. The three-hole P3 covers form H: core holes
012,013,023,024,034,124,134 and outside holes 02x,03x, x outside C.
Every image reached within six letters has holes in H. The distinct
images grow strictly until compression (a plateau would be invariant
under all letters and contradict synchronization), hence |R_i|>=i+1
for i<=9. Tests of maximum length L have a common H-preserving domain
containing R_(6-L). If a word leaves that domain, a failed test and a
P3 word compress in at most L+3 additional letters.

<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion--complete-letter-classification"></a>
#### Complete letter classification

Each letter is a permutation or a rank-(n-1) map with common kernel 01.
Its inverse pairs of 01 belong to {01,23}, and inverse pairs of 23
belong to {01,23,04}. Permutations have precisely three forms:

* A: preserve each pair 01,23;
* B: exchange those two pairs;
* T: map 23 onto 01 and 04 onto 23, with the image of state 1 outside
  {0,1,2,3}.

The first two have core images in {0,1,2,3} and arbitrary outside images.
In T the four images of 0,2,3,4 are all of {0,1,2,3}.

A singular letter cannot have its kernel image in a target pair whose
inverse pairs are required: that would give both 0x and 1x, which
cannot both lie in either allowed early-pair family. If its missing
output is outside 01, it must map 23 onto 01. Its missing output must
then be 2 or 3, since otherwise its inverse pair of 23 could be none
of the permitted pairs. If it omits 0 or 1, it must map 23 onto 23.
Thus all singular letters have one of these forms:

* U: missing e in {0,1}, map 23 onto 23, kernel image c in
  {1-e} union {4,5,...};
* V: missing e in {2,3}, map 23 onto 01, kernel image c in
  {5-e} union {4,5,...}.

Their images of other states are distinct and omit e and c. Only T
can create the new pair 04, so some T permutation is necessary. Swapping
labels 2 and 3, the chosen T has one of the normalized core rows

    I:  (2,a,0,1,3),   II: (2,a,1,0,3),   a>=4.

Call it closed when a=4 and mixing otherwise. The swap fixes 0,1,4
and preserves the ordered early-pair type.

<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion--orientation-ii"></a>
#### Orientation II

If a>=5, put v=T^-1(4). The common domain for T and TT is exactly

    a=v:  {013,034,134};
    a!=v: {034,134,03w},  w=T^-1(v) outside C.

For example the one-step domain is 013,023,034,134,02v and all outside
03x. The second test removes 023 and 02v; it retains 013 only if a=v,
and an outside 03x only if Tx=v. Since T1=a, exactly one of these
last possibilities exists. The domain has size three, fewer than
|R4|>=5, so mixing orientation II is impossible.

If a=4, the T,TT domain is precisely the five core holes

    D={012,023,034,124,134}.

All five images are reached by depth four, so every letter sends every
one of them to H. Complete projection to these five vertices and EXIT
gives 19 profiles. For every permutation d of 1,...,5, include all
profiles p with d(i)<=1+d(p(i)), d(EXIT)=0, then test whether every
vertex can exit. Exactly one of the 120 vectors survives: (2,3,4,1,5).
Its allowed profiles, in the displayed domain order, are

    (0,1,2,3,4), (3,0,1,4,2), (0,1,2,-1,2).

EVERY underlying partial row of these profiles maps C into itself.
If the initial vertex had exit distance five, its finite distances
would have to be such a permutation and hence C would be invariant.
This contradicts strong connectivity for n>=6. Otherwise first exit
has length at most four and compression follows within 4+2+3=9.

The finite projection covers every state count: A,B have four core
outputs in {0,1,2,3} and one additional output, T likewise has four
specified core outputs and one additional output. A U or V row has
two specified outputs on 23 and two other distinct outputs (kernel
image and image of state 4). At most two fresh outside labels are
needed, so output labels 0,...,6 cover all five-state partial rows.
The complete structural enumeration is type6_closed_II_actions.py;
audit_type6_closed_II.cpp independently generates literal forward rows,
checks inverse pairs, and searches forward from every domain vertex.
Every profile and underlying-row closure flag agrees.

There is a boundary control at n=5 with rows

    (1,1,2,3,4), (2,4,1,0,3), S={0,2}.

It is strongly connected and synchronizing, has reaching word abbbababbb
and reset word abbbabbbabbba. Ordinary BFS gives projected exit FIVE
and actual compression NINE. This is a positive projected-distance
control, not a compression-ten witness. No assertion excluding all
type-6 tightness at n=5 is made here.

<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion--orientation-i-requires-a-breaker"></a>
#### Orientation I requires a breaker

Let T=(2,a,0,1,3) on C, put v=T^-1(4), and sigma=[a=v]. The domain
for T,TT is exactly

    closed: {012,013,023,024,134} union {02x: x outside C};
    mixing: {012,023,024,03v} union {02x: x outside C},
            with 124 added only when sigma=1.

In the closed case v=1. In the mixing case v is outside C. These
identities follow by applying T to each of the seven core holes and
to 02x,03x separately; the one-step mixing domain is
{012,023,024,124,03v} union {02x: x outside C}.

For a permutation g, call it a keeper when {g0,g2}={0,2}. For a
singular g with missing output e, call it a keeper when {e,g2}={0,2}.
If every letter were a keeper, the family of holes 02x for all
x!=0,2 (including x=1,3,4) would be invariant. For singular letters,
the hole 012 maps to 02c, and every other 02x maps to 02gx; each is
again three distinct holes. Thus these (n-3)-images could never
compress, contradicting synchronization. There is a breaker g.

All orientation-II letters have already been excluded, so the complete
breaker list is as follows. Below h denotes g4, except in the T row
where h=g1; each free output obeys the rank and missing-output rules.

| Name | Core row or conditions |
| --- | --- |
| A03 | (0,1,3,2,h) |
| B03 | (3,2,0,1,h) |
| A_bad | (1,0,k,l,h), {k,l}={2,3} |
| B_bad | (k,l,1,0,h), {k,l}={2,3} |
| T_other | (3,h,1,0,2), h>=4 |
| U03 | (c,c,3,2,h), missing 0 |
| V03 | (c,c,0,1,h), missing 3 |
| U_bad | U missing 1 |
| V_bad | V with g2=1, g3=0 |

This is exhaustive from the A,B,T,U,V classification by checking whether
the carrier of the holes 02x is 02,03,12 or 13. Carrier 02 is precisely
the keeper case. It is important that carrier 12 or 13 also covers P3
when its third point is 0, as well as when it is 4; that boundary is
retained in the counts below.

<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion--uniform-two-step-counting-ledger"></a>
#### Uniform two-step counting ledger

Let D(T,g) be the H-domain of ALL words of length at most two on T,g.
Its core holes are among the displayed T,TT core holes. Its outside
holes are only 02x and, in the mixing case, at most the single 03v.
Write C_i=[c=i], H_i=[h=i]. Each triple in the tables bounds

    (number of core holes, number of outside 02x, number of outside 03x).

The closed-I ledger is:

| Breaker | Component bounds |
| --- | --- |
| A03 | (4,0,0) |
| B03 | (3,0,0) |
| A_bad, B_bad | (3+H4,1-H4,0) |
| T_other | (2+H4,1-H4,0) |
| U03 | (3+C1+H1,1-C1-H1,0) |
| V03 | (1+C2+H2+H4,1-C2-H2,0) |
| U_bad | (2C+2H,2-C-H,0), C=C0+C4, H=H0+H4 |
| V_bad | (3+C4+H4,1-C4-H4,0) |

Every sum is at most four. For U_bad, c,h are distinct so C,H are
each indicators, giving sum 2+C+H<=4. Negative-looking terms are
nonnegative under the distinct-output conditions.

The mixing-I ledger is:

| Breaker | Component bounds |
| --- | --- |
| A03 | (1+Hv+sigma H4,1-Hv,H4) |
| B03 | (1+Hv+sigma,1-Hv,0) |
| A_bad | (1+H4+sigma(1-H4),1-H4,1-H4) |
| B_bad | (1+H4(1+sigma),1-H4,H4) |
| T_other | (sigma H4,1-H4,H4) |
| U03 | (1+Cv+Hv(1+sigma),1-Cv-Hv,1) |
| V03 | (C+H(1+sigma),2-C-H,0), C=C2+Cv, H=H2+Hv |
| U_bad | (C+H(1+sigma),2-C-H,1), C=C0+C4, H=H0+H4 |
| V_bad | (1+C4+H4(1+sigma),1-C4-H4,H4) |

Here v>=5, so the indicator sums in the V03 row are again indicators.
Every row sums to at most four (some have the smaller upper three).

To verify the ledger algebraically, apply the hole formula given below
to the core holes and the two outside types. The restrictions on outside
02x reduce to unique preimages of these target sets:

* permutation bad rows: {4};
* U03: {v}, with v=1 in the closed case;
* V03: {2,v}, with target 1 already having core preimage 3 when closed;
* U_bad: {0,4};
* V_bad: {4}, since output 0 already has core preimage 3.

Every target occupied by kernel image c or core image h has no outside
preimage. This gives all the negative terms in the second column.
For permutation A03/B03 the targets of gT on 02x are {2,v}, but
output 2 already has a core preimage, leaving only v; when closed,
output v=1 also has a core preimage, leaving none.

Core counts are obtained by substituting the five/four candidate core
holes of T,TT into g,gT,Tg,gg. For illustration, U03 has three possible
unconditional closed core holes 013,023,134 and the two extra holes
012,024 only if c=1,h=1. In the mixing case it has unconditional 023,
012 only if c=v, and 024 (also 124 if sigma=1) only if h=v.

For V03 the closed hole 013 cannot survive: its first image would
require c=4 and be 134, but its second image then requires h=4,
contradicting distinct outputs. The remaining core candidates are
023,012 if c=2, 024 if h=2 and 134 if h=4. In the mixing case 023
fails gT, and 03v also fails gT: its possible first images 013 or
134 both fail T. The displayed C,H restrictions on 012,024,124
then give its table row. The bad U core counts simply test whether
c,h belong to {0,4}; the bad V rows have three unconditional possible
closed core holes, with 012/024 requiring c=4,h=4. In the mixing
bad V case only 023 is unconditional, 012 requires c=4, and 024,
the optional 124 and 03v require h=4. The permutation rows follow
from their explicit core templates in exactly the same substitution.

The hole formula is: a permutation sends holes J to g(J); a singular
common-kernel letter missing e sends J to {e} union g(J) if J contains
both 0,1, and to {e} union g(J minus {0,1}) otherwise. In particular
it correctly includes the kernel image when BOTH kernel points are
holes. This proves the entire finite ledger for arbitrary n, without
extrapolation from numerical instances.

It follows that |D(T,g)|<=4. But every image reached within four
letters belongs to it, whereas |R4|>=5. This contradiction excludes
orientation I and completes the claim.

<a id="problem4-type6-early-exclusion--independent-controls-and-reproduction"></a>
#### Independent controls and reproduction

audit_type6_domains.py uses ordinary subset images for every compatible
letter in the n6/n7 pools, checks the exact orientation domains, every
component of every ledger row, the keeper invariant family, the closed-II
profile comparison and the literal five-state control.

audit_type6_breakers.cpp independently generates all complete permutations
and common-kernel singular rows without reading those pools or the ledger.
It applies literal subsets and checks the two-step bound for all breakers.
The n6/n7 counts agree with Python: 100 and 1116 breaker pairs. At n9,
with four outside states, it enumerates all 7199 nonidentity compatible
letters, 120 normalized I permutations, 619200 breaker pairs and 215880
keeper pairs. All breaker domains have size at most four. Identity is
omitted from these pools only because it is always a keeper; it is included
in the structural profile enumeration. These are finite adversarial
controls of the symbolic ledger, not an extrapolated universal bound.

From the supplementary directory, using standard-library Python >=3.10
and a C++17 compiler with assertions enabled:

    python -B type6_closed_II_actions.py
    clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 audit_type6_closed_II.cpp -o type6_II
    ./type6_II type6_closed_II_independent.json
    clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 audit_type6_breakers.cpp -o type6_breakers
    ./type6_breakers type6_breaker_independent.json
    python -B audit_type6_domains.py

Use .exe on Windows. Both native audits also passed clang++ ASan/UBSan
builds with identical reports. The domain checker imports ordinary BFS
utilities from verify_certificates.py and uses the existing n6/n7 pools.
The standalone breaker audit has no such dependency.

This completes type 6 in [Uniform codimension-three compression bound](#problem4-codimension-three-upper-proof).

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion"></a>
<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--second-pair-tail-early-type-7-exclusion-at-codimension-three"></a>
### Second-pair-tail early-type-7 exclusion at codimension three

**当前证明依赖。** 本节的符号分类及测试域推导仍使用；后面的有限动作/距离排除
现由[纸面替代引理](#problem4-paper-dependency-reductions)代替，保留的枚举描述为历史独立控制。

**Claim.** For n>=6, no strongly connected synchronizing automaton has an
(n-3)-set whose shortest compression length is ten and whose early pairs are

    P1={01}, P2={01,23}, P3={01,23,24}.

The alphabet is arbitrary finite; reachability of the set is unnecessary.
This claim alone is one case of the complete nine-type exclusion, rather
than an asserted all-parameter avoid-or-compress formula.

Put C={0,1,2,3,4}. The three-hole covers H of P3 are the seven core holes
012,023,024,123,124,034,134 and outside holes 02x,12x, x outside C.
Every image reached in at most six letters has holes in H: otherwise a
pair in P3 is still in the image and a word of length at most three
compresses it before ten. The reached images R_i grow strictly until
compression, since a plateau is invariant under every letter and
contradicts synchronization. Thus |R_i|>=i+1 for i<=9.

For tests of maximum length L, their common domain of holes that stay in
H contains R_(6-L), and consequently has at least 7-L members. Upon
leaving this domain, one failed test followed by a merging word of length
at most three gives compression within L+3 additional letters.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--complete-letter-classification"></a>
#### Complete letter classification

Every letter is a permutation or a rank-(n-1) map with common kernel 01.
Inverse pairs of 01 must be 01 or 23; inverse pairs of 23 must be 01,23,
or 24. The compatible permutation core rows are precisely

    A: (k0,k1,l0,l1,h),
    B: (l0,l1,k0,k1,h),
    T: (k0,k1,l0,h,l1),

where (k0,k1) orders 0,1, (l0,l1) orders 2,3, and h>=4. Their outside
outputs are distinct and avoid the four specified outputs.

For a singular letter, write e for its omitted output and c=f0=f1.
If e is outside 01, the inverse pair of 01 must be 23. Its kernel
image cannot lie in 01, since then both 0z and 1z would be inverse
pairs. If e were also outside 23, its inverse pair of 23 would be
disjoint from 23, hence could only be 01. That would put c in 23 and
give two forbidden inverse pairs there. Therefore e is in 23. If e
is in 01, the inverse pair of 23 is 23 or 24, with c outside 23.
This gives precisely

    U_A: missing e=0 or 1, (c,c,l0,l1,h),
    U_T: missing e=0 or 1, (c,c,l0,h,l1),
    V:   missing e=2 or 3, (c,c,k0,k1,h).

For U, c is 1-e or at least 4; for V, c is 5-e or at least 4.
The other images are distinct and avoid e,c and the specified pair.
These conditions also suffice for compatibility. Identity letters are
included in the finite projections; omitting them from full-row pools
does not affect any domain or impossibility statement.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--the-seven-complete-finite-projections"></a>
#### The seven complete finite projections

For any domain D below, every letter sends all its images into H: the
six-member domains contain R5, the five-member domains contain R4, so
the domains are fully reached by those depths. Project letters to D and
EXIT=H minus D. Synchronization guarantees that every vertex can exit.
With k vertices, an exit distance k forces the vertex distances to be
a permutation of 1,...,k. For each such vector d, retain every profile p
satisfying d(i)<=1+d(p(i)), with d(EXIT)=0, and check whether all vertices
can exit under the retained profiles. Enlarging the actual alphabet in
this way can only create possible exits, so absence excludes the vector.

| name | ordered domain | profiles | vectors | surviving vectors |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| D6closed | 023,123,024,124,034,134 | 21 | 720 | none |
| D6Tmix | 024,124,034,134,02v,12v | 39 | 720 | none |
| D6Amix | 023,123,034,134,02v,12v | 37 | 720 | none |
| C_A | 012,024,124,034,134 | 27 | 120 | none |
| C_T | 012,023,124,034,134 | 23 | 120 | none |
| C_V | 023,024,124,034,134 | 23 | 120 | (3,1,4,5,2), (5,1,4,2,3) |
| D_w | 024,124,034,134,02w | 33 | 120 | none |

Here v,w are a single named outside state, relabeled 5. Every underlying
partial row of every allowed profile for either surviving C_V vector
maps C into C. This is incompatible with strong connectivity for n>=6.
Consequently first exit from a six-member domain occurs by length five,
and first exit from a five-member domain occurs by length four. The
charges are respectively 5+1+3=9 and 4+2+3=9.

This is a uniform finite certificate, not a test limited to small n.
On five inputs a permutation has four specified low outputs and at most
one free output; a singular row has two specified outputs and at most
two others, c and h. Two fresh labels beyond C suffice. On six inputs
the additional named input 5 adds one free output, so three fresh labels
beyond 0,...,5 suffice. Thus output labels 0,...,6 and 0,...,8 cover
every possible partial row up to renaming fresh states. Fresh labels
cannot become another input in these one-letter projections; their
identities matter only for equality and membership in P3 and D. The
structural templates enumerate all such partial rows. An independent
forward-row enumerator checks inverse-pair restrictions directly.
Every profile, closure flag, and distance vector agrees.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--eliminate-all-letters-taking-2-to-3"></a>
#### Eliminate all letters taking 2 to 3

For a permutation f with f2=3, its free core output is f4 in form A,
or f3 in form T. If that output is 4, the one-step H-preserving domain
is D6closed. Otherwise v=f^-1(4) is outside C, and the domain is
D6Amix or D6Tmix respectively. These are checked by mapping the seven
core holes and the families 02x,12x directly.

For a singular U row with f2=3 the domain size is 6-[c=4]. To see the
count, let z be its free core output. Hole 012 survives exactly when
c=4; the two holes 023,123 (form A) or 024,124 (form T) survive
exactly when z=4. The four other core holes survive. An outside preimage
of 4 supplies two outside holes unless 4 is already c or z. Since c
and z are distinct, the count is

    [c=4]+2[z=4]+4+2(1-[c=4]-[z=4]) = 6-[c=4].

If c=4, size five contradicts |R5|>=6. Otherwise it is precisely
D6closed when z=4, or D6Amix/D6Tmix with v=f^-1(4) outside C.
The six-member projections therefore exclude every letter with f2=3.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--eliminate-v-rows-omitting-3"></a>
#### Eliminate V rows omitting 3

For V missing 3 put A=[c in {2,4}], B=[h in {2,4}]. Its one-step
domain has size 4-A+2B: hole 012 contributes A, holes 023,123 fail,
the other four core holes contribute 4B, and the outside holes
contribute 2(2-A-B). If B=0 it has at most four members. If B=1 and
A=1 it has five. The only remaining case has six members, c>=5 and
h in {2,4}, and is D6Tmix with v the outside preimage of the other
member of {2,4}. It too is excluded.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--eliminate-b-four-cycles"></a>
#### Eliminate B four-cycles

After the preceding cuts a B permutation has B^2(2)=2 or 3. In the
latter case a simultaneous exchange of labels 0,1 normalizes it to

    b=(2,3,1,0,a), a>=4.

For a=4 the b,bb domain is C_V, and its projection excludes this case
by strong connectivity. For a>=5 put v=b^-1(4). The domain is

    a=v:  {023,034,024};
    a!=v: {023,034,02w}, w=b^-1(v) outside C.

It has only three members, contradicting |R4|>=5.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--a-b-two-cycle-and-a-breaker-are-necessary"></a>
#### A B two-cycle and a breaker are necessary

If no B permutation remains, every letter preserves the family I of
three-hole sets containing 2 and at least one of 0,1. The remaining
A,T permutations fix 2 and preserve 01; U maps the two carriers to
{e,2}; V omitting 2 maps them to {2,f2}. The both-kernel-endpoints
case also preserves I. Images with these holes never compress, contrary
to synchronization. Choose a B two-cycle and normalize it by exchanging
0,1 to

    b=(2,3,0,1,a), a>=4.

Call a permutation a keeper if {g0,g2}={0,2}, and a singular row a
keeper if {e,g2}={0,2}. Every keeper preserves the family F of all
holes 02x, x!=0,2. Thus synchronization requires a breaker. After the
preceding cuts the exhaustive breaker forms are

    P_A: (1,0,2,3,h),       P_T: (1,0,2,h,3),
    P_B: (3,2,1,0,h),
    U_A: missing 1, (c,c,2,3,h),
    U_T: missing 1, (c,c,2,h,3),
    V:   missing 2, (c,c,1,0,h).

Here h>=4 for permutations; c is 0 or >=4 for U and 3 or >=4 for V.
In singular rows h avoids the missing output, c, and the specified pair.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--mixing-b-two-cycles"></a>
#### Mixing B two-cycles

If a>=5 put v=b^-1(4). Directly testing b and bb gives the domain

    F union {12v} union ({034} if a=v, otherwise empty).

In particular it has at most two members outside F. For a breaker g,
write Nc for the count of core holes in D(b,g) intersect F, and No for
the count of its outside holes. The following upper bounds follow by
mapping the carriers of 02x under g and then under b. For U set
C=[c in {0,v}], H=[h in {0,v}]; for V set C=[c=v], H=[h=v]; for P_A,P_T
set H=[h=v].

| breaker | Nc | No |
|---|---:|---:|
| P_A,P_T | 1+H | 1-H |
| P_B | 0 | 1-[h=4] |
| U_A,U_T | C+H | 2-C-H |
| V | 1+C+H | 1-C-H |

For example U converts the carriers to 12; after b these are 03.
The third output must be 0 or v so that its b-image is 2 or 4.
The outputs already occupied by c or h remove precisely C+H available
outside preimages. The analogous V carrier is 12 with output 0
already on input 3, leaving only the target v. The bounds sum to at
most two; adding the at most two non-F members gives |D(b,g)|<=4,
contradicting |R4|>=5. Hence a=4.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--closed-b-two-cycles"></a>
#### Closed B two-cycles

For a=4 the b,bb domain is F union {124,034,134}. Count core and
outside 02x members of D(b,g) as Nc,No. For U put C=[c in {0,4}],
H=[h in {0,4}], H0=[h=0], H4=[h=4]; for V put C4=[c=4], H4=[h=4].

| breaker | Nc | No |
|---|---:|---:|
| P_A,P_T | 1+4H4 | 1-H4 |
| P_B | 1+3H4 | 1-H4 |
| U_A | C+2H0+4H4 | 2-C-H |
| U_T | C+H0+3H4 | 2-C-H |
| V | 3+C4+2H4 | 1-C4-H4 |

These bounds are obtained by testing the six core holes individually
and counting outside preimages of the same carrier targets. Their sums
are at most five; P_B and U_T have sums at most four. For U the cases
h=0 and h=4 must be distinguished: h=0 does not preserve 034,134.

Since |R4|>=5, equality is necessary. Testing its core holes gives:

* P_A has h=4 and domain C_A;
* P_T has h=4 and domain C_T;
* U_A has h=4. If c=0 its domain is C_A; otherwise c>=5 and its
  domain is D_w, where w=g^-1(0) is outside C;
* V has h=4 and domain C_V.

All these five-member domains are excluded by the projections above.
This exhausts every alphabet and proves the claim.

<a id="problem4-type7-early-exclusion--audit-records"></a>
#### Audit records

type7_reduced_actions.py and audit_type7_actions.cpp independently
generate all seven projections. audit_type7_domains.py tests every
symbolic component bound, exact domain, equality case, and invariant
family against all 95/359 nonidentity compatible full rows at n=6/7.
audit_type7_breakers.cpp independently generates full rows and literal
two-step domains at n=6,7,9. At n=9 it tests 10,079 compatible rows,
302,400 breaker pairs and 302,280 keeper pairs; all equality domains
have the four asserted shapes. These finite controls support the
uniform classification and count proof; the fresh-label projections
are the complete, all-n computational certificates.

<a id="problem4-universal-free-image-trap"></a>
<a id="problem4-universal-free-image-trap--universal-free-image-pair-trap"></a>
### Universal free-image pair trap

For a complete deterministic automaton write P_h for the distinct pairs
merged by a word of length at most h. Let K be a nonempty proper subset
of Q and R=Q-K. Suppose, for an integer d>=1 and e in R, that
(i) K covers P_(d+1), (ii) {k,e} is in P_d for every k in K, and
(iii) e belongs to R ell for every letter ell. Then R is forward
invariant. In particular the automaton is not strongly connected.

Indeed, if q in R has q ell=k in K, (iii) supplies x in R with x ell=e.
The two inputs are distinct, and ell followed by a word merging {k,e}
merges {q,x} within d+1. This contradicts (i). Thus no letter sends any
state of R into K. Nonempty proper forward invariance contradicts
strong connectivity. The proof does not require synchronization.

A useful one-target version uses only {k,e} in P_d: under the same
cover and image conditions, no input in R can map to this particular k.
The sentinel e may differ for different target states in K. If a set
O is contained in R ell for every letter, every e in O is available.
All statements retain these hypotheses; no universal F bound follows
without verifying them for the relevant entry flag.

Three literal n=3 SC/sync controls distinguish the hypotheses, with
K={0}, R={1,2}, d=1 and cycle a=[1,2,0].
- Drop the cover: b=[2,1,2], e=2. The seed {0,2} is in P1 and e is
  in every R-letter image, but the pair {1,2} is in P2.
- Drop the seed: b=[1,1,2], e=2. K covers P2 and e is universally
  covered by R images, but {0,2} is not in P1.
- Drop universal free-image coverage: b=[1,1,2], e=1. K covers P2
  and {0,1} is in P1, but 1 is absent from R a.

These are hypothesis controls, not new extremal-value claims.

<a id="problem4-zero-state-cut"></a>
<a id="problem4-zero-state-cut--a-safe-early-connectivity-cut-for-inverse-enumeration"></a>
### A safe early connectivity cut for inverse enumeration

In every enumerated first-letter normal form, state 0 has indegree zero
under a. Strong connectivity on n>=2 therefore requires an incoming b-edge
to 0 from another state. If the completely assigned inverse b-fiber at
output 0 is empty or the singleton {0}, no completion can satisfy this.
Discarding that partial branch is necessary and safe. A two-point kernel
fiber containing 0 is not discarded: its other point can enter 0.

The cut is enabled only in ordinary pruned mode. Unpruned orbit-export
mode retains every branch, so the labelled-orbit normalization audit is
unchanged. It does not alter the first-letter classification or any other
normalization choice. The submitted n=12 proof sources are preserved.
Both variants complete all 431 first forms at (n,s,target)=(13,10,10),
with identical mathematical counts: 19839983511 assignments, 185849863
prunes, 6761103983 complete maps and zero eligible strongly connected
synchronizing candidates. Every ten-set in every binary strongly connected
synchronizing thirteen-state automaton therefore compresses within nine.
The separate reachable-image lower construction gives F_bin(13,10,r)=9
for r=1,2,3. The unrestricted values remain in [9,10].

The second variant computes pair closure afresh using numeric
inverse fibers of the partial transition rows. It uses queue BFS, not the
first variant's pair bitsets, and recursively checks vertex covers instead
of explicit masks of all three-point hole sets. Both use the same safe
inverse-discovery normalization, whose independent labelled-orbit audit is
already available. Adaptive bitset priority affects assignment order only.
Synchronization is independently computed by inverse-fiber BFS to all pairs.

The normalization and short-pair bounds are proved in
[The two additional binary exceptions at n=12](#problem4-extended-binary-obstruction-proof); the original labelled-orbit audit
remains applicable because export mode disables this cut. The two variants
use the same assignment normalization but independently compute the graph
pruning predicates. This is not a claim of different traversal normalizations.

audit_inverse_fibers.py compiles audit_inverse_fibers.cpp against the actual
numeric declaration prefix, dropping only its entry point. It compares
possible() and synchronizing() with forward pair BFS and all three-hole
sets on 1000 partial maps at n=5,8,12,13,16. The original methods are not
copied or changed. A reachable C5 pair supplies a positive compression-ten
control. The audit passes address/undefined-behavior sanitizers.

check_n13_obstruction.py checks both saved negative reports and ordinary
subset-BFS lower witnesses. It does not itself rerun the complete C++ covers.

<a id="problem4-binary-supplier-cover-20261012"></a>
<a id="problem4-binary-supplier-cover-20261012--two-letter-supplier-coverage"></a>
### Two-letter supplier coverage

Let L be the retained literal pool, and suppose the actual alphabet E is
contained in L and meets every required domain R_j. If |E|<=2, the two
membership patterns of its letters must together cover every group index.
Repeated labels or equal transformation rows do not change this condition.
Every literal letter contributes one pattern. If no pair of these patterns,
including a pattern paired with itself, covers all indices, no binary
actual alphabet meets the necessary supplier requirements.

The generator tests every distinct pair of patterns. The independent
checker builds group memberships with ordinary sets, reconstructs the
complete pattern inventory and checks all pairs with replacement. An
empty required group is left to the existing missing-group rule. A
covering pair returns no cut and is not automatically a witness: safety,
strong connectivity, synchronization and reachable-image checks remain.

This elementary binary-only rule needs no extremal or alphabet-separation
claim. A complete native-geometry use must still cover every transported
prefix and pass the independent flag checker and isolated replay gates.

<a id="problem4-flag-stabilizer-quotient-20261012"></a>
<a id="problem4-flag-stabilizer-quotient-20261012--conditional-simultaneous-alphabet-child-transports"></a>
### Conditional simultaneous-alphabet child transports

At a flag node let L be its complete active literal-letter pool, R_j its
obligatory domains, and v_0,...,v_k its actual prefix images. The permitted
next-image inventory is C. A checked generator p must fix every old image,
each known forced image, the fixed states and premise graphs. Conjugation
is defined by f'(p(q))=p(f(q)). It must give a bijection of L fixing every
R_j as a set, and p must permute C.

For any actual alphabet E contained in L, apply this same p to every
letter. The conjugated alphabet still lies in L and meets all R_j. Words
have unchanged lengths and their images are relabeled by p; old images
are fixed. Strong connectivity, synchronization, reachable-image status,
alphabet size and the safety predicate are preserved. All products of
checked generators have these properties.

Suppose a prospective next image y is transported to representative z.
Conjugation sends letters mapping v_k to y to letters mapping v_k to z.
It also sends span(v_0,...,v_k,y) to span(v_0,...,v_k,z), because p fixes
the old characteristic rows and acts linearly by a coordinate permutation.
Consequently the filtered child letter pool, its new obligatory domain
and its rank-growth condition are transported correctly. A rejected
representative child therefore rejects every child explicitly transported
to it. This is an alphabet-independent conditional statement, not an F
bound or an all-parameter result.

The implementation starts with adjacent transpositions in cells agreeing
on all old and forced-image columns, outside conservative fixed-state
sets. Every proposed generator is verified on all active literal rows,
all required groups, all premise edges and the complete choice inventory.
Only successfully checked involutions are used. Each child stores a
sequence mapping it to its representative. Exact child coverage, row
transport digests and every stated invariant are independently replayed.
No node acquires safety at depth 12; a depth-11 survivor remains a candidate.

<a id="problem4-fold-compressibility-premise-20261012"></a>
<a id="problem4-fold-compressibility-premise-20261012--a-compressibility-premise-for-the-necessary-folded-model"></a>
### A compressibility premise for the necessary folded model

Auxiliary premise audit only. No numerical maximum, alphabet separation,
new construction or synchronization of the fold is claimed.

Let a complete strongly connected N-state automaton have a subset T of
size t>=2, with alpha in T. Assume alpha is avoidable from Q and
ac(T,{alpha})>N-t. Then T is compressible, even if the full automaton
is not synchronizing and T is not a reachable image.

To prove this, take a word z with alpha not in Qz and consider its state
transformation f. The f-orbit of alpha has a tail of length h>=1 followed
by a cycle of length d>=1: alpha cannot be on the cycle, because it has
no f-predecessor. Set p=f^d(alpha). Then p differs from alpha, and
f^h(p)=f^(h+d)(alpha)=f^h(alpha). Thus z^h merges alpha and p.

Strong connectivity supplies a path from a point of T to p of length
at most N-t. Indeed, a shortest path from the set T to p has no repeated
vertices, and after its initial vertex every vertex lies outside T.
Let its label be v. The assumed lower bound makes v safe: Tv contains
alpha and p and has t points. Appending z^h compresses Tv. Hence T is
compressible. This is only an existence argument; it gives no useful
short upper bound and does not assert that every pair merges.

In the qualified fold at N=13,t=9, ac=12, the previous avoidability and
strong-connectivity premises therefore suffice for eventual
compressibility. The existing transversal/rank-word lemma may now be
applied to T: no word of length at most six can have rank at most nine.
For rank below nine it compresses T directly; for rank nine the existing
bound is N-t+|u|+1<=11. This is exactly the previously used conditional
rank-word rule, with its missing folded compressibility premise supplied.

No historical certificate is enlarged or reinterpreted by this note.
The new premise does not repair the unproved synchronization or reachable
image status of the folded model. The proof uses ordinary functional
graphs and shortest paths; no novelty or priority claim is made.

The companion audit enumerates every unordered binary transition pair
through four states, including repeated letters. It checks avoiding
words, a literal merging partner, all applicable subsets and paths, and
eventual compression by independent ordinary subset BFS. These controls
support the argument; they are not extrapolated as a finite upper proof.

<a id="problem4-graph-first-transports"></a>
<a id="problem4-graph-first-transports--graph-first-relabelling-of-the-full-first-pair-domain"></a>
### Graph-first relabelling of the full first-pair domain

This is a symmetry reduction, not an extremal theorem or an exclusion.
It keeps the native parent domain and every ordered initial pair.

First apply one certified relabelling per retained P1 graph. It preserves
H,A,B,C,D, the mandatory frame intersection, and every individual native
preimage field; it transports the whole G=P1 union K_C union K_D and
each exact allowed kernel list. Its target is another retained graph in
the same native domain. A minimal representative is convenient but is
not a proof premise: any such certified target suffices.

Next fix every vertex incident to the target P1 graph. Permute only its
isolated vertices within each control cell, sorting their two membership
bits in the ordered pair of initial images. This fixes P1, all entrance
sets and all fields; it therefore also fixes G and every compatible
kernel domain. Compose the two relabellings. Every actual initial pair
is transported to one saved representative with its whole letter domain.
Counts cover every labelled ordered pair; the transport may deliberately
retain nonminimal orbit representatives.

The independent audit rebuilds the complete native graph list and frame
families. It validates the supplied first permutation literally, then
constructs the second permutation independently, tests every transported
kernel and all field sets, and recomputes the complete representative
multiplicities. It does not assume the compiler's canonical choice.
Only a subsequent full flag-tree audit could exclude the geometry.


<a id="problem4-obligatory-supplier-split-20261012"></a>
<a id="problem4-obligatory-supplier-split-20261012--conditional-compulsory-letter-splitting"></a>
### Conditional compulsory-letter splitting

The actual alphabet E is contained in the current literal pool L and
meets each required domain R_j. Pick a domain with two or more members.
Every actual E contains some a in R_j. Cover every such a by a branch
that adds the singleton requirement {a}. Overlapping branches are allowed:
E may contain several members and is then covered more than once.

In each branch, the singleton requirement justifies safe-image propagation
from the already justified actual prefix images, with their depth bounds.
The existing propagation proof applies without change. A branch closes
only when a required domain becomes empty or a complete obligatory-letter
product supplies explicitly checked unsafe words within the horizon.
If every branch closes, every possible actual alphabet is excluded under
the stated safety premises. Any unclosed branch makes the routine return
no cut. The independent checker reconstructs the entire split domain,
tests exact branch coverage and replays all image and word certificates.

The generator's caps (512 active letters, at most four split choices) only
skip cuts. They are not hypotheses of the conditional argument. No numerical
extremum, alphabet separation or complete geometry is asserted here.

<a id="problem4-rank-word-compression-pruning-20261012"></a>
<a id="problem4-rank-word-compression-pruning-20261012--existing-transversal-method-conditional-compression-pruning"></a>
### Existing transversal method: conditional compression pruning

Let |Q|=n, |S|=s>=2, and assume S is compressible. If a word u has
rank exactly s and length h, then S compresses within n-s+h+1 letters.

Put m=n-s. Suppose all words of length <=m+h+1 preserve |S|. The s
fibers of u partition Q. Each Sv for |v|<=m+1 is a transversal, since
|Svu|=s. Their trajectory rows lie in the space T whose fiber sums
are equal. Its dimension is m+1. For V_i=span{chi_S D_v:|v|<=i}, an
early plateau gives invariance and permanent containment in T, impossible
because a compressed trajectory has support <s and an empty fiber.
Thus V_m=T. Every generator of V_m maps into T under each letter, so
T is invariant, giving the same contradiction. This includes m=0.

If rank(u)<s, u itself compresses S. At (13,9,1), compression length
>=12 therefore forbids every word of rank <=9 and length <=6.
This requires eventual compressibility; it does not require S reachability.

No novelty claim: the transversal persistence argument is Pin's 1978
Corollaire 4, *Utilisation de l'algebre lineaire en theorie des automates*,
AFCET-SMF, pp.85-92. Primary author-uploaded text:
https://www.researchgate.net/publication/29616908_Utilisation_de_l%27algebre_lineaire_en_theorie_des_automates
Berlinkov--Szykula also cite its rank-word application:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.8363 (p.14).

This is an auxiliary reuse of existing theory, outside the article and
publication package. It does not determine a numerical F value.

<a id="problem4-real-filtration-pool-20261012"></a>
<a id="problem4-real-filtration-pool-20261012--conditional-rejection-using-the-real-flag-of-an-entire-literal-pool"></a>
### Conditional rejection using the real flag of an entire literal pool

Auxiliary thirteen-state proof. Let T have nine states and contain alpha=3.
Assume alpha is avoidable from Q and every word of length at most eleven
is safe from T. This is a necessary model for the manuscript domain at
(13,9,1), target twelve, and for its qualified folded counterpart. No new
F value, folded synchronization or folded reachable image is asserted.

Fix characteristic rows b_0,...,b_11, with b_0=chi_T, and let
W_i=span_R(b_0,...,b_i). The finite audit checks dim W_i=i+1, that all
b_i have total nine and alpha-coordinate one, and that every literal
action in the specified pool maps W_i into W_(i+1) for i<11. Consequently
W_11=H={x:sum x=9x_alpha}. These are statements about complete counting
rows chi_B D_f; the audit does not require safety of b_11 f at depth twelve.

For an actual alphabet E inside this pool, let V_i be the actual trajectory
row span from T through length i. The checked filtration implies V_i is
contained in W_i for i<=11. Under the safe-word premise V_i is in H. A
plateau V_i=V_(i+1) stabilizes forever under E, contrary to a word avoiding
alpha from Q, which also avoids it from T and has total nine. Hence
dim V_i>=i+1, so V_i=W_i for all i<=11.

For every i<11 some actual letter must map b_i outside W_i. If every
letter mapped b_i inside W_i, the earlier basis rows would also map
inside W_i by the checked filtration, causing a plateau. At i=11 the
same argument applies to H: the earlier basis rows already map inside H,
so some actual letter maps b_11 outside H. Its counting row has total
nine, hence this means alpha multiplicity differs from one. Define the
twelve growth domains by these exact tests. Every qualifying alphabet
must meet each of them. The argument does not require the b_i themselves
to be actual word images for that alphabet; it uses equality of spans.

The existing literal word conflicts are valid under the same premise.
An unsafe word of length at most eleven directly contradicts safety.
A word u of rank below nine compresses T. For rank exactly nine and
length at most six, every Tw with |w|<=5 is a transversal of its nine
fibers, since |Twu|=9. Their rows span a space of dimension at most
13-9+1=5, while the preceding no-plateau argument gives dim V_5>=6.
This contradiction is the standard row-span/transversal method, not a
novelty or priority claim. It needs no unproved folded reset word.

A finite cover tree checks all alphabets meeting the twelve growth
domains against these literal conflicts. Before using it at a native
node, every active transformation must literally belong to the audited
pool and its initial image must equal T. The growth domains replace
dependence on a particular choice of subsequent characteristic images.
Complete original-prefix and whole-geometry replay are still separate
requirements. No other geometry or numerical extremum follows from the
pool certificate alone.

<a id="problem4-supplier-escape-words"></a>
<a id="problem4-supplier-escape-words--combining-a-compulsory-supplier-with-a-connectivity-escape"></a>
### Combining a compulsory supplier with a connectivity escape

This is an auxiliary conditional pruning rule, not an extremal theorem.

Let L contain the actual alphabet E. Assume E meets every nonempty
supplier domain R_j in L and every actual word of length at most H
is safe for (S,A). A singleton R_j forces its unique literal letter;
let F collect all such forced letters.

First consider two obligatory domains R_j,R_k. If every pair b in R_j,
e in R_k has an unsafe literal word over F union {b,e} of length at
most H, the branch is impossible. The actual alphabet contains some
actual choices b,e, and the corresponding word is an actual unsafe word.
This part needs neither connectivity nor synchronization.
The identical argument applies to a product of three obligatory domains.
The implementation tests such a product only when one domain has at
most two members; this is a conservative heuristic, not a proof premise.

Alternatively suppose every letter in F fixes
state q. Strong connectivity requires some e in E with qe!=q.
Choose any other obligatory domain R_j. The actual alphabet contains
some b in R_j and some e in L escaping from {q}.

If for EVERY such pair (b,e) a literal word over F union {b,e} of
length at most H is unsafe, the branch is impossible. The word may
depend on the pair. It is an actual word of E for the actual choices,
contradicting safety. This proves the rule for every finite alphabet.

The implementation skips large products and returns no cut when a
pair has no found word. These are conservative search choices. A cut
stores every pair and its explicit word. The independent checker
reconstructs both domains, checks nonempty premises and the entire
Cartesian product, and simulates each word on ordinary sets. No
incomplete product, merely nonsynchronizing model, or solver timeout
supplies a cut. No word beyond H is used.

<a id="problem4-supplier-image-propagation"></a>
<a id="problem4-supplier-image-propagation--short-images-forced-by-a-whole-supplier-group"></a>
### Short images forced by a whole supplier group

Auxiliary pruning only. This does not establish an extremal value.

Let L be a finite overapproximation of the actual alphabet E, and let
R_1,...,R_t be supplier domains such that E meets each R_j. Suppose
every actual word of length at most H is safe for (S,A): its image has
size |S| and contains A. A known image X with depth bound d means that
there exists an actual word of length at most d sending S to X.

For every known X with d<H, any candidate letter taking X to an unsafe
image may be deleted: if it were actual, appending it to such a word
would contradict safety at depth at most d+1. This preserves E inside L.

If all remaining members of R_j have the same X-image Y, then E has a
member in R_j and hence Y is an actual image at depth at most d+1.
This is an existential statement about the image; no individual letter
is asserted to be forced. Add this depth bound and repeat the two rules.
If a supplier domain becomes empty, the conditional branch is impossible.
Finite domains and the finite collection of subset/depth pairs ensure
termination. Each deletion and each forced-image inference preserves
the actual alphabet and its actual short images, by induction.

In an equality-flag branch the supplied basis rows have actual depth
bounds 0,1,...,k, by the existing actual-image flag induction. These
are premises, not arbitrary Boolean vectors in the span. Every additional
image needs the explicit nonempty-group inference above. No safety at
depth H+1 is used; images at depth H are never used to delete letters.

The implementation uses cached masks of letters sending a source image
to each safe image. The independent checker simulates every literal
letter in each proof step. Supplied initial depth bounds must be justified
by the calling certificate. Controls do not replace this conditional proof.

### Ternary parameter maximum 2n-1

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
