this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**PROVED on paper for all n>=8.** The local image-extension maximum reaches
2n-1 while rt=P_best=n+2. This further sharpens the additive obstruction
to a universal 2n bound. C=2 remains OPEN, as does novelty; no general reset
upper bound or Cerny counterexample follows.

Let L=n-1>=7, C={0,...,L-1}, f=L. The letters a,b are the one-fixed-point
family: a cycles C and fixes f; fb=0, (L-1)b=L-2, and cb=f at every other
cycle state. Add c swapping 0 and 1 and fixing every other state. Write
P={f,0,L-2}, B={f,0}, H={0,L-2}, S={L-2,L-1}.

<a id="direct-attack-adjacent-swap-extension-theorem--full-image-structure"></a>
#### Full image structure

a and c generate every permutation of C, fixing f. Indeed, conjugating c
by powers of a gives all adjacent cycle transpositions, which generate the
symmetric group; inverse a powers are positive powers a^(L-j).
The full image family is Q, all singletons, all pairs, and every triple
{f,x,y} with distinct x,y in C. Qb=P gives all such triples. Pb=B gives all
f-pairs; {f,L-1}b=H gives all cycle-pairs. Hb={f} and SC gives all
singletons. This family is forward closed: b maps a triple to P or B, an
f-pair to H or B, and a cycle-pair to {f,L-2} or {f}. It has n^2-n+2 images.

<a id="direct-attack-adjacent-swap-extension-theorem--exact-target-lower-bound-includes-singleton-routes"></a>
#### Exact target lower bound includes singleton routes

Every first drop from a larger image to size <=2 yields B, and some actual
triple drops in one letter. Thus e(S)=1+D(B,S).
The first cycle-pair entry from B requires at least L letters: the cycle
state 0 must reach L-1, then b gives H. The swap can replace the first
forward a step 0->1 but cannot shorten the state path L-1; a b at a
default state resets the f-pair to B. Every later cycle-pair entry gives H.

After the last such entry, a pair route to S uses only a,c. We prove it
needs at least L letters. Label the two initial states of H as A=0 and
B=L-2. Suppose a word of length <=L-1 sends H onto S. Track signed
displacements: an a adds 1, and a c adds 1 at state 0, subtracts 1 at
state 1, or adds zero elsewhere. A cannot wrap around C in <=L-1 steps.
Its net c displacement is at most 1: repeated swaps near 0 can cancel
or undo forward steps, and after an a leaves 1 it cannot return there
within this length. Only this upper bound on net displacement is needed.

If A ends at L-2, the word has at least L-3 a's and at most two c's.
B's signed displacement is between L-5 and L-1. Since L>=7, none of these
integers is congruent to 1 modulo L, required for B to end at L-1.
If A ends at L-1, there are at least L-2 a's and at most one c. B's signed
displacement lies between L-3 and L-1, none congruent to zero modulo L,
required for B to end at L-2. Both orientations are excluded.
The word a^2 c a^(L-3) sends H to S in exactly L letters. Thus a pair
arrival from B costs 2L.

Every first merge is from a cycle-pair not containing L-1, and produces f.
This takes at least L+1 letters from B. The shortest state path from f
into S has L-1 letters: b to 0 and L-2 forward steps. Swaps do not shorten
that path, and b at L-1 first requires L letters from f. Singleton arrivals
therefore cost at least 2L as well. Consequently

    e(S)=2L+1=2n-1,

attained from P by b a^(L-1)b a^2 c a^(L-3).

<a id="direct-attack-adjacent-swap-extension-theorem--all-images-have-e2n-1-reset-and-policy-are-fast"></a>
#### All images have e<=2n-1; reset and policy are fast

Any triple contains f, so the full-Q reset word bb a^(L-1)bb, length L+3,
transports Q into that triple. An f-pair uses Pb a^j, length <=L.
For any cycle-pair T, an actual triple first drops to B in one b, then
a^(L-1)bb merges it to f. From f, b followed by at most L-2 a's reaches
some member of T. The total is at most 1+(L+1)+(L-1)=2L+1. Singletons
use H b={f}, followed by b a^j if needed, costing <=L+1. This covers the
whole image family, proving max e=2n-1.

Q needs at least two letters to first reach B, then at least L+1 more
to merge. The same reset word gives rt=L+3=n+2. Singleton f has e=1 via H;
H has e=L+1 via P, since reaching H as a pair needs L letters from B,
whereas reaching a singleton in H needs at least L+2. P has e=1 via Q.
Thus the exact policy chain f->H->P->Q costs L+3, proving P_best=rt.

<a id="direct-attack-adjacent-swap-extension-theorem--verification-boundary"></a>
#### Verification boundary

The complete single-transposition scan at n16/24/32 tested all 2676
additions to three base families, without truncation, before this proof.
All 21 retained arrays have independent ordinary all-source distances.
For the parameter family, all n4..63 full image closures and forward
entries, exact target e and the three-phase policy costs are independently
recomputed.
Five separate proof-frame distances are also recomputed at each n>=8:
0->last using a,c; H->S using a,c; B->singleton f; f->S; and B->S.
Every e/G/W entry is additionally checked by all-source BFS only through
n20 (17 cases). The arbitrary-n maximum follows from the
paper proof, not a claim of independent all-entry computation beyond n20.
Three corruptions are rejected. Small boundaries are retained without
extending the n>=8 quantifier. No new Lean theorem.

The image-extension formulation is known from
[Kisielewicz--Szykula, Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
The precise family and coefficient-two conclusion retain OPEN priority.

<a id="direct-attack-alternating-image-extension"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-alternating-image-extension--alternating-family-exact-image-structure-and-a-linear-extension-theorem"></a>
### Alternating family: exact image structure and a linear extension theorem

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**PROVED on paper; priority OPEN.** This is a special-family result, not
an unrestricted quadratic bound. For n=2m+1>=5, use Q={0,...,2m},
a(2i+1)=2i, a fixes evens, and b(q)=q+1 mod n. Put
E={0,2,...,2m}, F=E\{2m}, and E_r=E b^r.

<a id="direct-attack-alternating-image-extension--full-reachable-image-family"></a>
#### Full reachable-image family

    R={Q} union {nonempty T: T subset E_r for some 0<=r<n}.

Every word containing a has its last a-image contained in E and a suffix
b^r. Words without a leave Q unchanged. This proves the upper inclusion.
Conversely Q a=E. On E, c=b^2 a is the (m+1)-cycle advancing each even
point to the next even point, while d=ba fixes all points except 2m,
which it sends to 0. These are precisely the standard Cerny generators
on E, with actual ambient word costs 3 and 2.

To reach any nonempty T subset E, conjugates of d by powers of c merge
each chosen even point into its successor and fix the other even points.
For each consecutive block of E\T, process the points in cyclic forward
order, merging each into its still-present successor, ending at T.
Only undesired source points are changed, so every T point remains.
Starting from Q a gives a full-Q reach word. Append b^r to reach any
subset of E_r. This also proves synchronization; b itself proves SC.

Consequently for every proper X subset Q,

    rho(X)=max_r |X intersect E_r|,

while rho(Q)=n. The full-Q exception is essential. This is an exact
capacity formula, not an assumption of complete reachability of Q.

<a id="direct-attack-alternating-image-extension--linear-image-extension-for-every-proper-reachable-s"></a>
#### Linear image extension for every proper reachable S

**Theorem: e(S)<=2n for every nonempty proper S in R.** Choose a
representation S=S_0 b^r, where nonempty S_0 subset E and 0<=r<n.
If S_0=E, Q a b^r=S and 1+r<=n.

Otherwise there is an adjacent boundary h outside S_0, d inside S_0
on the cycle of even points. The following actual words have images
E\{h}, with exactly one double fiber at d and all other fibers single:

* If h=2m and d=0, the word a on V=E_1 has that property, with cost 1.
* If h=2i<2m and d=2i+2, the word u=a b^(2i+2) a on V=E_1 has
  that property, with cost 2i+4<=2m+2=n+1. Indeed E_1 a=F,
  F b^(2i+2) a=E\{2i}, and the initially doubled 0 maps to d.

Set T=V intersect S_0 u^-1. Its size is |S_0|+1, because h is absent
and the doubled image d is present. Every nonempty subset of V=E_1
is reachable by the image characterization, so T is a valid larger
image. T u=S_0, hence T u b^r=S. The cost is <=n+1+r<=2n.
This controls all reachable ranks, not only the measured middle rank.
The resulting class reset bound 2n(n-1) is not an improvement on known
circular-class bounds and says nothing universal about arbitrary DFAs.

<a id="direct-attack-alternating-image-extension--exact-middle-rank-reduction"></a>
#### Exact middle-rank reduction

At rank m, all images are rotations of E\{2i}; there are mn distinct
sets. Above rank m the only images are Q and the n sets E_r.
Any E_r first dropping below rank m+1 under a reaches F: direct checking
gives E_r a=E for even r and F for odd r. A transport from a larger
image into an m-set S must have such a drop before its final suffix.
Thus

    e(S)=1+D(F,S),

where D(F,S) is the shortest word taking F into a subset of S. The upper
bound chooses initial image E_1 and prepends a. The lower bound uses
the necessary rank-m+1 drop (from Q a stage as well, if starting at Q).
This includes transport ending in a proper subset of S; equality of
the transported image with S is NOT required.

<a id="direct-attack-alternating-image-extension--complete-finite-layer-evidence-and-open-lower-bound-target"></a>
#### Complete finite layer evidence and open lower-bound target

An inverse powerset BFS computes every rank-m cost through n=25.
An independently implemented forward presentation (B,r), B subset E,
computes D(F,S) and agrees on all entries through n=25. It then extends
the full layer calculation through n=37. Each presentation edge is an
actual a or b action; overlapping representations preserve exact word
distance after minimizing over all target representations.

The layer maxima at n=5,7,9 are 10,12,16. At every tested odd n from
11 through 37 the maximum equals 2n-4. For n>=13 the stored peak is

    S=(E\{2m-2}) b^(n-5),
    u=a b^(n-1) a b^(n-5), |u|=2n-4,

with larger image E_1. The same target's value is also checked at n=11.
The exact arbitrary-n LOWER bound e(S)>=2n-4 and the arbitrary-n maximum
formula remain **CONJECTURED**. The displayed word proves only an upper
bound. Finite agreement does not justify an asymptotic coefficient >=2
when an additive constant is allowed. The five-state exact cost 10
already forces C>=2 for the literal e(S)<=Cn envelope without slack.

The full reachable-family and 2n extension theorems above are separately
proved. Image extension itself is the known Kisielewicz--Szykula route:
[primary manuscript, Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
No new general Cerny proof, general upper bound or Lean statement follows.

<a id="direct-attack-anchored-image-profile"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-anchored-image-profile--reachable-fiber-anchoring-improves-the-image-rank-profile-bound"></a>
### Reachable-fiber anchoring improves the image rank-profile bound

**PROVED on paper; attribution/priority OPEN for the precise profile.**
This is a computable automaton-dependent bound, not a new bound in n alone.
Assume an SC synchronizing DFA with n>=2 and the exact image policy G.
Let E_k=max{e(S): S reachable, |S|=k}, with an empty rank contributing 0.
Define the actual reachable-fiber capacity

    kappa=max_{letter x, q} rho(x^-1{q}).

Equivalently kappa is the maximum size of a reachable image T merged by
ONE letter. It is not the maximum ordinary fiber size unless reachability
has separately justified that substitution.

<a id="direct-attack-anchored-image-profile--general-bound-and-its-actual-word-cost"></a>
#### General bound and its actual word cost

There is always such an image of size >=2. Take a shortest reset word;
its last proper prefix has an image U of size >1, and its last letter
merges U. Thus 2<=kappa<=n. Pick an attaining T, letter x and target q.
The singleton {q} is reachable (SC), e({q})=1, and T is an allowed first
endpoint. Later phases from T strictly increase cardinality and pay their
FULL transport costs, visiting each rank k>=kappa at most once. Hence

    rt(A)<=P(A)<=1+G(T)<=1+sum_{k=kappa}^{n-1} E_k=:U_kappa.

In particular

    P(A)<=U_kappa<=U_2=1+sum_{k=2}^{n-1}E_k<=sum_{k=1}^{n-1}E_k.

The last comparison uses E_1>=1. The existence of a reach word for T is
not treated as free: the later G(T) chain constructs and pays for the
actual Q-to-T transport. For kappa=n there is a constant letter and the
sum is empty, giving 1. The n=1 endpoint separately gives 0.

Every singleton has e({q})<=n: transport an attaining one-step larger
image into a singleton q0, then follow an SC state path from q0 to q of
length <=n-1. This is an actual word of length <=n. The existence of a
one-step reset-target seed also agrees with the established inverse-BFS
seed convention in Section 4 of the
[Kisielewicz--Szykula primary manuscript](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
The one-letter merged-fiber first phase is explicitly used for completely
reachable automata in [Ferens--Szykula, Corollary 6.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.05956).
It is a known step, not a new inverse-search or anchoring idea. The profile
here retains actual reachable capacity for incomplete image families.

<a id="direct-attack-anchored-image-profile--a-sufficient-square-condition-and-counterexample-rigidity"></a>
#### A sufficient square condition and counterexample rigidity

If e(S)<=n for EVERY proper reachable image, then U_2<=
1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2. In fact, from any singleton having e=1 every choice
of shortest extension ties costs at most this square: its first phase
costs 1, and at most n-2 remaining phases each cost <=n. This hypothesis
is false in general; it cannot be silently used as a universal theorem.

Any SC Cerny counterexample, and any failure of the global policy square,
must therefore have U_kappa>(n-1)^2. Using the proved top-rank E_(n-1)<=n,
at n>=4 this requires kappa<=n-2 and

    sum_{k=kappa}^{n-2}(E_k-n)>n(kappa-2).

Thus some INTERMEDIATE reachable rank k in [kappa,n-2] must have e(S)>n.
More quantitatively, one such rank has

    e(S)>=floor(n(n-3)/(n-kappa-1))+1.

This is a necessary condition, not a contradiction or a sufficient test.
Uniform e<=Cn only yields 1+Cn(n-kappa); for C=2 it proves the square
when kappa>=ceil((n+2)/2). No universal C=2 claim follows.

<a id="direct-attack-anchored-image-profile--why-the-stronger-rank-sum-still-cannot-prove-the-square"></a>
#### Why the stronger rank sum still cannot prove the square

The proposal U_kappa<=(n-1)^2 is **REFUTED at state-minimal n=4**:

    a=[0,2,1,1], b=[2,1,3,0], kappa=2,
    E_1=4, E_2=6, E_3=3,
    U_old=13, U_kappa=10>9, but P=rt=8.

This is the earlier inverse-greedy obstruction, now identifying failure
of the stronger profile envelope. At n<=3 the top-rank bound and kappa>=2
give U_kappa<=the square, over ANY alphabet. The n4 scan stops at the
first failure; it does not establish a larger complete covering result.

On C_n the image rank maxima are E_k=n for 1<=k<n, and kappa=2.
The new anchored bound is EXACTLY (n-1)^2, while the old rank sum is
n(n-1). Thus the valid bound handles the classical extremal without
discarding the known one-step first phase. This alone does not control
other automata's incompatible worst images at different ranks.

Under adding transformations already generated by actual words, R stays
fixed, each old e(S) weakly decreases, and kappa cannot decrease. Therefore
U_kappa cannot increase. The n4 word-shortcut counterexample has U dropping
7 to 6 while P rises 4 to 5. This separates a valid monotone majorant from
the nonmonotone policy itself. For arbitrary alphabet additions R may grow;
no monotonicity of this profile is asserted then.

<a id="direct-attack-anchored-image-profile--remaining-precise-charging-question"></a>
#### Remaining precise charging question

For a policy chain starting with an attaining one-step image of size kappa,
each later phase S->T has cost e(S) and jump j=|T|-|S|. The jumps sum to
n-kappa. Its cost fits the square exactly when

    sum_phases [e(S)-n j]<=n(kappa-2).

This is a precise compatibility/charging target on ACTUAL images and
transport words. It is not justified by independent rank maxima. Restricting
the first endpoint to one attaining kappa may be stronger than the original
global singleton minimum target; the retained checks alone do not prove
that stronger choice always suffices. No new n-only bound or Lean result.

<a id="direct-attack-circular-image-policy-theorem"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-circular-image-policy-theorem--exact-image-policy-costs-on-the-cerny-family"></a>
### Exact image-policy costs on the Cerny family

**PROVED on paper; novelty OPEN.** Let n>=2, Q={0,...,n-1}, a(q)=q+1
mod n, and let b fix q<n-1 and send n-1 to 0. Define
S_k={n-1} union {0,...,k-2} for 2<=k<=n. For the reachable-image
extension and all-tie policy recurrences in [Shortest image-extension policy: a surviving compatibility target](#direct-attack-image-extension-policy),

    e({q})=q+1,
    e(S_k)=n                 (2<=k<n),
    G_min(S_k)=G_max(S_k)=n(n-k),
    G_min({q})=G_max({q})=(n-1)^2+q.

Every critical larger-image target is unique: S_2 from a singleton and
S_(k+1) from S_k. Both extrema fix the initial set. The global best
singleton costs (n-1)^2; the maximum over initial singletons costs n(n-1).
This is a family policy theorem, not an unrestricted reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-circular-image-policy-theorem--proof"></a>
#### Proof

The actual word (ba^(n-1))^(n-k) maps Q to S_k, by
S_k ba^(n-1)=S_(k-1) for k>=3 and Q=S_n. The word
(ba^(n-1))^(n-2)ba^q resets to q. Only these reachable images are
needed; complete reachability need not be invoked.

Inverse a rotates an occupied set backwards by one. Inverse b replaces
the occupancy of n-1 with that of 0. On a nonempty proper circular
interval it fixes the interval, extends its left endpoint from 0 to
n-1, deletes its right endpoint n-1, or empties a singleton at n-1.
Empty inverse sets never grow. Until the first growth, a nonempty
inverse set stays a circular interval: deletion keeps its left endpoint,
and only inverse a changes that endpoint, decreasing it modulo n.

S_k starts with left endpoint n-1. Its first growth requires endpoint
0, hence at least n-1 inverse a steps and an inverse b. A preimage of
size >k must first grow, so the word has length >=n. At length n there
are exactly n-1 a steps and one b, and b must be the final inverse step.
The unique word is ba^(n-1), whose full preimage is S_(k+1). This image
is reachable. Its only contained image of size >k is itself, since it
has size k+1. Thus e(S_k)=n and the larger target is unique.

A singleton q starts with endpoint q. Its first growth needs q inverse
a steps; premature deletion makes the preimage empty. Its unique
shortest word is ba^q, with length q+1 and full preimage S_2, its only
larger contained image. This includes n=2, where S_2=Q.

The unique-target recurrence, with G_min(Q)=G_max(Q)=0, gives
G_min(S_k)=G_max(S_k)=n(n-k). Adding q+1 at the singleton gives
q+1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2+q. This proves all formulas without assuming the
classical lower bound on the reset threshold.

<a id="direct-attack-circular-image-policy-theorem--consequences-and-audit-correction"></a>
#### Consequences and audit correction

The average-singleton proposal sum_q G_min({q})<=n(n-1)^2 fails already
at n=2, with exact excess n(n-1)/2 on every C_n. Requiring every
initial singleton to meet the square also fails at n=2. The global
policy conjecture minimizes over q and remains unaffected.

The previously quoted C6 cost 30 is a maximum OVER initial singletons.
It does not come from extension-tie choice after fixing q=0: at each
fixed q both extrema equal 25+q. [Shortest image-extension policy: a surviving compatibility target](#direct-attack-image-extension-policy) corrects
that interpretation. The numerical arrays themselves were correct.

circular_image_policy.py recomputes ordinary-set inverse distances through
n=12, compares native arrays on all critical sets, and verifies exact e,
both tie extrema and full-Q reach/reset words. This finite audit supports
the parameter proof above, which remains outside Lean. Classical C_n
extremality and image-extension methods are known; priority of this exact
policy formulation remains OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension--direct-binary-quadratic-actual-image-extension"></a>
### Direct binary quadratic actual-image extension

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for every p>=2. This strengthens
[Quadratic actual-image extension with fixed ternary and binary alphabets](#direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension) without a selector encoding:
a binary SC irreducibly synchronizing n=2p+1 family has an actual p-image
with EXACT e(T)=n^2/8+O(n). Every fixed linear coefficient/slack therefore
fails already in this direct binary class. Independent finite audits are
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. Priority **OPEN**; no **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim. General Cerny and the global compatible-policy square remain **OPEN**.

Subsequent [A compatible shortest-phase chain despite binary quadratic local extension](#direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy) proves the stronger
charged upper rt<=P<=p^2+p-ceil(p/2)-1 for every p>=3 with genuinely
shortest actual-image phases. All-p equality remains CONJECTURED.
The looser interval below and its earlier independent seal remain valid.

The same family has a PROVED quadratic reset interval with leading n^2/4
and an explicit reset below the square. It is not a Cerny counterexample.
No exact arbitrary-parameter reset threshold or unrestricted minimum-state
assertion is made. The earlier ternary/simple and selector-coding results
remain valid and are not replaced by a simple-binary claim.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension--original-letters-actual-image-and-full-source-predicate"></a>
#### Original letters, actual image and full source predicate

Use right actions on two cycles

    C={C_0,...,C_(p-1)}, D={D_0,...,D_p}, n=2p+1,
    s=floor(p/2), k=p-s=ceil(p/2).

The TWO original letters are

    a: C_i -> C_(i+1 mod p), D_j -> D_(j+1 mod (p+1));
    b: q -> D_i if i<k, and q -> C_i if i>=k,
       where i=pi(q), pi(C_i)=i, pi(D_j)=j mod p.

Letter b is an idempotent of rank p, with full image

    E={D_0,...,D_(k-1),C_k,...,C_(p-1)}.

Both cycles have states sent across the bridge by b: C_0 -> D_0 and
D_k -> C_k. Thus the DFA is SC. Letter a is a permutation; b is a
nonconstant idempotent. Neither unary alphabet synchronizes, so the
binary DFA is irreducibly synchronizing once its reset is supplied below.

EVERY word containing b has rank at most p; every other word is a
permutation. Hence Q is the ONLY actual image of size greater than p.
For

    A={s,...,p-1} if p is even, and A={0,...,s-1} if p is odd,
    T=pi^-1(A),

|A|=s and |T|=p. Its actual reach word is proved below. Thus, for the
exact into-image definition allowing strict subsets,

    e(T)=min{|u|: Qu is contained in T}.                (1)

No unreachable inverse set or nonactual larger parent is admitted.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension--first-stall-costs-and-a-trajectory-lower-bound-for-all-words"></a>
#### First-stall costs and a trajectory lower bound for ALL words

Letter b preserves pi. Every a increases pi by one except its actual
transition D_p -> D_0, called a stall. If t is the total number of a's
and d_i the number of stalls on ONE original trajectory C_i, then

    pi(C_i u)=i+t-d_i mod p.                            (2)

This identity still tracks the original trajectory after any merges.
No letter b enters D_p. From D_0 at least p a's are needed to FIRST
reach D_p: before that visit pi advances by one per a, its required
positive return to zero is a multiple of p, and b does not enter D_p.
The actual stall then uses another a and returns to D_0. Thus between
any two counted stalls on the SAME trajectory are at least p+1 a's.
An uncounted b departure from D_p cannot speed up repeated counted stalls.

The minimum a-count through the first stall from C_i is

    delta_i=p-i+1        for 0<=i<k;
    delta_i=2p-i+1       for k<=i<p.                    (3)

For i<k, b can send C_i directly to D_i; p-i more a's first reach
D_p and one more stalls. A shorter path is impossible since the
pre-stall a-count must reach coordinate zero. For i>=k, b fixes C_i;
before first entering D the trajectory must traverse at least p-i
a's to C_0. Entering later at D_j, j<k, merely replaces j earlier
a's by j fewer later ones. At least another p a's from C_0 are needed
to reach D_p, proving the second case. These lower counts are attained
without detours. Consequently, when d_i>=1,

    t >= delta_i+(d_i-1)(p+1).                         (4)

If Qu is contained in T and alpha is the first coordinate of A, choose
i=alpha-1-t mod p. Its unstalled coordinate is alpha-1, at the far end
of the complementary interval. At least k=p-s backward steps are needed
to reach A, so d_i>=k. Equation (4) gives

    t >= B+delta_i,       B=(k-1)(p+1).                (5)

Since min_i delta_i=p-k+2, this already forces t>=kp+1. The dependence
of i on t gives the sharper EXACT lower bound

    t>=M_p=(p^2+3p)/2-k.                               (6)

Here is the residue check, including both parities. Write t=kp+u.

* For p=2s,k=s, every 1<=u<=p-1 gives
  i=s-1-u mod p. If i<k, use the first case of (3); otherwise use the
  second. BOTH give B+delta_i=t+1, impossible. Thus t>=kp+p=M_p.
* For p=2s+1,k=s+1, every 1<=u<=s-1 gives i=2s-u>=k, so
  B+delta_i=t+s+2>t. Thus t>=kp+s=M_p. For s=1 the excluded interval
  is empty and the initial bound kp+1 already equals M_p.

All t below kp+1 were excluded independently. This proves (6) for EVERY
word, all rank drops and every strict-subset arrival. At least one b is
also necessary because a alone preserves Q. Hence |u|>=M_p+1.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension--matching-actual-reach-word-and-exact-extension"></a>
#### Matching actual reach word and exact extension

The word

    U_p=b a^M_p                                         (7)

reaches T EXACTLY. For even p=2s, M_p=2s(s+1), with residues 0 mod p
and s mod (p+1). For odd p=2s+1, M_p=2(s+1)^2-1, with residues s mod p
and p mod (p+1). Applying these two rotations to E gives precisely
the two explicit target patterns in the preceding fixed-alphabet proof.
This establishes actual reachability before using (1). Together,

    e(T)=M_p+1=(p^2+2p+2-(p mod 2))/2=n^2/8+O(n).       (8)

At p=7, n15 has e(T)=32>30. This is the first strict 2n violation for
the CANONICAL targets (8) in this family. EVERY universal e<=Cn+d with
fixed C,d fails eventually. A separate finite target at p6,n13 has
e=28>26, checked below; (8) does not claim a maximum over all targets
or a globally smallest binary violation.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension--a-charged-reset-and-a-quadratic-all-endpoint-lower-interval"></a>
#### A charged reset and a quadratic all-endpoint lower interval

On E let d=a^(p+1)b and f=a^p b, retaining their original word costs.
Word d fixes D_0,...,D_(k-1) and moves each C_i forward, eventually
to D_0. After d^(p-k), the whole image is {D_0,...,D_(k-1)}.
On that common image, f sends D_j to D_(j-1) for j>=1 and fixes D_0.
Therefore

    W_p=b d^(p-k) f^(k-1)

resets Q to D_0 with exact FULL length

    |W_p|=1+(p+2)(p-k)+(p+1)(k-1)=p^2+p-k <= (n-1)^2.   (9)

There are no free macro letters: every a,b in each power is charged.
For a lower bound on ANY reset word and ANY endpoint coordinate alpha,
choose i=alpha-1-t mod p in (2). Its trajectory needs at least p-1
stalls to reach that singleton coordinate. Equations (3),(4), minimized
over i, force

    #a >= (p-2)(p+1)+(p-k+2)=p^2-k.

At least one b is necessary, giving the all-parameter interval

    p^2-k+1 <= rt <= p^2+p-k,       rt=n^2/4+O(n).       (10)

The interval width is p-1. Neither endpoint is asserted to be the exact
general reset threshold. The lower argument counts the same original
identity repeatedly; it does not sum stalls of unrelated states.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension--independent-audits-and-research-boundary"></a>
#### Independent audits and research boundary

`direct_binary_image_obstruction.py` retains 69 parameters, p2..65 and
p100,128,256,512,1024, through n2049. The separate
`check_direct_binary_image_obstruction.py` imports no generator, preceding
checker or policy solver. It reconstructs rows, SC, idempotence, rank gap,
the coordinate identity, unique D_p entrance and first-stall counts by
zero/one-cost BFS. Its direct residue calculation checks (6); original-row
composition verifies all charged powers and (9),(10). Twenty-three controls
p2..24 evaluate EVERY original letter of both words literally. Large word
powers retain their full exponents while being evaluated by row composition.

Eleven complete actual-image forward scopes p2..12 contain 276717
vertices; separate ordinary FULL-preimage BFS from each target visits
16978 vertices and matches EVERY extension minimum. The forward searches
include every smaller final image, so strict containment cannot evade
the checks. All reset thresholds lie in (10). Seven corruptions are rejected.

For the additional n13 target use the SAME p6 rows, and

    T_extra={C_0,C_1,C_2,D_0,D_1,D_6}=Q b a^27.

The complete 725-vertex forward graph and separate 263-vertex preimage
search give exact e(T_extra)=28>26. This is separately
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** finite evidence, not an arbitrary-parameter
extension-maximum formula or an unrestricted minimality result.

The exact arbitrary-parameter claims (8),(10) rest on the proof, not on
finite extrapolation. Their priority remains OPEN. The image-extension
quantifiers match the reread [2016 primary Conjecture 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
Two-cycle and idempotent constructions are established architecture; no
publication-level novelty inference is made. The earlier coding lemma
remains independently useful for preserving actual parents in reductions.

This direct binary improvement is continued check 99 with 184 regeneration
commands, preserving the 98-check checkpoint. Only the new generator,
replay and independent checker are run; no full 99-check rerun or formal
proof kernel. Global compatible choices and the unrestricted Cerny square
are still OPEN. One quadratically expensive actual target need not occur
on a best reset chain, and (9) explicitly avoids a Cerny counterexample.

The planned multi-shortcut attack on C_n was screened before computation:
[Reachable-fiber anchoring improves the image rank-profile bound](#direct-attack-anchored-image-profile) already proves that generated-map additions
preserve its image family, weakly decrease e, and cannot lower its actual
seed capacity. Since C_n has e<=n, ANY such additions are already covered
by its anchored square budget. Repeating that search would test a proved
condition. Future shortcut attacks must start outside this budget regime.

<a id="direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy--first-drop-normal-form-and-exact-singleton-policy-propagation"></a>
### First-drop normal form and exact singleton policy propagation

**PROVED on paper for every SC synchronizing DFA with n>=2, every finite alphabet.**
These are structural equalities for actual reachable images and the all-tie
image policy. No new n-only reset upper bound or Cerny proof follows.
Priority of the precise policy equalities remains OPEN. One-step inverse
seeds themselves are established, not a new algorithmic idea.

Use right actions, R={Qv}, and delta(T,S)=min{|w|: T w subset S}.
Assume n=|Q|>=2 throughout. At n=1, rt=P=0 and Cerny's bound is trivial;
the seed set is empty, so none of the nonempty-seed formulas is asserted.
For proper S in R, k=|S|, let e(S)=min_(T in R, |T|>k) delta(T,S).
G(S),W(S) use the minimum/maximum future tail over every T attaining e(S),
with G(Q)=W(Q)=0. Rank jumps and strict terminal subsets are permitted.

<a id="direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy--every-shortest-phase-crosses-the-target-rank-in-its-first-letter"></a>
#### Every shortest phase crosses the target rank in its FIRST letter

If |T|>k and w=xv attains e(S), then |T x|<=k. Otherwise T x is another
ACTUAL image of size >k, and its suffix v transports it into S in e(S)-1
letters, contradicting the definition of e(S). Thus x is nonpermutational
on T. All cardinality losses after that first drop are still allowed.

Define the boundary family

    B_k={U=T x: T in R, |T|>k, x a letter, |U|<=k}.

Put d(U,S)=min{|v|: U v subset S}. Then

    e(S)=1+min_(U in B_k) d(U,S).                       (1)

Indeed, every shortest phase has this boundary form, and every listed
boundary edge is an actual larger-image witness. If d(U,S)=e(S)-1, then
EVERY parent T of that boundary edge is an allowed policy endpoint:
delta(T,S)<=1+d=e(S), and global minimality excludes strict inequality.
Conversely every allowed endpoint supplies such an edge. Consequently
G/W tails are exactly min/max over the parents of winning boundary images.
This is a universal characterization, not merely a selected normal word.

<a id="direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy--singleton-seeds-and-exact-nearest-seed-formulas"></a>
#### Singleton seeds and exact nearest-seed formulas

Let H={p: T x={p} for some T in R, |T|>=2, letter x}. H is nonempty:
the last letter of a shortest reset merges its preceding actual image.
Let D(p,q) be ordinary state-graph distance and

    d(q)=min_(p in H) D(p,q),
    N(q)={p in H: D(p,q)=d(q)}.

Boundary (1) for k=1 gives e({q})=1+d(q). In particular H is EXACTLY
the set of singleton targets with e=1; an ordinary fiber with two states
is not sufficient without a reachable image inside that fiber.

All shortest extension endpoints into q are precisely the actual images
merged in one letter to some p in N(q). Therefore

    G({q})=d(q)+min_(p in N(q)) G({p}),
    W({q})=d(q)+max_(p in N(q)) W({p}).                 (2)

At a seed p, e=1 and G/W are 1 plus min/max tail over its one-letter
merged images; substitution proves both equalities with every tie included.
This implies the global normal form

    P=min_(q in Q) G({q})=min_(p in H) G({p})
     =1+min{G(T): T in R, |T|>=2, T x singleton}.       (3)

Thus an optimal image policy ALWAYS starts with a one-letter phase.
Longer initial singleton phases are unnecessary for the global minimum.
This does not make later image phases optimal reset prefixes or prove a
square budget. It explains why C_n's larger worst singleton values come
from initial state distance, while allowing independent future-tie losses.

In particular a POLICY square failure is equivalent to G(T)>=(n-1)^2
for EVERY actual image T merged by one letter. An actual Cerny counterexample
must satisfy this condition because rt<=P. The converse for rt is not
asserted. This isolates the missing budget on actual kernel-contained images;
it does not make their ordinary reach words or G tails free.

The nearest-seed constraint in (2) is essential. An unrestricted minimum
min_p[G(p)+D(p,q)] is a valid reset-to-q upper witness but can be smaller
than G(q). The retained n4 state-edge obstruction has G(0)=2,G(1)=4 and
D(0,1)=1, while 1 is itself a closer seed. Thus ordinary weighted shortest
state paths do not equal the restricted policy recurrence.

<a id="direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy--largest-seed-is-a-stronger-refuted-optimality-restriction"></a>
#### Largest seed is a stronger, refuted optimality restriction

Let kappa=max{|T|: T in R, T x singleton}. Define

    F_kappa=1+min{G(T): T merged by a letter, |T|=kappa}.

Always P<=F_kappa, but equality is REFUTED at state-minimal n4 over ANY
alphabet, already ternary:

    a=[0,0,0,3], b=[3,0,1,2], c=[3,0,1,3].

Here kappa=3, P=rt=2, F_kappa=4. Qac={3}; its first actual image is
{0,3}, a one-letter merge source. The only maximum source is {0,1,2},
merged by a. It has G=3, so insisting on it pays 4. Full actual reachability,
all distances and words are checked. At n<=3, either a constant letter
gives kappa=n and both costs 1, or every merged image has size 2, so (3)
gives equality. This proves arbitrary-alphabet state minimality.

The binary first failure is n5:

    a=[0,0,0,0,1], b=[4,1,1,2,3], kappa=3,
    P=rt=2, F_kappa=3.

Complete distinct-letter binary covers through n4 exclude earlier binary
failures; unary/duplicate letters cannot be SC synchronizing at n>=2.
Largest-seed square existence F_kappa<=(n-1)^2 remains OPEN. It is stronger
than the original global policy square conjecture, not a proved reduction
preserving optimality.
[An unbounded penalty for insisting on a largest seed](#direct-attack-maximum-seed-penalty-theorem) strengthens this to an unbounded additive
and multiplicative penalty: rt=P=2 but F_kappa=n-2 for every n=6h.
[Inclusion-maximal seeds and antitone policy tails both fail](#direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions) refutes the weaker inclusion-maximal
restriction at arbitrary-alphabet state minimum n5, and antitonicity of G
at state minimum n4. Neither negative statement refutes a square guarantee.

Nor can all future ties be ignored: the retained binary n6 extremal

    a=[0,1,2,4,3,3], b=[1,3,5,0,2,4]

has kappa=2, the ONLY seed target 3, P=rt=25 but W({3})=26. Thus even
largest one-letter seeds can exceed the square under worst ties. This
strengthening is binary-minimal n6 by the complete covers through n5.
The best-policy square conjecture remains intact. A concrete worst-tie
word and phase chain are independently checked, not just a scalar value.

<a id="direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy--attribution-and-limits"></a>
#### Attribution and limits

The image-extension proposal and singleton inverse-search seed convention
are known from [Kisielewicz--Szykula, Sections 3.1 and 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
Their ordinary inverse seed definition and the present actual-image
capacities are not silently identified. The exact all-tie formulas above
are proved here; priority remains OPEN. No new Lean theorem. Complete and
sampled search scopes are recorded separately in the accompanying audit.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--quadratic-actual-image-extension-with-fixed-ternary-and-binary-alphabets"></a>
### Quadratic actual-image extension with fixed ternary and binary alphabets

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for every parameter below.
Every universal linear actual-image extension bound is **REFUTED** even
for strongly connected, irreducibly synchronizing BINARY automata.
The ternary family is additionally simple. Independent finite audits are
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. Priority is **OPEN**; no **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim. The unrestricted Cerny conjecture and global policy square are **OPEN**.

The preceding fold/path obstruction has a growing alphabet. This proof
removes that limitation. Neither family is a Cerny counterexample: explicit
common reset words below satisfy the square. No unrestricted minimum-state
claim, exact reset-threshold formula, or general quadratic reset bound follows.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--the-fixed-ternary-family-and-its-actual-image-boundary"></a>
#### The fixed ternary family and its actual image boundary

Use right actions. For p>=2 let

    Q = C union D,
    C = {C_0,...,C_(p-1)}, D = {D_0,...,D_p}, n=2p+1.

The THREE original letters are

    a: C_i -> C_(i+1 mod p), D_j -> D_(j+1 mod (p+1));
    c: swap C_0 and D_0, fix everything else;
    b: C_i -> C_i, D_j -> C_(j mod p).

Thus a,c are permutations and b is an idempotent of rank p. The two
a-cycles and their c bridge give strong connectivity. Every word containing
b has rank at most p, while every other word is a permutation. The ONLY
actual image larger than any actual p-set is Q. We use exactly the repository
definition

    e(S)=min{|u|: R is actual, |R|>|S|, and Ru is contained in S}.

Strict containment, intermediate rank drops and arbitrary words are allowed.

Put s=floor(p/2), k=p-s=ceil(p/2). Define a contiguous coordinate interval

    A={s,...,p-1} if p is even;
    A={0,...,s-1} if p is odd,

and T=b^-1(A), interpreting A as the corresponding states of C. Explicitly

    p=2s:   T={C_s,...,C_(p-1),D_s,...,D_(p-1)};
    p=2s+1: T={C_0,...,C_(s-1),D_0,...,D_(s-1),D_p}.

In either case |A|=s and |T|=p. An explicit word below reaches T EXACTLY;
therefore T is actual before the larger-image boundary is used, and

    e(T)=min{|u|: Qu is contained in T}.                 (1)

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--a-lower-bound-on-the-number-of-original-as-in-any-entering-word"></a>
#### A lower bound on the number of original a's in ANY entering word

Define a coordinate projection to Z_p by

    pi(C_i)=i, pi(D_j)=j mod p.

Letters b,c preserve pi. Letter a increases pi by one except on the
transition D_p -> D_0, which preserves zero. Call precisely that original
a transition a stall. For the trajectory of an ORIGINAL state C_i in a
word u, let d_i count its stalls and let t be the TOTAL number of a's in u.
Even after trajectories merge, each original trajectory is still defined.
Consequently

    pi(C_i u)=i+t-d_i mod p.                            (2)

Before C_i can first enter D, it must reach C_0 and use c. Its first
entry into D is D_0, so at least (-i mod p) a's precede that entry.
From D_0 at least p a's are needed to FIRST reach D_p: b,c cannot enter
D_p, and before the first visit to D_p every a advances pi by one. The
first visit requires a positive multiple of p a's, hence at least p.
The stall itself uses one more a and returns the state to D_0.
The same argument applies between ANY two stalls of this same trajectory.
Exiting D by b or c cannot shorten it. Thus

    t >= (-i mod p)+d_i(p+1).                           (3)

This counts repeated stalls on ONE original trajectory, not unrelated
stalls distributed over distinct states. It remains valid after collisions.

Let alpha be the first coordinate of A. If Qu is contained in T, (2)
belongs to A for EVERY i. Choose

    i=alpha-1-t mod p.

Before its stalls are subtracted, its final coordinate is alpha-1, at
the far end of the complementary contiguous interval. At least k=p-s
backward steps are needed to reach A, so d_i>=k. Equation (3) implies

    t >= B+(-i mod p),       B=k(p+1).                  (4)

In particular t>=B. The dependence of i on t strengthens this bound:

* If p=2s, write t=B+u. For 0<=u<=p-2, i=p-1-u, so (4) requires
  u>=u+1, impossible. The first possible u is p-1.
* If p=2s+1, for 0<=u<=s-2, i=s-1-u, and (4) requires
  u>=s+2+u, impossible. The first possible u is s-1. When s=1 the
  excluded interval is empty and this is still the same formula.

Both cases give the all-word lower bound

    #a(u)=t >= L_p=(p^2+3p-2)/2.                        (5)

No hypothesis about final rank equality, avoiding b, or an optimal
normal form was used. A reset landing at one state of T is also covered.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--independent-lower-bounds-on-c-and-b-and-a-matching-actual-word"></a>
#### Independent lower bounds on c and b, and a matching actual word

Track the p original C identities which have NOT yet visited D.
Two such identities remain distinct: every original letter is injective
on C. Only c can export one of them into D, and one c exports at most
ONE previously unexported identity. Identities already exported and later
merged with an unexported one do not change this count. At the end, at
most s unexported identities can lie in the s states T intersect C.
Therefore EVERY entering word also satisfies

    #c(u)>=p-s=k.                                      (6)

At least one b is required since a,c are permutations and T is proper.
The three independent counts (5),(6) give

    |u|>=L_p+k+1=ceil(p(p+4)/2).                        (7)

Set M=L_p-k+1 and take the single actual word

    U_p=b (ca)^(k-1) c a^M.                            (8)

After b(ca)^(k-1)c, the image is

    {C_k,...,C_(p-1)} union {D_0,...,D_(k-1)}.

For even p=2s, M=2s(s+1), hence M=0 mod p and M=s mod (p+1).
For odd p=2s+1, M=2(s+1)^2-1, hence M=s mod p and M=p mod (p+1).
The final power of a therefore sends this image EXACTLY onto T in both
cases. It has L_p actual a's, k actual c's and one actual b. This proves
T's actual reachability and attains (7), establishing the exact theorem

    e(T)=ceil(p(p+4)/2),        n=2p+1.                 (9)

At p=5, n=11 and e(T)=23>2n=22. This is the first strict 2n violation
IN THIS specified ternary family, not an unrestricted minimum-state result.
Equation (9) is n^2/8+O(n), so it violates EVERY fixed linear coefficient
and additive slack with a fixed three-letter alphabet.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--a-charged-square-reset-and-the-simpleirreducible-boundary"></a>
#### A charged square reset and the simple/irreducible boundary

On C, the actual word

    d=c a^(p+1) b

acts as C_0 -> C_0 and C_i -> C_(i+1 mod p) for i>=1. It is rooted
at C_0 with height p-1. Hence

    R_p=b d^(p-1)

resets Q to C_0 with its FULL original length

    |R_p|=1+(p+3)(p-1)=p^2+2p-2 <= (n-1)^2.           (10)

This is an upper bound, not a claimed exact reset threshold. Deleting b
leaves permutations; deleting c preserves C with a,b acting there as
permutations; deleting a preserves distinct C identities (only C_0 can
visit D_0, whose b-image is C_0). Thus every proper subalphabet is
nonsynchronizing: the ternary family is irreducibly synchronizing.

Since p,p+1 are coprime, conjugates of the single c by actual powers of a
are every cross transposition C_i <-> D_j. Their abstract group generates
S_n, so the DFA is simple. For image membership, this also implies that
every k-set, 1<=k<=p, is actual: transport an actual k-set to one with
exactly one b-kernel pair and distinct remaining b-values, apply b to
drop one rank, and transport again. Thus the complete actual family is

    {Q} union {S:1<=|S|<=p}.

Abstract group membership is used ONLY for existence of these images and
absence of nontrivial congruences. No such conjugate or inverse is charged
as a free letter in (8),(10). All length bounds use original a,b,c.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--a-binary-encoding-preserving-the-actual-image-predicate"></a>
#### A binary encoding preserving the actual-image predicate

Here is a general coding lemma, proved explicitly because image reachability
and larger-parent capacity must survive the alphabet reduction. Let an
original alphabet be x_0,...,x_(h-1), h>=2, and assume union_i Qx_i=Q.
This assumption holds for every strongly connected DFA with n>=2.
On Q'=Q x {0,...,h-1} use TWO original letters

    0:(q,i) -> (q,i+1 mod h);
    1:(q,i) -> (q x_i,0).

Before the first 1, the full image is Q'. That first 1 has image Q x {0}
because of the stated union condition. Every later actual image is pure,
R x {i}, where R is an original actual image. Conversely, starting with
that first 1, codes 0^j 1 realize every original x_j on a pure selector-0
image, and trailing 0's realize every selector. Thus EXACTLY

    R_binary={Q'} union {R x {i}:R original actual, 0<=i<h}.             (11)

For a proper original actual target S, every larger binary actual source
is either full Q' or a pure R x {i} with |R|>|S|. A word from a pure
source decodes its successive 1's into an actual original word Ru contained
in S. From the full source its first 1 produces Q x {0}; the remaining
decoded word must take this larger original actual source into S. Therefore

    e_binary(S x {0})>=e_original(S).                  (12)

There is also an exact weighted characterization. Pure R x {i} is an
actual source for EVERY selector i, so the first decoded letter can be
selected with one 1 and no preceding 0. After every 1 the selector is 0;
the next x_j costs exactly j+1 original binary letters. Superfluous selector
cycles and trailing 0's cannot improve entry into selector 0. Starting
from Q' cannot beat the already eligible source Q x {0}. Consequently

    e_binary(S x {0})=
      min [1+sum_(ell=2)^m(index(x_ell)+1)],             (13)

where the minimum is over ALL original actual R with |R|>|S| and ALL
nonempty original words x_1...x_m transporting R into S. This is an exact
local phase-cost identity, not a statement about the full reset history.
It also gives e_binary<=1+h(e_original-1). All parent cardinalities in
(11)--(13) are actual; mixed nonactual selector sets are never added as sources.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--exact-fixed-binary-quadratic-obstruction"></a>
#### Exact fixed binary quadratic obstruction

Apply this coding with

    h=3,       x_0=c, x_1=b, x_2=a,       N=3(2p+1)=6p+3,
    T'=T x {0}.

Equation (11) shows that the ONLY actual sources larger than |T'|=p
are Q' and Q x {0},Q x {1},Q x {2}. In (13) the original source is Q.
Every original prefix before the first b consists of permutations and
can be deleted: it preserves Q. The corresponding binary prefix can be
deleted by beginning instead at the already actual source Q x {1};
the first 1 then executes b at cost one. All subsequent a,c,b cost
3,1,2 respectively. Bounds (5),(6) therefore give

    e_binary(T') >= 3L_p+k+1.

Encode (8) starting from Q x {1}. Its first b costs one and its remaining
letters use c -> 1 and a -> 001, attaining exactly that bound. Hence

    e_binary(T')=3(p^2+3p-2)/2+ceil(p/2)+1
                =(3p^2+10p-4+(p mod 2))/2
                =N^2/24+O(N).                         (14)

T' is actual: from Q', first apply 10 and then this entering word.
The FULL reachability word has length e_binary(T')+2. The two-letter
word 10 alone reaches the actual larger source Q x {1}; these costs are
not silently erased from any whole reset construction.

For p=6, N=39 and exact e_binary(T')=82>78=2N. This is the first strict
2N violation IN THIS encoded family. No global binary minimum is claimed.
Every fixed C,d fails eventually in (14), even restricted to binary DFAs.

The binary DFA is SC: select original letters by 0's and 1, follow any
original state path, then rotate to the desired selector. A charged
whole reset is the first 1 followed by the encoded R_p, using codes
c -> 1, b -> 01, a -> 001. Its length is

    3+(3p+6)(p-1)=3p^2+3p-3 <= (N-1)^2.               (15)

Letter 0 is a permutation. After the first unary 1, its image is Q x {0},
and all further 1's act there by the permutation c. Neither unary alphabet
synchronizes; the binary family is irreducibly synchronizing. No simple
binary claim is made: its selector partition is a congruence.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--relation-to-the-open-proof-route-and-literature"></a>
#### Relation to the open proof route and literature

[Kisielewicz--Szykula 2016, Section 3.1, Conjecture 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268)
uses precisely an actual image target and a preimage containing a larger
actual image. The primary definition was reread in this continuation.
The growing-alphabet family already refutes its unrestricted formulation;
(9),(14) remove the remaining fixed-alphabet and binary qualifications.
Two-cycle constructions and alphabet reductions are established ideas.
Priority of these precise families, exact costs and the explicit coding
identity remains OPEN; absence of a search hit is not a novelty proof.

The potential compatibility route must now tolerate QUADRATIC individual
phases even on binary SC irreducibly synchronizing inputs. This does not
prove a global policy square failure, and the actual reset words (10),(15)
leave the Cerny conjecture unthreatened. We do not promote this method
obstruction to a general reset theorem or stop the research objective here.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension--verification-and-reproducibility-boundary"></a>
#### Verification and reproducibility boundary

`two_cycle_image_obstruction.py` saves 69 controls, p2..65 and
p100,128,256,512,1024, through ternary n2049 and binary N6147.
`check_two_cycle_image_obstruction.py` imports neither that generator
nor any preceding policy solver. It reconstructs original rows, the
coordinate identity, C-injectivity/export boundary, and first-stall
distances by independent zero/one-cost BFS. It checks the small residue
inequality giving (5), evaluates the charged original word powers, and
checks both common resets and actual target words. Fifteen controls p2..16
add complete LETTER-BY-LETTER transformation evaluation. Larger powers
are evaluated from original-row compositions, with their full exponents
charged; they are not free new letters.

Ordinary-set full forward scopes p2..9 use 349520 ternary vertices;
independent full-preimage target BFS uses 89655 visited vertices. Binary
scopes p2..8 use 262135 full forward vertices and independently the same
count from ALL actual larger sources; pure/mixed image classification is
compared exactly. Five binary full-preimage target scopes p2..6 use 4896
vertices. All arriving subsets, including strict containment, participate
in these BFS minima. Seven deliberately corrupted fields/rows are rejected.

The arbitrary-parameter results follow from the proof, not extrapolation
of these finite scopes. The preceding 97-check record is preserved;
this independent check continues it as number 98. One deterministic
generator/replay raises the regeneration registry to 183 commands.
No full 98-check rerun, proof kernel, or unrestricted Cerny proof is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension--a-paid-n-extension-theorem-for-a-fixed-common-defect-root"></a>
### A paid n-extension theorem for a fixed common defect root

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), arbitrary n and alphabet under the
explicit hypotheses below.** This proves the Cerny square for this
subclass, including inputs with several cycles in EVERY original letter.
No novelty or FORMALLY VERIFIED claim; priority is OPEN. The unrestricted
Cerny conjecture and the general almost-circular class remain **OPEN**.

The familiar seed-plus-extension framework is attributed to the standard
extension approach reviewed in
[Volkov2022, Section3.4](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=rm&paperid=10005&what=fullteng).
The paid cycle-routing argument below is written and audited directly
here. No cited source is asserted to prove precisely this subclass.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension--hypotheses-and-theorem"></a>
#### Hypotheses and theorem

Let Q have n>=2 states, r!=s. There is an ORIGINAL permutation letter
b with b(r)=s. Let R be its cycle containing r and s, p=|R|.
Every original letter is of one of these types:

1. A permutation preserving R as a SET (including b).
2. A singular letter f with f(r)=f(s)=s, whose restriction to Q\{r}
   is a permutation fixing s. Thus its omitted state is r, its only
   kernel pair is{r,s}, and its defect root s is FIXED.

At least one singular letter is present. Assume the original DFA is
strongly connected. Then EVERY nonempty proper subset U of Q admits
an ORIGINAL word w, |w|<=n, such that

    |U w^-1|=|U|+1.                                      (1)

Consequently there is ONE original reset word of length at most

    1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2.                                   (2)

The completion of f fixing r is a permutation fixing r,s, but is NOT
an available original operation. All words below use only original
letters and nonnegative powers of ORIGINAL b. The notation w^-1
means a full preimage of a set, never an inverse word.

For binary a,b the condition reduces to a fixed defect root s and the
adjacent b edge r->s. There is no assumption that a or b is one-cluster,
nor that ab is almost circular. In the previous almost-circular normal
form, this proves the square whenever A(1)=1. Moving-root cases, including
the retained Kari example, are outside the theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension--exact-cardinality-changes"></a>
#### Exact cardinality changes

For every subset V, a singular letter has the literal identity

    |V f^-1|-|V| = 1_V(s)-1_V(r).                        (3)

Indeed every image point except s has one preimage, s has two, and r
has none. A permutation has change zero.

If V contains ALL of R or NONE of R, applying f^-1 leaves the total
cardinality unchanged and preserves the common membership of r,s:
both copy membership of s. A permitted permutation also leaves the
whole-root membership unchanged. Powers of b preserve each b-cycle.
Thus preparatory operations while R is uniform have zero net cost in
cardinality; they may move membership between the other cycles.

If R is mixed, its cyclic binary membership pattern has a transition
from0 to1. Because b(r)=s, for some0<=k<p,

    b^k(r) notin V,     b^k(s) in V.

For ANY singular f, the original word f b^k, cost k+1<=p, has a full
preimage larger by EXACTLY one, by(3). This step may rearrange other
cycles, which is harmless because(1) applies afresh to every subset.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension--route-a-missing-point-or-an-existing-point-into-r"></a>
#### Route a missing point or an existing point into R

Contract each b-cycle to one vertex. Add a directed edge I->J whenever
some ORIGINAL letter g maps a state x in I to y in J. The resulting
cycle graph is strongly connected because the original DFA is. Let
d(I) be shortest directed distance from R in this FIXED graph.

Suppose V contains all of R. Select a b-cycle J containing a missing
point whose distance d(J)>0 is MINIMAL among such cycles. All cycles
at smaller distance are full. Choose an edge I->J on a shortest path,
with d(I)=d(J)-1 and literal g(x)=y, x in I, y in J.
Some0<=k<|J| sends y under b^k to a missing point of J. Preimage by
the ORIGINAL word g b^k therefore removes x from the full cycle I.
This word costs k+1<=|J|. Its cardinality change is ZERO, since R was
full after rotating by b. If g is a permitted permutation, it preserves
R; if g is singular, r,s remain members. Thus R cannot become empty:
it is either still full, or becomes mixed and preparation stops.
If it remains full, the new minimum distance to a cycle with a missing
point is at most d(J)-1, STRICTLY less than before.

If V contains none of R, perform the same construction with an EXISTING
point in a cycle of minimum distance. All nearer cycles are empty.
The preimage puts x into I, preserves total cardinality, and keeps r,s
absent. Hence R remains empty or becomes mixed; if it stays empty,
the minimum distance to an occupied cycle strictly decreases.

In either case the selected distances strictly decrease, so a b-cycle
is charged AT MOST ONCE. No selected cycle is R. Therefore ALL
preparation costs together at most

    sum_{selected J}|J| <= n-p.                          (4)

Preparation terminates with R mixed. The final growth step costs at
most p. Combining(4) with that step gives one actual word of cost at
most n and net growth EXACTLY one. Word factors are prepended in the
order of taking preimages; all cardinality calculations concern ONE
compatible original word. This proves(1).

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension--the-compatible-square-and-connectivity-scope"></a>
#### The compatible square and connectivity scope

For any singular original f, {s} f^-1={r,s}, cost1. Apply(1) exactly
n-2 times, prepending each actual extension word to the accumulated
word. The final full preimage is Q, so the accumulated word resets
all states to s and obeys(2). This is a constructive unconditional
subclass theorem, not a collection of unrelated pair compressions.

Within the specified letter types, every edge of every permutation is
on a directed cycle. All edges of a singular f outside its tail are
also on cycles, and its exceptional edge r->s lies on the b-cycle.
Thus every edge of the underlying support is on a directed cycle;
its SCCs have no edges between them. A synchronizing input of this
type must consequently already be strongly connected. Therefore(2)
also applies to EVERY synchronizing input of the stated type without
needing to add strong connectivity as a separate assumption.

The n bound on arbitrary-subset extension is sharp: on ordinary Cerny,
U={r} needs the word f b^(n-1) of cost n. This is the known circular
boundary, not a new ordinary-family threshold.

<a id="direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension--essential-boundary-and-independent-finite-controls"></a>
#### Essential boundary and independent finite controls

Dropping the FIXED-root condition is **REFUTED for n-extensibility**.
At n4 take

    a=[2,2,1,3], b=[1,3,2,0], U={0,1,3}.

Here a has rank3 and level1, b(0)=1, ab is almost circular, and the
original DFA is SC. But a's defect root2 is not fixed; a(1)=2.
The exact minimum extension length of U is6>4. A positive-cost
independent Bellman certificate covers ALL16 subsets, and a literal
length6 word attains it. This refutes the proposed stronger extension
lemma without that hypothesis, not Cerny: the ordinary reset threshold
is9. It also identifies the proof failure: before routing, uniform
root membership need not make(3) zero, and the root can lose points.

The generator retains ALL159 binary pairs of these types at n2..5,
including nonsynchronizing inputs, plus sampled binary/multiple-letter
inputs and deep cycle chains through n257. The independent checker
imports no generator/old solver. It verifies the literal hypotheses,
strong connectivity, complete finite pair coverage, ALL nonempty proper
subsets on every retained n<=10 input, sampled larger subsets, exact
preimage words, each strict distance decrease, distinct selected-cycle
cost charges, net growth and ONE reset word. The finite witnesses do
not establish the all-n theorem; the proof above does. No formal claim.

Completed independent controls:219 inputs,ALL159 binary pairs n2..5,
146 SC inputs,94 with multicycle b,21 multiple-letter inputs,16411
proper-subset controls (645 root-empty,679 root-full,15087 mixed),
127 maximum preparation steps,2247092 literal particle/letter controls,
30 counter Bellman edges and eight rejected corruptions. The n4
ordinary rt9 is already certified in the complete normal-form audit
almost_circular_returns.json / check_almost_circular_returns.py.

The preceding sampled brute-force BFS on8927 valid binary inputs at
n4..10 checked2914082 subsets and found no extension above n. Its
negative coverage is only **EXPLORATORY** (terminal output, not an
independent complete implementation audit); it is not used as proof.

The hard almost-circular case A(1)!=1 remains OPEN at the square.
Indeed the n4 obstruction shows why a universal n-extension route
cannot simply drop the fixed point. Continue on compatible amortized
growth or another general route after saving this subclass result.

Later [Coprime root displacement, and a necessary amortized boundary](#direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement) weakens b(r)=s to a coprime
displacement of r,s on the SAME original b-cycle. It proves the same
all-n/alphabet paid n-extension and compatible square. Removing that
coprimality condition is separately REFUTED even on the size2 seed at
fixed-root SC sync n5 (minimum extension6>5, ordinary rt13<16).

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-image-extension--reachable-image-extension-and-its-exact-capacity-obstruction"></a>
### Reachable image extension and its exact capacity obstruction

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

The unrestricted Cerny conjecture and a universal linear image-extension
bound remain **OPEN in this work**. No quadratic upper bound is established.
Finite statements below are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. The capacity
reformulation and conditional implication have direct paper proofs; neither
is claimed as a new bound. No new Lean result.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension--definition-and-exact-reformulation"></a>
#### Definition and exact reformulation

Let R={Qv:v in Sigma*} be the actual reachable image family. For X subset Q,
define rho(X)=max{|T|:T in R, T subset X}, taking zero for an empty family.
For a proper nonempty reachable S, define

    e(S)=min{|u|: rho(Su^-1)>|S|}.

Equivalently, e(S) is the shortest transport word sending a larger reachable
image into S. Preimages may lose cardinality during that word. No condition
S subset Su^-1, nor equality Tu=S, is imposed.

The family R is forward closed. Capacity is certified on the subset lattice:

    rho(empty)=0,
    rho(X)=max(|X| if X in R else 0, max_{q in X} rho(X\{q})).

This identity follows by separating T=X from proper reachable T subset X;
any proper T omits some q. It uniquely determines capacity by induction.
For fixed k, the preimage graph has goals rho(X)>k. Its distance from S
with |S|=k equals e(S). Positive distance values satisfy the Bellman equality,
with zero at goals and -1 at the empty set. This yields a complete finite
certificate. It is not a universal upper potential.

If e(S)<=Cn for every proper reachable S in every strongly connected
synchronizing n-state DFA, choose any reachable singleton. Repeatedly pick
a larger reachable T and u with Tu subset S, and prepend u to the current
suffix resetting S. Cardinality increases strictly at each choice; at most
n-1 choices reach Q. This gives reset length <=Cn(n-1). Full reach words
for T are needed to certify membership in R but are not appended to the
reset suffix. This is why a universal linear image-extension theorem would
give a quadratic bound. It does not prove such a theorem.

The underlying conjecture and this conditional route are known:
[Kisielewicz--Szykula (2016), Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
Their lower-bound family requires asymptotic coefficient at least 3/2.
Priority of the particular finite witnesses retained here is **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension--five-state-obstruction-to-ceil3n2"></a>
#### Five-state obstruction to ceil(3n/2)

Use states 0,...,4 and right actions with

    a=[0,0,2,2,4], b=[1,2,3,4,0].

The reachable pair S={3,4} has exact image-extension cost 10. The ten-letter
word abbbbabbbb sends the reachable triple T={0,1,3}=Qab into S. The
independently checked full-Q reach word for S is stored literally in the
certificate; b is a full cycle, and full-Q reachability of a singleton
establishes synchronization. Exhaustive independent inverse BFS from S
finds no shorter preimage containing any reachable set of size at least 3.
Thus e(S)=10>ceil(15/2)=8, and an exact bound e(S)<=Cn for all n would
require **C>=2**, already from this finite example. This does not imply an
asymptotic coefficient lower bound 2 with additive corrections.

The proposal e(S)<=ceil(3n/2) is **REFUTED** at binary-minimal n=5.
Complete binary tests give maxima 3 at n=3, 6 at n=4, 10 at n=5 and 11 at
n=6. The n=3 value and n=2 bound are separately checked; no arbitrary-
alphabet minimality claim is made. All five/six-state first-map counts are
covering counts with overlap, not unique isomorphism class counts.

Exact inputs, full preimage Bellman values, capacities, endpoint words and
independent checks are in data/image_extension_n5/, data/image_extension_n6/
and data/image_extension_checks.json. No conclusion about the general
e(S)<=2n proposal follows from the absence of finite counterexamples.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension--structural-lesson-and-remaining-route"></a>
#### Structural lesson and remaining route

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension--exact-top-rank-boundary-proved-elementary-reconstruction"></a>
##### Exact top-rank boundary (PROVED, elementary reconstruction)

For every reachable (n-1)-image S, e(S)<=n, over any finite alphabet.
Before a word first reaches rank n-1, permutation letters leave Q unchanged,
so an initial rank-n-1 letter suffices. A shortest subsequent path inside
that rank layer has at most n-1 edges, since there are only n possible
(n-1)-subsets. Thus some full-Q word of length <=n reaches S; taking T=Q
proves the bound. Synchronization and strong connectivity are not needed
for this local statement. This is not a new asymptotic bound.

The constant is sharp for every n>=2. In C_n, let a be q->q+1 modulo n,
and b fix all states except n-1->0. Take S=Q\{n-2}. The word ba^(n-1)
reaches S and has length n. Any word with A<n-1 occurrences of a has its
holes contained in {n-1,0,...,A-1}; induction handles a by rotation, and b
by retaining holes other than 0,n-1 and introducing n-1 (a hole at 0 after
b requires both old holes 0,n-1, hence A>=1). The hole n-2 is absent.
An avoiding word must contain b and at least n-1 copies of a, so its
length is >=n. Since Q is the only reachable image larger than S, e(S)=n.
Independent short-image BFS checks n=2,...,12 in top_rank_boundary.py.

Thus the first inverse image phase at top rank has a linear boundary;
the unresolved image-extension difficulty lies in lower reachable ranks.

Ordinary inverse cardinality can grow before capacity grows. In the
five-state example, the gap in the reachable ranks (no four-state image)
and the geometry of reachable triples make that difference observable.
This is a concrete obstacle to applying an arbitrary-preimage extension
lemma without controlling reachable images.

Capacity need not be submodular: take a constant letter and a three-cycle
on three states. The reachable images are Q and all singletons. For
X={0,1}, Y={1,2}, rho(X)+rho(Y)=2, while rho(X union Y)+rho(X intersect Y)=4.
Thus rho is not a matroid rank function in general. That observation does
not rule out a different dimension or charging argument.

The four tested parameter families and random/adversarial runs are finite
data, not formulas or proof of a general linear bound. The promising open
target is a short preimage path with capacity growth, or an amortized
sequence of such paths whose full costs are quadratic. A failed local
constant does not close that target.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-native-search"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-native-search--direct-adversarial-tests-of-a-precise-linear-capacity-target"></a>
### Direct adversarial tests of a precise linear-capacity target

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**CONJECTURED / OPEN:** in every strongly connected synchronizing DFA,
every nonempty proper reachable image S satisfies e(S)<=2n, where

    e(S)=min{|u|: a reachable T has |T|>|S| and Tu subset S}.

The larger image may be Q; a preimage may first lose cardinality. This
candidate is stronger than the known conjecture that some universal linear
constant exists. It is not necessary for the Cerny square bound. The saved

without additive slack. Finite tests do not establish any uniform constant.

Complete binary image-extension coverage through n=6 has maxima 2,3,6,10,11.
The new dedicated native objective maximizes e over ALL proper reachable
images, rather than maximizing reset threshold or global policy cost. It

| n | binary frozen seeds | mutation proposals | SC synchronizing proposals | max e observed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 779 | 30000 | 23397 | 16 |
| 11 | 856 | 30000 | 23123 | 18 |

The n11 seeds explicitly include the alternating-folding family and the
