<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-policy"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-policy--shortest-image-extension-policy-a-surviving-compatibility-target"></a>
### Shortest image-extension policy: a surviving compatibility target

Status: universal square guarantee **CONJECTURED**, not proved. The finite
checks below are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. No unrestricted reset bound
or Lean result follows. This is distinct from ordinary inverse greedy,
which already fails a square guarantee at four states.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-policy--precise-policy"></a>
#### Precise policy

Let R be the full Q-reachable image family and e(S) the cost from
[Reachable image extension and its exact capacity obstruction](#direct-attack-image-extension). For proper reachable S, the allowed next images are

    E(S)={T in R: |T|>|S| and exists u, |u|=e(S), Tu subset S}.

All shortest words and all such images are permitted, including proper
reachable subsets of the whole inverse image. Set G(Q)=0 and

    G(S)=e(S)+min_{T in E(S)} G(T).

The minimum policy cost is min_q G({q}). Strong connectivity and
synchronization ensure every singleton is reachable. Cardinality strictly
increases along every policy phase, so the recurrence is acyclic. A chain
starting from a singleton gives an actual reset word by prepending each
phase word, in the correct right-action order.

The open proposal is min_q G({q})<=(n-1)^2 for every strongly connected
synchronizing n-state DFA over any finite alphabet. We do not claim that
every choice of ties satisfies the bound, or that G equals the exact reset
distance. The latter is already false on stored examples (largest saved
gap is 15 among the retained inputs, not a global maximum).
For n=1, G(Q)=0 handles the singleton endpoint without an extension phase.

The unrestricted image-extension conjecture requests a linear e(S) for
every image; this policy target only requests a compatible chain whose
total cost fits the square. Neither implication has been proved from the
other. A local Cn bound with C>=2 would give a different quadratic constant.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-policy--exact-finite-evidence"></a>
#### Exact finite evidence

Complete distinct-letter binary coverage at five states checks 146,828
first-map inputs, including 32,588 strongly connected synchronizing inputs.
The maximum minimum policy cost is 16 and no square failure occurs.

At six states, 6,065,150 first-map inputs include 1,122,529 strongly
connected synchronizing inputs. For 1,116,592 the simple sum

    sum_{k=1}^{n-1} max{e(S): S in R, |S|=k}

is <=25 (empty ranks contribute zero). It bounds every policy because
phases strictly increase cardinality and visit each rank at most once.
The remaining 5,937 inputs have their complete all-tie recurrence solved;
their maximum minimum cost is 25. Thus the best policy square guarantee
holds for the complete binary six-state range. These are overlapping
covering counts, not counts of unique isomorphism classes. Repeated-letter
cases reduce to unary and cannot be both strongly connected and
synchronizing at n>=2.

The previously retained six-state extremals of reset thresholds 25,25,23,23
all admit image policies of exactly those lengths. This observation does
not characterize all extremals. For C6 the maximum over initial singletons
costs 30; at a FIXED singleton q both extension-choice extrema equal 25+q.
Thus 30 refutes arbitrary initial-singleton choice, not extension ties
after fixing the best singleton. [Exact image-policy costs on the Cerny family](#direct-attack-circular-image-policy-theorem) proves
this distinction for every C_n.

Seven/eight-state sampled rank-one-defect neighborhoods have maximum
minimum costs 36 and 49, respectively, with no failure found. These are
only 5,000 and 3,000 proposed mutations. Further alphabet and rank-defect
checks are recorded separately in data/image_extension_policy*/summary.json;
absence of a sampled counterexample proves no general statement.

The four-state exhaustive ternary run checks 2,763,520 distinct-letter
inputs, including 1,825,392 synchronizing strongly connected inputs.
Its rank-sum shortcut covers 1,802,064; the other 23,328 have exact policy
minimum <=9. Binary cases cover repeated letters in a ternary input.
A separate sample of 20,000 six-state ternary inputs has 14,773 SC
synchronizing inputs, all with rank sum <=24. That sample is not a cover.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-policy--necessary-condition-for-a-cerny-counterexample"></a>
#### Necessary condition for a Cerny counterexample

The explicit policy construction proves rt(A)<=min_q G({q})<=U_image(A),
where U_image is the rank sum above. Hence a strongly connected
counterexample to the square bound must have U_image>(n-1)^2, and in
fact its minimum policy cost must exceed the square. This is an exact
automaton-dependent restriction, not a closed-form general bound. The
complete six-state binary rank-sum test eliminates 1,116,592 of the
1,122,529 SC synchronizing covering inputs before solving exact policies.
No contradiction for unbounded state size has been derived.

<a id="direct-attack-image-extension-policy--independent-verification-and-the-unresolved-proof-step"></a>
#### Independent verification and the unresolved proof step

The generator computes transport distances on the actual forward image
graph, allowing Tu to be a proper subset of S. The independent checker
instead performs inverse ordinary-set BFS from each S until the first
preimages containing larger reachable images, collects every shortest
endpoint, and solves the opposite-direction recurrence. Stored explicit
full-Q words agree with the computed minimum policy lengths. Deliberate
reset-word corruption is rejected.

The missing proof is a global compatible-choice bound for G. The local
e(S) can exceed 3n/2, inverse image capacity is not submodular, and G need
not equal optimal reset distance. It is not legitimate to replace the
all-tie minimum by an arbitrary shortest extension or by an unproved rank
potential. The complete computations identify a candidate to attack;
they do not certify its quantifiers for larger n or arbitrary alphabets.

The stronger local G(S)<=n(n-|S|) induction has now failed at binary-minimal
n=5, and capacity-based proper union transfer fails at state-minimal n=3.
See [Local rank potential and union transfer](#direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction). These failures leave the global
singleton minimum conjecture open. The restricted permutation-plus-corank-one
binary cover and broader exact searches are recorded in [Exact native image-policy search](#direct-attack-native-image-policy-audit).

<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction--proper-images-need-not-be-hereditary-even-with-a-unit-defect-letter"></a>
### Proper images need not be hereditary, even with a unit-defect letter

**PROVED on paper; priority OPEN.** The alternating-family extension
proof relies on every nonempty subset of each template being reachable.
That property is not universal, even for binary SC synchronizing
automata with one permutation and one rank-(n-1) letter.

<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction--an-infinite-unit-defect-family"></a>
#### An infinite unit-defect family

For every l>=3 put A={0,...,l-1}, B={l,l+1}, C={l+2}, n=l+3.
Let a cycle A, exchange the two B states, and fix C. Define b by

    b(0)=l, b(1)=l+1, b(i)=i-1 (2<=i<l),
    b(l)=b(l+1)=l+2, b(l+2)=l-1.

The only missing image of b is 0; its only double fiber is B.
Thus b has rank n-1. V=Q\{0}=Qb is reachable, but its subset
T=Q\{0,l+2}, of size n-2, is unreachable.

<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction--strong-connectivity-and-synchronization"></a>
##### Strong connectivity and synchronization

The a-cycles connect each of A,B,C internally. The b connections
A to B, B to C, and C to A prove SC.
Every pair can be synchronized:

* B-B is merged by b.
* B-C becomes A-C under b.
* A-C: rotate the A point to l-1, then apply b. The result is the
  adjacent A pair {l-2,l-1}. Apply a^2 b^2 to merge it through B.
* A-B: rotate the A point to any nongate in A\{0,1}; b gives A-C.
* A-A: some rotation puts exactly one point in {0,1}, so b gives A-B.
  Such a rotation exists because the consecutive gate pair {0,1}
  has no nontrivial cyclic period when l>=3. If membership of the two
  moving points always agreed, their nonzero displacement would be
  such a period. The previous cases finish the pair.

Sequentially merging pairs in the current full-Q image gives an actual
reset word. This proves synchronization without asserting its exact rt.

<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction--high-rank-hole-invariant"></a>
##### High-rank hole invariant

Write the holes as H=Q\image. Under a they rotate within A,B,C.
Under b the holes are

    {0} union {y in Qb: b^-1(y) subset H}.

While |H|=1, it lies in A: after the first b the hole is 0, a keeps
it in A, and another b either lowers rank or leaves that scope.
When corank first reaches 2, H={0,b(q)} for an A point q, hence has
an A point and no C point. At corank 2, a preserves that property.
For a rank-preserving b step, 0 remains a hole. C can be absent from
the image only if BOTH B states are holes, but the invariant has an
A hole, so that cannot happen. Any extra rank drop is permanent.
Thus every reachable rank-(n-2) image still contains C, whereas T does
not. This proves nonreachability for every l>=3.

The infinite family starts at six states; it is not state-minimal for
the restricted property (the four-state witness below is). The instance
at six states is a=[1,2,0,4,3,5],
b=[3,4,1,5,5,2]. Independent transition-closed high-rank certificates
and pair Bellman/reset checks cover the saved parameter instances.

<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction--state-minimal-failure-at-four-states-also-with-a-unit-defect-letter"></a>
#### State-minimal failure at four states, also with a unit-defect letter

Take a=[1,0,3,2], b=[1,2,1,3]. Here a is a permutation, b has rank 3.
The a-cycles {0,1} and {2,3} are connected in both directions by
b(1)=2 and b(2)=1, proving strong connectivity.
The complete image family consists of Q, the triples {1,2,3}, {0,2,3},
the pairs {0,2}, {1,3}, {2,3}, and all four singletons. This list is
transition-closed; the triples are Qb and Qba, the pairs arise by bab,
baba and babb, and babab resets Q to 1. Strong connectivity then makes
all four singletons reachable. Thus it is exactly the image family.
The proper reachable V={0,2,3} contains unreachable T={0,3}.
This gives a permutation/unit-defect binary failure at n=4.

The fast example a=[0,0,0,0], b=[1,2,3,1] is SC synchronizing.
Its image family is Q, {1,2,3}, and the four singletons. No pair is
reachable, so proper-image heredity fails. At n<=3 every proper image
has size <=2, and SC synchronization makes every singleton reachable;
therefore n=4 is minimal over any alphabet for this precise property.
The constant-letter example is retained separately. The new four-state
unit-defect example and the infinite family demonstrate the failure while
every nonpermutation letter has rank n-1. The n<=3 argument proves n=4
minimal over any alphabet and hence also in this restricted binary class.

<a id="direct-attack-image-heredity-obstruction--what-a-template-extension-certificate-actually-requires"></a>
#### What a template extension certificate actually requires

Suppose equal-size reachable templates V,W have all nonempty subsets
of V reachable. If an actual word u maps V onto W\{h}, has a double
fiber at d in W and singleton other fibers, then every S subset W
with h outside S and d inside S has a larger reachable predecessor
V intersect Su^-1, of size |S|+1. Its transport cost is |u|.
A strongly connected directed graph of such arcs h to d gives an
extension for every nonempty proper S subset W, by its incoming cut.
This is a valid conditional counting/word certificate. It supplies no
universal template-heredity assumption or universal bound on arc costs.
The alternating-family proof verifies these hypotheses with explicit
words; the family here defeats a direct unrestricted extrapolation.

<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction--local-rank-potential-and-union-transfer"></a>
### Local rank potential and union transfer

These claims concern G from [Shortest image-extension policy: a surviving compatibility target](#direct-attack-image-extension-policy). Neither refutes
the Cerny bound or the proposed min_q G({q})<=(n-1)^2 guarantee.

<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction--i3-every-reachable-s-has-gsnn-s--refuted"></a>
#### I3: every reachable S has G(S)<=n(n-|S|) — REFUTED

The binary five-state example is

    a=[0,2,3,4,1], b=[1,0,0,4,3], S={2,3,4}.

It is SC and synchronizing, and S is Q-reachable. Exact image-extension
cost e(S)=8; the best shortest-extension policy costs G(S)=11>10.
An optimal chain chooses T={0,1,2,3} with transport u=ba^3ba^3 into S,
then Q with transport v=ba^2 into T. The combined word is vu, not uv,
under right action. Every shortest-extension tie is included in the
lower-bound calculation. The shortest full-Q word into S also costs 11.
Its reset threshold is 11 and its minimum singleton policy is 13<=16.

Complete binary first-map covers at n=2,3,4 check 9,182,4845 overlapping
inputs with no violation. Thus n=5 is binary-minimal in this SC scope;
identical letters are unary and cannot be SC synchronizing at n>=2.
The complete four-state three-letter cover also passes (2763520 inputs).
No arbitrary-alphabet five-state minimality is asserted. Searches at
n=5 and n=6 STOP upon the first local violation and are not complete.

The six-state example is

    a=[0,1,3,4,5,2], b=[1,2,0,0,5,4], S={3,4,5}.

Here e(S)=9 and G(S)=9+7+3=19>18. Optimal full-Q transport into S
costs 16; reset threshold is 18 and minimum singleton policy is 23<=25.
This also separates shortest-phase policy cost from optimal transport.
Saved arrays are independently checked by inverse-set BFS; critical
chains and shortest reach words are in data/new_image_checks.json.

<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction--attempted-infinite-lifts--not-established"></a>
#### Attempted infinite lifts — NOT ESTABLISHED

For n=5,...,12, the fixed-swap/growing-cycle family with S=Q\{0,1}
has policy costs 11,11,11,12,13,14,15,16. The fixed-four-cycle/growing-arm
family with |S|=3 has costs 11,19,26,34,43,52,60,69. Only n=5,6 in
the latter violate n(n-3). Neither finite pattern proves an infinite
obstruction. All 16 instances have independently checked e, G, avoiding
and reset distances plus actual full-Q reset words. The growing-cycle
instances have 2^n-2 reachable nonempty images in this tested range;
no arbitrary-parameter reachability theorem is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction--i4-capacity-union-transfer--refuted"></a>
#### I4: capacity union transfer — REFUTED

The attempted statement: for reachable S,T,U=S union T with proper U,
if u properly extends U and rho(Uu^-1)>|U|, it image-extends S or T.
It fails even when a larger reachable witness maps ONTO U.

    n=3, a=[0,0,0], b=[1,2,1], S={1}, T={2}, U={1,2}, u=b.

The complete image family is Q, {1,2}, and the three singletons.
Su^-1={0,2}, Tu^-1={1}, Uu^-1=Q have capacities 1,1,3.
Qb=U, so the union expands properly, while neither singleton gains
image capacity. The expanding ordinary preimage {0,2} is unreachable.
This precise non-nested, nonempty, proper-union statement is state-minimal
at n=3 over any alphabet: two such sets cannot have a proper union at
n<=2. The search's word-length limit is not used for that minimality proof.
Independent ordinary-set checking confirms all fields.

<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction--a-valid-conditional-lemma"></a>
#### A valid conditional lemma

If V is reachable, Vu=S union T, |V|>|S union T|, and BOTH
X=V intersect Su^-1 and Y=V intersect Tu^-1 are reachable images,
then u image-extends S or T. Indeed, V=X union Y and the surjection
Vu=S union T gives |X intersect Y|>=|S intersect T|. Hence
|X|+|Y|=|V|+|X intersect Y|>|S|+|T|, and one set is larger
than its target. This proves a conditional counting lemma, not the
missing intersection-closure property or a general reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-local-image-potential-obstruction--literature-boundary"></a>
#### Literature boundary

Ferens--Szykula's quadratic reaching bound assumes complete reachability,
or reachability of all sets larger than the target. Their proper-extension
union lemma concerns ordinary preimages. Requiring a contained larger
image to be reachable adds the failed step above; the completeness
hypothesis has not been removed.
[Primary manuscript, Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 5.7](https://arxiv.org/html/2208.05956v5).
Exact reaching, transport into a subset and shortest-phase policy costs
are different quantities. Priority of these finite examples remains OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--logarithmic-dimension-in-genuinely-shortest-inverse-growth-histories"></a>
### Logarithmic dimension in genuinely shortest inverse-growth histories

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)**, with bounded independent checks
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** result. Priority
of the particular automaton realization is **OPEN**. General Cerny,
global actual-image policy square, and a slow-phase/dimension tradeoff
remain **OPEN**.

The subsequent [Maximal shortest jumps do not force linear history dimension](#direct-attack-maximal-jump-log-history) strengthens this obstruction
to only original permutation/unit letters and maximal-size shortest
parents, with every selected local cost two. It also counts ALL
single-letter intermediate preimages and keeps their dimension logarithmic.
Its rt grows at least n-1; the present exact-rt2 family remains separately
valid. Neither construction asserts global optimality of the long history.

For EVERY d>=3 there is an n=2^d-1 state strongly connected Eulerian
COMPLETELY REACHABLE DFA, with no constant letter and exact reset threshold 2,
having an ordinary inverse history

    {0} -> S_2 -> S_3 -> ... -> S_(n-1) -> Q.

Every arrow costs ONE original letter and is a genuinely shortest first
cardinality AND actual-image extension from its child. There are n-2 proper growth-stage
sets S_2,...,S_(n-1), but their normalized indicator span has EXACT
dimension d-1. The raw indicators together with Q have EXACT dimension d.
Thus even Eulerian balance and phase-by-phase shortestness cannot force
a dimension lower bound proportional to the number of stages. The
general logarithmic Boolean-vector lower bound is asymptotically tight
in this automaton context if arbitrary shortest ties are allowed.

Every displayed parent is an actual full-Q image, with separate charged
membership words. The same history is therefore allowed in the actual-image
parent recurrence G as well as ordinary inverse growth. Its long history
is not a globally shortest reset history: a different word resets in two letters. It does
not settle optimized histories or the tradeoff where many phases are
long. Those qualifications matter for using this result in a general proof.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--original-transformations-and-the-binary-weight-sets"></a>
#### Original transformations and the binary-weight sets

Use right actions and Q={0,...,n-1}. Partition Q into the contiguous
blocks

    B_i={2^i-1,...,2^(i+1)-2}, |B_i|=2^i, 0<=i<d.

For 1<=k<=n define S_k as the union of B_i for which bit i of k is one.
Then |S_k|=k, S_1={0}, S_2={1,2}, and S_n=Q.

Let a(q)=q+1 modulo n. Define the following n-1 rank-two base maps:

* b(q)=0 on S_2, and b(q)=1 otherwise;
* for 2<=k<=n-2, let u_k=min S_k and v_k=min(Q\S_k), and set
  f_k(q)=u_k on S_(k+1), and f_k(q)=v_k otherwise;
* f_(n-1)(0)=1 and f_(n-1)(q)=2 for q!=0.

Both parts of each nonterminal map's domain are nonempty, and its two
values are different. The final map also has rank two. The ORIGINAL
alphabet contains a and, for every base map x and every 0<=t<n,
the labeled transformation

    x_t(q)=(x((q+t) mod n)-t) mod n.

Thus x_0=x is an original single letter. Different labels may induce
the same transformation; they are retained with their multiplicities.
It also contains EVERY original unitary map u_(s,t), s!=t, taking s to t
and fixing all other states. The alphabet has exactly 1+2n(n-1) symbols. There is no assertion of
a fixed alphabet, distinct induced maps, or alphabet-minimality.
The formula is also the action of a^t x a^(n-t), but here each x_t is
specified as an ORIGINAL letter of cost one. No old word is silently
replaced by a free macro in a previously fixed automaton.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--strong-connectivity-eulerian-balance-and-exact-rt2"></a>
#### Strong connectivity, Eulerian balance and exact rt=2

The original n-cycle a makes the automaton strongly connected.
For a fixed base x, let deg_x(q) be the indegree of q under x. For any
state q the n conjugate symbols contribute

    sum_(t=0)^(n-1) deg_x((q+t) mod n)=n

incoming edges. There are n-1 base maps; a contributes one more edge.
These symbols give every state indegree and outdegree 1+n(n-1).
The unitary alphabet contributes n(n-1) to both degrees: its n-1 maps
with s=q remove one incoming edge, and its n-1 maps with t=q add one;
all remaining maps preserve the baseline edge. Thus both total degrees
are 1+2n(n-1), and the DFA is Eulerian as a labeled directed multigraph.

Every original nonpermutation has rank two or n-1, and a has rank n.
There is no one-letter reset. The original word f_(n-1),0 b_0 resets:
Q f_(n-1),0={1,2}=S_2, and S_2 b_0={0}. Hence rt=2 exactly.

For ANY desired nonempty S, choose r in S. Apply the ORIGINAL units
u_(q,r) for q outside S, in increasing state order. They fix every point
of S and move each outside point to r, so this charged word of length
n-|S| reaches S EXACTLY from Q. This proves complete reachability,
including every parent in the long history. No hereditary image family
is assumed. The membership words are separate certificates, not free
prefixes in the composed reset.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--the-long-history-uses-shortest-original-phases"></a>
#### The long history uses shortest original phases

Direct full preimages give

    b_0^-1({0})=S_2;
    f_k,0^-1(S_k)=S_(k+1), 2<=k<=n-2;
    f_(n-1),0^-1(S_(n-1))=Q.

Each preimage grows in cardinality by one. A zero-length word preserves
the set and cannot grow it, so one is the minimum extension cost at
EVERY phase. Other unit-cost words can give bigger jumps; shortestness
does not compel selection of those ties. Prepending the forward letters
in reverse phase order gives the single whole reset word

    f_(n-1),0 f_(n-2),0 ... f_2,0 b_0,

of length n-1. Full original-letter composition, rather than resetting
the current image to each nominal target, establishes its endpoint 0.

For the actual-image recurrence, every proper S has e(S)=1: an original
unit u_(q,r), q outside S and r in S, maps actual S union {q} onto S.
No empty word can send a larger image inside S. Hence EVERY displayed
parent is also a shortest actual-image parent, not merely an ordinary
preimage whose capacity is unproved. All phase lengths equal one,
and each phase grows cardinality, so W(S)<=n-|S|. Adding single outside
points with units attains it; therefore W(S)=n-|S| for every proper S.
Conjugating the two-letter reset by the original base symbols gives
two-letter resets to EVERY q. No original constant letter exists, so
G({q})=P=rt=2 for every q, while W({q})=n-1.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--exact-raw-and-normalized-dimensions"></a>
#### Exact raw and normalized dimensions

Every S_k indicator is constant on the d blocks, so raw dimension is
at most d. The proper history contains S_(2^i)=B_i for 1<=i<d, together
with S_2 and S_3; [S_3]-[S_2]=[B_0]. These d disjoint nonzero block
indicators are linearly independent. Therefore the raw proper-history
span already has dimension d and contains [Q]=sum_i[B_i]. Adding Q
does not increase it. The d>=3 guard ensures S_3 is a proper stage.

For a proper set X of size k, its usual zero-sum normalization is a
nonzero scalar multiple of

    [X]-(k/n)[Q].

Since Q belongs to the raw history span, these centered vectors span
the kernel of the nonzero coordinate-sum functional on that span.
Indeed, replacing every generator [S_k] by [S_k]-(k/n)[Q] loses at
most the Q direction; all centered generators have zero sum. The
normalized dimension is EXACTLY d-1.

The raw family of n-1 vectors S_2,...,S_n has rank d=ceil(log2(n-1)),
attaining the general Boolean-vector logarithmic bound. The normalized
dimension (d-1)/(n-2) tends to zero. No positive universal coefficient
in a linear-in-stages dimension guarantee can hold for all such histories.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--relation-to-the-literature-and-the-surviving-question"></a>
#### Relation to the literature and the surviving question

[Szykula 2026, Section 2.8, Lemmas 18--21 and Open Problem 22](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245)
uses multiple starting subsets to improve linear-algebraic bounds.
Its binary-weight Boolean-vector construction and logarithmic rank bound
are the source of the combinatorial architecture here. We explicitly
realize that low dimension as shortest inverse phases in an Eulerian DFA.
This is not a resolution of every interpretation of the informal open
problem. In particular, selecting the best ties or imposing long phases
can exclude this deliberately slow choice of a very easy automaton.

The earlier n5 dependence witness in [Shortest inverse growth does not supply a square proof or full independence](#direct-attack-inverse-history-barrier) remains
valid, and has a globally shortest whole reset history. The present result
has an arbitrary-parameter logarithmic dimension and Eulerian balance,
but does not replace that stronger global-optimality feature. Neither
result supplies a cost/dimension inequality that proves the square.

<a id="direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history--independent-verification-boundary"></a>
#### Independent verification boundary

`log_dimension_history.py` saves the definition, full stage descriptors,
charged membership descriptors, dimensions and original word labels
for d3..12, through n4095.
`check_log_dimension_history.py` imports neither the generator nor any
native, policy or previous checker. It rebuilds the original maps from
the block definition; checks every selected full preimage on every state;
literally composes the common long reset and the short reset; and computes
both dimensions by exact rational elimination on distinguishing block
columns. The block-constant check justifies that column reduction. It
checks the charged unit word for each actual parent; large scopes use
the exact disjoint-input composition certificate, while small scopes
literally compose every original unit in every membership word.

Four small scopes n7,15,31,63 additionally enumerate EVERY original
labeled row and its indegree, rather than relying on the conjugate
degree formula. Their full indicator vectors independently reproduce
the compressed-column ranks. Corrupted stage parents, stage costs,
dimension, alphabet degree and reset labels are rejected. These finite
controls support the paper proof. At n7 a separate full-image BFS and
all-parent one-letter inverse recurrence verify EVERY e/G/W value.
No formal proof kernel, optimized-history dimension theorem, slow-phase
tradeoff or general Cerny proof is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-native-image-policy-audit"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-native-image-policy-audit--exact-native-image-policy-search"></a>
### Exact native image-policy search

native_policy.cpp implements integer forward BFS, min-over-contained-subset
transport distances and the full all-tie image-policy recurrence. Scoring
uses no floating arithmetic or heuristic pruning. A persistent executable
accepts input rows via stdin; Python retains explicit word certificates.
native_policy.py records compiler argv/version and source/binary hashes.
GCC 4.9.2 builds the Windows executable on this host. An initial DLL load
failed during runtime initialization; the executable protocol replaced it.
No package or compiler was installed. Reproducible build products are
ignored and excluded from the source/data manifest. Python checkers use
the standard library; native checks require the executable or g++ on PATH.

Every e, best-G and worst-G value in retained certificates is compared
with the native scorer after independent inverse-BFS checking. A second
complete audit checks all 1303 overlapping SC synchronizing binary inputs
through n=4 against a separate ordinary-set inverse algorithm. Larger
enumerations are not independently repeated in full.

<a id="direct-attack-native-image-policy-audit--complete-permutation--rank-n-1-binary-class"></a>
#### Complete permutation + rank-(n-1) binary class

Conjugate the first permutation to its cycle-type representative.
Its centralizer rotates each cycle and exchanges equal-length cycles,
so it is transitive on states with the same cycle length. The second
rank-(n-1) map has one missing image, one double fiber and singleton
other fibers. Choose one missing-image state per distinct cycle length,
every unordered double-fiber source pair, and all permutations of the
n-1 available image values. This covers the designated ordered class;
conjugation preserves all costs. For a type with d distinct lengths the
count is d*binom(n,2)*(n-1)!. These counts overlap, not class counts.

All Q-reachable singletons imply SC synchronization: one singleton
establishes synchronization, and all singletons give state reachability
from every source. Conversely SC synchronization reaches every singleton.
The cover uses this exact filter.

At n=7 all 15 cycle types complete: 453600 representatives, 177398 SC
synchronizing, maximum minimum policy cost 36. At n=8 all 22 types
complete: 6350400 representatives, 2691892 SC synchronizing, maximum 49.
Neither cover includes
all binary automata: both letters can be singular, or the second can
have rank below n-1. audit_rank_cover.py explicitly conjugates every
labeled pair through n=5 (4,108,3456,144000 cases), checks missing-state
orbits and fibers, and checks cumulative counts of completed larger runs.
This is a completeness audit, not a formal verification or parameter proof.

<a id="direct-attack-native-image-policy-audit--frozen-sampled-and-structured-searches"></a>
#### Frozen sampled and structured searches

Mutations can change every letter and its rank. Actual seed rows are
frozen. Counts are proposals, not distinct automata/classes.

| Search | Proposals | SC synchronizing | Maximum minimum G |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| n7 binary, global | 100000 | 75022 | 36 |
| n8 ternary, global | 100000 | 93251 | 49 |
| n10 binary, global | 50000 | 40173 | 81 |
| n8 binary, local | 200000 | 158139 | 49 |
| n10 ternary, local | 100000 | 95594 | 81 |

No global square failure was found. The local runs find no positive
excess in these neighborhoods; this does not erase the five/six-state
local counterexamples. The n7 run is replayed from frozen seeds in a
temporary directory with exact count and retained certificate agreement.

The finite two-arm search tests 3616 SC synchronizing instances through
n12, with cyclic directions, defect positions and additional permutations.
Its maxima are (n-1)^2, attained by included Cerny seeds. This is neither
a complete cover of the two-arm class nor an arbitrary-parameter theorem.
Raw inputs, scalar results and commands are retained; no new uniform
upper bound follows.

<a id="direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem--exact-maximum-image-extension-2n-2-with-only-4n-2-images"></a>
### Exact maximum image extension 2n-2 with only 4n-2 images

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**PROVED on paper for all n>=6.** This improves the additive term in the
two-fixed-point 2n-4 family. The asymptotic necessary coefficient is still
2; neither a universal 2n upper bound nor Cerny is refuted. Priority OPEN.

Let L=n-1>=5, C={0,...,L-1}, and f=L. The letter a cycles C and fixes f.
The rank-three letter b satisfies

    fb=0, (L-1)b=L-2, cb=f for c in C\{L-1}.

Use right actions and write P={f,0,L-2}, B={f,0}, H={0,L-2},
S={L-3,L-1}. Strong connectivity follows from f b=0, the cycle on C,
and any default cycle state b=f.

<a id="direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem--complete-image-closure"></a>
#### Complete image closure

The reachable images are exactly Q, all singletons, and the three families

    {f,j}, {j,j-2 mod L}, {f,j,j-2 mod L},  j in C.       (R)

There are 4n-2 images: the cycle-pair orbit has L distinct members since
L>=5 (the possible two-point rotational symmetry occurs only at L=4).
Qb=P, and a reaches every triple. Pb=B, whose rotations give all f-pairs.
{f,L-1}b=H, whose rotations give all cycle-pairs. Hb={f}, and strong
connectivity reaches all singletons. The displayed family is closed:
triples containing L-1 map under b to P, others to B; f-pairs map to H
when the cycle state is L-1 and to B otherwise; cycle-pairs map to
{f,L-2} when they contain L-1 and to {f} otherwise. This proves (R).

<a id="direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem--exact-bottleneck-allowing-singleton-arrivals"></a>
#### Exact bottleneck, allowing singleton arrivals

Every first drop from a larger image to size <=2 gives B: a larger image
is Q or a triple, Q first becomes P, and the first triple rank drop is b
on a triple not containing L-1. Some actual triple drops in one letter.
Consequently e(S)=1+D(B,S), where D allows any terminal subset of S.

To reach a cycle-pair from B one must pass through {f,L-1}b=H. This first
entry costs at least L letters: L-1 rotations from 0, then b. Any later
entry again gives H. After the last entry, only a's can lead to S as a
pair: b either merges the pair or exits the cycle-pair family. The unique
rotation H a^j=S has j=L-1 modulo L, because L>=5 excludes the swapped
orientation symmetry. Thus every pair arrival costs at least 2L-1;
a^(L-1)b a^(L-1) attains it.

The first singleton is produced only by a cycle-pair not containing L-1,
and is f. It costs at least L+1 from B. The shortest state path from f
into S has length L-2: b to 0 and L-3 rotations to L-3. A b from a
default cycle state restarts at f; a b at L-1 first requires a path of L
letters from f and cannot shorten that path. Hence any singleton arrival also
costs at least (L+1)+(L-2)=2L-1. Both arrival types are covered, so

    e(S)=2L=2n-2.

The actual larger image P and word b a^(L-1)b a^(L-1) attain this value.

Every proper image has e<=2L. Triples use Qb a^j, cost <=L. f-pairs use
Pb a^j, cost <=L. Cycle-pairs use Pb a^(L-1)b a^j, cost <=2L. Singletons
use H b={f}, followed if needed by b a^j, cost <=L+1. These are actual
larger-image witnesses and account for every image in (R). Therefore
max e=2n-2, not just a lower estimate on one pair.

<a id="direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem--rtp_bestn2"></a>
#### rt=P_best=n+2

Q needs at least two letters to first reach B, then the first merge costs
at least L+1 as proved above. The word bb a^(L-1)bb resets Q to f in
L+3=n+2 letters, proving exact rt. Singleton f has e=1 via H and b.
H has e=L+1: a pair arrival from B requires L letters before the first
H entry, while a singleton in H requires at least L+1 to merge to f
and at least one further letter. Prepend the triple drop. The shortest
H extension can use P, and P has e=1 via Qb. Thus the exact policy chain
f -> H -> P -> Q costs 1+(L+1)+1=L+3. Since rt<=P_best, equality follows.

<a id="direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem--boundaries-and-verification"></a>
#### Boundaries and verification

n5 is excluded: L=4 gives a cycle-pair of period 2 and max e=6, not 8.
n4 separately has max e=6. All n4..63 saved arrays have independent
ordinary-set all-source forward distances, and their complete image
closures and full-Q words are checked. The general jump-location scan
has 147 parameter cases at nine n values; every saved summary is also
independently checked. This scan proves no arbitrary-jump formula.

This family was extracted after a n63 permutation-mutation search first
found e=123; normalization and a jump-location scan then found e=124.
The algorithm and parameter proofs are separate from that sampled evidence.
The underlying image-extension formulation is known from
[Kisielewicz--Szykula, Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
Novelty remains OPEN. There is no new Lean theorem or general reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem--polynomial-pair-graph-exact-extension-maximum-and-an-odd-state-obstruction"></a>
### Polynomial pair graph, exact extension maximum, and an odd-state obstruction

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**PROVED**, paper reconstruction; independent finite checks below.
Not Lean verified. No unrestricted synchronization bound or novelty claim.
All words act on the right, in their written order. n>=2.

Let A be a strongly connected synchronizing PU automaton: each letter is
either a permutation or a unit (s->t), fixing every other state. Any finite
alphabet is allowed. Write G for the group generated by the permutation
letters. Its inverses are positive words because G is finite. Define Gamma
by all arcs (sg,tg), for every original unit (s->t) and g in G.

<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem--reachability-prerequisite"></a>
#### Reachability prerequisite

G acts by automorphisms of Gamma. The union of its terminal strongly
connected components is G-invariant and preserved by all units. Strong
connectivity of A forces this union to be Q. Therefore every component of
Gamma is terminal, so there are no edges between different components.
Units preserve each component and permutations permute components. A
reset is impossible if there is more than one component. Hence Gamma is
strongly connected.

Conversely, if Gamma is strongly connected, every nonempty S is an actual
image Qw. Choose shortest Gamma paths toward S. For each vertex outside S,
choose the first arc of its path. Apply these conjugated units in descending
distance order; they move each outside vertex to its parent and leave S
fixed. The image becomes exactly S. A conjugated unit with arc (sg,tg) is
implemented by g^{-1} u g, a positive actual word. This also proves SC and
synchronization. Thus, under the stated SC hypothesis, synchronization is
equivalent to Gamma being strongly connected; Gamma-SC itself suffices
without a separate SC assumption. No analogous rejection criterion is
claimed for arbitrary non-SC PU automata.

<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem--exact-maximum-from-at-most-nn-1-ordered-pairs"></a>
#### Exact maximum from at most n(n-1) ordered pairs

For s!=t let d(s,t) be the shortest length of a word v consisting only of
permutation letters such that some original unit arc (x,y) satisfies
(xv,yv)=(s,t). Set d=infinity outside Gamma. Put

    Gamma_l = {(s,t): d(s,t)+1 <= l}.

For every nonempty proper S, the actual-image extension cost is

    e(S) = 1 + min { d(s,t): s not in S, t in S }.                 (1)

Proof: a shortest inverse extension can end as soon as its size first
exceeds |S|. Before that, any neutral or shrinking inverse unit can be
deleted: removing it leaves a superset, and all later preimages are
monotone. If the modified process grows earlier, it is shorter still.
Since every nonempty subset is an actual image, the larger set at that
first growth is admissible. Thus all preceding inverse steps are
permutations, followed by one growing inverse unit. A unit changes size by
at most one. Written forward, the word is u v. Its preimage is larger
exactly when xv is outside S and yv is inside S. This proves (1).

It follows that

    max_{empty != S != Q} e(S)
      = min { l>=1 : Gamma_l is strongly connected }.             (2)

A strongly connected directed graph enters every nonempty proper subset.
If Gamma_l is not SC, it has a nonempty proper forward-closed set R;
S=Q\R has no entering arc and e(S)>l. These implications prove equality.
Multi-source BFS on ordered pairs computes d in polynomial time; no
enumeration of 2^n images is required. The extension cost charges u v,
NOT the longer conjugation v^{-1} u v used in the reachability proof.

<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem--failure-of-es5"></a>
#### Failure of e(S)<=n in every odd dimension n>=5

Let n=2m+3, m>=1, L=n-2 odd. Use Q={0,...,n-1} and

    a=(0 1)(2 3 ... n-1),   b=(1 2),   u=(0 -> n-1).
    S={0,3,5,...,n-2}.

The permutation group is S_n. Indeed, a^L=(0 1), while a^2 fixes 0,1
and cycles {2,...,n-1} (gcd(2,L)=1). Conjugating b by its powers gives
all transpositions (1,q), q>=2; together with (0,1) they generate S_n.
Hence Gamma consists of every ordered distinct pair, and every nonempty
subset is reachable.

We prove e(S)=max_T e(T)=n+1 for all these n, independently of experiments.

For the lower bound, b preserves membership in S. Every a-transition flips
membership except n-1->2, whose endpoints are both outside S. Follow the
ordered pair (0,n-1) under a permutation word v. Before the first a, b
fixes the pair. The first a gives (1,2), both outside S. Membership then
remains equal until one coordinate takes an exceptional transition.

The source cannot take its first exceptional transition before n letters:
it must move 0->1 by a, enter the long cycle 1->2 by b, follow the L-1
successive a-edges from 2 to n-1, then take the exceptional a-edge. This
requires L+2=n steps. Detours through b at 1,2 cannot shorten the chain:
each vertex 3,...,n-1 has only its predecessor as an incoming transition
other than a self-loop. The target, after the first a, starts at 2; its
second exceptional transition requires at least L more steps, so occurs
no earlier than L+1=n-1. If it occurs before any source exception, both
coordinates are outside immediately before it; afterward the source is
inside and the target outside. This still is not a growing pair. Therefore
no word of length <=n-1 maps the unit arc to outside->inside S. The word
v=a^n does: it maps the pair to (1,3). Thus e(S)=n+1.

For the matching global upper bound, explicit arcs of Gamma_n give
reciprocal stars on the two parts S and B=Q\S:

* u a^j, even j=2,4,...,L-1: 0 to every other vertex of S.
* u a b a^j, odd j=1,3,...,L-2: every other vertex of S to 0.
* u a^j, odd j=1,3,...,L-2, and j=L: 1 to every other vertex of B.
* u a b a^j, even j=0,2,...,L-1: every other vertex of B to 1.

All have length <=n. The original u gives S->B. At length n+1, u a^n
adds B->S via 1->3. Thus Gamma_{n+1} is SC, proving (2)'s threshold n+1.
Gamma_n has exactly the two SC components S,B, with no B->S edge.
This is an infinite extension obstruction, not a counterexample to the
square reset bound. Observed rt=P=4n-10 for n5,7,9,11 is ONLY FINITE;
no all-n reset-threshold formula is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem--state-minimum-five-within-all-pu-alphabets"></a>
#### State minimum five within ALL PU alphabets

**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED finite cover with a proved reduction.**
No state minimum is asserted among unrestricted DFA alphabets.

Ignore identity/duplicate letters. An inclusion-minimal subset of the
permutation alphabet generating the same group is irredundant; deleting
other permutations cannot create a shorter extension. Irredundancy is
hereditary under subsets. At n4, all 8855 four-subsets of the 23
nonidentity permutations have a retained redundancy witness, independently
checked by tuple group closure. Hence every irredundant basis has <=3
letters. At n3, all three-subsets are redundant (the checked list has
5 singleton and 9 pair bases); larger irredundant sets are impossible.
At n2 there is just one nonidentity permutation.

For each basis and each cut cardinality k, relabel S to {0,...,k-1}.
Mark a unit safe if every permutation word of length <=n-1 maps its arc
away from the entering cut. Include ALL safe units. The full conjugate
graph of these units is certified non-SC by a forward-closed proper set.
There are 1,28,1233 cut designations for n2,3,4 respectively. Any purported
PU counterexample with e(S)>n has only safe unit seeds after restricting
to a minimal permutation basis. Its full conjugate graph remains SC
(same group and units), and adding safe units preserves SC. It would
therefore contradict one of the certified non-SC graphs. Pure-unit
alphabets have e=1 whenever Gamma is SC. This exhausts all finite PU
alphabets for n<=4. The displayed ternary n5 establishes the class minimum.

<a id="direct-attack-pu-prefix-extension-theorem--independent-audit-and-literature-boundary"></a>
#### Independent audit and literature boundary

data/pu_prefix contains 12 family cases n5..21,31,63,101, 186 previously
retained PU samples, four full ordinary-image arrays and the complete cut
cover. check_pu_prefix validates every pair-distance primal/Bellman
certificate, permutation closure, the SC upper graph and closed lower
cut. Its minimum-cover audit uses REVERSE pair BFS from the entering cut
and tuple group closure, unlike the generator's forward per-seed BFS and
indexed multiplication table. Ordinary reachable-image BFS independently
checks the small exact extension arrays. Six corruptions are rejected.
The all-n result rests on the paper proof, not these finite cases.

Rystsov conjugate graphs and PU complete reachability are known.
Szykula--Vorel (DLT2016) establish immediate-unit greediness; this is not
the stronger word-phase policy, which already fails at n4. Ferens--Szykula
(2026, DOI10.1145/3798283) give PU subset-extension bounds depending on
maximum group-orbit size, with general quadratic reset bounds. No new
general quadratic bound follows here. Priority of the exact prefix
threshold identity and the displayed obstruction remains OPEN.

Kisielewicz--Szykula, MFCS2015, arXiv1608.01268, Theorems1/2 give ordinary
quadratic extension obstructions. Section3.1 explicitly excludes their
difficult subsets from actual images and poses exactly the image-capacity
extension formulation used in this repository. That known obstruction
does not refute the present unrestricted actual-image e<=2n route. The
new PU family only refutes e<=n, and preserves complete reachability.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction--every-universal-linear-actual-image-extension-bound-fails"></a>
### Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails

Continuation update: [Quadratic actual-image extension with fixed ternary and binary alphabets](#direct-attack-fixed-alphabet-quadratic-image-extension) removes
the growing-alphabet qualification below. It proves exact quadratic
actual-image extension with fixed ternary and binary alphabets, including
SC irreducibly synchronizing binary inputs. Earlier binary/fixed-alphabet
universal-linear OPEN labels are historical. This original fold/path
family, its exact rt/e and the global policy equality remain valid.

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for all parameters below.
The previous unrestricted target e(S)<=2n is **REFUTED**, as is
EVERY bound e(S)<=Cn+d with fixed constants C,d, even with a transitive
symmetric permutation group and just one idempotent nonpermutation letter.
Finite audits are separately **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. Priority is
**OPEN**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. Cerny's conjecture remains **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction--actual-image-definition-and-the-family"></a>
#### Actual-image definition and the family

An actual image is Qv for an actual original-letter word v, including Q.
For a proper nonempty actual image S, e(S) is the least length of a word u
such that Ru is CONTAINED in S for some actual image R with |R|>|S|.
Equality Ru=S is not required; rank skips are allowed. The lower bound
below explicitly permits them and is not an exact-reaching obstruction.

For r>=1 put n=2r, Q={0,...,2r-1}, L={0,...,r-1}, H={r,...,2r-1}.
The original alphabet consists of every adjacent transposition

    tau_i: swap i and i+1, fix all other states, 0<=i<=2r-2,

and the single letter

    b(q)=q mod r.

Thus b has rank r and is idempotent. All products act on the right.
The transposition graph is the connected path, so the DFA is SC. Every
word containing b has rank at most r; every word not containing b is a
permutation and has Q-image Q. Hence the ONLY actual image larger than
the r-set H is Q. In particular,

    e(H)=min{|u|: Qu is contained in H}.                 (1)

H is an actual image: start with Qb=L, and for j=r-1,r-2,...,0 append
tau_j tau_(j+1)...tau_(j+r-1). This transports the largest remaining
left token to its right slot, without touching tokens already placed.
It gives L -> H and uses exactly r^2 swaps, so its whole cost is r^2+1.
The actual reachability of H is established before using (1).

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction--a-potential-for-arbitrary-full-preimages"></a>
#### A potential for arbitrary full preimages

For ANY subset T of Q, define

    F(T)=sum_(q in T) omega_q,
    omega_q=max(r+1-q,0).

The adjacent weights differ by at most one. Since a transposition is its
own inverse, replacing T by its full tau_i-preimage increases F by at
most one, for EVERY possible membership pattern of T.

For b, the full preimage consists of two copies of T intersect L.
Weights at r+1,...,2r-1 are zero, and the weight at r is one. Therefore

    F(T b^-1)-F(T) = 1_(0 in T)-1_(r in T) <=1.         (2)

Here b^-1 denotes a SET PREIMAGE, not an inverse word or a permutation.
Equation (2) does not assert that b is invertible. All original inverse
steps, including ones which shrink the target set, increase F by <=1.

If Qu is contained in T, then T u^-1=Q. Apply its full preimages in the
reverse order of the original letters of u. Telescoping gives

    |u| >= F(Q)-F(T).                                   (3)

Now F(Q)=(r+1)(r+2)/2, F(H)=1, and max_q F({q})=r+1.
Consequently

    e(H)>=r(r+3)/2,       rt>=r(r+1)/2.                 (4)

The second inequality applies to ANY reset endpoint. The first applies
to ALL words which enter H, even if their final rank is one or their
intermediate ranks skip many values. Thus it remains valid for the exact
capacity/actual-image formulation used throughout this repository.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction--matching-common-words"></a>
#### Matching common words

Set

    W_r=b (tau_(r-1) b)(tau_(r-2) tau_(r-1) b)...
                   (tau_1 tau_2 ... tau_(r-1) b).        (5)

After the first b, the image is {0,...,r-1}. If the current image is
{0,...,j}, the block tau_j...tau_(r-1) transports j to r and fixes
0,...,j-1. The following b sends r to 0, giving {0,...,j-1}.
Every block acts on the SAME actual image chain. Thus W_r resets to 0.
It uses r copies of b and r(r-1)/2 original swaps, so |W_r|=r(r+1)/2.
Appending tau_0 tau_1...tau_(r-1) transports this root to r in exactly
r letters, giving a whole-Q word entering H. Together with (4),

    rt(A_r)=r(r+1)/2,
    e(H)=r(r+3)/2 = n^2/8+3n/4.                         (6)

Both equalities are exact arbitrary-parameter theorems, not extrapolated
finite data. For n=12 (r=6), rt=21 and e(H)=27>2n=24. Within this family
the first strict 2n violation is r=6; no unrestricted minimum-state
assertion is made. For every fixed C,d, (6) eventually exceeds Cn+d.

This is NOT a Cerny counterexample:

    (2r-1)^2-rt(A_r)=(r-1)(7r-2)/2>=0.                  (7)

The abstract permutation group is S_n, hence primitive; any DFA
congruence is trivial. This gives the method obstruction already among
simple DFAs. The alphabet size is n. No binary or fixed-alphabet
refutation is claimed. The family is not completely reachable when
r>=2, since ranks r+1,...,n-1 are absent.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction--consequence-for-the-research-route"></a>
#### Consequence for the research route

The arbitrary-finite-alphabet image-extension quantifier in
[Kisielewicz--Szykula 2016, Section 3.1, Conjecture 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268)
is the actual-image/preimage-containment condition used in (1). We
rechecked that primary statement: it does not restrict the alphabet size.
Equation (6) refutes its universal linear formulation. No claim that this
refutation was previously unpublished follows from the source check.

Previous documents describing unrestricted e(S)<=2n, or ANY universal
linear actual-image extension bound, as OPEN are historical. They are
superseded by this refutation. Earlier binary 2n-1 lower examples and
low-rank/PU subclass theorems remain valid in their stated scopes.
The global best compatible image-policy square bound remains OPEN:
one expensive target H does not force a globally chosen reset chain to
visit it. Binary linear extension is now refuted by the separate fixed
alphabet continuation. Complete-reachability restrictions are not decided
by this growing-alphabet family or by that rank-gap continuation.

The obstruction separates cheap group MEMBERSHIP from target-dependent
original word cost. It also shows why allowing strict containment in the
extension definition does not in itself yield a linear theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction--independent-evidence"></a>
#### Independent evidence

transposition_fold_obstruction.py supplies 69 controls, r=1,...,64 and
{100,128,256,512,1024}, through n2048. Original-word rows and all charges
are checked independently in check_transposition_fold_obstruction.py,
which imports none of the generator or prior solvers. It verifies the
potential coefficient identity for EVERY subset on each retained input,
and literally applies expanded reset/entry/reachability words for r<=24.
For larger inputs it evaluates every original swap in exact permutation
blocks, then applies the blocks to the common actual image; no free group
words or abstract generator costs are substituted.

Complete forward actual-image graphs and separate reverse-target graphs
for r=1,...,9 verify both exact thresholds, totaling 207860/221364
vertices. Six corrupted certificates are rejected. These bounded checks
support the paper proof; they are not a formal proof kernel.

The same independent program audits the constructive positive boundary
in [A connected transposition alphabet and any singular letter satisfy the square](#direct-attack-connected-transposition-square): an actual connected transposition
alphabet and ANY singular letter admit a charged FORWARD square reset.
The sharper inverse extension proof uses rank n-1; that inverse mechanism
does not generalize to b of rank r=n/2, as (6) demonstrates.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-bounded-extension-search"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-bounded-extension-search--direct-linear-image-extension-adversarial-tests-with-sparse-exact-scoring"></a>
### Direct linear image-extension adversarial tests with sparse exact scoring

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).

<a id="direct-attack-rank-skip-image-bypass"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-skip-image-bypass--quadratic-exact-reaching-linear-into-image-bypass-and-linear-resets"></a>
### Quadratic exact reaching, linear into-image bypass and linear resets

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**PROVED** (paper reconstruction plus explicit word proofs).
This concerns a published special family; no general upper improvement,
novelty claim, minimal-state claim or Lean theorem.

Primary sources read on 2026-09-29:
[Gonze--Jungers, DLT2018, Proposition2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.02540)
and [Gonze et al., DLT2017, page13 and Section3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1704.04047).
The latter's Figure4 was rendered and visually inspected to recover exact
transitions. Its figures use ONE-based states q1,...,qn; saved arrays use
ZERO-based indices. All words act in written order on the right.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-skip-image-bypass--published-family-explicitly-reconstructed"></a>
#### Published family, explicitly reconstructed

Let n=4m+3, m>=1. The central permutation is a=(q1 q2 q3 q4).
There are two arms, q3,q5,q7,...,qn and q1,q6,q8,...,q(n-1).
On each arm the edges alternate transpositions b,a,b,a,... starting from
the central state. Unpaired arm endpoints are fixed by the missing letter.
The other central b-states q2,q4 are fixed. The singular letter is

    c=(q2 -> q3)(q4 -> q1), fixing all other states.

For n7 this is

    a=[1,2,3,0,6,5,4], b=[5,1,4,3,2,0,6],
    c=[0,2,2,0,4,5,6].

Put k=(n-5)/2=2m-1 and S=Q\{q(k+2),q(k+4)}.
The published exact-reaching result is

    d(Q,S)=n^2/4+5n/4-6.

No rank n-1 image exists: the first c drops Q to n-2 and rank never
increases. Thus Q is the only actual image larger than S, and

    e(S)=min{|w|:Qw subseteq S},

which allows Qw to be STRICTLY smaller. A subsequent c on an n-2 image
either returns to Qc or drops rank; shortest exact reaching discards such
drops. That is why its complement-pair diameter is quadratic. The actual
capacity question has no such prohibition.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-skip-image-bypass--explicit-into-image-bypass"></a>
#### Explicit into-image bypass

Let p_m be the length-m prefix of abab... . Then

    w = c a (ba)^m c p_m,
    |w|=3m+3=3(n+1)/4,
    |Qw|=n-4, Qw subseteq S.                                  (1)

Proof by holes: after c the missing states are q2,q4. After a(ba)^m,
they are the two arm endpoints q(n-1),qn. On the right arm, (ba) advances
q3 to q(4m+3)=qn; on the left arm it advances q1 along q8,q12,... and
finishes at the fixed endpoint q(4m+2)=q(n-1). Applying c again adds
holes q2,q4, so the new complement has exactly four states.

The final prefix p_m transports q2,q4 toward the arm interiors and the
two endpoints toward the center. For m>=2, its four holes are
q(2m+1),q(2m+2),q(2m+3),q(2m+4). For m1 they are q1,q3,q5,q6.
Both include the target holes q(2m+1),q(2m+3). This proves (1) for every
parameter. Therefore this published exact-reaching obstruction does NOT
refute actual-image e<=2n, or any fixed positive linear coefficient above
3/4 for this particular target.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-skip-image-bypass--a-linear-reset-construction-not-just-synchronization-assumed"></a>
#### A linear reset construction, not just synchronization assumed

Write g=ab. It is a full n-cycle. At n7 its order is
q1,q2,q5,q7,q3,q4,q6. Adding two arm states inserts one vertex in each
half of this cycle. An a-transposition replacing a fixed endpoint inserts
the new vertex after that endpoint in ab; a b-transposition does so before
that endpoint. Induction therefore preserves one full cycle. In its cyclic
coordinates i=0,...,n-1, with q1 at0, q2 is at1, q3 is at
d=(n+1)/2=2m+2, and q4 is at d+1. Each added arm pair increases the
q1-to-q3 segment by one, proving these coordinate assignments as well.

Thus g:i->i+1 modulo n and c changes only 1->d and d+1->0.
Let F=cg and H=cg^2. Their exceptional transitions are

    F: 1->d+1, d+1->1; otherwise i->i+1.
    H: 1->d+2, d+1->2; otherwise i->i+2.

H has a cycle C={1,d+2,d+4,...,n-1}. We claim

    Q H^(m+2) = I := {1,4,6,...,n-1}.                         (2)

The cycle C is retained. Every even coordinate 0,2,...,d reaches C
within m+2 H-steps. A lower odd coordinate 3+2j, 0<=j<=m, reaches
d+1 after m-j steps, jumps to2, and finishes at4+2j after m+2 steps.
An upper odd coordinate d+3+2j, 0<=j<=m-2, reaches0 after m-1-j
steps and finishes at6+2j. Together these images are exactly I; the
upper range is empty when m1. This proves (2).

Now F^(2m-1) sends I into {0,d+1}. For 1 it swaps an odd number of times,
ending at d+1. For an even i in [4,d], it reaches d+1 after d+1-i
steps and has i-4 (even) swaps remaining. For an even i>=d+2, it reaches
0 after n-i steps and has i-d-2 (even) steps remaining. With zero
remaining steps it stays0; otherwise it alternates via1 to d+1.
Finally c maps both 0,d+1 to0. Hence the literal actual word

    (c (ab)^2)^(m+2) (c ab)^(2m-1) c

resets Q to q1 and has length

    5(m+2)+3(2m-1)+1 = 11m+8 = (11n-1)/4.                    (3)

g is an actual two-letter word; each use costs2. No synthetic-letter
discount occurs. Its full-cycle action also proves strong connectivity.
Equations(1)--(3) are constructive all-n assertions. This does not assert
that the reset word or the into-image bypass is shortest.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-skip-image-bypass--independent-finite-audit"></a>
#### Independent finite audit

Eleven frozen cases n7,11,...,39,63,103 retain all rows, exact-reaching
words, complete bypass trajectories, reset words and inverse phase sets.
The constructor uses the published endpoint-insertion recursion. The
checker reconstructs the arm matching edges directly, verifies g's full
cycle and central positions, evaluates every word, and computes exact
reaching through complementary unordered-pair BFS. The constructor uses
a separate ordinary rank-range image BFS for that distance. n7 has full
ordinary ALL-SOURCE e/G/W/forward verification; sparse native arrays are
retained at n7 and n11. The measured target costs are6 and9 respectively.
Finite shortest-cost observations are not extrapolated to all n.

The known papers already emphasize that smaller contained images bypass
difficult exact targets. Priority of these precise words and constants
remains OPEN; they are not presented as a newly discovered general
mechanism. The research implication is concrete: exact-rank transport
must be distinguished from actual capacity, and globally useful rank
skips must receive their full benefit in a synchronization charging proof.

### Direct e(S) pressure from multiple permutations and rank three

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image

Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. All maxima below are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** for

`rank_three_two_perm_search.py` computes the complete actual image

into any subset of the target; it does not require exact arrival.
For triples, the only larger source is `Q`; for pairs, all actual
triples and `Q` are sources; for singletons, every non-singleton

| n | scope | proposed | SC synchronizing | largest e | target rank |

| 8 | deterministic random seed 20261008 | 200000 | 178688 | 11 | 3 |

not covering bounds or statistical evidence for every group shape.
`check_rank_three_two_perm_search.py` independently recomputes all

To probe structured long transport, `rank_three_two_transposition_scan.py`

[Exact maximum image extension 2n-2 with only 4n-2 images](#direct-attack-one-fixed-extension-theorem), then adds **every unordered pair of
distinct transpositions** as two extra letters. The scan includes

In each size, swaps `(0,1)` and `(1,2)` attain the retained maximum;

The general first-rank-drop lemma in

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--a-sparse-rank-three-family-with-exact-maximum-image-extension-2n-4"></a>
### A sparse rank-three family with exact maximum image extension 2n-4

**PROVED on paper for every n>=4.** This gives an asymptotic coefficient
obstruction 2, even with additive O(1) or o(n) slack. It is not a counterexample
to a universal 2n bound, a new general reset upper bound, or Cerny. Priority
of the precise family and image-capacity conclusion remains OPEN.

Put L=n-2, C={2,...,n-1}, and use right actions:

    0a=0, 1a=1, ca=2+(c-1) mod L for c in C,
    0b=1, 1b=2, cb=1 for 2<=c<n-1, (n-1)b=0.

Thus a cycles C and fixes 0,1; b has rank 3. Write P={0,1,2} and
S={0,n-1}. The automaton is strongly connected: 0 ->1 ->2 via b, C is
an a-cycle, and n-1 ->0 via b. Its full-Q reset word is

    b b a^(L-1) b b,

of length L+3=n+1.

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--the-whole-image-family-is-explicit"></a>
#### The whole image family is explicit

The nonempty reachable images are exactly

    {Q}, all singletons, {0,1},
    {0,1,c}, {0,c}, {1,c} for each c in C.                 (R)

There are 4n-4 such images. Qb=P, and a rotations reach all triples.
Pb={1,2}, so rotations reach all {1,c}. The last such pair satisfies
{1,n-1}b={0,2}, whose rotations reach all {0,c}; then {0,n-1}b={0,1}.
For c!=n-1, {0,c}b={1}; paths from 1 reach every state, giving all
singletons. Conversely the displayed family is forward closed. On triples,
b gives P if c=n-1 and {1,2} otherwise. On pairs, b gives

    {1,c} -> {1,2} (c!=n-1),  {1,n-1} -> {0,2},
    {0,c} -> {1}   (c!=n-1),  {0,n-1} -> {0,1},
    {0,1} -> {1,2}.

This proves (R), reachability and synchronization without treating any
ordinary subset as an image for free.

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--a-reachable-pair-with-exact-image-extension-cost"></a>
#### A reachable pair with exact image-extension cost

Every image larger than S is Q or one of the triples. Before its first
rank drop to <=2, it remains a triple (after Q's first b). That first drop
is necessarily b and its image is ALWAYS {1,2}. A triple with c!=n-1
attains this drop in one letter. Hence

    e(S)=1+min{|v|: {1,2}v subset S}.                     (1)

Starting from {1,2}, any rank-two arrival at {0,n-1} must first enter the
{0,c} family. This can happen only through {1,n-1}b={0,2}. Before this
entry at least L-1 a's are needed, and the entry b costs one. From {0,2},
another L-1 a's are necessary to reach {0,n-1}. Applying b earlier would
merge the pair, so no rank-two shortcut occurs. The exact pair arrival
cost is 2L-1, attained by a^(L-1)b a^(L-1).

Any singleton arrival has a first merge. The only pair merge is
{0,c}b={1} with c!=n-1. It takes at least L+1 letters to produce this
singleton from {1,2}: first enter {0,2} in L letters, then merge. From 1
the shortest state path into S has length L: b to 2 followed by L-1
a's to n-1. Every earlier b from C returns to 1, and reaching 0 requires
passing n-1 first. Thus singleton arrivals cost at least 2L+1, two more
than the pair arrival. Equation (1) proves

    e({0,n-1})=2L=2n-4.

The actual larger image P and word b a^(L-1)b a^(L-1) attain this cost.
Loss of intermediate cardinality and partial-target arrivals were both
included in the lower bound.

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--this-is-the-maximum-over-all-proper-images"></a>
#### This is the maximum over ALL proper images

For c=2+r, 0<=r<L, the following actual larger-image transports give
upper bounds (the source P is a triple):

* Q b a^r = {0,1,c}, cost 1+r<=L;
* P b a^r = {1,c}, cost 1+r<=L;
* P b a^(L-1)b a^r = {0,c}, cost L+1+r<=2L;
* P b a^(L-1)b b = {1} subset {0,1}, cost L+2<=2L.

Singletons use the reachable pair {0,2} as source: b reaches 1, bb a^r
reaches c, and bb a^(L-1)b reaches 0, with costs at most L+2<=2L.
Together with the exact lower bound this proves max_S e(S)=2n-4.
Consequently e(S)<=Cn+d for all such automata forces C>=2 for ANY fixed
d; the same follows with an o(n) additive term. This is stronger than a
single finite obstruction to a literal Cn envelope. It does not refute C=2.

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--reset-and-best-policy-costs-are-only-n1"></a>
#### Reset and best-policy costs are only n+1

Q needs at least two letters to first drop to {1,2}: its first b has rank
3, and the first triple-to-pair drop always yields that pair. The earliest
pair-to-singleton merge then costs L+1 as above. Thus rt>=L+3, matching
the displayed reset word. In particular the long extension is local.

The singleton 1 has e=1 via {0,2} and b. The pair {0,2} has e=L+1:
the proof above requires L letters from {1,2} to first reach {0,2}, whereas
a singleton in that target costs at least L+2; prepend the first triple
drop. P is an allowed endpoint of this shortest extension. Finally P has
e=1 via Q and b. This exact policy chain costs 1+(L+1)+1=L+3. Since
rt<=P_best, it follows that P_best=rt=n+1 for every n>=4. No policy
square counterexample follows from max e=2n-4.

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--ordinary-cardinality-extension-misses-the-image-deficit"></a>
#### Ordinary cardinality extension misses the image deficit

For n>=5, S has ordinary inverse-cardinality extension cost exactly n-1.
Read inversely: a^(L-1) brings S to {0,2}, b brings it to {1,n-1}, and
another b gives X={0} union (C\{n-1}), of cardinality L>2. An earlier
first b yields only {n-1}; it then needs L-1 a's, b to {1}, and b to X,
costing at least L+2 instead. Before that first b a alone preserves size.
Thus n-1=L+1 is minimal. The forward word is bb a^(L-1).

However rho(X)=2 by (R), because X omits 1 and contains no triple. Its
image deficiency is |X|-rho(X)=n-4, unbounded. So a short ordinary
extension is not an image extension here. At the excluded boundary n4,
L=2 gives no cardinality growth at X; ordinary extension cost is 4.

<a id="direct-attack-three-image-extension-theorem--verification-and-attribution-boundary"></a>
#### Verification and attribution boundary

The sparse multi-source native algorithm and an independent ordinary-set
ALL-SOURCE forward algorithm agree on EVERY e/G/worst/forward entry for
all 60 saved cases n4..63. The full closed image family, exact words, rt
and maximum e are independently checked. Three corruptions are rejected.
The arbitrary-n conclusions rest on the complete proofs above, not those
finite computations. No new Lean theorem.

Ordinary extension is a different problem with known larger lower bounds;
the image-extension formulation itself is known from
[Kisielewicz--Szykula, Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
Search results for ordinary 2n-4 extension/avoiding bounds do not establish
priority for the present reachable-image capacity statement. Novelty remains
OPEN; no exhaustive literature-priority conclusion is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension--a-weighted-target-for-the-unresolved-order-two-model"></a>
### A weighted target for the unresolved order-two model

2026-10-03. General Cerny OPEN. The target below is CONJECTURED / OPEN;
the algebra and its conditional square implication are PROVED paper.
No result in this note is FORMALLY VERIFIED.

Later progress: [Original square resets from paired output differences](#direct-attack-weighted-graph-square) proves WEXT and square for all
primitive paired output-difference inputs, hence every PRIME half-core L,
and gives a broader all-n sufficient graph criterion. Separate complete
M8/M12 graph audits now supplement the TSV scopes below. Automatic
all-input connectivity of that original graph is now REFUTED in
[A residual graph can fail while the actual extension is short](#direct-attack-weighted-graph-automaticity-barrier); general WEXT remains OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension--original-model-and-exact-mass"></a>
#### Original model and exact mass

Let M=2L>=6, Q=Z_M union {r}, b(q)=q+1 on the core and b(r)=r.
The ORIGINAL letter a satisfies a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r, and is any
bijection of the other M-2 core states onto themselves. Pair-splitting
is equivalent to synchronization, as proved in the prior order-two work.
All costs here count original a and b; no derived letter has unit cost.

Give each core state weight 1 and r weight 2. Write
nu=(1,...,1,2), mu(S)=|S|+1_{r in S}, and delta=e_0-e_L.
Direct output counting proves

    nu P_a - nu = delta,       nu P_b = nu,
    delta P_a = 0,             delta P_b^L = -delta.

Consequently nu P_a^k=nu+delta for EVERY k>=1, and

    (nu P_a + nu P_(a b^L))/2 = nu.

This is a stationarity identity for two ACTUAL WORDS of lengths 1 and
L+1. It is not a positive original-letter stationarity assertion and
does not supply a free linear extension theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension--target-and-compatible-implication"></a>
#### Target and compatible implication

**(WEXT), CONJECTURED / OPEN.** For every synchronizing input in this
model and every nonempty proper S subset Q, an original word w of cost
at most M satisfies mu(S w^-1)>mu(S).

If U=S intersect Z_M is not a union of opposite pairs, choose
j in U with j+L outside U. The ACTUAL word a b^j, 0<=j<M, gives
mass gain 1 and costs j+1<=M, whatever the root flag. Thus only the
2^(L+1)-2 proper nonempty whole-pair/root patterns require WEXT.

**PROVED paper, conditional:** WEXT implies ONE reset word of cost
at most M^2=(n-1)^2. Begin with {r}, of mass 2. Every inverse extension
increases integral mass by at least 1; total mass is M+2, so at most M
extensions are needed. Prepend each actual extension word to the prior
suffix. The final inverse image is Q, hence the concatenation resets
every original state to r and costs at most M*M. The root need not
remain in intermediate sets; its weight accounts for this possibility.

**PROVED paper local case:** a whole-pair S whose a-preimage T is not
whole has an extension within M. Since delta(S)=0, mu(T)=mu(S) is
even; the core of T has even size, so at least TWO opposite pairs split
in T. There are at least two positive orientations j, and one has
j<=M-2. Then a b^j a has cost j+2<=M and mass gain
delta P_b^j P_a chi_S=delta P_b^j chi_T=1.
This does not bound the first split after a longer word.

The TSV checker uses original forward particle maps for every retained

the factorial input count. Nonsync rows have a literal stable quotient
on opposite pairs plus root, with both induced letters permutations.

| 10 | COMPLETE | 40320 | 39936 | 2476032 |

| 14 | sampled | 5000 | 5000 | 1270000 |
| 16 | sampled | 2000 | 2000 | 1020000 |

These word upper bounds and resets are COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED for

Separate structured/hill searches favor permutations that split few

full Bellman checks over every subset: exact weighted minima 11 at M12,
13 at M14, and 12 at M16. The 42656/18898/4790 evaluated proposal counts
are EXPLORATORY; no independent all-proposal coverage theorem is asserted.
No retained case refutes WEXT. Previously proved three-a pool barriers
do not control words with unrestricted a-count.

`audit_order_two_weighted_extension.py` captures eleven actual commands,
checks all five TSV scopes and three peak Bellman arrays, rejects seven
corrupted TSVs, and protects all 35 prior release/Lean files by hash.
Its separate receipt is `data/order_two_weighted_extension_audit.json`;
neither the historical registry nor the ten-unit release is regenerated.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension--a-precise-limit-of-generalization"></a>
#### A precise limit of generalization

The same weighted M-extension assertion for ALL rank-one root/core
models is REFUTED. In the synchronizing reflection example M5,n6,

    a=[5,5,4,3,2,0], b=[1,2,3,4,0,5], S=Z_5,

mu(S)=5 and the minimum weighted positive extension is 6>M, attained
by a b a b^2 a. Its a/b-preimage removes only one core state, yielding
mass 6. The complement {r} has minimum weighted shrink 6; an independent
literal cut of eleven vertices proves every word of length<=5 fails,
checks the witness and synchronization, and rejects four corruptions.
See `data/weighted_extension_reflection_barrier.json` and its checker.
This is COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED, not FORMALLY VERIFIED, and it is not
an order-two WEXT counterexample or a Cerny counterexample.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension--remaining-obstacle"></a>
#### Remaining obstacle

When successive preimages remain whole, the first pair split can be
delayed. A signed defect may be available only after a long prefix;
switching its sign by b^L adds L original letters. Neither a dimension
argument with uncharged derived letters nor the averaged paired quotient
proves the required M cost. General WEXT, the unresolved c0,t2 square,
and the unrestricted Cerny conjecture remain OPEN.
