<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--two-neutral-singular-steps-can-be-unavoidable-in-a-simple-circular-dfa"></a>
### Two neutral singular steps can be unavoidable in a simple circular DFA

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for EVERY odd m>=3, n=2m.
Finite exact reset lengths and minimum singular-letter counts have separate
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** scopes. General Cerny, any general bound on
neutral-step costs, and formal verification remain **OPEN**. Priority of
this construction and precise lower bound is **OPEN**. The elementary
corank inequalities and the known circular-automaton theorem are not new.

The assertion that one may restrict a general square proof to reset words
whose total original-letter corank is exactly n-1 is **REFUTED**, even for
simple strongly connected binary circular automata. This strengthens the
boundary of [Rank-loss saturation preserves optimal histories under permutation augmentation](#direct-attack-optimal-saturation-transfer); its sufficient saturation
theorems are unaffected. This is NOT a Cerny counterexample.

<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--original-letters-and-a-general-matching-obstruction"></a>
#### Original letters and a general matching obstruction

On Q={0,...,2m-1} let a(q)=q+1 mod 2m. The only other original letter f is

    f(0)=1, f(1)=f(m+1)=m, f(2)=m+1, f(m)=2,
    f(q)=q at all other states.

It has rank n-1, excluded state 0, duplicate state m, and kernel pair
{1,m+1}. All occurrences of a and f below cost one. Define antipodal
blocks C_j={j,j+m}, with indices j taken modulo m.

For any target S the exact inverse cardinality change is

    |f^-1(S)|-|S| = 1_(m in S)-1_(0 in S).               (1)

Thus every union of whole C_j has zero inverse change. Rotating by a
preserves the family of whole blocks. The first inverse growth from a
singleton, whenever it occurs, has target {m} and gives C_1. Another
growth is impossible until at least one NEUTRAL inverse f occurs.
Consequently every reset word uses at least n copies of f.

This first obstruction is general: if a permutation alphabet preserves
a perfect matching, and every corank-one original letter has its kernel
pair equal to a matching block and its excluded/duplicate states in one
matching block, every reset on n>=4 needs a neutral singular step. There
is no connectivity hypothesis in this conditional statement. It does
not assert synchronization of all such alphabets.

<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--a-second-neutral-step-is-necessary-for-m5"></a>
#### A second neutral step is necessary for m>=5

**PROVED.** Every reset word uses at least n+1 copies of f for m>=5.
For an inverse singleton-to-Q trajectory write g,u,d for the numbers of
growing, neutral and decreasing f occurrences. Equation (1) gives

    g-d=n-1,        number of f = n-1+u+2d.              (2)

Suppose at most n copies occur. There are no decreases and at most one
neutral occurrence. The preceding matching obstruction consumes that
one neutral at cardinality two; an earlier neutral cannot escape the
block obtained by the first growth.

Directly from the ORIGINAL row,

    f^-1(C_1)={0,2},       f^-1(C_2)={m,m+2};
    f^-1(C_j) is a whole antipodal block for all other j. (3)

To permit a later growth with no neutral budget left, that sole neutral
must therefore produce a pair of cyclic separation two. Its next
growing rotation has target either {m,m+2} or {m-2,m}. The corresponding
preimages are respectively

    C_1 union {m+2},        C_1 union {m-2}.             (4)

In either triple the whole antipodal pair contributes zero to (1).
A subsequent growth must rotate the extra singleton to m; there is
exactly one such rotation. The resulting four-set is respectively

    C_1 union C_(m-1),      C_1 union C_3.               (5)

These are unions of TWO distinct blocks for m>=5. All subsequent
permutation rotations remain balanced, so no fifth inverse growth is
possible without another neutral f. Since n>=10, Q has not been reached.
This contradiction proves the bound. The exceptional m=3 is deliberately
excluded from this second argument: its special row entries overlap the
otherwise fixed states used in (5).

Equivalently, EVERY forward reset trajectory uses at least two f steps
that do NOT decrease its current image rank. Each decreasing f loses
exactly one point and a loses none, so only n-1 f occurrences can decrease
rank over the entire reset. This is a universal statement about ALL
reset words of this family, with no shortest-word or greedy assumption.

<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--strong-connectivity-simplicity-and-an-explicit-square-reset"></a>
#### Strong connectivity, simplicity and an explicit square reset

The original a-cycle proves strong connectivity. Every equivalence
invariant under a is a residue partition modulo a divisor d of n.
For each proper nontrivial divisor 1<d<n, necessarily d<=m:

* d=m is broken by the equivalent inputs 0,m, whose f-images are 1,2.
* d=2 is broken by 0,2: m is odd, so f(0)=1 and f(2)=m+1 have different
  parities.
* For 3<=d<m, f(d)=d, whereas f(0)=1; equivalent inputs 0,d split.

Thus every such congruence is broken and the DFA is SIMPLE.

Now take the ACTUAL original word v=f f a^(m-1), of length m+1.
Its row is

    v(0)=v(2)=2m-1,     v(1)=v(m+1)=m+1,    v(m)=0,
    v(q)=q+m-1 mod 2m at all other states.               (6)

The root m+1 is fixed. Since m is odd, the ordinary shift by m-1 has
one cycle on each parity class. In the odd class the row in (6) follows

    2m-1, m-2, 2m-3, m-4, ..., m+2, 1, then root;

this visits every odd state other than m, and the distance from 2m-1
to the root is m-1. State m instead goes to 0, then 2m-1, giving height
m+1. In the even class, the ordinary shift cycle is

    0, m-1, 2m-2, m-3, ..., m+3, 2, m+1, then 0.

The modified arrows send 0 and 2 into the odd path and fix m+1.
The longest remaining even segment starts at m-1 and ends at 2,
giving height 2m-3. All states therefore reach the root, with EXACT
rooted height

    H=4 if m=3;       H=2m-3 for odd m>=5.              (7)

Hence v^H resets ALL Q, with fully charged ORIGINAL length

    16 for m=3;       (m+1)(2m-3)=2m^2-m-3 for m>=5.   (8)

At m=3 the square slack is 9. Otherwise the slack is
(2m-1)^2-(2m^2-m-3)=2m^2-3m+4>0. Synchronization and this square
witness are proved directly; no inferred free inverse or added
permutation is used. Circular automata already satisfy Cerny's bound by
Dubuc's established theorem; no new positive class bound is claimed here.

For m=3, f a^3 f^2 a^2 f^2 a^2 f resets to 3. Its prefix-image masks are
63,62,61,59,55,58,44,25,50,40,36,9,18,8. It uses six f's, so the general
matching lower bound proves the exact minimum f-count SIX on paper.
Its unweighted minimum length THIRTEEN is a separate finite BFS result.

<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--what-is-and-is-not-established-about-the-slack"></a>
#### What is and is not established about the slack

The corank slack delta=number(f)-(n-1) is at least one for m=3, and
at least two for every odd m>=5. In complete finite audits at

    n          6    10    14    18
    rt        13    28    45    63
    min #f     6    11    15    19

the two-neutral lower bound is attained at n10/14/18. Minimum f-count
and minimum ORIGINAL length are different objectives: the retained
minimum-f words are longer, and are not asserted shortest in length.
Exact minimum f=n+1 for EVERY odd m>=5 remains **CONJECTURED**; no
all-parameter upper certificate with only two neutral steps is supplied.
Exact arbitrary-m reset threshold and any growing-slack lower bound
remain **OPEN**.

Positive slack does NOT imply a positive prefix-image/suffix-preimage
gap at any particular cut. This result must not be misreported as
refuting the existence of histories whose cuts are actual images.
Nor does it refute a slack-aware quadratic bound. Its obstruction is
the narrower restriction to total corank exactly n-1.

<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--independent-verification-and-provenance"></a>
#### Independent verification and provenance

antipodal_corank_slack.py builds the direct row, forward shortest-word
BFS and the zero-cost permutation-necklace quotient for minimum f.
check_antipodal_corank_slack.py instead builds a five-cycle permutation
followed by a source overwrite, uses ordinary set preimages and reverse
unweighted/0-1 BFS on FULL subsets, and recomputes every literal word.
It separately searches all inverse trajectories with at most one
neutral f and no decreases. At n10/14/18 their maximum size is four;
with no neutral it is two. These finite checks corroborate the two
paper obstructions rather than supplying the arbitrary-m proof.

Thirty-six parameters through n2050 check 2,881,864 literal macro
state/letter controls, balanced block preimages, both triple-growth
cases, congruence failures and rooted graph heights. The four exact
scopes use 277,186 unweighted and 278,690 weighted reverse vertices,
394 bounded-slack vertices, and reject seven corruptions. This is
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**, not **FORMALLY VERIFIED**. The continuation
registry adds one checker and one regeneration command to checkpoint107;
it does not claim a full rerun of every historical check.

Source context: [Szykula 2026, Section 2.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245)
discusses length versus dimension and the transitive corank-one class;
[Zhu 2024](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.08135) separates the defect cone
from the escape needed out of its orthogonal space. These explain why
neutral movement must remain available. This source comparison is not
an exhaustive priority audit of the present family.

<a id="direct-attack-antipodal-corank-slack--post-commit-pressure-and-the-remaining-fixed-slack-repair"></a>
#### Post-commit pressure and the remaining fixed-slack repair

An ignored adaptive cyclic/antipodal rank-one search then maximized the
minimum number of ORIGINAL singular occurrences at n6/8/10/12/14.
It found no required slack above two. This exploration is saved under
native_build/antipodal_slack_maximize.py and its JSON; it has NOT been
independently sealed and establishes no universal upper bound. In
particular a fixed additive slack repair has not been refuted, and
this finite search must not be repeated as if it were a new theorem.

For the explicit family there is also the elementary identity

    f^3: 0->2, 1->m+1, every other state fixed.

Indeed f cycles m,2,m+1 and its two transient states0,1 enter that
cycle. Its third power is therefore a product of two disjoint unit
maps and is idempotent of rank n-2. This may aid an eventual minimum-f
upper construction, but it costs THREE original letters. Replacing f
by two free unit generators would change the problem and erase the
forced-neutral obstruction. No exact arbitrary-m min-f upper, growing
slack, or general length improvement was obtained from this repair.

[Full singleton orbit span in a minimal corank-one automaton](#direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability) further proves that this SIMPLE
SC rank-one family has FULL n-dimensional singleton inverse orbit span
when ALL alternative words are admitted. That general paper theorem
does not bound neutral-word costs. It was added after checkpoint108;
the historical108/192 verification boundary is unchanged.

<a id="direct-attack-circular-rank-area-barrier"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-circular-rank-area-barrier--optimizing-every-reset-trajectory-still-leaves-a-cubic-rank-budget"></a>
### Optimizing every reset trajectory still leaves a cubic rank budget

**PROVED on paper.** On the classical Cerny DFA C_n, n>=3, EVERY reset
word has the rank-trajectory budget B(w)>(n-1)^2. In fact the minimum
possible rank area over ALL reset words is (1/2)n^3+O(n^2), so minimizing
the previous budget over arbitrary words still gives a cubic value.
This refutes the proposed universal existence of a reset trajectory
certifying the policy square. It fails at state-minimal n3, even binary.
C_n itself has rt=P=(n-1)^2: the failure is of this certificate route.
Priority of this weighted formulation is OPEN; classical C_n extremality
and inverse-interval arguments are known mechanisms. No Lean claim.

Let a be the n-cycle and b fix every state except n-1, which maps to 0.
Its largest proper image rank is r=n-1. Write A(w)=area_(n-1)(w).
We prove, for n>=2,

    (n-2)[n(n-3)/2+2] <= min_reset_w A(w)
                         <= (n-2)[n(n-1)/2+1].

The exact equality with the upper expression is CONJECTURED for arbitrary
n, and COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED only at n2..14. The two proved expressions
already agree in their cubic leading term; no exact extrapolation is used.

<a id="direct-attack-circular-rank-area-barrier--cardinality-only-lower-bound-for-resetting-any-subset"></a>
#### Cardinality-only lower bound for resetting any subset

Under reversed inverse actions, the preimage of a singleton is always
empty or a circular interval until it becomes Q. Inverse a rotates its
left endpoint down by one modulo n. Inverse b fixes the interval, grows
its left endpoint from 0 to n-1, deletes its right endpoint n-1, or
empties a singleton. Deletions do not change the left endpoint, and an
empty preimage never recovers. Thus after one growth, the next growth
requires at least n-1 inverse a steps; intervening deletions do not help.

If |S|=k>=2 and Su is a singleton, the full inverse image of that
singleton under u contains S and has cardinality >=k. Starting at rank
one requires at least k-1 growth steps. Ignoring any initial rotations,
there are at least k-2 intergrowth gaps, each of length >=n-1. Hence

    |u| >= (k-1)+(k-2)(n-1) = (k-2)n+1.

This is a lower bound for EVERY k-subset, not merely actual images,
and includes arbitrary deletions, extra growths, and reset endpoints.

<a id="direct-attack-circular-rank-area-barrier--every-reset-trajectory-has-large-area"></a>
#### Every reset trajectory has large area

Letter a preserves rank and b decreases it by at most one. Every reset
trajectory therefore visits every rank k=2,...,n-1. In the notation of
[Reset rank trajectories bound every shortest-image seed policy](#direct-attack-reset-rank-profile-budget), the prefix immediately after t_k has rank
exactly k. Its remaining suffix resets that k-set. The preceding lower
bound implies

    L_k-1 >= (k-2)n+1;     L_k >= (k-2)n+2.

Summing gives the displayed area lower bound. The usual reset
word b(a^(n-1)b)^(n-2) attains the upper area expression: its first
b has cost 1; while rank is n-h, the n-1 rotations cost h each,
and the following b costs min(h+1,n-2), h=1,...,n-2.
The resulting sum is (n-2)[n(n-1)/2+1]. This proves a cubic barrier
even if the optimizing reset word is longer than a shortest reset.

For r=n-1, the rank-area square threshold is (n-2)(n+1)/2. The proved
lower bound exceeds it by

    (n-2)(n-1)(n-3)/2,

strictly positive at every n>=4. At n3, every letter after the first
b has area cost one; leading a's can be discarded. Growing a singleton
inverse image to Q requires two b's and two a's, so A>=4 and B>=6>4.
At n2, r1 has area zero and B=1, establishing the arbitrary-alphabet
state minimum n3 (n1 is the separate zero-length base).

<a id="direct-attack-circular-rank-area-barrier--independent-finite-primaldual-certificates"></a>
#### Independent finite primal/dual certificates

rank_area minimizes the pair (area,length) on the COMPLETE actual-image
graph, without restricting to shortest reset words or extension phases.
At n2..14 it records every node value and attaining predecessor. The
ordinary-set checker does not run Dijkstra: every edge satisfies the
Bellman lower certificate, each predecessor attains equality with a
strictly smaller secondary length, and the reset word attains the best
singleton pair. These certify the global optimum over ALL reset words.
It separately computes ordinary reverse reset BFS and checks the subset
lower bound on EVERY vertex. There are 32751 vertices,65502 edges and
five corruption rejections, including an out-of-range parent mask and
a negative word token. Arbitrary-n claims follow from the proof,
while the exact polynomial remains a finite observation.

The loss is the uniform rank-envelope summation: it charges every rank
tail from a reset trajectory, even when a compatible image-policy path
costs only the square. Global charging must retain more target/source
compatibility than this scalar trajectory area.

<a id="direct-attack-connected-transposition-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-connected-transposition-square--a-connected-transposition-alphabet-and-any-singular-letter-satisfy-the-square"></a>
### A connected transposition alphabet and any singular letter satisfy the square

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)**. Priority is **OPEN**, not asserted.
Bounded independent checks are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**, with no
**FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. The unrestricted Cerny conjecture is **OPEN**.

Let a DFA on n>=2 states contain, as ORIGINAL letters, the transposition
of the endpoints of every edge of a connected undirected graph G, and
an ORIGINAL singular letter b of rank r<n. Other letters can be ignored.
No idempotence assumption on b is made. The whole class satisfies Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-connected-transposition-square--a-charged-two-token-transport-lemma"></a>
#### A charged two-token transport lemma

For any k-set S, k>=2, and any distinct prescribed p,q, a word g of
original edge transpositions puts BOTH p,q in Sg, within 2(n-k) letters.

First recall the elementary token bound on a tree with N vertices:
any two k-token configurations can be transformed into each other in
at most k(N-k) edge swaps. Induct on N, fixing a leaf. If its occupancy
already agrees, delete it and apply induction. Otherwise bring a nearest
hole to an occupied leaf (cost <=k), or a nearest token to an empty leaf
(cost <=N-k). All intermediate vertices have the opposite occupancy.
Delete the now correct leaf; the respective remaining bounds are
k(N-k-1) and (k-1)(N-k). Each sums with its paid path to k(N-k).
All swaps are original letters, and already fixed leaves are untouched.

Choose a simple path from p to q. If it contains at least two S-points,
move its first token back to p and its last token forward to q. Their
edge segments are disjoint and initially contain only holes between the
token and endpoint, so cost is at most the total n-k holes.
If it contains at most one S-point, grow a tree from that path, adding
one vertex at a time, until it contains exactly two S-points. This is
possible since G is connected and |S|>=2. Its N vertices consist of two
tokens and at most n-k holes, so N<=n-k+2. The tree token bound with k=2
puts those tokens at {p,q} within 2(N-2)<=2(n-k) swaps. Every S-point
outside this tree stays fixed. This proves simultaneous containment.

Take p,q in the SAME fiber of b. Append b to this charged transport,
to obtain the uniform compression bound in this class:

    c(S)<=2(n-|S|)+1.                                   (A)

Begin with b, whose actual image has size r. Repeatedly use (A) on the
current image, paying the same actual word on all its points. Rank skips
only omit positive costs. Thus

    rt<=1+sum_(k=2)^r [2(n-k)+1]
      =1+(r-1)(2n-r-1)<=(n-1)^2.                       (B)

The final inequality is monotonicity in 1<=r<=n-1, whose last value
is 1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2. This proves automatic synchronization and a
constructive square reset for ANY singular b, not just rank n-1.

<a id="direct-attack-connected-transposition-square--a-sharper-inverse-routing-statement-for-rank-n-1"></a>
#### A sharper inverse routing statement for rank n-1

When r=n-1, let d be the unique duplicated output and e the unique
missing output. Write D=dist_G(e,d).

<a id="direct-attack-connected-transposition-square--routing-one-included-and-one-excluded-point"></a>
##### Routing one included and one excluded point

For every proper nonempty k-set S there is a word g over those original
edge swaps such that e is outside Sg and d is inside Sg, with

    |g|<=max{k,n-k,D}<=n-1.                             (1)

Proof uses four cases.

* If e is outside and d is inside, use the empty word.
* If both are inside, choose a shortest path from e to an outside point.
  All its intermediate vertices are inside. Move the hole back to e by
  reversing its edge sequence. Every intermediate vertex stays inside,
  so d stays inside, even if it is on this path. Cost <=k.
* If both are outside, choose a shortest path from d to an inside point
  and move that token back to d. All intermediate vertices remain outside,
  so e stays outside. Cost <=n-k.
* If e is inside and d is outside, choose a shortest path from e to d,
  of length D. Let f be the first outside position on it. Move this hole
  back to e, using f swaps. If d is now inside, finish. Otherwise position
  f is now inside. Let t>=f be the last inside position along the path;
  move that token forward to d, using D-t swaps. The two edge segments
  are disjoint. e remains outside and total cost f+D-t<=D.

This is simultaneous transport of the whole set by one actual word,
not independently chosen paths for its points.

<a id="direct-attack-connected-transposition-square--exact-preimage-gain-and-a-compatible-reset"></a>
##### Exact preimage gain and a compatible reset

For any T, the rank n-1 fiber counts give the exact identity

    |T b^-1|-|T|=1_(d in T)-1_(e in T).                 (2)

Choose g from (1). Its inverse is available at the SAME charged cost:
reverse the actual edge word, since each original transposition is an
involution. The word u=b g^-1 has length <=1+max{k,n-k,D}. Its full
preimage of S is (Sg)b^-1, of size k+1 by (2), and u maps this larger
set ONTO S. Every letter of g^-1 is paid; no abstract group inverse is
inserted for free.

Start from {d} and the one-letter preimage {d}b^-1 of size two. Repeat
these actual onto extensions until Q. Reading the resulting words in
the reverse phase order gives a whole-Q reset, with bound

    rt<=1+sum_(k=2)^(n-1) [1+max{k,n-k,D}]
      <=1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2.                              (3)

The sum is empty at n=2. This proves automatic synchronization and the
Cerny square for this precisely realized alphabet. The cardinal bound
in (1) is useful when D<n-1; graph diameter is not confused with the
diameter of the entire permutation group in original generators.

The hypothesis is stronger than merely having group S_n or a transitive
group in the transition monoid. If edge transpositions are LONG words,
their lengths must be paid and (3) need not imply the square. The
INVERSE proof does not apply to arbitrary lower-rank b: its fiber
imbalance is no longer one positive and one negative unit. The forward
two-token proof (A)--(B) still applies. The exact quadratic actual-
image obstruction in [Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction) already
uses an original connected transposition alphabet but rank n/2.

[Arnold--Steinberg, Theorem 5.1 and concluding examples](https://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~margolis/Representation%20Theory%20Seminar/Monoid%20Representations%20and%20Applications/synchronizing%20groups.pdf)
give group-diameter reset bounds and discuss all-transposition versus
adjacent-transposition generating sets. The extension strategy is
established. The proof here is a direct, target-dependent routing
argument, together with a forward two-token proof for arbitrary rank;
no claim of publication novelty
or a new unrestricted result is made.

Independent check_transposition_fold_obstruction.py covers ALL connected
labeled graphs on n2..5 (771 graphs), all their ordered distinct endpoint
pairs and nontrivial subsets (443332 routing cases), and separately
recomputes exact routing costs by multi-source subset BFS. It also builds
and literally applies resets for ALL labeled rank n-1 rows on every
connected graph through n4 (5546 DFA inputs). It additionally checks
191837 prescribed-pair containment cases on the n2..5 connected graphs
and builds literal FORWARD resets for ALL singular labeled rows through
n4 (8902 DFA inputs). These counts describe
covering inputs, not isomorphism classes. The paper proves the all-n
statement; no finite cover is represented as such a proof.

<a id="direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement--coprime-root-displacement-and-a-necessary-amortized-boundary"></a>
### Coprime root displacement, and a necessary amortized boundary

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), arbitrary n/alphabet under explicit
fixed-root hypotheses.** Refines [A paid n-extension theorem for a fixed common defect root](#direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension).
No novelty or FORMALLY VERIFIED claim; priority OPEN. General Cerny
and the noncoprime/root-moving routes remain **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement--replace-adjacency-by-a-coprime-displacement"></a>
#### Replace adjacency by a coprime displacement

Keep all original-letter assumptions of the fixed-root theorem except
b(r)=s. Instead require r,s to lie on the SAME original b-cycle R,
p=|R|, with s=b^delta(r), 1<=delta<p, and gcd(delta,p)=1.
Permutational controls still preserve R as a set, and every singular
control has omitted r, fixed s, kernel{r,s}, and a permutation on Q\{r}.
At least one singular original letter is present. The original DFA is SC.

Then EVERY proper nonempty subset extends by EXACTLY one in ORIGINAL
cost<=n, and ONE compatible reset has cost<=1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2.

The preparatory routing proof is unchanged: root-full/root-empty
preimages have zero cardinality change; minimum distance in the original
b-cycle graph strictly decreases; each selected non-root cycle is paid
once, totaling<=n-p. It does not require adjacency, only r,s in R.

For the final mixed-root step, let x_i=1_V(b^i(r)), i modulo p.
The sum of differences x_(i+delta)-x_i is zero. If every difference
were zero, gcd(delta,p)=1 would make the entire cyclic pattern constant,
contrary to R being mixed. Thus some difference is POSITIVE, meaning
b^k(r) is absent and b^k(s) is present for some0<=k<p. The original
word f b^k has exact preimage growth1 and cost k+1<=p. Preparation
plus growth is<=n, as before. No b^delta macro is paid as a unit letter.

The seed {s} f^-1={r,s} still costs1. The support's exceptional edge
r->s still lies on the same b-cycle, so every underlying edge is on
a directed cycle and synchronizing inputs of these types are already
SC. Thus the square theorem also applies to all SYNC inputs of this
class without a separate SC hypothesis.

The original adjacency theorem is delta1. This is a genuine weakening
of its hypotheses, not an assertion that the general fixed-root class
is n-extensible. The cyclic sign argument also identifies exactly why
coprimality is sufficient. The standard extension framework is attributed
in [A paid n-extension theorem for a fixed common defect root](#direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension); no specific literature priority claim
is added here.

<a id="direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement--dropping-coprimality-fails-even-on-the-unavoidable-seed"></a>
#### Dropping coprimality fails even on the unavoidable seed

**REFUTED:** the same n-extension claim for every SC SYNC fixed-root
input, without coprimality. The FIRST tested relevant n5 proposal gives

    a=[1,1,3,2,4], b=[4,2,0,3,1], U={0,1}.

Here r0,s1, a fixes s; R=(0,4,1,2) has p4 and delta2, gcd2.
The original DFA is SC sync with EXACT ordinary rt13<square16.
But U's EXACT minimum extension cost is6>5. This U is the only
two-point seed supplied by the final singular original letter, so
the issue is not confined to an irrelevant arbitrary subset.

Independent positive-cost Bellman equations cover ALL32 subset vertices
for the extension-to-size>2 target problem, and a literal length6 word
attains it. A separate ALL32 ordinary-image distance certificate gives
rt13 and a matching original reset. The obstruction is finite and is
not a Cerny counterexample or a refutation of amortized growth.

In fact the independently reconstructed optimal reset is

    a b^3 a b a b^3 a b a,

of length13. Read its preimages backward from {1}: the initial a gives
{0,1} at cost1; the next growth factor a b^3 a b costs6 and gives
{0,1,2}; then a b costs2 and gives{0,1,3,4}; finally a b^3 costs4
and gives Q. The compatible positive growth costs are therefore

    1 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 13.

The first stage exceeds n, while later stages compensate. A universal
cap on each stage is false; a bound on one compatible sum is still
possible and still OPEN in general.

<a id="direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement--independent-finite-scope"></a>
#### Independent finite scope

398 retained inputs:ALL348 coprime binary pairs n2..5, plus50 sampled
nonadjacent coprime SC inputs n6..10. Independent checks certify293
SC inputs,207 nonadjacent,127 multicycle-b inputs,ALL26762 proper-subset
witnesses,1316620 literal particle/letter controls,32 counter extension
and52 ordinary Bellman edges, and eight rejected corruptions.

The checker imports no generator or shortest-path solver. It reuses
ONLY the preceding independent literal checker routines for paid cycle
descent, then independently checks coprime hypotheses, complete finite
pair coverage, sample counts, original-label words, compatible resets
and both counter Bellman systems. Its deletion-corruption self-test
initially caught a missing sample-count assertion; the assertion was
added and all eight corruptions now fail. These are finite
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** controls. The arbitrary-n theorem is
paper, not a finite extrapolation or a FORMALLY VERIFIED statement.

Research should now confront compatibility and amortized costs in
noncoprime or moving-root cases, rather than repeating the proven
coprime routing or the two refuted universal n-extension shortcuts.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability--full-singleton-orbit-span-in-a-minimal-corank-one-automaton"></a>
### Full singleton orbit span in a minimal corank-one automaton

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)**. This is an elementary representation
theorem, not a reset-length bound. Its priority is **OPEN**; no novelty,
**FORMALLY VERIFIED**, or new computational census claim is made.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability--the-general-statement"></a>
#### The general statement

Let A be a synchronizing n-state DFA, q a state reachable from a reset
endpoint, and M_w its deterministic row transition matrix. Suppose
every original letter has rank n or n-1. Set

    V_q=span_Q{ M_w chi_q : w is ANY original word },

where chi_q is a column singleton indicator. Suppose the observations
distinguish every two states: for s!=t some word w has exactly one of
sw,tw equal to q. Then

    V_q=Q^n.                                              (1)

In particular (1) holds for EVERY q in any SIMPLE strongly connected
synchronizing DFA whose letters all have rank at least n-1.

**Proof.** Let W=V_q^perp be the space of row annihilators. Prepending
an original letter preserves V_q, so W M_a is contained in W for each
letter a. Since a reset endpoint reaches q, there is a reset word to q;
its singleton inverse indicator is 1_Q. Thus V_q contains 1_Q and
every row in W has sum zero.

No pair difference e_s-e_t belongs to W: membership would say that s,t
have identical q-observations for EVERY word, contrary to the hypothesis.
For a permutation letter the row kernel of M_a is zero. For a rank-n-1
letter its row kernel is precisely span(e_s-e_t), where {s,t} is its
unique colliding pair. Consequently W intersects the row kernel of
EVERY original letter trivially. Each letter restricts to an injective
endomorphism of the finite-dimensional invariant space W, and therefore
is invertible on W. Every word is then injective on W.

A reset matrix, however, sends x to (sum x)e_r for its endpoint r,
and hence kills every x in W. Injectivity forces W=0, proving (1).

For the simple-automaton corollary, identical q-observations define a
right congruence: append any letter to a distinguishing continuation.
It cannot be universal since the empty word distinguishes q from every
other state. Simplicity therefore makes it equality. Strong connectivity
supplies the required route from a reset endpoint to q. QED.

This proof concerns the span of ALL alternative words. A single shortest
history need not span n dimensions: [Every optimal history can have only logarithmic dimension](#direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history)
already gives an infinite simple corank-one family with logarithmic
rank on EVERY shortest history. There is no contradiction. Nor is there
a bound here on the lengths of words whose inverse indicators form a
basis. The standard orbit-span chain finds a basis within n-1 layers,
but those vectors can correspond to different words; splicing them
into one inexpensive reset remains the general compatibility problem.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability--a-general-corank-obstruction-without-the-rank-one-hypothesis"></a>
#### A general corank obstruction without the rank-one hypothesis

Under the same observation and reset-endpoint hypotheses, if W is
nonzero, some ORIGINAL letter must act noninjectively on W. Otherwise
their reset product could not kill W. No rank-n-1 letter can do so,
because its kernel is a pair difference excluded by observability.
Thus any such rank deficit requires an original letter of corank at
least TWO. This does not imply that every high-corank letter creates
a deficit, or give an unweighted length bound.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability--hand-checkable-sharp-boundary-at-corank-two"></a>
#### Hand-checkable sharp boundary at corank two

Five states with ORIGINAL rows

    a=(1,2,3,4,1),        b=(2,0,0,1,1)

give a simple strongly connected synchronizing DFA. Letter a has rank4;
b has rank3, corank TWO. The main a-cycle is 1,2,3,4; state0 enters it,
and b brings 1/2 back to0. The word b a b a b resets:

    Q -> {0,1,2} -> {1,2,3} -> {0,1} -> {1,2} -> {0}.

Simplicity can be checked without a census. An adjacent pair on the
four-cycle forces all four states equivalent by rotation, and then b
adds0. An opposite pair rotates to the other opposite pair; applying b
to {1,3} identifies0,1, which under a yields the adjacent pair1,2.
If0 is identified with i, a^4 gives1 equivalent to i. For i!=1 this
reduces to the preceding cycle pairs; for i=1, a already gives1~2.
Every distinct pair therefore generates the universal congruence.

The row x=e_1-e_2+e_3-e_4 satisfies

    x M_a=-x,       x M_b=0,       x chi_0=0.

Hence x annihilates EVERY original-word preimage of0 and dim V_0<=4.
Four actual inverse indicators in V_0 are

    chi_{0},  chi_Q,  chi_{1,2},  chi_{0,1,4}.

They come respectively from the empty word, the stated reset word,
b, and a b. On coordinates0,1,2,3 their determinant is -1. Thus
dim V_0=4<5 exactly, despite simplicity and state distinguishability.
This is a paper construction and determinant proof; no state-minimal
claim over arbitrary alphabets is made.

The high-corank boundary confirms why pair distinguishability alone
does not imply full linear observability for general DFAs. It also
keeps the corank-one theorem separate from an unproved assertion about
all state-minimal Cerny counterexamples, whose letters need not have
rank n-1.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-singleton-observability--continuation-boundary"></a>
#### Continuation boundary

This paper proof was added after checkpoint108's independently checked
antipodal family. It introduces no new checker or generation command;
108/192 still describes that accumulated historical checkpoint, NOT
a computational verification of the present all-n theorem. The current
manifest covers this source and documentation. General Cerny remains
**OPEN**. Neither full orbit span nor the unavoidable neutral steps
provide the missing quadratic word-length coupling.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient--stable-kernels-and-the-canonical-group-quotient"></a>
### Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)**, arbitrary alphabet, all finite n.
The synchronization assertions are structural, with no general word-cost
bound. Reconstruction/generalization of standard stability arguments;
publication priority **OPEN**, unrestricted Cerny **OPEN**. No formal claim.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient--a-defect-one-kernel-is-stable"></a>
#### A defect-one kernel is stable

Let A be strongly connected. Other letters may have ANY ranks. If f has
rank n-1, its unique kernel pair K is stable: after EVERY original prefix
v there is an original suffix merging K v.

A rank n-1 functional graph consists of cycles and exactly one nonempty
tail attached to one cycle. There is one missing image state (the leaf)
and one double-image state (the root). If the double-image state were
off a cycle, a further cycle entry would have indegree at least2, which
is impossible. Thus the off-cycle vertices form a single tail. Write
its height h>=1, its leaf l, its height1 vertex t, and the cycle predecessor
of its root c. The kernel pair is {t,c}.

Choose an original minimum-rank image F containing l. Such an image
exists: start from ANY minimum-rank word image and use strong connectivity
to send one of its states to l. Every image of a minimum-rank image again
has minimum size r. In particular its points are pairwise unmergeable.
Then F'=F f^(h-1) has t as its ONLY off-cycle point; its other r-1 points
are cyclic. Let L be a common positive multiple of all f-cycle lengths.
The image F''=F' f^L replaces t by c and fixes all other points. The
point c is not already in F', since f would then lower its minimum rank.

These two minimum-rank images differ by exactly t/c. For ANY prefix v
and ANY fixed minimum-rank word u, both F' v u and F'' v u still have
r points. Their common r-1 points remain distinct, while their two
remaining points must coalesce: the union is mapped inside Q u, which
has only r points. Therefore t v u=c v u for EVERY v. This proves the
claim, even with the SAME u for all prefixes. The construction uses
minimum-rank existence and the possibly large cycle period L; it supplies
no short merging word.

The differing-F-clique argument and almost-group special case are standard;
see [Berlinkov--Nicaud2018, Lemmas1--3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.02154).
The broader unimodal/primitivity consequence is already known from
[Volkov2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.13317), and stable-vector methods
from [Kari2002](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/39e7/64a18388e249f90180ff37ea816d462cdf11.pdf).
None of these known qualitative synchronization results is claimed new.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient--all-letters-of-corank-at-most-one"></a>
#### All letters of corank at most one

Assume now that EVERY original letter has rank n or n-1. Let sigma be
the stability congruence. It is an equivalence relation: to merge x/y
and y/z after a prefix, first merge x/y, then merge their common image
with z using stability of y/z. Appending a letter preserves stability.

Every quotient by a congruence still has letter corank at most1. Indeed
every missing quotient class contains an original state missing from
the letter image, and different missing classes require different such
states. Strong connectivity also passes to the quotient.

Stability on A/sigma is equality. A stable pair of distinct sigma-classes
would lift to stable original points: after every prefix first merge the
quotient pair into one class, then merge inside that stable class. This
contradicts distinctness of its sigma-classes. By the defect-one lemma,
every letter on A/sigma is consequently a PERMUTATION.

Any pair merged by ANY original word must therefore already belong to
sigma: different quotient states cannot merge under permutations. Thus

    mergeability = stability = sigma.                     (1)

This is special to the stated SC and corank conditions. It need not hold
for general DFAs. Every minimum-rank word u has EXACT kernel sigma.
For one inclusion, if x sigma y but xu!=yu, stability would allow a
further merge inside the minimum-rank image Q u, contradicting minimality.
For the other, xu=yu implies mergeability and hence (1). In particular
ALL minimum-rank words have the SAME kernel and their rank is exactly
the number of stable classes.

Let beta be the least congruence whose quotient letters are permutations.
It can be computed without guessing reset words: start with singleton
classes, pass to the current quotient, join its letter kernels and all
their forward images to a congruence, and pull the joined classes back.
Repeat until every quotient letter is a permutation. Each nontrivial
round reduces the class count; there are at most n-1 rounds. Each stage
is contained in sigma, since the SC corank-one quotient kernel pairs
are stable and stability lifts through classes already inside sigma.
At termination any mergeable original pair lies in beta, by injectivity
of the permutation quotient. Hence

    beta=sigma;  A synchronizes IFF beta has one class.    (2)

This repairs the necessity failure of a SINGLE forward kernel closure:
the common-kernel chain in [Forward kernel congruence and terminal merge graphs have different boundaries](#direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary) requires
successive ORIGINAL quotient merges. It does not repair its cost problem.
Joining stable pairs or performing quotient rounds does NOT give actual
reset words of those round counts or forest label costs.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient--a-sharp-bound-on-the-stable-class-size-range"></a>
#### A sharp bound on the stable class-size range

Let s be the number of singular ORIGINAL LETTERS. For every SC input
as above, if m and M are the minimum and maximum stable class sizes,

    M-m<=s.                                               (3)

For a permutation letter, every stable class is carried bijectively to
its target class, so class sizes are preserved. For a singular letter f,
its quotient permutation phi has exactly one kernel-source class X
and one missing-image class Y. Every target class D has a UNIQUE incoming
source class C and contains all its states except the single missing
state when D=Y. Consequently

    |phi(C)|=|C|-1_(C=X)+1_(phi(C)=Y).                     (4)

Summing (4) around each phi-cycle shows that the two distinguished changes
belong to the SAME quotient cycle, or cancel in one step. Other cycles
have constant sizes. The distinguished cycle uses either a single size
or two adjacent sizes. Thus ONE singular letter can cross at most ONE
integer size boundary. A quotient path between a class of size m and
one of size M crosses each of the M-m boundaries, and each boundary
needs a distinct singular-letter type. Strong connectivity proves (3).

The bound is sharp for EVERY s>=1. Use classes C_j of size j for
j=1,...,s+1, with n=(s+1)(s+2)/2. One permutation letter g rotates every
class. The singular letter f_j exchanges C_j and C_(j+1): it sends the
j smaller-class points to the first j larger-class points, the first j
larger-class points back to their counterparts, and the final larger
point to the first smaller point. All other points are fixed. Its rank
is n-1 and its quotient is the adjacent class transposition.

The original automaton is SC because g moves within every class and the
class transpositions connect all classes. No word has rank below s+1,
since its quotient is a permutation. The ACTUAL word u_h=f_(h-1)^2 is
the unit mapping the final point of C_h to its first point, and fixes
every other point. On C_h, v_h=g^(h-1)u_h fixes0 and maps i>0 to i-1.
Thus

    w_h=u_h v_h^(h-2), |w_h|=h(h-1),                       (5)

merges C_h and preserves every class. Concatenating w_2,...,w_(s+1)
gives an original rank-(s+1) word of total charged length
s(s+1)(s+2)/3. By (1), the stable classes are exactly these C_j, and
M-m=s. This is a nonsynchronizing sharpness family, NOT a reset certificate.

<a id="direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient--boundary-checks"></a>
#### Boundary checks

The SC condition cannot be dropped: on three states take
f=(0,0,2), g=(0,2,2). Both letters have rank2, but the mergeable pair
{0,1} becomes the deadlock {0,2} under g. The two mergeable edges
{0,1}/{1,2} also fail transitivity. States0 and2 are distinct sinks.

The generator compares forward pair-reachability with repeated quotient
kernel joins. The independent checker uses COMPLETE original transformation
monoids on all recorded small SC inputs, reconstructs mergeability and
ALL minimum-rank kernels, and uses a separate bidirectional equivalence
closure for beta. The sharp families are checked from independently
constructed rows and charged class-rooted words. Finite computations
are COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED only within their recorded scopes.
No formalization, priority, short minimum-rank word or general square
bound follows from the paper proof. The main remaining problem is still
compatible ORIGINAL word costs.

Completed finite scope:28816 all-corank<=1 binary inputs n2..4,
12551 SC inputs,804310 COMPLETE original monoid transformations and
60426 ALL minimum-rank kernel controls. Separately37358 defect-one /
arbitrary-other binary inputs contain13348 SC cases,661550 monoid
transformations and432756 common-minimum-word/kernel-orbit controls.
The21 sharp parameters s1..16,20/24/32/64/128 reachn8385, with2505120
unit state/letter controls,860228 literal root controls,1556448 whole
rank-word state/letter controls and8 corruption rejections. The two
small exhaustive scopes overlap; their input counts are NOT added as
disjoint automata. This is not a fresh full116-check rerun or formal instantiation.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--protected-point-cycle-insertion"></a>
### Protected-point cycle insertion

Status: **PROVED** (paper); finite instances **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**.
Not formalized. Priority of this construction and its applications is **OPEN**.
Use right actions: S(uv)=(Su)v. This result is an obstruction to proposed
compression bounds, not an upper bound or a counterexample to Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--general-theorem"></a>
#### General theorem

Let A be a strongly connected synchronizing binary DFA on Q, with letters
a,b. Assume a is a permutation, a fixes p, b(p) != p, and S is Q-reachable,
p in S, |S|>=2. Write c=min{|w|: |Sw|<|S|}. Assume p belongs to Sw for
every word of length strictly less than c. Let M be the order of a.

For any t>=0 with gcd(t+1,M)=1, add new states N={q_1,...,q_t}, replace
a's loop at p with (p,q_1,...,q_t), and let b fix N. The resulting DFA is
strongly connected and synchronizing. Its reachable set S'=S union N has
exact compression cost c. Its corank equals that of S.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--short-word-invariant"></a>
##### Short-word invariant

For any w of length <=c, induction on prefixes gives

    S'w = Sw union N.

The assertion is immediate for b. For a, the preceding old image contains
p because that prefix has length <c. The new cycle sends the complete set
{p} union N onto itself; the other old transitions agree. Thus the lifted
and old ranks differ by exactly t through the first compression. Every
word of length <c preserves rank and an old shortest compression word
still compresses. This proves equality, not just a lower bound.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--reachability-and-connectivity"></a>
##### Reachability and connectivity

Choose a positive L with L=0 mod(t+1) and L=1 mod M, which exists by
coprimality. Replace each occurrence of a in any old word by a^L. The
encoded word acts like the old word on Q and fixes every new state. An
encoded full-Q reach word for S therefore reaches S'. Encoded old state
paths connect all old states. The new cycle connects p to every new state
and every new state to p, so the whole lifted graph is strongly connected.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--full-q-synchronization"></a>
##### Full-Q synchronization

Pick z in Q distinct from p. Strong connectivity allows an old reset word
followed by a state path that resets Q to z. Encode that word as V. Then
QV={z} and NV=N. Start by applying V to the full lifted Q. If a new state
q remains in its image, apply a^j with qa^j=p, then b, then V. The sole
selected cycle member reaching p moves into old Q under b, since b(p)!=p;
all other selected new states remain new and distinct. The old selected
state z stays old and avoids p during a^j, since it belongs to a different
permutation cycle. Finally V resets all old images to z. Exactly one new
image disappears. Repeat t times. This constructs a reset word; no claim
that this word is shortest is needed.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--reachable-corank-three-application"></a>
#### Reachable corank-three application

The independently checked twelve-state base has

    a=[2,5,8,4,1,7,3,6,9,0,10,11]
    b=[0,6,4,10,7,3,1,5,11,4,2,8]
    S=Q\{2,8,11}, p=10.

The permutation a has order 12. The word baaababbaa reaches S from Q;
aabaaabab compresses S in 9 steps. All shorter words preserve its size
and retain p. The exact pair-distance Bellman certificate, independent
set checks and the literal words are stored in
data/near_full_n12_r3/protected_witness.json. The independent checker uses
no search or lift-constructor imports.

For every n=12+t with gcd(t+1,12)=1, the theorem therefore supplies a
strongly connected synchronizing DFA and a Q-reachable (n-3)-set with
c(S')=9. There are unbounded such n.

For an unrounded universal harmonic proposal

    c(T) <= C n(n-|T|+1)/(|T|-1),

the family requires C >= 9(n-4)/(4n), hence **C>=9/4** in the limit.
In particular C=2 is false for all eligible n>36 (the saved n=46 instance
is one example). For the rounded proposal with a ceiling, every fixed
C<2 fails eventually. This family does **not** refute rounded C=2:
ceil(8n/(n-4))>=9. No statement about minimality of the C=2 counterexample
or nonexistence of stronger bases is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-cycle-insertion-theorem--limit-of-the-protected-point-approach"></a>
#### Limit of the protected-point approach

The known avoid-or-compress lemma gives c(S)<=|Q|-1 whenever a singleton
p persists in every shorter image in a strongly connected synchronizing DFA. Apply it with
A={p}: a word of length <=|Q|-1 either avoids p or compresses S. If
c(S)>|Q|-1, neither outcome is possible, a contradiction. Thus this
method cannot preserve a superlinear bottleneck from a fixed protected
base. This is a consequence of known theory, not a new avoiding bound.
Here p is avoidable: synchronization followed by a state path reaches an
old state different from p. This checks the avoiding lemma's hypothesis.

Primary source: [Szykula, Improving the Upper Bound on the Length of the
Shortest Reset Words (2018)](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol096-stacs2018/LIPIcs.STACS.2018.56/LIPIcs.STACS.2018.56.pdf).

<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square--arbitrary-rank-one-tails-at-gcdml2"></a>
### Arbitrary rank-one tails at gcd(M,L)=2

Date:2026-10-03. **PROVED (paper), ALL parameters in the stated class.**
Independent finite controls are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** separately.
The all-n theorem is not FORMALLY VERIFIED. General Cerny remains OPEN.
No novelty claim or reduction from arbitrary automata.

Let ORIGINAL b cycle C=Z_M and fix r, M>=3. ORIGINAL a has rank M,
doubled output r, a(r)=0, omitted output L in1..M-1, and any two
distinct kernel inputs K in the core. Every other core input maps
bijectively to C\{0,L}. If gcd(M,L)=2 and the automaton is synchronizing,
there is ONE ORIGINAL reset of length<=M^2=(n-1)^2. At M>=6 the proof
establishes synchronization without assuming it. Tail height and all
cycle structure of a are unrestricted. Larger alphabets inherit the
bound when the specified binary pair itself satisfies the theorem.

Together with [A kernel-return square criterion for arbitrary rank-one tails](#direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square) this proves the square bound
for ALL gcd(M,L)<=2 forms in this moving-root/doubled-b-fixed-state class
(the tiny nonsynchronizing M2 form is vacuous). If a(r)=r instead, the
same fixed doubled root has the elementary bound1+M(M-1): choose a b^j
to move its omitted output outside the current proper root subset at
each step. No coprimality condition is needed in that fixed-root case.

<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square--the-only-new-case-is-a-late-return"></a>
#### The only new case is a late return

Put g=2 and t=M/2. For M>=6, t>=3. A two-point kernel set cannot
be invariant under translation L, whose orbits have length t. Thus
some J in K has L+J outside K. If any such J<=M-2, the previous
kernel-return criterion J+g<=M already proves the bound.

The remaining case has unique admissible J=M-1 and other kernel input

    H=M-1-L,       K={H,J}.

Both H,J are odd, since M,L are even; H is positive. The literal
f=a b^J a, of cost M+1, fixes r and has full defect

    D(f)=e_r+e_0-e_L-e_z,       z=a(L-1) in C\{0,L}.

Let p=a^-1(M-L). This is a core state outside K, so p<=M-2.
The actual root inverse of f is {r,p}. The paid original seed
v=a b^p f has length p+M+2 and exact root inverse {r,H,J}.
Its designated first extension a b^J has length M, root retained,
and inverse {r,H,J,p}. In particular the next core size is THREE.

<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square--root-stages-and-their-potentially-excessive-cost"></a>
#### Root stages and their potentially excessive cost

Nonwhole core subsets extend by ONE, with root retained, using an
original a b^j of cost<=M. A proper nonempty whole core subset is
exactly ONE parity class, of size t. It extends by ONE under f b^s,
where s=0 or1 is the smallest shift with z+s outside that class.
Its cost is M+1+s. There is at mostONE such stage in the full core
size sequence2,3,...,M-1.

If no whole stage occurs, the total cost is at most

    p+M+2+M(M-2)=M^2-M+p+2<=M^2.

If it occurs with shift s, the preliminary bound is

    p+M+2+(M-3)M+(M+1+s)=M^2-M+p+3+s.

For p<=M-4 this is already<=M^2. The two extreme p values are
paid by two compulsory savings in distinct stages, as follows.

<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square--first-saving-when-pm-2"></a>
#### First saving when p=M-2

After the designated first extension the core is {H,J,p}. H,J are
odd and p is even. The sole even point p has p+L outside this set,
since L is a nonzero even shift. The next nonwhole step can therefore
use j=p, of cost M-1, saving ONE versus M. This is the stage of
core size THREE; taking the smallest boundary is at least as cheap.

<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square--second-saving-after-the-costly-whole-step"></a>
#### Second saving after the costly whole step

Only s=1 can need this second payment. The target whole subset U
contains z, since shift0 failed, and has size t. After f b it has
core size t+1. Both kernel points H,J occur in that preimage or
both fail to occur: f b maps each to core point1.

Write E for the even points of this new core set.

* E cannot be empty, because the core has t+1 points and there are
  only t odd points.
* If 0<|E|<t, translation L cycles all even points, so an even
  boundary j exists. It satisfies j<=M-2 and yields cost<=M-1.
* If |E|=t, there is exactlyONE odd point. Both kernel points
  therefore fail to occur, so that point is not J=M-1. It is a
  boundary of cost<=M-2.

In every case the next root extension costs<=M-1, saving at leastONE.
This step exists: t+1<M at M>=6. It is distinct from the core-size
THREE saving above, because t+1>=4.

Now p=M-3 needs onlyONE saving when s1, and the post-whole step
supplies it; s0 was already within square. For p=M-2, s0 needs
ONE saving supplied at core size3, while s1 needsTWO, supplied by
the two distinct steps. All paid factors form the SAME actual reset.
Thus no case exceeds M^2. No return word has been priced as one letter.

<a id="direct-attack-gcd-two-rank-one-square--m4-and-scope"></a>
#### M4 and scope

At M4, L2, a kernel set that is not an opposite pair has a return
J<=2 and is covered by the previous criterion. If K is an opposite
pair, the partition {0,2},{1,3},{r} is preserved by both original
letters, and each induces a permutation of its THREE blocks.
The remaining nonkernel pair necessarily maps to {1,3}, r maps to
{0,2}, and K maps to {r}. Consequently these cases cannot synchronize.
This handles every synchronizing M4 input; gcd2 has no other smaller M.

The independent checker tests2446 literal late-return inputs, including
COMPLETE1488 new forms M6/M8,78809372 particle controls and53700 root
stages. It checks592 critical first savings and96 post-expensive-whole
savings explicitly, all2446 compatible reset words through n257, and
seven rejected corruptions. Larger controls force the extreme p values
instead of relying only on random permutations.

This removes ALL gcd2 arbitrary-tail gaps in the stated class. It does
not remove the c0 opposite-pair order-two gap when M/2>2 (there g=M/2),
larger-g arbitrary kernel gaps, or the general Cerny gap. The new weighted
extension route for order two is CONJECTURED, not used in this proof.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-bridge"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-kernel-bridge--kernel-bridge-independent-reconstruction-of-pin-1978"></a>
### Kernel bridge (independent reconstruction of Pin 1978)

Status: **PROVED**, not **FORMALLY VERIFIED**. No improvement to the best
general asymptotic synchronization bound is claimed.

Let A be a complete synchronizing DFA with n states and arbitrary finite
alphabet. Words act on the right: S(uv)=(Su)v. Let u have rank k, 2<=k<=n.
For every k-subset S there exists a word v of length at most n-k+1 such that

    |S v u| < k.                                             (KB)

Neither strong connectivity nor reachability of S from Q is required. The
bound counts v only; the compression word is vu and costs |u|+n-k+1.

Stronger form: A need not synchronize Q. It suffices that S is compressible.
The fibers may be ANY partition into k nonempty blocks, whether or not they
come from a word. Some word of length <=n-k+1 sends S to a set missing a
block. To recover the word vu, the rank-k map u must be an actual word of A.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-bridge--complete-proof"></a>
#### Complete proof

Work over the rationals. For each letter a let M_a have entry (p,q) equal to
1 exactly when pa=q. Thus M_uv=M_u M_v. Write [S] for the row indicator
vector of S, and R=Qu. The k nonempty fibers F_q={p:pu=q}, q in R, partition Q.
Define the linear subspace

    W={x in Q^n : sum_(p in F_q) x_p is the same for all q in R}.

The k-1 equality constraints are independent: the linear map sending x to
its k fiber sums is surjective, since every fiber is nonempty. Consequently
dim W=n-k+1.

For any word v, x=[S]M_v is a nonnegative integer vector of total mass k.
If x lies in W, each fiber sum is exactly 1. Conversely, if |Svu|=k, every
fiber contains at least one image of an original member of S. The k fiber
sums are positive integers with total k, and hence all equal 1. Therefore

    [S]M_v lies outside W  <=>  |Svu|<k.                      (1)

This equivalence uses multiplicity vectors, not just image indicators. It
remains valid if S has already compressed under v.

Let L_i=span{[S]M_v: |v|<=i}. Then L_0 has dimension 1 and L_i is an ascending
chain. If L_i=L_(i+1), then L_i M_a is contained in L_i for every letter a;
induction gives L_j=L_i for every j>=i. Thus the chain cannot stop growing
before it contains the whole orbit span.

For a word z compressing S, [S]M_z has support size <k, so it misses at
least one of the k fibers. Its total mass is still k, so its fiber sums
cannot all be equal. Thus it does not lie in W. Hence the orbit span is
not contained in W. Put D=dim W. If all words of length <=D had vectors in W,
then L_D would be contained in W. Either the chain stabilized earlier,
contradicting the reset vector, or dim L_D>=D+1, contradicting dim W=D.
Some v of length <=D therefore satisfies (1). This proves (KB).

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-bridge--consequences-and-limits"></a>
#### Consequences and limits

Define lambda_r=min{|u|: |Qu|<=n-r}, lambda_0=0. For k=n-r>=2,

    c(S):=min{|w|: |Sw|<|S|} <= lambda_r+r+1,  |S|=k.        (2)

If a word attaining lambda_r has rank <k, apply it directly; otherwise apply
(KB). This also gives the same bound for all subsets of size >=k, by choosing
a k-subset and preserving its collision. Combining (2) with Pin--Frankl gives
the automaton-dependent bound

    rt(A) <= sum_(r=0)^(n-2) min{(r+1)(r+2)/2,lambda_r+r+1}.  (3)

Skipping ranks only reduces this positive sum. The lambda values in (3)
exclude the reset threshold lambda_(n-1), so the formula is not literally
the reset-distance tautology. However, large low-rank lambda values make it
revert to the cubic Pin--Frankl estimate. It gives NO new uniform coefficient.

For the saved four-state bottleneck automaton a=(0,0,1,3), b=(3,1,3,2),
lambda_2=2 and the pair {0,3} needs 5 letters. Thus (2) is sharp there:
2+(4-2)+1=5. The original bridge length n-k+1=3 is also sharp with u=aa and
S={0,3}: no bridge of length <=2 compresses Svu; v=bab does.

**KNOWN, not novel.** Pin's 1978 paper, Corollary 4, states precisely the
short-transversal persistence assertion whose contrapositive gives (KB),
including arbitrary partitions. Proposition 5 gives the rank recurrence
2|u|+n-k+1. The proof above independently reconstructs those mechanisms.
Source: [Pin, Utilisation de l'algebre lineaire en theorie des automates,
Corollary 4 and Proposition 5](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/AlgebreLineaire.pdf).
Formula (3) is a direct combination with Pin--Frankl, not a new general bound.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-bridge--audit"></a>
#### Audit

- k=1 excluded: no nonempty singleton can be compressed.
- n=1 handled separately by the empty reset word.
- u may be empty at k=n; then a non-permutation letter provides v of length 1.
- S is arbitrary, including unreachable subsets.
- The order is v followed by u. Reversing this order is not authorized.
- W is linear, while the actual orbit has fixed total mass k. Both facts are
  used; replacing integer occupancy by a real probability vector loses (1).
- Stabilization is invariant under right multiplication by every letter.
- An eventual compression vector ensures escape without global synchronization.
- This proof does not assert that v itself compresses S.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square--a-kernel-return-square-criterion-for-arbitrary-rank-one-tails"></a>
### A kernel-return square criterion for arbitrary rank-one tails

Date: 2026-10-03. **PROVED (paper), ALL parameters under the stated
original-letter condition.** Independent finite controls are
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. The all-n theorem is not FORMALLY VERIFIED.
No novelty claim and no reduction of general Cerny, which remains **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square--general-form-and-criterion"></a>
#### General form and criterion

Let Q={r} union Z_M, M>=3, and let ORIGINAL b cycle the core and fix r.
Let ORIGINAL a have rank n-1, doubled output r, omitted output
L in1..M-1, and a(r)=0. Its two kernel inputs K={u,v} are any distinct
core states. On C\K it is any bijection to C\{0,L}.
The omitted state need not be a kernel input. Arbitrary tail height,
root-cycle length, and all other a-cycles are allowed.

Set g=gcd(M,L). Assume there is J in K with

    (L+J) mod M not in K,        J+g<=M.

Then there is ONE compatible ORIGINAL reset word of length<=M^2.
Neither strong connectivity nor synchronization needs to be assumed.
Choose any c in K with (L+c) mod M outside K (J itself is available).
Let H be the other kernel input and p=a^-1((H-J) mod M). The sharper
constructive bound is

    rt <= M^2 - [(2M-3-p-c)+(M-J-g)] <= M^2.

Here p is a core state outside K. Thus p,c are distinct indices and
their sum is at most2M-3. This is a sufficient condition, not a
classification; the absence of such J is not a synchronization obstruction.
Larger alphabets containing these two ORIGINAL letters inherit the bound.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square--proof-with-all-original-costs-retained"></a>
#### Proof with all original costs retained

The rank-one full defect is D(a)=e_r-e_L. The literal f=a b^J a
fixes r. Its full defect is

    D(f)=e_r+e_0-e_L-e_z,       z=a(L+J) in C\{0,L}.

The value H-J is nonzero because the kernel inputs differ, and is
notL by admissibility. It therefore has unique original inverse p in
C\K. Direct particle tracing gives {r}f^-1={r,p}.
The original word v=a b^p f, of cost p+J+3, gives

    {r} --f^-1--> {r,p} --b^-p--> {r,0} --a^-1--> {r} union K.

This is the exact THREE-state seed, regardless of tail height. The
designated first extension a b^c costs c+1: the root image is c in K,
the omitted output becomes L+c outside K, and the full inverse growth
is exactly ONE. In particular K is not whole under translation L.

For every later proper root-present S={r} union U, a nonwhole U has
an oriented boundary j in U, L+j outside U, so a b^j grows by ONE,
retains r, and costs<=M. A whole U is a union of g-cosets. Choosing
s<g with z+s outside U gives literal f b^s with root retained, growth
1-chi_U(z+s)=1, and cost<=J+g+1<=n.

Core sizes along these ONE-growth stages are exactly2,...,M-1.
At most g-1 stages can have size divisible by t=M/g and hence be
whole. There are at least M-g-1 nonwhole stages, each saving one
versus n. The designated first saves a further M-c-1. Thus the cost
of the SAME word is bounded by

    p+J+3+(M-2)(M+1)-(M-g-1)-(M-c-1)
      =M^2+p+J+c+g-3M+3
      =M^2-[(2M-3-p-c)+(M-J-g)].

Both brackets are nonnegative. No assumption that a(L)=r was used.
The full multiplicity and the root inverse are literal, even if f's
rank is n-2 and a has a long tail. No composed letter is given unit cost.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square--automatic-all-n-corollaries"></a>
#### Automatic all-n corollaries

**Coprime displacement.** If gcd(M,L)=1, the criterion always holds.
Otherwise both elements of K would map back into K under translation L,
making K a union of length-M orbits. A two-element proper set cannot do
that at M>=3. An admissible J is at mostM-1, so J+1<=M.
This covers ALL kernel positions and ALL tail heights in the stated
rank-one/core-cycle model, including composite M with coprime L.

**A root two-cycle with a higher tail.** If 0 in K but L not in K,
choose J=c=0. Then f=a^2 is an ORIGINAL word of costTWO, its root
inverse has an additional core point, and all whole stages cost<=g+1<=M.
The designated first extension is a, of costONE. More sharply,

    rt <= p+3+M(M-2)-(M-1)
       = M^2-3M+p+4 <= M^2-2M+3.

The rank-one a's unique tail can be arbitrarily high. In contrast,
the c=0,L-kernel order-two model has a^2 with a unique root inverse;
that previously studied obstruction does not transfer to higher tails.

**All positive second kernels in the level-one form.** The automatic
J choices in [A square bound for every positive second kernel input](#direct-attack-positive-kernel-square) instantiate this broader theorem.
That proof is retained separately, including its stronger designated
first choice c even when c!=J.

<a id="direct-attack-kernel-root-return-square--verification-and-exact-limits"></a>
#### Verification and exact limits

The generator and independent checker are
`kernel_root_return_square.py` and `check_kernel_root_return_square.py`.
Their complete scope only includes L NOT in K, M3..7, and parameters
satisfying the criterion. This deliberately avoids repeating the completed
level-one tail input scope. Higher-order controls go through n257.
Literal full defects, root inverse, exact seed, every actual extension,
whole-coset controls, complete permutation coverage, sharper two-cycle
bound, tail paths and whole compatible resets are independently checked.
Tail paths end at r and have height at leastTWO.
The finite audit covers15213 literal inputs,12042 complete NEW higher-tail
forms,171455672 particles,160204 root-preserving extensions,1880 ALL-small
whole-coset controls, and eight rejected corruptions. Tail heights range
from2 to244;13511 coprime and4780 root-two-cycle controls are included.
These are actual reset witnesses and coverage checks, not exact threshold
computations for all these automata.

The generic criterion can fail for opposite kernel pairs under L at t2,
or for kernels too late in the core cycle. No general assertion is made
for those inputs. The specific original c=0,t=2 pair-splitting problem,
general higher-tail uncovered parameters, arbitrary doubled outputs not
fixed by b, and arbitrary original alphabets are still OPEN.

The release inventory and old Lean modules are unchanged. This theorem
is a paper result with scoped computational receipts, not a new member
of the frozen formal release.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-all-high-order"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-all-high-order--arbitrary-remaining-core-permutations-every-order-at-least-three-has-a-square-reset"></a>
### Arbitrary remaining-core permutations: every order at least three has a square reset

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), ALL parameters and arbitrary A under the
explicit model below.** No novelty or FORMALLY VERIFIED claim. General
Cerny remains **OPEN**. The synchronizing order-two mixed case is also
**OPEN** for this all-n square construction. Finite witnesses and separate
checks have their own COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED scope.

Let Q={r} union C=Z_M, n=M+1, M>=3. The ORIGINAL letters are

    b(x)=x+1 mod M on C, b(r)=r,
    a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r, a|_(C\{0,L})=A,
    L=M-d, 1<=d<M,

where A is ANY permutation of C\{0,L}. Put g=gcd(M,d) and t=M/g.
If t>=3, there is one ORIGINAL reset word of length at most M^2.
This removes the preceding arbitrary-A noncoprime gap at t>=3.
The proof does NOT assume that a^2 is a unit, that A preserves cosets,
that all core-staying extensions cost n, or that the truncated budget(TB)
holds. TB remains an open, now unnecessary, stronger local target.

Use right actions, P_(uv)=P_u P_v and D(w)=[Q]P_w-[Q]. The identities

    D(a)=e_r-e_L,       D(a^2)=e_0-e_L

hold with arbitrary A. The second word fixes r and maps C into C.
For a core subset U not a union of cosets modulo g, some
chi_U(j)-chi_U(L+j)=1. Thus a^2 b^j extends U by exactly ONE and
costs j+2<=M+1=n. No root endpoint is silently omitted.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-all-high-order--first-half-ordinary-n-extension-from-a-three-a-row"></a>
#### First half: ordinary n-extension from a three-a row

Suppose d<=M/2. Root-present proper subsets already extend by ONE in
cost <=their cardinality: a b^j works when L+j is absent. A core
noncoset subset is handled by a^2 b^j. It remains to extend a proper
nonempty core U that is a union of g-cosets.

Let p be the least positive period of its cyclic Boolean pattern.
Then p|g, p>=2, T=M/p>=3, and d,L are multiples of p. Its translation
stabilizer is precisely the multiples of p. Write z=A(d), which is
defined because t>=3 makes d distinct from0,L. For j in0..M-1 put

    F_j = a(a(L+j)+d),

where addition fixes r. These are the images of the M core particles
under a b^d a. Their EXACT multiplicity row is

    [C]P_(a b^d a) = [Q]+e_0-e_L-e_z.

Consequently EXACTLY T-1 of these particles lie in the core residue
class z modulo p. Among j=0,..,T-1 there is an index whose F_j is r
or lies in a different p-class. If F_j is core, its displacement from
z is not a period of U; equal-size translates of U then supply an
s in0..p-1 with z+s in U and F_j+s outside U. If F_j=r, choose s
with z+s in U, since U is nonempty.

The ACTUAL three-a word

    w=a b^j a b^d a b^s

has full-Q growth

    D(w)[U]^T = chi_U(z+s)-chi_U(F_j+s)=1.

The terms chi_U(s)-chi_U(L+s) cancel because U is periodic. Root
membership in U w^-1 is allowed; it has not been constrained to C.
Its ordinary cost is at most d+T+p+1.

Except for the case below, d+T+p<=M. To see this, write d=p l,
T=M/p. If T is even, l<=T/2-1: equality d=M/2 would give t=2,
which is excluded. Thus d+T+p<=pT for p>=2. If T is odd and p>=3,
l<=floor(T/2), and T<=p floor(T/2) proves the same inequality.
For p=2 and odd T the only possible exception is d=T-1. Then
M=2T, g=2, L=T+1, and U is an even or odd core coset.

In that exception choose the first nonneutral j. If z is in U, take
s=0, giving cost <=(T-1)+(T-1)+3=n. Otherwise s=1 suffices. If z
is odd, F_0=0 is already nonneutral, giving cost T+3<=n. If z is
even, BOTH F_0 and F_d are0, and d=T-1. Since there are exactly
T-1 neutral indices altogether, not all of j=0,..,T-2 can be neutral:
that would add the distinct neutral index d and give T of them.
Thus j<=T-2, and the cost is at most (T-2)+(T-1)+1+3=n.
This closes the single arithmetic exception using the actual doubled
particle; no additional conditional branch or averaging assumption is used.

This proves ORDINARY n-extension for every root-present proper S and
every NONEMPTY PROPER CORE U. It deliberately excludes U=C: avoiding r
can cost more than n. Extending all the way to C would leave a gap.

Instead start from {r}a^-1={0,L}, costONE, and force a^2 b^L,
costL+2, giving a sizeTHREE core preimage since 2L is distinct from0,L.
Continue the paid n-extensions while the set is core and has size<M-1.
Each growth is exactly ONE, so no core overshoot occurs.
If a root-present set appears, use the root-preserving policy below
until Q. The cost of THIS compatible chain is at most

    1+(L+2)+n(n-3)=M^2-d+1<=M^2.

Otherwise the inverse suffix s has preimage C\{q}, at cost
1+(L+2)+n(M-4). The preceding arbitrary-A paid preparation uses
u=A^-1(2L), j'=u-L mod M and

    v=a b^j' a b^d a,     Qv=C\{L},     |v|<=M+d+2.

With k=q-L mod M, the SAME word v b^k s resets Q, with cost

    (M+d+2)+(M-1)+1+(L+2)+n(M-4)=M^2.

All new noncoprime cases have M>=6. Small M=3 is coprime and is
covered by the preceding explicit small construction. This endpoint
dichotomy, not a claim of n-extension for the full core, closes the proof.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-all-high-order--a-root-preserving-policy-available-on-both-halves"></a>
#### A root-preserving policy, available on both halves

Let S={r} union U be proper. If U is not a union of g-cosets, choose
j with j in U and L+j outside U. The original word a b^j grows S
by ONE, and r is in its preimage because a(r)b^j=j. Its cost<=M=n-1.

If U is a union of cosets (including U empty), set z'=A(2L) and

    f=a b^L a.

The literal word f fixes r and has FULL row defect

    D(f)=e_r+e_0-e_L-e_(z').

For s<g choose z'+s outside U. Such an s exists because U is proper.
On S, the growth of f b^s is 1-chi_U(z'+s)=1, and its inverse set
retains r. Every letter is paid: cost L+2+s<=L+g+1<=M+1=n.
Thus every root-present proper subset has a ROOT-PRESERVING n-extension;
the noncoset branch saves at least ONE letter.

This uses t>=3: at t=2, 2L=0, the displayed z' would be undefined,
and f instead has defect e_0-e_L. No conclusion for that case follows.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-all-high-order--second-half-a-size-three-root-seed-pays-for-itself"></a>
#### Second half: a size-three root seed pays for itself

Suppose d>M/2 and g>=2. Write h=d-L>=2; h=1 would force gcd(M,d)=1.
Let p=A^-1(d) and z'=A(2L). The exact preimage of {r} under f is
S={r,p}, of sizeTWO, at costL+2. All of p,z' are distinct from0,L.

Three possible ACTUAL seeds give a ROOT-PRESENT sizeTHREE preimage:

* If p<=d-1, use a b^p f. Its preimage is {r,0,L}, and its cost
  L+p+3<=M+2=n+1.
* If p>=d and p!=z', use f f. Its growth on S is ONE, so its cost
  2L+4<=M+2=n+1.
* If p>=d and p=z', use f b f. Since p>=d>=L+2, p is neither1
  nor L+1. The defect of f b on S is EXACTLY ONE. Its cost is
  2L+5<=M+3=n+2. If h>=3 the better n+1 bound already holds.

With a seed costing <=n+1, the remaining n-3 root-preserving stages
cost at most n each, totaling <=(n+1)+n(n-3)=(n-1)^2.
Only h=2 in the last branch can cost n+2. Its core contains exactly
TWO points, and every whole coset has size t>=3. Therefore the FIRST
root-preserving extension uses the noncoset a b^j branch and costs
<=n-1. This pays the extra seed letter. The SAME compatible chain costs

    (n+2)+(n-1)+n(n-4)=(n-1)^2.

The remaining g=1 second-half cases reuse the already proved, paid
coprime construction in [Arbitrary core permutations: pay the longer preparation with the first growth](#direct-attack-moving-root-core-permutations) (including
the small M=3 case). This is an explicit theorem dependency, not a new
assumption or invocation of an uncharged circular macro alphabet.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-all-high-order--status-and-remaining-attacks"></a>
#### Status and remaining attacks

The theorem is a SUBCLASS result with an arbitrary permutation on all
remaining core points and both original letters having multiple cycles.
It does not reduce an arbitrary synchronizing DFA to this model. The
SYNC order-two inputs with a pair-splitting A still need an all-n square
proof. General Cerny, universal ordinary n-extension on the second half,
and the stronger truncated core budget(TB) remain OPEN.

The M12 complete native truncated/ordinary extension pressure and larger
sampled pressure are separately EXPLORATORY without an independent
coverage audit. They motivated the proof but do not prove any all-n
statement. The paper argument uses literal multiplicity rows, positive
boundaries, and one compatible inverse history throughout.

The separate checker verifies12147 retained inputs, including ALL11568
new noncoprime parameter/permutation inputs M6..9. It checks540384
root-present/37120 whole-core controls,76722918 literal particles,
