<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return--a-paid-two-point-return-removes-the-moving-root-coprimality-restriction"></a>
### A paid two-point return removes the moving-root coprimality restriction

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), ALL synchronizing parameters** of
[A moving-root square from a paid avoidance and a truncated return chain](#direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation). No novelty or **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim. General Černý remains **OPEN**. This was found AFTER the coprime
checkpoint eaadaa7 was committed; its noncoprime OPEN labels are historical.

Keep n=M+1, Q={r} union Z_M, L=M-d, the ORIGINAL letters a,b, and the
literal avoidance v=a b^L a b^d a of length M+3. Put g=gcd(d,M),
t=M/g. The previous paper proves SYNC iff t>=3. For EVERY t>=3, not
just g=1, ONE compatible ORIGINAL reset has length <=M^2.

The new statement is an explicit amortized core extension, sufficient
for the SAME truncated compatible chain. It is not universal original
n-extensibility or an arbitrary-DFA reset theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return--exact-return-with-all-original-letters-paid"></a>
#### Exact return, with all original letters paid

The restriction T of v to the core is

    T(0)=d, T(d)=0, T(L)=d, T(x)=x otherwise;
    v(r)=0.

At t>=3 the three core states0,d,L are distinct, so there is no
degenerate formula. The actual return

    R = a b v,             |R|=M+5,

sends ALL of Q into the core, since its final v does. It sends the
original r to core state1: r a=0, 0 b=1, and T(1)=1 when g>1.
Only the g>1 case will use R; at g=1 every proper core set has a unit
extension and this branch is never entered.

For g>1, let U be a union of whole core cosets modulo g. At coset
level T preserves every coset, while a replaces0,L by r and swaps r/0.
For the full-Q inverse preimage under R, direct counting gives

    |U R^-1|-|U| = 2 u_0-u_1,

where u_j is membership of the ENTIRE coset j. One way to check the
count is to follow the core particle row separately:

    [Z_M]P_R-[Z_M]
      =2e_0+e_d-e_L-e_1-e_(L+1).

The extra ORIGINAL r particle ends at1, so it cancels the -e1 term
in that core row. Subtracting [Q] instead adds -e_r. Thus the full
defect is 2e0+ed-eL-e_(L+1)-er. Pairing with U gives the stated
2u0-u1, because d,L lie in coset0 and L+1 in coset1.

Choose 0<=j<g with u_j=1 and u_(j+1)=0; such a boundary exists for
EVERY nonempty proper cyclic coset pattern. The ACTUAL word

    R b^j

therefore grows U by TWO. Its inverse preimage stays in the core:
the original r ends at1+j, which is in the absent coset j+1. Its
original cost is <=M+g+4<=2(M+1), since M=g t>=3g and g>=2.
The return has not been declared a unit-cost letter, and the original
r contribution is explicitly counted rather than silently discarded.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return--every-proper-core-set-has-growth-with-this-proportional-budget"></a>
#### Every proper core set has growth with this proportional budget

For any proper nonempty core U, first test the already paid unit
returns a^2 b^j,0<=j<M. Their full-Q inverse growth is

    1_U(j)-1_U(L+j).

Their differences sum toZERO. If some difference is nonzero, a
positive difference exists and the actual word grows by ONE at cost
<=M+1, with no r in its inverse preimage. If every difference isZERO,
the Boolean pattern is invariant under the d-shift, so U is a union
of whole cosets modulo g. For g=1 that would be empty or full, excluded.
For g>1 apply the above positive boundary return, with growthTWO
and cost<=2(M+1).

Hence EVERY proper core U has an actual core-staying extension w with

    Delta=|U w^-1|-|U| in{1,2},   |w|<=(M+1)Delta.

This bound applies to the selected compatible chain, not to its
arbitrary intermediate literal inverse subsets. Literal a may shrink.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return--the-same-compatible-square-with-a-cardinality-budget"></a>
#### The SAME compatible square, with a cardinality budget

Start with {r}a^-1={0,L}, costONE. Continue with the chosen actual
extensions only until the core preimage has size M-1. A TWO-growth
step cannot overshoot: at its coset-union input, at least one absent
coset has t>=3 points. A ONE-growth step also cannot overshoot.
The total net growth is exactly M-3, so summing proportional costs gives

    |s|<=1+(M+1)(M-3),  {r}s^-1=Z_M\{p}.

Choose k=p-L mod M. The original word v b^k s is reset because
Qv=Z_M\{L} and (Qv)b^k=Z_M\{p}. Its original cost is

    (M+3)+(M-1)+1+(M+1)(M-3)=M^2=(n-1)^2.

This strengthens the preceding coprime square to EVERY SYNC parameter
of the family. No new ordinary threshold formula, general alphabet
reduction, or unrestricted n-only upper bound follows. The exact
avoidance/positive-original support cost n+2 proved earlier is unchanged.
The family illustrates why a long repair can fit a square by paying for
TWO net points, rather than imposing a false uniform one-point cap.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return--independent-verification"></a>
#### Independent verification

The generator moving_root_amortized_return.py covers ALL noncoprime
SYNC parameter pairs at M3..40 and selected large coset controls.
check_moving_root_amortized_return.py imports no generator, graph solver
or preceding checker. It recomputes literal T/R rows, full-Q and core
counts, original-r endpoint, both extension branches and proportional
costs, every proper core subset at M<=10 and64 retained larger subsets,
the exact growth-weighted chain, final alignment and literal reset.
Finite controls are COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED. The all-parameter theorem
is paper, not formally verified. Earlier Lean Kari evidence is unchanged.

### Arbitrary core permutations: pay the longer preparation with the first growth

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), arbitrary n>=4 under explicit coprime
hypotheses.** No novelty or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. General Černý
remains **OPEN**. This continues AFTER commit85cfa05.

Keep n=M+1, Q={r} union Z_M, r=M, L=M-d, b fixing r and cycling the
core. Require gcd(d,M)=1 and 1<=d<M. Let the ORIGINAL a satisfy

    a(r)=0, a(0)=r, a(L)=r,
    a restricted to Z_M\{0,L} is ANY permutation of that set.

All remaining core points need no longer be fixed. There is ONE original
reset of length <=M^2=(n-1)^2. This includes multicycle original letters,
a moving doubled root, and arbitrary cycles away from the unique tail.
It is a further subclass theorem, not an assertion that an arbitrary
binary near-permutation input can be put in this form.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-core-permutations--the-return-is-not-assumed-to-be-a-unit-transformation"></a>
#### The return is not assumed to be a unit transformation

The ACTUAL c=a^2 fixes r and0, sends L to0, and permutes the remaining
core points by the square of a's restriction. Thus its core row is

    [Z_M]P_c=[Z_M]+e0-eL.

It is generally NOT the map fixing all other points. Only that row
identity and c(r)=r are used. Hence c b^j grows a proper core U by
1_U(j)-1_U(L+j), has cost j+TWO, and keeps its preimage in the core.
Coprimality supplies a positive cyclic difference for every proper U,
so exactONE growth costs at mostM+1. Permutational action inside the
set is fully retained in every compatible preimage.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-core-permutations--a-literal-preparation-with-a-variable-paid-cost"></a>
#### A literal preparation with a variable paid cost

The point2L mod M lies outside{0,L}, because M>=3 and gcd(d,M)=1.
Choose the UNIQUE p outside{0,L} with a(p)=2L, and put j=p-L mod M.
The word

    v=a b^j a b^d a

has cost j+d+3<=M+d+2. Its image holes successively are {L}, {p},
{L,2L}, {0,L}, {r,L}. The last a therefore gives

    Qv=Z_M\{L}.

The intermediate hole permutation is a(p), not p. The earlier
fixed-core formula j=L is not reused here. Nor is the earlier sharp
avoidance/support cost n+2 asserted for this broader class.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-core-permutations--the-forced-first-return-supplies-exactly-the-needed-savings"></a>
#### The forced first return supplies exactly the needed savings

Original final a seeds {r}a^-1={0,L}, at costONE. At M>=4, deliberately
choose FIRST the actual factor a^2 b^L. Its row pairing is

    1_{0,L}(L)-1_{0,L}(2L)=1,

so it grows the core seed toTHREE and costs L+2=M-d+2. This is at
mostM+1, with saving d-1 from that generic growth budget. There remain
exactlyM-4 ONE-growth factors to reach a core preimage S of size M-1.
Each costs at mostM+1. Their choices may change S in arbitrary ways;
each is computed from the CURRENT actual preimage.

With the accumulated ORIGINAL suffix s, we have

    S={r}s^-1=Z_M\{q},
    |s|<=1+(M-d+2)+(M-4)(M+1).

Take k=q-L mod M. The SINGLE original word v b^k s resets all Q to r.
Paying |v|<=M+d+2 and k<=M-1 gives

    |v b^k s|
      <=(M+d+2)+(M-1)+1+(M-d+2)+(M-4)(M+1)
      =M^2.

The cheaper first factor compensates the longer preparation. None of
the powers, the return a^2, rotation, initial seed or original final a
is free. At M3 there is onlyONE remaining core point, so its permutation
is identity; the preceding moving-root theorem handles this case using
the sizeTWO truncated seed directly, without an invalid first growth.

This theorem rests on the same cyclic-sign extension mechanism already
attributed in the unit/cycle and fixed-root documents; no priority claim
is made for this exact paid combination. The arbitrary-permutation case
with noncoprime d is **OPEN here**: both the preparation and the special
two-point return formulas from [A paid two-point return removes the moving-root coprimality restriction](#direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return) change.
That older all-parameter theorem for FIXED remaining points is intact.

### Noncoprime core permutations: a class return, and a mixed-class boundary

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper)** under the explicit class condition
below, arbitrary n. General Černý **OPEN**; no novelty/formal claim.
This verifies the conditional avenue recorded after committed ed5b9fb.

Use the moving-root letters of [Arbitrary core permutations: pay the longer preparation with the first growth](#direct-attack-moving-root-core-permutations), now
g=gcd(d,M)>1 and t=M/g>=3. Require the remaining-core permutation A
to map every coset modulo g onto a coset, preserving coset0. On coset0
remove0,L from both domain and range. Let phi be its induced coset
permutation, phi(0)=0. Other cosets may be arbitrarily permuted among
themselves, and all within-coset permutations are arbitrary.

Then ONE compatible original reset costs at most M^2-g+1<M^2.
The arbitrary noncoset-preserving case remains **OPEN here**.

Choose p with a(p)=2L and j=p-L mod M, as in the previous paper.
Both p,L are in coset0, so j is a multiple of g and j<=M-g. The literal
v=a b^j a b^d a avoids r with Qv=Z_M\{L}, and costs<=M-g+d+3.
Its core restriction T preserves coset0 and induces phi^3 on the other
cosets: both b powers are multiples of g, and each of the three a's
acts by phi on a nonzero coset. The original r ends in coset0 as well.

Choose 1<=h<g with phi^3(h)=1. The ACTUAL return R=a b^h v sends
all Q into the core. For a proper whole-coset subset U its full-Q
preimage growth is2u0-u1. One exact row calculation is

    D(R)=e0+e_(a(d))-eL+e_(v(r))-e_(T(L+h))-e_r.

The first three positive points have coset0, the L negative has coset0,
and T(L+h) has coset1. The original r ends in coset1, which must be
excluded at a positive boundary; its contribution is included in D(R).
Choose 0<=k<g with u_k=1,u_(k+1)=0. R b^k grows by TWO, and its
inverse preimage stays in the core. All letters are paid:

    |R b^k|<= (M-g+d+3)+1+(g-1)+(g-1)
             <=2M+2=2(M+1),

since d<=M-g. No root contribution, class permutation or rotation is
silently removed. If U is not a union of cosets, some a^2 b^k grows
by ONE at cost<=M+1, by the same signed row identity as before.

Start from the ORIGINAL final a, preimage{0,L}, costONE. Force first
a^2 b^L at cost M-d+2, giving sizeTHREE. Use the one-/two-growth
branches until M-1. A two-growth branch cannot overshoot since every
absent coset has t>=3 points. The remaining NET growth is M-4 and
cost<= (M+1)(M-4). Align the final omitted core point with one paid
b power, at cost<=M-1. The SAME word v b^k s is reset, with cost

    (M-g+d+3)+(M-1)+1+(M-d+2)+(M+1)(M-4)
      =M^2-g+1.

This proves the asserted class square. The earlier coprime arbitrary-A
theorem and fixed-core ALL-parameter theorem are unchanged.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-coset-permutations--directly-carrying-the-old-return-into-mixed-cosets-is-refuted"></a>
#### Directly carrying the old return into mixed cosets is REFUTED

The seven-state original rows

    a=[6,2,1,3,6,5,0], b=[1,2,3,4,5,0,6]

have M6,d2,L4,g2, and a swaps the remaining points1/2 across cosets.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two--exact-synchronization-and-singular-letter-avoidance-in-the-arbitrary-core-model"></a>
### Exact synchronization and singular-letter avoidance in the arbitrary core model

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), all n under the stated model.**
No novelty/formal claim. General Cerny and the unrestricted mixed-core
square remain **OPEN**. Independent finite scope is recorded separately.

Let Q={r} union Z_M, r=M, 1<=d<M, L=M-d, g=gcd(M,d), t=M/g.
Original b fixes r and cycles the core. Original a sends r to0 and
0,L to r; on the remaining core points it is an arbitrary permutation A.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two--an-exact-all-parameter-synchronization-classification"></a>
#### An exact all-parameter synchronization classification

The original automaton is SC. It synchronizes precisely when

    t>=3, OR t=2 and A does not preserve the pairs modulo g.

At t2 the pairs are {q,q+g}; preserving pairs means mapping each
nonzero pair onto a pair. These include an arbitrary permutation of
the nonzero pairs and arbitrary within-pair permutations.

Proof: use the previously proved SC corank-one stable-kernel quotient
in [Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient](#direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient). A nonsynchronizing input of this
model has a proper stable equivalence containing 0~L. Stability under
the cyclic permutation b forces the core equivalence classes to be
cosets modulo some h dividing g. If the class of0 has at least THREE
points, one of its points outside0,L maps into the core, whereas0,L
map to r. Thus r is equivalent to a core point. Since b fixes r and
cycles all core points, the equivalence is universal, a contradiction.
Hence a proper quotient is possible only at t2, with h=g and pair
classes. If A splits a pair, this equivalence cannot be stable, so
the input synchronizes. If A preserves pairs, a induces a permutation
exchanging class0 and {r} and permuting all other classes; b also induces
a permutation. This explicit nontrivial quotient forbids synchronization.
No short reset word is inferred from stable closure alone.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two--exact-minimum-number-of-original-as-needed-to-avoid-r"></a>
#### Exact minimum number of original a's needed to avoid r

Let nu(w) count ORIGINAL a occurrences, with every b still charged in
ordinary length. The minimum nu(w) among words avoiding r is

    3  if t>=3;
    4  if t=2 and A splits a pair;
    infinity  if t=2 and A preserves pairs.

Before the first avoidance, the image holes lie in the core. At a
nonavoiding a they update by

    H -> {L} union A(H\{0,L}).

The original root remains present. To avoid r, both0 and L must be
holes before the final a. One preceding a gives only one hole, so
at least THREE a's are needed for every synchronizing parameter.

At t>=3, choose p=A^-1(2L mod M) and j=p-L mod M. Exactly THREE
a's suffice in v=a b^j a b^d a. Its hole trace is
{L}->{p}->{L,2L}->{0,L}->{r,L}. In fact the minimum ordinary cost
among words with exactly THREE a's is precisely j+d+3. After two a's
the only possible two-hole set is {L,A(p)}. Rotating it onto{0,L}
requires A(p)=2L and rotation d; the alternative would require A(p)=0,
which is forbidden. Initial/final b powers and extra full b cycles
cannot improve the cost. In particular this three-a cost is <=2M=2n-2:
for d<=M-2 the general j<=M-1 suffices; for d=M-1, L1 and p!=0,1
give j<=M-2. This is an avoidance upper bound, not a reset bound.

At t2, 2L=0 and that two-hole preparation is impossible. Thus THREE
a's never avoid r. When A splits pairs, its inverse splits some
output pair {x,x+L}, outside{0,L}. Let p=A^-1(x), q=A^-1(x+L),
delta=q-p mod M !=L, z=A^-1(L+delta mod M). Put

    j=z-L mod M, h=p-L mod M, k=-x mod M,
    v=a b^j a b^h a b^k a.

Its holes after the four a's are

    {L}, {L,A(z)}, {L,x,x+L}, {r,L,A(L-x)}.

Therefore Qv=Z_M\{L,A(L-x)}, nu(v)=4, |v|<=3M+1.
Every four-a avoiding word has this form at minimum cost: the third
a must produce THREE holes; the opposite pair before the fourth a
must come from its two A-images, because no A-image is0 orL.
Consequently minimizing j+h+k+4 over ALL oriented split output pairs
gives the EXACT ordinary minimum subject to nu(w)=4. This optimization
does not minimize ordinary length over words with more a's.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two--the-same-singular-count-is-exact-for-positive-original-stationary-support"></a>
#### The same singular count is exact for positive-original stationary support

Consider any finite nonnegative full-Q stationary word mixture which
uses ORIGINAL a with positive coefficient. Its exact minimum maximum
nu(w) over support words is again3/4/infinity in the cases above.

The root coordinate of D(a) is +1. A word with an incoming root particle
has root defect >=0. Balancing a positive a term requires a word with
root defect -1, namely a word avoiding r. This proves the lower bound.
For ANY actual avoiding v, average the two literal pools

    {a b^j:0<=j<M}, {v b^j:0<=j<M}.

Their total full-Q row is 2M[Q]: the first pool has2M root particles
and M(M-1) core particles; the second has no root particles and
M(M+1) core particles, equally spread across the core. Every coefficient
is ONE, a itself is present, and all b powers are paid. Choosing the
three-/four-a preparation attains the asserted maximum a-count.
This metric counts singular occurrences, not total maximum word length,
one-step balancing, reset length, or free macro cost.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two--a-coprime-cost-comparison-and-an-exact-n5-boundary"></a>
#### A coprime cost comparison and an exact n5 boundary

At gcd(M,d)=1, let tau be the minimum ORIGINAL cost avoiding r, and
T the minimum maximum ORIGINAL word length of such a stationary
mixture with positive ORIGINAL a. Then

    tau <= T <= max{tau,n}; hence T=tau whenever tau>=n.

For the upper bound take a shortest avoiding v. D(a)+D(v) has zero
root coordinate and is an integer zero-sum core row. Actual a^2 b^j
has defect e_j-e_(L+j), cost j+2<=n. These form the directed edges
of one core cycle. Every integer zero-sum core row is a nonnegative
integer combination of these edge defects: solve the integer flow
equations and add a common circulation to make every flow nonnegative.
Use them to cancel D(a)+D(v). The root-coordinate argument supplies
the lower bound. This is a metric comparison, not a general square
proof or a claim that arbitrary noncoprime core defects can be canceled.

The literal n5 rows a=[4,4,3,2,0], b=[1,2,3,0,4] have tau=T=8,
so the wider-model claim tau=T=n+2 is **REFUTED**. An independent
ALL32 subset Bellman certificate proves tau8. The actual stationary
integer support is

    a + (a b^2 a b^3 a) + 2(a^2 b) + (a^2 b^2) + (a^2 b^3),

meaning a sum of full-Q defects equal to ZERO; its maximum cost is8.
The previously proved n+2 metric for FIXED remaining-core points is
unchanged. Its wider extension had deliberately not been asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-order-two--an-infinite-warning-against-minimizing-singular-count-alone"></a>
#### An infinite warning against minimizing singular count alone

For EVERY L>=7, M=2L and n=2L+1, define the remaining-core permutation
by the following eight mappings:

    1->L+2, L+1->1, L-2->L+1, M-2->2,
    2->L+3, L+2->3, L-1->L-3, M-1->M-3.

Map the other input pairs bijectively onto the other output pairs,
preserving each pair. The named classes are distinct at L>=7, so
this is well defined. Exactly the output pairs of classes1 and2 split.
The four oriented choices have four-a costs

    2M+2, 2M+2, 2M+3, 2M+3.

Thus minimum avoiding singular count isFOUR but minimum original cost
subject to FOUR occurrences is EXACTLY2M+2=2n. This **REFUTES** a
universal four-a preparation bound2M+1, on an infinite family. It does
not refute a smaller ordinary avoidance bound allowing more a's.
For the L7 named completion, its unrestricted avoiding minimum is12,
independently proved on ALL32768 subset vertices, rather than30.
At a separate n7 example, exactly four a's cost13, while ordinary
minimum9 uses five a's. Occurrence optimization and word cost differ.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation--a-moving-root-square-from-a-paid-avoidance-and-a-truncated-return-chain"></a>
### A moving-root square from a paid avoidance and a truncated return chain

Update2026-10-02 after commit eaadaa7: [A paid two-point return removes the moving-root coprimality restriction](#direct-attack-moving-root-amortized-return)
now proves the square at ALL synchronizing parameters of this family.
The noncoprime OPEN labels below describe the preceding proof boundary.
The exact avoidance/support-cost statements and coprime proof remain
unchanged; no general Cerny or formal-family proof is claimed.

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper)** at all parameters stated below.
General Černý remains **OPEN**. No novelty or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim.
Words act on the right; every occurrence of a macro costs its original
letter length. This continues after the exact binary one-step obstruction.

Let M>=3, n=M+1, Q={r} union Z_M, with r=M. Choose 1<=d<M and
L=M-d. The ORIGINAL binary letters are

    b(r)=r, b(x)=x+1 mod M;
    a(r)=0, a(0)=r, a(L)=r, a(x)=x otherwise.

Thus a has rank n-1, omitted output L, doubled output r, a two-cycle
r/0 and fixed points elsewhere. b has TWO cycles. In particular there
is no original one-cluster letter and a does not fix its doubled root.
These inputs are outside the earlier fixed-root square hypotheses.

The following are separate assertions:

* The input is SC. It is SYNC iff t=M/gcd(d,M)>=3. At t=2 it has a
  nontrivial permutation quotient and is NOT a Černý counterexample.
* At EVERY t>=3, the shortest word avoiding r has length n+2.
* At EVERY t>=3, the minimum maximum word cost of a full-Q row-stationary
  nonnegative mixture giving POSITIVE weight to the ORIGINAL a is n+2.
  Equivalently the positive-leading-a suffix-balancing cap is exactly n+1.
* If gcd(d,M)=1, ONE compatible original reset has length <=M^2=(n-1)^2.
  The noncoprime t>=3 square for this family remains **OPEN here**.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation--synchronization-without-conflating-strong-connectivity-and-a-reset"></a>
#### Synchronization, without conflating strong connectivity and a reset

The b-cycle reaches every core state. a moves r into that cycle and
moves its state0 back to r, so the original state graph is SC.

Reuse the proved SC corank-one stable-quotient theorem in
[Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient](#direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient): all minimum-rank kernels coincide in a
stable congruence, with permutation induced letters. It contains the
letter kernel {0,L}. Closure under b therefore identifies every core
coset modulo g=gcd(d,M). If t>=3, the coset containing0,L has another
point x. It satisfies a(x)=x, while a(0)=a(L)=r. Congruence closure puts
r in that coset. Since b fixes r and rotates the core cosets transitively,
every core point joins r. The minimum rank isONE, proving SYNC.

If t=2, take the g two-point core cosets and the singleton {r} as blocks.
b cycles the core blocks and fixes {r}; a exchanges the block {0,L}
with {r}, and fixes all other blocks. This is a nontrivial permutation
quotient, so there is no reset. It also proves r cannot be avoided: the
quotient of EVERY full-Q word still visits the singleton block {r}.
This reuses the earlier qualitative stability theorem, not a new bound
on the cost of a minimum-rank word.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation--an-all-word-avoidance-lower-bound-not-a-bounded-negative-search"></a>
#### An all-word avoidance lower bound, not a bounded negative search

Before the FIRST avoidance of r, let H=Q\Qw be the holes. Then H is a
subset of Z_M. Under b all holes rotate one position. Under a, unless
both0 and L are holes (which is precisely the avoiding step), the new
core holes are

    {L} union (H\{0,L}).

Thus each hole is inserted at L by an a, rotates under b, and may be
erased by a. Just before the first avoiding a there are holes at0 and L.
Trace the hole at L back to its latest insertion. Its number of b steps
is a multiple of M. This number cannot beZERO: immediately after ANY
nonavoiding a there is no hole at0, and a suffix of a's cannot create one.
It is therefore at least M. Producing two distinct holes requires at
leastTWO insertion a's; the first avoiding a is a third. Any avoiding
word has length >=M+3=n+2. Leading permutations, redundant a's, and
arbitrary intervening letters are included in this argument.

At t>=3, 2d is nonzero modulo M. The literal word

    v = a b^L a b^d a

has M+3 letters. Its successive pre-final hole sets are {L}, {2L},
{2L,L}, {L,0}; the final a avoids r. In fact its full-Q image is
Z_M\{L}, and its row defect is

    D(v) = -e_r-e_L+e_0+e_d.

This formula is for weighted full-Q columns, while the hole calculation
is for reachable SETS. Both are checked independently on literal rows.
The distinction matters because v has TWO doubled columns.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation--exact-positive-original-support-cost-with-a-weaker-mixture-distinguished"></a>
#### Exact positive-original support cost, with a weaker mixture distinguished

Put D(w)=[Q]P_w-[Q]. We have D(a)=e_r-e_L. Every word of cost <=n+1
still visits r, hence D(w)(r)>=0. A nonnegative stationary mixture that
gives positive weight to ORIGINAL a would have strictly positive total
defect at r, a contradiction. The lower bound n+2 concerns a specified
positive term; it is stronger than merely requiring some singular support.

For the matching upper bound let j_i=i d mod M, 1<=i<=t-1, and

    h_i = a^2 b^(j_i),
    D(h_i)=e_(j_i)-e_(j_i-d).

Use coefficientONE on a and v; use coefficientONE on h_1 and TWO on
h_i, 2<=i<=t-1. The two paths0->d->...->L and d->...->L telescope:

    sum_i beta_i D(h_i)=2e_L-e_0-e_d.
    D(a)+D(v)+sum_i beta_i D(h_i)=0.

Normalize their total mass to obtain an exact rational stationary
mixture. All h_i cost at most M+1=n; v costs n+2, so the maximum is
exactly n+2. All words start with a, so deleting that first ORIGINAL
letter proves suffix cap n+1 is sharp. A positive weight on b can also
be added without changing the row identity, because D(b)=0. The resulting
support contains original a,b and is SC/SYNC at t>=3.

There IS a cheaper weak stationary mixture: average a^2 b^(j_i) over
ALL j_i in the subgroup <d>, including j0=0. Its defects sum toZERO
and its maximum cost is at most n. But every one of these words fixes r
and never sends a core point to r. Even adding b leaves that support
nonsynchronizing. No sharpness assertion is made for this weaker cost.
Consequently the new obstruction does NOT contradict the earlier weaker
stationary-support metric or pretend they are the same problem.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation--pay-a2-as-two-stop-one-state-early-and-use-the-original-final-a"></a>
#### Pay a^2 as TWO, stop one state early, and use the original final a

Assume gcd(d,M)=1. On the core, c=a^2 is the UNIT map L->0, fixing
all other points; it also fixes r. For every proper nonempty core U,
some j in{0,...,M-1} satisfies j in U and j+L not in U. Otherwise the
d-shift would preserve its Boolean pattern, and coprimality would make
that pattern constant. The ACTUAL factor

    a^2 b^j

therefore increases the preimage of U by exactlyONE, at cost j+2<=M+1.
Its preimage stays in the core. This is the same cyclic sign mechanism
as the attributed unit/cycle extension proof, with the return paid as TWO.

Use the ORIGINAL final a: {r}a^-1={0,L}, at costONE. Prepend the above
factors only until the preimage is a core set S of size M-1. This needs
M-3 factors and costs at most

    |s| <=1+(M-3)(M+1),    S={r}s^-1=Z_M\{p}.

Choose k=p-L mod M, 0<=k<=M-1. Since Qv=Z_M\{L}, we have
(Qv)b^k=S. The SINGLE chronological word

    v b^k s

resets all of Q to r. Its paid original cost is at most

    (M+3)+(M-1)+1+(M-3)(M+1)=M^2.

There is no whole-core reset charge, free rotation, replacement of a^2
by an original letter, or independent final-pair optimum. Truncating at
M-1 and retaining original a at the very end supply exactly the needed
savings. The preparation itself is longer than n, so this is a concrete
compatible compensation proof rather than universal n-extensibility.

The unit/cycle extension mechanism is attributed in
[A positive averaging polynomial proves the square for one permutation plus units](#direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square) and [Coprime root displacement, and a necessary amortized boundary](#direct-attack-coprime-fixed-root-refinement);
the general orbit/averaging framework is
[Steinberg2010](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.0410). The literature search did
not establish priority of this exact family/cost combination. General
Černý remains OPEN, and the noncoprime core Boolean patterns are an
explicit obstruction to reusing the coprime step without further work.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-paid-compensation--verification-scope"></a>
#### Verification scope

moving_root_paid_compensation.py records every d at M3..20 and selected
larger M31,63,127,256. check_moving_root_paid_compensation.py imports NO
generator or graph solver. It checks literal transition rows, weighted
composition, exact positive support, complete pair Bellman certificates,
order-two permutation quotients, every proper core subset at M<=10 and
64 retained subsets for larger coprime parameters, one compatible original
word, and complete small-state avoidance Bellman equations. All-n claims
are paper proofs; finite controls are COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED. The earlier
Lean Kari sources remain unchanged; this new family is not formally proved.

Completed finite scope:213 inputs,203SYNC/10 nontrivial permutation
quotients,146 coprime compatible square words,16628 proper-core witnesses,
1132632 pair Bellman edges,14336 complete small avoidance Bellman edges,
84795818 literal particle/letter controls and12 rejected corruptions.
 Deterministic generation is replayed byte-for-byte.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget--a-precise-mixed-core-target-truncate-proportional-growth-before-the-full-core"></a>
### A precise mixed-core target: truncate proportional growth before the full core

Date:2026-10-02. General Cerny **OPEN**. The two lemmas and conditional
implication below are **PROVED (paper)**, with no novelty/formal claim.
The universal mixed-core truncated budget is **CONJECTURED / OPEN**.
Complete small certificates are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** separately.

Keep Q={r} union C=Z_M, n=M+1, b cycling C and fixing r,
a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r, L=M-d, and an arbitrary permutation A on
C\{0,L}. Put g=gcd(M,d), t=M/g>=3. No coset-map condition on A.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget--a-general-cheap-branch-whenever-the-doubled-output-is-present"></a>
#### A general cheap branch whenever the doubled output is present

More generally let a be ANY original rank(n-1) transformation whose
omitted output e is in C and doubled output is r. For EVERY proper
S containing r there is a ONE-growth original word of cost <=|S|.
No assumptions on its kernel, root movement, other cycles, SC or sync
are required. For w=a b^j, full-Q cardinality growth is

    1_S(r)-1_S(b^j(e))=1-1_S(b^j(e)).

The core contains |S|-1 members of S. Among the first |S| distinct
points e,b(e),...,b^(|S|-1)(e) one is outside S. Choose its first index
j<=|S|-1. Then |w|=j+1<=|S| and growth is EXACTLY one, with the full
actual preimage. Its root membership is retained, not prescribed.

The bound is sharp as an ALL-WORD extension bound in an elementary
absorbing-root family: let a fix all points except e=0 mapping to r,
and S={r} union {0,...,k-2}, 1<=k<=M. Until the first positive inverse
a, every a is neutral and only inverse b rotations change this set.
At least k-1 such rotations and one a are necessary; a b^(k-1)
attains cost k. These examples are synchronizing but need not be SC.
This sharpness does not concern a Cerny reset lower bound.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget--a-cheap-mixed-preimage-branch-when-class0-is-absent"></a>
#### A cheap mixed-preimage branch when class0 is absent

Let U be a proper nonempty union of cosets modulo g, with 0 not in U.
Set X=U a^-1. Then X is in C, has |X|=|U|, and omits both0,L.
Suppose X is NOT a union of cosets. The positive cyclic differences

    1_X(j)-1_X(L+j), 0<=j<M,

number at least TWO. Indeed every partially filled coset contributes
at least one positive boundary in its length-t cycle. If there were
only one positive boundary, exactly one coset would be partially filled;
then |X| would not be divisible by t. But |X|=|U| is divisible by t.
Consequently a positive index j<=M-2 exists. The ACTUAL word

    a^2 b^j a

grows U by ONE, stays in C, and has cost j+3<=M+1=n. Its initial
root maps to0, which is outside U. This proves a useful all-n branch,
not the full arbitrary-A extension conjecture. The earlier general
return a^2 may permute the other points; only its core row e0-eL is used.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget--the-sufficient-local-conjecture-must-prevent-overshooting"></a>
#### The sufficient local conjecture must prevent overshooting

For every U in C with 1<=|U|<=M-2 ask for an original word w with

    V=U w^-1 subset C,  |U|<|V|<=M-1,
    |w|<=(M+1)(|V|-|U|).                         (TB)

The general noncoset branch already gives this by a^2 b^j, growthONE.
The new cheap branch above handles further mixed cases. Whole-coset
patterns not covered by these remain OPEN at arbitrary M.

Assuming (TB), the square for this class follows from ONE compatible
chain. Seed {r}a^-1={0,L}, cost1. Force first a^2 b^L, costM-d+2,
growthONE because 2L is outside {0,L}. Apply (TB) until sizeM-1;
the remaining NET growth is M-4 and its cost <=(M+1)(M-4).
If the resulting suffix s has preimage C\{q}, choose
p with a(p)=2L and j=p-L mod M. The paid preparation
v=a b^j a b^d a has Qv=C\{L}, cost<=M+d+2.
With k=q-L mod M, the SAME original word v b^k s resets Q, at cost

    (M+d+2)+(M-1)+1+(M-d+2)+(M-4)(M+1)=M^2.

The untruncated variant allowing V=C is insufficient for this argument:
if the chain first reaches sizeM, no alignment is needed but its extra
one-point growth budget exceeds the omitted alignment by TWO. The
corresponding estimate is M^2+2. This is a gap in that proposed
implication, not a counterexample to either local conjecture or Cerny.
Earlier proved coset-map branches grow TWO with at least THREE absent
points, so they satisfy truncation and their square proofs are intact.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget--exact-obstruction-to-a-one-step-n-bound-with-root-excluded"></a>
#### Exact obstruction to a ONE-step n-bound with root excluded

At M9,d6,L3,g3 use the literal mixed rows

    a=[9,8,2,9,4,5,6,7,1,0],
    b=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,0,9],
    U={1,2,4,5,7,8}, mask438.

Minimum original costs to a core-staying inverse preimage of size7,8,9
are respectively11,11,15. Thus its minimum positive core extension is
11>n10: a universal ONE-step n-bound with this endpoint restriction is
**REFUTED**. The size8 witness

    a b a b^3 a b a b^2

has cost11, growthTWO, final core mask447, and satisfies (TB).
An unrestricted inverse extension has exact minimum9 and includes r
(mask877). Root membership is therefore a material condition. These
are independent Bellman certificates on ALL1024 subset vertices for
four goal sets, not a search cutoff or a Cerny counterexample.

<a id="direct-attack-moving-root-truncated-budget--verification-and-literature-boundary"></a>
#### Verification and literature boundary

The separate checker covers ALL11568 remaining-core permutations and
noncoprime t>=3 parameter pairs at M6..9, ALL63456 proper whole-coset
patterns, and a literal compatible square reset for every input. It
checks67824 compatible factors, the forced first saving and preparation.
Its retained BFS witnesses are not claimed ratio-optimal. The auxiliary
complete canonical root-present cover has2955 rank-one original rows
at n3..7 and170913 proper subsets. Ten corruptions are rejected.

A distinct native complete-enumeration pressure reaches M10 with
172848 inputs/386016 whole-coset controls. It is **EXPLORATORY** until
independently audited, not included in the complete Python checker scope.

[Dubuc1998, Proposition4.6](https://www.numdam.org/article/ITA_1998__32_1-3_21_0.pdf)
proves n-extension for every extensible subset of an n-state circular
automaton. The primary paper was now accessible through Numdam. This
can be applied to a synchronizing CORE alphabet {a^2,b}, when that
alphabet really synchronizes. It gives a bound in macro letters. The
fixed original root, possible nonsynchronizing core alphabet and costTWO
of a^2 prevent silently using that result as an original-word square
proof here. No contradiction to Dubuc is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-opposite-kernel-primitive-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-opposite-kernel-primitive-square--primitive-opposite-kernel-square-with-arbitrary-tail-geometry"></a>
### Primitive opposite-kernel square with arbitrary tail geometry

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper, ALL-n under d=1.** No restriction on tail
height, root-cycle length, or other a-cycles. General Cerny OPEN.
Not FORMALLY VERIFIED; no priority or arbitrary-automaton reduction.

<a id="direct-attack-opposite-kernel-primitive-square--original-model-and-theorem"></a>
#### Original model and theorem

M=2L>=6, Q=Z_M union {r}. ORIGINAL b is the core cycle fixing r.
ORIGINAL a has rank M, doubled output r, omitted output L, a(r)=0,
and ANY opposite core kernel {H,H+L}, 0<=H<L. All remaining core
inputs biject onto C minus {0,L}; domain and output sets need not agree.
Set

    d=gcd(L,a(j)-a(j+L), 0<=j<L).

**Theorem (PROVED paper):** if d=1, every proper nonempty target has
positive nu-extension at ORIGINAL cost<=M, nu core1/root2. Root-present
targets admit unit ordinary growth retaining r. ONE reset satisfies

    rt <= M^2-L+1 < M^2=(n-1)^2.

This generalizes the earlier primitive criterion beyond the c0,t2
normal form; no permutation restriction on a off {0,L} is assumed.

<a id="direct-attack-opposite-kernel-primitive-square--two-letter-extensions-retain-all-original-costs"></a>
#### Two-letter extensions retain all original costs

Literal weighted counting gives nu a=nu+delta, nu b=nu,
delta=e0-eL. If U is not whole under shift L, choose j in U with
j+L outside. The ORIGINAL a b^j gains1, costs<=M, and sends r to
its positive selected core endpoint. At an even positive core size,
there are at least two split pairs; a j<=M-2 saves one letter.

For whole U, the original a b^j a b^s has defect on S equal to
chi_U(a(j)+s)-chi_U(a(j+L)+s), with either root flag. The kernel
pair has both outputs r, while every other pair has both outputs core.
Translate the core pair labels by all s modulo L. Their differences
generate the Cayley subgroup of index d. At d1, no nonconstant whole
set can have zero crossings in every translate.

Moreover the FULL undirected output-pair graph on labels1,...,L-1
has degree2: each core output state except0,L has one core preimage.
At a translate with a crossing, a binary coloring of a cycle crosses
at least TWO input edges. For each nonzero edge, cyclic summation of
its membership difference over s<L is0, so it has a positive translate.
Some positive input j<=L-2 therefore exists, giving an ORIGINAL word
of cost j+s+2<=2L-1=M-1. Its root image is its positive endpoint.
This proof works for arbitrary tails, because only the exact one-step
weighted defect and the two-to-one kernel are used.

<a id="direct-attack-opposite-kernel-primitive-square--constant-targets-and-one-compatible-reset"></a>
#### Constant targets and ONE compatible reset

Mixing gives at least two mixed edges in the same degree2 graph.
Take a mixed j<=L-2, k=(H-a(j)) mod L. The original word
f=a b^j a b^k a fixes r. Its weighted defect is

    delta + delta b^k a + delta b^j a b^k a.

On {r}, the first term is0. The middle term is0: the opposite input
pair k,k+L is either the kernel pair (both go to r) or neither endpoint
goes to r. The last term is e_r-e_z for a core z, because mixing
prevents the other endpoint from reaching the kernel after the shift.
Thus f has root gain1, root retained, and length<=M. Its inverse is
exactly root plus ONE core state. Reverse orientation
k=(H-a(j+L)) mod L gives e_z-e_r and handles target C at cost<=M.
No root-cycle or tail-height assumption entered this argument.

Starting at {r}, prepend these root-retaining unit-growth words.
Exactly M stages reset Q to r. Every positive even core size
2,4,...,M-2 saves at least one letter, either by the split-pair one-a
rule or the whole two-a rule. These L-1 savings occur on THIS SAME
chronological word, proving M^2-(L-1).

Root-absent ordinary growth is not claimed: introducing the root can
increase weighted mass while ordinary cardinality stays fixed.

<a id="direct-attack-opposite-kernel-primitive-square--all-prime-half-core-lengths-with-arbitrary-opposite-kernel"></a>
#### All prime half-core lengths, with arbitrary opposite kernel

If d=L, all opposite pairs go to opposite pairs or both to r. The
opposite-pair classes plus {r} form a permutation quotient: r goes
to label0, the kernel label H to r, and every remaining input pair
bijects onto a nonzero output pair label. b also permutes the classes.
Thus a synchronizing BINARY pair must have d<L. For prime L>=3 this
forces d=1, proving the stated square for ALL synchronizing inputs
of this original model, with ANY tail geometry and ANY H. The tiny
L2 model is nonsynchronizing and vacuous. Additional letters inherit
the bound whenever the specified binary pair already satisfies d1;
synchronization supplied only by extra letters is not a reduction.

<a id="direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary--forward-kernel-congruence-and-terminal-merge-graphs-have-different-boundaries"></a>
### Forward kernel congruence and terminal merge graphs have different boundaries

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for the general forward-closure
lemma and all-n counterfamily. The separate n6 terminal witness is
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. Priority and general Cerny **OPEN**.
No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim or unrestricted reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary--a-general-short-forward-congruence-certificate"></a>
#### A general short forward-congruence certificate

Let E_0 contain all unordered ORIGINAL letter-kernel pairs. Let E_j
contain their noncollapsed forward images under ORIGINAL words of
length at most j; retain the earlier edges. Let Pi_j be its component
partition. These are NOT the pairs merged by short words.

For ANY DFA, if Pi_j=Pi_(j+1), every letter maps each Pi_j-class INTO
one Pi_j-class. Indeed an E_j path maps to a path of E_(j+1) edges
with some edges possibly collapsed. Thus Pi_j is a congruence, and
all further forward edges stay in its classes. Stagnation is permanent.
The final partition theta is EXACTLY the smallest original congruence
containing all letter kernels: each such congruence contains every
forward edge, and the stabilized partition is itself a congruence.

If Pi_0 has c_0 classes and theta has t, define D=c_0-t. Its first
stabilized partition occurs at depth at most D, since every preceding
layer strictly reduces the number of components. Select a spanning
forest of E_0 and extend it at each strictly growing layer. If layer j
joins m_j components, choose m_j new edges with image-word length<=j.
Since every preceding layer joins at least one component and
sum m_j=D, the total IMAGE-WORD cost is at most D(D+1)/2. Initial kernel
edges have image-word cost zero. This is a forest certificate, NOT a
reset word and NOT a collection of short merging words.

The depth and cost are sharp. In C_n, take a full n-cycle and the unit
0->1. Through depth j<=n-2 the forward kernel graph has successive
cycle edges {0,1},...,{j,j+1}; the unit adds no other joining edge.
Exactly one joining edge appears per layer. Its depth is n-2 and the
minimum forest image-word cost is (n-2)(n-1)/2. Every original letter
is counted in an edge label; virtual inverses are not used.

<a id="direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary--connectivity-is-not-necessary-for-synchronization-even-sc-corank-one"></a>
#### Connectivity is NOT necessary for synchronization, even SC corank-one

For every n>=3 use ORIGINAL letters

    a(q)=q+1 for q<n-1,       a(n-1)=n-1;
    b(q)=q+1 for q<n-2,       b(n-2)=b(n-1)=0.

Both have rank n-1 and the SAME sole kernel pair {n-2,n-1}. Every
nonempty original word collapses this pair, so its forward graph
contains only that initial edge at ALL depths. Its n-1 components are
singletons0,...,n-3 and {n-2,n-1}.

Nevertheless a^(n-1) resets. Corank saturation gives rt>=n-1, hence
rt=n-1 EXACTLY. Strong connectivity follows from b's cycle0,...,n-2
and the a-edge n-2->n-1 followed by b back to0. In fact the ONLY shortest
labeled words are a^(n-1) and a^(n-2)b: any b before the last step
leaves an image without n-1, so the following letter cannot decrease
rank with the common kernel pair. All preceding letters must be a.

Here theta is a genuine congruence, but its quotient a is singular:
the predecessor singleton and the last class both map to the last
class. Containment of original kernels in a congruence does NOT imply
permutational quotient actions. Unequal class sizes allow distinct
classes to map disjointly INTO one class. This explains why replacing
the virtual NORMAL graph of [Nearest permutation completions: a general necessary theorem and a sharp failure](#direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary) by this
original forward graph invalidates the necessary synchronization proof.

The corresponding tempting linear argument fails for the same reason.
With f=(1,2,2), W=span(e_1-e_2) is invariant and contains ker(M_f).
Yet e_0-e_1 lies outside W and maps INTO W, so the induced action on
Q^3/W is noninjective. Kernel containment does not give an invertible
quotient. The earlier observability theorem uses trivial kernel
INTERSECTION and injectivity ON its invariant space; that proof is
unaffected.

<a id="direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary--a-smaller-terminal-graph-witness-beyond-n-steps"></a>
#### A smaller terminal-graph witness beyond n steps

The graph F_L of pairs MERGED by original words of length<=L is a
different graph. [Terminal-pair components can stagnate and then merge](#direct-attack-terminal-kernel-component-stagnation) already
refutes permanent stagnation and the cutoff n-1. Furthermore the
retained Figure3 family has finite n9 witnesses with a specified state
requiring12 steps, which already rules out a universal cutoff n.
The present independently found n6 example makes this failure smaller:

    a=(2,3,4,1,0,5),         b=(0,5,3,2,3,1).

It is binary SC, with ranks6 and5. In pair order01,02,03,04,05,12,13,
14,15,23,24,25,34,35,45 the exact merge distances are

    6,2,3,3,7,7,10,4,9,5,1,9,6,8,8.

Through length6 state5 is isolated; the other five states form one
component. F_7 is connected. Its exact state5 compress-with-another
threshold and graph connectivity threshold are both7>n. Full subset
BFS independently gives its reset threshold and original reset word
in the certificate; its exact threshold is19, below the square25. No all-n
terminal lower bound or arbitrary-alphabet state minimum is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-original-kernel-graph-boundary--verification-and-continued-research"></a>
#### Verification and continued research

The generator covers all labeled binary maps at n2..4, with every
forward partition/depth/forest cost streamed into a semantic hash.
The checker uses repeated FULL-class-image partition joins, rather
than forward-edge propagation, and independently reconstructs the
minimum-depth forest. The chain counterfamilies are checked through
n4096, including literal a powers on small scopes and all shortest
words on very small scopes. For the n6 terminal witness the checker
enumerates EVERY original word through length10, reconstructs all
pair distances and component layers, and performs ordinary set BFS.
The report verifies66281 complete binary inputs,45 chain parameters
throughn4096,1558 literal reset letters and252 small-chain words. The
n6 checker uses2046 literal words and56 full-image vertices. Twelve
corruptions are rejected.  These scopes do not supply a universal
quadratic proof.

The continued literature attack inspected [Volkov2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.13317)'s known primitive
defect-one synchronizability theorem and two 2026 preprints:
[Miccinesi's extension certificates](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.21603)
and [one-cluster annular descent](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.19675).
Neither was treated as an unrestricted Cerny proof. A seeded exploratory
attack of the latter's binary annular membership relation found no
counterexample in205813 samples/301750 controls (n4..12, binary, tested
filtration indices1..4 and skipped once the preceding cycle space was
full), with exact rational
rechecking specified for candidate failures. This is a negative finite
search in ignored native_build, NOT an independent universal proof,
novel theorem, or new registered check. Its limitation is that distinct

<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square--square-for-arbitrary-paired-root-cycles-and-tails"></a>
### Square for arbitrary paired root cycles and tails

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper, ALL parameters in the stated paired class.**
This strictly contains [Residue congruence closes the original order-two square model](#direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square) and permits
arbitrarily long root cycles. General Cerny remains OPEN. Not formal;
no priority claim and no arbitrary-automaton reduction.

<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square--model-and-bound"></a>
#### Model and bound

M=2L; ORIGINAL b cycles Z_M and fixes r. Choose distinct pair labels
and representatives V=(v0=0,v1,...,v_(tau-2)), with all vi mod L distinct.
The ORIGINAL a has root cycle

    r -> v0 -> v1 -> ... -> v_(tau-2) -> r,

and missing-state tail

    L -> v1+L -> ... -> v_(tau-2)+L -> r

(all core additions mod M). The tail has height tau-1. On the remaining
opposite pairs R, a is an arbitrary permutation A. Write B=L-tau+1
for their number and H=v_(tau-2) mod L for the kernel pair label.
Let

    d=gcd(L,a(j)-a(j+L), 0<=j<L).

Assume d<L, equivalently A mixes an opposite pair. If it does not,
the opposite-pair classes plus root form a permutation quotient, so
the automaton is nonsynchronizing. The proof below constructs a reset
when it does. The kernel is {H,H+L}, with arbitrary H and tau.

**Theorem (PROVED paper).** Every proper nonempty target admits a
positive nu-extension of ORIGINAL cost<=M, nu=(1,...,1,2). Root-present
targets admit a root-retaining extension adding exactly ONE core state.
ONE chronological ORIGINAL reset satisfies

    rt <= M^2-(L-d) < M^2=(n-1)^2.

The root-two-cycle case is tau2, V=(0); it is not the whole scope here.

<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square--why-the-weighted-background-remains-balanced"></a>
#### Why the weighted background remains balanced

Literal counting gives nu a=nu+delta, delta=e0-eL. The consecutive
delta a^i are opposite-point differences e_(vi)-e_(vi+L) for
0<=i<=tau-2, and vanish for i>=tau-1, when both endpoints reach r.
Therefore

    nu a^k=nu+sum_(i=0)^(k-1) delta a^i

evaluates to nu on EVERY whole core target, with either root flag,
for ALL k. This does not claim stationary nu a=nu on individual states.
The actual powers on R are powers of its permutation A.

<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square--periodic-target-only-represented-residue-classes-are-counted"></a>
#### Periodic target: only represented residue classes are counted

Let U be a nonconstant period-d core pattern of least period p|d.
Let p0 be the number of p residue classes represented in R and set

    K=B-p0+1.

Consider ACTUAL words a b^j a^k b^s for each remaining lower-half
pair index j, 1<=k<=K, 0<=s<p. Their gain is the two-point difference
chi_U(A^k(j)+s)-chi_U(A^k(j+L)+s), because the weighted background
above vanishes. A positive difference is1 and its endpoint is the
root image, so a root-present inverse retains r and grows by one.

Every such word has cost<=M. Indeed removing tau-1 opposite pairs
can delete a full residue class only after removing L/p pair labels.
Thus p-p0<=floor((tau-1)/(L/p)), while p<=d<=L/2 gives L/p>=2. Hence

    j+k+s+1 <= M+(p-p0)-tau+1
             <= M-ceil((tau-1)/2) <= M-1.

Suppose none is positive. Summation over all p tail shifts forces each
two-point difference to vanish in ALL shifts, hence its two endpoints
have the same residue mod p, by least period. Build the graph on R
with the opposite pairs and their images under A through power K.
Initially it has B components, and throughout it has at least p0
components. K=B-p0+1 strict mergers would leave at most p0-1, impossible.
Some consecutive partitions stabilize. A and its inverse preserve that
partition, so inverse opposite-pair endpoints have equal residues mod p.

The inverse-output-pair graph on the remaining pair labels has degree2.
A mixed nonloop component has at least two mixed vertices of one
residue. Some mixed j<=L-p-1 exists. Take k=(H-A(j)) mod L and then
a b^j a b^k a fixes r; its other defect endpoint is a core state z.
Choose s<p with z+s outside U. The original word costs<=M and gains1:
delta and delta b^k a b^s evaluate to0 (all a-pair differences are
congruent mod d), leaving only e_r-e_(z+s). It retains r.

For a root-absent target, choose k=(H-A(j+L)) mod L and z+s IN U,
giving the opposite surviving edge e_(z+s)-e_r. This proves both
root flags' weighted extensions. Missing residue classes are explicitly
handled by p0; assuming p0=p would be an unjustified shortcut.

<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square--compatible-reset-and-the-other-targets"></a>
#### Compatible reset and the other targets

Nonwhole U extends by a b^j at a boundary j, cost<=M, with root retained
and one added core state. At an even positive core size there are at
least two split pairs, so cost<=M-1.

Whole U not period-d has a positive a b^j a b^s, cost<=M-1. All root/tail
path pairs map to opposite pairs or to the same root; they give zero.
On R the output-pair graph is degree2, so a translated nonconstant
coloring crosses at least two input edges. A positive translate exists
for each; some j<=L-2, s<L saves a letter. The core image of r is the
positive endpoint. The gcd criterion ensures such a crossing whenever
the whole set is not period-d.

For the initial {r}, the least mixed j<=L-2 and k=(H-A(j)) mod L give
a b^j a b^k a of cost<=M, root-fixed and nu-gain1. Its inverse is root
plus one core point. The opposite orientation handles target C.

Prepend the actual root-retaining unit-growth words. Exactly M stages
reset all states to r. Among the L-1 positive even core levels, only
d-1 can be period-d, so at least L-d stages save one letter on this
SAME chain. This proves the announced M^2-(L-d) bound.

<a id="direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square--independent-finite-scope-and-remaining-issue"></a>
#### Independent finite scope and remaining issue

Complete new mixed paired forms at M8/M10 with tau>=3 are covered;
their count is the sum of

    P(L-1,tau-2) * 2^(tau-2) * ((2B)!-2^B B!).

The factor 2^B B! counts exactly the nonsplitting permutations. Literal
model checks and unique signatures plus this count independently
verify coverage. Additional invariant-residue controls through n257

Small periodic target lists are COMPLETE with BOTH root flags; the

The checker uses original particle transitions for every word/full
reset, validates all chain budgets, reconstructs model and least period,
and independently checks the stabilization fallback. Six corrupted
certificates are rejected. Counts and command captures are in the
separate scoped audit. This is PROVED paper plus COMPUTATIONALLY
VERIFIED controls, not FORMALLY VERIFIED.

Counts:6249 compatible resets, COMPLETE6240 new paired inputs,
62992 original unit stages,25212 saved even stages,18836762 reset
particles.25454 periodic targets/33975363 particles include17142

The d64 list has only SIX named BOTH-root-flag controls; the small

Unpaired short-tail root components, late kernels at other displacement

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost--exact-uniform-permutation-averaging-can-require-quadratic-word-cost"></a>
### Exact uniform permutation averaging can require quadratic word cost

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)**, a method obstruction with no
publication-priority or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. The unrestricted
Cerny conjecture remains **OPEN**.

The single-permutation theorem has a positive averaging polynomial of
short original degree. A possible extension would use transitivity of
an arbitrary permutation group to average to J/n within original word
length n-1. This extension is **REFUTED** for all n>=6. The distinction
between group membership and original word cost is essential here.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost--exact-optimal-expected-cost"></a>
#### Exact optimal EXPECTED cost

On Q={0,...,n-1}, n>=2, take the n-1 adjacent transpositions tau_i
swapping i and i+1. They generate S_n. For a permutation word w set

    F(w)=sum_q |qw-q|.

Every letter moves exactly two original tokens by one line position.
The triangle inequality therefore gives F(w)<=2|w|. Suppose a
nonnegative probability distribution p_w on actual permutation words
has exact uniform matrix average

    sum_w p_w M_w = J/n.

Every state's final position is uniform. Consequently

    E F(w) = (1/n)sum_(q,r) |r-q| = (n^2-1)/3,
    E |w| >= (n^2-1)/6.                                (1)

This lower bound is attained. Use the uniform distribution on the
n cyclic shifts g_k(q)=q+k modulo n. The shift g_k has k(n-k)
inversions and is a product of exactly k(n-k) adjacent transpositions.
For a nonidentity row g, choose adjacent OUTPUT labels i,i+1 whose
preimages satisfy g^(-1)(i)>g^(-1)(i+1). Right multiplying by tau_i
swaps those values and decreases the inversion count by exactly one.
Repeat until identity and reverse the recorded letter indices. Since
each letter is an involution, this is an actual positive right-action
word for g of its inversion length. Their average matrix is J/n, and

    (1/n)sum_(k=0)^(n-1) k(n-k) = (n^2-1)/6.             (2)

Thus the exact minimum EXPECTED original word length of any uniform
permutation average is (n^2-1)/6. If a distribution had support entirely
on words of length at most L, its expected length would be at most L.
Hence its maximum support cost is at least ceil((n^2-1)/6). This is
strictly larger than n-1 for every n>=6, since

    (n^2-1)/6-(n-1) = (n-1)(n-5)/6.

The cyclic-shift construction supplies a quadratic maximum support cost
floor(n^2/4). No exact optimum for MAXIMUM support cost is asserted.
Nor is n6 asserted to be the minimum possible refutation of that
maximum-cost proposal; the all-n lower bound suffices.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost--synchronizing-embedding-and-scope"></a>
#### Synchronizing embedding and scope

Adjoin the unit letter sending n-1 to zero and fixing other states.
The base automaton is strongly connected because its permutation group
is S_n. It synchronizes: conjugating the unit by actual permutation
words gives every desired single-state collapse p->q, so one can
reduce any nonsingleton image until only one state remains.
Inverse words are reversals of adjacent-transposition words and their
costs are not removed. This is an existence argument, not a reset bound.

The obstruction (1) still applies to its PERMUTATION-only averaging
support. It makes no claim about averages that also use singular words,
one-row averages, target-dependent distributions, or other stationary
mass arguments. It does not refute a linear extension bound or the
square for this synchronizing family. In particular, a short transversal
for one state is not a simultaneous uniform average for ALL states.

This closes the proposed direct generalization of the earlier positive
cycle average. A general proof would have to exploit singular actions,
subset-dependent transport, or another compatible global mechanism.
Independent audit/check records are kept separately and must retain
the exact original-letter interpretation.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit--independent-audit-exact-uniform-averaging-pays-quadratic-word-cost"></a>
### Independent audit: exact uniform averaging pays quadratic word cost

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** as an obstruction to a proposed
averaging method. The bounded checks below are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**.
Publication priority is **OPEN**; no novelty or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim
is made. This does not prove or refute the unrestricted Cerny conjecture.

The current [Exact uniform permutation averaging can require quadratic word cost](#direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost) is mathematically sound,
including its explicit adjacent-OUTPUT-value sorting and reversed-word
construction. The averaging support must use actual original permutation
letters. Group membership and abstract inverses never have zero cost.
The exact optimum proved here concerns EXPECTED cost; it does not determine
the optimum MAXIMUM support cost or a minimum refutation state size.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit--1-a-precise-lower-bound-for-every-nonnegative-uniform-average"></a>
#### 1. A precise lower bound for every nonnegative uniform average

On Q={0,...,n-1}, n>=2, take the adjacent transpositions tau_i swapping
i and i+1. They generate the transitive group S_n. For a right-action
word w define its displacement

    F(w)=sum_(q in Q) |qw-q|.

At each step exactly two original trajectories are at output positions
i and i+1. Right multiplication by tau_i moves each one unit. The triangle
inequality gives F(w)<=2|w|. This remains true for a nonshortest word,
including cancellation pairs; redundant original letters cannot lower cost.

Let nonnegative weights p_w give the exact row-transition-matrix average

    sum_w p_w M_w=J/n.

If normalization was not separately required, summing any matrix row
already forces sum_w p_w=1. Every q consequently has uniform final image,
so

    E F(w) = (1/n) sum_(q,r) |q-r|
           = (2/n) sum_(d=1)^(n-1) d(n-d)
           = (n^2-1)/3.

Thus EVERY such distribution satisfies

    E |w| >= (n^2-1)/6.                                (1)

The argument also covers countable support. An infinite expected cost
satisfies the inequality; if the expectation is finite, the same
nonnegative sums and termwise bound apply. No uniform distribution on
the whole group and no independence of different states is assumed.

The displacement is the established Spearman footrule statistic. The
relation of footrule to inversion distance is classical; see
[Diaconis--Graham, 1977](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1977.tb01624.x).
The original-word inequality used above has been proved directly here.
This source supports the attribution, not a priority claim for this
particular averaging obstruction.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit--2-exact-attainment-with-the-right-action-checked"></a>
#### 2. Exact attainment, with the right action checked

Take g_k(q)=q+k mod n, k=0,...,n-1. Its one-line row is
`[k,k+1,...,n-1,0,1,...,k-1]`. It has k(n-k) inversions and displacement
`2k(n-k)`.

Here is a literal positive-word algorithm valid with right actions.
For a nonidentity permutation row g, choose adjacent output values i,i+1
whose preimages satisfy `g^(-1)(i)>g^(-1)(i+1)`. Such an i exists because
the preimage list is a nonidentity permutation and therefore has an
adjacent descent. Right multiplication by tau_i swaps these VALUES.
Comparisons with every other value are unchanged, so the inversion count
falls by exactly one. Repeat until identity. If the sorting word is
`tau_(i_1)...tau_(i_L)`, the reverse sequence
`tau_(i_L)...tau_(i_1)` realizes g starting from identity, and has the
SAME actual cost L. Each inverse letter is literally itself; none is
removed or charged for free. In particular g_k has an actual word of
length k(n-k). Inequality F/2 also proves that no shorter word realizes it.

Choose those n words with weights 1/n, including the empty identity word.
For each q, the images g_k(q) run through Q exactly once, so the average
matrix is J/n. Their mean original cost is

    (1/n) sum_(k=0)^(n-1) k(n-k)=(n^2-1)/6.              (2)

Equations (1)--(2) prove the exact minimum expected cost. The cyclic
construction has maximum support cost floor(n^2/4); the lower bound on
every possible maximum support cost is only ceil((n^2-1)/6). These two
quantities are not asserted to be equal.

For n>=6, the expected optimum is greater than n-1, since the difference
is `(n-1)(n-5)/6`. Therefore exact uniform averaging supported entirely
on permutation words of original length at most n-1 is **REFUTED** for
every n>=6 in this family. No state-minimum statement is inferred for
other alphabets or from the inconclusive smaller cases.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit--3-an-exact-six-state-separating-functional"></a>
#### 3. An exact six-state separating functional

At n=6 use the coefficient matrix H_(q,r)=|q-r|. Every word of length
at most five has `sum_(q,r) H_(q,r) (M_w)_(q,r)=F(w)<=10`. Therefore
the same upper bound holds for every convex mixture of these matrices.
The proposed uniform average has functional value

    sum_(q,r) H_(q,r)/6 = 35/3 > 10.

This is an exact rational separation certificate, requiring no numerical
optimization. Independent whole-group BFS finds 169 distinct permutation
actions obtainable through five adjacent transpositions; their largest
F is ten. The cyclic-shift certificate has lengths `[0,5,8,9,8,5]`, mean
35/6, and exact matrix average J/6. The functional excludes every allowed
short-word mixture, including arbitrary repeated words and zero weights.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit--4-strongly-connected-synchronizing-embedding"></a>
#### 4. Strongly connected synchronizing embedding

Adjoin the singular unit letter e taking n-1 to zero and fixing other
states. Adjacent permutations already make the base state graph strongly
connected. An explicit literal full-Q reset word is

    product_(j=n-1,n-2,...,1) (tau_j tau_(j+1)...tau_(n-2) e),

where the permutation part is empty at j=n-1. Before its j-stage the
current image is `{0,...,j}`. The permutation part sends j to n-1 and
fixes every smaller live state; e then merges that point with zero.
The resulting image is `{0,...,j-1}`. The total original cost is
`n(n-1)/2`. This is an upper-bound witness, not an exact threshold claim.
The checker supplies separate literal transition-row validation through
n=32.

The averaging support remains permutation-only. A word containing e
cannot act as a permutation: its full-Q rank drops and subsequent letters
cannot restore it. Thus the lower bound applies also if "permutation
support" is interpreted semantically as words whose resulting actions
are permutations. Averages using singular actions, a uniform image for
only ONE starting state, signed linear combinations, target-dependent
transport, and weaker stationary averaging conditions are outside the
assertion. Those methods are not refuted here.
