<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary--nearest-permutation-completions-a-general-necessary-theorem-and-a-sharp-failure"></a>
### Nearest permutation completions: a general necessary theorem and a sharp failure

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for arbitrary finite alphabets and
all n, with the scopes below. Priority **OPEN**. General Cerny **OPEN**.
No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. Virtual permutations are NEVER charged
as original letters or asserted to belong to the original monoid.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary--general-completion-theorem"></a>
#### General completion theorem

For a map f:Q->Q of rank r, a nearest permutation completion p agrees
with f on exactly r states: choose one representative in each fiber,
keep its f-image, and biject the other n-r sources onto the n-r missing
targets. These are EXACTLY the permutations minimizing Hamming distance
from f. Denote their set C(f). For a permutation f, C(f)={f}.
Given an arbitrary DFA, form the VIRTUAL group

    G=< C(a): a is an ORIGINAL letter >.

**Theorem.** If the DFA is synchronizing, G=S_n.

**Proof.** For any two states x,y in one fiber of a letter f, and any
p in C(f), the completion p' obtained by interchanging its x,y source
values is again in C(f). Their quotient p' p^(-1) is the transposition
(x,y). Thus G contains every original kernel-pair transposition.

Let E consist of all images of these kernel pairs under G, and let
the components of the undirected graph (Q,E) be C_1,...,C_t. G preserves
E and permutes these components. For any completion p of f, write

    f=e p,       e(q)=p^(-1)(f(q)).                         (1)

The map e sends every f-fiber to its selected representative. All of
its moves are within one graph component, because every fiber pair is
an initial edge. Consequently e fixes component MEMBERSHIP, and f
induces the SAME permutation of components as p. Original permutation
letters do so as well. Every original word therefore permutes the t
components. A reset word forces t=1.

Transpositions along a connected graph generate S_n: a spanning tree
and conjugations along its paths give any pair transposition. Every edge
transposition in E is a conjugate of an original kernel transposition
and belongs to G. Hence S_n is contained in G, proving equality. The
n1 case is immediate. No strong connectivity assumption is required.

This theorem is about a virtual GROUP, not reset-word membership or
length. It does not invoke a theorem about an ORIGINAL primitive group.
The distinction matters: for example the original-transitive-group
bound of [Zhu2024](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.08135) assumes actual
permutational generators, which the completions need not be.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary--exact-subset-compatibility-not-arbitrary-permutation-control"></a>
#### Exact subset compatibility, not arbitrary permutation control

For any map f and subset S, f is injective on S if and only if there
exists p in C(f) agreeing with f on EVERY point of S.

If f is injective, select all S-points as their fiber representatives,
choose one representative for every other fiber, and fill missing
targets as above. Conversely agreement with a permutation gives
injectivity. Therefore EVERY rank-neutral original step has a compatible
completion on its CURRENT image, even for arbitrary corank.
The compatible choice can change with the image. It does not permit
choosing arbitrary completion effects: all compatible choices have
the SAME action f on that image. A rank-dropping step has no such
permutation restriction on the full image.

For a corank-one f with kernel {x,y}, its two completions agree on
S if both x,y are outside S; exactly one agrees if precisely one is
in S; neither agrees if both are in S. This is an exact online token
description, not an additional alphabet. Ignoring its compatibility
condition destroys the original synchronization problem.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary--a-binary-sc-counterfamily-for-every-n3"></a>
#### A binary SC counterfamily for EVERY n>=3

Take states 0,...,n-1 and ORIGINAL letters

    a=(0,1) as a transposition, fixing all other states;
    0b=1b=2; qb=q+1 for 2<=q<n-1; (n-1)b=0.

The b-cycle is 0,2,3,...,n-1, and state1 enters it; a reaches1 from0.
This proves strong connectivity. The partition

    {0,1}, {2}, {3},...,{n-1}

is an ORIGINAL congruence. On its n-1 classes a is the identity and b
is a full cycle. Thus EVERY original word has rank at least n-1. Since
b has rank n-1, the minimum rank is EXACTLY n-1, not1.
The complete actual-image closure is just

    Q, Q\{0}, Q\{1}.

Indeed a exchanges the last two images and b sends either to Q\{1}.
Thus nonsynchronization holds at ALL word lengths, not only a BFS cutoff.

Yet the two nearest completions of b are

    p_plus: change 0b to1,     p_minus: change 1b to1.

p_plus is the FULL n-cycle 0,1,2,...,n-1. Together with original a it
generates S_n, by conjugating (0,1) around that cycle. The virtual
completion group is therefore S_n for every n>=3, although no original
word even makes a second rank drop. This REFUTES the converse of the
general theorem in binary SC corank-one automata, and REFUTES transfer
of synchronization from the virtual permutation group.

Neither completion belongs to the original transition monoid, at ANY
positive length. Any word containing b has rank at most n-1 and cannot
be a permutation. The words without b give only identity and a, while
p_plus and p_minus are different from both for n>=3. This is a membership
failure, stronger than an unbounded inverse cost. At n2 every singular
letter is already a reset, so n3 is minimal for this counterexample
over any finite alphabet.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary--general-signed-error-form-and-the-remaining-proof-target"></a>
#### General signed-error form and the remaining proof target

For ANY nearest completion p of f, its deterministic row matrix has
the exact form

    M_f=P+sum_(q not selected) e_q^T (e_(f(q))-e_(p(q))).   (2)

All coefficients are nonnegative, but each summand is SIGNED. Iterating
these identities yields the same type of source-weighted error expansion
used in [Sharp avoid-or-compress examples for every fixed cardinality gap](#direct-attack-avoid-compress-all-gaps). Unlike that construction, an arbitrary
DFA need not have a common error direction or useful distance separation.
Moreover P is a virtual permutation unless represented by an actual word.
Neither (1), (2), full G, nor subset compatibility proves a quadratic cost.

The next substantive target is a bound using only COMPATIBLE original
steps and paid rank drops. Replacing original singular letters by their
completions, assuming their inverse words exist, or importing an actual
transitive-group bound into this virtual group are all invalid shortcuts.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-completion-boundary--independent-finite-scope"></a>
#### Independent finite scope

permutation_completion_boundary.py records all-map completion controls,
complete designated binary rank-n/rank-(n-1) scopes, and counterfamily
certificates. The independent checker defines nearest completions by
enumerating EVERY permutation and maximizing agreement, without importing
the generator. It compares every fiber retraction/transposition identity,
independent set-image BFS and FULL group enumeration, SC and exact family
closure. Small counterfamily scopes additionally enumerate the entire
original transition monoid and exclude both completions. Corruptions are
rejected. The report gives the exact COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED finite scope;
the preceding arguments supply the all-n paper theorem and failure.

The completed finite report checks ALL 3412 maps at n2..5 and ALL their
24570 nearest completions, 104328 subset-compatibility controls, 79198
kernel swaps and 604308 signed-error coordinates. ALL 28816 designated
labeled binary inputs at n2..4 use 604128 independently enumerated group
elements and 231504 set-image vertices. The 45 counterfamily parameters
run through n4096; eight complete original monoids at n3..10 have 104
elements in total. Eleven deliberate corruptions are rejected.
 Not a full112
rerun, arbitrary-alphabet census, formal proof, or new reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop--sharp-linear-bound-for-the-first-permutation-mediated-rank-drop"></a>
### Sharp linear bound for the first permutation-mediated rank drop

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. **PROVED on paper** for arbitrary finite permutation
alphabets, arbitrary `n`, and every `2<=r<n`. The exact literature
priority is **OPEN**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. The unrestricted
`e(S)<=2n`, compatible square-cost image chain, and Cerny conjecture
remain **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop--rainbow-subspace-lemma"></a>
#### Rainbow-subspace lemma

Let `B` be an `r`-subset of an `n`-state set, let `Pi` be any collection
of permutation letters, and let `c:Q->{1,...,r}` be a surjective
coloring. A word `w` over `Pi` is *rainbow* if `Bw` contains exactly one
state of each color. Let `T` be the minimum length of a non-rainbow word,
or infinity if none exists. Then

    T<infinity  implies  T<=n-r+1.                       (1)

Proof. Regard each `Bw` as its incidence row vector `v_w` in `R^n`.
Let `V_k` be the real span of the `v_w` with `|w|<=k`. Write `F_j` for
the states of color `j`. On every `r`-set incidence vector, being
rainbow is equivalent to the `r-1` homogeneous equations

    sum_(q in F_j) v_q - (1/r) sum_(q in Q) v_q = 0,
    j=1,...,r-1.                                        (2)

Because all `r` fibers are nonempty, these linear forms are independent:
evaluating a linear dependence on a state in fiber `r` first forces the
sum of coefficients to zero, and then evaluating one state in each
earlier fiber forces every coefficient to zero. Their common kernel
`K` therefore has dimension `n-r+1`.

If `V_(k+1)=V_k`, then `V_k` is invariant under every permutation
generator: the image of each spanning `v_w`, `|w|<=k`, is `v_(wp)` in
`V_(k+1)`. If all words through depth `k+1` are rainbow, `V_k` is
contained in `K`, so invariance makes **every future word rainbow**.
If `T=0`, (1) is immediate. When a first failure occurs at `T>=1`,
every transition
`V_k` to `V_(k+1)` for `0<=k<=T-2` is a strict dimension increase.
Since `dim(V_0)=1` and `V_(T-1)` lies in `K`,
`T<=dim(V_(T-1))<=n-r+1`. This proves (1). The argument does not use
transitivity or strong connectivity, and it controls simultaneous
words over any number of permutation generators.

The bound is attained whenever `n mod r != 0`: let `a` be the full
`n`-cycle, `B={0,...,r-1}`, and color `q` by `q mod r`. For
`0<=t<=n-r`, `Ba^t` is a contiguous nonwrapping rainbow `r`-set.
At `t=n-r+1` it wraps around the cycle, and because the length-`n`
color sequence is not circularly `r`-periodic, that set repeats a
color. Hence `T=n-r+1`. The coloring can be realized by the rank-`r`
letter `b(q)=q mod r`, whose full image is exactly `B`.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop--first-drop-for-permutation-plus-rank-r-letters"></a>
#### First drop for permutation plus rank-r letters

Suppose every nonpermutation letter of an automaton has rank exactly
`r`, with `2<=r<n`. If some word reduces `Q` below rank `r`, take a
shortest such word. Permutations before its first rank-`r` letter do
nothing to `Q`. A later rank-`r` letter that preserves rank `r`
sends the current `r`-set onto that letter's **full** `Q`-image;
deleting the whole prefix through it would shorten the first-drop
word. Consequently the shortest first-drop word has the exact form

    d_i w d_j,                                           (3)

where `w` uses only permutations. The image `B_i=Qd_i` is an `r`-set,
and the fibers of `d_j` are an `r`-coloring. Its last letter drops rank
exactly when `B_i w` is non-rainbow. Applying (1) to the attaining pair
gives a first proper drop below `r` in at most

    1+(n-r+1)+1 = n-r+3 letters.                     (4)

For `r=2`, this recovers the `rt<=n+1` theorem in
[Linear reset and image extension when every singular letter has rank two](#direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations). For `r=3`, every synchronizing
automaton whose letters are permutations or rank-three maps reaches an
actual image of size at most two within `n` letters. A pair that can
be synchronized has a simple path in the pair automaton through at
most `binom(n,2)` pair vertices before its final merge. Therefore

    rt <= n + binom(n,2) = n(n+1)/2.                 (5)

The same (5) holds if lower-rank letters are also allowed: a rank-one
or rank-two letter immediately reaches size at most two, after which
the identical pair-path bound applies. For `n>=5`, (5) is strictly
below `(n-1)^2`, since their difference is
`(n^2-5n+2)/2>0`. This is a **PROVED** Cerny-square result for the
low-rank alphabet class at `n>=5`; it is not a general square proof.
The bound (5) by itself is one above the square at `n=4`, and we do
not use it to assert the four-state case.

The reset bound does **not** supply a compatible shortest-image policy.
The existing [A global shortest-image-policy penalty with reset threshold three](#direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty) family has exactly one
permutation letter, one rank-two letter, and one rank-three letter:
`rt=3` but complete-cost best image policy `P=n` for every even
`n>=6`. Hence even this low-rank class requires separate control of
the globally compatible chain. We assert no policy-square theorem for
it, and (5) gives no universal image-extension bound.

<a id="direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop--why-the-earlier-binary-component-proof-does-not-extend-verbatim"></a>
#### Why the earlier binary component proof does not extend verbatim

[A six-state rank-three boundary for signed components](#direct-attack-rank-three-color-stall-boundary) gives a strongly connected,
synchronizing six-state example with one rank-three letter and two
permutations. Its triple-edge graph is connected already at depth one,
is still collision-free at depth two, then suffers its first color
collision at depth three. The component sequence is `[4,1,1,1]`.
Hence the signed-component *stagnation* lemma for two colors is false
for three colors. The vector-space sequence can still grow after the
component partition stops growing; (1) survives and is sharp.

The exact finite n4/5 designated covers and the independent n6/7
counterexample checks are saved with scripts, literal commands, and
hashes under `data/`. Finite checks are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**
within their scopes; the all-n assertions above rest on the proof.

<a id="direct-attack-permuted-shadow-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-permuted-shadow-square--arbitrary-tail-order-on-an-opposite-root-cycle-state-set"></a>
### Arbitrary tail order on an opposite root-cycle state set

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper under the explicit remaining-A mixing
condition.** General Cerny OPEN; no formal verification or priority claim.

M=2L, ORIGINAL b cycles the core and fixes r. The ORIGINAL a-root cycle
is r,V0=0,V1,...,V_(h-1),r, with h distinct opposite-pair labels, so
tau=h+1. The missing-state tail is W0=L,W1,...,W_(h-1),r, where W is
ANY ordering of the opposite states {Vi+L}, with W_(h-1)=V_(h-1)+L.
The remaining core R is an arbitrary permutation A, assumed to MIX
an opposite pair. Thus B=L-h>=2. Define

    d=gcd(L,a(j)-a(j+L), 0<=j<L)<L.

**Theorem (PROVED paper):** WEXT holds at cost<=M; root-present targets
have root-retaining ONE-core extensions; ONE original reset has

    rt <= M^2-(L-d) < (n-1)^2.

This includes tail orders that are physically unpaired along time.
The exact ordered-pair model is retained in [Square for arbitrary paired root cycles and tails](#direct-attack-paired-root-cycle-square).

<a id="direct-attack-permuted-shadow-square--actual-period-alternative-without-a-summed-row-shortcut"></a>
#### Actual-period alternative, without a summed-row shortcut

With nu core1/root2 and delta=e0-eL, exact counting gives nu a=nu+delta.
The rows delta a^i are e_(Vi)-e_(Wi) for i<h, and0 for i>=h, because
both trajectories reach r at the SAME time. These are CORE point pairs.

Let a nonconstant period-d core target have least period p|d. If some
Vi,Wi have different residues mod p, choose the FIRST such index i.
All earlier differences evaluate to0 in every p shift. Least period
ensures the i-th difference has a positive shift s<p. The ACTUAL word
a^(i+1) b^s has nu-gain1; its root image is Vi+s, the positive selected
core endpoint. It retains r for a root-present target. Its cost is

    i+1+s <= h+p-1 <= (L-2)+(L/2)-1 <= M-1.

It is important to choose the FIRST individual difference. Equality
of a sum of later differences would not identify residue multisets;
the independently REFUTED period6 summed-row shortcut is not used.

Otherwise EVERY Vi and Wi has the same residue mod p. All transported
background rows then vanish on every shifted target, for ALL a powers.
Only in this alternative apply the remaining permutation proof:
let p0 be the classes represented in R and K=B-p0+1. The actual pool
a b^j a^k b^s, remaining lower-half j, k<=K, s<p, has gain equal to
the SINGLE pair A^k(j)-A^k(j+L). Its cost is at most

    M+(p-p0)-h <= M-ceil(h/2) <= M-1.

Here missing a full class requires deleting L/p pair labels, so
p-p0<=floor(h/(L/p))<=floor(h/2). If no pool word is positive,
the B-component matching stabilizes by power K inside its p0 residue
classes, implying inverse-pair congruence for A. Since A itself is
mixed, its degree2 inverse graph supplies a mixed j<=L-p-1.
With H=V_(h-1) mod L, k=(H-A(j)) mod L, a b^j a b^k a b^s
gives the root-retaining gain1 at cost<=M. Choose s with the other
core defect endpoint absent. The middle delta b^k a term vanishes
because p|d. Reverse orientation handles a root-absent target.

The condition that REMAINING A mixes is used exactly here. Mixing
caused only by the reordered root/tail paths does not supply this
inverse-R cycle. No theorem is asserted for that omitted case, although
the early-shadow branch still handles some of its targets.

<a id="direct-attack-permuted-shadow-square--one-reset-and-all-remaining-cases"></a>
#### ONE reset and all remaining cases

Nonwhole targets use a b^j at a boundary. Whole targets not period-d
use a b^j a b^s; the FULL output-pair graph on labels1,...,L-1 has
degree2 even when tail order is changed. A crossing has at least two
nonzero input edges, yielding j<=L-2 and cost<=M-1. Kernel pairs
have both endpoints r, while all other input pairs have both endpoints
core, so every nonzero edge has a positive translate.

The remaining mixed A supplies a cost<=M root seed a b^j a b^k a,
k=(H-A(j)) mod L, root-fixed with nu-gain1. The opposite endpoint
handles target C. Exactly M actual root-retaining unit-growth stages
give ONE reset. At least L-d positive even core levels are nonperiod-d
and save one letter on THIS chain, proving the announced bound.

<a id="direct-attack-permuted-shadow-square--independent-controls-and-remaining-boundary"></a>
#### Independent controls and remaining boundary

Complete NEW M12/tau5 reordered-tail forms with mixed remaining A:
7680 inputs, counted as P(5,3)*2^3*(4!-2^2*2!)*(2!-1). The last factor
excludes the already-proved identical tail order. Literal model checks
and unique signatures independently certify this entire finite scope.

Total7685 resets,92768 original unit stages,38695 even-stage savings,

<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square--a-square-bound-for-every-positive-second-kernel-input"></a>
### A square bound for every positive second kernel input

Date: 2026-10-03, after release HEAD ac948e7.

**PROVED (paper), ALL M>=3 and ALL positive c in the stated normal form.**
The independent finite audit is **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** separately.
This theorem is not FORMALLY VERIFIED and carries no novelty claim.
General Cerny remains **OPEN**; no reduction of arbitrary automata to this
normal form is asserted. The SYNC c=0 opposite-pair case remains **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square--original-letter-theorem"></a>
#### Original-letter theorem

Let Q={r} union Z_M, n=M+1, and let the ORIGINAL letter b cycle Z_M
and fix r. The ORIGINAL letter a has omitted output L in1..M-1,
doubled output r, a(r)=0, and a(L)=a(c)=r, where

    1<=c<M, c!=L.

On the other core inputs it is any bijection to C\{0,L}. Then ONE
compatible original reset word of length <=M^2=(n-1)^2 exists.
Synchronization need not be assumed. The root a-cycle can have any length
at least THREE; other a-cycles, gcd(M,L), and the core bijection are unrestricted.
A larger alphabet containing these two original letters inherits the bound.

The missing state L is required to be a kernel input: this is a rank-one,
level-one tail normal form, not every rank-one letter. The singleton root
is b's fixed state and a's doubled output. These conditions matter.

More precisely, set g=gcd(M,L). There is an admissible J in{L,c} with

    a(L+J)!=r,        J+g<=M.

Put H equal to the other kernel input, p=a^-1(H-J), with all core sums
modulo M. The construction has the explicit bound

    rt <= M^2 - [(2M-3-p-c) + (M-J-g)] <= M^2.

Both brackets are nonnegative. J, p and every b-power are original
costs; a b^J a is never treated as one free letter.

<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square--why-an-admissible-j-always-exists"></a>
#### Why an admissible J always exists

For any positive c,L, J=c is admissible: (L+c) mod M cannot equal
either L or c. Also g<=M-L.

* If c<L, choose J=c. Then c+g<=L-1+M-L=M-1.
* If c>L and c!=(2L) mod M, choose J=L. Then J+g<=M and
  a(2L)!=r (2L mod M cannot equal L).
* Otherwise c>L forces c=2L<M. Choose J=c. Since g divides the
  positive M-2L, g<=M-2L and c+g<=M.

No separate spectral, coprimality, or synchronization condition is needed.

<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square--paid-root-return-and-the-exact-seed"></a>
#### Paid root return and the exact seed

The literal f=a b^J a fixes r and has full multiplicity defect

    D(f)=e_r+e_0-e_L-e_z,      z=a(L+J) in C\{0,L}.

The target H-J is neither0 norL: equality0 would identify the two
kernel inputs; equalityL is excluded by admissibility when J=L,
and by c>0 when J=c. Thus p exists uniquely in the core and is
neither c nor L. Directly,

    {r}f^-1={r,p}.

Use v=a b^p f, of cost p+J+3. Its literal inverse action is

    {r} --f^-1--> {r,p} --b^-p--> {r,0} --a^-1--> {r,c,L}.

This is a sizeTHREE root seed for EVERY p, even when p is large.
The earlier short-return proof used this seed only when immediately cheap.
Here its entire cost is paid globally.

Immediately prepend the ORIGINAL word a b^c. Since (L+c) mod M
is neither L nor c, it grows {r,c,L} by ONE and retains r. Its cost
is c+1, and the seed's core is necessarily nonwhole under translation L.
This designated first step saves M-c-1 additional letters beyond the
one letter saved by an arbitrary nonwhole step. That saving is essential.

<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square--every-remaining-root-stage-costs-at-most-n"></a>
#### Every remaining root stage costs at most n

For proper S={r} union U with nonempty U:

* If U is not invariant under translation L, a cyclic boundary j exists
  with j in U, L+j outside U. The original word a b^j retains r,
  grows by ONE, and costs j+1<=M=n-1.
* Otherwise U is a union of the g-cosets. Choose s in0..g-1 with
  z+s outside U. This exists because S is proper. The literal
  f b^s retains r and has growth 1-chi_U(z+s)=1, because
  chi_U(s)=chi_U(L+s). It costs J+2+s<=J+g+1<=n.

All extensions grow by EXACTLY ONE. Starting after the sizeTHREE seed,
the stage core sizes are EXACTLY2,3,...,M-1. If t=M/g, a whole-coset
stage has core size divisible by t. At most g-1 of these M-2 stages
can be whole. Hence at least N=M-g-1 stages are nonwhole, including
the designated first step. They each save one versus n, and the first
saves the additional M-c-1 above.

Consequently the SAME chronologically compatible reset word costs at most

    p+J+3 + (M-2)(M+1) - (M-g-1) - (M-c-1)
      = M^2 + p+J+c+g-3M+3
      = M^2 - [(2M-3-p-c)+(M-J-g)].

Since p,c are distinct core indices, p+c<=2M-3. Together with
J+g<=M this proves the square bound. There is no switch to an
independently optimized endpoint, no guessed seed bound, no truncated
extension hypothesis, and no monotonicity assumption beyond the explicit
verified root stages.

<a id="direct-attack-positive-kernel-square--audit-scope-and-remaining-boundary"></a>
#### Audit scope and remaining boundary

The generator `positive_kernel_square.py` and independent checker
`check_positive_kernel_square.py` are separate. The checker imports no
generator and validates exact parameter coverage, full literal particle
images, f's defect and root preimage, the paid seed, every extension,
the designated first saving, global arithmetic, and each original reset.
For each small input it also verifies ALL proper whole-coset patterns.
Large random controls do not assert complete coverage.

Previously complete strict-return M5..7 inputs (3006) are deliberately
omitted. The new complete scope is ALL other positive-c forms M3..8,
including ALL M8 forms. Additional original-word controls go through n257.
The independent audit checks33532 inputs,31400 complete NEW inputs,
79586794 literal particle controls,238307 root-preserving extensions,
78200 ALL-small whole-coset patterns, and nine rejected corruptions.
Root a-cycle lengths range from3 to228 among these finite controls.
All33532 retained reset words satisfy the explicit bound; the maximum
retained reset length is3799 (not an exact reset threshold claim).
Actual scoped command captures and immutable release/old-Lean hashes are
recorded separately; no old registry or release rerun is implied.

The first step and the bound p+c<=2M-3 need c>0 and p!=c. At c=0,
a b^c does not extend the three-point seed in this argument, and the
paid return can cease to exist. Previous work settles ALL c=0 orders
t>=3. Thus within this level-one tail/core-cycle model, the remaining
synchronizing square gap is precisely c=0, t=2, arbitrary pair-splitting A.
The new three-a barrier concerns that remaining case. Neither statement
is a reduction of the general conjecture.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-profile-barrier"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-profile-barrier--rank-length-inequalities-alone-still-permit-a-cubic-tail"></a>
### Rank-length inequalities alone still permit a cubic tail

**PROVED (abstract inequality system).** No DFA realizing the profiles below
is claimed. In particular these are NOT counterexamples to Cerny's conjecture.

The rank-length inequalities used here are exactly:

1. lambda_0=0, lambda_1=1, and nonnegative gaps delta_r=lambda_(r+1)-lambda_r.
2. Pin--Frankl: delta_r <= T_r=(r+1)(r+2)/2.
3. The kernel bridge: delta_r <= lambda_r+r+1.
4. The singleton-rich plateau splice: for 1<=r<n/2 and every t with
   delta_t>2r, delta_r <= lambda_t+2r. The terminal infinite gap can be included.

Take n=2m, lambda_r=1 for 1<=r<=m, and thereafter define

    delta_r=min{T_r,lambda_r+r+1},  m<=r<=n-2.

This satisfies all four sets of constraints. Constraints 2 and 3 hold by
construction. Every gap appearing on the left of constraint 4 is zero, so
that constraint holds for every eligible t, not merely the first one.

Yet lambda_(n-1)=(7/48)n^3-O(n^2 log n).

To see this, put t=m^2/2. For r>=m, T_r>=t. While lambda_r<t, its increment
is at least lambda_r, so it reaches t after O(log n) steps. Once it reaches
t, its increment is at least t until it exceeds 2m^2; three further steps
suffice. All remaining T_r are <=2m^2, so every remaining gap equals T_r.
The sum from r=m to n-2 of T_r is (7/48)n^3+O(n^2). Deleting the initial
O(log n) terms costs O(n^2 log n). The constructed profile is bounded above
by this same sum plus 1, giving the stated asymptotic equality.

Therefore a proof using only these rank-length inequalities cannot yield
a subcubic bound. It needs an additional constraint tying the lower-rank
tail to actual fibers, subset geometry, backward expansion, or another
invariant. The point is logical insufficiency of this particular relaxation,
not an impossibility theorem about all rank-profile methods.

Computational checks in abstract_profiles.json verify the stated finite
constraints through n=2000. The construction and asymptotic proof are
independent of those checks.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-three-color-stall-boundary"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-three-color-stall-boundary--a-six-state-rank-three-boundary-for-signed-components"></a>
### A six-state rank-three boundary for signed components

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. The finite counterexample below is
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** by an independent full-word enumerator.
It **REFUTES** the direct three-color analogue of the binary
signed-component stagnation lemma. It does not refute the sharp
linear-algebra first-drop bound in [Sharp linear bound for the first permutation-mediated rank drop](#direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop),
the universal `e(S)<=2n` target, or Cerny's square.

On `Q={0,1,2,3,4,5}`, use permutations and a rank-three letter

    a = [5,3,1,2,0,4]
    c = [2,0,3,5,4,1]
    b = [0,2,4,0,2,4].

The actual first image is `B=Qb={0,2,4}`. Color a state by its image
under `b`, giving three colors `0,2,4`. The two depth-one triples are

    Ba={0,1,5},   Bc={2,3,4}.

All three displayed triples are rainbow. As hyperedges they form one
connected component on **every** state, so the component counts for
the graphs generated through depths zero and one are `4,1`. Exact
enumeration of all four length-two permutation words gives only

    {0,1,2}, {3,4,5},

both rainbow. The graph therefore remains connected and collision-free
through depth two. But `B a a c={1,4,5}`, whose colors are `{2,2,4}`.
This first collision occurs at depth three, with component counts

    [4,1,1,1].

The state graph is strongly connected. Ordinary full-subset BFS gives
`rt=9` and a shortest word `b a a c b c c c b`. This exceeds `n+1`
but remains far below `(n-1)^2=25`. The reset threshold is included
only as a finite contextual fact; the refutation needs just the
rainbow hyperedge sequence above. A second independent seven-state
witness and its literal check are also retained.

`rank_three_color_cover.py` exhausts one first-permutation
representative per cycle type, every second permutation, and every
labeled rank-three row. The complete designated covers have:

| n | tested triples | finite first collisions | stagnant before later collision |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 17280 | 16212 | 0 |
| 5 | 1260000 | 1239264 | 0 |

Conjugation covers every ordered two-permutation/one-rank-three input
up to state relabeling for these `n`; the counts are overlapping cover
designations, not isomorphism classes. The six-state witness is thus
state-minimal **within that precise alphabet shape**. No minimum for
larger alphabets is asserted. The n4/n5 negative counts are exact
finite computation, whereas the counterexample is also directly
checkable from the displayed words. The separate random probes at
n7/n10 are samples and prove no absence statement.

The failure mode is structural: rainbow triples sharing just one
vertex can be transported with different permutations of their three
colors. Connectivity alone does not force a uniform color action on
the whole component. The incidence-vector span in
[Sharp linear bound for the first permutation-mediated rank drop](#direct-attack-permutation-rainbow-first-drop) tracks information retained after
components have stopped merging.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-multi-perm-search"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-multi-perm-search--two-permutations-and-a-rank-two-letter-designated-finite-pressure-tests"></a>
### Two permutations and a rank-two letter: designated finite pressure tests

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** at the exact designated
finite scope below. The unrestricted `e(S)<=2n` and existence of any
universal linear image-extension bound remain **OPEN**. These tests prove
no all-parameter upper bound and no state-minimality claim.

The binary rank-two period theorem leaves the case of more than one
permutation generator. To test whether extra permutation transport can
push a local actual-image extension beyond `2n`, fix

* `a` as disjoint cycles of lengths `p,q`;
* `c` as the transposition of state `0` with state `p`, joining the cycles;
* `b` as **every labeled rank-two transformation** on `n=p+q` states.

The two permutations generate a transitive action, so every input is
strongly connected. Only `b` reduces rank, hence every proper actual image
has cardinality at most two. For a pair target, the sparse scorer computes
the shortest `Q`-to-subset path; for a singleton it computes the shortest
path from any actual pair. These are exact `e` values because the only
larger actual image of a pair is `Q`, and any shortest inverse singleton
extension crosses rank two in its first step. It also computes exact rt.

| (p,q) | rank-two rows | synchronizing | largest e | rt of retained peak |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (4,5) | 18360 | 18360 | 14 | 10 |
| (3,7) | 45990 | 45990 | 15 | 8 |
| (4,6) | 45990 | 45940 | 13 | 10 |
| (5,5) | 45990 | 45830 | 11 | 3 |
| (4,7) | 112530 | 112530 | 18 | 12 |
| (5,6) | 112530 | 112530 | 18 | 11 |
| (5,7) | 270204 | 270204 | 18 | 12 |

Thus the largest retained value is 18 at n11 or n12; none exceeds `2n`.
This says nothing about other permutation pairs, additional generators,
or larger states. The row counts are exactly
`binom(n,2)(2^n-2)` for each designated pair.

`rank_two_multi_perm_search.py` generated the seven JSON files
`data/rank_two_multi_perm_p*_q*.json`. `check_rank_two_multi_perm.py`
independently checks every retained peak with the full `2^n` capacity
array and reverse Bellman BFS in `image_extension.profile`, rather than
the sparse forward scorer. Its seven exact witness records are saved in
`data/rank_two_multi_perm_independent_checks.json`. The independent check
does not re-enumerate every input, so the covering maxima rely on the
enumerator plus independent verification of the peaks.

Reproduction uses, for each listed `(p,q)`,

    python -m direct_attack.rank_two_multi_perm_search --p P --q Q --swap-i 0 --swap-j P --out scripts/direct_attack/data/rank_two_multi_perm_pP_qQ.json

followed by

    python -m direct_attack.check_rank_two_multi_perm --out scripts/direct_attack/data/rank_two_multi_perm_independent_checks.json

This experiment gives no globally compatible-chain argument. Because
every proper image here has rank at most two, the previously proved theorem

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations--linear-reset-and-image-extension-when-every-singular-letter-has-rank-two"></a>
### Linear reset and image extension when every singular letter has rank two

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. **PROVED on paper** for all `n>=3` and every finite
alphabet in the precise class below. No Lean or other **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim. Literature priority of this exact linear class bound is **OPEN**.
The unrestricted `e(S)<=2n`, global square-chain, and Cerny conjectures
remain **OPEN**.

Let `A=(Q,Pi union D)` be a synchronizing `n`-state DFA. Every letter in
`Pi` is a permutation; every letter in the nonempty set `D` has rank
**exactly two**. There may be arbitrarily many letters of either kind.
The state graph need not be strongly connected for the reset theorem.
Write `B_d=Qd`, a pair, for each `d in D`. Words act on the right.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations--rank-two-erasure-and-an-exact-two-letter-normal-form"></a>
#### Rank-two erasure and an exact two-letter normal form

The first singular letter of a reset word sends `Q` to its full pair
`B_i`. A later singular letter `d` acting on any pair either merges it
or sends it to its full pair `B_d`. In the latter case, delete the entire
prefix through that occurrence of `d` and start the remaining suffix
from `Qd=B_d`; this preserves the later image and strictly shortens the
word. Permutation letters before the first singular letter also leave
`Q` fixed and can be deleted. Hence **every shortest reset word** is

    d_i w d_j,

where `d_i,d_j in D` and `w` uses permutation letters only. The empty
`w` is allowed. Its final pair `U=B_i w` is an actual reachable image,
and `d_j` merges `U`.

For any ordered pair of singular letters `i,j`, color each state by its
image under `d_j` (two colors), and let `T_ij` be the minimum length of
a permutation word `w` for which both states of `B_i w` have the same
color; set `T_ij=infinity` if none exists. The preceding erasure proves

    A synchronizes iff min_(i,j) T_ij is finite,
    rt(A)=2+min_(i,j) T_ij.                             (1)

There is no assumption that `{a,d_i}` or `{a,d_j}` alone synchronizes.
The two singular letters can be different.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations--signed-component-bound-applies-to-every-ordered-pair"></a>
#### Signed-component bound applies to every ordered pair

The signed-component lemma and complete proof are in
[One rank-two letter and arbitrarily many permutation letters](#direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet). They depend only on an initial pair,
permutation generators, and a **binary coloring**; the initial pair need
not be the image of the same letter that defines the coloring. For
completeness, form `H_k` from the images of `B_i` under all permutation
words of length at most `k`. If `H_{k+1}` is still properly two-colored
by the fibers of `d_j` and its component partition has not changed from
`H_k`, then each generator maps each old component into one old component
and either preserves or flips its two colors. Every later image of
`B_i` therefore stays bichromatic. Thus, before a first monochromatic
edge, each depth strictly merges components. `H_0` has `n-1` components,
so a first collision, if it exists, has depth at most `n-1`.

Apply this to an attaining `(i,j)` in (1):

    rt(A) <= n+1.                                      (2)

More precisely, if `M_i` is the union of the permutation-state orbits
of the two states in `B_i`, then `T_ij<=|M_i|-1`, hence
`rt<=|M_i|+1`. The argument requires only that the permutation letters
are bijective, not that their group action is transitive.

The odd full-cycle family in [A rank-two letter and one permutation: periodic collision bound](#direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem) uses only one
rank-two letter and has `rt=n+1` for every odd `n>=3`, so (2) is sharp
even inside this larger class. The separate two-rank-two-letter cover
below includes examples where **neither** one-letter rank-two
subalphabet synchronizes but their union does.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations--full-transport-and-a-globally-compatible-chain"></a>
#### Full transport and a globally compatible chain

Now assume `A` is strongly connected. Every proper actual image is a
pair or singleton. Any reachable pair `S` receives a valid transport
from `Q`: use a reset word of length at most `n+1`, then a shortest
state path from its reset state into `S`. The path uses at most `n-2`
letters because all preterminal vertices are distinct and outside the
two-point target. Any singleton `{q}` has `e({q})<=n`: the final actual
pair of a shortest reset merges in one letter to some state `p`, and a
shortest state path from `p` to `q` has length at most `n-1`.
Therefore, for **every proper actual image**,

    e(S) <= 2n-1 < 2n.                                 (3)

All strict-subset singleton arrivals are included in this upper bound;
no ordinary preimage is assumed to be reachable without a word.

The shortest reset `d_i w d_j` also gives a concrete compatible
reachable-image chain paying its **complete** transport costs. Let
`U=B_i w`, `Ud_j={q}`, and `t=|w|`. Then `e({q})=1`, with `U` an allowed
parent. The only actual image larger than `U` is `Q`. Since
`Qd_i w=U`, `e(U)<=t+1`. A shorter transport of `Q` into any subset
of `U`, followed by `d_j`, would reset `Q` in fewer than `t+2` letters,
contradicting shortestness. Thus `e(U)=t+1`. The inverse phase chain

    {q} --d_j (cost 1)--> U --d_i w (cost t+1)--> Q

has total cost `t+2=rt<=n+1`. The general `P=rt` theorem for automata
without proper reachable rank-three images is already recorded in
[Image policy can become worse when letters or word shortcuts are added](#direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction); the argument here supplies an explicit
two-phase shortest chain and word direction for this narrower class.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-only-nonpermutations--exact-finite-audits-and-boundaries"></a>
#### Exact finite audits and boundaries

`rank_two_two_perm_cover.py` exhausts all labeled second permutations
and rank-two rows relative to each representative first-permutation
cycle type. It covers 10080, 252000, and 7365600 designated triples
at `n=4,5,6`; every accepted SC synchronizing input satisfies (2)--(3).
`check_rank_two_permutation_alphabet.py` independently recomputes the
retained peaks with pair-orbit component BFS and ordinary all-source
transport. The finite maxima and their scopes are in
[One rank-two letter and arbitrarily many permutation letters](#direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet) and the JSON files under `data/`.

`rank_two_joint_nonsync_cover.py` fixes one two-cycle permutation and
enumerates every unordered pair of rank-two rows **each of which is
nonsynchronizing with that permutation alone**:

| cycle profile | tested row pairs | SC synchronizing combined inputs | max rt | max e |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (4,4) | 294528 | 208384 | 5 | 8 |
| (4,5) | 152076 | 10240 | 2 | 6 |
| (5,5) | 319600 | 255000 | 5 | 5 |
| (5,6) | 733866 | 34560 | 2 | 6 |

`check_rank_two_only_nonperm.py` independently checks the eight retained
peaks by pair-orbit BFS, actual all-source image transport, and literal
two-phase reset words. This verifies that the multi-letter theorem does
real work beyond applying the one-rank-two-letter theorem to an already
synchronizing subalphabet. These are finite covering counts, not
arbitrary-n irreducibility or minimality results.

The proof needs every singular letter to have rank at most two. The
already proved one-fixed rank-three family has `rt=n+2`, so merely
allowing one rank-three letter invalidates (2). Its long local pair
extension and the compatibility problem for larger actual images are
outside this theorem. No unrestricted reset bound follows.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem--a-rank-two-letter-and-one-permutation-periodic-collision-bound"></a>
### A rank-two letter and one permutation: periodic collision bound

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. Baseline HEAD: `16561d3307bb9be11537edd7c5a1f201929e85ce`.
**PROVED on paper**, for the precisely stated binary class. The finite
enumeration below is **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. Priority of the exact
class statement is **OPEN**; no novelty or formal-verification claim is made.
The unrestricted `e(S) <= 2n` and Cerny conjectures remain **OPEN**.

Let `A=(Q,{a,b})` be a strongly connected synchronizing DFA with `n>=3`.
The letter `a` is an arbitrary permutation, and `b` has rank exactly two.
All words act on the right. Let `B=Qb={x,y}`. The actual image family has
only `Q`, pairs, and singletons. In particular, the already proved
rank-two-image theorem in [Image policy can become worse when letters or word shortcuts are added](#direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction) gives `P=rt`;
that equality is *reused*, not newly attributed here.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem--short-reset-from-two-periodic-color-sequences"></a>
#### Short reset from two periodic color sequences

Put `X_t=b(xa^t)` and `Y_t=b(ya^t)`. These take values in `B`. A word
starting from `Q` must first use `b`, and after any later nonmerging `b` its
image is again `B`. Removing everything before that later `b` makes a
strictly shorter reset word. Consequently every shortest reset has form
`b a^t b`, where `t` is the first nonnegative index with `X_t=Y_t`.

If `x,y` lie on the same `a`-cycle of length `p`, both sequences have period
`p`. Since an equality occurs, its first index is at most `p-1`, and
`rt<=p+1`. If their cycles have lengths `p,q`, the sequences have periods
`p,q`. Suppose `X_t!=Y_t` for `p+q-gcd(p,q)` consecutive indices starting
at zero. Complement `Y` within the two-element alphabet `B`. The resulting
`p`- and `q`-periodic sequences agree on that many consecutive values, so
the Fine--Wilf periodicity theorem forces agreement at every index. This
would preclude synchronization. Hence the first collision satisfies

    t <= p+q-gcd(p,q)-1,
    rt <= p+q-gcd(p,q)+1 <= n.

The last inequality uses disjoint cycles and `gcd(p,q)>=1`. In the same-
cycle case, `p<=n`, so universally `rt<=n+1`. This argument also gives a
linear-time synchronization criterion once the two cycles and their color
sequences are known: synchronization is equivalent to the existence of
one collision. The use of Fine--Wilf is its classical theorem, not a new
periodicity claim; see Fine--Wilf, *Uniqueness theorems for periodic
functions*, Proc. AMS 16 (1965), 109--114,
https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1965-0174934-9 .

The reset bound `n+1` is sharp for every odd `n=2m+1>=3`. Let
`a=(0 1 ... 2m)` and

    qb = 0  for q in {0,...,m-1,2m},
    qb = m  for q in {m,...,2m-1}.

Then `B={0,m}`. At `t=0,...,m-1`, the two colors differ; at
`t=m,...,2m-1` they differ in the opposite order; at `t=2m` both are zero.
Thus the first collision is `n-1`, giving `rt=n+1`. The full cycle makes
the automaton strongly connected.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem--actual-image-extension-bound"></a>
#### Actual image-extension bound

For any singleton image `{z}`, a one-letter merged actual pair exists;
from its merge state a shortest state path into `z` has at most `n-1`
edges. The general first-drop theorem therefore gives `e({z})<=n`.

For a pair image `S`, a reset word followed by a shortest state path into
`S` is a valid transport from the larger image `Q`. Such a path has at most
`n-2` edges: before reaching `S` it visits distinct states outside `S`.
If `a` is not a full `n`-cycle, the previous section gives `rt<=n`:
different cycles give this directly, while one proper cycle has `p<=n-1`.
Therefore `e(S)<=2n-2`.

If `a` is a full `n`-cycle, every reachable pair has form `B a^j`:
`a` rotates a pair, while a nonmerging `b` returns it to `B`. Thus
`Q b a^j` reaches any pair in at most `n` letters, giving `e(S)<=n`.
The two cases prove, for **every actual proper image**,

    max_S e(S) <= 2n-2.

This is a special-class universal bound. It does not transfer to arbitrary
automata containing an additional letter, since that letter can create new
reachable images; the repository also records that adding even a generated
word as a new letter can increase the shortest-phase policy. It gives no
new unrestricted quadratic reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem--finite-audit-and-local-obstruction"></a>
#### Finite audit and local obstruction

`rank_two_period_audit.py` enumerates one representative of **every**
permutation cycle type and every labeled rank-two row for `n=2,...,8`.
Conjugation makes this cover every binary pair of the stated types. It
computes ordinary subset-graph BFS from `Q`, all larger-image transport
costs, the first pair collision, and strong connectivity. It asserts the
paper bounds input by input. Its frozen JSON is
`data/rank_two_period_audit.json`. No existing capacity or policy kernel
is called by the enumerator. `check_rank_two_period.py` separately checks
all 18 retained finite peak examples with the full-powerset inverse
capacity solver, including the saved words; its result is frozen in
`data/rank_two_period_independent_checks.json`. The exact maxima among SC
synchronizing inputs are:

| n | SC synchronizing inputs in cover | max rt | max e |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 22 | 4 | 3 |
| 4 | 110 | 4 | 4 |
| 5 | 476 | 6 | 6 |
| 6 | 1758 | 6 | 6 |
| 7 | 5186 | 8 | 10 |
| 8 | 16698 | 8 | 11 |

The `n=2` rank-two letter is itself a permutation, so no synchronizing
input exists. Counts use one fixed representative per cycle type and all
rank-two rows relative to it; they are not isomorphism-class counts.

For example, at `n=7` the two-cycle rows

    a=[1,2,0,4,5,6,3], b=[0,0,3,3,3,0,3]

have `e({2,6})=10>n`, even though `rt=7`. The retained shortest transport
from `Q` is `b a^6 b a^2`, ending at singleton `{2}` inside `{2,6}`.
The independent all-larger-image BFS proves no shorter transport. This
shows that a short reset by itself does not force each local `e(S)<=n`.

The exact sparse scan of the explicit two-cycle continuation (three-cycle
plus a `q`-cycle, `q=4,...,40`) is saved separately in
`data/rank_two_two_cycle_family.json`. It is finite evidence only: its pair
costs stop at 12 while its singleton cost eventually grows linearly. No
all-parameter formula or improvement of the proved bound is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet--one-rank-two-letter-and-arbitrarily-many-permutation-letters"></a>
### One rank-two letter and arbitrarily many permutation letters

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. Baseline HEAD: `e8aca607eb850aff274cdf4303e845dcb557d24d`.
**PROVED on paper** for the stated class. Not Lean or otherwise
**FORMALLY VERIFIED**. Priority/novelty of the exact theorem is **OPEN**.
The unrestricted image-extension and Cerny problems remain **OPEN**.

Let `A=(Q,Pi union {b})`, `n=|Q|>=3`, where every letter of `Pi` is a
permutation and `b` has rank exactly two. No transitivity or strong
connectivity is required for the reset bound. Put `B=Qb={x,y}`. Every
word acts on the right. Let `c(q)` be the binary color of `q`, meaning
which of the two states in `B` is `qb`.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet--exact-pair-orbit-reset-normal-form"></a>
#### Exact pair-orbit reset normal form

After its first `b`, the image is `B`. Any later `b` either merges the
current pair or returns it to `B`. A shortest reset cannot contain an
earlier nonmerging `b`: deleting the entire prefix through that `b`
leaves `Qb=B` and the same remaining suffix. Permutation letters before
the first `b` are also useless because they leave `Q` fixed. Thus every
shortest reset is `b w b`, with `w` a word over `Pi`, possibly empty.

Let `T` be the minimum length of a permutation word `w` for which
`c(xw)=c(yw)`, or infinity if none exists. Then

    A synchronizes iff T<infinity; if so, rt(A)=T+2.       (1)

This exact criterion includes a non-strongly-connected automaton. It
does not say an arbitrary shortest *state* path is a valid pair path:
both states are transported by the same permutation word.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet--a-component-merger-bound-for-the-first-color-collision"></a>
#### A component-merger bound for the first color collision

For `k>=0`, build an undirected graph `H_k` on all `n` states with an
edge `{xw,yw}` for every permutation word `w` of length at most `k`.
Its edges are genuine two-point edges because permutations are injective.
The graphs are nested. Before depth `T`, every edge joins opposite colors.
The initial `H_0` has one edge and exactly `n-1` connected components.

**Signed-component lemma.** Suppose `H_{k+1}` has no monochromatic edge
and has the same connected-component partition as `H_k`. Then no
monochromatic pair is reachable at any later depth.

Proof. Fix a permutation generator `p` and a component `C` of `H_k`.
The image of every edge of `H_k` under `p` belongs to `H_{k+1}`. Hence
`p(C)` lies in one component of `H_{k+1}`, which by assumption is also a
component of `H_k`. Along every edge of `H_k`, both its original ends
and their `p`-images have opposite colors. Connectedness therefore gives
one bit `epsilon(C,p)` such that

    c(up) = c(u) xor epsilon(C,p)    for every u in C.

Thus `p` preserves the equality/inequality of the two colors on every
pair lying in `C`, and sends that pair into another component of `H_k`.
Starting with the endpoints of `B`, which lie in one component and have
opposite colors while `T>0`, induction over any later word preserves their
different colors. If `T=0`, the collision was already present. This
proves the lemma without assuming that a generator preserves each
component individually; it may map one whole component into another.

If `T` is finite, for each `k=0,...,T-2` the graph `H_{k+1}` is still
collision-free. The lemma forces its component partition to be strictly
coarser than that of `H_k`. There can be at most `n-2` such strict
decreases from the `n-1` components of `H_0`. Consequently

    T-1 <= n-2,   T <= n-1,   rt(A) <= n+1.             (2)

There is an orbit-sensitive version. Let `M` be the union of the state
orbits of `x` and `y` under the permutation generators, and put `m=|M|`.
Every pair edge stays inside `M`, and every generator maps `M` to itself.
Repeat the identical component argument on the graph restricted to `M`:
it starts with `m-1` components, so `T<=m-1` and `rt<=m+1`.

The odd full-cycle family in [A rank-two letter and one permutation: periodic collision bound](#direct-attack-rank-two-period-theorem) has `T=n-1` for
every odd `n>=3`, so the reset bound is sharp within this broader class.
That older proof used Fine--Wilf for one permutation; the signed-component
argument handles **arbitrarily many** permutation generators at once.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet--full-transport-and-actual-image-consequences"></a>
#### Full transport and actual-image consequences

Assume additionally that `A` is strongly connected and synchronizing.
All proper actual images are pairs or singletons. For a reachable pair
`S`, concatenate a reset word of length at most `n+1` with a shortest
state path from its endpoint into `S`. The path has length at most
`n-2`, since its preterminal states are distinct and outside `S`.
The source is the larger actual image `Q`, and strict-subset singleton
arrival is permitted. Thus

    e(S) <= n+m-1 <= 2n-1   for every reachable pair S.

For each reachable singleton `{q}`, the established first-drop theorem
gives `e({q})<=n`. Therefore **every proper actual image** satisfies

    e(S) <= 2n-1 < 2n.                              (3)

This is a universal linear image-extension bound for the precise class,
not for arbitrary synchronizing DFAs. Extra nonpermutation letters can
create intermediate images of rank at least three, to which this proof
does not apply.

There is also a concrete globally compatible **two-phase** inverse-image
chain paying its full transport cost. Let `w` attain `T`, let
`U=Bw` (an actual pair), and let `Ub={q}`. Since `U` is an actual merged
pair, `e({q})=1` and `U` is an eligible first parent. Since `Q` is the
only actual image larger than a pair, `Qbw=U` gives `e(U)<=T+1`.
If a shorter word transported `Q` into any subset of `U`, appending `b`
would reset `Q` in fewer than `T+2` letters, contradicting (1). Hence
`e(U)=T+1`, with `Q` as its parent. The chain

    {q} --b (cost 1)--> U --bw (cost T+1)--> Q

has total cost `T+2=rt<=n+1`. Word arrows here show inverse-phase
transport: in forward order the reset is `b w b`. The pre-existing
rank-two-image theorem already proves `P=rt` for arbitrary alphabets
without proper rank-three images; this paragraph makes the particular
chain and every paid word explicit. It is not a new general policy
equality.

<a id="direct-attack-rank-two-permutation-alphabet--finite-audit-and-exact-scope"></a>
#### Finite audit and exact scope

`rank_two_two_perm_cover.py` fixes one representative for every cycle
type of the first permutation, then exhausts every second permutation
and every labeled rank-two row relative to it. Conjugation covers every
ordered two-permutation/one-rank-two input up to state relabeling at each
listed `n`; the counts are covering counts, not isomorphism classes.

| n | tested | SC synchronizing | max rt | max e |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 10080 | 6868 | 4 | 5 |
| 5 | 252000 | 180976 | 6 | 7 |
| 6 | 7365600 | 5425424 | 6 | 9 |

All accepted cases satisfy (2)--(3) in the exact sparse forward image
solver. The n8 random labeled probe has 86630 SC synchronizing inputs
among 100000 proposals, but is not a cover. Earlier designated
cross-cycle-transposition covers through n12 are recorded separately in
[Two permutations and a rank-two letter: designated finite pressure tests](#direct-attack-rank-two-multi-perm-search). The arbitrary-n theorem rests on the
signed-component proof, not any finite enumeration. Independent inverse
capacity checks of the retained finite peaks are recorded in the audit.

<a id="direct-attack-reset-rank-profile-budget"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-reset-rank-profile-budget--reset-rank-trajectories-bound-every-shortest-image-seed-policy"></a>
### Reset rank trajectories bound every shortest-image seed policy

**PROVED on paper**, elementary deduction; priority OPEN. Let A be any
strongly connected synchronizing DFA with n>=2 and finite alphabet.
Let r=max{|T|:T a proper actual image}. For ANY existing reset word w
of length ell, write rho_t=|Q w[1:t]|, 0<=t<=ell, so rho_0=n and
rho_ell=1. For 1<=k<=r define

    t_k=max{t:rho_t>k},       L_k=ell-t_k.

The prefix image U_k=Q w[1:t_k] is actual and has size >k. The remaining
suffix of length L_k resets it to the same endpoint as w. In the state
graph, a shortest walk from that endpoint to any k-set S has length at
most n-k: before its first entry it visits distinct vertices outside S.
Concatenating these words transports U_k into S (in fact into a singleton
inside S). Thus for EVERY actual proper S of size k,

    e(S)<=L_k+n-k.

No condition on the prefix image containing S, exact arrival rank, or
the reset being shortest is imposed. The source size is strictly larger
than k. This is exactly the actual-image condition needed by e.

Every initial one-letter seed has extension cost 1. Each subsequent
extension phase strictly increases parent cardinality, so its target
ranks belong to {2,...,r} and each is visited at most once. Q is the
zero-cost endpoint. ALL seeds and ALL subsequent shortest-word/parent
ties consequently satisfy

    W({h})<=B(w)=1+sum_(k=2)^r(L_k+n-k).

If the initial merge source is Q, the remaining sum is empty and the
cost is one; bounding it by B(w) is valid. For r=1 the displayed sum
is empty and B=1, covering n2. The n1 case remains rt=P=0 separately.

<a id="direct-attack-reset-rank-profile-budget--the-rank-area-identity-and-counterexample-restriction"></a>
#### The rank-area identity and counterexample restriction

Cardinality never increases along a word. Therefore i>t_k precisely
when rho_i<=k, and double-counting yields

    area_r(w)=sum_(k=2)^r L_k
             =sum_(i=1)^ell max(0,r-max(2,rho_i)+1);
    B(w)=2+(r-1)n-r(r+1)/2+area_r(w).

Since L_k<=ell, this improves the previous reset-length budget rank by
rank, and can cover instances with ell>(n+1)/2. A failure of the global
policy square NECESSARILY satisfies, for EVERY reset word w,

    area_r(w)>(n-1)^2-[2+(r-1)n-r(r+1)/2].

For r=n-1 this is area_r(w)>(n-2)(n+1)/2. An actual SC Cerny counterexample
must obey the same condition since rt<=P. The reverse implication for rt
is not claimed. Short rank tails can exclude a policy counterexample
even when the total reset length exceeds the previous sufficient regime.

These are bounds given a reset witness and its trajectory, not an
n-only upper bound or an efficient general procedure for obtaining a
short reset. A long plateau contributes differently depending on its
rank; it is the summed area, not total length alone, that enters this
deduction. Neither a quadratic nor a subcubic general reset bound follows.

<a id="direct-attack-reset-rank-profile-budget--adversarial-verification"></a>
#### Adversarial verification

check_first_drop independently constructs the ordinary actual-image graph
and ALL-SOURCE distances on its full finite corpus. It reconstructs a
shortest reset path on the BFS-level DAG, favoring a small area, then
directly verifies the word, every prefix rank, both expressions for the
area, EVERY local e inequality, and EVERY one-letter seed's worst tail.
The saved extra witnesses have rt>(n+1)/2 but B(w)<=(n-1)^2; their actual
words, ranks and bounds are retained in data/rank_profile_budget_cases.json.
No exhaustive priority or Lean verification is claimed.

The initial rank-profile checkpoint tested 8276 inputs (3658 accepted). All 43774 proper
image bounds and 5760 seed budgets pass. The trajectory refinement lowers
the previous rank-sum bound in 1000 accepted cases; it certifies the
square in 330 cases where that previous rank-sum bound exceeds the square,
and in 428 cases outside the simpler ell<=(n+1)/2 regime. Those two
comparisons are kept separate. In total 2711 accepted cases meet the new
sufficient condition. These are finite overlapping input counts.

For example n4, a=[0,0,0,3], d=[1,3,2,2], has shortest reset ddd and
rank trajectory (4,3,2,1). Here r=3, L_2=2,L_3=3, area=5, B=9;
the previous rank-dependent length bound was 10. The example is SC but
not irreducibly synchronizing, and is not presented as a minimal
counterexample rigidity witness.

The later [Optimizing every reset trajectory still leaves a cubic rank budget](#direct-attack-circular-rank-area-barrier) proves that on every C_n,n>=3,
NO choice of reset word can make this budget meet the square. Optimizing
over arbitrary words gives cubic leading growth. Therefore this valid
conditional bound cannot by itself become a universal square proof.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--rooted-period-rank-payment-in-the-original-order-two-model"></a>
### Rooted period-rank payment in the original order-two model

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper, ALL-n subclass bounds.** This closes further
infinite square cases and gives an unconditional17/16 quadratic bound
for the remaining model. It does NOT reduce arbitrary automata to this
model. General Cerny and the complete order-two SQUARE remain OPEN.
No new FORMALLY VERIFIED statement or priority claim is made.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--model-rank-parameter-and-theorem"></a>
#### Model, rank parameter and theorem

M=2L>=6, Q=Z_M union {r}; b is the ORIGINAL core cycle fixing r.
The ORIGINAL a has a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r; its restriction A to
R=Z_M minus {0,L} is an arbitrary permutation. Assume it mixes an
opposite pair; equivalently

    d=gcd(L,A(j)-A(j+L) for1<=j<L) < L.

Give core states weight1 and r weight2. For a nonconstant Boolean
d-pattern of weight c, let p be its least period and D the rational
rank of the p cyclic shifts of its p-pattern. Define

    e(pattern)=max(0,p-D-1),
    e_d(c)=max of e over ALL weight-c Boolean d-patterns,
    E_d=sum_(c=1)^(d-1) e_d(c).

**PROVED paper:** ONE compatible ORIGINAL reset word satisfies

    rt <= M^2 + E_d - (L-d).

In particular square holds whenever E_d<=L-d. Universally

    E_d <= (d-1)max(0,d-3),    d<=L/2,
    rt <= (17/16) M^2.

These are bounds for THIS rank-one/root-two-cycle/core-cycle model,
with every a and b charged. The17/16 statement is unconditional for
all mixed inputs in the model; it does not assert the Cerny square.
The crude square condition for d>=3 is L>=d^2-3d+3.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--every-chosen-extension-retains-the-root-and-grows-by-one"></a>
#### Every chosen extension retains the root and grows by ONE

With nu=(1,...,1,2) and delta=e0-eL, exact counting gives

    nu a=nu+delta, nu b=nu, delta a=0,
    nu a^k=nu+delta for all k>=1.

For S containing r, weighted and ordinary growth agree whenever its
inverse target also contains r. The following actual words ensure both
root retention and ONE additional core state.

If core U=S intersect Z_M is not whole under the opposite-pair shift,
choose j in U with j+L outside U. The word a b^j has weighted gain1,
and sends r to the selected state j. If |U| is even, there are at least
TWO split pairs, hence the least positive j<=M-2 and cost<=M-1.

For whole U not periodic mod d, translated edges from a b^j a b^s
(1<=j<L,0<=s<L) give positive gain. In fact cost<=M-1, not just M.
To see the saving, the undirected output graph on pair labels1,...,L-1
has degree2: input pair j is the edge joining the two output pair
labels A(j),A(j+L). A nonconstant coloring on a cycle cannot cross
exactly one edge. Thus at least two j have a nonzero translated
membership difference. Each nonzero difference has a positive translate
by cyclic summation, so some positive j<=L-2 exists. Its word costs
j+s+2<=M-1. Its root image A(j)+s lies in U.

The initial root alone has the earlier endpoint word
a b^j a b^k a of cost<=M, root-fixed, with inverse exactly root+ONE
core state. At least two pairs are mixed, so j<=L-2; take
k=(-A(j)) mod L. The next one-a word from that singleton core gives
root+{0,L}. These are genuine original words, not zero-cost seeds.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--periodic-extension-lemma-with-its-exact-cost"></a>
#### Periodic extension lemma with its exact cost

Let U be a nonconstant period-d pattern, of least period p|d. Since
d<L, all p residue classes occur in R. Its p translated characteristic
columns, restricted to R, span a space X of the same dimension D as
the p-state Boolean circulant. D>=2 and X includes the constant column.

Set K=L-D. Consider EVERY original word

    a b^j a^k b^s,     1<=j<L, 1<=k<=K, 0<=s<p.

Its mass difference on S is
chi_U(A^k(j)+s)-chi_U(A^k(j+L)+s). If positive, the difference is1,
the root maps to its positive endpoint, and the word costs at most

    (L-1)+(L-D)+(p-1)+1 = M+p-D-1.

Suppose none is positive. For each fixed j,k, summing over all p shifts
gives0. All those differences therefore are0. Let W_i be the rational
row span of (e_j-e_(j+L)) A^t for1<=j<L,0<=t<=i, on R.
W_0 has dimension L-1, and W_K annihilates X, whose annihilator has
dimension2L-2-D. If all K successive inclusions were strict, then

    dim W_K >= (L-1)+K = 2L-D-1 > 2L-2-D,

a contradiction. Some W_i=W_(i+1) occurs. Since
W_(i+1)=W_i+W_i A, it is A-invariant; A is a permutation, so it is
also A^-1-invariant. It follows that every inverse opposite pair
A^-1(j),A^-1(j+L) has equal membership in ALL p shifts of U. Least
period p then forces equal residues mod p for these two states.

Now use the degree2 graph of inverse output pairs on input pair labels.
Every edge has endpoints in the same residue class mod p. A mixed
component is a nonloop cycle, with at least two MIXED INPUT vertices
in the same residue class. One of them has j<=L-p-1. Take
k=(-A(j)) mod L. The original a b^j a b^k a fixes r; the other
opposite endpoint after the final a is a core state. A shift s<p
can make that core endpoint absent from U. The middle defect
delta b^k a b^s is0 because p|d. Thus this word has weighted/ordinary
gain1, retains the root, and costs

    j+k+s+3 <= (L-p-1)+(L-1)+(p-1)+3 = M.

Combining the alternatives proves a root-retaining ONE-core extension
of cost<=M+max(0,p-D-1). The dimension proof is on the actual
permutation of R; no averaged quotient or derived-letter unit cost
is used. This lemma remains valid when the earlier residual graph fails.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--one-chronological-chain-pays-the-periodic-surcharges"></a>
#### ONE chronological chain pays the periodic surcharges

Start at {r} and prepend each chosen word. Each inverse set retains r
and has one more core state; hence the core levels are EXACTLY
0,1,...,M. There are M charged stages, producing ONE reset to r.

Among the L-1 positive even core levels2,4,...,M-2, a period-d core
set is possible only at levels (M/d)c for1<=c<d. There are only d-1
such exceptional levels. Every other even level saves at least ONE
letter, by the nonwhole or degree2 translated-edge argument. Therefore
at least L-d savings occur on THIS SAME chain.

At exceptional level (M/d)c, the periodic surcharge is at most e_d(c).
The level occurs once; root retention is why a second root-absent
copy of the surcharge is NOT counted. Total surcharge is at most E_d.
Summing all actual stage lengths gives M^2+E_d-(L-d), as claimed.

Since D>=2, e_d(c)<=max(0,d-3), giving the crude E bound. A proper
divisor d of L satisfies d<=L/2=M/4; consequently E_d<=d^2<=M^2/16.
This proves the unconditional17/16 bound without any finite rank table.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--further-square-classes"></a>
#### Further square classes

If d is prime, each nonconstant d-pattern has shift rank d: its Boolean
polynomial cannot be a multiple of1+x+...+x^(d-1). Irreducibility follows
by applying Eisenstein to that polynomial at x+1. Thus E_d=0.
For d4, least-period4 patterns have both primitive fourth-root modes
and the constant mode, so D>=3 and again E4=0.

Exact small-period factor analysis gives

    E6=1, E8=4, E9=2, E10=3.

For p6 the only positive surcharge has three selected residues and
cost parameter1. For p8, weight2/6 has parameter at most1 and weight4
at most2. For p9 only weight3/6 can have parameter1. For p10 only
weight5 can have parameter3. Lower periods do not increase these maxima.
Integer cyclotomic divisions and independent RATIONAL circulant
elimination certify EVERY Boolean pattern through d12, including these
cases. All d<=11 have E_d<=d, and L-d>=d because d is a proper divisor.
Hence every such input satisfies square at ALL n.

In particular square is PROVED for ALL mixed inputs whenever L is prime,
a product of two primes (possibly equal), or L<=23. The last statement
is only about this original model, not all automata below n49.
Further infinite square cases follow from the E condition or crude bound.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-period-rank-payment--validation-failed-shortcuts-and-remaining-gap"></a>
#### Validation, failed shortcuts and remaining gap

Independent controls:8166 COMPLETE Boolean rank patterns through d12;
746 rooted chains including COMPLETE672 mixed M8;10488 original unit
stages;4496 checked saved stages;69447261 full-reset forward particles,
through n257. Five corrupted rank/chain certificates are rejected.
The chains happen to encounter no positive surcharge parameter; this
is NOT evidence that the surcharge never occurs.

A separate six-model COMPLETE periodic-pattern audit checks10036 targets
and20072 original extension words,40955518 forward particles. Of the
cost-saturation words,1688 exceed M and still satisfy the exact M+e bound.
These deliberately long valid witnesses test the payment parameter;
they do NOT establish necessity, shortest length, or a composable chain
of those separate target controls. Four corruptions are rejected.
The all-n compatible-chain proof is the argument above, not separate
row-wise minima or these saturation controls.

The literal period12 pattern on residues{0,1,5,6,9} has weight5 and
rational shift rank8. Therefore the guessed bound
D>=p-gcd(p,weight)+1 is REFUTED; coprime weight does not imply full rank.
The complete exact table has E12=28. At L24,d12, the global guarantee
is M^2+16, and at L36,d12 it is M^2+4. These are failures of this
budget proof, NOT Cerny counterexamples. At L>=48,d12 the same verified
finite rank table supplies a square bound.

General WEXT/RP remain OPEN. To complete the model square, one must
reduce the reachable periodic surcharges, secure more savings, or find
a different compatible policy in the large-composite-d/small-L/d gap.
Even that would leave the general automaton reduction unresolved.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square--residue-congruence-closes-the-original-order-two-square-model"></a>
### Residue congruence closes the original order-two square model

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper, ALL-n model theorem.** Every mixed input in
the original c0,t2 model has ONE reset word of length at most
M^2-(L-d) < M^2. The model's WEXT and RP are now PROVED paper.
General Cerny remains OPEN; no arbitrary-automaton reduction is asserted.
The theorem is not FORMALLY VERIFIED. No priority claim is made.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square--exact-model-and-theorem"></a>
#### Exact model and theorem

M=2L>=6; Q=Z_M union {r}. The ORIGINAL b cycles the core and fixes r.
The ORIGINAL a satisfies a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r, and restricts to an
arbitrary permutation A on R=Z_M minus {0,L}. Set

    d=gcd(L,A(j)-A(j+L), 1<=j<L).

Assume d<L, equivalently at least one opposite input pair is mixed by A.
The opposite-pair quotient proves nonsynchronization if d=L; the
construction below proves synchronization if d<L. Since d is a proper
divisor of L, d<=L/2. Every a and b occurrence is charged.

Give each core state weight1 and r weight2, with row vector nu. Then

    nu a=nu+delta, nu b=nu, delta=e0-eL, delta a=0,
    nu a^k=nu+delta for k>=1.

**Theorem (PROVED paper).** Every proper nonempty target has a positive
nu-extension of ORIGINAL length<=M (WEXT). If it contains r, the
extension can retain r and add exactly ONE core state. Consequently

    rt <= M^2-(L-d) < (n-1)^2.

This is a theorem about this specified model. Root-absent ordinary
cardinality growth is not claimed; weighted growth can introduce r.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square--the-essential-improvement-two-point-rows-distinguish-residues"></a>
#### The essential improvement: two-point rows distinguish residues

Let U be a nonconstant period-d core set, and let p|d be its least
period. Thus 2<=p<=d<=L/2. Consider the ACTUAL words

    a b^j a^k b^s,  1<=j<L, 1<=k<=L-p, 0<=s<p.

For S with core part U and either root flag, their nu-gain is exactly

    chi_U(A^k(j)+s)-chi_U(A^k(j+L)+s).

Indeed delta b^s evaluates to0 on U because p|L. If any gain is
positive, it is1 and the root image is the positive core endpoint.
The word therefore retains the root when S contains it. Every word
in this pool has cost at most

    (L-1)+(L-p)+(p-1)+1 = M-1.

Suppose no word in the pool has positive gain. For each fixed j,k,
the sum over all p shifts s is0, so EVERY gain is0. Equality of the
two membership rows in ALL p shifts forces

    A^k(j) == A^k(j+L) mod p.

Otherwise their nonzero residue difference would be a period of U;
Euclid's algorithm would give a positive proper divisor period of p,
contradicting least period. This uses that each row is a difference of
TWO STATES. It does not infer full circulant rank for a Boolean pattern.
The earlier period12 rank8 counterexample remains valid but irrelevant.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square--partition-stabilization-and-the-short-root-return"></a>
#### Partition stabilization and the short root return

For i>=0 build an undirected graph G_i on the 2L-2 states of R with
edges {A^t(j),A^t(j+L)}, 1<=j<L, 0<=t<=i. Its initial graph G_0 is
a matching with L-1 connected components. In the no-positive case,
all G_i through i=K=L-p have their components within residue classes
mod p. ALL p residue classes occur in R, so each has at least p
components. If every transition G_i -> G_(i+1) merged components,
G_K would have at most (L-1)-K=p-1 components, a contradiction.

Thus some i<K has exactly the same component partition in G_i and
G_(i+1). Applying A to any G_i edge yields a G_(i+1) edge, so A
preserves that partition. A is a finite permutation; its inverse is
a positive power of A and preserves the partition too. Hence

    A^-1(j) == A^-1(j+L) mod p,  1<=j<L.

This use of a permutation power proves a relation; it is not an
uncharged transition word in the reset construction.

Now form the inverse-output-pair multigraph on input pair labels
1,...,L-1. Each output pair {j,j+L} gives an edge between the labels
of A^-1(j),A^-1(j+L). Every vertex has degree2 and each edge joins
labels in the SAME residue class mod p. A mixed input vertex cannot
be a loop vertex, so mixing produces a nonloop cycle with at least
TWO mixed vertices of the same residue. Their indices differ by at
least p. Some mixed j therefore satisfies

    j <= L-p-1.

For a target CONTAINING r, take k=(-A(j)) mod L. Then
a b^j a b^k a fixes r, while its other defect endpoint after the final
a is a core state z. Pick s<p with z+s outside U; nonconstancy ensures
such s. The word's total nu-defect, evaluated on S, is1: its first
defect becomes e_r-e_z, while delta b^s and delta b^k a b^s evaluate
to0 because p|d. It retains r and adds one core state. Its cost is

    j+k+s+3 <= (L-p-1)+(L-1)+(p-1)+3 = M.

For a target EXCLUDING r, use k=(-A(j+L)) mod L and choose z+s IN U.
The surviving defect is e_z-e_r, again positive1 at cost<=M. The
inverse contains r. This proves the periodic WEXT cases with BOTH
root flags, and the root-retaining case needed for a compatible reset.
