<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square--other-targets-and-one-compatible-chronological-reset"></a>
#### Other targets and ONE compatible chronological reset

For a nonwhole core set U, choose j in U with j+L absent. The word
a b^j costs<=M, has nu-gain1 and sends r to its positive core endpoint.
If |U| is even, there are at least TWO split opposite pairs; some such
j<=M-2, so cost<=M-1.

If U is whole but not period-d, some translated output pair crosses it;
a b^j a b^s has positive gain1. The undirected output-pair graph has
degree2, so a coloring cannot cross just one edge. At least two input
indices admit a nonzero difference, each with a positive translate by
cyclic summation. Some positive j<=L-2, s<L gives cost<=M-1. Again
r goes to the selected core endpoint.

For S={r}, at least two mixed pairs exist and the least mixed j<=L-2.
The endpoint word a b^j a b^k a, k=(-A(j)) mod L, fixes r and has
nu-gain1 at cost<=M. Its inverse is r+ONE core state. For S=C, the
opposite orientation k=(-A(j+L)) mod L has nu-gain1 at cost<=M.
These cover the constant core patterns; the empty/full targets are
excluded from WEXT.

Start at {r}; prepend the chosen root-retaining words. Each stage
retains r and adds ONE core state. EXACTLY M stages give ONE original
word resetting Q to r, with cost at most M^2. The positive even core
levels2,4,...,M-2 number L-1. A period-d set can occur only at levels
(M/d)c for 1<=c<d, leaving at least L-d even levels where the one-a
or two-a saving applies. These savings occur on the SAME chain,
giving M^2-(L-d). No unrelated row minima are added.

<a id="direct-attack-rooted-residue-congruence-square--independent-validation-and-precise-boundary"></a>
#### Independent validation and precise boundary

The separate generator and checker exercise846 rooted reset chains,
including COMPLETE672 mixed M8 and explicit inputs through n257.
Ten models have COMPLETE29016 proper period-d targets with BOTH
root flags. Invariant residue models ensure the stabilization/root
fallback is actually exercised; the old graph-automaticity counter
and the former d12,L24/L36 payment gaps are included.

The checker executes original transitions for every extension and
EVERY complete reset, verifies weighted/root/cardinality budgets,
reconstructs the least period independently, and checks graph
stabilization and inverse residue equality in each fallback period.
Six deliberate corruptions must be rejected. Exact counts and captures
are in the scoped audit; these finite checks are COMPUTATIONALLY
VERIFIED, not a substitute for the all-n proof above.

The previous17/16 and period-rank payment bounds remain valid but are
superseded for this model. Their OPEN labels for complete model square
and WEXT are historical. The automaticity of the OLD triangular graph
remains REFUTED: the new pool includes actual a powers beyond that
triangular restriction. The original three-a pool barriers also remain
valid and are bypassed by these charged multi-a words.

General Cerny is OPEN. The next unresolved mathematical issue is a
general reduction or a broader rank-one/root-cycle theorem; it cannot
be inferred merely from this model square or its synchronization test.

<a id="direct-attack-short-rooted-word-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-short-rooted-word-obstruction--short-rooted-words-and-a-single-letter-power-template-can-fail"></a>
### Short rooted words and a single-letter power template can fail

Date: 2026-10-01. The proposed short-rooted-word lemma is **REFUTED**
by an exact finite certificate, **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** with a
separate literal evaluator. No minimum-state, priority, or
**FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim is made. Cerny's conjecture remains **OPEN**.

A transformation is called rooted here if some positive power is
constant. Equivalently its functional graph has exactly one directed
cycle, a fixed point; its height is the largest distance into that root.
This definition does not allow a unique nontrivial cycle to count as
rooted. If a rooted actual word v has height H on Q, v^H resets it,
with ORIGINAL cost H|v|. An entering prefix can reduce the relevant
height, but that prefix must also be paid.

After the reflected-return construction, a tempting generalization was:
every SC synchronizing n-state DFA has a rooted word of length <=n.
This would at least give a universal quadratic reset bound by taking
a power. It is false, even for a binary four-state automaton:

    a=[0,0,1,3],       b=[3,1,3,2].

All 31 literal binary words through length four, INCLUDING the empty
word, give 22 different transformations. None is rooted. The word

    v=a a b a b

has length five and row `[2,2,2,1]`. It is rooted at state 2 with
height exactly two: v itself has rank two, while v^2 is constant.
Thus the exact shortest rooted-word length is five, greater than n.
The enumeration through four is complete, not a truncated semigroup
search, and the positive five-letter witness proves attainability.

The whole DFA is strongly connected and synchronizing. Its actual
reset word

    a a b a b a a

has length seven; ordinary full-image BFS verifies rt=7, below the
square nine. The shortest rooted word's pure power costs ten, whereas
a shorter compatible varying suffix resets. Neither the Cerny square
nor a prefix-plus-rooted-word budget is refuted by this example.

It also refutes a more direct proposed square construction: choose ONE
letter x and an actual word v of length <=n so that x v^(n-2) resets.
Such a certificate would have cost at most 1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2. On this
four-state DFA, none of the 62 choices (two prefix letters times all
31 words through length four) makes x v^2 constant. This test permits
EVERY v, including transformations with nontrivial cycles; it does not
merely reject v for failing the rooted definition. Thus even that
single-prefix repeated-word template cannot replace a general compatible
schedule. Longer prefixes, longer repeated words, and different suffixes
are outside the refutation. The displayed seven-letter reset remains valid.

The lesson is precise: semigroup synchronization guarantees the
existence of rooted transformations (a reset word already supplies
one), but does not put a rooted word within original length n. A
general proof must control BOTH actual word cost and the height on the
entered image, or use a different compatible sequence. The public
family proof in [A charged reset construction for the published compress-with-another family](#direct-attack-published-compress-other-family) supplies those
quantities for its explicitly realized return structure only.

check_short_rooted_word.py imports none of the preceding generators or
solvers. It retains every short action, tests rootedness by literal
fourth powers, checks both positive words, recomputes rt/SC, and rejects
five deliberately corrupted fields. The complete certificate is in
data/short_rooted_word_checks.json.

<a id="direct-attack-short-root-return-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-short-root-return-square--a-short-root-return-criterion-without-a-two-cycle-assumption"></a>
### A short root-return criterion without a two-cycle assumption

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), ALL M>=5 under the explicit original
letter condition, with a strict quadratic bound at M>=6.** Finite checks COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED separately.
No novelty or FORMALLY VERIFIED claim. General Cerny **OPEN**.

Let Q={r} union Z_M, n=M+1. Original b cycles the core and fixes r.
Original a has omitted output L in1..M-1, doubled output r, a(r)=0,
and a(L)=a(c)=r for a second kernel input c!=L in the core. On the
remaining core inputs it is an arbitrary bijection to C\{0,L}.
In particular c need not be0: the root a-cycle can have any length.

Assume there is an ORIGINAL cyclic exponent J with

    J in {L,c},       1<=J<M/2,       a(L+J) != r,

where core sums are modulo M. Then there is ONE ORIGINAL reset word
of length <=M^2-M+5 for odd M, and <=M^2-M+4 for even M.
These are <=M^2=(n-1)^2 at M>=5, and strictly below it at M>=6.
No condition on gcd(M,L), permutation of cosets,
remaining cycle structure, or singular count is imposed.
Any larger alphabet containing these two ORIGINAL letters inherits the
bound by using the same word; no condition is imposed on its other letters.
For a positive c<M/2, J=c always satisfies the last condition.
Alternatively J=L works when L<M/2 and c!=2L modulo M.

Put g=gcd(M,L), t=M/g>=2, z=a(L+J), and f=a b^J a, of actual costJ+2.
The word fixes r, and its FULL multiplicity defect is

    D(f)=e_r+e_0-e_L-e_z.

Here z is a core point distinct from0,L. If H is the kernel input
other than J, the unique p with a(p)=H-J exists: H-J is neither0 nor
the omitted L. The latter exclusion follows from a(L+J)!=r.
The exact root preimage is {r}f^-1={r,p}, with p!=L,c (but p may be0).

For every proper S={r} union U a ROOT-PRESERVING extension costs<=M.
If U is not a union of g-cosets, choose j in U with L+j outside U.
The ORIGINAL a b^j grows S by ONE and retains r, in cost<=M=n-1.
If U is a whole-coset pattern, choose s<g with z+s outside U. Then
f b^s has growth 1-chi_U(z+s)=1 and retains r. Its cost<=J+g+1<=M,
because J<M/2 and g<=M/2 give the INTEGER bound J+g<=M-1.
Every extension grows by EXACTLY ONE, and saves a letter versus n.

The paid root-present sizeTHREE seed is chosen as follows.

* If p<=M-J-1, a b^p f has exact preimage {r,c,L}, cost<=M+2=n+1.
* If p>=M-J and p!=z, f f grows {r,p} by ONE, at cost2J+4.
* If p>=M-J and p=z, use f b^q f, where q=1 unless p=L+1,
  in which case q=2. Its growth on {r,p} is exactly ONE, and its
  cost is2J+q+4<=2J+6. Since M>=5 and p>M/2, p>1; when q2 is
  needed, p>2 also. These bounds avoid the possible e0 boundary term.

Starting from any such sizeTHREE seed, the successive root core sizes
are EXACTLY2,3,...,M-1, so there are M-2 extensions of cost<=M.
For even M, J<M/2 gives M-2J>=2, and every seed costs<=M+4.
For odd M the seed costs<=M+5. The first branch costs<=M+2.
Thus the SAME compatible word costs at most

    (M+4)+M(M-2)=M^2-M+4       (M even),
    (M+5)+M(M-2)=M^2-M+5       (M odd).

The initial derivation counted only the guaranteed noncoset stages,
M-g-1 of them. Checking the WHOLE-coset word cost strengthens the
result: those stages save a letter too. This improvement is part of
the final proof, not a numerical threshold conjecture.

This proves synchronization directly and does not assume it separately.
The global saving replaces the earlier demand for a single immediately
cheap next step. No root-preserving return is treated as a free letter.
The restricted M>=5 statement avoids unchecked small seed coincidences.

The order-two moving-root model c0,L=M/2 has no J satisfying the strict
shortness condition, so its arbitrary pair-splitting case is NOT solved
by this criterion. Nor is there a universal reduction from arbitrary
automata to this normal form. Its complete native root-extension/seed
pressure through M12 remains EXPLORATORY without an independent
coverage audit. A root-present sizeTHREE seed cost<=n+1 is REFUTED by
the separately retained n7 and n9 complete subset certificates; a
sizeFOUR seed cost<=2n+1 and root-preserving n-extension for the entire
order-two model remain CONJECTURED/OPEN at arbitrary n.

Two precise sufficient targets for the outstanding c0,L=M/2 SYNC model
are: (RP) every proper root-present whole-core pattern has an actual
root-retaining positive extension of cost<=n; (SEED) {r} has an actual
root-present preimage of size>=3 in cost<=n+3. Together they imply the
square for this model. If any subsequent stage grows by at leastTWO,
at most n-4 stages suffice and save an entire n-budget, paying the TWO
extra seed letters. If every stage growsONE and the seed has sizeTHREE,
its successive core sizes are2..M-1; at least L-1>=2 are nonwhole and
have the already proved original a b^j extension of cost<=n-1.
These savings again pay the TWO extra seed letters. A larger seed only
improves the budget. SYNC inputs here start at L>=3; L1/2 are nonsync.
This is a PROVED CONDITIONAL implication, not a proof of(RP)/(SEED).

Independent4542 inputs include ALL3006 eligible c-positive normal forms
M5..7. The separate checker replays15997240 literal particles/48838
root-preserving stages,3840 complete Bellman edges and ten corruptions.
It checks the exact multiplicity row, seed, root cycle, ONE compatible
reset, strict cost bound and total paid savings. These finite controls do
not formally quantify the arbitrary-M theorem. The earlier Lean Kari
and abstract Reflection certificates retain their distinct formal scope.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--exact-policy-for-one-permutation-and-unitary-letters"></a>
### Exact policy for one permutation and unitary letters

Status: **PROVED (paper proof)**, with independent finite model checking below.
No new general reset upper bound, no Lean verification, novelty **OPEN**.

Let A be a strongly connected synchronizing complete DFA with n>=2 states.
Its alphabet consists of ONE permutation a (arbitrary cycle structure) and
any finite nonempty collection of unitary letters u=(s->t), s!=t, fixing
every other state. Duplicate letters are immaterial. Composition is on
the right: S(xy)=(Sx)y. Inverse actions are taken in the opposite order.
Identity a is allowed. Pure unitary alphabets are covered by adjoining an
identity letter, which never occurs in any shortest reaching/extension word.

Write R={Qw:w in Sigma*}. For nonempty S in R, let
e(S)=min{|v|:Tv subset S, T in R, |T|>|S|}. All eligible larger T at this
minimum participate in G(S)=e(S)+min G(T) and W(S)=e(S)+max W(T), with
G(Q)=W(Q)=0. Let d(Q,S) be the shortest word reaching S EXACTLY.

**Theorem.** R contains every nonempty subset, and

    G(S)=W(S)=d(Q,S) for EVERY nonempty S subset Q.

In particular P=min_q G({q})=rt(A). Every shortest-extension parent choice
is optimal for its fixed target S. This is not a claim that all endpoint
states have the same reset length, nor that max_q W({q}) equals rt(A).

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--1-complete-reachability-proved-without-assuming-arbitrary-predecessors"></a>
#### 1. Complete reachability, proved without assuming arbitrary predecessors

Let o be the order of a. Form the directed graph Gamma whose edges are
all conjugates of the unitary edges by a^t, 0<=t<o. The word
a^t u a^(o-t) is a unitary map with the corresponding conjugated edge.
Thus a acts as an automorphism of Gamma. Let Z be the union of terminal
strongly connected components of Gamma. This nonempty set is closed
under a and all units. Strong connectivity of A forces Z=Q. Consequently
EVERY Gamma component is terminal and no Gamma edge joins components.

Each unit preserves every component, while a permutes them. If Gamma
had two or more components, states in different components would remain
in different components under every word, contradicting synchronization.
Gamma is therefore strongly connected.

For any desired nonempty S, measure the shortest Gamma distance to S.
For each q outside S choose an edge q->p decreasing that distance by one.
Apply the corresponding conjugated units in decreasing distance order.
They fix all roots in S and move every other state to some root. This
gives an actual word taking Q onto S. No short-length estimate is used.
This argument also establishes the known PU complete-reachability fact;
the same argument works with a finite permutation group in place of <a>.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--2-shortest-inverse-trajectories-and-proper-reaching"></a>
#### 2. Shortest inverse trajectories and proper reaching

Put D(S)=min{|w|:Qw subset S}. This is finite. Consider a shortest inverse
trajectory from S to Q. For a unit u=(s->t), its inverse either adds s
(t in S,s notin S), deletes s (s in S,t notin S), or fixes S.
If an occurrence fixes or deletes, omit it. Every preimage map is
inclusion-monotone, so the resulting trajectory still ends at Q and is
strictly shorter. Thus EVERY unit in a shortest trajectory grows by one;
permutations preserve cardinality. There are exactly n-|S| units.

Each growing inverse unit is proper: u(u^-1(S))=S. The same holds for
permutations. Composing these equalities shows that the associated forward
word reaches S exactly. Hence D(S)=d(Q,S), including S=Q (both zero).

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--3-characterization-of-all-shortest-extension-parents"></a>
#### 3. Characterization of ALL shortest extension parents

An extension word of minimum length e(S) can have no fixing/deleting unit:
omitting it leaves a larger final preimage by monotonicity, contradicting
minimality. Nor can it have a growing unit before its last letter, because
that prefix already extends S. Its inverse sequence therefore is

    a^-1 repeated t0 times, followed by c^-1,

where t0 is the earliest nonnegative time at which ANY unit grows the
rotated S. Therefore e(S)=t0+1. Complete reachability from section 1 is
essential when identifying actual-image capacity with full preimages.

For every winning forward word c a^t0, its full preimage T has size |S|+1
and is actual. An eligible winning larger image must be contained in
this T; its larger size forces equality. Thus this describes ALL parents,
without ignoring any capacity tie or allowing an unreachable subset.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--4-exchange-for-an-arbitrary-shortest-extension-choice"></a>
#### 4. Exchange for an ARBITRARY shortest extension choice

Fix ANY such c and t0. Take a shortest inverse S-to-Q trajectory of length
L=D(S). Before its first unit it follows the same unique path a^-t, with
t>=t0. Insert c^-1 after the first t0 inverse permutation steps, leaving
all original letters in place. At insertion the new trajectory contains
the old set. Inclusion remains true through every later preimage.

Every original unit grew on the old trajectory, so its target t belongs
to the new set as well. It therefore grows or fixes the new set; it cannot
delete. The inserted unit grows by one. The final set contains Q and is
Q. There were n-|S|+1 units, and exactly n-|S| actual increases; exactly
ONE original unit must be neutral. Delete that occurrence. It is after
the insertion; deleting a neutral operation leaves the later trajectory
unchanged. The resulting word has length L and starts with the prescribed
inverse phase a^-t0,c^-1.

Its remaining inverse suffix takes T to Q in L-e(S) steps. Conversely
any T-to-Q inverse word can follow that phase. Consequently

    D(S)=e(S)+D(T) for EVERY winning larger parent T.

Downward induction on |S| now gives G(S)=W(S)=D(S)=d(Q,S). This avoids
an unproved lexicographic convergence assumption. It works for t=t0 too,
and for a chosen c different from the original first unit. The sole
permutation assumption ensures the earliest rotation lies on the ORIGINAL
permutation prefix; with multiple permutations that implication fails.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--5-sharp-limitation-two-permutations"></a>
#### 5. Sharp limitation: two permutations

Four states, letters

    a=[0,1,3,2], b=[1,2,0,3], c=[2,1,2,3].

This is SC, synchronizing, completely reachable; rt=6, P=7. Its shortest
reset is c b c b a c, ending at 2. The optimal last phase c has parent
{0,2}. That pair has e=2 and unique winning parent {0,1,2}, via forward
word c b. Its tail cost is G({0,1,2})=4, so G({0,2})=6, whereas its true
reaching length is 5 (c b c b a). Then G({2})=1+6=7>6.
All three endpoint alternatives are checked; the failure is GLOBAL P,
not only a badly chosen endpoint or tie. See the full saved arrays and
independent ordinary forward/reverse BFS certificate.

State minimum is four WITHIN arbitrary permutation/unit alphabets:
all nonempty subsets of the 6 distinct permutations and 6 distinct units
at n=3 are exhausted (3969 designations), and at n=2 (9). Alphabets with
no units cannot synchronize for n>=2. Pure units attain every target in
n-|S| steps by the forest construction, so are exact as well. Duplicates
do not affect shortest costs. This is a finite complete class minimum,
not an unrestricted-DFA minimum claim. Alphabet minimum three follows
on all n: two permutations cannot synchronize, one permutation plus a
unit is covered above, and pure units are exact. n=1 is trivial.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy--6-validation-and-attribution"></a>
#### 6. Validation and attribution

The machine-readable summary is authoritative. Specifically n2..6
test 6,189,20475,9450,49775 inputs, accepting 4,117,14780,2160,7751.
n<=4 cover every nonempty unit subset and every permutation cycle type;
n5/6 cover unit subsets of sizes 1,2,3 only. Every accepted FULL array
has G=W=forward, and every input is checked with two native algorithms.
The independent checker replays ordinary reverse BFS for every n<=4
designation and retained larger samples; separate ALL-SOURCE BFS audits
the counterexample and retained arrays. The separate positive-polynomial
proof [A positive averaging polynomial proves the square for one permutation plus units](#direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square) now establishes e<=n-c+1 and the
square bound for all n; finite patterns alone are not used as proofs.
No large permutation-order running time is bounded by the exchange proof.

Szykula--Vorel, *An Extremal Series of Eulerian Synchronizing Automata*
(DLT 2016), section 3, Proposition 3 and Lemma 5, already prove straight
shortest words and immediate-unit greediness for ALL PU alphabets:
https://ktiml.mff.cuni.cz/~vorel/bib/VO7conf.pdf . The deletion/insertion
mechanism here rederives that known method. Phase-cost and all-target,
all-tie exactness with one permutation is an explicitly restricted
corollary/extension; its publication priority is OPEN, not claimed new.
Ferens--Szykula (2026), DOI 10.1145/3798283, confirms known PU complete
reachability and existing quadratic class bounds. None is a new general
Cerny bound. The four-state counter distinguishes immediate-letter
greediness (known to hold even there) from shortest-WORD phase policy.
[Commuting permutations do not rescue shortest-phase policy optimality](#direct-attack-commuting-unit-policy-obstruction) further refutes replacing the one
permutation by mutually commuting permutations: two such letters and two
units give rt8,P9 at n6. Commutativity does not make the shorter branch
a prefix of the original permutation path. Its exact class minimum and
finite scope are stated separately; the one-permutation proof is unaffected.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--a-positive-averaging-polynomial-proves-the-square-for-one-permutation-plus-units"></a>
### A positive averaging polynomial proves the square for one permutation plus units

Status: **PROVED (paper)**, independently model checked; novelty **OPEN**.
This is a special class result, not an unrestricted Cerny proof.

Let A be a strongly connected synchronizing n-state DFA, n>=2, with
ONE permutation letter a and any nonempty finite set of unitary letters
(s->t), each fixing all other states. Let a have c cycles, of lengths
l_1,...,l_c (including fixed points). Then EVERY nonempty proper S has
an extending word of length at most n-c+1, with a full actual preimage.
Consequently

    rt(A) <= 1+(n-2)(n-c+1) <= (n-1)^2.

If c>=2 this is a strict improvement over the square for n>=3. The
bound is tight at c=1 on the classical Cerny family. Identity a gives
c=n, hence rt<=n-1; pure unit alphabets are covered by deleting identity.
n=2 gives one unit as a reset, and n=1 has rt=0 separately.
No restriction on alphabet size, cycle lengths, coprimality between
cycle lengths, or permutation order is hidden in the theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--1-graphs-and-actual-images"></a>
#### 1. Graphs and actual images

[Exact policy for one permutation and unitary letters](#direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy) section 1 proves that the directed
graph Gamma of all cyclic conjugates of unitary edges is strongly
connected, and every nonempty subset is an ACTUAL Q-image. This uses
both SC and synchronization; SC alone would permit distinct Gamma
components permuted by a, giving an unsynchronizable congruence.

Collapse each a-cycle to a vertex. The unitary edges between these
vertices form a strongly connected quotient graph H: permutation a
never leaves an a-cycle, and every path of A projects to a path of H.
H may have one vertex, in which case equality of its means is vacuous.
Do not confuse H with Gamma; synchronization is needed for Gamma, but
only SC of A is needed for H.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--2-positive-averaging-with-degree-n-c-even-when-ordera-is-large"></a>
#### 2. Positive averaging with degree n-c, even when order(a) is large

For a function f:Q->R, let (Bf)(q)=f(a(q)). Set

    p(x)=product_(i=1)^c (1+x+...+x^(l_i-1)),
    d=degree(p)=sum_i(l_i-1)=n-c, K=p(1)=product_i l_i.

Every coefficient p_0,...,p_d is STRICTLY positive (p_0=p_d=1).
On an a-cycle C of length l_i, its own factor averages all positions.
The other factors commute with it and multiply its constant output
by their values at 1. Therefore

    (p(B)f)(q)=K * mean_C(f), for q in C.

This equality is exact. It uses a PRODUCT of sums, not a single sum
over 0..n-1; that single sum need not average unequal cycle lengths.
No length-order(a) word is used in this argument.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--3-contradiction-to-a-delay-of-d1"></a>
#### 3. Contradiction to a delay of d+1

Fix nonempty proper S and f=1_S. Suppose no unit extends any a^-j S
for 0<=j<=d. For each unit (s->t) this says

    F_j=f(a^j(t))-f(a^j(s)) <= 0, 0<=j<=d.

The inverse word a^-j followed by that unit corresponds to the FORWARD
word u a^j, of length j+1. Thus finding F_j>0 proves the claimed bound.
Average these inequalities with the positive coefficients of p:

    sum_(j=0)^d p_j F_j=K*(mean_cycle(t)(f)-mean_cycle(s)(f)) <=0.

Along every edge of H the mean cannot increase. Since H is strongly
connected, ALL cycle means equal some mu. The displayed sum is then
zero. Strict positivity forces F_0=...=F_d=0 for EVERY unit.

Now p(B)f=K*mu*1_Q is globally constant. For every integer h>=0,

    sum_(j=0)^d p_j F_(h+j)=0,

because B commutes with p(B), and the difference of two coordinates of
B^h(p(B)f) is zero. Since p_d=1, the first d consecutive zero terms
force all later terms to be zero by recurrence. For d=0 the same
identity directly says F_h=0 for all h. Hence f agrees across EVERY
cyclic conjugate of EVERY unitary edge. Strong connectivity of Gamma
forces f to be constant. This contradicts S nonempty and proper.

There is therefore some j<=d and some unit u growing the preimage
of a^-j S by exactly one. Its full preimage T is actual by section 1,
and (T)(u a^j)=S exactly. In particular this proves the actual-image
capacity e(S)<=d+1. Intermediate cardinality never decreases.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--4-concatenation-and-square-arithmetic"></a>
#### 4. Concatenation and square arithmetic

Choose the target t of ANY unit (s->t). Its singleton has a one-letter
extension, with preimage {s,t}. Repeatedly apply section 3 to this pair
and each later set, increasing size by exactly one until Q. There are
n-2 remaining phases, each of length <=d+1. Reversing their order
and concatenating the FORWARD phase words gives a reset ending at t.
Its length is <=1+(n-2)(d+1). Since d+1=n-c+1<=n, this is at most
1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2. Empty phases at n=2 have the correct base value.

In particular every state q has an avoiding word of length <=n-c+1:
take the k=n-1 set Q\{q}. Its first full-preimage extension reaches Q,
and the corresponding forward word reaches that complement exactly.

Every fixed-target k-set can be reached exactly within
(n-k)(n-c+1). Fixed singleton endpoints need not all satisfy the square;
the improvement to the square uses the target of an ORIGINAL unit,
not a conjugated unit whose conjugation cost was silently ignored.
The all-tie policy theorem establishes G=W=d(Q,S), but is not needed
for this constructive bound. The averaging proof is therefore a
separate reconstruction of the class upper bound.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--5-dangerous-steps-and-scope"></a>
#### 5. Dangerous steps and scope

* Positivity includes EVERY coefficient, including fixed-point factors.
* Cycle averaging is an exact matrix identity verified on basis vectors.
* SC forces equality of cycle MEANS, not pointwise membership. The
  recurrence and Gamma connectivity are required to get pointwise equality.
* The recurrence is applied only AFTER p(B)f is globally constant.
* Complete reachability makes full preimages legal actual parents.
* Additional arbitrary letters are covered for the reset bound if the
  indicated subalphabet itself is SC and synchronizing. Policy equality
  need not survive adding letters (previous monotonicity refutations).
* No simultaneous averaging of noncommuting permutation generators is
  assumed. The four-state rt6/P7 example refutes that policy extension;
  it does not refute a square bound for all PU automata.

An SC Cerny counterexample cannot have a synchronizing SC subalphabet
consisting of one permutation and units. In particular, an all-PU SC
counterexample must use at least two distinct nonidentity permutation
actions after duplicate/identity letters are omitted. This is a class
exclusion, not a complete minimal-counterexample classification.

<a id="direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square--6-literature-boundary"></a>
#### 6. Literature boundary

Rystsov (2022), *Cerny's Conjecture for Automata with Simple Idempotents*,
DOI 10.1007/s10559-022-00428-3, already proves the square for a trivial
group and for a regular permutation group. The publisher abstract was
checked; full publisher text is subscription-only. Rystsov's public
2025 manuscript arXiv:2501.19166 explicitly defines regular as transitive
and semiregular (section 4). Its regular-group/single-unit class does
not directly encompass unequal disjoint cycles and arbitrary unit sets.
The circular c=1 part here is known theory. The mixed-cycle formulation,
specific n-c+1 extension bound, and all-tie policy equality have OPEN
publication priority pending deeper comparison; absence in these searches
is not evidence of novelty. Szykula--Vorel (DLT 2016, Lemma 5) supplies
the known unit-insertion mechanism. Ferens--Szykula (2026), DOI
10.1145/3798283, surveys PU complete reachability and known quadratic
class bounds. None of these results settles unrestricted Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-tail-cycle-weighted-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-tail-cycle-weighted-square--a-long-tail-weighted-square-bound-with-arbitrary-kernel-positions"></a>
### A long-tail weighted square bound with arbitrary kernel positions

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper, ALL-n under h>=tau.** General Cerny OPEN.
This is separate from the exact opposite-kernel c0,t2 result and does
not reduce arbitrary automata to a fixed-root/core-cycle model.
No formal verification or priority claim is made.

<a id="direct-attack-tail-cycle-weighted-square--model-and-theorem"></a>
#### Model and theorem

Q=Z_M union {r}, M>=3. ORIGINAL b is the core cycle fixing r.
ORIGINAL a has rank M, doubled output r, omitted core output L!=0,
and a(r)=0. Its core kernel K is any two distinct inputs; the other
core states biject onto C minus {0,L}. The unique path from omitted
L reaches the root r after h steps. The a-cycle through r has length
tau>=2; other a-cycles may be arbitrary. Suppose h>=tau. Write

    g=gcd(M,L),        q=floor(h/tau)>=1.

**Theorem (PROVED paper):** ONE original reset satisfies

    rt <= M^2-q(M-tau) <= M^2.

Neither synchronization nor an admissible early kernel return is
assumed. All original a and b occurrences are charged.

<a id="direct-attack-tail-cycle-weighted-square--proof"></a>
#### Proof

Use core weight1 and root weight2, nu=(1,...,1,2). Literal indegree
counting gives nu a=nu+e0-eL and nu b=nu. Let f=a^tau, a word of
ORIGINAL cost tau, so r f=r. Exactly the root and ONE tail state,
at distance tau, map to r under f. Thus nu f has root mass3, while
its total mass stays M+2. A longer PAID seed a^(q tau) has exactly
q core root preimages, at distances tau,2tau,...,q tau.

The first paid inverse of {r} under a^(q tau) is r plus q core states. Let
S=r union U be a later proper target.

If U is not invariant under translation L, choose j in U with L+j
outside U. ORIGINAL a b^j has nu-gain1, sends r to j, retains r in
the inverse, and costs<=M. Ordinary cardinality also increases by1.

If U is whole, it is a union of g residue classes mod g, say c<g.
For the actual words f b^s, 0<=s<g, average the weighted gain over
these g tail shifts. Every core state lands in U in exactly c shifts,
while the root stays in S in every shift. The total gains therefore
sum to

    g + c*(-1) = g-c>0.

Some actual shift has positive integer gain. Since f b^s fixes r,
its inverse retains r and its ordinary cardinality grows by that gain.
Its cost is<=tau+g-1<=M-1: tau+h<=M+1 and h>=tau give
tau<=floor((M+1)/2); g is a proper divisor of M, so g<=M/2 for even
M and g<=M/3 for odd M. The tiny M3 case also gives cost<=2.
The weighted average is used only to select an ORIGINAL word; it is
not a stochastic letter or a free macro.

After the cost-q tau seed, at most M-q growth stages remain, each at
most M. Prepend those actual root-retaining words, obtaining ONE
chronological reset to r of total length at most q tau+M(M-q).
This proves the stated bound, with arbitrary cycle structure off r.

<a id="direct-attack-tail-cycle-weighted-square--status-and-verification-scope"></a>
#### Status and verification scope

The independent finite audit covers only NEW small inputs outside
the earlier J+g<=M kernel-return criterion, with g>2, together with
explicit larger controls. Its coverage is defined by the original row
constraints and h>=tau; no old completed input scope is re-enumerated
as a new absence result. Every word and full reset is checked with
original particle tracing. Small complete whole-coset targets check
the exact g-c average, and larger patterns are named controls only.

Short-tail inputs h<tau, kernels lacking an early return, doubled
outputs not fixed by the core-cycle letter, and general alphabets
still require further arguments. This theorem is an additional class,
not a complete rank-one/core-cycle square theorem.

Independent counts:1863 inputs, COMPLETE1752 new excluded M3..8,
20238 root-retaining stages,1231 whole-chain stages,25970 weighted
average targets,29413257 original particles, n257, h254, q84.
Seven deliberate corruptions are rejected. The initial shortcut
claiming q tail preimages already under a^tau was rejected by the
generator; the independent checker explicitly verifies ONE under
a^tau and q under the longer paid a^(q tau).346 q>1 controls exercise
this distinction. The valid theorem uses the corrected cost throughout.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-component-stagnation"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-component-stagnation--terminal-pair-components-can-stagnate-and-then-merge"></a>
### Terminal-pair components can stagnate and then merge

Date: 2026-10-01. **REFUTED**: the two attempted general statements
below. Their finite witness is **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**; the
state-minimum argument is **PROVED (paper)**. No priority or
**FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. The Cerny conjecture remains **OPEN**.

Let F_b contain all pairs merged by actual words of length <=b, and
let Pi_b be the connected-component partition of this undirected graph.
The following attractive shortcuts are false:

1. In a synchronizing n-state DFA, F_(n-1) is connected.
2. If Pi_b=Pi_(b+1), then all subsequent component partitions stabilize.

Both fail for the SC synchronizing four-state alphabet

    a=[0,0,3,2],       b=[2,0,1,3].

In pair order (01,02,03,12,13,23), exact merge distances are

    (1,3,4,2,4,5).

Consequently F_1={01}, F_2={01,12}, and F_3={01,02,12}.
Pi_2=Pi_3={{0,1,2},{3}}, yet F_4 adds 03 and 13 and is connected.
Its connectivity threshold is 4>n-1. The literal reset word
`a b b a b b a` has length seven; independent subset BFS proves its
exact full reset threshold is seven, below the square nine.

The failed closure step is visible: in F_2, vertices 0 and 2 are
connected only through 1. But a has no preimage of 1. Thus lifting that
path through a does not create an edge from 3 to 0 or 1. At F_3 the
new DIRECT edge 02 exists; its a-preimage contains 03 and 13, which
appear at F_4. Connectedness is not a substitute for the actual edges
when a singular letter deletes an intermediate path vertex. For the
same reason, stagnation of these component counts is not the usual
invariant linear-span stagnation lemma.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-component-stagnation--four-states-are-necessary-over-arbitrary-finite-alphabets"></a>
#### Four states are necessary, over arbitrary finite alphabets

For n=2 any synchronizing alphabet has a constant letter, so F_1 is
connected. For n=3 a constant letter or two different length-one kernel
pairs already connect F_1. Otherwise all singular letters have rank
two and the same kernel pair P; a synchronizing alphabet contains at
least one such letter. Let x be the other state.

Suppose F_2 is still disconnected. Each permutation letter must
preserve P, or its preimage of P would be a second kernel edge.
For a rank-two letter its image cannot be P: if it were, preimages
of the two points of P would connect x to P in F_2. Its image therefore
consists of x and one point of P. As its kernel is P, it maps the two
classes P and {x} to DIFFERENT classes. Thus every letter induces a
permutation on this two-class quotient. Such an alphabet cannot
synchronize. This contradiction proves F_2 connected for every
synchronizing three-state alphabet, without an SC assumption.

It also excludes an eventual nontrivial stagnation in this n<=3 scope:
the only disconnected nonempty component partition has two blocks;
if it persists through the next layer, the preceding quotient argument
prevents synchronization. Hence the displayed failures have the
smallest possible state number among synchronizing DFAs, not merely
within a binary sample.

This refutation concerns only COMPONENT closure. The established terminal
exterior-span theorem remains valid. The new public-family construction
in [A charged reset construction for the published compress-with-another family](#direct-attack-published-compress-other-family) instead preserves actual core
actions and constructs one compatible rooted word, paying all its costs.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--terminal-kernels-refine-frankl-compression-at-every-rank"></a>
### Terminal kernels refine Frankl compression at every rank

Date: 2026-09-30. **PROVED (paper)** for arbitrary finite alphabets.
The proof is a refinement of the established skew set-pair / Frankl
argument; publication priority is **OPEN**, not asserted. Finite checks
below are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** in their stated scope. No Lean
or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim and no new unrestricted n-only bound.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--1-general-terminal-wedge-bound"></a>
#### 1. General terminal-wedge bound

Let theta be any congruence, and S a compressible k-set inside one
class, k>=2. For a class D of size s>=k set d_D=s-k+2 and
T_D=binom(d_D,2). For an integer b>=1 let F_D(b) be the pairs in D
which some word of length <=b merges.

Choose vectors v_q in a d_D-dimensional space, independently for each
class, such that EVERY d_D of its state vectors are independent.
Let tau_D(b) be the dimension of the span of v_p wedge v_q over
{p,q} in F_D(b). Then

    c(S) <= b + sum_(D: |D|>=k) [T_D-tau_D(b)].             (1)

Any such choice of vectors is valid. One may maximize the wedge
ranks over generic vectors for a stronger bound; choosing them does
not require them to be a representation of the letter actions.

Proof. Let w be a shortest compressing word of length L. For each
preterminal image S_i after i letters, pull back the final merged
pair to a pair P_i subset S_i; all earlier prefixes are injective on
S. For j<i one has P_i NOT subset S_j. Otherwise the prefix ending
at S_j followed by the suffix beginning at S_i would compress S
earlier. This argument remains valid when those two images lie in
the same class and the subsequence skips visits to other classes.

If L<=b, (1) is immediate. If L>b, keep the L-b indices
i=0,...,L-b-1. None of their S_i contains a pair in F_D(b): a word
of length <=b merging that pair would finish strictly before L.
For the subsequence in D put B_i=D\S_i, of size s-k=d_D-2, and
define a functional on wedge^2 V_D by

    phi_i(x)=x wedge (wedge_(q in B_i) v_q),

using any fixed volume form. The diagonal phi_i(v_(P_i)) is nonzero,
because the d_D involved state vectors are distinct and independent.
For j<i in this subsequence, P_i meets B_j, so phi_j(v_(P_i))=0.
This triangular evaluation matrix has nonzero diagonal. Thus the
phi_i are independent.

Every B_i hits every pair in F_D(b), since S_i avoids those pairs.
Hence phi_i annihilates their entire wedge span. The dimension of
this annihilator is T_D-tau_D(b), bounding the number of retained
indices in D. Sum over D and add the b omitted indices. This proves
(1). In particular, the subtraction concerns all EARLY images, not
only the last pair phase, and the final b indices are charged.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--2-a-whole-letter-kernel-gives-independent-terminal-wedges"></a>
#### 2. A whole letter kernel gives independent terminal wedges

Partition s states into r nonempty fibers. The K=sum_f binom(|f|,2)
within-fiber pairs are a disjoint union of cliques. In a space of
dimension d>=s-r+1 their wedge vectors can be made ALL independent,
simultaneously with the general-position condition used in (1).

Proof. Initially choose one center in each fiber and give all centers
the vector e_0. Give each of the s-r other states a different vector
e_0+e_j. Center-leaf edges give the distinct coordinates e_0 wedge e_j.
Leaf-leaf edges additionally give the distinct coordinates e_i wedge
e_j for leaves of that fiber. Subtracting the center-leaf coordinates
shows that all K edge wedges are independent. The construction uses
1+(s-r) coordinates, within d. It need not itself be in general
position: a nonzero K-minor remains nonzero on an open set. Intersect
that open set with the finitely many open dense conditions asserting
independence of each d-subset of state vectors. Their intersection
is nonempty, and gives the required simultaneous properties.

For a letter on D of rank r>=k-1, d_D=s-k+2>=s-r+1, so its ENTIRE
K-pair kernel supplies tau_D(1)>=K. More generally, if the letter
has rank <=t with k-1<=t<=s, split its actual fibers into exactly t
nonempty subfibers. Their pairs remain terminal; their pair count
is at least

    K_0(s,t)=u binom(q+1,2)+(t-u)binom(q,2),
    s=qt+u, 0<=u<t.                                      (2)

Thus tau_D(1)>=K_0(s,t), even when the original rank is smaller.
If t>s, formula (2) gives K_0(s,t)=0 and the same inequality is
trivial; no split into more than s nonempty subfibers is used.
If a letter has rank <k on D, all k-sets in D are immediately
compressible; dropping this class from the early-index sum is an
additional possible refinement, not needed below.

One can select kernels of DIFFERENT letters in different classes.
Their lower bounds add. Several kernels in one class need a rank
calculation for their UNION; their pair counts cannot be added
without checking wedge independence.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--exact-one-kernel-combinatorial-barrier"></a>
##### Exact one-kernel combinatorial barrier

Let G be any graph, and let M_k(G) be the maximum length of a
sequence of k-cliques S_i with pairs P_i subset S_i which do not
occur in any earlier S_j. Then, exactly,

    M_k(G)=|E(G)|-wsat(G,K_k).                            (8)

Here weak saturation means adding missing edges one at a time so
that each new edge completes a k-clique. To prove (8), delete the
distinct witness edges P_i from G. Add them back in order: every
other edge of S_i is already present, because later witnesses cannot
occur in S_i. Conversely, each weak-saturation witness clique avoids
every future edge in that sequence and hence gives the required
renewing sequence. This is an exact translation, not a DFA
realizability claim.

For the complement of a SINGLE rank-r letter kernel, G is complete
r-partite. When r>=k, the bound in section 2 is EXACT:

    M_k(G)=binom(s-k+2,2)-K.                              (9)

For an elementary attaining construction, first coarsen the r parts
to k nonempty parts. Choose one base vertex in each. Start with the
base k-clique minus one edge; attach each nonbase vertex to k-2 base
vertices in other parts. This uses binom(k,2)-1+(k-2)(s-k) edges.
Restore the base edge, then each vertex's one missing base neighbor,
then all remaining cross-part edges, each completed by a base clique.
Finally restore any edges between original parts coarsened together,
using base vertices in k-2 other coarsened parts. This weakly
saturates G with exactly binom(s,2)-binom(s-k+2,2) initial edges.
The lower bound follows from the terminal-wedge argument. Equation
(9) follows from (8).

The complete-partite weak-saturation mechanism is established theory;
the k-partite case also follows from
[Bulavka--Tancer--Tyomkyn 2023, Corollary 1.2](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-023-00049-0).
The construction above is a reconstruction. Thus improving (3)
solely by squeezing the ONE-letter kernel set-pair bound is impossible.
Several terminal kernels or restrictions imposed by ACTUAL word
trajectories are needed. For general short-word terminal graphs,
one may replace T_D-tau_D(b) in (1) by the exact M_k(G_D(b)).
Computing this graph parameter does not bound it in n alone.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--3-profile-bound-with-savings-at-every-remaining-rank"></a>
#### 3. Profile bound with savings at every remaining rank

Let A be synchronizing, its quotient SC, and its minimum class size
h>=2. Choose a simple quotient path from a largest class to a
smallest. On every decreasing-size edge D->E select (2) with
t=|E|>=h. For every k<=h the wedges give at least |D|-|E|
dimensions. Distinct source classes on the path are distinct.
Their total is at least s_max-h. If all classes are equal,
synchronization requires a letter singular within some class, giving
at least one terminal wedge. Consequently put

    K_*=max{1,s_max-h}.

For exactly two classes (h,t), strong connectivity supplies a direct
letter t->h and one may instead use

    K_*=max{1,K_0(t,h)}.

Using b=1 in (1) proves, for EVERY k-subset inside a class,
2<=k<=h,

    c(S)<=sum_D binom(|D|-k+2,2)-(K_*-1).                  (3)

This strengthens the old final-pair subtraction to EVERY rank.
Write N=n-m(h-1), rho=max_D dist_quotient(D,C) for a minimum class
C, and J_(h-1)(s)=sum_(k=2)^(h-1) binom(s-k+2,2).
First compress C using [Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class](#direct-attack-profile-class-compression), then apply (3)
at the at most h-2 remaining ranks. For h>=3 this yields

    reset_A(C)<=N+rho+sum_D J_(h-1)(|D|)
                         -(h-2)(K_*-1).                 (4)

Skipped ranks only improve the result: each displayed rank budget
is at least one, as follows also from the annihilator proof. After
a square quotient reset and routing, use rho<=m-1 to get

    rt(A)<=m(m-1)+N+(m-1)+sum_D J_(h-1)(|D|)
                         -(h-2)(K_*-1).                 (5)

For a FIXED class in a uniform profile, first compression costs at
most m: follow a shortest path of bijective class edges to a source
of a singular restriction and apply that letter. Such a path exists
because the class is compressible. For a whole-DFA reset we can do
better: CHOOSE a class having a singular restriction. All classes
are minimum classes, so route the quotient reset there and compress
it in ONE letter. Provided the quotient satisfies
rt(quotient)<=(m-1)^2, even without terminal savings this proves

    rt(A)<=(m-1)^2+m binom(h+1,3).                        (6)

Indeed the quotient, route, first drop, and tail cost at most
(m-1)^2+(m-1)+1+m[binom(h+1,3)-1]. The square gap is

    (mh-1)^2-[(m-1)^2+m binom(h+1,3)]
      =m(h-1)[(h+1)(6m-h)-12]/6.                         (7)

It is nonnegative whenever 2<=h<=6m-1, m>=2: the concave product
(h+1)(6m-h) is minimized at an endpoint of that integer interval,
and its smaller endpoint value is 6m>=12. Equality occurs only
at m2,h11. Thus every uniform congruence in a STATE-MINIMAL Cerny
counterexample has h>=6m. Equivalently h>=sqrt(6n) and
m<=sqrt(n/6). This is stronger than the earlier uniform growing-size
restriction. It does not apply to nonuniform profiles. It also
combines with the necessary non-SC bijective-edge graph from the
return-monoid theorem. Formula (6) is a conditional quotient lift,
not an unrestricted n-only estimate.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--4-every-n22-congruence-is-excluded-from-a-state-minimal-counterexample"></a>
#### 4. Every n22 congruence is excluded from a state-minimal counterexample

The previous all-n class floor and all n<22 exclusions remain valid.
At n=22 the four NONUNIFORM two-class gaps now have strict bounds:

| profile | bound (5) | square |
|---|---:|---:|
| (7,15) | 423 | 441 |
| (8,14) | 435 | 441 |
| (9,13) | 436 | 441 |
| (10,12) | 439 | 441 |

The triple profile (7,7,8) is already strictly covered. The sole
remaining uniform profile (11,11) is excluded by (6), at equality
441. Equality is sufficient to exclude a counterexample, whose
reset threshold would have to be STRICTLY larger than the square.
Therefore a state-minimal Cerny counterexample has NO nontrivial
congruence at n<=22. This is not a proof of Cerny for all n<=22
automata. Simple automata remain untouched.

If (11,11) has at least TWO distinct within-class pairs merged by
letters, for k=2,...,10 two distinct wedges give total rank at least
two (d_D>=3), so each tail rank saves one and the bound is 432.
This extra saving is not required for the n22 exclusion. No exclusion
of every h7 congruence is asserted; larger nonuniform gaps remain.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl--5-computational-audit-boundary-and-the-next-obstacle"></a>
#### 5. Computational audit boundary and the next obstacle

check_terminal_kernel_frankl.py verifies renewing-sequence maxima on
all kernel partitions through six states, independently by a clique
coverage dynamic program; it checks the explicit kernel-wedge basis,
exact pair distances and compression bounds on saved DFA certificates,
and the new profile arithmetic. The completed audit covers 277 kernel
partitions, 870 exact sequence instances, 87448 coverage-DP vertices,
64 saved DFA inputs and 54655 reachable nonsingleton images. In 53189
of those images the static bound improves the old fiber-Frankl value.
These are finite checks; (1)--(7) are justified by the paper proofs.
The checker also audits uniform-profile inequalities, including
the sole equality case. Its report gives the exact arithmetic count.

The exterior argument adapts the established skew set-pair proof:
[Frankl 1982](https://doi.org/10.1016/0195-6698(82)90003-4).
Priority of this terminal-kernel formulation has not been established.
It does not turn individual short-pair witnesses into a compatible
reset chain: (4) still pays the worst remaining rank costs, which
remain cubic for growing classes. The stronger class-reset proposal,
the general quotient lift, and the unrestricted square are OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--independent-adversarial-audit-of-the-terminal-kernel-continuation"></a>
### Independent adversarial audit of the terminal-kernel continuation

Date: 2026-10-01. Audited starting HEAD
`c05a8c49b286bb5cc8c6a5ff468a9636052c89fa` on
`scripts/cerny-direct-attack`. This audit changes no existing source or
ledger. Its own script, report, and finite data are confined to
`direct_attack/`. No historical expensive search was replayed.

**PROVED (paper audit):** the terminal-wedge bound, generic single-kernel
independence, complete-partite weak-saturation equality, conditional
uniform lift, and stated state-minimal-counterexample consequences have
valid arguments under their explicit hypotheses. I found no mathematical
counterexample or missing substantive step. **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**
below refers only to the separate finite tests and their stated scopes.
Publication priority is **OPEN**. No novelty, Lean, or **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim is made. The unrestricted Cerny conjecture remains **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--1-a-minor-quantifier-repair"></a>
#### 1. A minor quantifier repair

The section-2 instruction to split a rank-at-most-t kernel into exactly
t nonempty subfibers requires `t<=s`. Its substantive application on a
decreasing-size quotient edge satisfies this automatically. For the
full written range `t>=k-1`, add the case `t>s`: then `q=0,u=s` in the
balanced-fiber formula, so `K_0(s,t)=0` and the claimed lower bound is
trivial without splitting. At `t=s` splitting into singletons works.
This is an exposition repair, not a refutation of the lower bound or any
downstream profile consequence. The root agent was informed before this
report was written.

The generic-vector argument should be understood over an infinite field,
for example the real numbers. An unrestricted finite field need not admit
arbitrarily many state vectors in the required general position. The
paper argument can choose real vectors, and its DFAs have no field
restriction.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--2-independent-derivation-of-the-terminal-wedge-argument"></a>
#### 2. Independent derivation of the terminal-wedge argument

Fix a shortest compression word of length L for a k-set S. Its images
before the last letter all have size k. Pull a pair merged by the last
letter back through the injective prefixes, obtaining P_i in S_i. If
`j<i` and `P_i subset S_j`, the prefix of length j followed by the suffix
after position i compresses S in `j+L-i<L` letters. Hence every later
witness pair avoids every earlier image, including earlier visits to
the same class separated by visits elsewhere.

For `L>b`, retain exactly `i=0,...,L-b-1`. If S_i contained a pair
merged by a word of length at most b, that word after the prefix would
compress S in at most `i+b<L` letters. Thus every retained image avoids
the entire short-terminal graph, not just a selected letter kernel.

In a class D of size s, put `d=s-k+2` and `B_i=D\S_i`. Wedge with the
`d-2` state vectors indexed by B_i, followed by a fixed volume form,
defines a functional on `wedge^2 R^d`. Its value on the wedge of P_i is
nonzero because the d involved vectors are independent. For `j<i`, P_i
meets B_j, making the jth functional zero on the ith pair wedge. The
resulting square evaluation matrix is triangular with nonzero diagonal,
so the functionals are independent. Each B_i hits every short-terminal
edge, so every functional annihilates that edge span. There are therefore
at most `binom(d,2)-tau_D(b)` retained indices in D. Summing over the
classes and charging the omitted b indices proves the displayed bound.
The case `L<=b` is immediate. No representation of the letter actions by
these vectors is used.

This also explains why b cannot be silently subtracted without its
charge, and why terminal pairs from several letters cannot have their
counts added without a union-rank calculation.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--3-generic-independence-and-exact-weak-saturation"></a>
#### 3. Generic independence and exact weak saturation

For one kernel partition into r fibers, give every fiber center e_0 and
give each remaining vertex its own `e_0+e_j`. Each center-leaf wedge has
a unique `e_0 wedge e_j` coordinate. After subtracting those coordinates,
each leaf-leaf wedge has a unique `e_i wedge e_j` coordinate belonging to
that fiber. This explicitly proves independence of all K kernel wedges
in dimension `1+s-r`, and hence in any larger dimension.

Take a K-minor nonzero at this configuration. It is a nonzero polynomial
in the vector entries. Each determinant requiring independence of a
d-subset is another nonzero polynomial. Their finite product is nonzero,
and consequently has a real point where all these conditions hold
simultaneously. This proves kernel independence together with general
position; it does not assume the displayed center configuration itself
has general position. For `r>=k-1`, the required dimension inequality is
`s-k+2>=s-r+1`.

For a rank at most t with `k-1<=t<=s`, split actual fibers until there
are t. Convexity of `binom(x,2)` makes the balanced sizes minimize the
total pair count. Those subfiber edges are still genuinely merged by
the letter. The preceding independence result applies with rank t.

For an arbitrary graph G, the exact translation
`M_k(G)=|E(G)|-wsat(G,K_k)` has the correct sequence orientation. Given
a renewing sequence, delete all its distinct witness edges. Restore them
in sequence order: later witnesses are absent from the current witness
clique, while earlier witnesses have already been restored. Each step
therefore completes a clique. Conversely, in a weak-saturation addition
sequence, the witness clique for an added edge cannot contain a future
missing edge, exactly the renewing condition. Both directions are needed
to get equality.

For a complete r-partite G with `r>=k`, coarsen its parts to k nonempty
groups, choose a base vertex per group, and start from the base clique
minus one edge. Give each nonbase vertex k-2 neighbors among the bases
outside its own coarse group. The initial edge count is

    binom(k,2)-1+(k-2)(s-k)
      =binom(s,2)-binom(s-k+2,2).

Restore the base edge, then each nonbase vertex's remaining base neighbor.
Restore all remaining edges between coarse groups using the other k-2
bases. Finally restore edges between original parts in the same coarse
group using any k-2 other coarse-group bases. Every stated witness is a
literal k-clique in the target graph. At k=2 the witness uses zero other
vertices, and the construction still works. This gives the attaining
weak-saturation bound. The wedge argument with the K independent
within-part edges gives the converse renewing bound, so

    M_k(G)=binom(s-k+2,2)-K.

Thus one cannot improve the one-kernel barrier by a sharper argument that
uses only the allowed set-pair sequences. A claim of DFA realizability of
the attaining sequence would require additional work and is not present.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--4-profile-and-uniform-lift-quantifiers"></a>
#### 4. Profile and uniform-lift quantifiers

On a simple quotient path from a largest class to a minimum h-class,
select kernels only at decreasing-size edges. Each source class is used
at most once. Since `binom(a,2)>=a-1` for `a>=1`, its balanced subfiber
kernel contributes at least the source-target size drop. The sum of all
positive drops is at least `s_max-h`. At every remaining rank `k<=h`,
all these classes have size at least k and all selected target sizes are
at least h, so the same savings apply. If all classes have equal size,
synchronization implies a singular class restriction somewhere: otherwise
every word would remain injective on each class. This supplies the one
terminal wedge needed for `K_*=max(1,s_max-h)`.

For exactly two classes, a shortest quotient path from the larger to the
smaller consists of a single letter. The direct balanced-kernel count is
therefore legitimate. For more classes this direct-letter assertion is
not used.

The full-class first-compression theorem also checks out independently.
Under its contradiction assumption, each return map r_D surjects D onto
C because a short C-to-D path followed by r_D maps the whole C bijectively
onto C. The h-1 balance forms on each D are independent: all h fibers are
nonempty, and evaluating a linear relation on the last fiber first forces
the sum of its coefficients to zero, then evaluation on the other fibers
forces each coefficient to zero. Supports in different D are disjoint.
The common kernel has dimension N. The orbit span through length N lies
there, so some ascending-span step must stabilize and make every later
orbit row lie there. A compressed C-return row has mass one but support
smaller than h; the balance equations on C require it to be uniform on
all of C, a contradiction. This uses quotient strong connectivity and C
compressibility, and does not need strong connectivity or synchronization
of the whole base DFA.

After this first drop, compression at each actually visited remaining
rank gives the stated tail sum. Skipped ranks can be omitted because every
displayed rank budget is at least one: it is b plus a sum of annihilator
dimensions. Formula (5) additionally assumes a square quotient and pays
both the quotient reset and its one subsequent route.

For a uniform profile, choose a class D carrying a singular restriction;
one exists by synchronization. Reset the quotient, route its endpoint to
D in at most m-1 letters, and pay one singular letter. All h-classes are
minimum classes, so this choice does not conflict with the first-drop
argument. The unrefined Frankl tails total
`m[binom(h+1,3)-1]`, including the empty h=2 tail. This gives

    rt(A)<=(m-1)^2+m binom(h+1,3).

The square gap is exactly
`m(h-1)[(h+1)(6m-h)-12]/6`. On the integer interval
`2<=h<=6m-1`, the concave factor `(h+1)(6m-h)` is minimized at an
endpoint. Its smaller endpoint is 6m, which is at least 12. Equality
requires exactly `(m,h)=(2,11)`. Hence a state-minimal counterexample
with a uniform congruence must have `h>=6m`; using `n=mh`, the stated
square-root equivalents follow. A quotient-square hypothesis suffices
for this uniform lift; the argument does not claim an unrestricted
n-only bound.

At `(2,11)`, the complete cost is literally
`1+1+1+2(220-1)=441`. Equality is sufficient to exclude a counterexample,
defined by reset threshold strictly greater than 441. It is not necessary
to prove strictness or assume two letter-merged pairs. If two distinct
letter-merged within-class pairs do exist, their wedges have total rank
at least two at each tail rank: within one class, proportional wedges
would put at least three general-position vectors in one plane, which
is impossible when `d>=3`; across classes ranks add. This validates the
optional 432 bound, without using it in the exclusion.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--5-historical-class-floor-and-the-n22-inference"></a>
#### 5. Historical class floor and the n<=22 inference

The inference starts with a hypothetical counterexample minimal in
number of states among all synchronizing finite-alphabet DFAs. Its proper
terminal strongly connected component would give a smaller reset problem;
the outside-state routing argument yields the square, so it must be
strongly connected. Its quotient is synchronizing and strongly connected,
and every smaller synchronizing return automaton satisfies the square by
state minimality. Thus both smaller-state assumptions used in the inherited
short-return lift are available. No induction on alphabet size is needed.

I checked the short-return orbit-span and stationary-distribution proof
used by that lift. Restricted excursions span by outside dimension d,
and the congruence ensures nonzero restricted products are actual first
returns. Invariance under short returns implies invariance under all
returns. The base's reset words ending at each member of C force every
stochastic row's return-orbit span to be all of `R^h`. A stationary row
must have positive support; otherwise its zero coordinates remain zero
under every macro word. Averaging the orbit rows then provides a strict
preimage mass increase for every proper subset, and finitely many subsets
force a reset. The resulting short-return alphabet is an actual smaller
synchronizing DFA, making its square use noncircular.

For `h=1`, quotient reset and routing to a singleton suffice. For
`h=2,3,4`, the inherited return-lift square gaps at `n=hm` are positive
for every `m>=2` and increase with n. For `h=5,m>=3` the same is true;
for `m=2,n>=14` it is strict, and the four profiles `(5,5)` through
`(5,8)` have explicit Frankl bounds 42,56,74,96 against squares
81,100,121,144.

For `h=6,m>=4`, the minimum-n gap is
`35m^2-161m+126`, positive at m=4 and increasing thereafter. Its n
increment is `2n-26>0` in that range. For m=3, the return lift is strict
from n=22 onward; for m=2 it is strict from n=22 onward. Only n=18..21
and n=12..21 respectively remain. The integer-convex Frankl sum is
maximized by concentrating all excess size in one class, so the finite
extreme profiles cover every profile in these ranges. The independent
arithmetic below verifies these cases using the old Frankl/return bounds
and the new first-drop bound; the two repaired old gaps are strict.
Consequently every class of every nontrivial congruence of a state-minimal
counterexample has size at least seven.

For n<=22 this leaves only two-class profiles with each size at least
seven, plus `(7,7,7)` at n=21 and `(7,7,8)` at n=22. There cannot be
four classes. Independent integer-profile enumeration covers every one
of these profiles. The new nonuniform n=22 bounds are 423,435,436,439
for `(7,15),(8,14),(9,13),(10,12)`; the triple bound is 202. The
uniform `(11,11)` profile has bound 441. Hence the precise conclusion
is that a state-minimal counterexample at n<=22 cannot have a nontrivial
congruence. It does not prove the square for all n<=22 DFAs and does not
touch simple automata.
