<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--7-what-would-constitute-genuine-additional-progress"></a>
#### 7. What would constitute genuine additional progress

The exact complete-partite equality closes off a stronger conclusion
derived solely from one letter kernel and unrestricted renewing sequences.
A next general result must use either several short-terminal kernels
with their union rank correctly charged, or constraints of literal DFA
trajectories beyond arbitrary set-pair sequences. Varying b also must pay
its literal b charge and should be audited on the Cerny family before it
is presented as a route to a square bound. The current tail still takes
a separate worst compression budget at every rank; no compatibility
between minimizers at different ranks has been established.

A concrete necessary distinction is that an attaining weak-saturation
sequence only supplies abstract k-cliques and witness pairs. It supplies
neither letters implementing the consecutive set images nor suffixes
pulling every witness back to one final merged pair. A future bound using
those additional constraints would be stronger than the already sharp
one-kernel combinatorial barrier. This audit supplies no such theorem
and does not upgrade finite negative searches to universal claims.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--8-independent-attack-on-the-subsequent-cerny-family-barrier"></a>
#### 8. Independent attack on the subsequent Cerny-family barrier

After the preceding audit, the root agent proposed a separate all-n
obstruction to window optimization and rankwise worst-case summation.
I derived its potential and token arguments independently, and found
both sound under the following precise scope. These are **PROVED (paper
audit)** barriers for the standard Cerny family and the specified bounding
methods; they are not new unrestricted DFA upper bounds.

Write `a(q)=q+1 mod n` and let b fix every state except `b(n-1)=0`.
For `1<=r<=floor(n/2)`, define

    P_(r,j)={r-1-j mod n, n-1-j mod n}.

Its a-orbit period is n, except that the even half-distance orbit has
period n/2. Taking `0<=j<period`, the potential is

    D(P_(r,j))=(r-1)n+1+j.

The pair at `j>0` goes under a to phase j-1, decreasing D by one.
At `j=0,r>1`, b sends the pair to orbit r-1, phase n-1, also decreasing
D by one; at r=1 it merges immediately. These give literal shortest-word
witnesses recursively. The a-transition at phase zero wraps to the last
phase and cannot improve the potential lower bound. Apart from phase
zero, the only b-active phase in a full orbit is j=r. When a further
distance orbit exists, b sends it to orbit r+1, phase r, increasing D
by n. In the final odd orbit it stays in the same orbit at phase n-1,
increasing D by r. In the even half orbit there is no second active
phase among its distinct representatives. All other b-transitions fix
the pair. Thus every letter satisfies `D(P)<=1+D(P letter)`, taking
merged pairs to have potential zero, and the recursive witnesses achieve
equality. The potential is exactly the pair distance.

The intervals of values of D partition `1,...,binom(n,2)`. Therefore
`|F_b|=min(b,binom(n,2))`. For every k and every valid vector choice,
`tau_b<=|F_b|<=b`, so

    b+binom(n-k+2,2)-tau_b >= binom(n-k+2,2).

At b=1 the single terminal pair has a nonzero wedge, giving equality.
Consequently optimizing b, even with the maximal generic wedge rank,
does not improve the ordinary Frankl rank budget anywhere in this family.
This conclusion includes the full rank k=n and the even half orbit;
neither is an omitted edge case.

For the stronger rankwise barrier, choose a k-set whose successive
circular gaps are all at least `g=floor(n/k)`, for instance
`S={floor(i*n/k):0<=i<k}`. Follow its labeled tokens until the first
collision. An effective unmerged b moves exactly one token forward by
one, while a moves all tokens equally. Cyclic order is preserved until
collision. The trailing token of the colliding initially adjacent pair
must therefore have at least g effective b-advances: its excess advances
over the leading token equal their initial gap. Between consecutive
effective b applications to that same token, at least n-1 a letters
are required, since b has just moved it from n-1 to zero and all other
b applications leave it fixed. Hence every compressing word has length
at least

    (g-1)(n-1)+g=n(g-1)+1.

All nonempty subsets are actual images: positive-word conjugates of b
give each cyclic adjacent unit `i->i+1`, and applying those units along
each gap outside a desired subset deletes the unwanted states into the
next desired state while fixing every desired state. Thus the spaced
sets above are included even if the budget is restricted to actual
images. Any bound that independently maximizes the compression cost at
every rank and then sums these maxima must be at least

    n sum_(k=2)^n [floor(n/k)-1]+(n-1)
      >=n^2 H_n-3n^2+3n-1
      =Omega(n^2 log n).

This is a method barrier. It does not say that a single reset trajectory
visits all the worst spaced sets, and it does not contradict the square
reset length of the Cerny family. Replacing the wedge rank by an exact
terminal-graph sequence capacity still cannot make such a universal
per-rank budget smaller than an actual subset's compression cost.

The independent script was extended and replayed after this derivation.
It verifies all 20,825 pair distances for n=2..50 against a separate
reverse pair BFS, all 2,035 actual images at n=2..10 by forward image
BFS, and 91 spaced-set lower bounds at n=2..14 by literal compression
BFS. These scopes and counts are recorded in the same audit JSON.
The all-n statements rely on the explicit potential and token proofs,
not on extrapolating those finite checks.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit--9-independent-audit-of-the-exact-rankwise-maxima"></a>
#### 9. Independent audit of the exact rankwise maxima

The subsequent stronger root derivation is also valid. It gives an exact
formula at every rank, rather than merely the spaced-set lower bound.
Let

    R_k(C_n)=max_(|S|=k) c(S),
    g=floor(n/k), e=n-gk, m=k-e.

Then for `2<=k<=n`,

    R_k(C_n)=g(n-k+e+1)=g(n-m+1).                 (A)

For any k-set, let d be its smallest circular gap. An arc between selected
vertices is a sum of adjacent positive gaps. Thus the pairs of smallest
circular distance d are precisely the adjacent pairs with gap d. Larger
distances belong to later pair-distance intervals and cannot determine
the first compression. If x is the starting label of a gap d, its phase
is `j=n-1-x`, and its pair distance is `dn-x`. Consequently

    c(S)=dn-max{x : the forward circular gap at x equals d}.  (B)

For the even half-distance case, the two endpoints supply both possible
tight starting labels; taking their maximum automatically restricts the
phase to its distinct half-orbit range. Thus (B) handles that orientation
case as well.

Necessarily `d<=g`. If `d<g`, (B) gives `c(S)<=(g-1)n`. This is strictly
less than the proposed value because `g(m-1)<=g(k-1)<n`. When `d=g`,
the total surplus e over k gaps of size g allows at most e longer gaps.
There are at least m tight-gap starts. In increasing numeric label order
they are separated by at least g, so their largest label is at least
`(m-1)g`. Equation (B) gives the upper bound `gn-(m-1)g`, exactly (A).

For attainment, begin at state zero and use the circular gap vector
consisting of m copies of g followed by e copies of g+1. It sums to n
and has exactly k gaps. Its tight starts are
`0,g,...,(m-1)g`; every other gap is larger. Equation (B) achieves (A).
When e=0 this specializes to the equally spaced set and gives
`n(g-1)+g`. At k=2 the formula gives `binom(n,2)` in both parity cases;
one may equivalently establish that rank directly from the pair spectrum.

The comparison to the square budget is exact:

    R_k(C_n)-[2(n-k)+1]
      =(g-1)[(g-2)k+2e+1].

This is zero for g=1 and positive for g>=2. Summing `2(n-k)+1` over
`k=2,...,n` gives `(n-1)^2`. At n>=4 the pair rank has g>=2, so

    sum_(k=2)^n R_k(C_n)>(n-1)^2       for every n>=4.

Thus summing independent worst-case rank budgets already fails the
square on the Cerny family at every n>=4, even if those budgets are exact
compression times and all sets are required to be actual images. The
harmonic asymptotic barrier remains valid. This does not rule out a
trajectory-dependent argument that selects favorable successive images.

The separate script now enumerates every one of the 32,647 nonsingleton
subsets at n=2..14, using independently computed pair BFS distances.
It checks (B), all 91 exact rank maxima (A), the difference identity,
and the summed strict/equality cases. The JSON retains the complete
rank-sum table for that finite scope. All assertions passed on the saved
replay. The proof above establishes the all-n statement; the table alone
would not.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-graph-square"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-weighted-graph-square--original-square-resets-from-paired-output-differences"></a>
### Original square resets from paired output differences

2026-10-03. **PROVED paper, all-n sufficient criterion and infinite
subclasses.** Finite controls COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED. NOT FORMALLY
VERIFIED. Automatic connectivity in the last theorem was later REFUTED
by [A residual graph can fail while the actual extension is short](#direct-attack-weighted-graph-automaticity-barrier); its sufficient implication
remains valid. The complete order-two model and general Cerny remain OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-graph-square--model-and-endpoints"></a>
#### Model and endpoints

Use exactly the original model and mass from [A weighted target for the unresolved order-two model](#direct-attack-weighted-order-two-extension):
M=2L>=6, Q=Z_M union {r}, b is the core cycle fixing r,
a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r, and A=a|_(Z_M minus {0,L}) is an arbitrary
permutation. Core weight is1; root weight2. With delta=e0-eL,

    nu a = nu+delta, delta a=0, nu b=nu,
    nu a^k=nu+delta for all k>=1.

All products and costs below are ORIGINAL words.

**Endpoint lemma, PROVED paper.** Every mixed input has a root-fixed
word of cost<=M with root preimage mass exactly3, and a word of cost<=M
with root preimage mass exactly1. The latter gives weighted growth of
the whole core by complementing the root.

There cannot be exactly one mixed opposite input pair: the other full
output pairs would leave exactly one full output pair for it. Therefore
there are at least two mixed j in1,...,L-1. Take the least, j<=L-2.
For k_plus=(-A(j)) mod L and k_minus=(-A(j+L)) mod L, both <=L-1,
the words a b^j a b^k a cost j+k+3<=M. Their root masses are2+1
and2-1, respectively. Indeed

    nu a b^j a b^k a - nu = delta + delta b^k a
                               + delta b^j a b^k a.

The first two terms evaluate to0 on the root: the two kernel inputs
are opposite. The final term evaluates to+1 or-1, since k sends one
of the two different output residues into {0,L} and the other outside.
The plus word fixes r; the minus word does not map r to r. Hence the
literal root preimages are respectively root+ONE core and ONE core.
This proves an endpoint statement, not the formerly guessed short
root seedTHREE bound or an ordinary all-set extension theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-graph-square--a-simple-primitive-difference-theorem"></a>
#### A simple primitive-difference theorem

Define

    d = gcd(L, A(j)-A(j+L) for 1<=j<L).

**PROVED paper:** if d=1, EVERY proper nonempty set has an original
weighted extension of cost<=M. Consequently rt<=M^2=(n-1)^2.
In particular this holds for EVERY synchronizing input with PRIME L.
No separate condition on the permutation A is required for prime L:
mixing supplies a nonzero difference mod L, hence d=1.

Proof: nonwhole sets have the one-a extension already proved. If S is
whole, then for a b^j a b^s its mass difference is

    chi_S(A(j)+s)-chi_S(A(j+L)+s),

where core addition is mod M. The delta b^s term vanishes. Every
j in1,...,L-1 and every s in0,...,L-1 costs j+s+2<=2L=M.
On pair labels Z_L these words give every translate of an oriented
edge of step A(j)-A(j+L). The directed cyclic graph has components
exactly the residue classes mod d. If d=1, any nonconstant core
pattern has a positive edge. Constant core patterns leave only {r}
and the whole core as proper nonempty possibilities; the endpoint
lemma handles both. Integral mass increases from2 toM+2 in at most
M stages, with each actual word prepended to the existing suffix.
The same chronological word resets Q to r and costs<=M^2.

**Further PROVED paper sufficient case:** if d>1 and a mixed j satisfies
j<=L-d-1, the same conclusion holds. Nonperiodic patterns have a two-a
edge. For a period-d pattern choose k_plus when the root flag is1,
k_minus when it is0. The other endpoint after the last a is a core
state, because the pair is mixed. A final shift s<d can give this
endpoint the opposite membership from the root. In the displayed
three-a defect, delta b^k a b^s is0 on a period-d pattern by the
definition of d. Thus mass increases by1. Total cost is at most
(L-d-1)+(L-1)+(d-1)+3=M. No preservation of residue classes by A is
needed for this argument.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-graph-square--more-a-powers-with-every-cost-charged"></a>
#### More a powers, with every cost charged

For 1<=k<L and 1<=j<=L-k, define the differences
A^k(j)-A^k(j+L), and let

    h = gcd(L, ALL these triangular differences).

In particular h divides d. The ACTUAL words

    a b^j a^k b^s,       0<=s<L,

cost j+k+s+1<=M. On any whole S their mass differences are exactly
chi_S(A^k(j)+s)-chi_S(A^k(j+L)+s). The same translated-edge argument
therefore extends every core pattern that is not periodic mod h.
This uses arbitrarily many a, up toL, so it is not contradicted by
the previous restricted three-a barriers.

It remains to extend the period-h patterns, including their root flag.
Use vertices Z_h union {root}. For every triple j,k,s with

    1<=j<M, j!=L, k>=0, 0<=s<h, j+k+s+3<=M,

insert the directed edge from

    label(a(A(j+L)+k)b^s)  to  label(a(A(j)+k)b^s),

where core label is residue mod h and root has its own label. Its
literal witness is a b^j a b^k a b^s. For a period-h target, the
first two terms in the three-a defect vanish: h divides every
one-step paired difference. The edge is therefore the EXACT remaining
mass difference, even if either endpoint is the root.

**Graph criterion, PROVED paper:** if this finite directed graph is
strongly connected, all period-h targets have a positive entering
edge of cost<=M. Together with the triangular words and nonwhole
formula this proves WEXT and ONE original square reset for the input.
If h=1, the endpoint lemma automatically supplies both directions
between the two vertices, so the criterion holds. A mixed j<=L-h-1
is another automatic sufficient case, by the previous argument with h.
Construction/checking is polynomial in M. This is an input-dependent
general theorem, not a claim that the graph always is connected.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--every-optimal-history-can-have-only-logarithmic-dimension"></a>
### Every optimal history can have only logarithmic dimension

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper), EVERY d>=2**. Bounded independent
controls are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim. Priority of this automaton realization is **OPEN**. General
Cerny, policy square and expensive-phase/dimension compatibility remain
**OPEN**. The alphabet grows; no all-parameter binary claim.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--precise-all-optimal-theorem"></a>
#### Precise all-optimal theorem

For n=2^d-1 there is an SC Eulerian DFA with 2(d-1) original
rank-(n-1) letters and exact rt=P=n-1. EVERY shortest original word
resets to0 and has the SAME image history S_n,S_(n-1),...,S_1.
EVERY optimal actual-image endpoint chain is its reverse, with n-2
proper stages and exact one-letter phases e=1. Raw proper rank with
Q is d and normalized rank is d-1. Including the initial singleton
and ALL letter-level intermediate vectors still has raw rank exactly d.
The number of shortest labeled words is product j^binom(d-1,j), j1..d-1.

Adjoining n-1 ORIGINAL adjacent swaps makes the DFA simple and completely
reachable, retaining SC/Eulerian balance and EVERY optimum. Hence EVERY
positive linear-in-stages dimension guarantee for EVEN SOME optimized
history, with any fixed additive error, is REFUTED: (d-1)/(2^d-3)->0.
All these histories are cheap, with LINEAR reset length; no conditional
expensive-phase inequality or general Cerny bound is refuted.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--original-unitcarry-maps"></a>
#### Original unit/carry maps

Let Q={0,...,n-1}, B_i=[2^i-1,2^(i+1)-2], |B_i|=2^i. B_0={0}.
For 1<=i<d put s_i=2^i-1. Define h_i by 0->s_i, fixing all other
states. Define c_i by

    q<s_i:       q -> s_i+1+q;
    q=s_i:       q -> 0;
    s_i<q<=2s_i: q -> q-s_i-1;
    q>2s_i:      q -> q.

Put L_i=B_0 union ... union B_(i-1)={0,...,s_i-1}. The map c_i
swaps each lower q with s_i+1+q, then sends carrier s_i to0. It
maps L_i bijectively onto B_i minus {s_i}, and maps B_i onto L_i
with only collision {s_i,s_i+1}->0 and missing state s_i. The sole
collision of h_i is {0,s_i}->s_i, with missing state0. Both have rank
n-1 and lose at most one image point per step.

The incoming excess/deficit of h_i is canceled by c_i, so every state
has incoming/outgoing degree 2(d-1): the DFA is Eulerian. It is SC
by induction: carrier s_i is reached from0 by h_i and returns by c_i;
each other B_i state is paired in both directions by c_i with a lower
state. Thus every block joins the strongly connected lower set.

S_k is the union of B_i selected by the bits of k, of cardinality k.
S_1={0}, S_n=Q. The weighted Boolean-vector architecture is attributed
to [Szykula 2026, Section2.8, Lemmas18--21](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245).
No novelty is claimed for that rank mechanism. Here explicit maps force
it on EVERY globally shortest history.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--key-all-set-invariant-a-missing-carrier-partial-block"></a>
#### Key all-set invariant: a missing-carrier partial block

Call X bad if for some i>=1, X intersects B_i nontrivially, misses
s_i, and has a point outside B_i. Such X has at least two points.
Other blocks need not be uniform.

**PROVED: EVERY original step that strictly decreases the cardinality
of a bad X leaves a bad set.** Fix witnessing B_i. For h_i a decrease
requires both0 and s_i, impossible. For h_j, j!=i, B_i is fixed and
outside points stay outside, leaving a nonempty outside image. For c_i
a decrease requires both s_i and s_i+1, impossible. For c_j, j<i,
the support lies below B_i: it fixes B_i and keeps outside points
outside, preserving the same witness.

For c_j, j>i, a decreasing step requires its collision pair
{s_j,s_j+1}, hence puts0 in the output. The nonempty X intersection
B_i lies in L_j and maps into B_j minus {s_j}. State s_j is globally
missing from c_j's image. Thus B_j becomes a nonempty carrier-missing
partial block, and0 is a point outside it. The output is bad. This
covers EVERY letter and EVERY bad subset, not just counter sets.

Consequently no path of strictly decreasing original steps starting
from a bad set reaches a singleton. Neutral steps or added permutations
can repair it, but cannot occur in a length-(n-1) reset.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--all-minimum-words-decrement-the-same-counter"></a>
#### All minimum words decrement the same counter

Every reset has length>=n-1. On block union S_k:

* For odd k>1, the decreasing good letters are exactly h_i with bit
  i selected. They remove0, giving S_(k-1). Every decreasing c_i has
  a nonempty selected lower set containing0 and creates a bad set.
* For even k, no h_i decreases. Let i be the least set bit. Its
  lower set is empty; c_i replaces full B_i by full L_i, giving
  S_(k-1). Any other decreasing c_j sends the nonempty lower selected
  set into a nonempty carrier-missing B_j partial image and sends full
  B_j onto full L_j, creating a bad set.

A good letter exists at every k=n,...,2, yielding a length-(n-1)
reset to0. Thus rt=n-1. EVERY shortest word must decrease at every
letter and cannot enter a bad set, so its image list is exactly the
same counter decrement. At even k its label is unique; at odd k there
are popcount(k)-1 choices. There are binom(d-1,j) odd k with j selected
higher bits. This proves the exact labeled-word count.

Corank-one saturation makes every forward prefix equal its full inverse
suffix preimage. Every S_k is actual already before augmentation, and
every inverse phase has e=1, hence P=rt=n-1. The all-optimal-cut theorem
in [Rank-loss saturation preserves optimal histories under permutation augmentation](#direct-attack-optimal-saturation-transfer) forces EVERY optimal policy onto these
same one-letter cuts, not just the displayed reset's cuts.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--exact-rank-and-completion"></a>
#### Exact rank and completion

All vectors are constant on the d blocks. They span each block indicator:
chi_(B0)=chi_(S3)-chi_(S2), chi_(Bi)=chi_(S_(2^i)) for i>=1. Raw rank
with Q is therefore d; centering removes one Q direction, giving d-1.
The initial singleton is B_0 and adds no dimension. Phases are single
letters, so no intermediate vectors are omitted.

The charged adjacent-swap completion in [Rank-loss saturation preserves optimal histories under permutation augmentation](#direct-attack-optimal-saturation-transfer)
gives simple complete reachability. Each added permutation contributes
one incoming/outgoing edge at each state, preserving Eulerian balance.
No minimum word uses a permutation: it would lose at most n-2 points
in n-1 letters. Every shortest word and optimal endpoint history is
unchanged. The bad invariant need not apply to arbitrary permutations;
they are excluded from every optimum. The completed original alphabet
has n-1+2(d-1) letters, and is not fixed-size as d grows.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--independent-checks-and-boundary"></a>
#### Independent checks and boundary

`optimal_counter_history.py` retains eleven parameters d2..12 through
n4095, exact counts and EVERY good label choice, whole reset indices,
original-row/counter-mask hashes and rational block-coordinate ranks.
`check_optimal_counter_history.py` imports no generator/native kernel.
It reconstructs carries by paired swaps plus overwrite, checks original
degrees, and SC in both directions. Direct original-row block images
test EVERY letter at EVERY counter stage: 163716 row/state controls,
163584 stage/label controls. Every decreasing departure is checked bad.
Integer Bareiss minors give centered determinant n^(d-2); whole-word
controls throughn255 pay494 original letters.

COMPLETE n3/7/15 universes independently verify EVERY bad-set decreasing
edge (31448 total), then build full FORWARD drop DAGs without assuming
the counter theorem. Exact minimum label counts are1/2/24. Original
adjacent swaps independently reach ALL7/127/32767 nonempty subsets.
Six corruptions, including a supposedly good wrong carry, are rejected.
These are bounded corroborations, not a computational universal proof
or formal kernel. The arbitrary-d result is the paper case analysis.

 The exact unconditional
optimized-positive-linear interpretation is now REFUTED; the informal
2026 question is not declared resolved under every interpretation.
General Cerny, global policy square and expensive-phase/dimension
compatibility remain OPEN. All thresholds of this family are LINEAR.

<a id="direct-attack-all-optimal-log-counter-history--continued-attack-after-the-theorem-commit-macro-inflation-fails"></a>
#### Continued attack after the theorem commit: macro inflation fails

We then tried to turn a carry into an expensive phase. Let u_i be the
unit s_i->s_i+1 and let p_i cycle through L_i followed by the paired
B_i minus {s_i}, in matched order. With s_i=2^i-1, its half-power
p_i^s_i is the lower/upper paired swap, so c_i=u_i p_i^s_i. Replacing
the ORIGINAL c_i by those original unit/cycle generators expands the
counter schedule to d*2^(d-1)-1 letters.

**REFUTED, paper, as a claim of preserved optimality:** every expanded
schedule ends in u_1 p_1. Before that last p_1, u_1 already merges
B_1 to a singleton. Removing the trailing permutation preserves reset
and strictly shortens the word, for EVERY d>=2. More generally any
word ending in a permutation cannot be a globally shortest reset.
Trimming this suffix alone is not a proof that the remaining inflated
schedule is optimal. Exploratory longer-parameter comparisons are kept
in the ignored native_build directory and are not claimed as independent
certificates here.

The original theorem uses c_i as an ORIGINAL cost-one map; it remains
valid. This failed cost-inflation route emphasizes why the open expensive-
phase question must constrain ALL competitive original words rather
than attach an implementation length to one displayed schedule.

<a id="direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction--image-policy-can-become-worse-when-letters-or-word-shortcuts-are-added"></a>
### Image policy can become worse when letters or word shortcuts are added

**REFUTED, state-minimal n=4 over any finite alphabet:** the global policy
P(A)=min_q G_A({q}) need not be nonincreasing under alphabet inclusion.
The failure also occurs when the added transformation is already induced
by an actual word, so the complete monoid and reachable-image family stay
the same. This refutes neither the global policy square target nor Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction--the-stronger-failure-with-the-monoid-unchanged"></a>
#### The stronger failure with the monoid unchanged

On Q={0,1,2,3}, take right-action rows

    a=[1,0,0,2], b=[1,2,3,0],
    c=[2,0,1,2]=b^2 a b^3 a.

The equality is equality of transformations on EVERY state. The shortest
word inducing c in {a,b} has length 7, independently checked by complete
individual-transformation BFS. Adding c as a one-step letter preserves
the entire transformation monoid (176 elements, computationally counted)
and image family. Both alphabets are SC synchronizing: b is a full cycle
and aaba resets Q in length 4.

The image family is all 15 nonempty subsets. The triples are rotations of
Qa={0,1,2}; Qaa={0,1} supplies all four adjacent pairs by b rotations;
Qaba={0,2} supplies both diagonal pairs. Q aaba={0}, then b rotations
supply all singletons. This is a paper reachability argument.

Independent set BFS / all-tie recurrence gives:

| Quantity | alphabet {a,b} | alphabet {a,b,c} |
|---|---|---|
| Exact reset threshold | 4 | 4 |
| G({0}),G({1}),G({2}),G({3}) | 4,5,6,7 | 5,6,6,7 |
| Global minimum P | 4 | 5 |
| e({1,2}) | 2 | 1 |
| G({1,2}) | 3 | 4 |

The mechanism is exact. Originally T={0,1,2} is reached from Q by a,
so G(T)=1; its word ab maps T onto {1,2} with cost 2. Hence the old
cost there is 2+1=3. No one-step extension into {1,2} exists originally.
After adding c, T'={0,2,3} maps onto {1,2} in one step. It is the ONLY
larger image qualifying in one step: b preserves cardinality and a maps
every triple to a set containing 0. Thus the policy must take T'.
It has G(T')=3, making the new cost 1+3=4. After one or two letters
the possible proper full-Q images are {0,1,2}, {1,2,3}, {0,1}; none
is contained in T'. The word ab^2 reaches T' in length 3, proving that
top-rank cost. Finally e({0})=1 has only the larger endpoint {1,2},
so G({0}) rises by one. The other singleton values above independently
exclude another initial singleton repairing this increase.

All old exact transport distances weakly decrease: every old word is
still present. On every old image, e_new<=e_old as well. The independent
checker finds 64 strict improvements of exact image-to-image distances,
yet the minimum policy becomes worse. The phase restriction, rather than
failure to improve distances or loss of images, causes the increase.

<a id="direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction--a-separate-failure-that-adds-reachable-images"></a>
#### A separate failure that adds reachable images

The earlier first failure in the arbitrary-map scan is

    a=[0,0,2,2], b=[1,3,0,2], c=[0,0,2,1].

Its global policy rises from 3 to 4 while rt remains 3. The image family
grows from 9 to all 15 nonempty subsets. The base has no proper reachable
image larger than a pair, whereas the added letter has rank 3. This example
is retained separately; the actual-word example above does not need image
family growth.

<a id="direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction--why-four-states-is-minimal-a-positive-policy-theorem"></a>
#### Why four states is minimal: a positive policy theorem

**PROVED on paper.** If a strongly connected synchronizing DFA has no
proper reachable image of size >2, then P(A)=rt(A). Equivalently for n>=3,
every nonpermutation letter has rank <=2. For n=1 the empty word gives 0;
for n=2 a synchronizing DFA has a constant letter and gives 1.

If a constant letter exists, both costs are 1. Otherwise take a shortest
reset w of length L. Its last proper prefix has image U of size 2: a
nonpermutation has already appeared, and a singleton at an earlier prefix
would contradict shortestness. Let the last letter map U to {q}.
Then e({q})=1, with U an allowed larger endpoint. The only image larger
than U is Q, so G(U)=e(U)<=L-1, using the actual prefix word sending Q
into U. Consequently G({q})<=1+G(U)<=L. Every policy constructs a reset
word, giving rt(A)<=P(A), and equality follows. The proof allows arbitrary
alphabet size, inverse cardinality losses and transport into proper subsets.

Every DFA with n<=3 satisfies this image-rank hypothesis. Thus P=rt for
every SC synchronizing DFA in that range, and alphabet inclusion cannot
increase P because it cannot increase rt. This proves the four-state
minimum over ANY alphabet, beyond the small binary augmentation covers.
The n4 word-shortcut example also shows that the rank cap 2 cannot be
replaced by 3 in this policy-optimality theorem. This is a conditional
policy theorem, not a new general synchronization bound.

<a id="direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction--exact-evidence-and-proof-boundary"></a>
#### Exact evidence and proof boundary

The binary first-map cover at n=2,3, with every extra transformation,
checks 16 and 1593 additions. Restricting additions to the full generated
monoid checks 15 and 899. The n4 scans STOP at the first failure, after
83978 arbitrary and 34227 generated additions; they are not full covers.
Repeated-letter additions are included and harmless; covering counts
overlap and are not unique isomorphism-class counts.

Both complete base/augmented e, best and worst arrays, actual reset words
and phase words are retained. The checker recomputes policies using
ordinary inverse-set BFS, exact set transport using forward BFS, strong
connectivity, the complete 176-element monoids and the actual seven-letter
transformation. Three deliberately corrupted fields are rejected. Negative
search counts use the enumerator, not a second complete enumeration;
state-minimality rests on the paper rank-two theorem. No new Lean result.

The global square policy remains OPEN. Standard letter-deletion arguments
for Cerny use monotonicity of rt. For a hypothetical failure of the POLICY
square bound, deleting a letter can lower P even while synchronization is
preserved. Thus that standard argument alone does not produce an
alphabet-minimal policy failure. This does not alter the valid alphabet
reduction for an actual Cerny counterexample or give a square-bound failure.

There is a valid cost-preserving macro statement. Add finitely many
nonempty actual words as new labels, assigning each its ORIGINAL word
length as positive weight. Every weighted word expands into an old word
of the same total length; conversely every old word remains available.
Thus the monoid, image family, every transport distance, e, the sets of
shortest allowed endpoints, and G are all unchanged. This is a direct
word-expansion observation, not a new synchronization bound. Assigning a
seven-letter word cost 1 changes those distances; the example defeats the
stronger hope that this improvement at least monotonically improves P.
The image-extension framework is known from
[Kisielewicz--Szykula 2016, Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.01268).
Priority of these exact policy obstructions and conditional theorem is OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-annular-multicluster-boundary"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-annular-multicluster-boundary--the-unmodified-annular-formula-fails-on-multiple-clusters"></a>
### The unmodified annular formula fails on multiple clusters

Date: 2026-10-01. **REFUTED, PROVED (paper)** for the precise extension
below, in infinite SC synchronizing corank-one families. General Cerny
**OPEN**. This does NOT refute the original ONE-CLUSTER paper lemma.
Publication priority **OPEN**; no formal verification claim.

The annular descent in [Zhu2026](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.19675)
is formulated for ONE cycle. The earlier binary and new ternary pressure
searches found no counter within their sampled one-cluster scopes, but
those searches are not an independent proof audit of that paper.

Consider ONLY the following proposed extension: let C be the union of
ALL cyclic states of a, put m=|C|, let ell be its maximal tail height,
t=n-m, and keep the SAME annular limits and prior subspace. For another
letter f put u_f=[C]P_f-[C], and

    L_0=span{u_f P_a^h: f!=a, h>=0}; M_0=L_0 P_a^ell.

At order r1, kappa=min(t,ell). The proposed condition is

    Omega= sum_(h0,h1>=0; max(0,kappa-1)<=h0+h1<=m+kappa-2)
                u_f P_a^h0 P_g P_a^(h1+ell) in M_0.       (1)

We disprove (1), without asserting that any revised multicluster formula
or a different method must fail.

<a id="direct-attack-annular-multicluster-boundary--binary-counter-for-every-n3"></a>
#### Binary counter for EVERY n>=3

Let a fix0,...,n-2 and send n-1 to0. Let b be the full forward n-cycle.
This is the ordinary Cerny family, with the unit as distinguished a.
Here C={0,...,n-2}, m=n-1, ell=t=kappa=1. Direct original-row calculation
gives u_b=e_(n-1)-e_0 and u_b P_a=0. Therefore M_0={0}.

In (1), EVERY term with h0>=1 vanishes. For h0=0 and each h1=0,...,m-1,
the term is e_0-e_1, since a is idempotent and fixes0/1. Thus

    Omega=(n-1)(e_0-e_1)!=0,                              (2)

so it is outside M_0. The automaton is SC and synchronizes with the
literal word a(b^(n-1)a)^(n-2), of fully charged length(n-1)^2. The
rooted row b^(n-1)a fixes0 and maps i>0 to i-1; after the initial a the
largest root height is n-2. This is a known reset, not a new Cerny result.
At n3, Omega=2(e_0-e_1) already fails at the FIRST annular order.

<a id="direct-attack-annular-multicluster-boundary--two-equal-nontrivial-cycles-every-m2"></a>
#### Two EQUAL nontrivial cycles, EVERY m>=2

To exclude a repair that merely forbids loop cycles, take n=2m+1.
Let a cycle0..m-1 and m..2m-1 separately, and send the tail z=2m to0.
Let b be the unit0->1. Let g be the permutation(0 m)(1 z).
All other points are fixed by b/g. The original ranks are n-1/n-1/n.
C consists of the two m-cycles, so |C|=2m, ell=t=kappa=1.

The seeds are u_b=e_1-e_0 and u_g=e_z-e_1. After multiplication by a,
both seeds are supported inside the FIRST cycle and have zero total.
Every further a-power stays in that subspace. Consequently ALL M_0
vectors have zero mass on the second cycle.

Use f=b and g=g in (1). The final a-powers preserve second-cycle mass.
On u_b P_a^h0 the coefficient at0 is -1 when h0=0 mod m and +1 when
h0=m-1 mod m, with the other residues giving0. The ONLY first-cycle
point carried by g to the second cycle is0. Therefore the second-cycle
mass of Omega is

    sum_(h0=0)^(2m-1) (2m-h0)*coefficient_at0(u_b P_a^h0)
      = -2m-m+(m+1)+1=-2(m-1)!=0.                        (3)

Hence Omega is not in M_0 for EVERY m>=2, despite identical cycle periods.
This is the eigenvalue1 cycle-mass obstruction, not a mismatch between
different periods.

The original state graph is SC: a traverses both cycles, g exchanges
points between them and connects the tail, and a returns the tail to0.
Synchronization follows from the proved stable-kernel theorem in
[Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient](#direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient). Its actual forward kernel graph is
connected: the a-orbit of b's kernel01 connects the first cycle; a's
kernel{m-1,z} attaches the tail; g sends01 to{m,z}; its subsequent a^j
images attach EVERY second-cycle point to the first component. All
letters have corank<=1, so these kernel pairs and their images are stable;
a connected graph then makes stability universal. This is an existence
proof, not a short reset word or an all-n exact threshold claim.

<a id="direct-attack-annular-multicluster-boundary--verification-and-the-remaining-route"></a>
#### Verification and the remaining route

The generator records original rows, seeds and integer Omega vectors.
The independent checker sums in the opposite order, using ORIGINAL
particle steps for the full annular sum. It checks the explicit linear
functional obstruction, literal kernel-image edges and SC, and verifies
the binary rooted reset. Small ternary complete subset computations
corroborate synchronization only in their finite scopes. Deliberate
corruptions are rejected. The infinite proofs are paper proofs.

The old one-permutation cycle-averaging theorem already uses a product
of cycle polynomials; it must not be replaced by the single-cycle annular
expression (1). That product still leaves several eigenvalue1 modes.
No bound for a common original word killing those modes has been proved.
At this historical checkpoint the original one-cluster lemma remained
unaudited. The 2026-10-02 continuation [Independent reconstruction of the one-cluster upper proof](#direct-attack-one-cluster-upper-proof-audit)
now reconstructs the source's MAIN UPPER proof without an identified gap,
with attribution and no formal or source Section10 lower-bound audit.
This specific unrestricted extrapolation remains REFUTED and should not
be retried; completing the subclass audit does not repair cycle mass.

Completed finite scope:42 binary and26 equal-cycle parameters, n through
257,111480 original annular particle/letter controls,111722 annular
summands,118151 original rooted-row controls,80498 literal reset controls
and1072 connected kernel-image edges. Five small ternary subset scopes
use9864 vertices. Eight deliberate corruptions are rejected.
<a id="direct-attack-balanced-history-saturation-rigidity"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-balanced-history-saturation-rigidity--binary-rigidity-at-the-balanced-hyperplane-counting-limit"></a>
### Binary rigidity at the balanced-hyperplane counting limit

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), arbitrary n>=5**. This is a
necessary structural condition, not a general reset upper bound.
General Cerny and ALL/SOME shortest-history cost/rank remain **OPEN**.
No publication priority or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim.

Let alpha=(1,1,-1,-1,0,...,0), W=ker alpha and V=W intersect {0,1}^n.
There are6*2^(n-4) vertices and c=n-4 singleton directions. Suppose
W is the FULL inverse-history span of ANY globally shortest reset w,
and its length attains the refined bound

    L=6*2^(n-4)-(n-4)-1.                               (1)

Assume the alphabet has TWO original letters a,b, neither preserving W.
For a row transformation matrix M_f, put beta_f=alpha M_f. For an
inverse target vector x in W, M_f x belongs to W exactly when beta_f x=0.
Also beta_f Q=0, because deterministic row matrices fix the all-ones
column. Nonpreservation means beta_f restricted to W is nonzero.

Then, after possibly exchanging a,b, their restricted guards are

    beta_a|W = lambda*(x_0-x_2),
    beta_b|W = mu*(x_0-x_3), lambda*mu != 0.             (2)

In particular EVERY free-coordinate coefficient of BOTH beta rows
vanishes. This is stronger than merely counting one intersection space.
At n6/d5 it constrains the still-open L21 saturation case to two
opposite pair-match guards, unless at least one letter preserves W.
It neither constructs such an automaton nor excludes the constrained
case. Larger alphabets are not covered by the binary conclusion.

**Practical limitation, added after attacking this result:** the REAL-
space classification is arbitrary-n, but the DFA saturation hypothesis
(1) is already IMPOSSIBLE at EVERY n>=8 by the classical Pin--Frankl
upper bound T(n)=(n^3-n)/6-1, valid at n>=4; see
[Szykula2026, Section2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245).
Writing A(n) for (1), A(8)=91>T(8)=83. For n>=8,
A(n+1)-2A(n)=n-4>0, whereas
2T(n)-T(n+1)=n(n+1)(n-4)/6-1>0. Induction proves A(n)>T(n).
Thus this saturation-specific necessary condition cannot deliver a
new large-n automaton bound by itself. No novelty is asserted for
combining the known cubic bound with the exponential space count.
The general near-saturation/common-word cost problem remains OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-balanced-history-saturation-rigidity--why-saturation-forces-guard-coverage-of-every-vertex"></a>
#### Why saturation forces guard coverage of every vertex

Equation (1), together with distinct history sets, says that the
history visits EVERY vertex of V except zero and the c-1 unused free
singletons. Every nonterminal vertex has an actual next letter with
its guard zero; Q has both guards zero.

If both guards were nonzero at any vertex x in V, they would also
be nonzero at Q-x, since beta_a Q=beta_b Q=0. Neither vertex is zero
or Q. At least one is a nonsingleton, since n>=5, and therefore is
visited by the saturated history. This is impossible. Hence

    (beta_a x)*(beta_b x)=0 for EVERY x in V.            (3)

No assumption that either letter preserves W has been introduced.

<a id="direct-attack-balanced-history-saturation-rigidity--exact-covering-classification"></a>
#### Exact covering classification

More generally, let F,G be ANY real linear functionals on W, both
nonzero, with F(Q)=G(Q)=0. If F(x)G(x)=0 for every Boolean x in W,
then (2) holds for F,G up to exchange and nonzero scaling. Conversely
the two functionals in (2) cover V.

Separate the first four coordinates from the k=n-4 free coordinates.
On a vertex with first four bits zero, the restrictions to free bits
are homogeneous linear forms A,B satisfying A(y)B(y)=0 for ALL
y in {0,1}^k. Evaluating one-hot bits gives A_i B_i=0. If both forms
were nonzero, choose A_i!=0 and B_j!=0. Necessarily i!=j, and the
single-coordinate equations give B_i=A_j=0. At e_i+e_j the product
would be A_i B_j!=0. Thus one free restriction vanishes.

Say A vanishes. The six Boolean first-four patterns span the
three-dimensional core hyperplane. Since F is nonzero and independent
of free bits, some core pattern z has F(z)!=0. For EVERY free y,
F(z)G(z+y)=0, so G vanishes on the entire free cube translated by z.
Subtract the value at y0 from the values at its one-hot successors:
EVERY free coefficient of G is zero. Both forms are now core forms,
and their values on the all-ones core are zero by F(Q)=G(Q)=0.

The four nonconstant, nonzero core patterns are the pair indicators
02,03,12,13. Complementation pairs02 with13 and03 with12, and negates
the values of either functional. Modulo the all-ones direction these
are TWO independent lines: 1111, indicator02 and indicator03 are
independent in the core hyperplane. A nonzero core functional that
vanishes on1111 can vanish on at most one of those two lines.
To cover all four pair patterns, one functional must vanish on the
02/13 line and the other on03/12. Their respective one-dimensional
annihilators are x0-x2 and x0-x3 on W. This proves (2).

For the converse, every balanced first-four Boolean pattern has
x0=x2 OR x0=x3. Indeed when x0=0, one of x2,x3 must be0, and when
x0=1, one must be1. Thus the two guard hyperplanes cover every V.
The result is an exact REAL-space classification, not merely a
bounded integer search.

<a id="direct-attack-balanced-history-saturation-rigidity--control-and-continuation-boundary"></a>
#### Control and continuation boundary

An independent finite checker reconstructs the core from its six
support patterns and classifies canonical exact integer functionals.
It exhausts all pairs in the recorded grids, tests their product at
every Boolean vertex, and separately checks the free one-/two-bit
argument. These are finite controls of the paper proof, not all real
functionals, all DFAs, or a formal verification.
The four grids n5..8 contain176088 ordered form pairs,15756432
Boolean-vertex product controls and176088 separate free-restriction
pair controls; exactly32 ordered pairs cover their grids. Six
corruptions are rejected.
