<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid--short-return-monoids-with-bijective-transport-between-equal-classes"></a>
### Short return monoids with bijective transport between equal classes

Date: 2026-09-30. **PROVED (paper)** under the explicit transport
hypothesis below. Priority is **OPEN**; the finite literature search does
not establish novelty. **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** applies only to the
saved finite certificates. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** statement is added.
The unrestricted Cerny conjecture and general congruence hereditariness
remain **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid--1-entire-return-monoid-not-just-a-synchronizing-basis"></a>
#### 1. Entire return monoid, not just a synchronizing basis

Let a DFA have a congruence with m>=2 classes, each of size h>=2.
Make a directed graph J on these classes: include a labeled edge D--a-->E
exactly when the restriction of a from D to E is a BIJECTION. Assume J
is strongly connected. A letter may be bijective on one class and
singular on another; global permutation letters are not required.

Fix a class C. Let p_D be a shortest path in J from C to D, and r_D
a shortest path from D to C; p_C=r_C=epsilon. These word restrictions
are bijections. Form a return alphabet B on C using the actual words

    p_D a r_(Da)             for every class D and letter a,
    p_D r_D                  for every D != C.                 (1)

Duplicates may be removed. There are at most m|Sigma|+m-1 generators.
Every word in (1) is a FIRST return to C: its two shortest routing
paths have no internal visit to C. Let L be the maximum length in
(1). Then L<=2m-1, and

    M(B) = {w restricted to C : Cw subset C}.                  (2)

The right-hand side includes the identity and all word lengths.
Thus B synchronizes iff C can be reset in the original DFA. Neither
strong connectivity of the base DFA nor synchronization is needed
for the monoid equality itself.

Proof. Use p_D as an abstract coordinate bijection C->D. For an
edge D--a-->E, define the coordinate transformation

    f_(D,a)=p_D a p_E^(-1).

Here p_E^(-1) is initially an abstract bijection, not a free word.
The actual loop ell_E=p_E r_E is a permutation of C and is a B
generator (or the identity at E=C). Its inverse belongs to M(B),
because a permutation of a finite set has a positive-power inverse.
The other generator in (1) is

    g_(D,a)=p_D a r_E=f_(D,a) ell_E.

Consequently f_(D,a)=g_(D,a) ell_E^(-1) is in M(B). This argument
uses only transformation membership; it does NOT charge the inverse
as length zero or assert a short original word representing it.

Along any quotient path beginning and ending at C, the successive
coordinate transformations telescope: p_E^(-1)p_E is the identity
on E, and p_C is the identity. Their product is the original word
restricted to C. It lies in M(B). Conversely every generator of B
is an actual C-return word, and concatenations remain C-return
words. This proves (2).

The alphabet is constructible in polynomial time by class-graph BFS
and literal word composition. Enumeration of the full monoid is
used only in the finite audit, not in the construction or proof.

<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid--2-conditional-square-lift-and-a-general-minimal-counterexample-exclusion"></a>
#### 2. Conditional square lift and a general minimal-counterexample exclusion

Assume A synchronizes, its quotient has reset threshold R, and H(h)
is ANY proved reset bound for arbitrary h-state DFAs. By (2), B is
an actual synchronizing h-state DFA. Reset the quotient, route its
terminal class to C using J, and reset C using B. This pays the
quotient and class route once, and proves

    rt(A)<=R+dist_J(quotient reset endpoint,C)+L H(h)
          <=R+(m-1)+(2m-1)H(h).                              (3)

If BOTH the quotient and arbitrary h-state DFAs satisfy the square,
the bound is m(m-1)+(2m-1)(h-1)^2. Since n=mh,

    (n-1)^2-[m(m-1)+(2m-1)(h-1)^2]
       =(m-1)[(m-1)h^2+2h-m-2]>0.                          (4)

For h>=2 the bracket is at least 3m-2. This proves a strict lift
for EVERY m,h under those two smaller-state assumptions. A quotient
square assumption ALONE is not asserted to settle all h.

In a state-minimal Cerny counterexample both smaller-state squares
are supplied by minimality. Therefore EVERY uniform nontrivial
congruence in such a counterexample has a NON-strongly-connected
bijective-edge graph J. This all-n restriction is additional to the
earlier growing class-size floor; it includes arbitrarily large h.

In particular, a minimal counterexample cannot have a congruence on
which its permutation letters act transitively. Such transitivity
forces equal class sizes and makes J strongly connected. If the
permutation subgroup is transitive on all states, a minimal
counterexample must be SIMPLE as a DFA. This does not imply that
its permutation subgroup must be primitive: other letters may break
the group's block systems. It does not establish the square for
all automata with transitive permutation subgroups.

<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid--3-the-cutoff-2m-1-is-sharp-independently-of-h"></a>
#### 3. The cutoff 2m-1 is sharp, independently of h

For every m,h>=2 take states (i,j), 0<=i<m, 0<=j<h. Classes are
the fixed-i fibers. Define three letters R,L,c:

    R(i,j)=(i+1,j)                   if i<m-1;
    R(m-1,j)=(m-1,j)                 if j<h-1;
    R(m-1,h-1)=(m-1,0);
    L(i,j)=(max(i-1,0),j);
    c(0,j)=(0,j+1 mod h), c(i,j)=(i,j) if i>0.

The bijective-edge graph contains the two directed paths between all
classes, hence is strongly connected. The whole DFA is SC: move to
class zero using L, choose any fiber coordinate using c, and move
to any class using R without using its terminal loop.

A singular C_0-return must use R at class m-1. Reaching it needs
m-1 letters, the singular step needs one, and returning to zero
needs m-1 more. Thus every first return shorter than 2m-1 is a
permutation. At length 2m-1, R^m L^(m-1) is exactly the adjacent
unit collapse (h-1)->0 on C_0. Together with c it gives the usual
Cerny h-state alphabet. Thus the short return alphabet first
synchronizes at EXACTLY 2m-1. The usual macro square is attained
by this alphabet, although its actual letter costs are unequal.

The original DFA synchronizes: R^m maps ALL states to class m-1
and performs the adjacent collapse. The explicit word

    R^m (L^(m-1) c^(h-1) R^m)^(h-2)                         (5)

resets Q, with length m+(h-2)(2m+h-2). No exact original reset
threshold is claimed. This family also shows why a worst macro
cost times a macro reset length can overcharge the original problem.

<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid--4-removing-bijective-connectivity-fails-even-with-uniform-classes"></a>
#### 4. Removing bijective connectivity fails even with uniform classes

For each odd h=2t+1>=3 use two h-classes C and O. Write both with
local indices 0,...,h-1. Define x(q)=0 for q<t or q=h-1, and
x(q)=t otherwise. Let a map C into O by x and cycle O by +1;
let b fix C and map O to C preserving its local index.

This DFA is SC: O cycles, b reaches every member of C, and a
exits C. Its bijective-edge graph has no path C->O.
First returns at C are b and a^(s+1)b, inducing identity and
x followed by the O-cycle shift s. Put B={0,t}, and color q by x(q).
For s=0,...,h-2, B+s has different colors; at s=h-1 both colors
are zero. This follows directly by splitting s into 0..t-1,
t..2t-1, and 2t.

All short nonidentity return images are B+s, 0<=s<=h-2. Applying
any further such return first applies x, so preserves their rank
two and returns them to this same pair family. Therefore the
first-return alphabet through length h is NOT synchronizing.
At length h+1 the shifted pair B+h-1 appears and the length-two
return ab merges it. Thus the exact synchronizing cutoff is h+1,
which equals n-h+1. An actual full reset is

    b a^h b a, of length h+3.                               (6)

Uniform congruences alone therefore admit NO return cutoff depending
only on the number m of classes. These examples refute removal of
the hypothesis of (2); they do not refute Cerny or a stronger class
reset bound such as (h-1)(n-1).

<a id="direct-attack-bijective-fiber-return-monoid--5-verification-and-subsequent-research"></a>
#### 5. Verification and subsequent research

bijective_fiber_returns.py tests 3000 deterministic sampled alphabets
with h,m in {2,3,4}: all 3000 short/full return monoids agree;
2166 base DFAs synchronize and 834 do not. This is not a cover.
It retains 48 improving sample records, 30 sharp-cutoff controls,
and 10 nonbijective boundary controls. The exact subset reset
claims for small macro DFAs are checked, not assumed from the sample.

check_bijective_fiber_returns.py independently uses packed deterministic
matrix multiplication and ordinary reverse-subset distances. It
checks all 88 records, the smaller gauge alphabet as well as all
short returns, 17915 return-orbit vertices, 1120 reverse-subset
vertices, every literal lifted word, and four corrupted fields.
The family controls include full-Q resets and separate SC checks.
Neither implementation imports the other's return solver.

The coordinate-change argument is an elementary finite-semigroup
construction. The conditional quotient comparison is the context of
[Rodaro--Venturi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17992), while general
short-return synchronization is proved separately in
[Short first returns, compression of a block, and a stronger quotient lift](#direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift). Exact priority of the present monoid
generation statement and exclusion remains OPEN.

The next unresolved cases are uniform congruences without bijective
connectivity, nonuniform classes, and simple automata. The inverse
permutations in section 1 do not give a length estimate outside the
finite macro alphabet; replacing them by inverse singular maps is
invalid. The stronger class-reset proposal from
[Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class](#direct-attack-profile-class-compression) remains OPEN. No universal n-only reset
or image-extension bound follows from the result above.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-balancing-characterization"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-binary-balancing-characterization--exact-binary-boundary-of-original-one-step-positive-balancing"></a>
### Exact binary boundary of original one-step positive balancing

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), EVERY n>=2.** No novelty or
FORMALLY VERIFIED claim. General Cerny remains **OPEN**. This is
an exact scope audit of [Positive original-letter defect balance gives a compatible square reset](#direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal), not an
ordinary reset-threshold search or a refutation of its square theorem.

Let the ORIGINAL binary alphabet be{f,b}, rank(f)=n-1, with b a
permutation. Write e for f's unique omitted image and d for its unique
doubled image; they are distinct. There is NO assumption on f's kernel
inputs, level, fixed points, SC or synchronization. Put D(w)=[Q]P_w-[Q].

Then positive one-step balancing

    alpha D(f)+beta_f D(f f)+beta_b D(f b)=0,
    alpha>0, beta_f>=0, beta_b>=0,

is feasible IFF

    b(e)=d and b(d)=e.

Weights may be real/rational/integer; the equivalence holds in each
case, and the sufficient certificate has alpha=beta_b=1,beta_f=0.
Thus positive weights enlarge the preceding criterion for richer or
higher-corank alphabets, but NOT for this binary rank-one/permutation
class. The permutation must literally exchange the two OUTPUT defects;
having them on the same longer cycle does not satisfy this criterion.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-balancing-characterization--necessity-by-two-single-state-coordinates"></a>
#### Necessity by two single-state coordinates

Here c_f=[Q]+e_d-e_e, so

    D(f)(e)=-1, D(f)(d)=1.

Because f never outputs e, f f never outputs e either:

    D(f f)(e)=-1.

Let p!=q be the TWO original preimages of d under f. The column at d
of f f has mass c_f(p)+c_f(q). Only e has c_f(e)=0, while every other
state has mass at leastONE. Two distinct states cannot both be e.
Therefore

    c_(f f)(d)>=1, D(f f)(d)>=0.

Finally b is a permutation, giving

    D(f b)=e_(b(d))-e_(b(e)).

If b(d)!=e, this last vector is nonpositive at e. ALL three balanced
terms are then nonpositive at e, with the alpha D(f) term strictly
negative. No nonnegative beta weights can make the sumZERO.

If b(e)!=d, D(f b) is nonnegative at d. ALL three terms are then
nonnegative at d, with alpha D(f) strictly positive. Again their sum
cannot vanish. These are explicit single-state dual obstructions;
no linear-program numerical infeasibility claim is used.

Feasibility hence requires BOTH b(d)=e and b(e)=d. Conversely these
equalities give D(f b)=-D(f), so alpha=beta_b=1,beta_f=0 works.
This proves the equivalence for EVERY n.

The positive coefficient on the leading singular f is essential.
Permutation-only stationary distributions cannot replace it in the
negative-change repair argument. The criterion's failure still gives
NO lower bound beyond the Cerny square, and does not refute a different
compatible extension or reset policy.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-balancing-characterization--complete-finite-matrix-cover-independent-of-the-generator"></a>
#### Complete finite matrix cover, independent of the generator

Relabel e=0,d=1. Every allowed f is an arbitrary map with column
counts(0,2,1,...,1), so there are n!/2 distinct f rows. There are n!
possible original permutation rows b. The independent checker validates
all rows, uniqueness and these exact combinatorial counts, then ALL
matrix pairs and their state-coordinate duals.

The complete labeled canonical scope n2..5 has7508 inputs:
2,18,288,7200 respectively. Exactly388 satisfy the criterion:
1,3,24,360 respectively. Those are precisely the earlier positive
canonical binary cover, now characterized as the ENTIRE eligible binary
class. The additional7120 have certified infeasibility, not an alleged
synchronization or threshold failure:5989 use coordinate e,1131 use d.

74420 literal composition controls check f f and f b, and eight corruptions
are rejected. The checker imports NO generator, LP routine or graph
solver. Exact finite coverage is **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**; the
arbitrary-n equivalence follows from the paper coordinate proof.
No full/general proof, new automaton counterexample, external reviewer
or FORMALLY VERIFIED all-n characterization is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-unit-letter-class"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-binary-unit-letter-class--all-sc-binary-automata-with-a-unit-idempotent-letter"></a>
### All SC binary automata with a unit idempotent letter

**PROVED on paper; attribution/priority OPEN.** Let n>=2 and let one
letter b fix every state except a single source, which it sends to a
different target. Every strongly connected binary DFA with such a letter
has the normal form below. It is synchronizing exactly when gcd(n-j,h)=1,
and every synchronizing member has an explicit reset within the square.
This excludes this ENTIRE binary class from Cerny counterexamples,
including a second letter that is not a permutation. It is a special-class
result/reconstruction, not a new unrestricted bound or novelty claim.

After relabeling the target as 0 and its forward a orbit in order,

    a(q)=q+1 for q<n-1, and a(n-1)=j;
    b(h)=0, b(q)=q otherwise;      1<=h<n, 0<=j<=h.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-unit-letter-class--the-normal-form-is-complete"></a>
#### The normal form is complete

From state 0, b is either neutral or returns a trajectory to 0. Hence
every state reachable from 0 by any word lies on the unary a orbit of 0.
SC forces that orbit to visit ALL n states before its first repetition.
Label them 0,...,n-1 in that order; the repeated state is j. The b-source
has label h>=1. States j,...,n-1 form a cycle of length L=n-j. Returning
from that cycle to 0 requires h to be on it, unless j=0 where 0 already
lies on the cycle. Thus h>=j. Conversely these guards give SC: 0 reaches
all states along a, and every state reaches h then returns to 0 via b.
This is a classification modulo relabeling; multiplicities are not silently
called distinct isomorphism classes.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-unit-letter-class--synchronization-iff-gcdlh1"></a>
#### Synchronization iff gcd(L,h)=1

If g=gcd(L,h)>1, color state q by q mod g. Letter a increments the color
by one, including its wrap since g divides n-j. Letter b preserves color,
including h->0 since g divides h. Different colors never merge, so the
DFA is nonsynchronizing.

If gcd(L,h)=1, a^j maps Q onto C={j,...,n-1}. On C the word t=ba^h
fixes state h: hb=0 and 0a^h=h. Every other state follows rotation by h
around C. That rotation is a SINGLE cycle because gcd(L,h)=1; replacing
the outgoing edge of h by its self-loop cuts the cycle into a chain ending
at h. Hence Ct^(L-1)={h}. For j>=1 the reset

    a^j (ba^h)^(L-1)

has length j+(h+1)(n-j-1) <= j+n(n-j-1)
=n(n-1)-(n-1)j <=(n-1)^2. This includes L1, when a^j alone resets.

For j=0, the same chain argument applies on Q. In this pure-cycle case
the final a^h can be omitted, since a^h is a permutation: if its output
is singleton, its input already was. Thus

    (ba^h)^(n-2)b

resets and has length (h+1)(n-2)+1 <= n(n-2)+1=(n-1)^2.

The trimming step is INVALID when j>0 because a^h is then noninjective.
An immediate exact attack found n4,j2,h3: a=[1,2,3,2],b=[0,1,2,0],
rt=P=5. The mistakenly trimmed aab has length 3 and is not a reset.
The full aabaaa construction works. This failed candidate is recorded
as a refutation, rather than silently promoted to a stronger bound.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-unit-letter-class--minimal-counterexample-and-policy-boundaries"></a>
#### Minimal-counterexample and policy boundaries

An SC binary Cerny counterexample therefore cannot contain a unit
idempotent letter. For larger alphabets, this excludes a synchronizing
SC two-letter subalphabet of this form; it does NOT classify arbitrary
additional letters or replace the general counterexample analysis.

Complete parameter tests n2..12 have P=rt and max e<=n. Those two
stronger policy claims remain CONJECTURED for arbitrary parameters;
For the pure-cycle j0 subcase, these are now PROVED by the more general
[Exact policy for one permutation and unitary letters](#direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy) and [A positive averaging polynomial proves the square for one permutation plus units](#direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-square).
The unresolved parameter statement above concerns the nonpermutation tail.
the square reset proof above does not establish them. No exact reset
threshold formula is asserted for the class, and the constructive bound
can exceed the true rt. The j0,h=n-1 classical C_n boundary is tight.

<a id="direct-attack-binary-unit-letter-class--independent-checks"></a>
#### Independent checks

All 352 parameter instances n2..12 are retained, including 130 nonsync
controls; EVERY saved e/G/W/forward entry on all 222 sync instances has
ordinary per-target reverse BFS checks (n<=7 also ALL-SOURCE). Explicit
words, SC, modular invariants and the failed trimming witness are checked.
Separately all 50068 arbitrary second maps at n2..6 with fixed unit b
are enumerated: ordinary SC and image closure agree with the full-orbit
normal form and gcd synchronization test. Three corruptions are rejected.
The paper proves the unbounded class; finite coverage is not extrapolated.

Classical circular synchronization, unit contractions and one-cluster
methods belong to an established literature. The present proof is a
short constructive reconstruction; precise priority remains OPEN pending
a full primary-source comparison. No new general n-only bound or Lean.

The j0 square conclusion is already contained in
[Don 2015, Proposition 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1507.06070): the circular
distance from excluded state h to contraction state 0 is n-h, and its
coprimality condition is gcd(n,h)=1. That part is explicitly reconstructed
known theory. The cyclic-tail normal form, complete class classification
and explicit words retain OPEN attribution; no exhaustive novelty claim.

<a id="direct-attack-bounded-cerny-returns-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-bounded-cerny-returns-obstruction--every-square-reset-of-cerny-requires-a-long-cyclic-run"></a>
### Every square reset of Cerny requires a long cyclic run

Status: **PROVED (paper)**, EVERY n>=4. The fixed-return paid square
shortcut is **REFUTED** even inside the ordinary Cerny family. No novelty
or FORMALLY VERIFIED claim. This uses a consequence of the established
Wielandt-digraph proof, not a new lower bound for the ordinary family.
The unrestricted Cerny conjecture remains **OPEN**.

Let Q={0,...,n-1}, M=n-1, a(0)=1 and a(q)=q for q>0,
b(q)=q+1 mod n. The original reset threshold is M^2, attained by

    a (b^M a)^(M-1).

Our previous almost-circular route includes this normal form: ab has
a cycle of length M and level1, S=Q a={1,...,M}. Its three actual
returns a,ba,bba have original costs1,2,3. Their existence/synchronization
equivalence remains correct, but retaining all three does NOT repair
the square-cost method. At n4 the exact return cost is10, so entering
with a costs11>9. The formerly suggested full-three-return square
shortcut is thus **REFUTED**. The all-length return alphabet is different.

<a id="direct-attack-bounded-cerny-returns-obstruction--a-letter-count-consequence-of-an-attributed-lower-bound-proof"></a>
#### A letter-count consequence of an attributed lower-bound proof

**Lemma.** EVERY original reset word contains at least M(M-1) letters b.

For an arbitrary reset word, delete an initial b-run, truncate at its
first singleton image, and remove redundant consecutive a's. The result
w is still a reset, begins and ends with a, contains no aa, and has no
more b's than the original. Write w=w' a. Immediately before the final
letter its image is exactly {0,1}, because a has only that nonsingleton
fiber. Every a in w' is followed by b. Parse each ab as a new label c,
and every remaining b as label b, obtaining v over {b,c}. Each new label
contains exactly ONE original b, so |v|=#b(w).

On Q the labels b and c=ab define a complete DFA W. Both send every
q>0 to q+1 mod n. At0, b sends0 to1 and c sends0 to2. Since
Q v={0,1}, the word vc resets W to2. Write L=|vc|=|v|+1. For any length
ell>=L, prefix vc by an arbitrary W-word of length ell-L. From ANY
state, this gives a path of length ell to2. In particular it gives a
closed walk of length ell from2.

Every closed walk in the support of W decomposes into simple cycles.
There are only the n-cycle through1 and the (n-1)-cycle skipping1.
Consequently every closed-walk length has form xn+y(n-1), x,y>=0.
The integer g=n^2-3n+1 has no such representation: modulo n it forces
y=n-1 mod n, hence y>=n-1; then y(n-1)>=M^2>g. Thus L>g.
If L=g+1, the length-L path from1 to2 starts with its forced edge
1->2, leaving a length-g closed walk at2, again impossible. Therefore
L>=g+2 and |v|>=g+1=M(M-1), proving the lemma for arbitrary resets.

Attribution: the parsing and two-cycle walk argument are the known
lower-bound proof in [Ananichev--Gusev--Volkov2013, Theorem3/Proposition3,
with the W-family bound in Theorem2]
(https://arxiv.org/pdf/1302.5793v2), also presented in
[Volkov2022, Proposition3.1, pp.850-851]
(https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=rm&paperid=10005&what=fullteng).
Here the b count is explicitly retained, the normalization is stated
for arbitrary words, and its consequence for the paid return cutoff is
drawn. These are paper deductions; no priority claim is made.

<a id="direct-attack-bounded-cerny-returns-obstruction--the-entire-bounded-return-pool-fails-below-the-square"></a>
#### The entire bounded-return pool fails below the square

Fix a cap1<=K<M. Consider ALL actual returns b^j a, 0<=j<=K,
each paid j+1, after the original entering a. They preserve S, since
a sends Q into S. Let an expanded reset have B b's and A a's. It starts
and ends with a. There are at most A-1 b-runs, each of length at most K.
Hence B<=K(A-1), so A>=ceil(B/K)+1. The lemma gives

    length >= M(M-1)+ceil(M(M-1)/K)+1.

Because K<=M-1, the right side is at least M^2+1. This proves that NO
word formed from this entire pool can achieve the original square.
Allowing redundant consecutive a's cannot help; the count argument
already includes them. For K=1 the return DFA is nonsynchronizing;
for K>=2 it synchronizes (the previously proved qualitative equivalence
applies), but only above the square. For K=M the displayed ordinary
reset is allowed and attains M^2.

In particular EVERY original reset of length <=M^2 must contain a
b-run of length at least M. For a fixed cap K>=2 and growing n>K+1,
the lower bound is asymptotically (1+1/K)n^2. Qualitative synchronization
by a finite set of short returns cannot preserve the square budget.
This also rules out every cap up to n-2, not merely the chosen ba/bba
pair. Alternative original-alphabet strategies and all-length returns
are outside the refutation; this is not a counterexample to Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-bounded-cerny-returns-obstruction--independent-finite-controls-and-the-remaining-route"></a>
#### Independent finite controls and the remaining route

bounded_cerny_returns.py retains ALL subset costs for n4..14 and every
cap K=1..n-1. check_bounded_cerny_returns.py imports no generator or
old solver. Positive-cost local Bellman equations uniquely certify the
ordinary and return distances, with literal original-label witnesses.
For the zero-cost a / unit-cost b metric, the checker uses edge
inequalities that telescope to a lower bound, and a separate known
literal reset attaining the whole-set bound; it makes no uniqueness
claim for zero-cost Bellman equations. Eight corruptions are rejected.
These finite controls are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** after the literal
checker capture; the every-n theorem is paper, not a finite inference.

Completed independent scope:11 parameters,88 caps,66 finite entered
square failures,1550308 positive-cost Bellman edge controls,65504
zero-cost lower-potential edge controls,127934 literal particle/letter
controls, and rejection of all eight corruptions. The whole entered
cap2 costs at n4..14 are11,20,33,48,67,88,113,140,171,204,241.

The exact all-n weighted cost for the ba/bba pool is not proved here.
The earlier observed formula is only an exploratory pattern and is
unneeded for this obstruction. A possible square theorem for the
almost-circular class must exploit returns whose lengths grow with n,
or work directly in the original letters. A universal reduction from
general synchronizing DFAs to that class is also still OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-class-reset-pressure"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-class-reset-pressure--direct-pressure-on-the-stronger-full-class-reset-proposal"></a>
### Direct pressure on the stronger full-class reset proposal

Date: 2026-09-30. The general proposal

    reset_A(C) <= (|C|-1)(n-1)

for a congruence class in a strongly connected synchronizing DFA is
**OPEN**. These searches attack it directly, rather than interpreting
first compression as full reset. There is no new unrestricted bound,
publication-priority claim, or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim.

<a id="direct-attack-class-reset-pressure--fixed-two-class-protocol"></a>
#### Fixed two-class protocol

The states are C={0,...,h-1} and O={h,...,h+t-1}, t>=h.
Letter a injects C into O and cycles all t states of O. Letter b
permutes C and maps O onto C. Every candidate has this congruence
and is strongly connected: from C one reaches the whole O cycle,
and b reaches all C states. Synchronization is checked exactly.

In this protocol, **PROVED**:

    rt(A) = 1 + reset_A(C).

Indeed b maps Q onto C. Before the first b, a nonempty a-prefix
maps Q onto O; an a-only word cannot synchronize. The first b
therefore maps the current full image onto C, whether or not there
was an a-prefix. Removing that prefix never increases length.

The C++ search builds the COMPLETE subset graph reachable from C,
then computes reverse distances from its singletons. Any graph
reaching the vertex cap is rejected. It mutates the injection,
the C permutation and the O color map, with fixed deterministic
restarts. This is an adaptive sample, not an isomorphism cover.

Two streams propose 120000 and 1000000 candidates, respectively,
with seeds 20261016/20261017 and caps 30000/150000. The first has
twelve profiles with h=3,...,5; the second has twenty-one profiles
with h=3,...,10. Their counts are 119483 and 990818 strongly
connected synchronizing accepted evaluations. There are no capped
evaluations and no violations of the proposal. Repeated candidates
are possible: 1110301 accepted evaluations are not that many
different automata.

<a id="direct-attack-class-reset-pressure--an-exact-equality-certificate-with-h3"></a>
#### An exact equality certificate with h=3

For h=3,t=7,n=10, the retained automaton is

    a = [8,7,4,4,5,6,7,8,9,3]
    b = [1,0,2,0,2,2,2,1,0,1].

Its complete C-image graph has 35 vertices, and independent
ordinary-set BFS gives

    reset_A(C)=18=(h-1)(n-1),   rt(A)=19<81.

A shortest class reset is a^6 b a^4 b a^5 b. Consequently the
strict version of the proposal, even when restricted to h>=3, is
**REFUTED**. The non-strict general proposal remains **OPEN**.
No minimal-state claim is made; the earlier h=2 equality family
already rules out a universal strict version without that restriction.

<a id="direct-attack-class-reset-pressure--independent-checks-and-reproducibility"></a>
#### Independent checks and reproducibility

check_class_reset_pressure.py uses ordinary sets and a separate
forward BFS, checks the displayed word and exact distance, verifies
strong connectivity from each state, and derives the full reset
threshold from the protocol above. It verifies all 13/23 retained
records in 1731/36253 subset vertices and rejects three corruptions
per file. This verifies the saved certificates, not the whole
adaptive search history or the general proposal.

class_reset_native.py captures compiler version, literal build/run
argv, stdout, stderr and hashes. replay_fiber_continuation.py
rebuilds if necessary and reproduces BOTH streams, comparing the
whole parsed JSON with the frozen outputs. It also replays the
3000-alphabet bijective-return sample. All three comparisons pass.
The literal replay children are saved in
data/fiber_continuation_replays.json. The explicit --profile-mode
small switch reconstructs the original twelve-profile protocol;
it is not asserted to have been present in the historical argv.

The combinatorial terminal-kernel improvement is proved separately
in [Terminal kernels refine Frankl compression at every rank](#direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl). It does not establish this full-class
proposal: summing independent worst-rank compression costs still
loses the compatibility of successive images. The two-copy embedding
in [Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class](#direct-attack-profile-class-compression) shows why a general proof of this
proposal would be a major quadratic advance.

<a id="direct-attack-commuting-unit-policy-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-commuting-unit-policy-obstruction--commuting-permutations-do-not-rescue-shortest-phase-policy-optimality"></a>
### Commuting permutations do not rescue shortest-phase policy optimality

Status: **REFUTED**, exact ordinary ALL-SOURCE and reverse BFS audit.

The attempted weakening of [Exact policy for one permutation and unitary letters](#direct-attack-single-permutation-unit-policy) was:
"Replace one permutation by any set of mutually commuting permutations,
retaining unitary letters; then the GLOBAL P still equals rt."

Six states suffice. Use letters in this order:

    a=[0,1,2,3,5,4], b=[1,2,3,0,5,4],
    c=[4,1,2,3,4,5], d=[0,1,2,3,1,5].

a and b commute; c is (0->4), d is (4->1). The DFA is SC, synchronizing,
and completely reachable (63 nonempty images). Exact rt=8, P=9; a
shortest reset is c d b c b b c d, ending at1. Full singleton reaching
lengths are [11,8,9,10,10,11], while G is [12,9,10,11,10,11]. Every
singleton is worse than the global rt, so choosing another endpoint
does not eliminate the policy failure. W is [12,9,10,11,13,14].

The critical target S={0,1,4} (mask19) has e(S)=2. Its ONLY winning
larger actual parent is T={0,1,4,5} (mask51), via forward d a. Since
G(T)=5, G(S)=7. But its exact Q-reaching distance is6, attained by
c d b c b b. Parent {0,1,4} then wins the one-letter c phase into
{1,4}; that pair wins the one-letter d phase into {1}, giving P=9.

In inverse reading, the globally optimal prefix for mask19 waits for
b^-2 then c^-1, a three-letter expansion. The shortest expansion uses
a^-1 then d^-1, a different two-letter route with a more expensive tail.
Commutativity does not put the shorter permutation route on the original
path. Consequently the unit insertion in the one-permutation proof cannot
be made at the shorter route without paying for additional permutations.

State minimum6 is certified ONLY in the stated restricted class of TWO
distinct commuting permutation letters plus one to three distinct unit
letters: complete labeled covers at n2..5 test 3,246,14304,486000 inputs,
accepting 3,171,7536,161940, with no P>rt. Ordinary set BFS audits every
small accepted input n<=4; all486000 n5 inputs are checked with two
native algorithms. The counter has ordinary ALL-SOURCE and reverse BFS
e/G/W/forward arrays, and ALL critical parent ties are enumerated.
No state minimum across arbitrary numbers of commuting generators or
arbitrary unit alphabets is asserted. No general alphabet-minimum claim.

The original n6 adaptive search terminated on its first refutation; it
was not a complete cover. Its initial terminal stdout was not persisted,
and that exploratory count is not reported as a durable exhaustive result.
The saved counter and complete smaller covers have literal reproduction
commands, child stdout/stderr, summaries and independent checks.

This does not refute Cerny: rt8<25. It also does not refute a possible
cycle-orbit-sensitive EXTENSION bound for commuting PU alphabets (OPEN).
It refutes the proposed exact policy compatibility bridge. Known
immediate-letter greediness for all PU automata is not shortest-phase
greediness; Szykula--Vorel's DLT2016 Lemma5 remains valid.

<a id="direct-attack-complete-union-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-complete-union-obstruction--complete-reachability-and-modular-capacity-do-not-repair-union-transfer"></a>
### Complete reachability and modular capacity do not repair union transfer

**REFUTED, state-minimal n=4 over ANY alphabet:** even in a completely
reachable binary DFA, e(S union T)<min(e(S),e(T)) can hold for a proper
union. Thus neither availability of all larger images nor modularity of
rho suffices to transfer the proper-extension union argument to our
image-extension policy.

    a=[2,0,0,1], b=[1,2,3,0],
    S={0,3}, T={2,3}, U={0,2,3},
    e(S)=3, e(T)=3, e(U)=2.

All 15 nonempty subsets are actual images, with independently checked
reach words. The word aa has Q aa={0,2}, strictly inside U. Hence
pre_aa(U)=Q, while pre_aa(S)={1,2} and pre_aa(T)={0,3}. It image-extends
U and neither component. The independently exact costs also show that no
OTHER word of length <=2 can image-extend either component. The obstruction
therefore defeats both same-word and bounded-cost transfer.

At n<=3 every proper union has size <=2. If one component is the union,
transfer is immediate. Otherwise its nonempty components are two disjoint
singletons. If pre_w(U) contains a larger reachable image, its cardinality
is at least 3, so one singleton fiber has size >=2. In a completely
reachable automaton any two states in that fiber form a reachable image,
and the same word image-extends that singleton. This proves minimum n4
over arbitrary alphabets. The fixed-cycle binary scans at n2/3 are checks,
not the basis for arbitrary-alphabet minimality.

The distinction from [Ferens--Szykula, Lemma 3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.05956)
is the onto condition. Their properly extending word has a larger
predecessor mapping ONTO the union. Here aa omits state 3 of U. In a
completely reachable DFA rho is cardinality and therefore modular, but
that omitted overlap still gives a negative intersection contribution.
The cited proper-extension lemma remains valid. The precise route requiring
union transfer for maps INTO an image is unavailable even in this stronger
reachability class. This example is not a counterexample to the global
policy square or to Cerny; priority of the specific policy obstruction OPEN.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--a-compatible-shortest-phase-chain-despite-binary-quadratic-local-extension"></a>
### A compatible shortest-phase chain despite binary quadratic local extension

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for the direct binary family:

    P<=p^2+p-ceil(p/2)-1 for EVERY p>=3;
    P=5 for p=2.

P is the GLOBAL best actual-image policy in [Shortest image-extension policy: a surviving compatibility target](#direct-attack-image-extension-policy);
ALL phases constructed below are genuinely shortest, with their actual
parents and full original-letter costs verified. Exact arbitrary-p
equality P=p^2+p-ceil(p/2)-1 is only **CONJECTURED**. It is separately
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** in five complete scopes p2..6. Priority
**OPEN**; no **FORMALLY VERIFIED** statement. General Cerny and the
unrestricted policy square remain **OPEN**.

This is a positive compatibility result for the binary quadratic local
obstruction, not a universal proof. It improves that family's charged
reset upper bound by one for p>=3. Its e(T)=n^2/8+O(n) theorem remains
valid: a best compatible chain need not use that particular expensive target.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--notation-and-actual-membership-before-selecting-any-parent"></a>
#### Notation and actual membership, before selecting any parent

Use the original a,b,C,D,E,pi,p,s,k from
[Direct binary quadratic actual-image extension](#direct-attack-direct-binary-quadratic-image-extension), with n=2p+1, s=floor(p/2),
k=ceil(p/2). On E the CHARGED words d=a^(p+1)b and f=a^p b remove
one C-tail point and one D-prefix point respectively, fixing the other part.
Define, for the ranges used below,

    B_j={C_0,...,C_(j-1),D_0,...,D_(j-1),D_p}, |B_j|=2j+1;
    H_j(t)={C_t,...,C_(t+j-1),D_t,...,D_(t+j-1)}, |H_j(t)|=2j.

The following original whole words reach them EXACTLY:

    Q b d^(s-j) f^(k-j-1) a^((j+1)(p+1)-1)=B_j,  1<=j<=k-1;
    Q b d^(s-j) f^(k-j) a^(j(p+1)+t)=H_j(t),       2<=j<=s, t=k-j.

After the two shrinking powers their image has C-tail size j and
D-prefix size j+1 or j; the two a-cycle residues give the displayed
targets. Every exponent is nonnegative in its stated range. These are
actual-membership certificates only. They are NOT charged as free
histories in the later reset construction: the later chain explicitly
transports Q into each parent and pays its own words.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--a-general-safe-preimage-lower-certificate"></a>
#### A general safe-preimage lower certificate

Let a be a permutation and b any transformation. For an arbitrary set X
write X_t=X a^(-t), meaning full preimages by t copies of the ORIGINAL a.
If

    b^-1 X_t is contained in X_t for 0<=t<L,

then EVERY inverse word with fewer than L copies of a has preimage of X
contained in X_t, where t is its total a-count. This follows inductively:
a^-1 takes a contained set into X_(t+1); monotonicity of full preimages
and the assumed containment keep every b^-1 step inside X_t.
Thus no such word can contain a larger actual image, since |X_t|=|X|.
An extending word also needs a b, as a alone preserves cardinality.
Consequently any actual-image extension costs at least L+1.
This lemma uses SET preimages, not an inverse b word. Shrinking steps,
strict arrivals, and arbitrary orders of a,b are all included.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--exact-shortest-phases-for-the-odd-and-even-targets"></a>
#### Exact shortest phases for the odd and even targets

For B_j with 2j+1<p, set L=p-k+j+1. Direct inspection gives

    b^-1(B_j a^(-t)) contained in B_j a^(-t), 0<=t<L.

For t<=j the paired interval wraps at zero and its needed D_p fiber
is present. For j<t<L, the sole unpaired D endpoint has coordinate
p-t+j>=k, so it is NOT a b-output. Its deletion introduces no point.
Every selected b-output has its whole fiber already present. This also
covers t=0, where B_j is already a union of full b-fibers.
The general certificate yields e(B_j)>=L+1.

At t=L, the unpaired D endpoint first reaches k-1, a selected output.
The full preimage contains the ACTUAL parent

    H_(j+1)(k-j-1),

whose cardinality 2j+2 is larger than |B_j|. The word b a^L maps this
parent into the D-only subset {D_p,D_0,...,D_(j-1)} of B_j. Hence

    e(B_j)=p-k+j+2, with parent H_(j+1)(k-j-1).         (1)

If that full preimage has an extra point, we retain the actual smaller
parent H; nonactual supersets are not substituted into the policy.

For H_j(t), t=k-j and 2j<p, its paired coordinates are positive before
t inverse a's. Every b^-1 step fixes the corresponding paired set.
At t inverse a's the pair interval begins at zero and its b-preimage
adds D_p, giving the ACTUAL B_j. The same certificate and matching
word b a^t therefore give

    e(H_j(k-j))=k-j+1, with parent B_j.                 (2)

Here too the forward arrival can be a strict D-only subset. Actual
membership, shortestness and cardinality growth are separate facts.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--the-terminal-p-image-phase"></a>
#### The terminal p-image phase

When p=2s+1, the terminal image is B_s, the canonical target in the
direct binary proof. Its sole larger actual source is Q, and that proof
gives the exact terminal word b a^M, M=2(s+1)^2-1.

When p=2s, the terminal image is H_s(0), also of size p. Its sole
larger actual source is Q. Its projected coordinate target is {0,...,s-1}.
The first-stall proof gives at least kp+1 a's. For t=kp+u, 1<=u<s,
the complementary initial coordinate i=p-1-u is in the C-selected part;
its repeated-stall inequality requires t>=t+s+1, impossible. Thus at
least kp+s=s(p+1) a's are needed. The word b a^(s(p+1)) reaches H_s(0)
exactly, proving

    e(H_s(0))=1+s(p+1).                                (3)

Both terminal costs are genuinely shortest into-image transport; neither
designates an arbitrary reset prefix as a shortest phase.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--one-compatible-whole-chain-and-its-sum"></a>
#### One compatible whole chain and its sum

For p>=3 start at singleton D_0. Its cost-one phase b has ACTUAL parent
B_1. Then alternate

    B_j -> H_(j+1)(k-j-1) -> B_(j+1),

using (1),(2), stopping the alternation as soon as cardinality p is reached.
The terminal target is H_s(0) for even p and B_s for odd p. Use (3) or
the canonical odd terminal word to reach parent Q. All arrows are inverse
policy arrows: prepend their actual forward words in REVERSE phase order.
Every word maps its entire parent inside its child. Therefore their
composition sends the single common full-Q image into D_0, even when
intermediate images are strict inside the nominal policy targets.

For odd p, each complete alternating pair costs p+2; there are s-1 such
pairs, a seed cost one, and terminal cost 2(s+1)^2. For even p, there
are s-2 complete pairs of cost p+2, one final odd phase of cost p+1,
the seed, and terminal cost 1+s(p+1). Both sums are exactly

    p^2+p-k-1 < (2p)^2=(n-1)^2.                        (4)

The even sum is used only for s>=2. At p2 use actual pair {C_0,D_0}
as the cost-one b parent of D_0, then the shortest whole-Q phase baaa
of cost four. Direct evaluation of all words through length three
excludes earlier entry to that pair. The common policy word baaa b
costs five, agreeing with its exact reset threshold.

Equation (4) proves P at most this compatible cost for every p>=3.
It does NOT prove that no different chain costs less. The arbitrary-p
equality suggested by the finite values remains CONJECTURED.

<a id="direct-attack-direct-binary-compatible-policy--independent-verification-and-boundary"></a>
#### Independent verification and boundary

`check_direct_binary_policy_chain.py` imports no generator, previous
checker, native solver or policy algorithm. It uses only the 69 retained
parameter values, reconstructs all original rows, and proves membership
by original-row composition with FULL charged exponents. Across these
controls through n2049 it verifies 4027 whole actual-image membership
words and 743444 safe-preimage containment/fixing controls. Every proposed
parent word is checked, and the ENTIRE common image chain is composed
without resetting to its nominal target at intermediate phases.
Twenty-three controls p2..24 additionally evaluate every original letter
of the complete concatenated reset literally.

Five complete actual-image scopes p2..6 (1147 images) have independently
computed per-target ordinary full-preimage BFS, collecting ALL shortest
larger-parent ties and solving G by descending cardinality. They visit
22746 inverse vertices and give P=5,9,17,26,38, respectively, matching
the upper construction. At p5,rt25<P26; at p6,rt36<P38. Thus even this
binary obstruction's shortest-image policy is not asserted equal to rt.
Four deliberately corrupted chain fields are rejected.

The new result is continued check 100, with the 184 regeneration commands
unchanged. The 99-check checkpoint is preserved verbatim; only this new
literal checker is continued. No full 100-check rerun, formal proof
kernel, general policy-square theorem or complete Cerny proof is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-extremal-arbitrary-letter-search"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-extremal-arbitrary-letter-search--every-single-arbitrary-letter-on-the-retained-near-extremal-bases"></a>
### Every single arbitrary letter on the retained near-extremal bases

**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED, finite scope only.** For the 16 retained binary
n5 automata with rt>=14 and four retained binary n6 automata with rt>=23,
EVERY single added transformation is scored exactly: 16*5^5+4*6^6=236624
cases. Identity, constant and duplicated transformations are included.
None raises P over its base value, and none violates the policy square.
This extends the earlier 76676 generated-map additions to arbitrary maps;
it does not reinstate general alphabet monotonicity, refuted already at n4.
Arbitrary multiple additions and all ternary inputs are not covered.

The generator enumerates each map in product(range(n),repeat=n) and uses
the exact sparse full-image solver. Source rows and their summary SHA256,
complete (P,rt) histograms, maxima, added maps and 40 base/peak arrays are
saved. Generation retains literal argv, stdout/stderr and timing.
Adding letters preserves the known base reset, so these inputs cannot be
Cerny counterexamples; the stronger image-policy conjecture is what is
being attacked. Exact rt is independently recorded, not inferred from P.

check_extremal_arbitrary re-enumerates EVERY addition with the separately
audited FULL-CUBE transport kernel, checking each individual (P,rt) against
the sparse kernel before comparing the entire histogram and all maxima/counters.
Forty base/peak e/G/W/forward arrays additionally have
ordinary ALL-SOURCE BFS checks. There is no claim that ordinary BFS scores
every addition. The source hashes and base-membership records are checked.
The short-reset subset count is independently matched; its square guarantee
also follows from [An elementary reset-length-dependent bound for every seed tie](#direct-attack-short-reset-seed-budget). No universal theorem, minimum
counterexample result, Lean theorem or novelty claim follows from this run.

<a id="direct-attack-extremal-shortcut-search"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-extremal-shortcut-search--exhaustive-single-shortcut-attack-on-retained-near-extremal-bases"></a>
### Exhaustive single-shortcut attack on retained near-extremal bases

The n4 and infinite shortcut obstructions show why ordinary alphabet
monotonicity cannot filter a global policy counterexample. We therefore
exhausted ALL generated transformations as individual new unit-cost labels
for the 16 retained binary n5 classes with rt>=14 and the four n6 classes
with rt>=23. Original base rows and source hashes are frozen in each record.

There are 22,136 n5 additions and 54,540 n6 additions, 76,676 total.
Every resulting DFA remains SC and synchronizing with the same monoid and
image family. None has P larger than its original base. The two n5 maximum
policy values are 16 (one base has rt=15); the n6 maxima are 25,25,23,23.
Full histograms of exact (P,rt) values, monoid sizes, peak transformations,
actual peak words and captured generation argv/stdout are retained.

These are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED finite negative results**, not a
new monotonicity theorem, characterization or unrestricted square proof.
They cover every SINGLE generated-map addition to these 20 specific bases.
They do not cover all ternary automata, larger states, or simultaneous
multi-shortcut additions. Since P is nonmonotone, individual robustness
does not justify a sequence of alphabet additions.

The checker independently enumerates each entire transformation closure
and replays every score histogram with the audited unrestricted native
solver. Forty base/peak policy certificates have independent ordinary-set
inverse BFS and Bellman checks. All 76,676 scores are not individually
recomputed with the ordinary-set checker; that narrower boundary is explicit.
No Lean result or priority claim.

<a id="direct-attack-extremal-shortcut-search--two-permutationunit-defect-shortcuts"></a>
#### Two permutation/unit-defect shortcuts

The follow-up uses the same 20 bases and adds every pair of DISTINCT
generated transformations of rank >=n-1, excluding the original two labels

and 1767876 n6 pairs, 2444342 total. No policy increase or square violation

Original single-shortcut data remain preserved in their own directory.

check_extremal_shortcuts --pairs independently reconstructs the closures,
selects the eligible transformations, and replays every pair's score
