<a id="direct-attack-fold-global-policy-equality"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-fold-global-policy-equality--the-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction-still-has-an-optimal-global-policy"></a>
### The quadratic image-extension obstruction still has an optimal global policy

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** for EVERY r>=1 in the fold/path
family of [Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction). Priority **OPEN**;
bounded audits are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**, with no formal kernel.
General Cerny and the unrestricted policy-square target remain **OPEN**.

Let P be the best complete inverse image-policy cost: every phase must
use a word attaining e(S), then choose an actual larger image R contained
in that word's full preimage. Every complete chain composes to a reset,
so P>=rt. We now construct a permitted chain with

    P=rt=r(r+1)/2.                                     (1)

This is not obtained by simply designating the earlier reset word's
arbitrary phases as shortest ones. Several of those phases are not shortest.

<a id="direct-attack-fold-global-policy-equality--reachability-and-a-tight-terminal-entry-class"></a>
#### Reachability and a tight terminal-entry class

Every k-subset with 1<=k<=r is an actual image. Start with Qb of rank r;
when k>=2, use S_n to place exactly two of its points in one b-fiber and
the other k-2 in distinct different fibers, then apply b. This drops the
rank by exactly one. Permutations then reach every subset of each attained
size. The adjacent swaps generate S_n as actual words; this assertion is
about membership, not a zero-cost reset construction. Only Q has rank >r.

For every target T of size AT MOST r containing BOTH 0 and r, there is a word entering T
from Q of length F(Q)-F(T), where F is the inverse potential in the
quadratic-obstruction proof. To see this, use full preimages from T.
There is initially a left hole, since T contains r and |T|<=r.
Let i be the LARGEST missing left position.
Then i>=1, positions i+1,...,r are occupied, and 0 is occupied. Apply
the inverse swaps tau_i,...,tau_(r-1); they move the hole to r, each
increasing F by one. The following full b-preimage copies the left half,
restores r because 0 remains occupied, and increases F by one. Repeat
until the left half is full; the last b-preimage is Q. This is one
literal reverse-word construction, paying EVERY swap and b.

If |T|=r, its only larger actual source is Q. The potential lower bound
therefore matches the construction and proves

    e(T)=G(T)=F(Q)-F(T)   for |T|=r, {0,r} subset T.     (2)

<a id="direct-attack-fold-global-policy-equality--shortest-intermediate-phases"></a>
#### Shortest intermediate phases

For 1<=j<=r define the doubled actual subsets, when their size permits:

    A_j={0} union {r-j+1,...,r-1},
    B_j=A_j union (A_j+r),        |B_j|=2j.

For 2j<r,

    e(B_j)=j+1.                                        (3)

Lower bound: a permutation alone never increases the full-preimage
cardinality. A b-preimage has size twice the number of occupied left
positions. To obtain a preimage of size >2j, some b step must therefore
be preceded by a set with >j occupied left positions. b never changes
left occupancy. Initially the left holes of B_j lie at positions
1,...,r-j. Track individual holes under the original swaps. A net
increase of left occupancy forces at least one of these INITIAL holes
to leave the left interval. Its closest possible starting position is
r-j, so exiting across the boundary at r needs at least j original
swaps. Holes later created by exports cannot erase this necessity.
At least one b is also needed, proving cost >=j+1. This argument allows
all intermediate shrinkage and any number of earlier b steps.

Upper bound: the actual word

    u_j=b tau_(r-1) tau_(r-2)...tau_(r-j)               (4)

has full preimage B_j u_j^-1=B_(j+1). Indeed its inverse swaps move
the highest initial left hole to r; the b-preimage duplicates the
enlarged left set. This preimage has 2j+2 points. Since 2j<r, it
contains an actual source of size min(2j+2,r)>2j, proving (3).
Strict containment of the target image is allowed by the policy.

<a id="direct-attack-fold-global-policy-equality--the-entire-compatible-chain"></a>
#### The entire compatible chain

For r=1 the one-letter reset is already optimal. For r>=2 start at
{0}, whose e=1 is attained by b with actual parent B_1={0,r}.
For each 2j+2<=r, use (4) to take the actual parent B_(j+1).
If r is even, the chain reaches B_(r/2), an r-image containing 0,r;
finish with the shortest entering word (2), with parent Q.
If r is odd, the last small target is B_((r-1)/2). Use its shortest
phase (4), then choose an r-subset T of B_((r+1)/2) by deleting ONE
zero-weight right point. T retains 0 and r and all positive-weight
points. Finish by (2). In both cases these are valid actual parents.

The potential values telescope exactly:

    F(B_j)=r+1+j(j+1)/2,
    F(B_(j+1))-F(B_j)=j+1=|u_j|.

Deleting the zero-weight point in the odd case does not change F.
The seed phase gains one; the terminal phase costs F(Q)-F(T). Thus
the whole cost is F(Q)-F({0})=r(r+1)/2. Every phase is shortest by
(2)--(3), not merely cheap. Since P>=rt, equation (1) follows.

This proves that an unbounded quadratic LOCAL image-extension cost
can coexist with exact globally optimal shortest-phase synchronization.
It does not prove an unrestricted P=rt statement; earlier policy
counterexamples remain valid. The missing general square mechanism
still concerns which compatible images and phases can be chosen.

check_fold_policy_chains.py independently verifies the original-letter
preimages and full terminal words on all 69 retained fold parameters,
plus complete bounded searches for the asserted shortest phase costs.
No old policy solver or generator is imported. Its controls do not
replace the arbitrary-parameter hole-tracking and telescoping proofs.

The size condition in the terminal lemma is essential to this statement:
the NONACTUAL target L union {r} has potential F(Q) but is not Q when
r>=2, so an empty word cannot enter it. This failed overgeneralization
was identified and removed during proof audit; every terminal target
used in the actual policy has size exactly r.

<a id="direct-attack-full-history-boolean-capacity"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-full-history-boolean-capacity--boolean-capacity-of-a-shortest-full-inverse-history"></a>
### Boolean capacity of a shortest full inverse history

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper)** for ANY synchronizing finite DFA
and ANY globally shortest original reset word. These bounds do not
prove the general square. General Cerny and the unrestricted cost/rank
hypothesis remain **OPEN**. The cube counting mechanism is elementary
and follows the Boolean rank architecture already attributed to
[Szykula2026, Section2.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.24245). No novelty or
**FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim is made for this refinement.

Let w have length L and reset to q. Let S_i be the full preimage of
{q} under the length-i suffix of w, i0..L. Thus S_0={q}, S_L=Q,
and EVERY original-letter intermediate is included. Put

    W=span_R{[S_i]: 0<=i<=L}, d=dim W,
    V(W)=W intersect {0,1}^n,
    c=number of standard basis vectors e_p belonging to W.

All S_i are distinct: a repeated full-preimage set lets us delete the
intervening factor and still reset. No S_i with i>0 is a singleton:
if S_i={p}, the complementary length-(L-i) prefix already resets to p,
contradicting GLOBAL shortestness. This second assertion need not hold
for a word shortest only among resets to a specified q.

W contains both [Q] and e_q, so c>=1. The full history uses none of
the other c-1 singleton vertices or the zero vertex. Consequently

    L <= |V(W)|-c-1.                                    (1)

<a id="direct-attack-full-history-boolean-capacity--a-gap-below-the-full-cube"></a>
#### A gap below the full cube

Select d state-coordinate functionals which are linearly independent
on W. Projection onto these coordinates is an isomorphism W->R^d.
Every Boolean vertex projects to a DISTINCT point of {0,1}^d, so
|V(W)|<=2^d. Every remaining state coordinate is a linear form in
the d selected coordinates.

If one such form uses two nonzero coefficients a,b, fix all the other
selected bits. On these two bits its four values are

    x, x+a, x+b, x+a+b.

At most THREE of them belong to {0,1}. If all four belonged, the
nonzero differences a,b would each be +/-1. Equal signs make the
sum differ by2; opposite signs give both x-1 and x+1. Neither is
possible inside {0,1}. Partitioning the projected cube into these
four-point faces therefore gives

    |V(W)| <= 3*2^(d-2).                                (2)

Otherwise every state coordinate uses at most one nonzero coefficient.
Since [Q] belongs to W, each coefficient is1 and no form is zero.
Hence the original coordinates are copies of the d selected ones:
W is EXACTLY the space constant on the blocks of a partition of Q
into d nonempty blocks. Conversely such a space has2^d Boolean
vertices. Thus there is an exact dichotomy:

* partition space: |V(W)|=2^d;
* every other space: |V(W)|<=3*2^(d-2).

No automaton invariance of W is assumed or inferred. The letters used
at different history positions need not preserve the whole space.

For a partition space, c is its number of singleton blocks. There
are d-c other blocks of size at least2, so n>=2d-c. Combining this
with c>=1 and (1) proves

    L <= 2^d-1-max(1,2d-n)       if W is a partition space,
    L <= 3*2^(d-2)-2             otherwise.              (3)

For n=d, W is the whole state space and necessarily the partition
space with c=n. For n>1 one has d>=2, since e_q and [Q] are independent.

The factor3/4 in (2) is sharp for REAL spaces containing both [Q]
and a singleton: at d>=4, n=d+1, use the hyperplane

    x_0+x_1=x_2+x_3.

Exactly six of the sixteen first-four bit patterns satisfy it;
the remaining n-4 coordinates are free. Thus |V(W)|=3*2^(d-2),
and c=d-3>=1. This is a SPACE example, not a realization by the
full history of an optimal DFA word.

<a id="direct-attack-full-history-boolean-capacity--a-proved-low-dimension-part-of-the-open-cost-hypothesis"></a>
#### A proved low-dimension part of the open cost hypothesis

Equation (3) proves

    L <= (n-1)(d-1)                                      (4)

for EVERY shortest full history with d<=3, at ANY n. For d=2 the
partition bounds are1 atn2 and2 atn>=3. For d=3 they are4 atn3,
5 atn4 and6 atn>=5; the nonpartition bound is4. Each is within
(4). At n1 the empty reset has L=0 and d=1.

It also proves (4) for d=4 at EVERY n>=5. The partition bounds
are12 atn5,13 atn6 and14 atn>=7, and the nonpartition bound is10.
These are all within3(n-1). The case n4/d4 is the ordinary four-
state Cerny theorem and is NOT newly proved by (3).

More generally, define B(n,d) as the larger of the two applicable
right sides in (3), omitting the nonpartition option when n=d.
If B(n,d)<L, no such history rank is possible. This allows the
adversarial cost/rank search to omit cases already excluded by
Boolean capacity rather than count them as new evidence for (4).

The remaining difficult ranges include n6/d5, where the partition
bound is27 and the nonpartition bound is22, while (4) permits only20.
[Hyperplane support and actual-letter guards of a full history](#direct-attack-history-hyperplane-and-guards) subsequently refines the nonpartition
bound to21; its nonbalanced-support branch is at most14. A binary
partition history whose BOTH letters fail to preserve its span is at
most20. The balanced saturation and the one-preserving-letter case
are not settled by those paper counting bounds.
At n7/d5 and n8/d5 the nonpartition range is already within (4),
but the partition bounds28/29 exceed24/28. The full d=n cases still
include the original Cerny problem. No rankwise minima, free returns
or unproved control of a COMMON original word is used here.

Independent finite controls exhaust rational four-point faces, Boolean
vertices of the recorded real spaces, and integer boundary cases.
They corroborate the paper argument, not an unrestricted DFA theorem
by enumeration. The focused ALL-shortest-path pressure uses these
capacity cuts, finite-field subspaces, and rational candidate rechecks;
its raw negative results remain EXPLORATORY until independently audited.

The finite-field rank is exact on these scopes, not merely a numerical
heuristic. For an h-by-h Boolean matrix D, augment it with a first
row/column of1 and lower block J-2D. Subtracting the first row from
the others shows that the augmented determinant is(-2)^h det D.
Its +/-1 rows have norm sqrt(h+1), so Hadamard gives

    |det D| <= (h+1)^((h+1)/2)/2^h.

For EVERY h<=16 the square of this bound is below1000003^2, as the
independent integer controls check; trial division verifies the prime.
Thus a nonzero Boolean minor cannot vanish modulo1000003. Rational
and field ranks agree for ANY number of Boolean rows with <=16
columns. Equal field spans from two such histories also have equal
real spans, by applying this rank equality to their union. This
justifies subspace memoization in the focused search, but does not
replace a complete independent audit of its implementation or scope.

Completed exact finite controls:11132 rational four-point faces,
66 partition spaces (16332 Boolean vertices),11 nonpartition spaces
(24564 vertices),12281 arithmetic boundary cases throughn4096,
16 minor-dimension inequalities and999 prime trial divisors. Ten
corruptions are rejected.
The two raw pressure stages covered7814 non-baseline neighbors of the
four saved n6 extremals/C7..C12, then ALL90834 exact distance-two
C7..C12 neighbors. These stages are disjoint within their labeled
scopes:98648 inputs,68664 synchronizing,65634 capacity exclusions,
3030 ALL-shortest-path searches, no counter and no timeout. They are
archived separately as EXPLORATORY, outside the mathematical checker;
the counts do not imply ALL-automata or arbitrary-alphabet coverage.

<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction--exact-quadratic-bridge-costs-for-every-fixed-rank-excess"></a>
### Exact quadratic bridge costs for every fixed rank excess

**PROVED (paper); novelty OPEN.** For every k,m,h with 2<=k<m and h>=1,
let n=kmh. In the binary circular Cerny DFA on Z/nZ, put

    qa=q+1 mod n,  (n-1)b=0,  qb=q otherwise;
    S={0,kh,2kh,...,(m-1)kh};
    F_j={jmh,...,(j+1)mh-1},  0<=j<k.

There is an actual rank-k word u with precisely the fibers F_j, and S is
reachable from Q. The exact minimum bridge length is

    min{|v|: |Svu|<k} = (m-k)h*n+kh
                       = (m-k)n^2/(km)+n/m.                 (GB)

This generalizes the k=2,m=3 balanced obstruction. For every fixed k,m,
the length is quadratic. In particular even any fixed positive rank excess
m-k admits no universal linear bridge length. These are not counterexamples
to Cerny; the DFA itself has the familiar square-length reset word.

<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction--lower-bound-without-an-assumption-about-cyclic-order"></a>
#### Lower bound without an assumption about cyclic order

Track each original q in S through a word v. Let A count its a letters,
and B_q count the b letters applied when that trajectory is at n-1. Then

    qv = q+A+B_q mod n.

Suppose every B_q<=D=(m-k)h. Fix any target block F_j and subtract A from
it modulo n. This gives an interval of mh consecutive positions. Its first
kh positions contain exactly one original state q in S: S has spacing kh,
and kh divides n. Since q lies within the first kh positions and 0<=B_q<=D,
the position q+B_q lies within the same interval (offset at most
kh-1+D=mh-1). Thus qv is in F_j. This holds for every j, so no block is
missing. No order of the final images or distinctness assumption is used.

Every successful v consequently has B_q>=D+1 for some original q. After
each counted b hit that trajectory is at 0. Between successive counted hits
it needs at least n-1 a letters; other b letters leave it fixed. Before the
first hit it needs at least kh-1 a letters, the minimum over the original
states 0,kh,...,n-kh. These disjoint intervals and the counted hits give

    #a >= kh-1+D(n-1),   #b >= D+1,
    |v| >= kh+Dn.

The counting remains valid after trajectories merge: original labels are
still followed, and each B_q counts actual letter occurrences on that label.

<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction--matching-word-including-all-collision-cases"></a>
#### Matching word, including all collision cases

Take v=a^(kh-1)b(a^(n-1)b)^D. After the first b the image is

    {0} union {t kh-1 : 1<=t<m}.

The block a^(n-1)b acts on numerical states as x -> max(x-1,0).
After j blocks the image is

    {0} union {max(t kh-1-j,0) : 1<=t<m}.

At j=D its largest state is

    (m-1)kh-1-D = (k-1)mh-1.

It therefore misses F_(k-1), and hence |Svu|<=k-1. The length is kh+Dn,
matching the lower bound. The max formula handles m>=2k and duplicate images;
a proof based on preserved cyclic order would not cover those cases.

<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction--actual-words-and-general-hypotheses"></a>
#### Actual words and general hypotheses

The local transformation e_i=a^((n-1-i) mod n)b a^((i+1) mod n) sends i to
i+1 mod n and fixes all other states. For each F_j concatenate its internal
e_i in increasing cyclic order. The union of these merges maps F_j to its
last state, giving exactly the required k kernel fibers. The word length is
(n-k)(n+1), not asserted minimal. S is reached by the same local operation
inside the m cyclic intervals ending at the elements of S.

The letter a is a full cycle, so the DFA is strongly connected. The word
b(a^(n-1)b)^(n-2) resets it in (n-1)^2 letters: its image successively is
{0,...,n-2}, {0,...,n-3},...,{0}. All constructions use the original two
letters. In particular u is not treated as a unit-cost added letter.

<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction--what-this-rules-out-and-what-it-leaves-open"></a>
#### What this rules out, and what it leaves open

The linear-excess candidate (m-k+1)(n-k+1) is eventually false for every
fixed m>k>=2. For k=2,m=3 the optimal universal asymptotic order is quadratic:
Pin--Frankl compresses a 3-set within binom(n-1,2) letters and then a pair
within binom(n,2), totaling (n-1)^2; full synchronization of S suffices to
miss a block. The lower family gives n^2/6+O(n). No optimal coefficient is
claimed for arbitrary automata or partitions.

The obstruction controls a PRESCRIBED kernel. It does not rule out choosing
a different rank-k word, a different current image, or a coordinated reset
history that bypasses this bridge. Those choice costs remain the central
uncontrolled part of a general quadratic proof.

<a id="direct-attack-generalized-bridge-obstruction--independent-computational-audit"></a>
#### Independent computational audit

generalized_bridge.py stores exact Bellman distance potentials on every
nonempty subset of size at most m, a transition-closed universe. The
independent check_bridges.py verifies the complete universe, all Bellman
inequalities, a matching shortest witness, actual kernel fibers, and Q-to-S
reachability in ordinary set semantics. The finite audit is evidence about
those parameter instances; the all-parameter theorem is the proof above.
No new statement has been Lean-kernel verified.

<a id="direct-attack-harmonic-envelope-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-harmonic-envelope-obstruction--reachable-almost-full-subsets-attain-the-six-step-bound-at-unbounded-n"></a>
### Reachable almost-full subsets attain the six-step bound at unbounded n

**PROVED (paper, with explicit finite base); novelty OPEN.** There are
strongly connected synchronizing binary DFAs for infinitely many n, with a
Q-reachable subset S of size n-2 whose shortest compression length is exactly
6. Thus Pin--Frankl's corank-two bound is attained even at unbounded n.

In particular the tempting harmonic estimate

    c(S) <= ceil(n(n-|S|+1)/(|S|-1))                         (H1)

is **REFUTED**, with state-minimal witness n=8 over ANY alphabet. Summing
this estimate would give O(n^2 log n), so the failure blocks a concrete
subcubic route. The counterexample concerns actual reachable images, not
only arbitrary subsets.

<a id="direct-attack-harmonic-envelope-obstruction--explicit-eight-state-base"></a>
#### Explicit eight-state base

On Q0={0,...,7}, take

    a=(6,7,1,3,0,5,4,2), b=(0,4,2,7,5,6,3,4),
    S0={0,1,3,4,5,6}=Q0\{2,7}.

a has cycles (0,6,4), (1,7,2), and fixed states 3,5. The directed graph
is strongly connected. The following actual words suffice for the proof:

    Q0 (baabaa) = S0;
    |S0 (aabaab)|=5;
    Q0 (baababaababbaababbaababbbaabbbbabaaba)={0}.

To audit that no word of length <=5 compresses S0, write a set by its bitmask
sum_(q in S) 2^q. The sets first reached at each distance from S0 are:

| distance | masks |
|---|---|
| 0 | 123 |
| 1 | 249 |
| 2 | 125 |
| 3 | 237 |
| 4 | 126, 221 |
| 5 | 95, 187, 189, 252 |

Every listed set has size six and contains state 3. Direct multiplication by
the two displayed letters checks the table inductively. Together with the
six-letter word aabaab this proves c(S0)=6. The independent checker also
tests every one of the 63 words of length <=5, not just a selected path.

For n<=7 and every 2<=k<=n, the H1 right side is at least
binom(n-k+2,2), so Pin--Frankl proves H1 for all such n over arbitrary
alphabets. At n=8,k=6 it is ceil(24/5)=5. Hence n=8 is state minimal.

<a id="direct-attack-harmonic-envelope-obstruction--padding-that-preserves-the-bottleneck"></a>
#### Padding that preserves the bottleneck

Let n>=8 and 3 not divide d=n-7. Add N=n-8 states 8,...,n-1. The letter b
fixes each added state. Replace a's fixed point 3 by the cycle

    (3,8,9,...,n-1), of length d=N+1,

leaving its other cycles unchanged. Put S_n=Q_n\{2,7}=S0 union new states.

As long as the base image contains 3, applying a to an image enlarged by ALL
new states gives exactly its old a-image union all new states: the new cycle
is entirely occupied. Applying b always has that property. The base table
therefore lifts every word of length <=6, because its prefixes through length
5 contain 3. No word of length <=5 compresses S_n, and aabaab compresses it
to n-3. Thus c(S_n)=6 for every parameter of this family.

Strong connectivity is preserved. The only changed old edge is the a-loop
at 3; removing a self-loop cannot destroy paths among old states. New states
are connected to those old paths through the added cycle.

<a id="direct-attack-harmonic-envelope-obstruction--synchronization-and-reachability-are-not-assumed"></a>
#### Synchronization and reachability are not assumed

Choose L=d if d=1 mod 3, and L=2d if d=2 mod 3. Then L=0 mod d and
L=1 mod 3. The word a^L acts on Q0 exactly as the original a and fixes all
new states. Encode any old word by replacing every a with a^L and keeping b.
The encoded 37-letter reset word displayed above, call it V, maps Q0 to 0
and fixes every new state. The encoded baabaa maps Q_n precisely to S_n.

To reset Q_n, start with V, whose image is {0} union new states. Pick a new
state q still in the current image. Some a^j, 1<=j<=N, sends q to 3. The old
state 0 stays in its old three-cycle, and hence does not enter the new cycle.
Applying b sends 3 to old state 7 and fixes every remaining new state.
Applying V then resets all old images to 0, leaving the others unchanged.
Exactly one new image has been removed. Repeating this step at most N times
resets Q_n. This supplies an actual reset word; its length is not asserted
minimal, and its long length is not a lower bound on rt.

<a id="direct-attack-harmonic-envelope-obstruction--quantitative-limits-of-the-harmonic-route"></a>
#### Quantitative limits of the harmonic route

On these subsets, n(n-|S_n|+1)/(|S_n|-1)=3n/(n-3) tends to 3,
whereas c(S_n)=6. Therefore any uniform UNROUNDED envelope
c(S)<=C*n(n-|S|+1)/(|S|-1) needs C>=2. With a ceiling, every C<5/3 fails
for sufficiently large members of the family. A larger constant envelope,
which could still imply subcubic total cost, remains **OPEN**; this argument
does not refute it.

Eleven finite instances through n=60 retain the full transition rows, S,
actual reach/reset words and the shortest compression word. A separate set
checker verifies every short word, strong connectivity, full-Q reset and
reachability. The all-n proof is the simulation and padding argument above.
No new Lean theorem or new general upper bound follows from this family.

<a id="direct-attack-history-hyperplane-and-guards"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-history-hyperplane-and-guards--hyperplane-support-and-actual-letter-guards-of-a-full-history"></a>
### Hyperplane support and actual-letter guards of a full history

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper)**, with explicitly conditional
consequences below. General Cerny and the unrestricted ALL/SOME shortest
history cost/rank assertions remain **OPEN**. No novelty or formal proof
is claimed. These are refinements of [Boolean capacity of a shortest full inverse history](#direct-attack-full-history-boolean-capacity);
they count actual full histories and never assume their spans invariant.

Let w be ANY globally shortest reset, L its length, and W the real span
of ALL its singleton inverse suffix indicators, including the initial
singleton and Q. Write d=dim W and c=number of singleton vectors in W.
The earlier proof gives L<=|W intersect {0,1}^n|-c-1.

<a id="direct-attack-history-hyperplane-and-guards--a-codimension-one-refinement"></a>
#### A codimension-one refinement

Suppose d=n-1. Write W=ker alpha, alpha nonzero. Since W contains Q,
sum alpha_i=0; since it contains a singleton, some alpha_i=0.
Moreover its Boolean vertices span W, by the definition of the history.
Let s be the number of nonzero alpha_i. The singleton count is EXACTLY
c=n-s. Support one is impossible. Support two gives alpha proportional
to e_i-e_j, hence a partition space with one double block.

Support three cannot occur: its only zero-sum Boolean patterns on those
three coordinates are 000 and111. Their span has dimension one, whereas
the restriction of ker alpha has dimension two.

At support four, every proper nonempty zero-sum subset is a pair and
its complementary pair is also zero-sum. With at most one such pair
partition, the Boolean span has dimension at most two on the support,
too small for the required dimension three. Two distinct pair partitions
force alpha proportional, up to coordinate order, to (1,1,-1,-1).
Indeed their two perfect matchings form a four-cycle, and opposing
coefficients along each edge force equal absolute values. Conversely
this normal has six Boolean support patterns spanning its hyperplane.
Thus in this case

    |V(W)|=6*2^(n-4), c=n-4,
    L<=3*2^(d-2)-d+2.                                  (1)

At s>=5, flip the bits at negative coordinates. Zero-sum support
patterns become subsets of s POSITIVE weights with one fixed sum.
They form an antichain. The standard Sperner chain-count proof gives
at most binom(s,floor(s/2)) such subsets: a subset of size k belongs
to k!(s-k)! permutation chains; an antichain meets each chain at most
once. The middle-layer density is at most5/16 for every s>=5.
For completeness, the densities at5/6 equal5/16; the density at an
odd successor2k+1 is (2k+1)/(2k+2) times that at2k, and at2k+2 it
stays equal to the preceding odd density. Consequently

    |V(W)|<=5*2^(d-3), L<=5*2^(d-3)-2.                 (2)

For d>=4, (1) is the larger bound: their difference is
2^(d-3)-d+4>0. A nonpartition codimension-one history therefore has
L<=3*2^(d-2)-d+2. This is a SPACE/counting bound, not an assertion
that a DFA realizes the extremal count.

In the first unsupported proper-rank case n6/d5 it gives L<=21,
instead of22. More sharply, either the normal is (1,1,-1,-1,0,0)
up to scaling/order, or L<=14. The latter case has support five,
since a singleton rules out support six. At sign split1/4 there
are only empty/full patterns. At split2/3, let a,b be the two
positive weights. With three negative absolute weights summing a+b,
let T count their subsets summing a. Complementation counts equally
many subsets summing b. There are2+2T zero-sum patterns, and T<=3
by the same three-element antichain bound. Thus V has at most16
vertices, c=1, and L<=14. Equality L21 in the balanced case would
require visiting EVERY Boolean vertex except zero and the unused
free singleton. Its realizability is still **OPEN** here.

<a id="direct-attack-history-hyperplane-and-guards--necessary-guards-from-letters-that-do-not-preserve-a-partition-span"></a>
#### Necessary guards from letters that do not preserve a partition span

Now suppose W is the partition space on d blocks, c of them singletons.
For every original letter a that does NOT preserve W, choose states
p_a,q_a in one source block whose images land in DIFFERENT destination
blocks U_a,V_a. Such witnesses exist exactly when a fails to preserve
the partition space under inverse images.

If S is a union of blocks and a^(-1)S is again a union of blocks, its
destination-block bits MUST satisfy x_(U_a)=x_(V_a): the two source
states must have identical membership in a^(-1)S. These equations
are necessary guards, not sufficient conditions or free transitions.

Assume EVERY letter fails to preserve W. Build the undirected graph H
on the d blocks with one chosen edge U_a V_a per letter. At each
nonterminal history vertex, the next actual letter has its guard
satisfied. Q also satisfies every guard. Thus ALL history vertices
belong to the Boolean cube minus the proper two-colorings of H.

If H is bipartite with k connected components, including isolated
vertices, it has exactly2^k proper two-colorings. Let t be the number
of singleton blocks whose one-hot Boolean vectors are such colorings.
The allowed union has2^d-2^k vertices and c-t singleton vectors.
Excluding zero and every singleton other than the start proves

    L <= 2^d-2^k-c+t-1.                                (3)

The initial singleton is allowed because an actual next letter exists;
this also handles c-t explicitly. If H is not bipartite, this argument
reduces to the earlier partition bound; it gives no further saving.
The graph contains NO loops, since destination blocks differ.

For a binary alphabet, if both letters fail to preserve W, the graph
is bipartite. Equal guard edges give k=d-1 and t<=2, so
L<=2^(d-1)-c+1. Distinct edges give k=d-2 and t<=1, so

    L <= 3*2^(d-2)-c.                                  (4)

Disjoint guard edges have t=0 and save one further step. At n6/d5,
the partition has c4 singleton blocks. Hence (4) gives L<=20;
equal edges give L<=13. Therefore ANY binary n6/d5 partition-history
counter to L<=20 must have at least ONE original letter preserving
that partition space. This does NOT show that the other letter does,
or that the partition is a congruence.

For arbitrary alphabets, odd guard cycles can eliminate the counting
saving. No arbitrary-alphabet extension of (4) is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-history-hyperplane-and-guards--conditional-quotient-consequence-with-the-final-route-paid"></a>
#### Conditional quotient consequence, with the final route paid

If EVERY letter preserves a proper partition history space, its blocks
form a genuine d-state quotient. The reset endpoint q lies in a
singleton block. A shortest quotient reset has length rt(quotient);
from its endpoint block there is a route to {q} of length at most d-1,
because the original word w proves reachability. Lifting the reset
and then this route resets the original DFA. Thus unconditionally

    rt(original)<=rt(quotient)+d-1.                    (5)

IF Cerny holds for that smaller quotient, (5) gives
L<=d(d-1)<=(n-1)(d-1), since d<n. The condition is explicit; this is
not a proof of smaller-state Cerny within this note. It does not cover
the one-preserving/one-nonpreserving binary case left by (4).

<a id="direct-attack-inverse-history-barrier"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-inverse-history-barrier--shortest-inverse-growth-does-not-supply-a-square-proof-or-full-independence"></a>
### Shortest inverse growth does not supply a square proof or full independence

**Continuation (2026-10-01).** [Logarithmic dimension in genuinely shortest inverse-growth histories](#direct-attack-log-dimension-shortest-extension-history)
now refutes EVERY positive linear-in-stages dimension guarantee for ALL
shortest-phase histories, even in SC Eulerian completely reachable DFAs.
It realizes n-2 actual proper stages but normalized rank log2(n+1)-1.
Its phases all cost one and its whole chain is not globally optimal, so
the optimized-history and slow-phase/dimension questions remain OPEN.
The globally shortest n5 dependence certificate below retains that
separate feature. Historical constant-factor OPEN labels here are thus
superseded only for unrestricted ALL-CHOICES dimension guarantees.

[Maximal shortest jumps do not force linear history dimension](#direct-attack-maximal-jump-log-history) additionally rules out maximal shortest
cardinality jumps and inclusion of every intermediate preimage as
unconditional linear-dimension repairs. It uses only original
permutation/unit letters and rt>=n-1, but still does not claim that its
logarithmic history is globally optimal or that its cost-two phases
refute a long-phase tradeoff.

**REFUTED:** even the best choices of shortest first-extension phases need
not produce a reset word of length at most (n-1)^2.

Start with any fiber of a single letter of size at least two, charging one
letter. At every phase choose a shortest word whose preimage increases the
current subset's cardinality, permitting a temporary decrease. Optimize over
ALL ties and ALL initial fibers. A four-state strongly connected example is

    a=(0,2,1,1), b=(2,1,3,0).

Its exact rt is 8. The only initial fiber of size >=2 is {2,3}. Its unique
shortest extension endpoint is {0,2,3}, at cost 3. Extending that triple to Q
costs 6. Best and worst inverse greedy cost are both 1+3+6=10>9.
Another saved four-state example has rt=9 and inverse greedy cost 11.
This is independent of the forward greedy C4 counterexample.

For n<=3 this failure cannot occur, over any alphabet. A shortest reset word
has a final letter with a nontrivial fiber. In three states it has size two
(unless a constant letter resets immediately), and there is only one
remaining inverse expansion, to Q. Taking the shortest expansion is optimal.
The two-state case has a constant letter. Thus n=4 is state minimal.

Even choosing the better ORIENTATION does not repair the square guarantee.
The saved noncircular six-state extremal
a=(0,1,2,4,3,3), b=(1,3,5,0,2,4) has exact rt=25, best forward greedy 26,
and best inverse greedy 27. Complete binary coverage through n=5 has no
both-orientations failure; this establishes binary state-minimality only.

Allowing a SINGLE SWITCH with overlapping forward/backward frontiers also
fails on that same example. Allow every tie among shortest first-drop and
first-extension phases, permit the switch inside either phase, and meet
whenever the forward image R is contained in the backward preimage T.
The minimum attainable cost is 26. Bidirectional.py computes this by macro
phases and shortest partial phases. An independent checker instead builds a
unit-edge policy automaton whose reverse nodes record (phase size,current
set), and obtains the same minimum. Both retain the final chronological word.
This is not an impossibility theorem for arbitrary repeated switching or
for non-greedy frontiers. The exact shortest reset word necessarily makes
at least one choice outside this restricted single-switch class.

**REFUTED:** the indicator vectors of subsets in a shortest-extension
history, including the final Q, must be linearly independent.

The five-state strongly connected example

    a=(0,0,2,4,3), b=(2,0,3,4,1)

has an exact shortest inverse history

    {0,1} -> {0,1,2} -> {0,1,3,4} -> Q,
    lengths: 1 initial + 5 + 5 + 3 = 14 = rt.

Writing these subsets as S1,S2,S3,Q, their indicators satisfy

    [S1]+[Q]=[S2]+[S3].

The raw rank is 3 and the normalized zero-sum rank is 2, although there are
three proper stages. Thus even globally shortest reset histories can lose
dimension, and monotone cardinalities do not repair this. With initial fiber
size >=2, five states is minimal for this independence failure: on <=4 states
there are at most two proper stages, of sizes 2 and 3. Their indicators and
1_Q are independent since two distinct proper 0-1 vectors can be affinely
dependent with 1_Q only if they are complements; those sizes cannot sum to 4.

This does NOT refute a constant-factor or logarithmic lower bound on history
dimension. It also does not refute a tradeoff between slower phases and higher
dimension: the dependence witness has one phase of length 5 and another of 3.
That sharper question remains OPEN. The newest multi-subset dimension method
provides context, not a claimed solution of this tradeoff.

<a id="direct-attack-inverse-history-barrier--exact-scope-and-checks"></a>
#### Exact scope and checks

All 395 strongly connected synchronizing four-state binary isomorphism
classes were checked, with 771 complete first-extension histories: five
classes have best inverse greedy above rt; two above the square; no dependent
histories. The complete saved near-extremal sets add 16 five-state classes
(21 histories, five classes with a dependent history) and four six-state
classes (five histories). These are not exhaustive over all larger automata.
The independent checker uses ordinary set preimages and a separate forward
reset BFS. It computes exact rank by determinant minors rather than the
searcher's rational Gaussian elimination. All 13 saved witness profiles pass.

See data/*_history_dimensions and data/history_checks.json. The general
multi-start span methods are known; no priority claim is made for these
finite obstruction examples.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--binary-irreducibly-synchronizing-short-reset-policy-penalty"></a>
### Binary irreducibly synchronizing short-reset policy penalty

**PROVED on paper.** For n>=7 and 4<=j<=n-3, the strongly connected
binary DFA below has rt=3 and global best shortest-image-policy cost
P=j+1. Neither letter alone synchronizes. Taking j=n-3 gives P=n-2,
so even binary irreducible synchronization does not give a constant-factor
or constant-additive approximation of rt by P. The previously constructed
ternary penalty could have its third letter deleted while keeping rt=3;
this theorem removes that possible explanation. Priority remains OPEN.
No policy-square counterexample, Cerny counterexample, new general n-only
reset bound, or Lean result is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--construction-and-exact-image-family"></a>
#### Construction and exact image family

Use right actions on Q={0,...,n-1}; let m=n-j>=3. Set

    a(q)=0 for q in {0,j-1}, and 1 otherwise;
    d(q)=q+1 for q<n-1, and d(n-1)=j.

The word ada resets Q to 1: Qa={0,1}, Qad={1,2}, and a(1)=a(2)=1
because j>=4. None of aa,ad,da,dd resets: aa preserves {0,1}, ad has
image {1,2}, da has image {0,1}, and dd has at least m states. Hence
rt=3. Letter a fixes distinct states 0,1, and d has a cycle of length
m on {j,...,n-1}; both unary subautomata are nonsynchronizing.
For SC, any state maps by a to 0 or 1; from 1, d^(j-2)a reaches 0;
from 0 successive d steps reach every state. This proves irreducibility
with respect to deletion of letters, not merely absence of duplicate maps.

Write T_s={s,...,n-1}, 0<=s<=j, A_i={i,i+1}, 0<=i<=n-2, and
E={n-1,j}. The COMPLETE actual image family is

    R={T_s:0<=s<=j} union {A_i:0<=i<=n-2} union {E}
      union {{q}:q in Q};             |R|=2n+j+1.

Reach T_s by d^s, and all n pairs by ad^i, 0<=i<n. The reset ada,
followed by SC state paths, reaches every singleton. Closure follows
from T_s d=T_(s+1) for s<j and T_j d=T_j; T_s a=A_0 for s<j,
and T_j a={1}. Letter d takes adjacent pairs along the tail and cycle,
with A_(n-2)d=E and Ed=A_j; a takes every pair into a singleton or A_0.
The guards j>=4 and m>=3 ensure that the listed ranks/orbits are distinct.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--every-high-rank-shortest-parent-is-forced"></a>
#### Every high-rank shortest parent is forced

Recall delta(U,S)=min{|w|:Uw subset S}, allowing strict subsets and
arbitrary intervening rank drops. e(S) minimizes delta over actual
U with |U|>|S|. G and W add e(S) to the minimum/maximum parent tail
over ALL parents attaining that minimum, with G(Q)=W(Q)=0.

For 1<=s<=j, only T_t with t<s can be larger actual sources for T_s:
all other actual images have rank <=2<m. No such T_t can enter T_s
under a, since T_t a contains 0. Under d, T_t d subset T_s holds
exactly when t=s-1. Thus e(T_s)=1, its sole winning larger parent is
T_(s-1), and G(T_s)=W(T_s)=s. This one-letter characterization is
complete because e=1; longer paths cannot tie it.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--the-unique-rank-two-winning-boundary"></a>
#### The unique rank-two winning boundary

The first-drop boundary from rank >2 consists exactly of A_0 and {1}.
Every T_s with s<j maps to A_0 under a. Only T_j maps to {1}, under a.
Letter d keeps all these suffixes at rank >=m>=3.

For a listed pair S!=A_0 let i=min S>=1. Starting at singleton {1},
d^(i-1) enters S, and no shorter word does: each transition increases
the ordinary integer state index by at most one. Therefore
delta({1},S)=i-1. Starting from A_0, the trajectory of state 0 must
finish at index >=i, so delta(A_0,S)>=i. These arguments include
singleton arrivals and strict-subset transport, not only exact pair images.

The universal first-drop normal form says every shortest phase from a
larger actual image begins by dropping to rank at most the target rank.
The singleton boundary consequently wins strictly for S!=A_0, and its
ONLY larger parent is T_j. Hence, with no unresolved parent tie,

    e(S)=i;             G(S)=W(S)=j+i       (S a listed pair !=A_0).

For A_0, EVERY T_s with s<=j is a winning unit-cost parent: T_j maps
to the strict subset {1}. Thus e(A_0)=G(A_0)=1 and W(A_0)=j+1.
Ignoring that strict-subset arrival would give the wrong worst tie.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--all-one-letter-merge-sources-and-the-global-optimum"></a>
#### All one-letter merge sources and the global optimum

The only nonsingleton fiber of d is {j-1,n-1}. It is absent from R:
the gap is m>=3 and the wrap pair is {j,n-1}. No suffix of rank >=3
can be merged by d. The zero fiber of a is {0,j-1}, also absent from R.
Thus every actual one-letter merged image maps to 1 under a. Such
sources are T_j and the a-monochromatic listed pairs. No T_s with s<j
is merged, and A_0 is not merged. Therefore kappa=m and T_j is the
unique largest-cardinality merge source.

The global seed normal form gives

    P=1+min{G(U): U an actual one-letter merge source}.

Here G(T_j)=j, while every merged pair S has G(S)=j+min S>=j+1.
It follows that P=j+1, witnessed by d^j a. Each suffix step in this
word is a shortest unit phase, followed by a shortest singleton phase.
In contrast, Qad=A_1 is a two-letter phase from Q; it is disallowed
because T_j a={1} subset A_1 gives e(A_1)=1. The complete parent tail
is the obstruction even though a true reset of length three exists.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--complete-singleton-values-and-local-extension-maximum"></a>
#### Complete singleton values and local extension maximum

The sole singleton seed is 1. Ordinary state distance from 1 to q>=1
is q-1: d achieves it, and every transition increases the index by at
most one. Distance to 0 is j-1, since a can reach 0 only from 0 or
j-1, and d never reaches 0; d^(j-2)a attains that distance.
The nearest-seed formula therefore gives

    e({0})=j;   e({q})=q for q>=1;
    G({0})=2j; G({q})=j+q for q>=1.

For the worst tail at seed 1, the pair A_(n-2), merged by a, has
W=j+n-2; it dominates T_j and every other merged pair (E has min=j).
Thus W({1})=j+n-1, and the same nearest-seed formula yields

    W({0})=2j+n-2; W({q})=j+n+q-2 for q>=1.

Suffix extensions are 1, pair extensions at most n-2, and singleton
extensions at most n-1, attained at {n-1}. Consequently max e=n-1.
The maximum W is j+2n-3, attained at {n-1}. These are policy parameters,
not lower bounds on the shortest reset threshold.

<a id="direct-attack-irreducible-short-reset-policy--proof-and-finite-check-boundaries"></a>
#### Proof and finite-check boundaries

The inequalities above prove the arbitrary-n result for the entire
parameter range, not an extrapolation of samples. Saved certificates use
every n7..63 and each valid distinct j in {4,floor(n/2),n-3}. An independent
ordinary actual-image graph checker recomputes EVERY e/G/W/forward entry
by per-target reverse BFS; n<=12 additionally uses ordinary ALL-SOURCE BFS.
It verifies complete R, SC, both unary controls, all suffix parents, the
rank-two boundary, exact reset/policy words, formulas and corruptions.
The native kernel is used only for certificate generation in this check.

The reset-length-dependent all-seed budget still gives the square bound
in this rt=3 regime. Irreducibility does not rescue approximation to rt,
but this family does not threaten the surviving square policy conjecture.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction--any-length-inverse-monotonicity-fails-on-the-retained-kari-dfa"></a>
### Any-length inverse monotonicity fails on the retained Kari DFA

Date:2026-10-02. **REFUTED:** universal existence of a reset word whose
inverse sets never decrease at EACH ORIGINAL LETTER. This is a method
obstruction, not a Cerny counterexample. No novelty claim. General Cerny
and the compatible amortized square remain **OPEN**.

**FORMALLY VERIFIED:** for the literal n6 rows below, EVERY resetting
inverse word has at least ONE cardinality decrease; a literal cost25
reset has EXACTLY one. Lean checks unbounded word length, the actual
row/preimage correspondence, a closed cut, its induction and the
one-shrink witness. The ordinary optimal-length lower bound25 remains
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** by an independent ALL-subset Bellman
certificate in this checkpoint. The later `KariProductBase.reset_length_lower`
in `KariShrinkProducts.lean` formally proves the same base lower bound25.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction--literal-original-model"></a>
#### Literal original model

The original letters, each at cost1, are

    a=[4,4,2,3,1,5], b=[1,5,3,4,2,0].

They are the prior retained n6/rt25 rows

    old_a=[0,1,2,4,3,3], old_b=[1,3,5,0,2,4]

under the checked canonical-to-old state relabeling[5,4,0,1,3,2].
No new automaton or ordinary reset threshold is claimed.

For a word resetting to q, start from{q} and take preimages in reverse
original-letter order. Its final preimage is Q. A monotone inverse
word is one for which every such intermediate cardinality is at least
the preceding one. This concerns individual ORIGINAL letters.

It does NOT refute extension policies that grow at macro boundaries
while allowing shrinkage inside a macro. The previous fixed-root
cycle-routing proofs in fact use zero-growth preparation and one final
positive step; they remain valid within their explicit hypotheses.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction--the-exact-closed-cut"></a>
#### The exact closed cut

Encode subsets by six-bit masks. The set of masks reachable from ANY
singleton through nondecreasing literal preimage steps is exactly

    [1,2,3,4,5,7,8,10,11,12,14,15,16,20,21,24,28,32,
     33,34,35,37,39,42,43,47,48,49,50,51,53,55,56,58,59].

It contains all six singleton masks and excludes full mask63.
Every permitted nondecreasing edge from one of these35 masks remains
inside it. Therefore induction on ANY finite word forbids reaching Q
without a decrease. There is no bounded-word-length assumption.

Independent literal reach words for every listed mask certify that
the cut is exactly the reachable set, not just a guessed invariant.
Its maximum cardinality is5, so the obstruction is not an inability
to reach large sets at all: it is the final compatible trajectory.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction--exact-shrink-count-and-a-shortest-reset-attaining-it"></a>
#### Exact shrink count and a shortest reset attaining it

A second certificate assigns to EVERY mask the lexicographic optimum
(number of decreasing letters, original length) for reaching Q by
inverse preimages. The local edge cost is(1,1) for a decrease, otherwise
(0,1). All64 local Bellman equations and infinite-state edges are checked
independently. The singleton values, in state order0..5, are

    (1,28),(1,26),(1,26),(1,27),(1,25),(1,27).

The whole automaton's exact minimum reset length is25. The target4
witness has that length and exactly one inverse decrease:

    a b b a b a b a b b a a b a b b a b b a b a b b a.

Its inverse cardinalities, including the initial singleton, are

    1,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,3,3,3,3,3,3,4,4,4,5,5,4,4,5,5,5,6.

The unavoidable 5->4 decrease is compensated later on ONE literal
reset word. Thus minimum decrease count is exactly1, and a globally
shortest reset attains it. The earlier greedy length25 witness had
two decreases; it was not evidence that two were necessary.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction--formal-and-computational-verification-boundaries"></a>

<a id="direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction--consequence-for-the-active-research-route"></a>
#### Consequence for the active research route

The coprime fixed-root subclass now has a paid compatible square proof,
but its literal-monotonicity property cannot be universal. On the
larger almost-circular class the root moves, and this retained critical
input requires backtracking even when optimizing the entire word.
General proofs must permit individual-letter decreases as well as
occasionally expensive positive extensions. The full history/cost-rank
approach did not assume otherwise and is not refuted by this result.
No general square bound or complete Cerny proof has been obtained.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-product-shrink-tradeoff"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-kari-product-shrink-tradeoff--unbounded-inverse-decreases-and-an-exact-product-costloss-tradeoff"></a>
### Unbounded inverse decreases and an exact product cost/loss tradeoff

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), ALL integer d>=1.** The literal
six-state foundation is **FORMALLY VERIFIED** in KariShrinkProducts.lean;
the arbitrary-d Cartesian lifting below is paper, NOT formally verified.
No novelty claim. General Cerny is **OPEN**. These automata synchronize
quickly; they refute constant inverse-backtracking budgets, not Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-product-shrink-tradeoff--the-actual-product-alphabet"></a>
#### The actual product alphabet

Let K have states0..5 and original rows

    a=[4,4,2,3,1,5], b=[1,5,3,4,2,0].

For d>=1 take Q={0,..,5}^d, n=6^d. The2d ORIGINAL letters (c,i),
0<=c<d, i=0,1, apply K's ith letter to coordinate c and fix all other
coordinates. Each costsONE. This is independent-coordinate control,
not the diagonal direct product with only two simultaneous letters.

K is SC, and independent coordinate routing makes the product SC.
Projection of any word to coordinate c keeps precisely its(c,0)/(c,1)
letters, in order. A product word resets IFF ALL d projections reset K.
Their lengths SUM to the original word length; no macro is free.

Starting an inverse run from any singleton tuple, every set is a Cartesian
rectangle S_1 x ... x S_d. A step on coordinate c replaces only S_c
by its literal K-preimage. All factors remain nonempty in any reset run:
an empty factor would make the full inverse set empty forever.
Hence a global inverse cardinality decrease occurs IFF the changed
coordinate decreases; its absolute loss is

    (|S_c|-|S'_c|) * product_{j!=c}|S_j|.

Define h(w) as the number of such decreases, and Delta(w) as the largest
absolute decrease. Every K letter changes preimage size by at mostONE;
b never changes it. The same delta-one assertion is about the coordinate
factor, NOT the size of the entire Cartesian rectangle.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-product-shrink-tradeoff--literal-base-facts-including-every-possible-last-decrease"></a>
#### Literal base facts, including every possible last decrease

The forward35-mask cut from [Any-length inverse monotonicity fails on the retained Kari DFA](#direct-attack-kari-inverse-shrink-obstruction) forbids
a monotone inverse reset at EVERY word length. The new backward set C,
consisting of masks from which Q is reachable without another decrease,
is exactly

    [22,23,25,29,30,31,44,46,57,60,61,62,63].

It contains Q and has minimum cardinality3. It is closed BACKWARD under
nondecreasing preimage edges. Independent primal suffixes plus finite
Bellman controls certify exactness; the Lean proof needs only the backward
invariant and Q membership, then inducts over arbitrary suffix words.

The ONLY decreasing literal edges entering C are

    a:45 ->44, cardinality4 ->3;
    a:47 ->60, cardinality5 ->4.

Therefore the LAST decrease in EVERY K reset is one of these. A K reset
with onlyONE decrease has a prefix in the forward35-mask cut and a suffix
in C. Of the two bridges, only47 is in that forward cut. Its sole decrease
is thus47->60, and its remaining cardinalities are at least4.

All K resets have length>=25; a25-letter reset with one decrease exists.
The lower bound is now kernel-verified for ALL inverse word lists, using
a Nat potential satisfying p(S)<=1+p(pre_i(S)), with p(Q)=0 and all
singleton potentials>=25. The earlier checkpoint's ordinary lower
bound was only computational; this NEW standalone source upgrades it.

If a K reset's last decrease is45->44, its length is at least27:
EVERY path from ANY singleton to45 costs>=16, that edge costs1, and
EVERY nondecreasing path44->Q costs>=10. These are separately
kernel-verified all-word inequalities. A matching27-letter reset has
exactlyTWO decreases. Its inverse prefix costs17 and ends at44; its
remaining nondecreasing suffix costs10. The25-letter one-decrease
reset splits into cost20 to60, then a nondecreasing cost5 suffix.

The finite potential value1000 is a cap for unreachable masks; all local
inequalities are kernel-checked, including those masks. No infinity
arithmetic, truncated word-length search or negative-cost Bellman
uniqueness argument is used to prove an all-word lower bound.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-product-shrink-tradeoff--the-all-d-conclusions-and-compatible-attainments"></a>
#### The all-d conclusions and compatible attainments

1. **min_w h(w)=d, and rt=25d.** Each coordinate projection resets K,
   so needs at leastone decrease and25 letters. Projection lengths add.
   For attainment, apply each coordinate's cost20 prefix to60, keeping
   completed factors at size4; then apply every coordinate's cost5
   nondecreasing suffix. This is ONE actual inverse word, hence ONE
   compatible original reset obtained by reversing it. It has length25d,
   exactlyd decreases, and largest loss4^(d-1).

2. **min_w Delta(w)=3^(d-1).** Consider the LAST global decrease in
   any reset. All other coordinates have already taken their last
   decrease. Their subsequent sizes are nondecreasing and at least3,
   by the last-bridge classification. The current factor decreases byONE,
   so this single global loss is at least3^(d-1). For attainment, prepare
   coordinates0..d-2 with the two-decrease cost17 prefix to44, retaining
   each at size3. Prepare coordinate d-1 with the one-decrease cost20
   prefix to60. Finally apply all corresponding nondecreasing suffixes.
   Every decrease during preparation costs at most3^(d-1) elements, and
   the last preparation step attains that loss. This is again ONE actual
   original word; its length is27(d-1)+25=27d-2 and count2d-1.

3. **Among Delta-optimal resets, minimum length=27d-2 and minimum
   h=2d-1.** At the last global decrease the product of the otherd-1
   factor sizes must be EXACTLY3^(d-1), since each factor is at least3.
   Thus EACH such factor has size3. Its own last decrease must have been
   45->44, rather than47->60 (after the latter it stays at least4).
   Each of these d-1 coordinate projections costs>=27 and needs>=2
   decreases. The last coordinate costs>=25 and needs>=1. Lengths
   and counts add. The schedule in item2 simultaneously attains both.

4. **Among ordinary shortest resets, min Delta=4^(d-1).** Every
   coordinate projection of a25d-letter reset has length EXACTLY25.
   Its last decrease cannot be45->44, since that costs>=27. Thus ALL
   projections have last decrease47->60 and afterward size>=4.
   At the last global decrease all other factors have size>=4, giving
   loss>=4^(d-1). The compatible schedule in item1 attains it.

These proofs quantify over arbitrary words and singleton targets, not
just the displayed schedules. For d>=2, reducing the optimal largest
loss from4^(d-1) to3^(d-1) necessarily adds at least2d-2 ORIGINAL letters.
Thus neither a constant backtracking count nor minimizing unweighted
backtracking damage can be imposed without an independent cost argument.

<a id="direct-attack-kari-product-shrink-tradeoff--scope-independent-checks-and-formal-boundary"></a>
