<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--positive-original-letter-defect-balance-gives-a-compatible-square-reset"></a>
### Positive original-letter defect balance gives a compatible square reset

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), arbitrary n>=2 and alphabet under
the stated row condition.** No novelty or FORMALLY VERIFIED claim;
priority OPEN. General Cerny remains **OPEN**. All word costs below
are ORIGINAL letter counts, with right actions and P_(fg)=P_f P_g.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--the-broader-positive-weighted-criterion"></a>
#### The broader positive weighted criterion

Write D(w)=[Q]P_w-[Q]. For EACH original nonpermutation letter f,
require a positive integer alpha_f and nonnegative integers beta_(f,g),
g ranging over ORIGINAL letters, such that

    alpha_f D(f) + sum_g beta_(f,g) D(f g) = 0.                (B1)

Then every proper nonempty subset extends in ORIGINAL cost<=n.
If M=max_(f,q) c_f(q), one compatible reset costs

    rt <= 1+n(n-M) <= (n-1)^2.

There are no fixed-root, collision-kernel, rank-one, permutation-group,
separate SC or permutation-corrector assumptions. The weights may differ
for different f. In particular, columns with in-degree>2 are permitted.
This is a sufficient explicit balancing condition, not a universal claim.
Rational feasibility can be tested by linear programming after normalizing
alpha_f=1; clearing denominators gives the stated integer certificate.
The retained checker verifies GIVEN integer certificates exactly, without
an LP solver. No existence certificate is guessed from floating point.

For the proof, take the shortest nonzero change w=f v as derived below,
with |w|<=n-1 and |U v^-1|=|U|=k. If its change delta is positive,
w works. Otherwise apply(B1) to P_v[U]^T. It gives

    alpha_f delta + sum_g beta_(f,g)(|U(f g v)^-1|-k)=0.

Since alpha_f delta<0, at leastONE positive-weight term is positive.
Choose that actual original g. The literal word f g v extends U and
costs at mostn. OnlyONE g is applied, not a probabilistic mixture or
an uncharged word. The intervening set need not be cardinality-monotone.

A synchronizing n>=2 input has a nonpermutation letter. The pigeonhole
principle gives M>=2. Start with the singleton having M preimages under
the attaining original letter, at costONE. At mostn-M positive growth
stages of cost<=n complete ONE compatible reset. This proves the bound.
Every hypothetical Cerny counterexample must fail(B1) at some original
singular letter. Neither positive-weight availability nor universal
one-step balancing has been assumed for an arbitrary automaton.

If the balanced terms use actual suffix WORDS u of length<=K rather
than original letters g, the same proof pays K and gives extension
<=n-1+K and reset<=1+(n-M)(n-1+K). On ordinary Cerny the minimum
possible maximum balancing-suffix cost is n-1: the earlier
[A short stationary mixture cannot use singular words in Cerny automata](#direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost) proves singular stationary support
needs maximum total word cost n, while the actual prefix words
a b^j,0<=j<n, attain it. This is a REUSE of that proved result, not a
new stationarity search. Weighted balancing is cheaper there than one
exact opposite, but the generic escape-plus-suffix bound still costs
2n-2 per stage and does not recover the known square by itself.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--exact-reversal-corollary-and-its-explicit-paid-proof"></a>
#### Exact-reversal corollary and its explicit paid proof

Let A=(Q,Sigma) be a complete synchronizing DFA, |Q|=n. Write
c_f=[Q]P_f for the ORIGINAL letter f's column in-degree row.
For EVERY nonpermutation original letter f, require an ORIGINAL
letter g_f satisfying

    c_f + c_(f g_f) = 2[Q].                                  (R1)

Different f may have different correcting letters. They need not be
permutations, inverses or group elements. No common fixed root, collision
kernel, level, transitive permutation group or separate SC assumption
is imposed. Permutation original letters need no correction.

Then EVERY proper nonempty U has a literal extending word of length<=n.
There is ONE compatible reset of length<=1+n(n-2)=(n-1)^2.
Growth may exceedONE. The general theorem concerns cardinality at
macro boundaries; when the correcting letters are permutations, the
construction can keep cardinality nondecreasing at every literal letter.

This is the alpha=1/beta_(f,g_f)=1 special case of(B1).
Condition(R1) is directly checkable from the original transition rows,
in O(|Sigma|^2 n) integer operations. It is a sufficient structural
criterion, not a claim that every synchronizing automaton satisfies it.
Any hypothetical Cerny counterexample must have some original singular
letter with no such original one-letter corrector.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--a-short-nonzero-change-without-assuming-its-sign"></a>
#### A short nonzero change, without assuming its sign

For proper nonempty U, k=|U|, use the NONZERO centered column
x=n[U]^T-k[Q]^T. Put V_j=span{P_w x:|w|<=j}. Initially
dim V_0=1 and [Q]x=0. If V_j=V_(j+1), every original-letter operator
preserves V_j, so the chain stabilizes permanently.

A reset w has |U w^-1| either0 or n, and hence
[Q]P_w x=n(|U w^-1|-k)!=0. Thus the full orbit is not contained in
the(n-1)-dimensional hyperplane [Q]^perp. If every word of length<=n-1
had zero change, V_0,...,V_(n-1) would all be in that hyperplane.
No equality could occur, or the full orbit would remain there. The
n-1 strict dimension increases starting from1 would give dimension>=n,
a contradiction. Therefore SOME cardinality-changing word has cost<=n-1.

This is the usual orbit-chain escape mechanism, attributed to
[Steinberg2010, Lemma6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.0410).
The argument is restated here to make its SIGN and cost scope explicit:
in a general synchronizing DFA the short change can be NEGATIVE.

Choose a SHORTEST nonzero-change word w=f v, |w|<=n-1. Every shorter
suffix has zero change. In particular V=U v^-1 has |V|=k, and the
inverse processing of v remains at size k. The leading f cannot be
a permutation. Set delta=|U w^-1|-k !=0.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--pay-the-correcting-letter-and-flip-the-sign"></a>
#### Pay the correcting letter and flip the sign

If delta>0, w already extends U at cost<=n-1. If delta<0, use the
actual original word

    f g_f v,

of length |w|+1<=n. Condition(R1) gives

    |U(f g_f v)^-1|-k
      = (2[Q]-[Q]P_f) P_v [U]^T-k
      = 2k-(k+delta)-k
      = -delta >0.

The order is essential: g_f is inserted BETWEEN f and the existing
suffix v. It is not applied as a free transposition of coordinates.
The preparatory suffix is the SAME actual word. If g_f is a permutation,
the suffix and g_f's preimage preserve cardinality, then f gives growth.
For a singular g_f, intermediate shrinkage is permitted; the final
preimage calculation still proves literal positive growth at cost<=n.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--the-seed-and-one-compatible-reset"></a>
#### The seed and one compatible reset

Condition(R1) and nonnegative in-degrees imply c_f(q)<=2 for everyq.
A nonpermutation f must have some double column: otherwise all counts
are<=1 and their sum n would force a permutation. Therefore a singleton
{q} with c_f(q)=2 has a sizeTWO preimage under f at costONE.

Starting from that actual two-point preimage, repeatedly extend the
CURRENT subset by the paid word just proved. Sizes strictly increase,
so at mostn-2 stages are needed. Prepend each extending word to the
accumulated original word. Its preimage of the SAME singleton becomes
Q, proving a compatible reset, not a sum of unrelated optimal stages.
Total cost<=1+n(n-2). No independent final-pair or initialization
cost is omitted.

The full proof also gives a paid-word variant. If every original singular
f has an actual correcting WORD u_f of length<=K, K>=1, with
c_f+c_(f u_f)=2[Q], then every proper U extends in cost<=n-1+K,
and one reset costs<=1+(n-2)(n-1+K). Every corrector letter is paid.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--a-previously-retained-sharp-boundary-at-correcting-costtwo"></a>
#### A previously retained sharp boundary at correcting costTWO

Reuse the already certified fixed-root n5 rows

    a=[1,1,3,2,4], b=[4,2,0,3,1], U={0,1}.

Here c_a+c_(a b^2)=2[Q], but NEITHER original a nor original b is
a one-letter corrector for a. The short NEGATIVE change word a b a b
costs4=n-1. Inserting the actual b^2 gives a b^3 a b, which extends
U at cost6=n-1+2. The existing ALL32-state positive-cost Bellman
certificate proves no extension of U costs less. Thus a cost2
correcting WORD cannot be silently substituted into(R1) at costONE.
No new search or rediscovery is claimed for this counterexample.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--on-ordinary-cerny-automata-exact-correcting-suffix-cost2n-3"></a>
#### On ordinary Cerny automata, exact correcting suffix cost2n-3

For EVERY n>=2 let a=(0->1), fixing all other states, and b:q->q+1
modulo n. A row-reversing suffix u must satisfy

    c_a+c_(a u)=2[Q],

so a u has omitted image1 and doubled image0. Its rank is n-1.
Starting from a, no intermediate rank can drop and later recover.
Every intermediate row therefore has exactlyONE omitted p andONE
doubled q, p!=q, with all other columnsONE. Under b, both indices
increase modulo n. Under a, rank n-1 is retained only if p=0 or p=1.
If p=0, the row is unchanged. If p=1, the new omitted index is0;
the doubled index stays q unless q=0, when it becomes1.

Truncate u at the FIRST occurrence of the target(p,q)=(1,0).
Before that occurrence define delta=q-p mod n in{1,..,n-1}.
b and the p=0 a-steps keep delta fixed. A p=1 a-step before the
target has q!=0 and increases delta byONE. Starting delta1 and
ending delta n-1 therefore require at leastn-2 such a-steps.
Each starts at omitted p=1 and returns it to0; from the initial p=0,
and between successive such steps, at leastONE b is needed. After
the last one, at leastONE more b is needed to reach target p=1.
Thus u has at leastn-2 a's and n-1 b's: |u|>=2n-3.

The actual suffix

    u=(b a)^(n-2) b

attains2n-3: each b a raises the doubled index while returning the
omitted index to0, and the final b gives omitted1/doubled0.
For n2 the exponent is0 and u=b. This is PROVED paper ALL n,
with no novelty claim. It is a new cost metric here, NOT a new ordinary
reset threshold; Cerny's ordinary square remains the known value.
Even this sharp family fails(R1) at n>=3 and needs a growing paid
corrector. The criterion cannot be asserted as a universal reduction.
Letters with an in-degree>=3 admit no such row-reversing suffix at
ANY cost, since the complementary in-degree would be negative.
That last restriction concerns exact opposites in(R1), not(B1).
Indeed the retained high-in-degree controls below satisfy(B1).
Ordinary Cerny also fails(B1) at n>=3: at coordinate0, D(a) and
D(a a) are-1 while D(a b) is0, so a positive coefficient on D(a)
cannot be balanced with nonnegative coefficients on the other two.

<a id="direct-attack-original-letter-defect-reversal--independent-finite-verification"></a>
#### Independent finite verification

430 retained inputs:ALL388 canonical binary rank-one/swap-permutation
pairs n2..5,35 sampled four-letter multi-defect inputs n6..12, plus
an explicit all-original-multicluster n6 input and an all-singular
corrector n3 input. Completeness of the388 is checked using unique
row signatures and the exact count n!(n-2)!/2 at each n. Their singular

Five further controls n4,8,16,32,64 use XOR translations as ORIGINAL
permutation letters and collapse0 and the standard binary basis states
to0, fixing all others. Every original letter has at leastTWO cycles;
the singular letter has in-degree log2(n)+1. Taking alpha=1 and beta=1
for all nonidentity translations satisfies(B1), since the average of
all translations distributes each row uniformly. No exact row-reversing
word exists for that singular letter at ANY cost. Pair Bellman and literal
compatible words independently check synchronization; no all-n threshold
for this control family is asserted.

309 SYNC inputs,37 with original corank>=2,133 with at leastTWO cycles
in EVERY original letter,4 singular correcting-letter designations.
ALL proper nonempty subsets are checked at n<=10; n11/12 have64
retained subsets each (also64 at n16/32/64). Controls:18780 literal extension witnesses,
9403 negative changes flipped,319898 pair Bellman edges,481632 literal
particle-letter controls, compatible seed/growth/reset words and TEN
rejected corruptions. All these retained witnesses happen to be

The existing n5 boundary has32 independent extension Bellman edges.
Nineteen Cerny parameters n2..16,31,63,127,257 have COMPLETE retained

<a id="direct-attack-paid-one-cluster-word-bound"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-paid-one-cluster-word-bound--one-cluster-words-with-original-costs-and-a-failed-universal-bridge"></a>
### One-cluster words with original costs and a failed universal bridge

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper, derived conditional bound).** General
Cerny **OPEN**. No novelty or formal verification is claimed. The proof
uses the reconstructed annular mechanism of
[Zhu2026, Sections3..8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.19675v1), documented in
[Independent reconstruction of the one-cluster upper proof](#direct-attack-one-cluster-upper-proof-audit). One-cluster WORDS and their paid costs
already occur in [Kisielewicz--Kowalski--Szykula2016, Theorem2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.04025).
The formula below is a direct cost refinement of the reconstructed
mechanism, not a claim to have originated the weighted-word approach.

Let A be ANY synchronizing n-state DFA over its ORIGINAL alphabet Sigma.
Let v be a nonempty actual Sigma-word of length s. Suppose its functional
graph has a unique cycle C of size m and level ell, and put t=n-m. All
original letters remain available with cost1. Add a macro T=v with cost s;
it is not a new cost-one letter. At m1, the elementary bound is s*ell.
For m>=2 put

    h=ceil(t/ell) if ell>0, and h=0 if ell=0,
    E=1+s*(m-1)+max_(0<=r<=n-2){s*min(t,ell*r)-(s-1)*r}
     =s*(n-1)+1-(s-1)*h,
    B=t+1+m*s*ell+(m-2)*E
     =s*((m-1)*(n-1)+m*ell)-(s-1)*(n-1+(m-2)*h).

Then every nonempty proper S in C extends relatively by w v^ell with
ORIGINAL |w|<=E, and ONE actual reset has ORIGINAL length<=B. The
distinguished-word cost is paid every time it occurs, including both
initialization and entry. The case ell0 necessarily has t0,m=n and gives
B=(n-1)+s*(n-1)*(n-2). At s1 this recovers the square/subclass bound.

<a id="direct-attack-paid-one-cluster-word-bound--paid-annular-proof"></a>
#### Paid annular proof

Keep the fixed-seed spaces L_r/M_r and the annular sum from the preceding
audit, but let EVERY original letter be a control. This includes letters
used inside v and may include a transformation equal to T. Redundancy is
harmless. Crucially, the control alphabet Sigma itself synchronizes.
The algebra depends on T's transformation, not on the macro's cost.

At order r1..n-2 put kappa=min(t,ell*r). An annular term with a prepended
seed has r+1 unit-cost controls and at most m+kappa-r-1 macro occurrences,
excluding the common terminal v^ell. Its ORIGINAL prefix cost is at most

    r+1+s*(m+kappa-r-1)
      =1+s*(m-1)+s*kappa-(s-1)*r <= E.

At r0 the m cycle shifts have prefix costs<=1+s*(m-1)<=E. Thus assuming
no extending original prefix through cost E makes every annular pairing
nonpositive. Fixed-seed descent and the old-space induction force them
all to vanish. The same generating families remain complete; a label
with r controls has macro-exponent total<=Dplus-1. Padding by a cycle
period puts it in the annulus without changing its R-row. Its padded
prefix is one of the costed terms above. Stabilization at r=n-2 and
leftmost-control deletion give the same contradiction with an ORIGINAL
reset. No polynomial projection is used as a free or positive word.

For ell0 there is no nilpotent space. The nontrivial eigenlines are simple
and exclude1. Here kappa=0, and Dplus=m-r-1 for r1..n-2. Repeated
eigenvalues remove controls; for distinct eigenvalues the numerator has
degree m-r-2, one below Dplus, so the annular coefficient vanishes. The
generating bounds reduce to d_r-1; the same induction and stabilization
work. This supplies the stated circular macro-cost refinement directly.

For ell>0, ell<=t and m>=2 imply ceil(t/ell)<=t<=n-2. Writing t=ell*j+k,
0<=k<ell, the maximum defining E occurs at r=j if k0, and at r=j+1 if
k>0: the slope before saturation is s*(ell-1)+1>0; at the final partial
step its increment is s*(k-1)+1>0; after saturation the slope is1-s<=0.
Thus the displayed closed form is exact for this worst-layer budget.

Initialization uses the ORIGINAL Sigma span chain, not a weighted macro
chain. Centered columns T^ell(chi_q-Q/m), q in C, have dimension m-1 and
sum0. Since Sigma alone synchronizes, their left orbit escapes ker[C]
within t+1 ORIGINAL letters. Some q then has positive relative pairing,
giving an initial factor costing<=t+1+s*ell and covering at least two
cycle states. At most m-2 extensions cost E+s*ell each. Prepending
v^ell costs another s*ell and sends Q into C. Hence the same reset costs
t+1+m*s*ell+(m-2)*E, exactly B. Every factor is compatible and literal.

This theorem does NOT apply with unit initialization cost to an arbitrary
weighted alphabet whose only synchronizing generator has cost s. Its
assumption is that the original Sigma alphabet has unit costs and already
synchronizes; the macro is an actual word in that alphabet.

<a id="direct-attack-paid-one-cluster-word-bound--useful-necessary-conditions-and-the-bridge-obstruction"></a>
#### Useful necessary conditions and the bridge obstruction

At m2 the bound simplifies to (n-1)+2s*ell. Since ell<=n-2, ANY sync
DFA with such a word of length s<=floor((n-1)/2) satisfies the square.
In particular a two-letter ORIGINAL word with a unique two-cycle excludes
a Cerny counterexample at EVERY n>=5. Rooted words of length<=n-1 also
exclude a counterexample by their fully paid power. These conditions
concern WORDS, with costs retained, and can exclude inputs whose individual
original letters all have multiple cycles. They are not universal claims.

The proposed bridge was: every SC sync DFA has a NONCONSTANT one-cluster
word for which its B formula (or s*ell at m1) is within the square.
It is **REFUTED**, even outside the trivial fast-reset cases:

    n5: a=[0,0,1,3,4], b=[3,1,3,4,2], rt=13 < square16.
    n4: a=[0,2,1,1],   b=[2,1,3,0],   rt=8  < square9.

Both graphs are SC and both original letters have multiple functional
cycles. ALL511 literal words through length8 at n5, and ALL31 through
length4 at n4, fail the proposed NONCONSTANT budget certificate. These
finite enumerations suffice for ALL lengths: every eligible rooted row
has ell>=2, hence s*ell>=2s; for m>=2, B has the form C0+s*D with C0>=0
and D=(m-2)*(n-1-h)+m*ell>=2. The circular case has D=(n-1)*(n-2)>=2
in these n4/n5 inputs. Thus any eligible longer word exceeds the square.
The best short n5 formula is18, attained by v=a a b a b a a with m2,
ell1,s7; at n4 the best is11, attained by v=a b with m2,ell2,s2.
Actual reset words remain below the square; no Cerny counterexample results.

The obstruction refutes ONLY this worst-case FORMULA bridge. Better
initialization, original compression of C, or other compatible factors
can be cheaper. Indeed the finite checker constructs an actual reset on
each retained input; its exact cost need not equal B. Allowing a constant
reset word as the selected macro makes the bridge tautological and is
explicitly excluded from the refuted proposition. One-cluster word
methods as a whole are not refuted.

The new generator/checker retain original-word macros, all proper cycle
extension certificates, initialization and common literal resets. Their
verification is finite **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**, not an all-parameter
computational or formal proof. The counterexample enumerations are
independently checked and threshold minimality is verified by full subset
distances. General Cerny and a universal cheap compatible structure remain
**OPEN**; the goal continues after saving this conditional result.

Completed finite scope:293 original-word macro cases,5758 complete proper
cycle-subset extensions,5713 macro state/letter controls,283495 literal
state/letter controls and542 complete obstruction words.166 formula
cases fit the square;15 cases have multicycle EVERY original letter.
Eight deliberate corruptions are rejected.  Native builds remain8. The 293 controls include circular
and rooted boundaries, non-SC inputs and a seven-letter composite macro.

<a id="direct-attack-pair-information-and-lp"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-pair-information-and-lp--pair-information-and-the-direction-of-the-bellman-dual"></a>
### Pair information and the direction of the Bellman dual

<a id="direct-attack-pair-information-and-lp--an-exact-three-state-information-obstruction"></a>
#### An exact three-state information obstruction

**PROVED by explicit finite computation, independently checkable.** Two
strongly connected binary synchronizing DFAs on {0,1,2} have identical labeled
pair compression distances but different reset thresholds:

    A: a=(0,0,2), b=(1,2,0), rt=3;
    B: a=(1,1,2), b=(1,2,0), rt=4.

For BOTH, d({0,1})=1, d({0,2})=2, d({1,2})=3. Their full reset-distance
vectors on masks 1..7 are respectively

    A: (0,0,1,0,2,3,3),
    B: (0,0,1,0,2,3,4).

A resets by aba and B by abba (right action). Every pair distance can also
be checked directly in the three-vertex pair graph. There is no smaller
state example: a synchronizing two-state DFA has a constant letter and
reset threshold 1. Thus three states are minimal even without fixing the
alphabet size.

The complete labeled pair-distance matrix cannot determine exact reset
threshold. This is stronger than failure of just a pair-distance histogram.
It does not rule out a universal upper bound built using the entire matrix
plus additional transformation information. A four-state pair of examples
with the same matrix and reset thresholds 4 and 6 is saved as well.

The shared pair graph labels/edges need not be identical: the claim is about
distances. Each pair distance can be realized by a different word. Treating
their individually optimal words as simultaneously compatible loses essential
information. The first compression in A and B places the surviving pair at
different positions despite the initial pair-distance data being identical.

<a id="direct-attack-pair-information-and-lp--bellman-lp-orientation-standard-reconstruction"></a>
#### Bellman LP orientation (standard reconstruction)

For a fixed synchronizing automaton, the shortest reset distance d(S) is the
pointwise largest feasible nonnegative potential h satisfying

    h({q})=0; h(S)<=1+h(Sa) for EVERY letter a.

Indeed, summing inequalities down any reset path bounds h(S) by its length,
while d itself is feasible. Maximizing h(Q) is therefore an exact LP for
the reset distance. Its flow dual is a unit flow from Q to singleton goals,
with unit edge costs. Standard shortest-path integrality makes an optimal
flow a path (cycles can be removed). Writing down this LP does not reduce
the exponential number of subsets or provide a uniform flow construction.

An arbitrary feasible h with h(Q)<=(n-1)^2 is only a LOWER certificate and
cannot prove Cerny's upper bound. For an upper certificate one needs a
nonnegative integer H with H(singleton)=0 and, for each non-singleton S,
SOME letter a satisfying H(Sa)<=H(S)-1. Following such choices produces a
reset word of length <=H(S). This is an existential descent requirement,
unlike the universal lower-potential inequalities.

A potential depending only on rank cannot satisfy this one-step upper
condition whenever a subset has no immediately compressing letter, since
all its outgoing targets have the same rank. Such subsets occur even in C3.
A rank potential on macro compression edges needs an actual phase-cost
bound; the proposed square-telescoping bound was refuted by C4. Pair-based
features need the compatibility information exposed above. These facts
explain the current LP obstruction without declaring all potential methods
impossible.

<a id="direct-attack-periodic-three-a-gap"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-periodic-three-a-gap--no-fixed-additive-allowance-rescues-the-three-a-extension-pool"></a>
### No fixed additive allowance rescues the three-a extension pool

Date:2026-10-03. **PROVED (paper), infinite two-parameter family.**
Finite controls are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**, not FORMALLY VERIFIED.
Every universal three-a root-extension pool of cost n+C, for ANY fixed
constant C, is **REFUTED**. Ordinary RP, SEED, order-two square and general
Cerny remain **OPEN**. No novelty or general reset lower-bound claim.

<a id="direct-attack-periodic-three-a-gap--construction"></a>
#### Construction

Generalize [A three-a root-preserving extension barrier](#direct-attack-order-two-three-a-barrier) from period3 to any p>=3.
Let m>=2, L=2pm, M=4pm, delta=pm, h=2m. Original b cycles the core
and fixes r; a(r)=0, a(0)=a(L)=r. Let G0 be the nonzero multiples
of p among1,...,L-1 and fix both members of these input pairs.

Partition the other input pair indices into p-1 groups G1,...,G_(p-1),
each of size h and invariant under delta modulo L. Require G1 to contain
{delta-2,delta-1,L-2,L-1}. Such a partition exists: those are two
delta-orbits, and each group is filled with m orbits. The required
indices are nonzero mod p, even when p=3. Define

    a(L-2)=1, a(M-2)=1+delta,
    a(L-1)=1+L, a(M-1)=1+delta+L.

Map the other G1 pairs bijectively to output pairs with base1 mod p,
excluding bases1,1+delta. Map each other G_color bijectively to all
output pairs with that color mod p. Either orientation is permitted.
These rows form a bijection on C\{0,L}; exactly TWO opposite pairs
are split. The proved order-two classification gives synchronization.

Take S={r} union {q in C:q mod p !=p-1}. It has |S|=M-4m+1,
least core period p, and is proper and root-present.

<a id="direct-attack-periodic-three-a-gap--exact-restricted-minimum"></a>
#### Exact restricted minimum

The leading b-prefix deletion, between-a reductions modulo M and final
power reduction modulo p are exhaustive for all words with at mostTHREE a.
The full defects and root-retention formulas from the period-three proof
apply literally: paired output colors agree modulo p.

Zero, ONE or TWO a letters cannot give rooted positive growth.
For THREE a, a b^j a b^k a b^s, growth is
1-F_s(a(L+j)b^k), while root retention is F_s(a(j)b^k), where

    F_s(x)=chi_S(a(x)b^s),      F_s(r)=chi_S(s).

For every 0<=s<p-1 the zero set modulo L is a nonzero-color group
G_(p-1-s), invariant under delta. All such shifts fail. For s=p-1,
the zero set is G0 while F_(p-1)(0)=1. Thus its ONLY oriented
delta-boundary is0: F(0)=1, F(delta)=0.

Only the four exceptional input indices have different output bases
modulo L. For j=L-2,L-1 their root-side base is1; hence k=L-1 mod L.
The minimum cost is attained at j=L-2,k=L-1,s=p-1 and equals

    3+(L-2)+(L-1)+(p-1) = M+p-1 = n+p-2.

For the upper j=M-2,M-1, k=delta-1 mod L, with cheapest cost
M+delta+p-1, strictly larger. As before there are eight successful
standard triples in the complete ranges. The displayed minimum is
attained and grows by ONE, so the minimum singular count is THREE.

For any constant C choose p>C+2. Then n+p-2>n+C. Already m=2
gives n=8p+1 and restricted minimum9p-1, whose ratio to n tends to9/8.
The additive gap p-2 is linear in this subfamily. This is an objective
failure for a restricted witness pool, not a Cerny threshold lower bound.

<a id="direct-attack-periodic-three-a-gap--independent-controls-and-ordinary-cost"></a>
#### Independent controls and ordinary cost

The separate generator/checker are `periodic_three_a_gap.py` and
`check_periodic_three_a_gap.py`. There are19 structural controls through
n4097 and ten complete canonical controls, covering151056 THREE-a words.
The checker imports no generator. It checks colors, delta invariance,
the actual full words and all zero/one/two/three-a standard forms in
the complete scope, and eight literal small reset witnesses. Seven
corruptions are rejected. Single-letter particle checks total19467444;
the forward particle total includes the separate upper witnesses.

At p4,m2,n33 the unrestricted ordinary minimum is13, versus restricted35.
At p5,m2,n41 it is16, versus restricted44. The ordinary lower certificates
have36308 vertices in total and38680 checked edges; closure induction
covers ALL words below the corresponding minimum, including any a-count.
Literal witnesses attain the minima. These are finite computational
proofs only; the existing Lean n25 minimum10 remains separate.

At p8,n65 and p16,n129, an ordinary BFS reaches its200000-state cap.
That event is explicitly INCOMPLETE, not an absence or lower-bound result.
A separate pruned beam search supplies literal ordinary upper witnesses
of lengths21 and39, respectively, both<=n and both with more thanTHREE a.
The checker independently checks those words but makes NO minimum claim.
No ordinary cost bound is asserted for all p,m or for the largest controls.

The scoped audit preserves the release snapshots, old formal sources and
historical registry. It does not claim a full historical or release rerun.
This refutes a broader short-word shortcut and leaves the actual general
mathematical targets open.

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--sharp-profile-sensitive-compression-of-a-minimum-congruence-class"></a>
### Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Continuation notice: [Terminal kernels refine Frankl compression at every rank](#direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl) strengthens the tail
bound at every rank, repairs the four nonuniform n22 gaps, and routes
a uniform quotient reset to a singular class. Thus all congruences
are excluded from a state-minimal counterexample at n<=22, and a
uniform profile must have h>=6m. The older bounds and arithmetic
gaps below document the original checkpoint, not the current boundary.

Date: 2026-09-30. **PROVED on paper**, for arbitrary finite alphabets and
all state sizes under the hypotheses below. Publication priority is
**OPEN**. No Lean or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim. The finite sample and
independent exact certificate checks are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED**
only in their stated scope.

This continues [Short first returns, compression of a block, and a stronger quotient lift](#direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift). It strengthens first
compression of a minimum class, rather than claiming a smaller cutoff
for a synchronizing first-return alphabet.

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--theorem"></a>
#### Theorem

Let A be an n-state DFA with a congruence theta having m>=2 classes.
Assume its QUOTIENT is strongly connected. Let C be a smallest class,
of size h>=2, and assume C is compressible in A. The base DFA need not
be strongly connected or synchronizing. Define

    rho = max_D dist_(A/theta)(D,C),
    N = sum_D (|D|-h+1) = n-m(h-1).

Then

    c(C) <= N+rho <= n-m(h-2)-1.                         (1)

Both are bounds on literal original-letter word length. There is also
a singular word returning C into C of length at most N+2rho. At least
one singular FIRST-return word has length at most N+2rho, by factoring
this return at consecutive returns to C. This last statement supplies
one nonpermutation macro; it does not assert that the entire alphabet
below that smaller cutoff synchronizes.

If C is not a minimum class, a shortest quotient path to any smaller
class already gives c(C)<=m-1. Thus the difficult whole-class case is
precisely the minimum-class case of (1).

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--proof"></a>
##### Proof

Set g=[C]/h, the uniform stochastic row on C. For each class D, choose
a shortest quotient-state word r_D sending D into C; r_C is empty.
All these words have length at most rho. Put T=N+rho. Since every
class has at least h states, N>=m.

Suppose no word of length at most T compresses C. For each D, a
quotient-state path from C to D has length at most m-1. Concatenate
it with r_D. Its length is at most m-1+rho<T. The resulting h-set
must still have h states and lie in C, so it is all of C. In particular
the restriction of r_D to D surjects onto C.

Write C={c_1,...,c_h}. On rows x in R^n define h-1 forms supported
in D, one for each j<h:

    F_(D,j)(x) = sum_(p in D, p r_D=c_j) x_p
                 - (1/h) sum_(p in D) x_p.

Surjectivity of D r_D onto C makes these h-1 forms independent.
Different D have disjoint supports, so all m(h-1) forms together are
independent. Their common kernel K therefore has dimension N.

For ANY word w of length at most N, Cw lies in one congruence class D.
The word w r_D has length at most N+rho=T, so by the supposition it
maps C bijectively onto C. Consequently (g M_w) M_(r_D)=g.
Every form supported in D vanishes on g M_w; the forms supported in
other classes vanish because g M_w has no coordinates there. Therefore

    V_N = span{g M_w : |w|<=N} subset K.

Let V_i be these ascending orbit spans. Starting from dim(V_0)=1,
N strict increases would give dim(V_N)>=N+1, which is impossible.
Thus V_i=V_(i+1) at some i<N. Such an equality makes V_i invariant
under every letter matrix. Its span then contains every later orbit
row, all of which must lie in K.

Now use the assumption that C IS compressible: let z compress it,
with Cz contained in D. Appending r_D still leaves fewer than h
states, all in C. But its row g M_(z r_D) belongs to K and is
supported in C. The h-1 equations for C, together with total mass
one, require this row to be g, whose support is all h states. This
contradiction proves (1).

Appending the appropriate r_D to a compressing word from (1) proves
the N+2rho return claim. If every first-return factor were a permutation
of C, their composition would be a permutation of C, contradicting
its smaller rank. This proves the singular first-return corollary.

The proof uses a standard ascending-chain span argument, but includes
one independent family of h-1 balance equations for EVERY quotient
class. Its dimension budget is N, rather than the n-h outside-state
budget in the short-return theorem. It concerns the full initial class.

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--sharp-infinite-family-at-every-class-size-h2"></a>
#### Sharp infinite family, at every class size h>=2

Fix h>=2 and t=jh+1 with any integer j>=1. Let

    C={0,...,h-1}, O={h,...,h+t-1}, n=h+t,
    a(q)=h+q                     for q in C,
    a(h+k)=h+(k+1 mod t)         for 0<=k<t,
    b(q)=q                       for q in C,
    b(h+k)=k mod h               for 0<=k<t.

The partition C|O is a congruence, with h as its minimum size and
rho=1. The DFA is strongly connected: a cycles O, b reaches every
member of C, and a exits C into O.

Every first return is b or a^k b, k>=1. For k<=t-h+1 the h outside
trajectories are a contiguous nonwrapping window and b maps them
bijectively onto C. At k=t-h+2 the window wraps for the first time.
The induced colors are 2,3,...,h-1,0,0 (for h=2 they are 0,0), so
that return loses one state. Before it, every returning factor is a
permutation and a acts injectively on the outside trajectories. Hence

    c(C)=t-h+3=n-2h+3=N+rho.                           (2)

The DFA is synchronizing, not merely compressible. The short return
a^2 b is an h-cycle on C. Compose the first singular return a^(t-h+2)b
with (a^2 b)^(h-2) to obtain the map fixing 0,...,h-2 and sending h-1
to h-2. This adjacent collapse and the h-cycle are a conjugate of the
Cerny alphabet, hence reset C. Prepending b sends the whole Q into C.
For h=2 the h-2 exponent is zero and the singular return is constant.

Thus (1) is SHARP at infinitely many n, for every fixed h>=2,
already for binary SC synchronizing DFAs with two classes. The h=2
case includes the earlier n-h+1 sharp cutoff family. These examples
still have e(C)=1, since Qb=C; they do not refute a linear extension
bound.

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--counterexample-first-computation-and-verification-boundary"></a>
#### Counterexample-first computation and verification boundary

class_compression_pressure.py proposes 20000 deterministic adaptive
alphabets with injective class maps where sizes permit, over fourteen
fixed profiles. It retains 18 improving SC synchronizing inputs and
35 sharp-family controls (h=2..8, j=1..5). Of the proposals, 3588 are
SC synchronizing. This is a sample, not an exhaustive automaton cover.

check_class_compression_pressure.py uses a separate reverse-subset
distance computation and a separate forward quotient-distance BFS.
It verifies all 53 retained certificates, 30727 subset vertices,
literal compression/reset/routing words, all 35 equality cases, and
rejection of four deliberately corrupted fields. The generator and
checker are distinct implementations; neither replaces the proof.
The weaker theorem hypotheses (quotient SC and class compressibility)
are justified by the proof, not by claiming that the SC synchronizing
sample exhausts them.

Reproduce with:

    python -m direct_attack.class_compression_pressure --trials 20000 --seed 20261014 --out scripts/direct_attack/data/class_compression_pressure.json
    python -m direct_attack.check_class_compression_pressure

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--a-stronger-all-profile-minimal-counterexample-reduction"></a>
#### A stronger all-profile minimal-counterexample reduction

Now assume A is SC synchronizing. Once the first word from (1) drops
the whole class below h, the fiber-Frankl bound from
[Short first returns, compression of a block, and a stronger quotient lift](#direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift) applies at each remaining rank. With
J_(h-1)(s)=sum_(k=2)^(h-1) binom(s-k+2,2), this proves

    reset_A(C) <= N+rho+sum_D J_(h-1)(|D|).               (4)

There is a useful elementary refinement at the final pair step. Let
P=sum_D binom(|D|,2) be the number of pairs lying within classes,
and let K be the number of those pairs merged by at least one letter.
A shortest pair-compressing path cannot visit a pair of this terminal
kind before its last transition: at such a pair it could merge in
one step. The earlier pairs are distinct. Hence ANY synchronizable
pair inside a class compresses within P-K+1 steps.

In a synchronizing DFA K>=1. Also K>=s_max-h: follow a simple quotient
path from a largest class to a smallest one. On every decreasing-size
edge D->E, its letter collapses at least |D|-|E| pairs in D. Distinct
source classes have disjoint pairs, and the sum of positive size drops
on the path is at least s_max-h. With exactly two classes of sizes
(h,t), strong connectivity forces some letter to map the t-class
directly into the h-class. Writing t=qh+r, 0<=r<h, gives the stronger
balanced-fiber lower bound

    K >= K_0=max{1, r binom(q+1,2)+(h-r)binom(q,2)}.

For arbitrary profiles use K_0=max{1,s_max-h}. For h>=3, replacing the
rank-two term in (4) consequently proves

    reset_A(C) <= N+rho+sum_D J_(h-1)(|D|)-(K_0-1).      (5)

This terminal-pair count is a basic shortest-path refinement, not
a novelty claim. It is not applied at h=2, where (1) already resets C.
After quotient reset and routing, a square quotient gives the literal
reset upper bound

    m(m-1)+n-m(h-1)+(m-1)
        +sum_D J_(h-1)(|D|)-(K_0-1),    h>=3.            (6)

Take the minimum of (6), the short-return lift, and the old fiber
bound. The old two bounds already excluded every minimum-h=6 profile
except (6,14) and (6,15). Applying (4), WITHOUT needing a pair saving,
repairs exactly those two gaps:

    (6,14): rt<=337<361;  (6,15): rt<=388<400.

Thus in a STATE-MINIMAL Cerny counterexample every nontrivial
congruence has EVERY class of size at least SEVEN. This is an all-n
statement: for h=6,m>=4 the old minimum-n gap
35m^2-161m+126 is positive and increases with n; m=3 requires only
n=18..21 and m=2 only n=12..21, handled by the convex fiber sum and
the two repairs above. The use of the six-state square is supplied
by state minimality; (6) itself uses only the quotient square.

Combining this with the previous growing-size inequality gives the
stronger necessary condition on EVERY class:

    |D| >= max{7, ceil((3+sqrt(4n-3))/2)}.               (7)

It also excludes all nontrivial congruences at n<22 in a state-minimal
counterexample. After h<=6 is removed, n<=21 allows exactly twenty
two-class profiles with h>=7, plus (7,7,7). Applying (6) gives the
following maximum bounds over the two-class profiles at each n:

| n | maximum bound | square |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 14 | 115 | 169 |
| 15 | 141 | 196 |
| 16 | 171 | 225 |
| 17 | 206 | 256 |
| 18 | 246 | 289 |
| 19 | 291 | 324 |
| 20 | 341 | 361 |
| 21 | 397 | 400 |

The triple profile has bound 176<400. These are all the possible
profiles in that bounded range, not a claim that all automata with
n<22 satisfy Cerny. In particular simple automata are untouched.
At n=22 the combined bounds are still inconclusive for the two-class
profiles (7,15), (8,14), (9,13), (10,12), (11,11), with upper bounds
455,460,454,446,443 against the square 441. They are bound gaps, NOT
automata violating Cerny. Larger profiles remain open as well.

The independent checker verifies the two repaired bounds, 9900 h=6
integer cases, all twenty-one bounded profiles and the n22 arithmetic
gaps. The proof and profile convexity supply the all-n conclusion.

<a id="direct-attack-profile-class-compression--why-a-full-class-reset-bound-remains-a-major-problem"></a>
#### Why a full class-reset bound remains a major problem

After the first drop, the current image is a proper subset of a class.
Returning it to C no longer forces the uniform row on ALL of C, so
the m(h-1) balance equations above cannot be reused at lower ranks.
The n=3 reachable-image counterexample in [Short first returns, compression of a block, and a stronger quotient lift](#direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift)
already refutes treating those proper subsets as nonsplitting classes.
Neither (1) nor its equality family supplies a compatible global chain.

One stronger sufficient statement would be

    reset_A(C) <= (h-1)(n-1).                            (3)

This is **OPEN**, with no all-n proof or counterexample supplied here.
If (3) held for every minimum congruence class in every SC synchronizing
DFA, a square quotient would lift strictly for EVERY size profile:
after quotient reset and routing the total would be at most

    m(m-1)+(h-1)(n-1) < (n-1)^2,  n>=mh, h,m>=2.

Indeed the gap is (n-1)(n-h)-m(m-1), increasing for n>=mh, and at
n=mh it is h(m-1)(mh-1)-m(m-1)>0. Singleton classes are handled
directly by quotient reset and routing.

But (3) itself would already give a UNIVERSAL QUADRATIC reset bound.
For any SC synchronizing h-state DFA D, form A on Q(D)x{0,1}. Lift
every original letter diagonally, add a block swap preserving q,
and add a block collapse (q,i)->(q,0). This is SC synchronizing and
has two congruence classes of size h. A word resets Q(D)x{0} exactly
when deleting the two new letters gives a reset word of D: those
new letters never change q. Thus reset_A(Q(D)x{0})=rt(D).
Applying (3) with n=2h would give rt(D)<=(h-1)(2h-1).

This exact reduction is **PROVED**, while (3) stays **OPEN**. It
explains why improving the full class-reset cost cannot be treated
as a routine consequence of having solved its first compression.
No universal e(S)<=2n, universal linear extension constant, or
unrestricted Cerny square is established by this continuation.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-bridge-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-bridge-obstruction--one-extra-state-already-forces-a-quadratic-kernel-bridge"></a>
### One extra state already forces a quadratic kernel bridge

**PROVED (paper), NOVELTY OPEN.** This is a negative structural result, not
an improvement of a general reset upper bound. It isolates why the linear
kernel bridge cannot be used at the neighboring, larger rank. The obstruction
occurs in the classical circular Cerny family.

For every integer h>=1 put n=6h. Use states Z/nZ and letters

    qa=q+1 mod n;  (n-1)b=0;  qb=q otherwise.

Let S={0,2h,4h}. Partition Q into the two intervals
F0={0,...,3h-1}, F1={3h,...,6h-1}. There is an actual rank-two word u whose
two fibers are exactly F0,F1 (constructed below). The exact shortest length
of a bridge v satisfying |Svu|<2 is

    6h^2+2h = n^2/6+n/3.                                    (QB)

Thus no universal O(n) bound exists for the bridge v even when |S|=3,
rank(u)=2, and A is strongly connected, synchronizing, binary and circular.
S is also reachable from Q; this is not an unreachable-subset obstruction.
In particular, the tested candidate

    |v| <= (|S|-rank(u)+1)(n-rank(u)+1)

fails for all h>=2 in this family, and already has a separate C7 witness
with exact distance 13 rather than its proposed 12.
No state-minimality is claimed until the six-state rank-excess case is audited.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-bridge-obstruction--full-lower-bound-repeated-hits-on-one-original-trajectory"></a>
#### Full lower bound: repeated hits on one original trajectory

For any word prefix let A be its number of a's. For each original state
q in {0,2h,4h}, let B_q count the b's at which its current trajectory is
n-1. Its image is congruent to q+A+B_q modulo n: a always advances one
position and b does so precisely at n-1.

Suppose all three final counts B_q are <=h. Put y_q=q+A+B_q. The differences

    y_(2h)-y_0 = 2h+B_(2h)-B_0,
    y_(4h)-y_(2h) = 2h+B_(4h)-B_(2h),
    n+y_0-y_(4h) = 2h+B_0-B_(4h)

lie in [h,3h] and sum to n. Thus the images are distinct and these are
their cyclic gaps. Every gap is at most 3h. But a subset contained in an
interval of 3h states has a gap at least n-(3h-1)=3h+1. It cannot miss a
fiber. Every successful bridge therefore has B_q>=h+1 for some fixed
original q.

After each counted b hit of q its trajectory is 0. Before the next counted
hit it must reach n-1. No intervening b changes this trajectory (otherwise
it would be another counted hit). Hence there are at least n-1 a's between
consecutive counted hits. Before its first hit there are at least 2h-1 a's:
the possible initial states are 0,2h,4h. These intervals are disjoint, so

    #a >= (2h-1)+h(n-1),  #b >= h+1.

Their sum is 6h^2+2h. Original labels remain tracked after a collision;
the argument allows collisions, ineffective b's and extra rotations.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-bridge-obstruction--matching-upper-bound"></a>
#### Matching upper bound

Take v=a^(2h-1)b(a^(n-1)b)^h. After its first b the subset is
{0,2h-1,4h-1}. After j further blocks, 0<=j<=h, it is
{0,2h-1-j,4h-1-j}. At j=h this is {0,h-1,3h-1}, contained in F0. At h=1
the duplicate 0 is removed as set semantics require. The length is
2h+hn=6h^2+2h. This proves the exact formula including h=1.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-bridge-obstruction--actual-kernel-word-with-the-right-composition-order"></a>
#### Actual kernel word, with the right composition order

For i in Z/nZ define

    e_i=a^((n-1-i) mod n) b a^((i+1) mod n).

Its transformation sends i to i+1 and fixes every other state. Concatenate
e_0 e_1 ... e_(3h-2), followed by e_(3h) ... e_(6h-2). This sends F0 to 3h-1
and F1 to 6h-1; these targets are distinct and fixed throughout the opposite
block's merges. Its fibers are exactly the claimed partition. The word has
length (n-2)(n+1); its length is not asserted to be minimal. We do not add u
as a new letter: doing so changes the search alphabet and invalidates the
gap lower bound.

For reachability of S, concatenate the local e_i's inside each of the three
cyclic intervals ending at 0,2h,4h. Each interval collapses to its endpoint,
and these endpoints are not changed by the other intervals' maps. The
certificate stores this actual reach word and the independent checker
maps Q through it. No shortest-rank reach assertion is needed for the
obstruction theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-quadratic-bridge-obstruction--independent-audit-and-interpretation"></a>
#### Independent audit and interpretation

The computer experiment works on the complete transition-closed collection
of all nonempty subsets of size <=3, rather than a 2^n graph. A saved
Bellman potential plus a target-reaching word certifies each exact bridge
distance, independently of the trajectory argument. Kernel words are verified by
mapping every original state. See bridge_obstruction.py and check_bridges.py.
The h=1..10 instances (n=6..60) agree with the exact formula. The checker
also rejects deliberately corrupted potentials and kernel transformations.

The ordinary |S|=rank(u) bridge remains linear. This theorem concerns
|S|=rank(u)+1. A hypothetical splice with a larger plateau image therefore
cannot simply replace the singleton-rich mechanism with a constant-excess
linear bridge. It does not refute other averaged, fiber-aware, or amortized
bridges.

<a id="direct-attack-quotient-fiber-lift"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-quotient-fiber-lift--a-bounded-fiber-quotient-lift"></a>
### A bounded-fiber quotient lift

**PROVED (elementary conditional bound); priority OPEN.** This is a
necessary-condition result for a state-minimal counterexample, not an
unrestricted proof of the Cerny conjecture. Words act on the right.

Let A be a synchronizing n-state DFA and let theta be a congruence with
classes C_1,...,C_m, where 1<m<n. Assume its quotient admits a reset word
of length at most B. Set

    M(theta) = sum_i (2^|C_i| - |C_i| - 1).

Then

    rt(A) <= B + M(theta).                                      (1)

Indeed, a quotient reset word u puts Qu inside one theta-class. Every
subsequent image of Qu remains inside one theta-class: this is precisely
congruence compatibility. The directed subset graph on the non-singleton
subsets contained in individual classes has M(theta) vertices. Since A is
synchronizing, Qu has a path to a singleton. A shortest such path repeats
no non-singleton subset and hence uses at most M(theta) letters. This
proves (1). It does not assume that Qu equals its containing class, that
individual classes are invariant, or that A is strongly connected.

For a state-minimal hypothetical counterexample, the smaller synchronizing
quotient obeys the square, so B=(m-1)^2 is available. Thus every nontrivial
congruence of such a counterexample must satisfy

    M(theta) > (n-1)^2 - (m-1)^2
             = (n-m)(n+m-2).                                   (2)

<a id="direct-attack-quotient-fiber-lift--rank-truncated-lift-in-the-strongly-connected-case"></a>
#### Rank-truncated lift in the strongly connected case

Suppose A is also strongly connected, so its quotient is strongly
connected. For h>=1 define

    V_h(theta) = sum_i sum_(k=2)^min(h,|C_i|) binom(|C_i|,k).

Let u be ANY quotient reset word ending in class C_t. Choose a class C_j
and a shortest quotient-state path v from C_t to C_j, of length d(t,j)
at most m-1. The actual image Quv lies in C_j and has rank at most
h=|C_j|. All later ranks are at most h, and all images stay inside a
single congruence class. A shortest residual path to a singleton repeats
no eligible non-singleton subset. Therefore

    rt(A) <= |u| + d(t,j) + V_|C_j|(theta).                 (3)

One may minimize over j and over quotient reset words u. In particular,
if the quotient has a reset word of length at most B and s is its
smallest class size, then

    rt(A) <= B + (m-1) + V_s(theta).                        (4)

The transport cost is explicitly charged. It is zero if u already ends
in a smallest class. For the n=4 counterexample below, V_2=2 and u=b
ends in such a class, so (3) gives 1+0+2=3, exactly its reset threshold.
The coarser (4) would give 4; (1) also gives the exact 3.

For s=1, (4) is strictly below (n-1)^2 whenever m>=2 and
B<=(m-1)^2. For s=2 put d=n-m>=1. Then

    V_2 = sum_i binom(|C_i|,2)
        <= (n/2) sum_i(|C_i|-1) = nd/2.

Subtracting the upper estimate (4) from the square leaves at least

    d(n/2+m-2) - (m-1).

Since n>=m+1 and m>=2, the parenthesis is at least 3(m-1)/2;
the remainder is therefore positive. This independently reconstructs
the qualitative published 1/2-class lift. No priority claim is made.

<a id="direct-attack-quotient-fiber-lift--pair-truncated-lift-and-three-state-fibers"></a>
#### Pair-truncated lift and three-state fibers

Put P(theta)=sum_i binom(|C_i|,2). Every unordered pair initially inside
one congruence class stays inside some class until it merges. Because A
is synchronizing, a shortest merger path exists; it cannot repeat any of
the P(theta) nonmerged pairs. Its length is at most P(theta). From any
subset of rank at most h inside a class, merge an arbitrary pair and
repeat. Rank never increases, so at most h-1 mergers suffice. Using the
same quotient reset word and charged class transport as (3) proves

    rt(A) <= |u| + d(t,j) + (|C_j|-1) P(theta).            (5)

One should take the minimum of (1), (3), and (5), not sum their costs.
For class sizes (4,7), (5) gives 1+1+3(6+21)=83, strictly below the
square 100. The full-subset count and (4) do not settle this profile.

In fact, (5) strictly lifts the square whenever the smallest class has
size three. For m=2, let the other class have size t>=3. A quotient reset
costs at most one, class transport at most one, and P=3+binom(t,2).
The resulting upper bound is t^2-t+8, while (n-1)^2=(t+2)^2;
their difference is 5t-4>0. For m>=3, put d=n-m and note that every
class then has size at least three, so d>=2m. Since
P<=nd/2, the difference between the square and (5)'s coarse estimate
with |u|<=(m-1)^2, d(t,j)<=m-1 is at least

    d(m-2) - (m-1) >= 2m(m-2)-(m-1) > 0.

Thus **a state-minimal counterexample cannot have ANY congruence class
of size at most three**: sizes one and two follow from (4), and size
three from (5). The same strict conditional result applies to a
square-extremal automaton whenever its quotient obeys the square.
The conclusion still leaves simple automata and larger-fiber quotients.

This is a computable rigidity condition on the entire fiber-size profile.
In particular, if all classes have sizes between 3 and 6, (2) is impossible.
For m=2, direct checking of the ten unordered pairs of sizes in {3,4,5,6}
shows M <= (n-1)^2-1; the closest cases are (3,6), with 61<=63, and
(6,6), with 114<=120. For m>=3, each summand satisfies

    2^s-s-1 <= (s-1)(n+m-2),  3<=s<=6.

To see this, n>=3m. If s<=5, n+m-2>=10 and the largest ratio
(2^s-s-1)/(s-1) is 26/4. If s=6, n>=3m+3,
so n+m-2>=13>57/5. Summing proves the inequality.

Rodaro--Venturi, Proposition 3.1, already proves the qualitative 1/2-class
lift. Since a state-minimal counterexample is strongly connected,
combining the independent (4) argument with (2) gives: **every
nontrivial congruence of a state-minimal
counterexample has a class of at least seven states.** This is only a
necessary condition; simple automata have no nontrivial congruence.
The pair bound (5) above gives the stronger independent restriction that
*each* class has at least four states.

There is a sharper distinction when theta has at least three classes.
If all classes have sizes 3..7 and m=3 or 4, the 105 unordered size
profiles satisfy (2)'s opposite inequality by direct integer enumeration.
For m>=5, put d=n-m. If no class has size 7, each summand of M is at most
(57/5)(s-1), while n+m-2>=4m-2>=18. If some class has size 7, every
summand is at most 20(s-1), while n>=3m+4 implies
n+m-2>=4m+2>=22. Hence (2) is impossible for every m>=3.
Combining again with the self-contained 1/2-class result: **a nontrivial
congruence of a state-minimal counterexample has a class of size at least
seven if m=2, and at least eight if m>=3.**

The counted inequalities are in fact strict. For m=2, class sizes 3..6,
the smallest square slack after subtracting M is 2, at (3,6). For m=3,4,
sizes 3..7, the smallest is 8, at (3,7,7). The m>=5 inequalities above
also have strict slack. Rodaro--Venturi's 1/2-class proof is strict for
n>=3. Consequently, if a strongly connected synchronizing A has a
nontrivial congruence whose quotient obeys the square, then A cannot be
*square-extremal* when its largest class is at most six; with m>=3 the
threshold is seven. The qualifier about the quotient is essential here.

The full-subset count (1) alone stops at seven: the profile (3,7) has
M=124 and square slack 80. But (4) uses only V_3=4+56=60 and gives
rt(A)<=1+1+60=62<81 if its two-state quotient obeys the square and A is
strongly connected; (5) sharpens that upper bound to 50. Formula (5)
also excludes (4,7) with bound 83<100. Thus a two-class congruence with
maximum class size seven in a state-minimal counterexample must have its
other class of size at least five. A failure of a counting criterion is not an automaton
violating the square. The new bound and corollary are not
claimed to be new in the literature. They refine the repository's earlier
blanket warning that quotient synchronization has an uncontrolled tail.

The frozen 20260930 sample contains 230 synchronizing two-class lifts over
all ten unordered profiles with sizes 3..6. An independent reverse-subset
Bellman checker verifies each complete DFA, its quotient action, reset
distance, post-quotient tail and both inequalities; it also enumerates
all 5440 ordered profiles of three through six classes in this size range,
plus the 105 unordered m=3,4 profiles with class sizes 3..7.
These checks audit the statement and its arithmetic, but do not replace
the general proof or exhaust the automata in any class.

Primary context: [Rodaro--Venturi, *The hereditariness problem for the
Cerny conjecture*, Proposition 3.1 and Section 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.17992).

<a id="direct-attack-quotient-fiber-lift--a-stronger-additive-lift-fails-at-the-smallest-possible-state-size"></a>
#### A stronger additive lift fails at the smallest possible state size

**REFUTED:** the tempting assertion

    rt(A) <= rt(A/theta) + (max_i |C_i|-1)^2

even for strongly connected synchronizing A. At n=4 take

    a=[2,3,0,1], b=[1,0,0,0],
    C_0={0,1}, C_1={2,3}.

The quotient has a swapping letter a and a constant letter b, so its reset
threshold is 1. On Q, b yields {0,1}; a sends this set to {2,3}; then b
merges it. The word bab resets in three letters. No word of length at most
two resets: a preserves Q, b gives {0,1}, and both a and b preserve its
cardinality at the next step. Thus rt(A)=3>1+(2-1)^2=2. A is strongly
connected: from 0, b reaches 1, a reaches 2, and ba reaches 3.
The residual set must *move to another fiber* before it can merge.

This is state-minimal over arbitrary alphabets within the stated SC class.
At n=2 there is no proper nontrivial congruence. At n=3 such a congruence
has classes of sizes 2 and 1. The quotient is a strongly connected
two-state synchronizing DFA and therefore has a one-letter reset. If it
lands in the singleton class, it resets A. If it lands in the doubleton,
strong connectivity of the two-state quotient gives a one-letter move to
the singleton class, so A resets in at most two letters. That is the
proposed additive bound for max class size two. A complete unary/binary/
ternary n=3 scan independently checks 3714 qualifying ordered alphabet/
congruence designations with no violation; the all-alphabet minimum rests
on the preceding short proof.

The counterexample does not challenge (1): here M=2, so its valid bound
is rt(A)<=1+2=3, attained exactly. This shows why the proof counts
non-singleton subsets in *every* congruence class.

<a id="direct-attack-reflection-core-tradeoff--a-fast-reset-with-a-strict-singular-count-versus-word-cost-tradeoff"></a>
### A fast reset with a strict singular-count versus word-cost tradeoff

Date:2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper)** for the explicit all-n family below,
with a **FORMALLY VERIFIED abstract finite-depth lemma** and separate
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** literal controls. No novelty claim.
General Cerny remains **OPEN**; this family is already in the coprime
square class, and the result strengthens its behavior and method boundary.

For M>=3 take Q={r} union Z_M, r=M, b cycling the core/fixing r, and

    a(r)=0, a(0)=a(1)=r,
    a(q)=M+1-q for 2<=q<M.

Thus the remaining core permutation is a reflection, L1,dM-1. Both
original letters have multiple cycles. The return c=a^2 is literally
