<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--1-adversarial-audit-of-the-existing-return-statements"></a>
#### 1. Adversarial audit of the existing return statements

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--actual-first-returns-and-the-full-monoid"></a>
##### Actual first returns and the full monoid

For an equal-size congruence and strongly connected bijective-edge graph J,
choose shortest J-paths p_D:C->D and r_D:D->C, with empty paths at C.
A shortest p_D has no internal visit to C, and a shortest r_D has no
internal visit to C. Thus every `p_D a r_(Da)` is a genuine first return:
if Da=C, the a-step is the final return; otherwise the suffix first enters
C at its end. This also covers D=C and an immediate return letter. Every
nonempty `p_D r_D` is likewise a genuine first return. All lengths are
at most 2m-1; the latter loops have length at most 2m-2.

Composition must be read in the repository's right-action convention.
Let `f_(D,a)=p_D a p_(Da)^(-1)` as an abstract coordinate transformation.
The actual generator is `g_(D,a)=f_(D,a) ell_(Da)`, where
`ell_E=p_E r_E` is an actual permutation return. Its inverse is in the
generated finite transformation monoid: if its order is t, its inverse
is its `(t-1)`st power. Therefore every f_(D,a) belongs to that monoid.
The f's telescope along any quotient path beginning and ending at C.
Conversely, every generator is an actual C-return. This proves the claimed
monoid equality, including the identity, without synchronization or base
strong connectivity assumptions.

The inverse argument is exclusively a membership argument. It cannot be
used to shorten original words. An explicit obstruction is the unary
automaton on two h-fibers in which a maps the first fiber identically to
the second and maps the second back with the h-cycle. Then J is strongly
connected, `ell=a^2` has order h, and its inverse has shortest original
return length exactly `2(h-1)`. This can exceed 2m-1 arbitrarily far.
Section 7 independently checks h=3,...,12. The unary example need not
synchronize, because the membership theorem makes no such assumption.

The statement that the generated alphabet synchronizes iff C is resettable
in A also holds: a word resetting C to a singleton in a different class
can be followed by a J-path back to C. That routing is used only for the
equivalence, not supplied as a free word in any length bound.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--sharpness-and-the-equal-two-class-boundary"></a>
##### Sharpness and the equal-two-class boundary

In the R,L,c sharp family, any singular C_0-return must first reach class
m-1, use R there, and then reach class zero again. The necessary lengths
are m-1, one, and m-1, even if identity loops are inserted. The first
singular return is consequently at length 2m-1. At that cutoff, the only
nontrivial short return actions are the cycle c and the unit collapse
`(h-1)->0`. Their macro reset threshold is the usual `(h-1)^2`; this is
a macro statement, and the original costs are unequal. The explicit
full-Q word displayed in the existing paper indeed resets. No exact
original threshold is implied.

For the nonbijective two-class family, put h=2t+1 and B={0,t}. The two
points of B+s have different x-colors for 0<=s<=2t-1: in the first half
their colors are 0,t, and in the second half they are t,0. At s=2t the
points are 2t,t-1, both with color zero. First returns through length h
are identity or x followed by those first h-1 shifts. Their rank-two
images remain in the same pair family after any further short return.
Therefore no product synchronizes. At length h+1 the exceptional pair
appears and ab merges it. The full-Q reset `b a^h b a` is valid.
The failure concerns the return cutoff, rather than the original reset
threshold or Cerny. It shows that removing bijective connectivity cannot
leave a cutoff depending only on m.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--general-short-returns-and-the-quotient-lift"></a>
##### General short returns and the quotient lift

For a congruence class C and d outside states, the row exit-span chain
stabilizes by outside depth d-1. Restrictions to the outside kill a
trajectory after a return. The congruence condition ensures every
surviving product is an actual first return, because an entire class
returns together. Hence all first-return outputs of each row lie in the
span of the outputs of actual returns of length at most d+1.

Applying this fact to each row of the short-return orbit span establishes
invariance under every return. Base strong connectivity and synchronization
then supply all reset singletons in C. The stationary-span argument is
sound: stationarity with positive letter weights makes the support of a
stationary row invariant under every letter; full orbit span forces full
support. Uniform averaging of words of lengths 0 through h-1 then supplies
strict inverse expansion for every proper subset. Strictly increasing
stationary mass on a finite set of subsets must terminate at C.

The matrix-basis algorithm truncates exit products at original exit length
d. It does not assume the h-by-d matrix space stabilizes after d-1 rounds.
The code's `range(1,len(O)+1)` and its depth guard implement that truncation.
Choosing an actual matrix basis preserves orbit spans, not transition
monoids. The stated h^2 basis bound is safe; the elementary row-sum
constraints would also give the optional sharper bound h^2-h+1.

The nonsplitting-set interpretation and its canonical membership
congruence are valid. An arbitrary reachable image cannot be substituted
for a class. The C_3 example gives the advertised failure even for
all-length first returns.

Both quotient lifts correctly pay the quotient reset and class routing
once. A macro square requires a square bound for the smaller h-state
return automaton; quotient square alone is insufficient for arbitrary h.
State minimality supplies the smaller-state hypotheses in the
minimal-counterexample deductions, with no circular n-state assumption.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--permutation-transitivity"></a>
##### Permutation transitivity

Every permutation letter's inverse is a positive power of that same
letter, so it also preserves the congruence. Hence a permutation sends
an entire class bijectively onto an entire class, not merely into it.
Class transitivity forces equal sizes and strong connectivity of J.
State transitivity implies class transitivity for every congruence.
Thus the stated exclusion and the conclusion that a state-minimal
counterexample with a state-transitive permutation subgroup is simple
are valid. Group primitivity does not follow: a block system of the
permutation subgroup need not be preserved by other letters.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--2-exact-confined-monoids-for-every-bijective-edge-scc"></a>
#### 2. Exact confined monoids for every bijective-edge SCC

**PROVED (paper).** Let theta be any congruence, potentially nonuniform,
and let K be a strongly connected component of its bijective-edge graph.
Its k classes have a common size h, since each bijective edge preserves
size. Fix C in K. A K-confined C-return is an original word whose quotient
path starts and ends at C and never leaves K. Define p_D and r_D as
shortest J-paths within K. Form the actual return alphabet

    p_D a r_(Da)      for D in K and Da in K,
    p_D r_D           for D in K\{C}.

There are at most k|Sigma|+k-1 generators, all genuine first returns, all
of length at most 2k-1. Their monoid is EXACTLY the restrictions to C of
all K-confined C-returns, including identity. The alphabet may be empty
at an isolated one-class SCC; then both monoids are the identity monoid.

Proof: use exactly the coordinate construction in section 1, but only for
edges with both endpoints in K. The loops ell_E have positive-power
inverses in the generated monoid. The coordinate maps telescope on every
K-confined quotient path. Every generator itself stays in K, proving the
reverse inclusion. This proof does not use any properties of outside
classes or an actual inverse letter.

If this confined monoid synchronizes, a quotient reset u ending at T,
followed by a quotient path from T to C, and then a macro reset gives

    rt(A) <= |u|+dist_quotient(T,C)+(2k-1)H(h).

Here A must synchronize, the quotient must allow the route, and H(h)
must be a proved reset bound for arbitrary h-state DFAs. For a uniform
congruence, k<=m, so the existing strict square comparison applies with
the larger coefficient 2m-1. Consequently a state-minimal counterexample
with a uniform congruence has a NONSYNCHRONIZING confined return monoid
in EVERY bijective-edge SCC. Requiring only that J is not strongly
connected is a weaker necessary condition.

This statement does not claim that an SCC's confined monoid equals its
all-length return monoid when returns leave K. The nonbijective boundary
is an explicit obstruction to that replacement. Nor does global
synchronization imply synchronization within some SCC.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--3-a-general-charged-local-wordprofile-lift"></a>
#### 3. A general charged local-word/profile lift

**PROVED (paper).** Let A synchronize and let its congruence quotient
be strongly connected, with class sizes s_1,...,s_m. The base DFA need
not itself be strongly connected. Let u reset the quotient to T, let D
be ANY class, and let v be ANY actual word, of original length L, whose
restriction to D has rank r. Define

    Phi_r(s_1,...,s_m)
      = sum_i sum_(k=2)^min(r,s_i) binom(s_i-k+2,2).

Then

    rt(A) <= |u|+dist_quotient(T,D)+L+Phi_r(s_1,...,s_m).   (A)

Proof of the compression ingredient: for a shortest word compressing a
k-set within a congruence class, all preterminal images S_i are k-sets
inside classes. Pull back a final merged pair along each injective
prefix to P_i subset S_i. If P_i were contained in an earlier S_j,
that earlier prefix followed by the suffix beginning at S_i would
compress sooner. Within a size-s class the standard Frankl renewing
sequence theorem bounds this subsequence by binom(s-k+2,2). Sum over
classes of size at least k. A synchronizing A guarantees compressibility
of every such set, so these bounds apply at each actual remaining rank.

Now u followed by the quotient route sends Q into D. Applying v sends
that image to rank at most r within one class. Compress at each rank
k=r,r-1,...,2, skipping ranks that do not occur. The displayed positive
rank budgets sum to Phi_r, proving (A). All routing, v, and compression
words are charged original words. No return condition is imposed on v.

If the quotient satisfies the square, coarsening only its reset and route
costs gives

    rt(A) <= m(m-1)+L+Phi_r.                              (B)

Thus in a state-minimal counterexample every actual local rank-r word
must satisfy the necessary condition

    L > (n-1)^2-m(m-1)-Phi_r.                            (C)

This is useful only when its right side is nonnegative; no unconditional
quadratic bound follows for arbitrary ranks or profiles.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--4-all-n-exclusion-of-low-class-restriction-rank"></a>
#### 4. All-n exclusion of low class-restriction rank

**PROVED (paper).** Let A synchronize and its quotient be strongly
connected. Suppose its congruence is uniform with m>=2 classes of size
h>=2, and the quotient satisfies the square. If ANY letter has
a singular restriction of rank r<=2m+1 on ANY class, then

    rt(A) <= m(m-1)+1
             +m[binom(h+1,3)-binom(h-r+2,3)] < (mh-1)^2. (D)

The graph J can be disconnected. The restriction rank is measured on
one h-class, and is not the letter's rank on the full mh-state DFA.

The non-strict bound is (B) with L=1 and the telescoping binomial sum.
It remains to prove strictness for all integers m,h. The budget increases
with r. If h<=2m+2, use r<=h-1; its maximum is
`(m-1)^2+m binom(h+1,3)`. Its square gap equals

    m(h-1)[(h+1)(6m-h)-12]/6.

For 2<=h<=2m+2, the concave product `(h+1)(6m-h)` is bounded below
by the smaller of its two endpoint values, `18m-6` and
`8m^2+8m-6`. Both exceed 12 for m>=2. The gap is strictly positive.

If h>=2m+2, use r<=2m+1. Direct summation gives

    sum_(k=2)^(2m+1) binom(h-k+2,2)
       =m h^2-2m^2 h+m(4m^2-1)/3.

The square gap in (D) at this maximal r is

    2m(m^2-1)h+m-(4m^4+2m^2)/3.

It increases with h. At h=2m+2 it is
`m(8m^3+12m^2-14m-9)/3`, strictly positive for m>=2. This proves
(D) for every size, with no finite size assumption.

In particular, EVERY singular letter restriction in a state-minimal
counterexample with a uniform congruence must have rank at least
2m+2. This adds a local-rank barrier to the existing h>=6m restriction
and the SCC conditions. For m=2 it prohibits all singular ranks 1,...,5
on either class, regardless of how large h is. Equation (C) is the
stronger length-sensitive constraint for actual words, including those
that leave and revisit a bijective-edge SCC.

The counterexample corollary uses the complete strong-connectivity
reduction in [Necessary conditions, with quantifiers kept explicit](#direct-attack-minimal-counterexample): state minimality forces the base
DFA to be strongly connected, so every quotient is strongly connected.
A square quotient without the routing hypothesis is not sufficient for
the arbitrary-source-class theorem.

This rank barrier covers alphabets whose full-DFA letters have large
rank. In the equal-two-class boundary family, both letters have full
rank h, but a has rank two on C; J is disconnected and (D) still applies.
For example h=13 gives n=26 and full letter ranks 13, despite local rank
two. The saved boundary controls explicitly check this distinction.

The threshold 2m+1 is the largest FIXED r for which this unsaved Frankl
budget can give an all-h exclusion. At r=2m+2 its h^2 coefficient is
`m(r-1)/2=m^2+m/2`, exceeding the square's m^2 coefficient. The saved
large-h controls show this budget failure. This is a limitation of the
bound; it is not a realizable automaton counterexample and does not
refute a stronger theorem using several terminal kernels or actual
trajectory restrictions.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--5-all-nonuniform-profiles-local-rank-at-most-three-lifts-the-square"></a>
#### 5. All nonuniform profiles: local rank at most three lifts the square

**PROVED (paper).** Let A synchronize, let its quotient be strongly
connected, and let theta be ANY nontrivial congruence, with m classes
of positive sizes s_1,...,s_m and `2<=m<n`. Assume the quotient satisfies
the square. If a word v of original length L has rank at most three on
ANY class, then

    rt(A) <= m(m-1)+L+Phi_3
          = sum_i s_i^2-2n+m^2+L.                         (E)

In particular a LETTER of class-restriction rank at most three gives
`rt(A)<=(n-1)^2`. The displayed budget is strictly below the square
except possibly for the profile (1,2), where equality suffices to
exclude a counterexample. Neither uniform class sizes nor bijective
connectivity is assumed.

Proof. The identity

    Phi_3(s_1,...,s_m)=sum_i(s_i-1)^2

holds also for singleton classes: s=1 contributes zero, s=2 contributes
`binom(2,2)=1`, and s>=3 contributes
`binom(s,2)+binom(s-1,2)=(s-1)^2`. Formula (E) follows from (B) and
`Phi_r<=Phi_3` for r<=3. Its gap below the square is

    K+1-L, where K=n^2-sum_i s_i^2-m^2.                  (F)

If all s_i>=2, then

    K=2 sum_(i<j) s_i s_j-m^2
       >=4m(m-1)-m^2=m(3m-4)>0.

For arbitrary positive class sizes, put s_i=1+x_i, with x_i>=0 and
sum_i x_i=t=n-m>=1. Since `sum_i x_i^2<=t^2`,

    sum_i s_i^2=m+2t+sum_i x_i^2 <= m+2t+t^2,
    K >= 2t(m-1)-m >= m-2 >= 0.

Thus L=1 always gives a nonnegative square gap. It can vanish only
when m=2,t=1, hence for the profile (1,2). All other nontrivial profiles
give a positive gap. This proves the letter conclusion without relying
on a separately established singleton-class exclusion. The routing
hypothesis remains necessary; quotient square alone does not provide
a path to an arbitrary source class.

For a state-minimal counterexample, base strong connectivity supplies
the routing, and state minimality supplies the square for its smaller
quotient. Consequently EVERY letter restriction on EVERY class of
EVERY nontrivial congruence has rank at least four. This includes
nonsingular restrictions on small classes: no class of size at most
three can occur. More strongly, EVERY actual word of local rank at
most three must satisfy

    L > n^2-sum_i s_i^2-m^2+1 = K+1.                    (G)

These ranks concern one class, not the full DFA. The rank-two/rank-one
specializations of (C) may give still stronger length constraints.
The identity congruence m=n and the universal congruence m=1 are excluded
from this theorem; their substitution would invalidate the profile-gap
argument or the smaller-quotient interpretation.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--a-family-separating-local-rank-three-from-whole-letter-rank-three"></a>
##### A family separating local rank three from whole-letter rank three

For h>=4 and j>=1 put t=jh+1. Use classes C={0,...,h-1} and O indexed
0,...,t-1. Let a send local states 0 and 1 of C to indices 0 and 1 of O,
and all other states of C to index h of O; let a cycle O. Let b fix C
and map index q of O to q mod h in C. Both letters have full-DFA ranks
t and h, respectively, while a has rank THREE on C. The base DFA is
SC: O cycles, b reaches every C-state, and every C-state exits under a.
The graph J has two isolated one-class SCCs.

The literal word `b a^t b a b` resets Q. The initial b sends Q onto C.
After a^t the three O-indices are `{t-1,0,h-1}`; b maps them to
`{0,h-1}`, a maps those to O-indices `{0,h}`, and b merges them at zero.
Its length is t+4; no exact reset threshold is claimed.

This family makes the scope difference explicit: neither full-DFA
letter has rank at most three. For h=13,t=27, n=40, full letter ranks
are 27 and 13, while (E) with L=1 gives 823<1521. The twelve saved
controls use h in {4,7,13,21} and j in {1,2,3}; their full transitions,
literal resets, local ranks, SC properties, and disconnected J are
checked separately. The family illustrates the theorem; it is not
claimed to attain its reset bound.

<a id="direct-attack-return-monoid-independent-audit--6-proof-limitations-and-attribution"></a>
#### 6. Proof limitations and attribution

The new consequences use the existing class-sensitive Frankl mechanism
and the elementary finite-semigroup coordinate argument. Exact priority
is not established. The current primary-source records checked for
context are [Rodaro--Venturi, arXiv:2509.17992v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17992)
and [Berlinkov--Szykula, arXiv:1412.8363v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.8363).
The former describes the general hereditary lifting problem as open;
the latter explicitly studies low-rank-word reset bounds. These facts
support the context, not a novelty claim for (A)--(G).

There is no general theorem that every synchronizing uniform congruence
has a synchronizing bijective SCC. There is no claim that every singular
letter has small LOCAL rank. In particular, near-permutation restrictions
can obey the new rank barrier. Neither the SCC nor local-rank mechanisms
reach simple automata. For nonuniform local ranks above three, the exact
profile bound (A) remains available without an alleged clean all-profile
rank threshold.

* 8192 SCC-confined monoid comparisons, containing 17116 monoid elements.

* Complete fixed-labeled binary covers of profiles (2,1) and (3,1):

<a id="direct-attack-seed-budget-search"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-seed-budget-search--exact-seed-budget-covers-and-sampled-attacks"></a>
### Exact seed-budget covers and sampled attacks

The structural equalities in [First-drop normal form and exact singleton policy propagation](#direct-attack-first-drop-image-policy) are **PROVED on
paper for arbitrary finite alphabets and n>=2**. This file records finite search
evidence and the exact scopes of minimality and negative results.

Let F=1+min G(T) over all actual images merged by one letter; let F_kappa
restrict to maximum cardinality; let W_kappa=1+max W(T) on those maximum
sources. The theorem proves F=P. F_kappa=P and W_kappa<=the square are
refuted; F_kappa<=the square remains OPEN. Ordinary fibers may be larger
than actual merge sources and are not substituted for them.

|---|---:|---:|---|
| Binary n2 | 9 | 4 | F=F_kappa=P; W_kappa<=1 |
| Binary n3 | 182 | 59 | F=F_kappa=P; W_kappa<=4 |
| Binary n4 | 4845 | 1240 | F=F_kappa=P; W_kappa<=9 |

| Ternary n4 | 2763520 | 1825392 | F=P; max F_kappa-P=2; W_kappa<=9 |

Binary enumeration fixes the first map to conjugacy representatives;
it covers all distinct-letter inputs, with overlap between isomorphism
classes. Ternary enumeration covers every unordered set of three distinct

n>=2. The binary covers are additionally independently enumerated and

<a id="direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions--inclusion-maximal-seeds-and-antitone-policy-tails-both-fail"></a>
### Inclusion-maximal seeds and antitone policy tails both fail

**REFUTED with paper-proved state minima over every finite alphabet.**
The best-policy square conjecture remains OPEN; these are failures of
stronger selection and potential rules. All sets below are actual images.
Seed selection statements assume n>=2; the n1 empty-reset base has no seed.

<a id="direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions--policy-tails-need-not-decrease-under-inclusion-minimum-n4"></a>
#### Policy tails need not decrease under inclusion: minimum n4

Let a=[1,2,0,0] and b=[3,2,0,1]. For S={0} and T={0,3}, exact
G(S)=5 but G(T)=6, despite S being a proper subset of T. Every e/G/W and
forward distance, actual reach word and best policy word is independently
checked. Thus G cannot serve as an antitone potential on actual images.

At n<=3, any nontrivial proper inclusion of nonempty actual images has
singleton S and rank-(n-1) image T. Q is the only larger image than T,
so G(T)=delta(Q,T). A G(S) policy constructs an actual word from Q into S,
and therefore into T, giving G(T)<=G(S). Inclusions into Q are immediate
from G(Q)=0. This proves the arbitrary-alphabet minimum n4.

<a id="direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions--even-allowing-every-fibers-inclusion-maximal-seed-loses-optimality"></a>
#### Even allowing every fiber's inclusion-maximal seed loses optimality

For a letter x and state p, consider actual images U with |U|>=2 and
Ux={p}. Call U maximal for (x,p) if no strictly larger actual image V
containing U is merged by that SAME letter to that SAME state. Let M be
the UNION of these maximal images over all (x,p), and put

    F_max=1+min_(T in M) G(T).

A seed maximal for one of its merge labels is eligible. This definition
does not discard it merely because it has another nonmaximal label.
Every maximum-cardinality seed is maximal, so P<=F_max<=F_kappa.
Nevertheless F_max=P is false. A state-minimal example is n5:

    a=[0,3,1,4,2], b=[0,1,0,4,3], c=[1,3,3,1,1].

Here P=rt=3 but F_max=4. All maximal sources are {0,2}, {1,2},
and {0,3,4}; their masks are 5,6,25. Full actual image membership and
every merge label are independently checked. Explicit best global and
best restricted policy chains attain the claimed budgets.
A second n5 example has P=5 and F_max=7:

    a=[1,3,2,0,0], b=[1,2,4,3,0], c=[0,1,0,3,0].

Its maximal sources have masks 21 and 24. It is a larger finite gap,
not a stronger minimality result or an infinite approximation obstruction.

<a id="direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions--why-n4-is-excluded-for-every-alphabet"></a>
#### Why n<=4 is excluded for every alphabet

Choose an optimal one-letter seed U using the universal first-drop normal
form: 1+G(U)=P. Among actual images containing U in that same merge fiber,
extend it to an inclusion-maximal T. If U=T there is nothing to prove.
If T=Q, its merging letter is constant and P=F_max=1. Otherwise |U|>=2
and U is strictly contained in proper T. At 2<=n<=4 this forces |T|=n-1.
Hence Q is its only larger image and G(T)=delta(Q,T)<=G(U), by the actual
word from Q into U constructed by a G(U) chain. Therefore
F_max<=1+G(T)<=P, proving equality. This establishes arbitrary-alphabet
state minimum n5 independently of the search. No binary minimum is claimed:
complete binary covers through n5 have no inclusion-maximal failure.

The n5 counterexample necessarily uses a smaller actual seed whose cheap
tail is lost when replacing it by a containing merged image. Shortest
phase selection on that larger image chooses a different future tail.
This is compatible with the inclusion monotonicity of the unrestricted
distance delta(Q,T); it concerns the shortest-phase policy G instead.

<a id="direct-attack-seed-inclusion-obstructions--computational-boundary"></a>
#### Computational boundary

The frozen ternary n5 adaptive search uses seed 20261024 and 200000
mutations, with 185268 SC synchronizing scores, and finds gaps 1 and 2.
Sampling does not establish absence of other failures. The exact same
mutation stream, counters and both retained full arrays are replayed.
All saved arrays and maximal-source memberships have a separate ordinary
per-target reverse BFS check; explicit words additionally use the older
inverse-set checker. Complete binary inputs n2..5 are independently
enumerated, with no F_max>P. Three corrupted certificates are rejected.
Original exploratory counts are retained with their explicitly narrower
provenance; the frozen search has literal argv and stdout/stderr.

There is no new n-only upper bound, no Lean addition, and no priority claim.
F_max<=(n-1)^2 is still OPEN, as are P's square bound and Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation--even-the-unique-globally-shortest-binary-reset-can-have-dependent-indicators"></a>
### Even the unique globally shortest binary reset can have dependent indicators

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)** with a separate
**COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** finite certificate. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED**
claim. Priority is **OPEN**. General Cerny and global policy square remain
**OPEN**. No positive-fraction dimension or long-phase tradeoff refutation.

The immediately preceding n5 audit refuted independent OPTIMAL locally
shortest actual-image policies, but its two witnesses still had independent
NONGREEDY shortest reset words. We continued and now refute that weaker
existence repair as well, using a new simple strongly connected binary
example. The distinction about those earlier witnesses remains correct.

<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation--the-exact-automaton-and-a-paper-uniqueness-proof"></a>
#### The exact automaton and a paper uniqueness proof

On Q={0,1,2,3,4}, use ORIGINAL letters

    a=(2,1,1,4,3), b=(3,0,1,1,2).

Both have rank four. The only collision of a is {1,2}, with image 1
and missing state 0. The only collision of b is {2,3}, with image 1
and missing state 4. Thus any original letter decreases the size of
ANY current subset by at most one, giving rt>=4. Literally

    Q --a--> {1,2,3,4} --b--> {0,1,2}
      --a--> {1,2} --a--> {1}.

Hence rt=4. Moreover **abaa is the UNIQUE shortest original reset word**.
Indeed the full inverse history of any length-four reset must increase
by exactly one at EVERY letter, from singleton to Q. The only possible
first growths are:

| Current target | Inverse letter | Larger full preimage |
|---|---|---|
| {1} | a | {1,2} |
| {1} | b | {2,3} |

Neither letter grows {2,3}: both inverse preimages are {0,4}.
From {1,2}, a gives {0,1,2}, while b gives {2,3,4}. Neither letter
grows {2,3,4}: a gives {0,3,4} and b gives {0,4}. From {0,1,2},
a does not grow and b gives {1,2,3,4}. Only a grows that four-set to
Q; b does not. Thus the ONLY all-growing inverse label sequence is
a,a,b,a, equivalent to the original forward word abaa. This argument
covers every reset endpoint and every original length-four word.

The automaton is strongly connected. From 0 one reaches 2 by a, 1 by
ab, 3 by b and 4 by ba. Conversely 1 reaches 0 by b, 2 by bb,
3 by bb, and 4 by bbb. Both unary subalphabets are nonsynchronizing:
a has the fixed state 1 and the separate cycle (3,4); b has the
three-cycle (0,3,1). Thus both original letters are necessary.

<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation--no-nontrivial-state-congruence"></a>
#### No nontrivial state congruence

Every distinct pair can be taken to {1,2} without collapsing it:

| Pair | Original word |
|---|---|
| 0,1 | a |
| 0,2 | a |
| 0,3 | ab |
| 0,4 | aaba |
| 1,2 | empty |
| 1,3 | ba |
| 1,4 | ba |
| 2,3 | aba |
| 2,4 | b |
| 3,4 | b |

These ten words are literal finite certificates. Any nontrivial
congruence therefore identifies 1 and 2. Applying b identifies 0 and
1; applying b to 0 and 1 adds 3; applying a to 0 and 3 adds 4.
The congruence is universal. The DFA is consequently simple. This is
state congruence simplicity, with no stronger semigroup assertion.

<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation--the-dependence-survives-every-optimization-of-the-reset-word"></a>
#### The dependence survives every optimization of the reset word

In state masks the unique inverse growth history is

    2 -> 6 -> 7 -> 30 -> 31.

All its proper stages are ACTUAL images: forward prefixes of abaa give
Q,30,7,6,2. Every reverse stage has exact actual-image local e=1,
since a zero-cost transport from a larger set is impossible. Hence the
same chain is an optimal compatible image policy, with P=rt=4. Any
cost-four policy must compose to abaa and start at its reset endpoint.
Each successive target on its inverse path has e=1, and an original
inverse letter can grow by only one, so its actual larger parent equals
that full preimage. This forces every cut and the same endpoint chain.

The three proper growth indicators obey

    chi_6 + chi_31 = chi_7 + chi_30.

Raw rank after adjoining Q is three; normalized rank is two. Even
adjoining the initial singleton, and counting ALL letter-level intermediate
preimages, gives raw rank only four for five vectors. There are no
non-growth intermediates here: each phase is one ORIGINAL letter.

Thus existence of a fully independent proper record-growth history among
globally shortest original reset words is **REFUTED**, including simple
SC irreducibly synchronizing binary inputs with rt=n-1. Allowing locally
longer phases cannot change the unique shortest original word. This
strengthens D3's policy obstruction and does not use a greedy choice.

Five states are minimal for this PROPER-STAGE assertion over ANY finite
alphabet: at n<=4 there are at most two proper record-growth sets, of
strictly increasing sizes. Two distinct proper indicators together with
Q can be dependent only if the two sets are complements. The only
two-stage case at n4 has sizes two and three, summing to five, so that
cannot happen. The exact Boolean proof is also given in
[Optimal local phases can force dependent growth indicators](#direct-attack-optimal-phase-independence-refutation). It applies equally to the
unrestricted record-growth convention with temporary shrinking.

<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation--counting-the-initial-singleton-is-a-different-question"></a>
#### Counting the initial singleton is a different question

A separate SC binary n3 control has

    a=(1,0,0), b=(1,2,1).

Its unique shortest word is ba, of length two. Both letters have rank
two, so no one-letter reset exists. The only growing inverse path to
Q is {0} --a^-1--> {1,2} --b^-1--> Q. These THREE full-history vectors
obey chi_{0}+chi_{1,2}=chi_Q and have raw rank two. Its ONE proper
stage has normalized rank one and is independent. This is NOT a
three-state counterexample to the proper-stage assertion above.

At n2 a synchronizing DFA must contain a constant original letter,
because every other nonconstant transformation is a permutation. A
shortest reset then has length one and its singleton/Q indicators are
independent. Thus the full-history assertion INCLUDING the initial
singleton already has a state-minimal n3 failure. The two conventions
must not be silently interchanged.

<a id="direct-attack-shortest-binary-independence-refutation--independent-verification-and-research-boundary"></a>
#### Independent verification and research boundary

`shortest_binary_independence.py` uses forward subset BFS, exhaustive
original words and rational Gaussian ranks. `check_shortest_binary_independence.py`
imports neither it nor another policy checker. It enumerates ALL +1
inverse growth branches (11/6 tree vertices), using the paper rank-defect
lower bound to make this exhaustive for shortest words. It also runs
EACH original state literally through ALL 16/4 original words at the
two lower bounds. All 76 letter/subset rank-defect controls, six ranks
by integer Leibniz determinant minors, all actual images (19/6), SC
paths and the ten simplicity pair words are verified independently.
Seven deliberate corruptions are rejected.

This is check105 / regeneration189. The previous104-check record is
preserved verbatim; only the new generator, replay and checker continue.
No full105 rerun or formal kernel. The proof is a small exact obstruction
to a quantified dimension assertion, not an asymptotic reset lower bound.
Positive-fraction guarantees for optimized histories, dimension versus
EXPENSIVE-phase costs, and general quadratic compatibility remain OPEN.
The informal 2026 dimension question is not declared wholly settled.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--a-global-shortest-image-policy-penalty-with-reset-threshold-three"></a>
### A global shortest-image-policy penalty with reset threshold three

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

**PROVED on paper.** For every even n>=6, the ternary strongly connected
DFA below has exact rt=3 and global best shortest-image-policy cost P=n.
Every proper actual image has e<=n-1, with equality attained. Thus the
policy's ratio to the true optimum is n/3, unbounded. This refutes EVERY
fixed-factor and fixed-additive approximation P<=C rt or P<=rt+C.
It does not refute P<=(n-1)^2, the universal e<=2n target, or Cerny.

A second DFA differing in ONE transition has the same full actual image
family and the same rt=3 but P=3. The change modifies eligible shortest
phase parents, not the existence or ordinary length of a short reset.
Priority of the precise parameter obstruction remains OPEN. No new Lean
theorem or general n-only reset upper bound is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--construction-and-complete-image-family"></a>
#### Construction and complete image family

Use right actions on Q={0,...,n-1}. Define

    a(q)=1 if q mod 4 is 1 or 2, and 0 otherwise;
    b(q)=q+1 mod n;
    c(q)=q mod 2 except c(n-2)=1 and c(n-1)=2.

Both a and c fix 0,1; a sends 2 to 1. The word aba resets Q to 1.
No word of length <=2 resets: Qa={0,1}, Qc={0,1,2}; applying a or c
to either preserves at least 0,1, and applying b preserves cardinality.
A leading b preserves Q. Thus rt=3, and the cycle b supplies SC.

Write A_i={i,i+1}, B_i={i,i+2}, C_i={i,i+1,i+2}, with indices modulo n.
The full image family is

    R={Q} union all singletons union {A_i,B_i,C_i: i in Z_n},
    |R|=4n+1.

Reachability is explicit: Qa=A_0, Qc=C_0, Qa b^(n-1)c=B_0, and Qaba={1};
rotations by b reach every listed image. The family is closed: a maps into
{0,1}, c into {0,1,2}, and every nonempty subset of either belongs to R.
The n>=6 guard makes the n rotations in each of the two pair orbits distinct.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--rank-three-transport-a-full-lower-proof-into-the-critical-triple"></a>
#### Rank-three transport: a full lower proof into the critical triple

Let T=C_(n-3). Q is the only actual image of size greater than 3, so
G(T)=W(T)=e(T)=delta(Q,T). The word cb^(n-3) maps Q onto T in n-2 letters.
Suppose a shorter word of length ell<n-2 transported Q into ANY nonempty
subset of T. It has a last nonpermutation letter x in {a,c}; write it
v x b^r, with t=|vx|>=1. Its image J after x is a nonempty subset of
{0,1,2}. Since r<=n-4, translating J by r cannot wrap around the cycle.

For t=1 or 2, J contains 0: the one-letter images are A_0,C_0; aa,ac,ca,cc
have image A_0, and ba,bc have image A_0,C_0. Hence r>=n-3 and ell>=n-2.
For t>=3, min J<=2, so r>=n-5 and ell>=3+n-5=n-2. Both contradict
strict shortness. The proof includes strict subset and singleton arrivals,
not only words reaching the triple exactly. Therefore G(T)=W(T)=n-2.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--exact-shortest-rank-two-parents"></a>
#### Exact shortest rank-two parents

No cyclic triple is monochromatic under a: the period 0110, including the
even-cycle boundary when n mod 4 is 2, has no cyclic run of three equal
values. The triples' c-images are

    C_i c=A_0 for 0<=i<=n-4;
    C_(n-3)c=A_1;
    C_(n-2)c=C_(n-1)c=C_0.

Thus no triple is merged by a single letter, and kappa=2. The rank-two
first-drop boundary consists EXACTLY of A_0 and A_1. A_0 has Q as a
parent (via a) and every triple as a parent (via a); A_1's ONLY larger
parent is T=C_(n-3), via c. Permutation b has no boundary edge.

For a rank-two target S, let d_j(S)=delta(A_j,S), j=0,1. If S!=A_0,
then d_0(S)=1+d_1(S): a,c preserve A_0, so any shortest successful word
starting there must begin with its first effective b, which sends A_0 to
A_1. Removing preceding neutral letters proves the lower equality;
prepending b proves its upper equality.

By the universal first-drop theorem, A_1 is the UNIQUE winning boundary
image for EVERY rank-two target S!=A_0. Its only larger parent is T. Hence

    e(S)=1+d_1(S), G(S)=W(S)=e(S)+n-2 for S!=A_0;
    e(A_0)=G(A_0)=1.

These equations preserve all shortest-word ties; they do not select one
convenient extension word and ignore other winning parents.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--global-optimum-of-the-policy"></a>
#### Global optimum of the policy

Every actual one-letter merge source has size 2 and is different from
A_0, which a,c preserve and b permutes. Therefore EVERY such source S
has G(S)>=n-1. The general one-letter-seed normal form gives P>=n.
The source A_1 is merged by a and has e(A_1)=1, so G(A_1)=n-1 and P=n.
A concrete optimal policy word is cb^(n-3)ca, of length n: it first
reaches T, c transports T onto A_1 in its shortest phase, and a merges A_1.

The contrast with aba is precise. Transporting Q into A_1 by ab costs 2,
but the policy forbids that phase because T c=A_1 costs 1. The compulsory
shorter local phase chooses a parent whose full transport costs n-2.
The singleton initial phase alone cannot repair this future-tail loss.

All images have e<=n-1. For triples, ab^i gives e(C_i)<=i+1 for
0<=i<=n-2, and Qa is contained in C_(n-1). For pairs S!=A_0, a sends
A_1 to 1. Choose a positive q in S with q<=n-2 to obtain d_1(S)<=q,
so e(S)<=n-1. The only remaining pair is {n-1,0}, reached from A_1 by
b^(n-2), again giving e<=n-1. The singleton seed targets are exactly 0,1;
every nonpermutation letter is nonincreasing in the ordinary state index,
while b increases it by at most one. Hence seed distance to q>=1 is q-1,
and e({q})=q, e({0})=1. In particular e({n-1})=n-1, proving exact maximum.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--the-single-transition-control-and-excluded-odd-parameters"></a>
#### The single-transition control and excluded odd parameters

Replace c(n-2)=1 by c(n-2)=0, leaving every other transition unchanged.
The resulting c_0 still fixes 0,1, still has image C_0, and has the SAME
complete R by the same reachability/closure words. Its rank-two boundary
is A_0 and B_0: the special triple C_(n-2) maps to B_0, and there is no
larger image mapping in one letter into A_1. No triple is a-monochromatic.
Therefore e(A_1)>=2, and Qab=A_1 attains 2 with Q as an eligible parent.
So G(A_1)=2, and rt<=P<=1+G(A_1)=3 proves P=rt=3.

For odd n>=5, the construction's assignment c(n-2)=1 changes nothing in
the parity map; triple c-images are only A_0 or C_0. The only possible
a-monochromatic cyclic triple (when n mod 4 is 1) maps to 0, which is
outside A_1. Thus again no one-letter larger-image transport into A_1
exists, Qab attains e=G=2, and P=3. Saved odd controls delimit the even
obstruction. The n4 boundary has 15 images rather than 4n+1 and is handled
as a separate finite check, not silently included in the image-count proof.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-policy-penalty--verification-boundary"></a>
#### Verification boundary

The family certificates contain both transition versions at every even
n6..62, odd controls n5,n7,n9,n11, and the separate n4 case. Every saved
e/G/W/forward entry is independently recomputed using ordinary ALL-SOURCE
forward BFS. Complete image closure, the rank-two boundary, critical triple
lower cost, reset and policy words, parity/transition controls and corruption
rejection are checked. Arbitrary-n claims follow from the proof above.
The four adaptive short-reset searches are separate sampled evidence;
no absence of a policy square counterexample is inferred from them.

The four frozen searches n6/8/10/12 contain 400000 mutations plus 512 scored
seeds, all 400512 exact. Maxima P are 6,10,14,14 while rt remains 3.
All 27 retained search arrays and all 63 family/control arrays have independent
ordinary ALL-SOURCE checks; three corruptions are rejected. Every search
counter, full P histogram, retained array and seed byte is replayed. Replay
advances the mutation RNG through the deterministic construction of all 128
initial seeds even when loading frozen rows, retaining the original stream.

[An elementary reset-length-dependent bound for every seed tie](#direct-attack-short-reset-seed-budget) then settles this regime in advance: whenever
an existing reset has ell<=(n+1)/2, EVERY one-letter seed and every future
tie satisfies the square budget. Therefore further rt=3 square attacks at
n>=5 would repeat a proved conditional result. The infinite P/rt penalty
is retained as a structural obstruction, and future global-policy attacks
must leave this short-reset regime.

<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-seed-budget"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-short-reset-seed-budget--an-elementary-reset-length-dependent-bound-for-every-seed-tie"></a>
### An elementary reset-length-dependent bound for every seed tie

**PROVED on paper for SC synchronizing n>=2 over every finite alphabet.**
This is a bound on the shortest-image policy given an EXISTING reset word,
not a new general reset bound. It uses the ordinary SC state-distance
argument and the previously proved seed normal form. Novelty is not claimed.

If a reset word of length ell is known, then every proper actual image S
of size k has

    e(S)<=delta(Q,S)<=ell+n-k.                       (1)

After the reset, walk from its endpoint to S in the ordinary state graph.
A shortest first-entry path has distinct intermediate states outside S,
so its length is at most n-k. This proves (1) with full concatenation cost;
the walk is not a free change of the reset endpoint.

Let r be the maximum proper-image rank, and H the ACTUAL one-letter seed
targets. From any p in H the initial phase costs 1. Every subsequent phase
starts at an actual image of rank at least 2; ranks strictly increase, so
each k=2,...,r is visited at most once. Applying (1) to each phase gives,
including EVERY future shortest-phase tie,

    W({p}) <= B_r(ell)=1+sum_(k=2)^r (ell+n-k).

If the first merged source is Q, that chain has cost 1 and bypasses the sum.
If r=1 the sum is empty. Since r<=n-1 and all summands are positive,

    rt<=P<=min_(p in H) W({p})
         <=1+(n-2)ell+(n-2)(n-1)/2.                 (2)

For n>=3, subtraction of the square gives exactly

    [right side of (2)]-(n-1)^2
        =(n-2)(ell-(n+1)/2).

Consequently, if ell<=(n+1)/2, EVERY initial one-letter seed and every
future tie has total cost <=(n-1)^2. At n2 all chains have one letter,
so the same conclusion holds directly. Nonseed initial targets are not
covered by this all-tie square statement. Conversely a failure of the
best-policy square necessarily has rt>(n+1)/2 (n>=3).

This explains why the new rt=3 search family cannot violate the policy
square for n>=5, regardless of alphabet size or other letter ranks. Its
unbounded ratio P/rt is still substantive; it cannot be upgraded to a
square counterexample. The short-reset square corollary is not progress on
Cerny's reset bound by itself: its hypothesis already supplies a much
shorter reset. Future direct policy-counterexample searches should exclude
that settled regime rather than repeatedly mutate it.

check_first_drop independently reconstructs rt, every e/G/W value and
all actual seed targets, then checks (1), the rank-sensitive B_r bound,
and the conditional square statement. These finite checks supplement the
paper argument; no Lean theorem and no n-only bound is asserted.

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--short-first-returns-compression-of-a-block-and-a-stronger-quotient-lift"></a>
### Short first returns, compression of a block, and a stronger quotient lift

**Status update (2026-10-01).** The unrestricted linear actual-image
extension target is now **REFUTED** by
[[Every universal linear actual-image extension bound fails](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction)](#direct-attack-quadratic-image-extension-obstruction).
Earlier universal-linear OPEN labels below are historical and superseded;
this document's stated subclass results retain their original scope.

Date: 2026-09-30. **PROVED on paper**, for arbitrary finite alphabets and
arbitrary state sizes under the stated hypotheses. The exact publication
priority is **OPEN**. The stationary-span ingredient and the Frankl
renewing-sequence bound are known; no novelty claim is made for them.
There is no **FORMALLY VERIFIED** or Lean claim. Independent finite checks
are **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED** in their explicitly sampled scope.

The unrestricted Cerny conjecture, universal `e(S)<=2n`, existence of any
universal linear image-extension constant, and the best-policy square
remain **OPEN**. This is a general block/compression mechanism with
conditional quotient consequences, not an upper bound in `n` alone.

The later [Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class](#direct-attack-profile-class-compression) strengthens first compression
for a minimum class, repairs the two h=6 profile gaps below, and raises
the current minimal-counterexample class floor to seven. It also
excludes nontrivial congruences below n22 in a state-minimal counterexample.

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--1-a-short-return-reduction-valid-for-every-congruence-class"></a>
#### 1. A short-return reduction valid for every congruence class

Let A be a strongly connected synchronizing n-state DFA. Let C be a
congruence class, `h=|C|<n`, and `d=n-h`. A **first-return word** w is
nonempty, satisfies `Cw subset C`, and satisfies `Cv intersect C=empty`
for each nonempty proper prefix v of w. A length-one letter mapping C
into C is included. Define B on the h states C, with one letter for each
distinct transformation of C induced by a first-return word of length
at most `d+1`. Then

    B is synchronizing.                                      (1)

Its alphabet may contain many words, but there is a synchronizing
subalphabet of at most `h^2` actual first-return transformations. Every
macro letter is charged at its original word length, at most `n-h+1`.
For h>=2, synchronization of B forces a nonpermutation macro letter.
Consequently a particularly direct compression theorem is

    c(C) <= n-h+1,                                         (2a)

with a compressing word that RETURNS the whole C into C. More generally,
for EVERY k-subset S of C, 2<=k<=h, apply the established Frankl
compression bound in the h-state B and expand its macro letters:

    c(S) <= (n-h+1) binom(h-k+2,2).                        (2b)

These are all-n, arbitrary-alphabet compression theorems under the
congruence hypothesis; S itself need not be Q-reachable. They are not
universal bounds for arbitrary subsets in arbitrary DFAs. The family in
section 2 makes (2a) sharp at unbounded n, already for h=2.

If H(h) is ANY proved reset upper bound for arbitrary h-state DFAs, then
EVERY subset of C can be reset in A within

    (n-h+1) H(h).                                            (2)

In particular the entire class C can be compressed/reset within that
budget. Neither a reset word for the quotient nor an arbitrary reaching
word is repeated inside (2).

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--complete-proof-of-1"></a>
##### Complete proof of (1)

Use row transition matrices `M_a`, and order coordinates as `C,O=Q\C`.
Let `E_a=(M_a)_(C,O)`, `D_a=(M_a)_(O,O)`, `R_a=(M_a)_(O,C)`, and
`I_a=(M_a)_(C,C)`. A congruence ensures every word sends the WHOLE
current class into one class. Thus a path starting in C either returns
with all its original trajectories together, or keeps them all outside;
there are no partial returns.

Fix ANY row g on C. The rows `g E_a` span a subspace `U_0` of R^d.
Put

    U_j = span{g E_a D_v : |v|<=j}.

If `U_0=0`, every outside excursion is zero. Otherwise `dim U_0>=1`.
As usual `U_j=U_(j+1)` implies invariance under all `D_a`, hence
stabilization forever. Therefore `U_(d-1)` spans EVERY outside excursion:
there are at most d dimensions, and a nonstabilized chain grows at each
step. Applying `R_b` shows that the output row of ANY first return of g
lies in the span of its outputs under first returns of length at most
`1+(d-1)+1=d+1`, together with immediate returns `g I_a`.

Products with an intermediate return are zero after the restriction to
O. Every nonzero restricted product corresponds to an actual first
return: the congruence rules out partial survival. Thus the spanning
rows are induced by legal actual words, rather than artificially gated
partial maps. Zero products do not change the span.

For a stochastic row g on C, let L be its orbit span under B. L is
invariant under every short first return by definition. Apply the
preceding argument separately to EACH row in L: it follows that L is
invariant under EVERY first return, of any length. An arbitrary word
mapping C into C factors at its consecutive class returns into such
first returns, so L is invariant under that word as well.

Strong connectivity and synchronization of A give, for every q in C,
an actual reset word z_q ending at q. It maps C into C and hence
`g M_(z_q)=[q]` lies in L. Consequently

    span{g M_w : w a B-word}=R^h
    for EVERY stochastic g on C.                           (3)

For clarity, the known stationary-span synchronization criterion used
to finish the proof can be derived directly. Choose a stationary
distribution alpha for the uniform random walk on B. Equation (3)
forces alpha to be positive: a zero coordinate of alpha stays zero
under every letter, by stationarity and positivity of letter weights,
and therefore under every word, contradicting (3). The ascending-chain
argument makes the orbit rows through B-length `h-1` span R^h.
For any proper nonempty X subset C, not all those rows have the same
mass on X; otherwise their span would satisfy the nontrivial homogeneous
equation `row(X)=alpha(X) row(C)`. Averaging equally over word lengths
0..h-1, and uniformly over letters at each length, gives alpha again.
Hence some such word has mass on X STRICTLY GREATER than alpha(X).
Its preimage of X has strictly greater alpha mass. Iterating this
inverse extension terminates at C, since only finitely many subsets
exist. This constructs a reset word for B and proves (1).

To obtain an alphabet of at most `h^2` words, choose a matrix basis from
the short first returns. Its span equals the original letter-matrix
span, so its orbit spans are the same; (3) and the preceding argument
still apply. Selecting a basis does NOT assert equality of the two
transition monoids or equality of their reset thresholds.

There is a polynomial construction of such a matrix basis. In the
space of `h by d` matrices, retain a basis of all restricted exit
products of depth at most d, with an actual representative word for
each basis member. Extend the basis by the matrices `D_a`, truncating
at that depth. Apply all final `R_b`, add the immediate-return matrices,
and choose a basis of the resulting `h by h` matrices. Both spaces
have polynomial dimension (`hd` and `h^2`), and d rounds suffice.
Unlike the row proof, the matrix space need NOT stabilize at depth
`d-1`; the construction is explicitly truncated. Every nonzero retained
representative is a legal first return. This distinction is audited by
exact rational arithmetic in `check_return_word_lift.py`.

The same proof holds for any nonempty proper C satisfying
`Cw subset C OR Cw intersect C=empty` for EVERY word w. We use a
congruence class as a readily certified instance of this nonsplitting
condition. In fact this semantic condition introduces no additional
scope: define p~q if, for every word w, `pw in C iff qw in C`.
This is a congruence, and the nonsplitting condition makes C exactly
one of its classes. When h>=2 and C is proper, the congruence is
nontrivial. Thus the mechanism cannot reach simple automata through
a different choice of a nonsplitting proper set.

The complementary linear separation fact is a reconstruction of DFA
partition refinement. If C is NOT nonsplitting, some word of length
at most `n-h` has both an inside and an outside image of its members.
Start refinement with the two classes C and Q\C. Before the first
split of C, there are at most n-h+1 blocks. A stable refinement never
splits later, so each earlier depth increases the block count. A first
split at depth T therefore has T+1<=n-h+1, proving T<=n-h. This is a
short membership-separation word, not a compressing or extending word.

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--2-the-return-cutoff-is-sharp-a-shorter-universal-repair-fails"></a>
#### 2. The return cutoff is sharp; a shorter universal repair fails

For each odd `t>=3`, let C={0,1}, O={2,...,t+1}, n=t+2. Let

    a(0)=2, a(1)=3, a(2+j)=2+(j+1 mod t);
    b(0)=0, b(1)=1, b(2+j)=j mod 2.

The two-class partition C|O is a congruence. A is SC: a cycles O,
b reaches both members of C, and a exits C. The word `b a^t b`
resets A, so it synchronizes.

Every first return is either b or `a^(k+1) b`. For k<=t-2, the two
outside trajectories have indices k,k+1 without wrapping and have
different b-colors. These return maps are permutations of C. At
k=t-1, the indices t-1 and 0 both have color zero, and `a^t b`
is constant. Therefore the cutoff `n-h=d=t` yields a nonsynchronizing
reduced automaton, whereas `n-h+1=t+1` first admits a constant letter.

Thus replacing the cutoff in (1) by `n-h` is **REFUTED** at arbitrarily
large n. These are not image-extension counterexamples: C=Qb has e(C)=1.
The lower obstruction concerns the whole return alphabet, not a claim
that every individual long return word must be shortened to the same map.

The cutoff refutation has an even smaller general-class witness, proved
directly: at n=3 take a=[2,2,0], b=[1,0,0], C={0,1}, O={2}.
The partition is a congruence, the DFA is SC, and baa resets Q. The only
length-one return is the transposition b; aa is a constant return of
length two. Thus cap n-h=1 fails, while n-h+1=2 works. This n3 witness
is state-minimal for the general class statement, since h>=2 and h<n.
C is not a MINIMUM class here. For a minimum-class witness at its own
state minimum n4, take a=[2,3,2,2], b=[1,0,0,1], classes {0,1}|{2,3}.
It is SC and baab resets Q. The first returns of length at most two
are b and ab, both permutations; aab is constant at length three.
These small witnesses concern the return cutoff. Their whole-class
compression costs are 1 and 2, respectively, so they do not attain
the n-h+1 compression upper bound. The infinite odd-t family does.
These additional minima have direct paper proofs; the 53-record matrix
certificate count above refers to the separate sampled/control corpus.

Dropping the nonsplitting assumption is even more decisive. In C_3 take
`a=[1,2,0]`, `b=[0,1,0]`, and the actual image C=Qb={0,1}.
Its a-image {1,2} partially meets C, so no first return can start with a.
The b-image is C and b acts there as the identity, so the ONLY first
return is b. The all-length first-return alphabet is nonsynchronizing,
although `b a a b` resets A in four letters. Thus the assertion that
arbitrary reachable images have a synchronizing return alphabet is
**REFUTED**, even with no word-length cutoff. It is state-minimal because
a proper set of size >=2 first exists at n=3.

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--3-general-conditional-quotient-lift"></a>
#### 3. General conditional quotient lift

Let theta have m>=2 classes, let h be its smallest class size, and let
u reset the quotient into a class T. Choose a smallest class C and a
shortest quotient-state path from T to C, of length at most m-1. The
concatenation sends all Q into C. Then (2) gives the general bound

    rt(A) <= |u| + dist_(A/theta)(T,C) + (n-h+1) H(h).         (4)

This theorem applies to ANY SC synchronizing DFA and any finite alphabet;
it pays the quotient reset and class routing exactly once. With a square
quotient, and any h for which its square is established, it yields

    rt(A) <= m(m-1) + (n-h+1)(h-1)^2.                       (5)

For h<=5 the small-state square used here is known; no new finite
small-state theorem is claimed. For a state-minimal counterexample,
the h-state reduced automaton is smaller than A, so the square in (5)
also follows from minimality itself, for arbitrary h. No circular
assumption about the n-state square is used.

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--4-every-class-of-a-state-minimal-counterexample-has-size-at-least-six"></a>
#### 4. Every class of a state-minimal counterexample has size at least six

The conditional square lifts STRICTLY when h<=5, for EVERY class-size
profile and every n. This improves the repository's former h<=3 exclusion.

For h=1 the quotient reset and routing already reset A. For h=2,3,4,
compare (5) with the square at the smallest possible n=hm. The gaps are

    h=2: 3m^2-5m+2;
    h=3: 8m^2-17m+9;
    h=4: 15m^2-43m+28.

Each is strictly positive for m>=2 (the h=4 gap is 2 at m=2).
The gap only increases with n>=hm: its increment when n increases by
one is `2n-1-(h-1)^2>0` in these ranges.

For h=5 and m>=3 the minimum-n gap is `24m^2-89m+65`, positive at
m=3 (14) and increasing thereafter. At m=2, (5) is already strict
for n>=14. It remains to cover the profiles `(5,t)`, t=5,6,7,8.

Here use a fiber version of the standard Frankl argument. A shortest
word compressing a k-set within a congruence class has a renewing
sequence of pairs and k-sets. Split that sequence by its current class.
Within a class of size s, Frankl bounds its length by
`binom(s-k+2,2)`. The original renewal condition holds on each
subsequence. Thus EVERY k-set inside a class compresses within

    sum_(classes D, |D|>=k) binom(|D|-k+2,2).               (6)

More explicitly, along a shortest compressing word, all preterminal
images S_i have size k. Pull back its final merged pair uniquely along
the injective prefixes to obtain P_i subset S_i. If P_i were contained
in an earlier S_j, that earlier prefix followed by the suffix at i
would compress the initial set sooner. This is exactly the renewing
condition needed for each class subsequence. Summing the bounds proves
(6), including paths that move to other classes.

After routing Q into a smallest h-class, apply (6) at most once per
rank k=h,h-1,...,2. With `J_h(s)=sum_(k=2)^h binom(s-k+2,2)`, this gives
another general bound

    rt(A) <= |u|+dist(T,C)+sum_D J_h(|D|).                  (7)

For the four leftover profiles, the coarse bound `2+J_5(5)+J_5(t)` is
42,56,74,96, respectively, strictly below 81,100,121,144. This completes
the all-profile h<=5 proof.

Consequences: a state-minimal Cerny counterexample cannot have a
nontrivial congruence with ANY class of size <=5. A square-extremal SC
automaton also cannot have such a congruence when its quotient obeys
the square. Simple automata, larger classes, and unrestricted
hereditariness are not settled.

For h=6 the two bounds (5)/(7) ALONE are inconclusive at `(6,14)` and `(6,15)`.
These are arithmetic gaps, not automaton counterexamples. The remaining
profiles with minimum six are strictly excluded by (5)/(7): for m>=4,
the minimum-n gap is `35m^2-161m+126>0`; for m=3 only n=18..21 require
(7); for m=2 only n=12..21 require (7), leaving those two profiles.
Convexity of J_6 concentrates fixed excess size in one class, so checking
`(6,...,6,n-6(m-1))` bounds every other size profile at that n,m.
These h=6 assertions use `H(6)=25`, as supplied by state minimality (or
a separately known six-state square); they are not derived from a
quotient-square assumption alone. The subsequent profile-sensitive
first-compression theorem repairs both gaps; see [Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class](#direct-attack-profile-class-compression).

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--5-a-growing-class-size-restriction-in-any-state-minimal-counterexample"></a>
#### 5. A growing class-size restriction in ANY state-minimal counterexample

For a state-minimal counterexample, (5) is valid for every h<n by
minimality of A, even if h is arbitrarily large: B is an actual smaller
synchronizing DFA over a finite alphabet. Therefore EVERY nontrivial
congruence, with m classes and minimum class size h, must satisfy

    m(m-1)+(n-h+1)(h-1)^2 > (n-1)^2.                       (8)

There is a useful all-n corollary, independent of the number of classes:

    n <= h^2-3h+3,  and h>=7.                              (9)

Equivalently, every class has size at least

    max{7, ceil((3+sqrt(4n-3))/2)}.

Thus any nontrivial congruence has fewer than about sqrt(n) classes,
and EVERY class has size at least sqrt(n)+3/2+o(1). These restrictions
do not assert that a hypothetical counterexample has a congruence.

Proof of (9). Sizes h<=5 were excluded above; h=6 is excluded by the
subsequent [Sharp profile-sensitive compression of a minimum congruence class](#direct-attack-profile-class-compression). For h>=4, suppose
`n>=n0=h^2-3h+4`. Since m<=n/h, the gap between the square and the
right side of (5) is at least

    D_h(n)=(n-1)^2-(n/h)(n/h-1)-(n-h+1)(h-1)^2.

At n0 this equals `3h-16+28/h-16/h^2`. It is positive for h>=4:
at h=4 it is 2, and its derivative in h is
`3-28/h^2+32/h^3>0`. Its derivative with respect to n at n0 is
`h^2-4h+3+7/h-8/h^2>0` for h>=4, and that derivative increases with n.
Hence D_h(n)>0 for all n>=n0, contradicting (8). Since n is integral,
(9) follows. This is a general conditional reduction for a minimal
counterexample, not a guessed growth law inferred from enumeration.

The exact profile condition (8) is stronger than its n-only corollary.
For example it excludes h=6,m>=4 directly; the additional fiber bound
handles the leftover m=3 cases. The profiles (6,14) and (6,15) are
inconclusive for (5)/(7) alone, but are repaired by the later theorem.
Combining (5) and (7) also excludes every nontrivial congruence when n<20
in a state-minimal counterexample: once h<=5 is removed, the only
profiles to check are twenty two-class profiles with sizes >=6 and
the two three-class profiles (6,6,6), (6,6,7). Their integer bounds are
strict. This is a necessary condition on counterexamples, not a claim
that all automata below twenty states satisfy Cerny.

<a id="direct-attack-short-return-quotient-lift--6-verification-attribution-and-the-remaining-bottleneck"></a>
#### 6. Verification, attribution, and the remaining bottleneck

The counterexample-first sample proposes 6000 congruence-respecting
alphabets, with 435 SC synchronizing exact inputs accepted and 53
retained records including controls. This is sampling, not an exhaustive
automaton cover. The controls include reduced Cerny automata with macro
thresholds 4,9,16,25, and the sharp cutoff family through n=65.

The independent checker uses a polynomial exact rational MATRIX basis,
rather than the generator's first-return tuple-orbit BFS. It checks the
equality of the short-return matrix spans, synchronization of the basis
alphabet, reverse-subset Bellman distances, all literal lifted words,
8832 full-image vertices, 3999 minimum-n inequalities, four exceptional
profiles, and rejection of three deliberately corrupted certificates.
The all-n theorems rest on the proofs, not on those finite counts.

The full-orbit stationary criterion is the known mechanism of
[Berlinkov--Szykula, Criterion 1 and Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.8363).
Their general low-rank construction appends a fixed rank-h word to
every macro letter. The present return reduction uses a class preserved
by actual return words and charges the quotient transport once.
Frankl's set-sequence bound is also established theory. The quotient
context is [Rodaro--Venturi, Propositions 3.1--3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.17992).
Their paper leaves the general hereditary square problem open. Priority
of this precise short-return reduction and h<=5 consequence remains
OPEN after the current comparison; absence in a search is not evidence
of novelty.

The largest unresolved issue remains a target-sensitive compatible
compression/extension mechanism for simple automata, or for arbitrary
reachable images whose trajectories split at a proposed return set.
This proof cannot silently replace a class by such an image: the
restricted products would then describe partially gated maps instead
of actual word actions. No universal image-extension theorem follows.

General Cerny and the unpaired short-tail square remain OPEN.

NEW metric: original rank-one a, doubled root r fixed by the core-cycle

Tail height2<=h<root-cycle tau. Targets have whole core parts and
