<a id="direct-attack-singleton-transport-obstruction"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-singleton-transport-obstruction--singleton-target-transport-does-not-preserve-greedy-policy-cost"></a>
### Singleton target transport does not preserve greedy policy cost

**I6 — REFUTED, binary-minimal n=4 in the SC synchronizing scope.**
The proposed directed-edge inequality is G({q x})<=G({q})+1 for every
state q and letter x. Such an inequality would let a good reset target
control the costs at other targets. It is valid for the Cerny policy
formula but fails generally.

    a=[0,0,1,1], b=[1,2,3,0], q=0, x=b.

All singleton best/worst costs are [2,4,5,6]. The actual reset word aa
has length 2 and ends at 0. Appending b resets to 1 in length 3, while
G({1})=4>G({0})+1=3. Independent ordinary-set forward BFS gives exact
shortest reset-to-1 distance 3. The global policy minimum is still 2.

The failure mechanism is explicit. For target {1}, the shortest extension
word is a, of length 1, with reachable larger preimage {2,3}; that
image's policy tail costs 3. The word ab of length 2 can instead choose
the reachable image {0,1}, whose policy tail costs 1. Taking a longer
first phase saves overall transport cost. The appended reset aab is
therefore not a shortest-extension policy for its final target.

Complete binary covers at n=2 and n=3 pass (9 and 182 overlapping inputs).
The n=4 cover stops at its first refutation after 873 inputs; it is not
a complete four-state failure enumeration. Duplicate letters reduce to
unary and cannot be SC synchronizing for n>=2. No arbitrary-alphabet
minimality is asserted. Stored full arrays are independently checked by
inverse BFS, and check_singleton_transport.py separately verifies the
edge, both full-Q words and the exact target distance.

<a id="direct-attack-singleton-transport-obstruction--the-unrestricted-transport-recurrence-is-exact-but-not-a-bound"></a>
#### The unrestricted transport recurrence is exact but not a bound

Let delta(T,S) be the shortest word sending T into S, and define
F(Q)=0 and F(S)=min_{reachable T, |T|>|S|}(delta(T,S)+F(T)).
Then F(S) equals the shortest full-Q transport distance D(Q,S).
The construction of phase words gives D<=F. The allowed choice T=Q
gives F<=delta(Q,S)=D. This identity is valid for every reachable S
in a synchronizing automaton, but supplies no bound in n: the direct
Q choice already contains the original shortest-word problem.
The unresolved task is a cheaper globally compatible family of phases,
not merely removing the shortest-phase restriction from exact search.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--a-single-collision-fiber-does-not-make-the-entire-kernel-stable"></a>
### A single collision fiber does not make the entire kernel stable

Date: 2026-10-02. **REFUTED, PROVED (paper)**, every odd n>=5.
The five-state boundary is state-minimal under strong connectivity,
over ANY finite alphabet. Exact minimum-rank-word length is **PROVED**
for the displayed infinite family. Publication priority **OPEN**;
general Cerny **OPEN**, and no new **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim.

The corank-one theorem in [Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient](#direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient) cannot be
extended by requiring only ONE nontrivial letter-kernel block. A letter
of kernel type (3,1,...) is unimodal and ensures SOME nontrivial stable
pair in an SC automaton, as in [Volkov2023, Lemmas2/8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.13317).
That known existence statement does not make EVERY pair in that block
stable. The original corank-one theorem remains valid.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--binary-original-rows-every-m2"></a>
#### Binary original rows, every m>=2

Put N=2m, n=N+1, and Q={0,...,N}; the extra state is z=N.
Let g cycle the original base states 0,...,N-1, and send z to m+1.
Let f fix every state except

    f(0)=m, f(1)=f(m)=f(z)=0, f(m+1)=z.                 (1)

Thus f has rank n-2 with its ONLY nontrivial fiber {1,m,z}; g has
rank n-1 with its ONLY nontrivial fiber {m,z}. The original graph is
SC: g traverses all base states, f takes m+1 to z, and g returns z
to the base cycle. No virtual completion or extra letter is used.

Let pi(q)=q for q<N, pi(z)=m. The classes of pi form a congruence,
with just one two-state class {m,z}. The quotient rows on Z/NZ are

    G(i)=i+1 mod N,
    F(0)=m, F(m)=F(1)=0, F(m+1)=m, F(i)=i otherwise.     (2)

Both commute with the fixed-point-free involution tau(i)=i+m mod N.
Consequently any quotient antipodal pair stays antipodal under EVERY
word. Its original lifts can NEVER merge. In particular minimum rank
is at least2, so these are nonsynchronizing automata, not counterexamples
to the reset-length conjecture.

For m=2 the original rows are

    f=(2,0,0,4,0), g=(1,2,3,0,3).                       (3)

The f-kernel pair {m,1} is unstable. At m=2 the prefix gf takes it
to {0,z}; at EVERY m>=3 the literal prefix

    v=g^(m-1) f g^(m+1) f                             (4)

takes it to the same {0,z}. Its quotient is {0,m}, an antipodal
deadlock. All exponents and original-letter costs in (4) are paid.
The pair {m,z} IS stable: under any word it stays inside one pi-class;
if that class is the double class, appending g merges it, and the
other classes are singletons.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--a-general-minimum-rank-kernel-identity"></a>
#### A general minimum-rank-kernel identity

For ANY finite DFA, let r be its minimum rank and let U be the set
of ALL original transformations of rank r. Then

    sigma = intersection_(u in U) ker(u).                (8)

If x/y is stable but xu!=yu for a minimum-rank u, a merging suffix
after u would lower rank below r, impossible. Conversely, suppose
every u in U merges x/y. For any prefix v and any fixed u in U,
the word vu also has rank r: its rank is at most r and cannot be
below the global minimum. Hence xvu=yvu for every v. This proves
stability, with the SAME minimum-rank suffix u for all v.

This identity requires neither SC nor any letter-rank restriction.
It reconstructs the usual stability interpretation, without a novelty
claim or a short-word assertion. The special corank-one structure
makes all those kernels equal; the present family shows why taking
their INTERSECTION is essential in general. The independent full-monoid
checker uses (8), separately from the generator's pair graph.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--exact-stability-and-mergeability-not-just-one-bad-pair"></a>
#### Exact stability and mergeability, not just one bad pair

On the quotient, any non-antipodal pair has circular distance
1<=k<=m-1. Rotation can put it at {1,1+k}. For k<=m-2, F sends
this to {0,1+k}, increasing distance to k+1. At distance m-1,
rotation can put the pair at {1,m}, where F merges it. These are
ACTUAL G/F words, and the final original f merges the corresponding
points at1 and in {m,z}. Hence every non-antipodal original lift is
mergeable. The double class itself is mergeable by g.

For m>=3, a distance-(m-1) quotient pair can instead be rotated to
{m,N-1}; F sends it to {0,N-1}, of distance1. Every adjacent pair
can be rotated to {m,m+1}, and F sends it to the antipodal {0,m}.
Thus every DISTINCT quotient pair can reach a deadlock: use the
distance increases first, this return to distance1 next, and the
last adjacent step. At m=2 every non-antipodal pair is already
adjacent. Antipodal pairs themselves are already deadlocks.

It follows that the stability congruence sigma has EXACTLY the pi
classes: only {m,z} is a nontrivial class. Mergeability consists of
ALL original pairs EXCEPT those with antipodal pi images. The deadlock
count is m+1: one antipodal block pair has two original lifts, and
each of the other m-1 antipodal pairs has one.

Mergeability is not transitive, already on {0,1,m}. The pair {1,m}
merges by f, the pair {0,1} merges by the word g(fg)^(m-1) below,
and {0,m} is a deadlock. The least congruence beta with a permutation
quotient is nevertheless UNIVERSAL. Any such congruence contains every
mergeable pair, since permutations cannot merge distinct classes.
It contains {0,1}; its g-images join the whole original N-cycle.
It also contains g's kernel {m,z}, so z joins that class. Therefore
beta!=sigma, despite SC and a unique triple collision fiber. The
all-corank<=1 hypothesis in the canonical-group-quotient theorem is
essential; this weaker test would give a false positive.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--exact-minimum-rank-and-paid-threshold"></a>
#### Exact minimum rank and paid threshold

The ACTUAL composite fg fixes1 and m+1. Its two rooted trees have
basins

    {1,...,m,z}, {0,m+1,...,N-1},                       (5)

and maximum height m-1. Hence

    w=(fg)^(m-1), |w|=2m-2=n-3, rank(w)=2.             (6)

This proves minimum rank EXACTLY2, without an unspecified suffix.
It also supplies two different minimum-rank kernels: w separates
0/1, while gw merges them; gw still has rank2 because g(Q) contains
every base state, and both basins in (5) have base points. Thus ALL
minimum-rank kernels are not unique, and their rank2 is much smaller
than the number N of stable classes.

For the matching lower bound, pass from the pi quotient to its m
antipodal blocks. G acts as the forward m-cycle c, and F as the
idempotent unit u:1->0. Any resetting word needs at least m-1 u
occurrences. A shortest word has no consecutive uu (idempotence),
so it needs at least m-2 separating c letters. Its length is at
least2m-3. The word u(cu)^(m-2) attains this: cu fixes0 and maps
i>0 along i->i+1->...->m-1->0; the initial u removes1.

Let t be the first prefix of an original rank2 word which resets
this m-block quotient. Necessarily t>=2m-3. This first reset step
must be f, and its preceding block image includes both0 and1.
The pi image is tau-invariant, since it starts at all N states and
both quotient letters commute with tau. Therefore the ORIGINAL
preceding image contains0,1,m+1 and at least one point of {m,z}.
Their f-images contain the THREE distinct states m,0,z. Immediately
after this first block reset the original rank is at least3, so
at least one more original letter is necessary. Thus EVERY rank2
word has length>=2m-2. Together with (6),

    min{|x|: rank(x)=2}=2m-2=n-3.                       (7)

The quotient threshold2m-3 and the original threshold2m-2 are different;
the final duplicate-fiber collapse has an actual one-letter cost.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--why-five-states-are-the-first-possible-failure"></a>
#### Why five states are the first possible failure

Here is an elementary reconstruction of the known nontrivial-stability
argument for a unimodal letter h. Choose a maximum-height leaf l in
a minimum-rank image E, using SC. All states at maximum height H
have the same root, so E contains only ONE such state: otherwise
h^H would reduce minimum rank. The image E h^(H-1) therefore has
only one off-cycle point t. Applying a common multiple of all h-cycle
lengths replaces just t by its root's cycle predecessor c. The two
minimum-rank images differ only in t/c. The differing-clique argument
in [Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient](#direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient) makes t/c stable. In particular
sigma is nontrivial for a single nontrivial kernel block, since every
tail enters the same root.

If n<=4, the SC quotient by this nontrivial sigma has at most3 states
and has trivial stability. Each singular letter there either resets
it outright or has defect1. The former makes stability universal,
and the latter has a stable kernel by the general defect-one theorem;
both contradict trivial stability on a quotient with at least2 states.
Thus all quotient letters are permutations. Every original mergeable
pair is already stable, including the ENTIRE distinguished kernel.
At a one-state quotient the same conclusion is immediate. This proves
state-minimality at n5 for ANY finite alphabet, not just binary inputs.
It does not assert binary alphabet-minimality or publication novelty.

<a id="direct-attack-single-fiber-stability-boundary--verification-boundary"></a>
#### Verification boundary

The generator uses original pair reachability and deadlock pullbacks.
The independent checker imports no generator, reconstructs rows from
the quotient lift, and uses COMPLETE original transformation monoids
on its small scopes. It checks ALL minimum-rank maps there, not a
selected word. Separate literal rooted-word and instability-prefix
controls and local quotient distance controls cover the large family
parameters. Exhaustive small binary inputs corroborate the low-state
boundary; the ANY-alphabet minimality and all-m statements are paper
proofs. Corruptions are rejected. Finite records, once checked, are
COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED only within their explicit scopes.

Completed independent controls:745 arbitrary n2/3 binary inputs,5616
complete transformations and16766 original prefix/pair controls for
(8). Separately50751 single-fiber/arbitrary-other n2..4 inputs contain
15934 SC cases,712892 complete transformations and67958 ALL minimum-
rank kernels. The68 family parameters reachn2049, with16532 macro
controls,16660 instability particle steps,38525 literal minimum-word
controls and8196 local quotient distance controls. Each of10097 pairs
has separate forward mergeability and deadlock-reachability checks.
Four small family FULL monoids supply24704 transformations and316
minimum-rank maps; full forward subset graphs contain90 vertices.
Ten corruptions are rejected. The scopes overlap, so their automata
counts are NOT added as disjoint sets.  No fresh
full119-check run, new formal theorem or all-parameter computation.

The earlier broad single-fiber probe did not vary the cycle containing
the collision root; its negative sample could not support this conjecture.
The root-cycle length2 in (1) provides the missing failure mechanism.
The original single-cluster annular paper has not received a complete
independent audit; the partial spectral review is not a verified result.
General Cerny and the cost/dimension hypothesis remain OPEN. The next
general step must handle unstable higher-corank kernel pieces with a
common original word rather than join them as if they were stable.

<a id="direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost--a-short-stationary-mixture-cannot-use-singular-words-in-cerny-automata"></a>
### A short stationary mixture cannot use singular words in Cerny automata

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper), EVERY n>=2.** A method obstruction,
not a general reset theorem. Publication priority **OPEN**; novelty is
not claimed. General Cerny **OPEN**. No **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim.

Later continuation [A fast-reset family needing longer weak stationary support](#direct-attack-weak-stationary-linear-cost-counterfamily) shows
that maximum support n is NOT universal: an SC sync fast-reset family
has exact maximum singular stationary-support cost ceil(3n/2)-1 for
EVERY n>=4. The Cerny-family statement below remains valid. No general
cost-n theorem should be inferred from this particular family's optimum.

Use Q={0,...,n-1}, a(q)=q+1 mod n, and b(n-1)=0 with b fixing all
other states. Words act on row vectors on the right. Let h be the column

    h(q)=n-2-q for 0<=q<=n-2,    h(n-1)=n-1.

For EVERY literal original word w with |w|<=n-1, let r_b(w) be its
number of maximal nonempty consecutive b-runs. Then

    ([Q] M_w-[Q]) h = -r_b(w).                           (1)

Thus a nonnegative probability mixture of words of length at most n-1
satisfying ONLY

    [Q] sum_w p_w M_w = [Q]                              (2)

has zero weight on every word containing b. Its positive-weight support
therefore consists entirely of permutations, so cannot itself generate
a synchronizing semigroup. This includes singular words in the allowed
search: their weights are forced to zero by an exact separating functional.
The condition in (2) is much weaker than asking for matrix average J/n.

<a id="direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost--all-word-proof-including-redundant-words"></a>
#### All-word proof, including redundant words

For ANY word w=a_1...a_L, deterministic row matrices give the exact
telescoping identity

    `Q` = sum_i `Q`-I) M_(a_(i+1)...a_L).

An a term is zero; a b term is (e_0-e_(n-1)) M_v for its literal suffix v.
When L<=n-1, this suffix has length<=n-2. Until the first a in v,
an initial b merges the pair0,n-1 and its term becomes zero. If the suffix
is empty, the two outputs are0,n-1 and their h difference is -1.
Otherwise if its first letter is a, let k>=1 be its number of a's.
There are at most n-2 such letters. Its two trajectories are k,k-1:
no later b acts on either, since neither has reached n-1. Their h
difference is again -1. Hence a b occurrence contributes -1 exactly
when it is the last letter or is immediately followed by a; it contributes
zero when immediately followed by b. These are precisely the final
letters of the b-runs. Summing proves (1). Redundant b's and arbitrary
initial a's are allowed; no shortestness assumption enters the proof.

Applying h to (2) gives sum_w p_w r_b(w)=0. Every term is nonnegative,
so no word containing b has positive weight. Such a word is always
singular, and a word without b is a permutation, because rank cannot
increase after the first b. This proves the stated support obstruction.

<a id="direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost--exact-optimum-for-maximum-support-word-length"></a>
#### Exact optimum for maximum support word length

Consider all nonnegative probability mixtures on actual words which
satisfy (2) and assign POSITIVE mass to at least one singular word.
Their minimum possible maximum support length is exactly

    n.                                                  (3)

The lower bound is (1). For the upper bound use the n words

    w_k=b a^k, k=0,...,n-1,     p_(w_k)=1/n.

For every starting state q, the n outputs (b(q)+k) mod n run through Q
once. In fact the entire matrix average is J/n, implying (2). All support
words are singular and their largest cost is n. The support semigroup
is strongly connected and synchronizing. Strong connectivity follows
already from b and b a: repeatedly applying b a follows0,1,...,n-1,
and b sends n-1 back to0. The literal word

    (b a^(n-1))^(n-2) b

is reset and belongs to the support-generated semigroup; it costs
n(n-2)+1=(n-1)^2. After j copies of b a^(n-1), j>=1, the whole-Q
image is {0,...,n-j-2} union {n-1}; the final b completes the collapse.
At n=2 the repeated factor is empty and b already resets.

The optimum in (3) is a MAXIMUM support-cost statement. There is no
positive lower bound on EXPECTED cost under these weak assumptions:
mix an arbitrarily small positive amount of the displayed distribution
with the empty word. It stays stationary, and still has synchronizing
support. The cost is never silently charged as an expectation instead
of a worst-case original word.

<a id="direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost--relation-to-the-existing-route"></a>
#### Relation to the existing route

The earlier [Independent audit: exact uniform averaging pays quadratic word cost](#direct-attack-permutation-averaging-word-cost-audit) excludes cheap
simultaneous J/n averages using permutation-only words in a different
adjacent-transposition family, with an exact quadratic expected cost.
It explicitly left singular support and weak stationarity outside scope.
The present theorem attacks that weaker alternative on Cerny's binary
family, allowing ALL original words; it has the distinct sharp lower
bound n for maximum support cost. It is not a claim of quadratic cost
for weak stationarity or a refutation of every averaging argument.

The general method is attributed to
[Steinberg, The averaging trick and the Cerny conjecture, Lemma2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.0410).
His two-factor distributions and their support costs must remain intact.
This obstruction does NOT contradict that lemma: its hypotheses and
total support bounds are different. Nor does it refute an average on a
proper invariant subspace or a subset-specific construction. For the
present a-cycle, however, a letter-invariant column space containing
any singleton already contains every singleton under powers of a and
is the full space. Such a space cannot bypass (1) by projection.

Finite controls check all literal words at n2..16, pair suffixes, exact
stationary attainment at retained larger sizes, and literal common reset
words with actual intermediate images. They are separate from the
all-n proof and do not formally verify it. Any new global square approach
must still account for compatibility, singular support, and actual costs;
one must not substitute this obstruction for a positive general theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost--a-positive-projected-stationarity-statement-with-its-hypotheses-paid"></a>
#### A positive projected-stationarity statement, with its hypotheses paid

**PROVED (paper, a dimension-refined reconstruction of the averaging
lemma):** let A be strongly connected and synchronizing. Suppose a column
space W of dimension d contains1_Q and e_q, is invariant under EVERY
original letter, and some strictly positive probability on ALL original
letters defines P satisfying

    [Q] P x = [Q] x for EVERY x in W.                    (4)

Then there is one actual reset word ending at q with length at most

    (n-1)(d-1).                                         (5)

For a proper nonempty Boolean S in W, put x=chi_S-(|S|/n)1_Q. This
nonzero vector lies in W intersect ker[Q], of dimension d-1. The orbit
span chain starting at x cannot stay in that hyperplane forever: a reset
word ending in S, which exists by strong connectivity, has positive
[Q] M_w x. Before escape the chain grows at every layer, so some word
of length<=d-1 gives nonzero [Q] M_w x. Invariance and (4) give
[Q]P^j x=0 for every j. Average P^j over j0..d-1. Strictly positive
letter probabilities assign positive mass to EVERY word through d-1,
and the mean of that functional is0. Its nonconstant values must include
a positive one. Thus an actual word of length<=d-1 strictly increases
|S| under full inverse image. The new indicator stays in W. Starting
from e_q and repeating at most n-1 times reaches Q. Prepending these
actual extension words constructs one common reset, with every letter
charged; this proves (5). At n1 the word is empty.

The proof fails if W is merely the span of ONE history but is not
letter-invariant, if the probabilities omit required original letters,
or if stationarity is imposed only on a few tested vectors without a
spanning/invariance certificate. No universal W,P satisfying these
hypotheses is asserted. The obstruction (1) excludes a full-space
strictly positive original-letter P already in Cerny's family.

Projected stationarity is actually weaker than full pseudo-Eulerian
stationarity. A five-state example with three ORIGINAL letters is

    f=[4,0,4,0,0], g=[1,2,2,1,4], h=[1,3,3,1,0].

Take alpha=(1,1,-1,-1,0), W=ker alpha, q4, d4. Every alpha M_letter=0,
so W is invariant. The equal-weight average has
[Q]P-[Q]=alpha/3 and therefore satisfies (4). The DFA is SC; f g f
resets it in3 steps. Each one- or two-letter word has rank>=2, so rt=3
exactly. No nonnegative probability on the ORIGINAL letters can make
the full matrix doubly stochastic: columns2 and3 force weights of g,h
to each equal1/2, leaving f weight0, but then column4 sums only1/2.
This small example distinguishes the hypotheses, not a new asymptotic
class result. The finite checker verifies every Boolean S in W and
actual inverse-extension witnesses. The general existence problem for
suitable invariant W and paid P remains **OPEN**.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-window-cerny-barrier"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-terminal-window-cerny-barrier--exact-barrier-to-terminal-window-and-rankwise-worst-case-budgets"></a>
### Exact barrier to terminal-window and rankwise worst-case budgets

Date: 2026-10-01. **PROVED (paper)**. This is a reconstruction on
the classical Cerny family and an audit of the NEW terminal-window
method. No novelty or **FORMALLY VERIFIED** claim is made. The
unrestricted Cerny conjecture remains **OPEN**.

Let C_n have Q={0,...,n-1}, a:q->q+1 modulo n and b:n-1->0,
with b fixing all other states. Assume n>=2. For a pair P let
d(P) be its exact shortest merging length.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-window-cerny-barrier--1-exactly-one-pair-at-every-distance"></a>
#### 1. Exactly one pair at every distance

Put N=binom(n,2). For r=1,...,floor(n/2) set

    E_r={r-1,n-1},
    ell_r=n, except ell_(n/2)=n/2 when n is even,
    P_(r,j)=E_r a^(-j),  0<=j<ell_r.

These are the distinct a-orbits, classified by their shorter
circular separation r. They partition all unordered pairs. Exactly,

    d(P_(r,j))=(r-1)n+1+j.                              (1)

Here negative powers only specify states; the resetting words below
use positive a powers. To prove (1), assign the displayed value D
to each pair and zero to singletons. For j>0, a sends P_(r,j) to
P_(r,j-1), lowering D by one. For j=0, a sends it to the last
pair of its SAME orbit, so D(P)<=1+D(Pa) still holds.

Letter b fixes pairs not containing n-1. If it acts on E_r, then
r1 collapses and for r>=2 the result {0,r-1} is the last pair of
orbit r-1. Its value is (r-1)n, exactly one below D(E_r).
The only other n-1-containing pair in orbit r is {n-1-r,n-1},
at j=r. It is distinct from E_r unless r=n/2. Its b-image is
{0,n-1-r}. If r<floor(n/2), this is in orbit r+1 at j=r,
with larger D. The same is true for r=n/2-1 with n even.
If n=2r+1 and r is the last orbit, the b-image is the last pair
{0,r} of that SAME orbit, with value rn, again not smaller than
D(P)-1. Therefore

    D(P)<=1+D(Pa),  D(P)<=1+D(Pb)

for every pair. Telescoping along any merging word proves the lower
bound d(P)>=D(P). Conversely apply a^j b, then recursively merge
the last pair of orbit r-1; its length is j+1+(r-1)n. For r1
the pair collapses directly. This proves the upper bound and (1).

Consequently the exact pair distances are a permutation of
1,2,...,N. In particular the terminal graph F(b) of pairs merged
within b letters has

    |F(b)|=min(b,N).                                    (2)

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-window-cerny-barrier--2-optimizing-the-new-terminal-wedge-window-gives-no-improvement"></a>
#### 2. Optimizing the new terminal-wedge window gives NO improvement

Use the trivial congruence with the single class Q. At rank k set
d=n-k+2 and T=binom(d,2), as in [Terminal kernels refine Frankl compression at every rank](#direct-attack-terminal-kernel-frankl).
For any allowed general-position vectors and any b>=1, the span
rank tau(b) of the terminal-pair wedges is at most |F(b)|<=b.
Hence its guaranteed compression budget satisfies

    b+T-tau(b) >= T.

At b=1 there is exactly one terminal pair, whose wedge is nonzero
in general position; its rank is one. Therefore, for EVERY rank
2<=k<=n, even optimizing the window and the vector choice,

    min_(b>=1) [b+T-tau(b)] = T.                         (3)

Summing these independent rank budgets gives exactly

    sum_(k=2)^n binom(n-k+2,2)=binom(n+1,3).

This exceeds (n-1)^2 at EVERY n>=4. Indeed the difference is
(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)/6. The refinement can strengthen congruence-profile
bounds, but even its best window does not improve the ordinary
Frankl rankwise bound on C_n. This statement concerns the wedge
method, not every possible use of the whole terminal graph.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-window-cerny-barrier--3-even-exact-terminal-graphs-cannot-rescue-separate-worst-rank-sums"></a>
#### 3. Even exact terminal graphs cannot rescue separate worst-rank sums

Define R_k=max{c(S):S is a reachable k-image of C_n}. Every nonempty
subset is reachable: the conjugate unit sending i to i+1 and fixing
the others is a^(n-1-i) b a^(i+1). For any target S, delete each
run of states in Q\S in circular order toward its succeeding state
in S. Every deleted state maps into a still-present successor, so
each unit reduces the image by one. Their product maps Q onto S.
These are existence words, not a claimed short reaching bound.

In fact the exact maximum has a closed form. Set g=floor(n/k),
e=n-gk and t=k-e. Then

    R_k = g(n-k+e+1) = g(n-t+1).                        (4a)

For k=2 this equals binom(n,2), already proved in section 1.
For k>=3, a set with minimum circular gap d<g has compression
at most dn<=(g-1)n, strictly below the displayed value. For a set
with minimum gap g, at most e of its k gaps can exceed g, so at
least t gaps equal g. Their starting labels x, in increasing
ordinary order, are separated by at least g. Thus their maximum
label is at least (t-1)g. From (1), the pair corresponding to a
gap starting at x has phase n-1-x, so its distance is gn-x.
All other pairs have separation at least g+1 and larger distance.
The set therefore compresses in at most gn-(t-1)g. Attain this
by the circular gap sequence consisting of t gaps of length g
followed by e gaps of length g+1, starting at zero. Its tight-gap
starts are exactly 0,g,...,(t-1)g, proving (4a).

The half-orbit ambiguity occurs only at k=2 and was handled above.
At e=0 the same expression is n(g-1)+g, so no extra exception
is needed. A set compresses exactly when some pair in it merges.
In particular

    R_k >= n(floor(n/k)-1)+1.                           (4)

Even before the asymptotic consequence, (4a) gives
R_k>=2(n-k)+1: at g=1 this is equality; at g>=2 the difference
is (g-1)[(g-2)k+2e+1]>0. At n>=4, k2 has g>=2, so

    sum_(k=2)^n R_k > sum_(k=2)^n [2(n-k)+1]
                   = (n-1)^2.                          (4b)

Thus separate rankwise worst-case budgets already exceed the square
at EVERY n>=4, not merely at an asymptotically large size.

Thus any method which proves separately valid budgets B_k for ALL
reachable k-images and then pays every rank must have

    sum_(k=2)^n B_k >= n sum_(k=1)^n floor(n/k)
                        -2n^2+2n-1
                     >= n^2(H_n-3)+2n-1.               (5)

The last inequality uses floor(n/k)>=n/k-1. H_n>=log(n+1), so
this is Omega(n^2 log n). Already for every n>=32, H_n>4,
and the lower bound exceeds the square. A finite check of smaller
n can sharpen that threshold, but is unnecessary for the all-n
barrier. Replacing the wedge allowance by exact graph sequence
capacities still gives valid all-image budgets and cannot evade (5).

This does NOT forbid a square proof using terminal information,
rank jumps or adaptive budgets. The obstruction is the sum of
independent worst phases; the equally spaced worst sets at different
ranks need not occur together in a shortest reset. A successful
general proof needs their compatibility or a different global invariant.

<a id="direct-attack-terminal-window-cerny-barrier--verification-boundary"></a>
#### Verification boundary

check_terminal_window_barrier.py independently recomputes original
pair-graph distances, verifies the entire Bellman/word certificate,
counts terminal layers and checks the rank sums. For small n it
enumerates ordinary reachable images and computes every R_k exactly.
The all-n conclusions (1)--(5) rest on the proofs above, not the
finite calculations. This is separate from the earlier circular
rank-area barrier: (3) tests the new optimized terminal-window bound;
(5) excludes EVERY independently valid worst-rank sum on actual C_n.
The exact formula (4a) and both barriers received an independent
adversarial derivation in [Independent adversarial audit of the terminal-kernel continuation](#direct-attack-terminal-kernel-independent-audit).

<a id="direct-attack-two-letter-almost-circular-route"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-two-letter-almost-circular-route--an-actual-return-model-for-a-two-letter-almost-circular-product"></a>
### An actual return model for a two-letter almost-circular product

Date: 2026-10-02. Normal form below **PROVED (paper, elementary)**,
with no novelty or formal-verification claim. Its general square cost
consequence is **OPEN**. This is a next-route note, not a Cerny proof.
Do not conflate a completed permutation with an available original word.

Later [A paid n-extension theorem for a fixed common defect root](#direct-attack-fixed-root-cycle-extension) proves the ORIGINAL square for
the entire subclass A(1)=1, by a direct paid n-extension construction.
It does not require the almost-circular product in its broader theorem.
The root-moving case A(1)!=1 remains OPEN at the square; removing that
condition from n-extensibility is independently REFUTED already at n4.

Consider a synchronizing binary n-state DFA, n>=3, with original letters
a,b. Assume b is a permutation, a has rank n-1 and level1, and ab has
one cycle of size n-1 and level1. The hypothesis on a's level is explicit;
a longer original tail is outside this normal form. Write r for a's
unique omitted image state, S=Q minus{r}. Since a has level1, a restricted
to S is a permutation A; a's unique collision pair is{r,s} for some s in S.

The image of ab omits b(r). Because ab has one tail vertex and level1,
its omitted state is one member of its unique collision pair. b is
injective, so that pair is still{r,s}. Hence b(r) is r or s. If b(r)=r,
both original letters preserve S and act as permutations on S, making
synchronization impossible. Therefore

    b(r)=s,       C=Q minus{s}=S b.

Complete a to a permutation abar by fixing r and agreeing with a on S.
Then a=u_(r->s) abar. Put G=abar b. G(r)=s, while G(s)=(ab)(s)=(ab)(r).
Every other transition of G agrees with ab. Thus G is obtained from ab's
cycle C by inserting s immediately after r, and is a FULL n-cycle.
This proves an exact transformation normal form. It does NOT make abar
or G available at cost1, or at any known small original cost.

Actual original returns to S are instead

    A = a|S,          cost1, a permutation;
    c = (b a)|S,      cost2, a full (n-1)-cycle;
    f = (b b a)|S,    cost3, rank n-2=|S|-1 on S.

The WHOLE-Q transformation bba still has rank n-1, since b is a
permutation. Its smaller rank above is explicitly the restriction to S.

The full cycle c follows by conjugating ab|C through the bijection b:S->C.
Every b^j a returns S into S, since the last a sends ALL Q into S. To
prove f's rank, note that b^2 S omits b(s). A loses rank on that image
unless its omitted state is r or s. b(s) cannot equal s, by injectivity
and b(r)=s. If b(s)=r, the b-cycle containing r has length2. Then after
the first a, b only toggles the omitted state r/s, while every subsequent
a returns an (n-1)-set omitting r and is injective on it. All words retain
rank at least n-1, contradicting synchronization. Thus b(s) lies outside
{r,s}; both collision points are present in b^2 S, and f has rank |S|-1.

The FULL original return monoid is circular via c and synchronizes because
an original reset followed by a is a return. Initially synchronization of
the chosen c/f subalphabet was left open. The quotient lifting argument
below now proves it. A or other b^j a returns nevertheless can be essential
for a SMALL PAID COST. Connected cycle translates of one kernel pair are
only a sufficient synchronization test; further f images cannot be ignored.
The proved information is an ACTUAL cheap full cycle plus an ACTUAL
cheap singular return, with all labels paid; neither a formal inverse of
A nor the completed G may be used as a free original operation.

For the retained n6/rt25 example

    a=[0,1,2,4,3,3], b=[1,3,5,0,2,4],

r5,s4,S={0,1,2,3,4}. It satisfies the normal-form hypotheses. The exact
cycle-entry pressure already found ab, cost2, level1, cycle size5,
followed by an original cycle reset of cost23, for a whole reset of25.
The cycle C is not invariant under every original letter; C a=S differs
from C. The return model keeps track of this movement rather than treating
C as an invariant five-state original DFA. These are retained finite
observations, not a new all-parameter cost theorem.

The unresolved task is to prove ONE paid reset of the return monoid on
S with cost at most (n-1)^2-1, then prepend the actual entering a. An
unweighted circular theorem on |S| states does not supply this because
c/f have costs2/3 and other returns may be longer. The generic macro
bound in [One-cluster words with original costs and a failed universal bridge](#direct-attack-paid-one-cluster-word-bound) still approaches twice the square
here. A useful next step would exploit the relations forced by a,b and
G's completed cycle while keeping only actual return labels and their
costs. This class is a plausible intermediate route, not a universal
reduction: arbitrary potential Cerny counterexamples need not have an
almost-circular two-letter product or a level1 original singular letter.

<a id="direct-attack-two-letter-almost-circular-route--chosen-cf-synchronization-a-quotient-lifts-back-to-the-original-dfa"></a>
#### Chosen c/f synchronization: a quotient lifts back to the original DFA

This qualitative equivalence is **PROVED paper**, using the established
all-corank<=1 permutation-quotient theorem in
[Stable kernels and the canonical group quotient](#direct-attack-corank-one-stability-quotient). Relabel the completed G-cycle as
0,1,...,M, M=n-1, with r0,s1. Then abar fixes0 and acts as a permutation
A on S={1,...,M}; a=u_(0->1) abar, b=abar^-1 G. Let H be the full cycle
1,...,M on S. Conjugation by A is ONLY a relabeling, never a paid word.
It transforms the actual return c into H and f into F, where

    P=H A^-1 H is a permutation of S,
    F(q)=P(q) for q!=M, and F(M)=1.

Put t=H^-1(A(M)). P(t)=1. If t=M, equivalently A(M)=1, then b swaps0/1,
and both original and return automata are nonsynchronizing, as shown above.
Otherwise F has unique kernel{M,t}, omitted image P(M), and rank M-1.

Suppose the circular all-corank<=1 return DFA{H,F} is nonsynchronizing.
Its established stable minimum-rank quotient is a nontrivial permutation
quotient. Since H is a full cycle, its classes are the residue classes
modulo some d>1 dividing M, all of equal size. F preserves those classes
and induces a permutation rho; its kernel points M,t have the same class0.
For every other class, P=F maps that whole class bijectively onto its
rho-image class. Since P is a permutation, its remaining images of class0
fill precisely the remaining rho(0) class. Thus P induces the SAME rho.
Consequently A=H P^-1 H also preserves the residue classes and induces a
permutation pi. A(M)=H(t) has class1, so pi(0)=1 modulo d.

Extend this partition to Q by putting the extra state0 into class1.
Original a preserves it: on S it induces pi, and a(0)=A(1) has class
pi(1), as required. Original b induces

    sigma(k)=pi^-1(k)+1 modulo d.

For core states, this follows from b=abar^-1 G. Its only exceptional
core transition, where abar^-1(q)=M and G sends M to0, has source
class pi(0)=1, and sigma(1)=1, exactly the assigned class of state0.
Also b(0)=1 has class1, consistent with sigma(1)=1. Thus the original
DFA has a nontrivial permutation quotient and cannot synchronize.
Contraposition proves that original synchronization forces chosen c/f
synchronization. The converse holds by entering S with original a and
expanding a c/f reset literally. This is a qualitative equivalence,
not a bound on its word cost.

<a id="direct-attack-two-letter-almost-circular-route--the-paid-cf-only-square-shortcut-fails-at-the-retained-n6-example"></a>
#### The paid c/f-only square shortcut fails at the retained n6 example

On its S={0,1,2,3,4}, the actual rows are

    c=[1,4,3,0,2], cost2; f=[4,0,3,1,3], cost3;
    A=[0,1,2,4,3], cost1.

The exact weighted reset cost using ONLY c/f is25. Prepending the entering
original a makes26, ABOVE the square25. Adding the actual A return gives
exact cost24, with entering a giving25. Thus synchronization of the two
cheap returns does not suffice for the proposed paid square certificate;
retaining other cheap original returns is essential even at six states.
This is a **REFUTED c/f-only method shortcut**, not a Cerny counterexample.
The finite weighted shortest costs are checked by complete subset Bellman
certificates, independently of discovery Dijkstra. The all-n cost theorem
for the full return monoid is still OPEN. No FORMALLY VERIFIED claim.

Completed finite independent audit:ALL872 normal-form permutations n3..7,
685 synchronizing inputs,277020 positive-cost subset Bellman edge controls
and173987 literal particle/letter controls. The entered c/f-only budget
exceeds the square in100 finite inputs, including the exact n6 obstruction.
Eight corruptions are rejected. This finite scope is COMPUTATIONALLY
VERIFIED, not an all-parameter computational or formal proof.  Native builds remain8. The all-n synchronization equivalence is
PROVED paper; the full-return paid square theorem remains OPEN.
The subsequent [Every square reset of Cerny requires a long cyclic run](#direct-attack-bounded-cerny-returns-obstruction) refutes the fixed
THREE-return square shortcut as well: on ordinary Cerny n4 it costs11
after entering, above9. Indeed, for EVERY n>=4 the entire return pool
b^j a capped by j<n-1 must exceed the square. The all-length return
monoid and the class's general original-alphabet square bound remain
OPEN. The qualitative synchronization equivalence above is unchanged.

<a id="direct-attack-union-defect-accounting"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-union-defect-accounting--quantifying-the-two-losses-in-image-capacity-union-transfer"></a>
### Quantifying the two losses in image-capacity union transfer

**PROVED on paper, elementary identity; priority OPEN.** This is a general
conditional image-extension lemma, not a new n-only synchronization bound.
Let R be the family of actual Q-images, rho(X)=max{|V|:V in R,V subset X},
rho(empty)=0, and Delta(X)=|X|-rho(X). For an ACTUAL word w define

    F_w(X)=rho(pre_w(X))-|X|,
    I=S intersect T, U=S union T,
    m_w(I)=|I\Qw|.

For any S,T (no reachability assumptions are needed for the identity),

    F_w(S)+F_w(T)
      = F_w(U)+|pre_w(I)|-|I|
        +Delta(pre_w(U))-Delta(pre_w(S))-Delta(pre_w(T)).

Proof: preimages preserve unions and intersections, so their cardinalities
satisfy inclusion-exclusion; substitute rho=cardinality-Delta and apply
inclusion-exclusion also to S,T. Each nonempty state fiber contains at
least one source, hence |pre_w(I)|-|I|>=-m_w(I). Consequently, if

    F_w(U)>m_w(I)+Delta(pre_w(S))+Delta(pre_w(T))-Delta(pre_w(U)),

then F_w(S)>0 or F_w(T)>0. For reachable S,T this means the SAME word
image-extends one component, so e(S)<=|w| or e(T)<=|w|. The source image
exists by rho's definition; no ordinary fiber is declared reachable for
free. Conversely, if w image-extends U but neither component, its positive
capacity gain is at most the right-hand defect budget. An actual chosen
endpoint V with |V|-|U|=g satisfies the same necessary g bound, because
g<=F_w(U). This does not by itself bound how such losses accumulate along
a reset construction.

The strict inequality is necessary in general. The earlier n3 union
obstruction has S={1},T={2},w=b=[1,2,1], F_w(U)=1, missing overlap 0,
Delta(pre_w(S))=1, the other defects 0. Its failure is entirely image
availability. The completely reachable n4 obstruction has S={0,3},
T={2,3},w=aa, F_w(U)=1, missing overlap 1, all defects 0. Its failure
is entirely target omission. Both saturate this accounting inequality.

On completely reachable inputs every Delta is zero. A union capacity
gain exceeding the number of omitted overlap states therefore transfers.
The known proper-onto extension union lemma is contained in the case of
zero omitted overlap. These deductions reconstruct the combinatorial
mechanism rather than claiming a novel general union principle. The
unrestricted into-image route still needs control of BOTH loss terms.

check_union_defects.py uses ordinary sets, actual-word transformation
closures and independently enumerated image capacities. It checks the
identity and sufficient condition at every tested proper union, and
verifies both equality obstructions. Its finite counts do not prove the
general lemma: the displayed inclusion-exclusion proof does. No Lean result.

### Only open unpaired short tails: retained weighted cuts and a barrier

2026-10-03. **COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED retained controls only.**
The driver explicitly skips the already-PROVED physical paired class
and all h>=tau inputs. Proposal and omitted-target counts remain
EXPLORATORY, with no exhaustive absence theorem. General Cerny OPEN.

At M8/10/12/14/16/18/20 the seven retained weighted minima are
6/8/8/8/8/9/8. Every original attaining word, sparse lower cut and
actual full reset is independently checked. The resets have lengths
23/28/40/42/55/45/53, below their respective squares. Four corruptions,
including substitution of a solved paired input, are rejected.

**REFUTED constant8 weighted extension conjecture for unpaired short
tails:** the n19, M18 row

    a=[17,10,18,3,13,15,2,14,7,8,1,18,6,12,5,11,16,4,0]

with core-cycle b/root18 fixed, has opposite kernel{2,11}, root-cycle
tau8 and tail height7. The root-absent opposite target{1,10} has
exact positive nu-extension minimum9, nu core1/root2.52 lower-cut
vertices and66 closure edges prove all original words of length<=8
fail; a^3 b a^4 b attains9. Its actual reset upper word has length45.
This does NOT refute the M extension conjecture, the square, or Cerny.

**REFUTED extension of the two-point residue inference to sums:** on
period6, U={0,1,2} has least period6, yet positive multiset{0,3} and
negative multiset{1,4} have equal membership totals in EVERY cyclic
shift. They are different residue multisets. Thus a sum of point
differences can cancel across all shifts without identifying residues.
The independent checker tests every shift and every smaller period.
The PROVED two-point congruence lemmas are unaffected.

This is the concrete obstruction in a naive generalization: for an
unpaired root component, nu a^k-nu is a sum of transported point
differences rather than a single isolated difference. Cyclic averaging
may lose the individual information. In short tails h<tau-1, root
mass can also drop below2 for intermediate a phases, so nonpositive
averaged gains cannot simply be declared zero.

The following limited lemma remains PROVED by direct counting. Before
the tail hits r, if the first transported defect pair distinguishable
by all shifts of an actual-period p target occurs at index i<h, then
a^(i+1) b^s has gain1 for a suitable s<p and retains r for a root-
present target. Earlier differences vanish. Since h<tau and tau+h<=M+1,
for order-two displacement p<=L one has i+1+s<=h+p-1<=M-1. This
eliminates an early mismatch, but does not solve the later cancellation
or root-deficit phases. No complete general unpaired theorem is claimed.

<a id="direct-attack-weak-stationary-linear-cost-counterfamily"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-weak-stationary-linear-cost-counterfamily--a-fast-reset-family-needing-longer-weak-stationary-support"></a>
### A fast-reset family needing longer weak stationary support

Date: 2026-10-02. **PROVED (paper, EVERY n>=4).** General Cerny **OPEN**;
no novelty or formal-verification claim. This directly attacks the proposed
universal maximum-support-cost n bridge after [A short stationary mixture cannot use singular words in Cerny automata](#direct-attack-singular-stationary-word-cost)
established cost n for the Cerny family. The same universal claim is
**REFUTED** here. This is not a lower bound on expected cost or reset cost.

On Q={0,...,n-1}, let a fix0 and cycle1,...,n-1, and let

    b(0)=1, b(n-1)=1, b(q)=0 for1<=q<=n-2.

The state graph is SC. The ORIGINAL letter b has a unique two-cycle0/1
and level1, so this is already within the proved one-cluster subclass.
Write N=n-2 and M=n-1. The ordinary reset threshold is EXACTLY n,
attained by b a^(n-2) b. Nevertheless the EXACT minimum maximum ORIGINAL
support cost for a nonnegative full-Q stationary average with positive
singular mass is

    K*=ceil(3n/2)-1.

The attaining mixture uses only singular words, and its macro-word support
itself is SC and synchronizing. Thus even a fast-reset SC one-cluster DFA
can require maximum stationary-support cost larger than n.

<a id="direct-attack-weak-stationary-linear-cost-counterfamily--exhaustive-all-word-row-classification-and-original-minimum-costs"></a>
#### Exhaustive all-word row classification and original minimum costs

Leading a's preserve [Q], so the first b gives N e0+2 e1. After a b has
occurred, a nonreset word has only two particle positions:0 and a core
point j. A subsequent b either swaps their two masses and returns their
positions to0/1, or merges them at1. The latter occurs exactly when the
intervening a-run has length n-2 modulo M. This exhausts ALL literal
words, including redundant words and leading/trailing powers.

The possible singular full-Q rows and their minimum ORIGINAL costs are:

    A_j=N e0+2 e_j,       b a^(j-1),                cost j;
    B_j=2 e0+N e_j,       b b a^(j-1),              cost j+1;
    R_j=n e_j,           b a^(n-2) b a^(j-1),      cost n+j-1;
    R_0=n e0,            b a^(n-2) b b,             cost n+1.

Here1<=j<=M. At n4 the A/B rows coincide, so their minimum cost is j;
the displayed B witness still has its charged cost j+1. No false claim
of distinct row types is made at this degeneracy. At n>4, the two mass
orientations distinguish A/B. The shortest final core phase j needs
at least j-1 trailing a's; orientation B needs at least two b's. Before
the first merge every completed b block returns the pair to0/1, so a
merge needs a FULL contiguous a-run of n-2 between two b's. Its earliest
cost is n and its endpoint is1. Getting to core j afterwards costs at
least j-1; reaching0 costs at least one more b. This proves the costs,
the ordinary threshold n, and the completeness of the row classification.

<a id="direct-attack-weak-stationary-linear-cost-counterfamily--a-strict-all-short-word-separator"></a>
#### A strict all-short-word separator

Let L=K*-1 and k=L-n+1. Reset rows attainable by cost L can only have
core endpoints j<=k, together with0 if there is enough budget. Define
H={k+1,...,M}; equivalently H={ceil(n/2),...,n-1}. Give the functional
phi the values

    phi(0)=N, phi(j)=-2 for j in H, phi(j)=0 otherwise.

Its full-Q value is N-2|H|, equal to-2 at even n and-1 at odd n. Every
singular row of ORIGINAL cost<=L has NONNEGATIVE phi value. For A_j
it is N^2 minus4 if j in H, otherwise N^2; for B_j it is0 on H and2N
off H. Available R_j off H have value0, and R_0 has value nN. Therefore

    ([Q]M_w-[Q])phi >= 2|H|-N >0

for EVERY singular word |w|<=L. Pure a words are permutations and have
deviation0. A nonnegative average with positive singular mass therefore
cannot be full-Q row stationary within L. This includes ALL redundant
short words, not just the minimum-cost representatives. It disproves the
proposed universal maximum-support bound n for every n>=4.

<a id="direct-attack-weak-stationary-linear-cost-counterfamily--exact-positive-attainment-including-its-support-lifecycle"></a>
#### Exact positive attainment, including its support lifecycle

Put k*=ceil(n/2), H*={k*+1,...,M}. All B_j in H* cost at most n, and
all R_j with1<=j<=k* cost at most n+k*-1=K*.

For even n, give each high B_j weight1/N and each low R_j weight1/n.
The high rows give mass1 to every high coordinate and mass1 to0; the
low rows give mass1 to each low coordinate. Total weight is1/2+1/2=1.

For odd n, give each high B_j weight1/N, add B_1 with weight1/(2N),
give R_1 weight1/(2n), and each R_j,2<=j<=k*, weight1/n. The additional
B_1 fills the missing1/N at0 and gives1/2 at1; R_1 supplies its other
half. The remaining coordinates are exactly1. The two weight groups
again each sum to1/2. These are exact positive rational weights.

The longest low reset R_(k*) has positive weight and cost exactly K*.
Every supported word is singular; R_1 is constant, so the support
synchronizes. From every state the low constants reach all low core
states. From1, each high B_j reaches j, including n-1. From n-1 any
high B_j reaches0. Thus the support state graph is SC as well. All
actions and costs are literal ORIGINAL words, with no free macro letters.

This boundary does NOT refute general linear bounds with a larger
constant, the two-factor averaging framework, or a general square reset
bound. Expected support cost still has infimum0 when a small positive
amount of the attaining mixture is combined with the empty word. Weak
stationarity does not by itself make its maximum support budget<=n.

The independent finite checker verifies the proposed row classification,
separator, rational weights, support SC and literal original reset
certificates. Finite checks are COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED; the every-n
argument above is PROVED paper and receives no FORMALLY VERIFIED label.
General Cerny and universal paid compatibility remain OPEN.

Completed independent finite scope:63 parameters n4..64,127,257;
7308 closed row vertices /14616 original-letter closure edges,6031
short singular row classes,2427 exact supported words and23497012
literal particle/letter controls. Complete closure covers ALL words
on each fixed retained family input, not all DFA inputs or all n.
Eight corruptions are rejected.  Native builds8.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-class-reset-pressure"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-weighted-class-reset-pressure--exact-weighted-returns-and-larger-cycle-class-reset-pressure"></a>
### Exact weighted returns and larger-cycle class-reset pressure

Date: 2026-10-01. The unrestricted proposal

    reset_A(C) <= (|C|-1)(n-1)

remains **OPEN**. This continuation gives an exact scorer for the fixed
two-class schema and fresh finite evidence at much larger n. It does not
establish the proposal, a new unrestricted reset bound, publication
priority, or a **FORMALLY VERIFIED** result.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-class-reset-pressure--exact-weighted-identity-proved-on-paper"></a>
#### Exact weighted identity: PROVED on paper

Fix C={0,...,h-1}, O={h,...,h+t-1}, with h>=2 and t>=h. Letter a
injects C into O and is the full t-cycle on O. Letter b permutes C and
maps O onto C. This is a congruence; every candidate is strongly
connected. From a C-state, a enters O; from any O-state its a-orbit is
all of O, and b reaches every C-state.

Consider the h-state alphabet of actual C-return transformations

    B_0 = b|C,             weight(B_0)=1,
    B_j = (a^j b)|C,       weight(B_j)=j+1,  1<=j<=t.

On the nonempty subsets of C, let d_weight(C) be the minimum total
weight of a path from C to a singleton, or infinity if no such path
exists. Then, exactly,

    reset_A(C) = d_weight(C).

Proof. Every image of C is wholly in C or wholly in O. On either class,
a preserves cardinality, because its restriction to C is injective and
its restriction to O is a permutation. Thus every **shortest** resetting
word from C ends in b. (An arbitrary resetting word need not end in b:
one may append a after reaching a singleton.) Its unique decomposition
at successive b letters is a concatenation of blocks b or a^j b,
j>=1. After the first a of a positive block, the image lies in O;
therefore on C the block a^j b has the same transformation as

    a^(1+((j-1) mod t)) b.

Replacing a longer block by this representative preserves every
successive C-image and never increases length. Every shortest ordinary
reset therefore produces a weighted path of cost no greater than its
length. Conversely, every weighted path expands to its literal blocks
and produces an ordinary word of exactly that path's cost. The two
inequalities give equality, including equivalence of nonsynchronization.

If two return blocks have the same transformation on C, retaining the
cheapest weight preserves every subset transition and can only shorten
an expanded word. There are at most h^h distinct transformations and
at most 2^h-1 nonempty subset vertices. Unlike the previous full-state
64-bit subset scorer, the state count n=h+t can exceed 64 without
affecting subset mask width. The new native implementation uses only
h<=6 in its large-cycle stream and h<=3 in its exhaustive stream; no
unbounded-size implementation claim is made.

The already proved full-reset relation also applies:

    rt(A) = 1 + reset_A(C).

Indeed the first b in any full reset maps its pre-b image, either Q
or O, onto C. Removing any preceding a-prefix saves letters; an a-only
word cannot reset Q. Starting with b and a shortest C-reset attains the
displayed value. Hence weighted synchronization is full synchronization
for this schema, rather than merely pair or first-drop compression.

<a id="direct-attack-weighted-class-reset-pressure--fresh-adaptive-pressure"></a>
#### Fresh adaptive pressure

weighted_class_reset_pressure.cpp uses the exact identity above. It
deduplicates return transformations in increasing literal block cost,
then runs Dijkstra on all reachable nonempty C-subsets. Every stored
word expands to the actual original binary word. No subset vertex cap,
approximate score, or heuristic distance enters an accepted score.

Seed 20261021 proposes 1000000 candidates in 21 profiles:

| h | t values |
|---|---|
| 3 | 25,49,97,193,385,769,1537,3073 |
| 4 | 33,65,129,257,513 |
| 5 | 41,81,161,321 |
| 6 | 49,97,193,385 |

These profiles and this stream are distinct from the previous 1120000
proposals at h3..10,t<=28. The new search mutates O colors, C injections
and the C permutation, and permits occasional score decreases. Its

<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family"></a>
<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family--a-constant-length-word-shortcut-worsens-the-policy-for-infinitely-many-n"></a>
### A constant-length word shortcut worsens the policy for infinitely many n

**PROVED on paper:** for every n>=6 the SC binary base below has rt=P=n,
but adjoining a unit-cost label for its existing length-seven word gives
rt=n and P>=n+1. The transformation monoid and all reachable images stay
unchanged. This is an obstruction to policy monotonicity, not to Cerny.
Priority of this precise family remains OPEN. Right actions are used.

Let Q={0,...,n-1}, n>=4, and

    a=[1,0,0,2,3,...,n-2], b(q)=q+1 mod n,
    u=b b a b b b a, c(q)=q u.

For n>=5, c(0)=c(n-1)=2, c(q)=q+3 for 1<=q<=n-5,
c(n-4)=1, c(n-3)=0, c(n-2)=3. For n=4 it is [2,0,1,2].
Both nonpermutations have rank n-1 and image V=Q\{n-1}; their only
double fibers are {1,2} for a (target 0) and {0,n-1} for c (target 2).
Adding c changes word costs, while it cannot change the generated monoid.

<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family--all-nonempty-subsets-are-actual-images-and-extend-within-n"></a>
#### All nonempty subsets are actual images, and extend within n

Induct downwards on subset size. For a nonempty proper S choose a cyclic
boundary h outside S with d=h+1 inside S. Let r=d and Y=S b^(-r).
Then 0 belongs to Y and n-1 does not. Hence |a^-1Y|=|Y|+1 and
(a^-1Y)a=Y. By induction T=a^-1Y is an actual image (or Q).
The word a b^r, of length <=n, maps T ONTO S. This proves complete
reachability and e(S)<=n for every proper S in the binary base. The
augmented automaton has the same image family and no larger extension
cost. Strong connectivity follows from b. Thus the sufficient square
condition in [Reachable-fiber anchoring improves the image rank-profile bound](#direct-attack-anchored-image-profile) applies to both automata.
This reconstruction of an extension mechanism is not claimed as a new
general complete-reachability theorem.

<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family--exact-reset-threshold-and-base-policy"></a>
#### Exact reset threshold and base policy

The word a^(n-2) b a resets Q to 0, with length n. Each letter can drop
rank by at most one. A reset shorter than n would therefore have exactly
n-1 steps, every step a rank drop. Its first a or c gives V. Since n-1
is absent from V and every subsequent a-image, c cannot drop rank there;
b never drops rank. The subsequent steps must all be a. Its repeated
images end at {0,1}, which a swaps. This excludes such a reset, proving
rt=n in both alphabets for every n>=4.

For the base, {0} has extension cost 1 via the image {1,2} and a.
The pair {1,2} has extension cost 2 via {0,1,2} and ab: its one-letter
inverse images have size <=2. For S_k={0,...,k-1}, 3<=k<n, the one-letter
inverse a^-1 S_k=S_(k+1) is an image. These phases cost
1+2+(n-3)=n. Since rt<=P, this proves P_base=n.

<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family--a-critical-three-image-requires-another-neutral-step"></a>
#### A critical three-image requires another neutral step

Now n>=6, and T={0,n-4,n-1}. For any subset X,

    |a^-1X|-|X|=1_(0 in X)-1_(n-1 in X),
    |c^-1X|-|X|=1_(2 in X)-1_(n-1 in X),
    |b^-1X|-|X|=0.

Any word carrying Q into T of length <=n-2, read inversely from T to Q,
would need net gain n-3. These unit-defect letters allow no decrease and
at most ONE neutral step within that budget. Initially T contains n-1,
so no positive step is possible. Its possible first neutral steps are:

* a^-1T={1,2,n-3}, which excludes 0 and includes 2;
* b^-1T={n-1,n-5,n-2}, still containing n-1;
* at n=6, c^-1T={0,3,n-1}, still containing n-1. For n>=7
  c^-1T has size 2, so it is a forbidden decrease.

After the first a step, the only positive next step is c. That step
introduces n-1, yielding a four-set still smaller than Q. Another neutral
step is then necessary before any further growth. The other neutral
choices already retain n-1 and permit no growth. All possibilities
contradict the budget. Consequently D(Q,T)>=n-1, where D allows the
terminal Q-image to be a subset of T. At n=5 the analogous guard DOES
reach Q; the excluded boundary is necessary.

<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family--every-initial-singleton-costs-more-than-n"></a>
#### Every initial singleton costs more than n

Because all subsets are reachable and each inverse edge gains at most
one, a shortest image extension from rank k first reaches exactly rank
k+1. Its endpoint must be that whole inverse image: no larger contained
image exists at that first distance. Every policy chain from a singleton
therefore has n-1 phases, each with positive cost.

In the augmented alphabet singleton 0 has e=1 with the ONLY endpoint
{1,2} (via a). That pair has e=1 with the ONLY endpoint T (via c).
Thus G({0})=2+G(T)>=n+1, since the policy constructs an actual transport
Q into T and G(T)>=D(Q,T).

Singleton 2 has e=1 with the ONLY endpoint {0,n-1} (via c). This pair
has e=2 and ONLY first-growth endpoint T, through inverse a then inverse
c. Inverse b retains n-1 and cannot grow at the next step; inverse c
decreases to a singleton, which cannot grow to rank 3 in one step.
Thus G({2})=3+G(T)>=n+2.

Every other singleton has e>=2. If e>=3, its first cost plus n-2
remaining positive phases already gives >=n+1. If e=2, its intermediate
inverse prefix must be a singleton, and the next step grows only at
target 0 or 2. Its first endpoint is therefore {1,2} or {0,n-1}, whose
values just proved give total >n. This proves P_augmented>=n+1.

<a id="direct-attack-word-shortcut-family--exact-finite-data-and-boundaries"></a>
#### Exact finite data and boundaries

For n=4,...,22 the exact augmented P values are

    5,5,9,9,13,13,17,17,21,21,25,25,29,29,33,33,37,37,41.

The apparent formula 2n-3 for even n and 2n-5 for odd n>=5 is
**CONJECTURED**, not an arbitrary-n theorem. In particular an unbounded
policy gap is not proved by the lower bound n+1. The n4 failure is the
state-minimal word-shortcut witness in [Image policy can become worse when letters or word shortcuts are added](#direct-attack-alphabet-policy-obstruction);
n5 has P=rt=5. A different shortcut b^2 a b^(n-1) a gives P=n in the
tested n5..12, so replacing the fixed three b's by that parameter rotation
does not preserve the observed failure.

The full-cube native solver and an independent ordinary-set sparse inverse
all-tie recursion agree on EVERY saved singleton e/G/worst value through
n22. The older forward-transport kernel additionally agrees through n12.
Independent closed graphs exclude all reset words of length <n and all
critical transports of length <=n-2 for the saved cases. Paper proofs,
not finite graphs, establish the arbitrary-n claims above. No Lean result.
